## D591 — Two-faced cards from printed data: adventure, modal double-faced, transform

The largest single gap left was not a sentence but a shape. **622 legal cards were refused
outright** as "layout … has more than one face" — 388 transforming, 136 adventurers, 98 modal
double-faced — so a pasted deck with a Bonecrusher Giant, a Pathway or a Delver got cardboard. The
engine has played all three kinds since #140, #141 and #217, for hand-written cards; nothing could
build one from data.

**Where the faces come from.** The corpus is built from Forge's card files, which keep every face
in one file after an `ALTERNATE` line. The converter (`scripts/corpus/from-forge.mjs`) threw
everything after the first face away. It now writes `card_faces`, Scryfall's own field in
Scryfall's shape, so the same code reads a real Scryfall import when one lands; the regenerated
corpus is identical to the old one in every other field, row for row. The corpus loader writes the
faces to `scryfall_cards.card_faces`, a column that has always been there and always been null.

**What the compiler does with them.** The front face is compiled as the card; every other face is
compiled on its own and put on the definition (`CardDef.faces`), where the engine already looks.
Each face's unread lines are the card's, so an adventurer whose creature reads and whose adventure
does not is not counted as read whole. A transforming card's back face has no cost and the front's
mana value (CR 712.4c); an adventure and a modal back face are cast for their own. A row with
faces missing is still refused, rather than read as its front alone.

**Battles are refused**, and that is new. Five Invasions read whole the moment faces were built —
their text is one enter trigger — but the engine has no defense counters, no protector and no way
to attack a battle, so a compiled one would sit on the board for ever and never turn over. A
reading with nothing left unread to flag it is the worst kind (D362); 36 battles are now refused
with that reason instead.

**And in production.** The realtime card lookup selects `card_faces` and matches a pasted name
against the part of Scryfall's "Akoum Warrior // Akoum Teeth" before the slashes; the pasted-deck
builder indexes such a row under its front face too. A live-Postgres test inserts a Scryfall-shaped
row and builds a deck from "Akoum Warrior".

    two-faced legal cards:                  622
    now compiled:                           582  (transform 350, adventure 134, modal 98)
    still refused:                          40   (36 battles, 4 whose size is a */* nothing reads)
    newly read whole, every face:           72   (adventure 40, modal 32, transform 0)

No transforming card reads whole yet: the line that says *when* it transforms is almost always
unread, so at the table these play as their front face and are turned over by hand. That family
("transform ~" in triggers, daybound and nightbound) is the next lever here.

**The pool's own faces, checked for the first time.** The standing check of every built-in card
against its Oracle row (D571) could not see a back face, because the corpus had none, and listed
nine faces as unverified. With faces in the corpus all nine have rows, and five facts were wrong:
**Venture Deeper costs {U}**, not {1}{U}; **Shield's Might gives +2/+2**, not +3/+3 (its script
pumped +3/+3 too); and Hagra Broodpit and Vastwood Thicket carried the older "enters the
battlefield tapped" wording. All corrected, and the unverified list is down to the three whole
split cards, whose halves are each checked under their own names.

**One convention kept, and kept out of the rules.** The pool writes an adventurer's Adventure on
the creature too ("Venture Deeper {U} (Sorcery) — …"), so a card in hand shows both halves; the
Oracle check already lists it as deliberate. Compiled as the creature's own text that quote became
an unread line on Merfolk Secretkeeper, and the gate's coverage test caught it. At play time the
quote is now left out of the front face, since the face carries those rules itself.

**Not built:** split cards (126 rows; the pool's two are hand-written), flip, meld, prepare,
specialize and omen. Each has its own rules.

**Tests.** 8 engine tests on corpus rows (Curious Pair, Akoum Warrior, Barkchannel
Pathway, Delver of Secrets, Invasion of Belenon): faces built and counted; a back face's unread
line is the card's; an adventurer offers both casts and its adventure resolves and exiles it; a
modal card plays its land back face, which enters tapped from its own text; a pathway is a land
either way; the derived definition compiles again at play time; a battle is refused; a row
without faces is still refused. Plus a live-Postgres test of the lookup and a loader test that
the faces reach the table.

## D592 — Transforming cards turn themselves over from printed text

D591 compiled 350 transforming cards and not one of them read whole: the line that says **when**
the card transforms was unread on every one, so a pasted Huntmaster or Gatstaf Shepherd played as
its front face for the whole game. This reads the commonest of those lines.

**"Transform ~" and "transform it."** An effect clause, through the same `transformPermanent` that
Delver of Secrets and Thing in the Ice use. The name is whichever face the line is printed on,
because each face is compiled under its own name — the front says "transform Gatstaf Shepherd" and
the back "transform Gatstaf Howler", and both mean this permanent. "It" is what the trigger is about
and falls back to the card, explore's rule: on Vildin-Pack Alpha, "Whenever a Werewolf you control
enters, you may transform it", the Werewolf that entered turns over, not the Alpha. The first draft
read "it" as the card, and the corpus listing of every printed "transform it" is what showed the
one card where that is wrong.

**Only if it has not transformed since (CR 701.28f).** The resolving ability carries the face its
source showed when it went on the stack (`EffectContext.sourceFace`, from the stack object's
`cardKey`). Showing another face means something turned it over in between, and the ability does
nothing: "{4}{G}: Transform Kessig Prowler" activated twice in response to itself turns it over
once. A permanent turned over **twice** in between shows the same face again and is not caught;
nothing in the corpus can do that with one ability waiting, and the gap is written beside the code.

**The werewolves' clock.** "At the beginning of each upkeep, if no spells were cast last turn,
transform ~" and the back face's "if a player cast two or more spells last turn". Neither can be
answered from the turn's own tally, which the cleanup step empties before the upkeep, so the
cleanup step now copies it first: `GameState.spellsCastLastTurnBy`, per seat, because "a player
cast two or more" is one seat's count — one spell each from two players keeps the back face up.
Empty before any turn has ended, which reads as no spells, the honest answer on turn one. Plus
"if ~ is equipped" (Avacynian Missionaries), read live off the board.

**"When this creature transforms into <this face>".** The `transformed` event Awoken Horror
already used, now read: alone, as "enters or transforms into" (two events, one effect — Huntmaster,
Brigid, Ashling and eight more), and as "transforms into ~ or dies". The name after "into" has to be
the face the line is printed on; a line naming the other face is left unread rather than looked up.
And "When ~ deals combat damage to a player" now reads with "When" as well as "Whenever" (Uninvited
Geist): the same event.

**An engine bug the tests found.** `settle` only starts a pass when one of its event lists is
non-empty, and the guard listing them had never included `transformed` or `copied`, though the
pass drains both. So a transform **on its own** was never announced until some unrelated event
carried it: Brigid turning back to her front made no Kithkin. Thing in the Ice hid this for every
test since #217 — its trigger is a spell cast, and the instant reaching a graveyard starts the pass
in the same action. The same was true of a copy made by a trigger, which is storm and replicate:
magecraft saw the copy late. Both are in the guard now, each with a test that fails without it.

**Still unread on transforming cards:** daybound/nightbound (36 cards — day and night is a rule of
its own, CR 726), Sagas whose last chapter returns them transformed (28), disturb (24), "More Than
Meets the Eye" and living metal (13), craft (9), and the transform abilities paid with Phyrexian
mana (17). Most "transforms into" lines that remain are blocked by their effect, not the event.

**Tests.** 12 engine tests on corpus rows (Gatstaf Shepherd, Kessig Prowler, Geier Reach Bandit,
Avacynian Missionaries, Uninvited Geist, Huntmaster of the Fells, Brigid): a werewolf turns over
after a turn with no spells and back after one player casts two; one spell keeps the front, one
each from two players keeps the back; the cleanup step keeps the tally and a new game has none;
the double activation turns over once; "it" is the trigger's subject; "if ~ is equipped"; "When"
combat damage; the two-event and one-event "transforms into" shapes and the wrong-face refusal;
Brigid pays to turn over and turning back makes a Kithkin; a storm copy is announced in the action
that made it; and a pasted list finds a card whose data is named "Front // Back" (D591's break-run
miss, below), and every face's read lines are counted. Each of the two guards and CR 701.28f was
removed by hand and its test failed.

    engine tests: 4,204, all passing
    web 264, realtime 60, api 326, all passing (no change there)

**D591's line figure was low, and this corrects it.** Measured first, the line total *fell* by 50
while coverage rose, which cannot happen if every line is counted once. `compileFaces` kept each
back face's unread lines but dropped its read ones, so a back-face line that became readable left
the count instead of moving across it, and the back faces' read lines were never in D591's 25,795
at all. The compiler now returns every face's read lines; the measure is the only consumer. Cards
read whole are unaffected — that count never looked at read lines. On the same build before the
fix the figure was 25,884 of 57,981 (44.6%): under the old count D592's readers added 89 lines to
D591's 25,795, and the 543 between the two counts are back-face lines that were already read and
never counted.

## D593 — Day and night: daybound and nightbound

The second werewolf rule, Innistrad: Midnight Hunt's (CR 726, CR 702.145), and the one 36 legal
transforming cards print instead of D592's upkeep sentence. It is a fact about the **game**, not a
card: `GameState.dayNight` is `day`, `night` or `null`, and every game starts `null`.

**Three rules, three functions** (`effects.ts`):

- `establishDayNight` — the first time a permanent with daybound is on the battlefield and it is
  neither, it becomes day (night for nightbound). Asked in every `settle`, after arrivals.
- `dayNightAfter` — as a turn begins, day becomes night if the **previous turn's active player**
  cast no spells during it, and night becomes day if they cast two or more. That player's count
  only, from D592's per-seat last-turn tally: two instant-speed spells from somebody else do not
  keep it day. Called where `advanceStep` hands the turn on.
- `matchDayNight` — every daybound permanent shows its back by night and every nightbound one its
  front by day. Read off live characteristics, so a werewolf that has lost all abilities stays as it
  is. Turning over because the time changed **is** a transform, and "transforms into" sees it; a
  card that arrives already matching the time of day enters transformed and does not (CR 712.14) —
  `transformPermanent` takes a `record` flag for that one case, and `arrivalReplacements` uses it.

**Daybound and nightbound are keywords**, changeling's reason: the rule asks a permanent whether it
has one. **"Whenever day becomes night or night becomes day"** is a new event, `day-night`, raised
at the change and not when a game that was neither first becomes day. **"If it's neither day nor
night, it becomes day as ~ enters"** is `becomesDayAsItEnters`, applied on arrival. The ten cards
that print the trigger print that line too.

**On the table:** a Day or Night pill in the top bar once it is either, with the rule in its
tooltip, and the same word in the watchers' header. `GameView.dayNight` is optional, so a view
from an older server reads as neither.

**Not read yet:** "it becomes night/day" as an effect (Into the Night, Unnatural Moonrise, The
Celestus's ability, Tovolar's upkeep), "if it's night" conditions (Olivia's Midnight Ambush, Wolf
Strike, Moonrager's Slash), Angel of Eternal Dawn's "it can't become night", and Sunstreak
Phoenix's trigger, which fires from a graveyard and stays unread rather than read as a battlefield
one. CR 702.145b's restriction — a daybound permanent cannot be transformed by anything else — is
not enforced; nothing the compiler reads tries.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests on corpus rows (Bird Admirer, Firmament Sage) and a probe built on Bird
Admirer's shape with a "transforms into" line on each face: the keywords, the line and the trigger
read; a game starts neither and a daybound card makes it day, in the view too; no spells makes it
night and turns the card over, two make it day and turn it back; only the previous active player
counts, and one spell changes nothing either way; a daybound card cast at night enters on its back
face without its trigger, and becoming day turns it over with its front's; the Sage makes it day
without a change and draws on the next one. Three faults were put in by hand — the arrival recorded
as a transform, the change not raised, the wrong seat counted — and each failed its test. The pool's
mechanic check names all four new mechanics as compiler-only, with this evidence.

## D594 — The Clone family from printed text

"You may have ~ enter as a copy of …" was the commonest one-line-short shape left in the corpus,
and it is a Commander staple: Clone, Stunt Double, Phyrexian Metamorph, Sculpting Steel, Copy
Enchantment. The pool has had a hand-written Clone since the layers work; nothing could read one.

**Read into exactly the hand-written Clone's shape**: a "you may" question over the whole
battlefield as the spell resolves (`min: 0`, so declining is legal) and `becomeCopyOf` on the
answer, which points the arriving permanent at the copied card — so its abilities, its statics and
its entry trigger are the copied card's, as the printed card says. What is new is the noun and the
exceptions.

**The noun** is a disjunction of type runs, each word read by `permanentWordMatch` against the
**live** type line: "any creature", "any artifact or creature", "any nonland permanent", "any Ally
creature", "any Equipment", "any land". And the side: "on the battlefield" is anybody's, "you
control" yours, "an opponent controls" theirs. A clone whose noun is creatures only also sets
`copiesACreature`, the hand-written Clone's hint to the computer player.

**The exceptions** are three printed forms joined by commas and "and": "it's a <types> in addition
to its other types" (card types and subtypes both — Synth Infiltrator's "Synth artifact creature"),
"it isn't legendary", and "it has <keywords>". They become a derived definition through
`TokenCopyProfile`, the one embalm and eternalize already use, registered under the copied card's
key plus a suffix so the copied card itself is untouched; a keyword is a line appended to the text,
which `printedKeywords` reads back. Because the exceptions live in the definition, a Clone of the
clone copies them too, which is the rule (CR 707.9b). Anything else after "except" — a quoted
ability, a changed name, counters, "with power 4 or greater", Dack's Duplicate's dethrone (not a
keyword the engine has) — refuses the line rather than copying without it.

**Not built, and the same as the pool's own Clone:** the question is asked when the spell resolves,
so a clone put onto the battlefield another way — reanimated, blinked — arrives as itself. "Enter as
a copy" is a replacement on any entry (CR 707.5); that wants the arrival replacements to be able to
ask a question, which they cannot yet.

**Tests.** 7 engine tests on corpus rows (Stunt Double, Mirror Image, Malleable Impostor, Glasspool
Mimic's front face) and one probe for "isn't legendary", which no card prints alone: all read
whole; "any creature" offers both sides and arrives as the copy with its haste; "you control"
offers only yours; "an opponent controls" with two added subtypes and flying, and the copied card's
own definition unchanged; a Stunt Double copying a Glasspool Mimic is a Shapeshifter Rogue too; a
non-legendary copy of Krenko leaves two Krenkos; an exception it cannot build leaves the line
unread. The exceptions dropped, and the derived definition written over the original's key, were
each put in by hand and failed. Plus the two D593 tests below.

    engine tests: 4,219, all passing; web 264, realtime 60, api 326

## D595 — Restricted mana: "Spend this mana only to …"

179 legal lines print a restriction on what a mana ability's mana may pay for, and the engine had
no way to say it, so every one was unread — and an unread mana line is a land that taps for
nothing. Ancient Ziggurat, Mishra's Workshop, Haven of the Spirit Dragon and the rest arrived in a
pasted deck as dead lands.

**The model: the mana never floats.** A pool cannot tell restricted mana from free mana, and giving
it a second bucket would mean teaching every payment in the engine which bucket it may draw on. So
the restricted mana is made only **while paying** for something it may pay for:

- `AbilityDef.spendOnly` — the restriction, as a test of a `PaymentFor` (a spell's live type line,
  or the live type line of an ability's source) and the printed words.
- `manaSources(state, seat, paying?)` lists a restricted source only for a payment it allows, and
  never when the caller does not say what it is paying for — so every caller that has not been
  taught about it under-offers rather than over-offers. A land with a free row and a bigger
  restricted one (Eldrazi Temple's shape) offers the bigger row where it may be spent and the free
  one elsewhere; one-mana rows are simply more choices.
- `payFrom` takes `paying`; casting a spell passes the spell's type line, activating an ability
  passes its source's. Mana a restricted source made beyond the cost is **lost** rather than left
  in the pool, where it could pay for anything: Mishra's Workshop's three for a one-mana artifact
  leaves nothing floating.
- `legalActions` asks the same question when it offers a cast or an ability, and does not offer a
  restricted mana ability as a button at all; activating one by hand is refused with the reason.

**The vocabulary** (`spending.ts`, shared by the land mana-line parser and the line reader): a
casting half — "to cast creature spells", "an instant or sorcery spell", "a noncreature spell",
"artifact spells", "Dragon spells", "spells" — and an activating half — "to activate abilities",
"of artifacts", "of an artifact source" — either or both. Type words only, read live: lowercase is
a card type, "noncreature" or "legendary"; capitalised is a subtype. Anything else is refused and
the line stays unread: "a multicolored spell", "colorless Eldrazi spells", "the chosen type",
"kicked spells", "costs that contain {X}", and every rider ("and that spell can't be countered").

**Two older tests pinned the old refusal** on purpose — Ancient Ziggurat's line and a land probe
with a creature-spell restriction. Both now pin a restriction that is still refused (a multicolored
spell), with a note that the type-word ones are read since this entry.

**Not built:** the bot's own planning counts mana without restricted sources (it plays what
`legalActions` offers, which does count them, so it casts with them — it just does not plan around
them); the faint "mana you could make" pips count them as if free, which is the optimistic display
they have always been; and convoke, delve and the special payments (morph, foretell, suspend) do
not draw on them.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests on corpus rows (Ancient Ziggurat, Mishra's Workshop) and two probes: the
restriction is read onto the ability and an unknown one leaves the line unread; Ziggurats pay for
Grizzly Bears and not for Lightning Bolt, are not a button, refuse a hand-pressed activation and
are tapped by the cast; Mishra's Workshop casts Bonesplitter and leaves no {C} floating; "to
activate abilities" offers an equip and not a spell; the two-row land offers {C}{C} for a creature
and {C} otherwise. Unused restricted mana kept, and restricted sources counted for any payment,
were each put in by hand: the first failed one test, the second three.

    engine tests: 4,224, all passing; web 264, realtime 60, api 326

## D596 — Protection from more than colours

Protection was modelled as a list of colours, and `printedPart` refused any other quality on
purpose: a card promising more than the engine could check was left to a human. 37 legal lines
promised more, and 27 cards were one line short of it — Beloved Chaplain, Foothill Guide, Baneslayer
Angel, Progenitus, Elite Inquisitor, Enemy of the Guildpact.

**One list beside the colours.** `Characteristics.protectionQualities` holds the qualities that are
not colours, as tags: a card type ("from artifacts", "from creatures", "from instants"), a creature
type ("from Goblins", "from Demons and from Dragons", read against the corpus-derived creature-type
list in its plural), the snow supertype, "multicolored", "monocolored" and "everything". It is a
printed, base characteristic like the colours and cleared with them when a permanent loses all its
abilities.

**One test for all four rules.** `protectionApplies` already answered DEBT (CR 702.16) — damage,
enchanting and equipping, blocking and targeting all call it, directly or through `protectedFrom` —
so the qualities are checked there, against the **live** characteristics of the other object: a
land animated into a creature is a creature to protection from creatures, a spell on the stack is
an instant to protection from instants, a gold card is multicoloured. Nothing else had to change.

**A list printed with commas is one ability.** "Protection from Vampires, from Werewolves, and from
Zombies" split on its commas was three parts, two of them nonsense; the line is joined back into
the "and from" form the part reader already takes before it is split.

**Still refused, each a quality with a condition the tag cannot hold:** "from non-Spirit
creatures", "from permanents with corruption counters on them", and the chosen-colour and
chosen-player forms.

**D595's break run** caught 9 of 10. The miss was "a noncreature spell" read as its opposite, which
no test had asked; a probe land restricted to noncreature spells now casts a Lightning Bolt and not
a Raging Goblin, and fails with the fault in.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests on corpus rows (Beloved Chaplain, Foothill Guide, Enemy of the Guildpact,
Elite Inquisitor) and a probe for protection from artifacts: every row reads, the comma list is
three subtypes, a conditional quality stays unread; a creature cannot damage or block the Chaplain
and a spell can still damage it; Foothill Guide is protected from a Goblin and not from Bears, Enemy
of the Guildpact from Selesnya Charm and not from a mono-red Goblin, and the probe from Bonesplitter,
which then cannot be equipped to it while it still equips Grizzly Bears. The qualities ignored, and
the comma join removed, were each put in by hand and failed.

## D597 — Affinity for anything

Affinity was `'artifacts'` and nothing else, and the type's own docblock said so: "`artifacts` is
the one the pool has cards for. The day another arrives it is a second member of this union rather
than a second field." 38 legal lines print another, and 17 cards were one line short of it.

`CardScript.affinity` is now `'artifacts'` or an `AffinityFor` — the printed phrase and a test of
one permanent — and `costChangeFor` counts the caster's permanents with whichever it has, live, as
the cost is computed. The keyword reader reads "affinity for <phrase>": a card type in the plural,
a subtype in the plural (the basic land types, Equipment, Gates, Foods, Vehicles and every creature
type the corpus knows, through `isCreatureType`), "historic permanents" (legendary, artifact or Saga,
CR 700.6), "outlaws" (Assassin, Mercenary, Pirate, Rogue, Warlock, CR 700.12) and "tokens". A
phrase it cannot count ("blue permanents") stays unread. Only generic mana moves, as before.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests on Razor Golem's corpus row and a probe with affinity for creatures: both
read and an uncountable phrase stays unread; six Plains pay for the Golem entirely, five Forests
take nothing off, three Plains and two Forests take {3}; two Grizzly Bears take {2} off the probe and
the lands do not count. The phrase's test replaced by the artifact count was put in by hand and
failed two of them. Plus the two D596 tests above.

## D598 — Disguise

Murders at Karlov Manor's morph: cast face down for {3} as a 2/2 with **ward {2}**, turned face up
for the disguise cost (CR 702.168). 46 legal lines print a bare "Disguise {cost}", and 12 cards were
one line short of it.

**Read as morph with one flag.** `keywordWithCost` reads Disguise beside Morph and Megamorph and
returns `disguise: true`; `morph.disguise` carries it on the script, in all three places a costed
keyword becomes a morph. The face-down cast and the turn-up are morph's own, unchanged.

**The ward is a granted trigger, and that is the whole design.** A face-down permanent has no
script, which is how the engine keeps morph's rule, and both the place triggers are collected and
the place a trigger is resolved ask the face-down card for nothing. The ward a disguised one has is
the rules' gift rather than the card's text — exactly what a granted trigger is. So `raise` fires
it from a reserved reference, `DISGUISE_GRANT`, and `scriptFor` answers that reserved name with
`DISGUISED_FACE_DOWN`, whose one granted trigger is the pool's `ward(…, '{2}')`. Every site that
fires, aims or resolves a granted trigger already goes through that lookup, so nothing else had to
learn about disguise. The first attempt gave the face-down permanent a script instead; the trigger
fired and then resolved as the card's own first trigger, because the stack looks a trigger up by
the card and its index. Not while it has lost all its abilities.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests on Riftburst Hellion's corpus row and the pool's Battering Craghorn: the
keyword reads as a disguised morph with its cost; face down, the Hellion's ward counters a Lightning
Bolt whose caster has no mana left, and it survives undamaged; a face-down Craghorn has no ward and
the same Bolt kills it. The ward's firing removed was put in by hand and failed. Plus the two D597
tests above.

## D599 — Retrace

"You may cast this card from your graveyard by discarding a land card in addition to paying its
other costs" (CR 702.81). 18 legal lines, 10 cards one line short: Flame Jab, Raven's Crime and the
rest of Shadowmoor and Eventide's cycle.

**Flashback's zone, the printed cost, and D585's discard narrowed to land cards.** `CardScript.
retrace` from the keyword; `castablePlays` lists a retrace card in the graveyard beside the
flashback and escape lists, offers it for its printed cost with the hand's **land cards** as the
play's `discardOptions`, and does not offer it at all with no land in hand. It is kept out of the
paths a hand cast takes (morph, foretell, suspend, the alternative costs) exactly as escape is.
`castSpell` checks the card is in its caster's graveyard and that the discard named is one of
those land cards, and pays the discard through the same field D585's additional cost uses. A card
that prints both retrace and a discard cost would be two discards, which nothing prints; it is not
offered. The spell goes back to the graveyard as it resolves, which is the rule.

**On the table** the play travels a `retrace` flag the web sends with the cast, beside flashback
and escape; the land is chosen with the table's existing discard picker.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests on Flame Jab's corpus row: it reads; it is offered from the graveyard with
only land cards to discard and not at all with none in hand; a non-land discard is refused, and a
land discard casts it, deals its damage, and leaves both the land and the Jab in the graveyard. The
land check removed was put in by hand and failed. The pool's mechanic check names `script retrace`
as compiler-only, with this evidence. Plus the two D598 tests below.

## D600 — Mass effects over a scope, and overload by its own rewrite

Overload was the plan: 28 legal lines, 11 cards one line short. CR 702.96b says what paying it does —
"change its text by replacing all instances of the word 'target' with the word 'each'" — and that is
a rewrite the compiler can do literally and then read. Doing it showed the bigger gap underneath: the
rewritten sentences did not read because **no mass effect but "destroy all creatures" did**. "Destroy
all artifacts." was unread. So was "Destroy all lands", "Destroy all enchantments", "Return all
creatures to their owners' hands", "Tap all creatures your opponents control" — 150 legal lines,
118 cards one line short.

**One mass reader.** "Destroy / exile / tap / untap / return … all or each <scope> [to their owners'
hands]", with the scope read by `massScope`: `boardScope`'s controller clause ("you control", "you
don't control", "your opponents control", "each opponent controls") and "other", over a wider noun —
type words plural or singular, "permanent(s)", "non-" plus a type or subtype, and a list of
alternatives joined by commas and "and" ("artifacts, creatures, and enchantments" is any of the
three). Every word has to classify, read live off `characteristicsOf`, so a colour, a size, "with
flying" or "attacking" refuses the line rather than widening it. The board is read once, before
anything moves, as the wrath does; destroy honours "can't be regenerated".

**Overload, by the rewrite.** `spellScriptFor` holds an "Overload {cost}" line back, reads the
resolution as printed, then reads it again with "target" replaced by "each". If that reading comes
back **with no targets** it is `overload.onResolve`, the field the hand-written Mizzium Mortars
already uses, and the line is read; otherwise it is reported unread and the spell plays at its
printed cost. The first version lost the held line on the paths that never read it — the modal
shape and an unread resolution — and the measured line total fell by 15 for it; every path now
reports it.

**And Cyclonic Rift's target.** "Target nonland permanent you don't control" is the same set as
"… an opponent controls", which the target reader already had; it now reads both, as `boardScope`
always has.

**Tests.** 7 engine tests on corpus rows (Vandalblast, Cyclonic Rift, Armageddon, Evacuation,
Akroma's Vengeance, Planar Cleansing) with a second custom deck giving the opponent artifacts and
creatures: every row reads, overloads included; overloaded Vandalblast destroys both of theirs and
not yours; overloaded Rift returns every nonland permanent they control and leaves their land and
your creature; the printed Rift offers only their nonland permanents; Akroma's Vengeance takes every
listed type on both sides and spares lands, and Planar Cleansing spares lands; Armageddon takes
every land; Evacuation returns every creature to its owner's hand and leaves the Equipment; a colour
in the scope stays unread. The controller clause ignored, "non-" read as its opposite, and the
overload rewrite removed were each put in by hand and failed.

    engine tests: 4,249, all passing; web 264, realtime 60, api 326

## D601 — Damage to every creature of a kind, spells that cost less, and the D600 gaps

The unread dump after D600 ranked "~ deals N damage to each …" first among the one-short shapes. The
reason was narrow: `sweepDestination`, the reader for where a damage sweep lands, matched only "each
creature [with/without K] [and each player]". D600 had just written `massScope`, which reads a
scope's type words, controller clause and "non-". So the first half of this increment connects the
two.

**Damage over a scope.** When the fixed shape fails, `sweepDestination` now reads "each <scope>
[and each player | and each opponent]" through `massScope`. That reads "each creature your opponents
control" (Blazing Volley, Cosmotronic Wave), "each nonartifact creature" (Whipflare), "each non-Pirate
creature" (Fiery Cannonade), and overloaded Electrickery. Electrickery's rewrite reads "each creature
you don't control", which D600 had to leave unread. "And each opponent" skips the caster. A scope must
name a creature or a planeswalker: "each artifact your opponents control" would read as a scope and
deal damage to nothing (CR 120.3), so it is refused.

**Spells that cost less.** `CardScript.selfCostChange` had one user, Hagra Mauling, written by hand
(D578). It now has a reader for three shapes:
- "This spell costs {N} less to cast if <condition>": the condition is `interveningConditionFor`'s.
- "… for each <count>": the count is `forEachCount`'s.
- "{X} less …, where X is the number of <count>".

A new optional `per` field multiplies the rate by the count. Both the condition and the count run
against a context whose controller is the caster and whose source is the card being cast.
`costChangeFor` now takes the card's id, so the offer in `legalActions` and the payment in
`castSpell` see the same number.

Four shapes are refused:
- "If it targets …": this engine prices a spell before its targets are chosen.
- A phrase naming the card itself.
- A coloured discount: only generic mana moves.
- "More": dropping a cost increase would make a card better than printed.

**The count learned two things.** First, the party (CR 700.8): one each of Cleric, Rogue, Warrior
and Wizard, where a creature with two of those types fills one slot. That makes it a matching. It
is computed over the sixteen sets of filled roles, so the cost is linear in the number of creatures.
Second, any `massScope` scope, as a last row after every existing one, so a phrase that already
read keeps its reading. "Creature on the battlefield" (Blasphemous Act) and "creature your opponents
control" (Primeval Protector) now count, and so does every "for each" and "where X is" elsewhere in
the compiler. That widened three readings that tests had pinned as refusals:
- Idolized's "nonland permanents you control".
- "Each Bird on the battlefield", which the D520 comment said the vocabulary "could be taught".
- Ral, Caller of Storms's −7.

Each test now uses a count that still has no reader (colours among permanents). Ral's test expects
the +1 and the −7, with the divided −2 still refused. Mizzium Mortars now compiles whole too. The
keyword-without-builder test moves to Angel of Sanctions (Embalm), and the hand-written Mortars gains
the `removesACreature` hint the compiled reading carries, which is what
compiled-vs-written flagged.

**Sweep 46801 threw, and the bot was why.** The game threw at seed 46821 with "that card is not in
your hand". The bot had cast Glamerdye from its graveyard with the land to discard but without
`retrace: true`, because the bot's cast action carries every alternative-cast flag by hand and
retrace (D599) was missing from the list. The line is added. Two tests now pin it:
- The bot, with its land drop spent, retraces Flame Jab and says so.
- A source check: every field that `LegalPlay` and `AutoCastAction` both declare must appear as
  `play.<field>` in `bot.ts`. Thirteen flags have needed that line one by one, and the fourteenth
  will fail this test rather than a sweep.

**The D600 break run: 10 faults, 5 caught.** Four of the five misses are pinned:
- "You control" ignored: Evacuation's row with the clause returns only your creature.
- "Other" ignored: a creature whose enters trigger returns all other nonland permanents stays on the battlefield.
- Exile read as destroy: "Exile all artifacts" puts them in exile.
- Untap read as tap: "Untap all lands you control" untaps them.

The fifth, the overload guard against a rewritten reading that still has targets, is **vacuous**.
The rewrite replaces every "target" with "each", so no reading can still come back with targets. The
guard stays as a check that costs nothing.

**Tests.** 18 new engine tests:
- 6 on damage sweeps, using corpus rows plus one custom row for "and each opponent".
- 6 on cost reductions: Bone Picker, Ghoultree, Blasphemous Act (cast for {4}{R} with four creatures
  out, and resolved), Deadly Alliance with three party shapes, and three refusals.
- 2 on the bot's retrace.
- 4 pinning the D600 break-run gaps.
- 3 existing tests updated for the wider reading.

Every new reader was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The "and each opponent" seat filter.
- The creature guard on a damage scope.
- The `massScope` fallback in `sweepDestination` and in the count.
- The bot's retrace line, caught by both tests.
- `per` ignored.
- `when` ignored.
- Party as a headcount.

    engine tests: 4,267, all passing; web 264, realtime 60, api 326

## D602 — Combat-damage triggers with a subject, an aimed edict, a tutor to the top, and attacking counts

The unread dump ranked "Whenever … deals combat damage to a player" third among the one-short
families. What blocked its readable part was the subject, not the effect: "whenever a **Ninja** you
control", "an **artifact creature** you control", "a creature you control **with deathtouch**",
"whenever a **Goblin** deals combat damage". `combat-damage` had `who` and `of` and no filter at
all.

**The event carries the creature, and the board filters ask it.** `raise` now enriches a
`combat-damage` event with the live facts of the creature that hit: types, subtypes, keywords, power,
toughness and counters. That is what D478/D479 gave `etb` and `dies`. The matcher asks the same
filters of it (`ofSubtypes`, `withKeyword`, `withCounter`, the size bounds) and adds
`what: 'artifact'`.

A new prologue row reads three subject shapes, with the filter from `boardFilter`:
- A tribe ("Ninja", "Dinosaur creature").
- "Artifact creature".
- "Creature" with a filter.

"You control" is `of: 'you'`. Without it, the trigger is about anybody's creature, which is
Cabal Slaver's "a Goblin". A lower-case word it cannot filter on ("modified", "nontoken", a colour)
refuses the line. "It" in the effect is the creature that hit: Rakish Heir's counter goes on the
Vampire that connected, as printed.

**"That player sacrifices a creature."** "Target player/opponent sacrifices a creature" now reads.
It is the each-player edict aimed at one player, who chooses from their own creatures. Through
`referentEffect`'s "that player" swap, it is also Cabal Executioner's and Demon of Loathing's line on
the hit player.

**A tutor to the top.** "…, reveal it, then shuffle and put that card on top" covers the Harbingers,
the Forerunners and Campus Guide. Two compile tests refused it on the argument that the search's own
shuffle would undo it. It does not: `answerDecision` shuffles as the search is answered and the
effect runs after, so the card lands on top. Both refusal rows are removed with a note. `clausesOf`
cut the line at its ", then ", so the phrase is now held together past the split.

**Attacking counts.** "for each [other] attacking <creature | Tribe>" (Goblin Piledriver, Aurochs,
Dire Fleet Captain, Rampaging Classmate) is read off the live attack declaration. "Other" is the
creature whose ability it is.

**The D601 break run: 8 runnable faults, 4 caught. All 4 misses are pinned here:**
- A {2}-per rate and a "where X is" discount, on custom rows.
- The guard that keeps a cost phrase from naming the card itself ("for each +1/+1 counter on it",
  which would read with the guard removed).
- Party counting noncreatures (a Kindred Wizard artifact fills no slot).

Two of my D601 faults did not typecheck, so they tested nothing; the harness reports 6 of 10. Both
were rewritten type-safely (the "and each opponent" seat rule, and the players tail skipped), and the
D601 test failed on each.

**Tests.** 10 new engine tests on corpus rows, plus custom Vampire, Goblin and Elf rows:
- Rakish Heir: the Vampire gets the counter, the Heir and a Bear do not.
- Curious Altisaur draws for a Dinosaur only.
- Research Thief draws for an artifact creature only.
- White Widow: only a creature with deathtouch gets the counter.
- Cabal Slaver: an opponent's Goblin makes them discard, a Bear does not.
- Cabal Executioner: the player hit sacrifices their own creature.
- Elvish Harbinger: only the Elf is offered, and it ends on top.
- Goblin Piledriver is a 5/2 attacking beside two Goblins and a Bear.
- A subject word it cannot filter on stays unread.

Also 2 new D601 pins, and 2 compile refusal rows removed.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The filters not asked of `combat-damage`.
- The artifact test.
- "Anybody's" read as yours.
- The edict asking its controller.
- The tutor leaving the card where it was.
- "Other" ignored.
- The tribe ignored.

    engine tests: 4,277, all passing; web 264, realtime 60, api 326

## D603 — Counters a card names for itself, damage to each player, and the D602 gaps

Ranked by the unread dump, the largest one-short family is the step trigger, "At the beginning of
…" (785 cards), and its largest single shape was the Thallids: "At the beginning of your upkeep,
put a spore counter on ~". Fourteen cards print exactly that, and every one already read its other
line, "Remove three spore counters from ~: Create a 1/1 green Saproling".

**Any counter whose meaning is another line of the card.** "Put a/N <kind> counter(s) on ~ | it"
now reads for any lower-case kind, keyed by the printed word, as every counter here is. That is
177 lines across 60 kinds:
- charge (Aether Vial, the Mana Batteries)
- spore
- quest (the Ascensions)
- oil
- storage (the storage lands)
- verse, ki, page, growth, and a tail of single-card kinds

Two groups are refused:
- **`RULES_COUNTERS`**, the kinds the rules or the engine give a meaning of their own: loyalty,
  defense, lore (a Saga chapter), time and fade (suspend, vanishing, fading), stun, shield,
  finality, age (cumulative upkeep), level, and the player counters. Placing one with no other
  machinery would be a wrong reading.
- **The keyword counters** (CR 122.1b), any kind that is a keyword name. The first measurement read
  Spontaneous Flight's "Put a flying counter on it" as a counter called "flying", which grants
  nothing here. Fully Grown, Wing It and Sudden Spinnerets were the same. All four are unread again.

**Damage to each player.** `damageEffect` read "each opponent" and not "each player". It now reads
every seat still in the game, its controller included (Rumbling Slum).

**The D602 break run: 8 faults, 5 caught. All 3 misses are resolved here:**
- **"A <Tribe> creature you control"** losing its "creature" word: pinned by a reading test.
- **The edict offering any permanent**: Cabal Executioner's hit player now holds an artifact that
  sorts before their Bears. The test helper takes the first choice, so the artifact would be the
  one sacrificed.
- **The guard that refused "a creature deals combat damage" with nobody's control named.** This
  was the fault that changed nothing because the guard was wrong: that sentence is anybody's
  creature, exactly as Cabal Slaver's Goblin is. The guard is removed, and a reading test pins the
  sentence.

**Tests.** 6 new engine tests:
- Thallid reads whole.
- A spore counter at each of your upkeeps and none at the opponent's, and three of them remove
  for a Saproling.
- Rumbling Slum takes a life from each player at your upkeep, you included.
- Lore, stun, time and flying counters are refused.
- 2 D602 pins.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The kind ignored (every counter a +1/+1).
- The rules kinds allowed.
- The keyword kinds allowed.
- The reader removed.
- "Each player" leaving out its controller.
- The tribe's "creature" word dropped.
- The edict's creature filter.

## D604 — Attachment riders, counted card types, and the D603 gaps

After the step triggers, the next one-short families in the dump are the attachments: 177 cards stop
at "Enchanted creature gets …" or "Equipped creature gets …". The common reason is a rider after the
size that `attachmentBonus` had no row for:
- "and can't block" (Copper Carapace, Cast into Darkness)
- "and attacks each combat if able" (Furor of the Bitten, Tormentor's Trident)
- "and can't be blocked"
- "and loses flying" (Colossus Hammer)
- "and loses all abilities" (Mystic Subdual)
- "and is every creature type" (Amorphous Axe)
- "and has mountainwalk" (Cave Sense)
- "and doesn't untap during its controller's untap step" (Leaden Fists)

**One rider reader.** `attachmentRider` maps each of those onto the `PumpOptions` field the layer
system already applies (`cantBlock`, `mustAttack`, `cantBeBlocked`, `removeKeywords`,
`losesAllAbilities`, `allCreatureTypes`, `doesntUntap`, `landwalk`). It reads the rider alone ("Enchanted
creature can't block") and after a size. The size form is tried only when the existing keyword
reading would fail, so every line that read before reads the same. `harmful` follows the rider:
a creature that cannot block, must attack, will not untap or loses its abilities is one the
computer opponent aims the Aura at somebody else's creature for.

**Counted card types.** `StaticCountable` gains `permanents-of-type`:
- "for each enchantment you control" (Helm of the Gods, Tempest Technique)
- "… artifact and/or enchantment you control" (All That Glitters)
- "… land on the battlefield"

It reads the printed type line, which is metalcraft's compromise and the reason `artifacts-you-control`
gave. The first version counted creatures too, and two D523 tests refused it. They were right: D523
refuses a creature count on a static size because whether a permanent is a creature *now* is
exactly what a printed line cannot say (a crewed Vehicle, an animated land). "Creature" is taken out,
and a test pins that the creature count stays refused.

**The D603 break run: 6 faults, 3 caught. All 3 misses are pinned:**
- "It" read as the source: a Thallid row that marks each other creature you control as it enters
  puts the counters on the Bears, not on itself.
- The amount read as one: the same row puts two charge counters.
- "A creature" with nobody named read as yours: a seat-1 watcher gains life when seat 0's Bears
  connect.

**Tests.** 8 new engine tests:
- 4 on riders: every row reads; each rider lands on its creature with the size; a bare creature has
  none of them; "loses all abilities" takes the printed flying, and an unread rider stays unread.
- 1 on counted types: an enchantment of yours, an artifact and an enchantment, the opponent's
  enchantment not counted, and the creature count refused.
- 3 D603 pins.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The size dropped from a rider line.
- "Can't block" read as "can't attack".
- "Loses" read as "has".
- Landwalk lower-cased.
- "Loses all abilities" dropped.
- The count read over everybody's board.
- A list of types read as its first type.
- The three D603 faults.

    engine tests: 4,289, all passing; web 264, realtime 60, api 326

## D605 — A static with any condition it can answer, and the D604 gaps

The unread dump holds 603 one-short cards with "as long as" on the line that stops them. Until now
three readers covered that phrase, each for one condition:
- metalcraft: "three or more artifacts"
- threshold: "seven or more cards in your graveyard"
- monstrous / a +1/+1 counter on it

Most of what remains needs no new effect, only a condition:
- delirium (23)
- "~ is untapped" (13)
- "you control N or more artifacts" (12) and "an artifact" (11)
- "it's attacking" (12)
- "~ is equipped" (11)
- hellbent (8)
- "you control a Plains/Island/Swamp/Mountain/Forest/Gate" (~20)
- "~ is enchanted" (6)
- "it's not your turn" (5)
- "you have N or more life"

**The conditions are data.** `ContinuousEffect.while` gains eight kinds, each answered by
`conditionMet` without reading any permanent's live characteristics. That is the constraint every
condition here lives under: `conditionMet` runs inside `characteristicsOf`. The new kinds read:
- a zone's printed cards: `graveyard-card-types`, delirium's count of *types* (CR 207.2c);
- the source instance: `source-tapped`, and `source-auras` beside the existing `source-equipment`;
- the combat record: `source-attacking`;
- a hand's size: `controller-hand`, with at-least and at-most;
- a life total: `controller-life`;
- whose turn it is: `turn`;
- a printed subtype on your battlefield: `controller-subtype`, metalcraft's compromise.

`controller-artifacts` takes any number.

**One reader for both word orders.** "As long as <condition>, ~ <predicate>" and "~ <predicate> as
long as <condition>" now read through `staticCondition`, with the predicate read by threshold's own
`thresholdEffect` (a pump, keywords, can't block, a colour, protection from a colour, a quoted
ability). The branch sits after the three specific readers, so every card they read keeps its
reading. A condition `staticCondition` does not know refuses the line rather than applying the
effect always.

**Three refusal tests that the reader has outgrown, rewritten as readings:**
- "Nearly Metalcraft … as long as you control two or more artifacts." This was refused because the
  only reader was metalcraft's, so a two could only have been misread as three. It now reads as two.
- "Narrow Champion has protection from red as long as …" was refused as coverage with no card
  behind it (D57). Threshold's grammar has read "protection from <colour>" since D513, so it now
  reads as exactly that.
- D495's "As long as you control a Forest, Aesthir Glider can't block." was a refusal row; it reads
  now, and the row is removed with a note.

**The D604 break run: 6 faults, 4 caught. Both misses are pinned:**
- A rider printed alone: "Equipped creature can't block." reads.
- The rider's harmful flag ignored: an Aura of "+1/+1 and can't block" is removal
  (`removesACreature`), and one of "+1/+1 and can't be blocked" is not.

**Tests.** 8 new engine tests, all with corpus rows except a custom hellbent row:
- Every row reads.
- Kird Ape is 2/3 with a Forest and 1/1 without.
- Castle Raptors is 3/5 untapped and 3/3 tapped.
- Backwoods Survivalists stays 4/3 with four cards of three types in the graveyard and becomes a
  5/4 with trample at four types.
- Mesa Lynx is 2/3 on the opponent's turn only.
- Hellbent applies only with an empty hand.
- A condition it cannot answer stays unread.
- One D604 pin.

Also 2 compile tests rewritten and 1 refusal row removed.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- Delirium counting cards instead of types. The first version of the test missed this, because its
  three-type graveyard was also three cards; it now holds four cards of three types.
- Tapped inverted.
- Whose turn inverted.
- Hellbent's at-most ignored.
- The subtype ignored.
- The lead word order removed.
- Both D604 misses.

## D606 — The duration printed first, three more spell descriptors, and the D605 gaps

Two small families, each a reading the engine could already execute:

**"Until end of turn, <clause>."** Ninety-nine legal lines put the duration first: "Until end of
turn, target creature gets +1/+0 and gains indestructible" (Armor of Shadows). Every pump and grant
reader already read "<clause> until end of turn". `readEffect` now rewrites the leading form into
the trailing one and reads that, so a clause the trailing form does not read stays unread. Most of
the 99 carry a quoted grant or a base-size change behind the duration, which is other readers'
work; the plain ones finish.

**Three spell descriptors on the cast trigger:**
- **historic**: artifact, legendary or Saga (CR 700.6). D435 refused it as "not one field", and it
  now is one. The cast event carries the spell's supertypes, so "legendary" can be asked.
- **colorless**: no colours (CR 105.2c), asked of the event's colours, so a face-down spell counts.
- **"an instant, sorcery, or Wizard spell"**: any of a list of card types and subtypes (Rockslide
  Sorcerer, Umara Mystic, Master of Winds, Windrider Wizard). The cast prologue's descriptor could
  not contain a comma. It now accepts one in exactly the printed list shape, "x, y, or z", so a
  comma that ends the prologue is never taken into the descriptor.

The refusal row for "historic" is removed with a note. "A legendary spell" stays refused: no field
asks for a supertype alone.

**The D605 break run: 7 faults, 3 caught. All 4 misses are pinned here:**
- "It's attacking" true while any creature attacks: a Raider is 2/2 while only the Bears attack and
  4/2 when it does.
- "Is enchanted" counting Equipment: a Paladin wearing a Bonesplitter has only the Bonesplitter's
  +2/+0, and gets its own +1/+1 when an Aura goes on.
- "N or more life" read as more than N: a Steward is 2/2 at exactly 20 life and 1/1 at 19.
- The general reader dropping a quoted grant: a creature that has "{T}: You gain 1 life" while
  untapped compiles with the grant and its index.

**Tests.** 7 new engine tests:
- 5 for D606: every row reads; historic fires for an artifact and a legendary spell and not a
  Bears; colorless fires for an artifact only; the mixed list fires for an instant and a Wizard and
  not a Bears; Armor of Shadows makes a 3/2 indestructible that is 2/2 again next turn.
- 3 D605 pins.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- Legendary ignored.
- Colorless ignored.
- The mixed list's subtypes ignored.
- The leading-duration rewrite removed.
- The four D605 faults.

## D607 — "If you cast it", every static condition on a trigger, and the D606 gaps

The intervening "if" on a trigger had its own vocabulary (D563, D564), separate from the one D605
built for statics. The two most-printed conditions that neither had were about **how a permanent
arrived**: "if you cast it" (15 one-short lines) and "if you cast it from your hand" (12). The engine
did not remember that at all.

**How a permanent arrived.** Every spell's stack object now records the zone it was cast from
(`StackObject.castFrom`). As a permanent spell resolves, `GameState.castPermanents` records it with
that zone and the object's `objectSeq`. "If you cast it [from your hand]" asks whether there is a
record whose sequence number is the permanent's current one. Any later zone change bumps the
sequence, so a creature that is blinked, or bounced and put back by other means, reads as never
cast (CR 400.7), and nothing has to clear the record.

The obvious alternative was a marker counter, which is how kicked and evoked are recorded. It is
wrong here, because every cast permanent would then carry a counter: proliferate would find it,
and so would "a creature with a counter on it".

**Every static condition, on a trigger.** `interveningConditionFor` keeps its own rows first, since
they read the board live. When none of them reads a condition, it now falls back to D605's
`staticCondition` and answers it with the same `conditionMet` a static uses, through a new export,
`conditionHolds`. That brings "if ~ is untapped", "if you have no cards in hand", delirium,
"if you control a Plains" and "if you have 30 or more life" to triggers at no new cost.

**The D606 break run: 5 faults, 4 caught.** The miss was a guard of mine that refused a two-type
list such as "an artifact or enchantment spell", on the belief that the rows above it covered such
lists. Only "instant or sorcery" is covered, so the guard was turning away a correct reading. It is
removed, and a test shows "an artifact or enchantment spell" fires on Bonesplitter and not on a
Bears. D563's "how the card was cast" refusal row is removed with a note.

**Tests.** 6 new engine tests:
- Every row reads.
- Cast from hand: both conditions hold.
- Put onto the battlefield without being cast: no effect. A control row with no condition shows
  the same move does announce an arrival.
- Cast, then bounced and put back by other means: no effect a second time.
- Hellbent on a trigger.
- The D606 pin.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The sequence number ignored.
- The cast zone always "graveyard".
- The record never written.
- The static fallback removed.

    engine tests: 4,308, all passing; web 264, realtime 60, api 326

### Measurements

    cards fully read 9,675 of 31,292 (was 9,660); lines read 27,500 of 58,524 (47.0%, was 27,472)

Most "if you cast it" cards still stop on their effect: a mass bounce with an exception, an extra
turn, a copy of a spell. The condition is no longer what stops them.

## D608 — Pump, then it fights or bites; and the D607 gaps

D542's bite-and-fight reader named the half it left: the **referent** forms. "Target creature you
control gets +1/+2 until end of turn. **It** fights target creature you don't control." The second
sentence's "it" is the first sentence's target, and it declares a target of its own. The composer
refuses two clauses with two target choices, and `referentEffect` supplies exactly one object.

**One shape, both targets.** `pumpThenBiteResolution` reads the line whole, before clause
composition: "Target creature you control gets +A/+B until end of turn. [Then] it fights | deals
damage equal to its power to <target>". It declares both targets once, in printed order, and the
effect pumps the first, then fights or bites with it, so the pump is in the numbers. That is the
whole point of these cards: Epic Confrontation's Bears win a fight they would otherwise trade in.

"Up to one" target may choose nothing, and then the pump still happens. The bitten target must be a
permanent, and for a fight a creature. "Then that creature …" and other spellings stay unread.

The cards finished include Ambuscade, Assert Perfection, Bridgeworks Battle, Clear Shot, Epic
Confrontation, Huatli's Final Strike and Rabid Gnaw. D542's refusal test is rewritten as the
reading, with "Then that creature fights …" still pinned as unread.

**The D607 break run: 4 faults, 2 caught.**
- **"From your hand" ignored**: pinned. A creature given retrace and cast from the graveyard
  triggers "if you cast it" and not "… from your hand".
- **The face-down cast's zone not recorded**: **vacuous**, and recorded as such. A face-down
  permanent has no abilities, so no enters trigger of its own can ask how it arrived, and the
  default zone makes the record identical either way.

**Tests.** 4 new engine tests:
- Both rows read whole, with two targets.
- Epic Confrontation's 3/4 Bears kill the opposing Bears and survive with 2 damage.
- Clear Shot kills a 3/3 with three damage, and the biter takes none.
- The D607 graveyard-cast pin.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The pump dropped.
- The fight read as a bite.
- The bite read as a fight.
- "From your hand" ignored.

    engine tests: 4,312, all passing; web 264, realtime 60, api 326

## D609 — A sacrifice cost of any permanent kind, and the D608 gaps

Ranking the one-short activated abilities turned up a pattern. Of the 362 lines with a sacrifice in
the cost, the bodies were mostly readable ("Draw a card", "You gain 3 life", "Add {C}"), and what
refused them was the **cost**. `AbilityCost.sacrifice` knew four kinds: a creature, another
creature, an artifact, and an artifact or creature. The cards print:
- a land (Cephalid Scout, Overgrown Estate, Ripchain Razorkin)
- an artifact or land (Akki Scrapchomper, Destructive Digger)
- a token (Hardened Tactician, Fountainport)
- a permanent (Claws of Gix)
- a nontoken permanent (Infernal Tribute)
- an enchantment
- another artifact (Chronomancer)
- another creature or artifact (Ahriman)
- a Forest (Dark Heart of the Wood)

**Nine more kinds.** The union gains each of those. `sacrificeOptions` answers every kind from the
live characteristics, and "another" in any kind excludes the source. A land subtype ("a Forest", "a
Desert", "a Gate") is a land narrowed by `sacrificeSubtypes`, the D578 mechanism. The cost parser
reads the phrases. Plain "an artifact" keeps its older row, and capitalised land types are added to
the typed-sacrifice branch that already caught "a Goblin" and "a Food".

**The table asks in the cost's own words.** `LegalPlay.sacrificeWords` is now set on every play
whose cost sacrifices something, and the web bar's `feedWords` prefers it, so a land cost says "tap
a land to sacrifice" rather than "tap a creature". The engine's refusals use the same words.

The bot is deliberately left where it was. Outside artifact costs it offers only creatures as
fodder, so it does not use a land, token or permanent sacrifice. That is a choice it would get
wrong by spending its lands, and a person at the table makes it instead.

Two compile refusal rows ("a land, which has no field", "a land type, which is not a creature or
an artifact") are removed with a note.

**The D608 break run: 4 faults, 1 caught. All 3 misses are pinned here:**
- The bite's damage source read as the spell: a deathtouch 1/1 pumped by Clear Shot kills a 6/6,
  which it can only do if the damage is the creature's.
- "Up to one" choosing nothing and skipping the pump: Assert Perfection with one target still makes
  the Bears 3/2.
- A fight aimed at a noncreature: "It fights target artifact" stays unread.

**Tests.** 6 new engine tests:
- 3 for D609: every row reads; each cost is offered exactly the permanents it names, and the play
  says "land"; the land is paid and the effect resolves, and a creature offered for a land cost is
  refused in the cost's words.
- 3 D608 pins.

Plus 2 web assertions on `feedWords` with the cost's words.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- "Another" keeping the source.
- Token read as nontoken.
- The land subtype ignored.
- "Artifact or land" dropping land.
- The three D608 faults.

## D610 — A cost that taps other permanents you control, and the D609 gaps

After D609, the most common cost component still refusing an activated ability was "Tap an untapped
creature you control" (26 one-short lines), with its relatives:
- "Tap an untapped Ally you control" (9)
- "Tap two untapped creatures you control" (9)
- "… three untapped creatures" (6)
- "… two untapped artifacts" (4)

None of them had a field.

**`AbilityCost.tapUntapped`: a count, a kind, and an optional creature type.** `tapCostPlan` chooses
which permanents to tap the way crew already does, because nothing at the table asks: weakest first,
the source last. A creature that may tap itself (Bramblesnap) does so only when nothing else will.
When the cost also prints {T} (cohort's "{T}, Tap an untapped Ally you control"), the source is never
one of the creatures tapped, because it is tapping itself already. `legalActions` does not offer the
ability without enough to tap, and `activate` taps them with the crew.

Summoning sickness does not stop a creature from being tapped this way: the {T} symbol is what asks
that (CR 302.6), and this cost is not the creature's own {T}.

**Refused on a mana ability.** Mana abilities are paid inside the mana planner, which knows nothing
of this cost, so "Tap an untapped creature you control: Add {G}" would be free mana. It stays unread.

D581's "tapping somebody else, which has no field" refusal row is removed with a note.

**The D609 break run: 6 faults, 3 caught. All 3 misses are pinned:**
- "A permanent" excluding its own source: the source is now in the offered list.
- "An enchantment" read as an artifact: the Bonesplitter beside the enchantment is not offered.
- "Another creature or artifact" read as a creature: the Bonesplitter is offered.

**Tests.** 4 new engine tests:
- Every row reads, and the mana form is refused.
- The weakest other creature is tapped first, then the source, then the ability is no longer offered.
- With {T} in the cost, the source alone is not enough.
- An Ally and not a Bears; two artifacts and not one.

The D609 test is extended for its three misses.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The source ranked first.
- The {T} exclusion removed.
- The subtype ignored.
- The count read as one.
- The permanents never tapped.
- The mana guard removed.
- The three D609 faults.

    engine tests: 4,319, all passing; web 264, realtime 60, api 326

## D611 — A spell that costs less for what it targets, and fodder that was also the mana

**"This spell costs {3} less to cast if it targets a tapped creature"** was 43 printed lines, 29 of
them the line keeping their card unfinished. D601 refused the whole family: the cost was computed
before the engine knew the targets. But the cast action carries its targets, and CR 601.2c (choose
targets) comes before 601.2f (determine the total cost). So the cost can be the chosen target's.

**`selfCostChange.targets`** is a predicate on one target. The phrase after "it targets" goes
through `targetSpecFrom`, the reader every "target …" phrase uses, and is asked with
`isLegalTarget`. Phrases that reader cannot say stay unread:
- "a creature that was dealt damage this turn"
- "an attacking or tapped creature"
- "a creature token"
- "a creature card with mana value 3 or less"
- "a spell or ability that targets …"

`costChangeFor` takes `aimedAt`:
- **At the cast** it is the chosen targets.
- **At the offer** it is every legal candidate, so the offer shows the cheaper cost when any
  candidate earns it.
- **When only the cheaper cast is affordable**, the play's candidates are narrowed to the ones that
  earn it, on the first spec that has any. Animist's Might's legendary creature is its first
  target, and its second target is left alone.
- **A client that aims elsewhere anyway** is refused with "cannot pay".
- **Alternative costs** are offered at the full price, and the payment may then come out cheaper.

### Sweep 47801, seed 47815: fodder that was also the mana

Thraxodemon ("{3}, {T}, Sacrifice another creature or artifact: Draw a card") was offered with a
Treasure as its fodder. The {3} was paid by cracking that same Treasure, so the sacrifice found no
card. This came from D609's wider sacrifice kinds.

`payFrom` now takes `exclude`, a hard exclusion where `avoid` is only a preference:
- `activate` excludes the source tapped by {T}, the creatures crew and "tap an untapped creature"
  tap, and the sacrifice.
- `castSpell` excludes an additional-cost sacrifice.

On the offer side:
- Fodder is offered only where the mana is there without it.
- An ability whose cost-tapped permanents are also its only mana is not offered.

**Tests.** 8 new engine tests:
- D611:
  - The rows read, and two phrases stay refused.
  - {3} less at a tapped creature, full price at an untapped one.
  - Off two lands, it is offered only at the tapped creature, and refused at another.
  - Only the spec that can earn it is narrowed.
- Sweep 47815:
  - The rows read.
  - A Treasure needed for the mana is not fodder, and is refused with "cannot pay" if sent.
  - Elves tapped for the cost do not also tap for mana.
  - The spell form of the same.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The narrowing removed.
- The cast passing no targets.
- Every spec narrowed.
- The narrowing applied even when the full cost is affordable.
- The offer asked of no candidates.
- Each of the five exclusions.

The D487 and D601 refusal rows that used "a tapped creature" now use "a creature that was dealt
damage this turn".

    engine tests: 4,327, all passing

## D612 — Descend, and the D611 break-run gap

The Lost Caverns of Ixalan cards print two descend forms. Neither read.

**1. "If you descended this turn."** This is a fact about the turn, so it is kept beside raid,
morbid and revolt as `GameState.descendedThisTurn`:
- It is written by `relocate` when a permanent **card** goes to its owner's graveyard from
  anywhere: milled, discarded, died, or a land sacrificed.
- It is keyed by the owner, since a graveyard is its owner's.
- A token is not a card and does not count. Neither does an instant or a sorcery.
- It is cleared with the other turn facts, and it is optional so older saves load.
- The condition reads "you descended this turn".

**2. "Descend 4 —" and "Descend 8 —".** These are ability words with a digit in them (CR 207.2c),
which the letters-only label pattern in `withoutAbilityWord` could never strip. The sentence after
the dash restates the whole condition, so the label comes off exactly as any other ability word
does. The condition "there are four or more **permanent** cards in your graveyard" is threshold's
`controller-graveyard` with `permanents: true`. That is counted by `isPermanentCard`, the printed
type before the dash, so a Kindred Instant is not one. Triggers with the same condition read
through D607's static-condition fallback.

**D611 break run: 6 faults, 5 caught.** The miss: "no targets given means any target qualifies".
An alternative cost is offered with no `aimedAt`, and would have taken the reduction. It is now
pinned by asking `costChangeFor` directly: no targets, empty targets, and a tapped creature.

**Still unread:**
- Akawalli's "an additional +2/+2"
- Molten Collapse's "If you descended this turn, you may choose both instead"
- the descend-8 activated and copy abilities

Two older refusal rows used descend as the example of something unread. They now use Akawalli's
descend-8 line and "if you scried this turn".

**Tests.** 4 new engine tests:
- Both rows read.
- A Grizzly Bears put into the graveyard is descending; a Lightning Bolt and a dying Pest are not.
- The fact is gone next turn.
- Descend 4 counts permanent cards, not cards: three Bears and two Bolts are not enough, and a
  Mountain makes four.

There is also the D611 pin. Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- Every card counted, not only permanent cards.
- Tokens counted.
- The automated reset removed.
- `permanents` ignored.
- Land dropped from the permanent types.

The tabletop-path reset in `engine.ts` is not exercised by these tests. It mirrors the four turn
facts beside it.

## D613 — A cost that exiles cards from your graveyard

"Exile a creature card from your graveyard" (25 lines), "Exile two cards" (10), "Exile a card" (6),
"Exile three cards" (5), and smaller rows that name a kind ("an instant or sorcery card", "an
artifact or creature card", "an Elf card", "two legendary cards"). About 60 unread ability lines,
and none of them had a field.

**`AbilityCost.exileFromGraveyard`** has a count, the printed words, and a `matches` test of the
printed type line, built by `graveyardKind`. That test accepts:
- nothing, meaning any card;
- card types and "legendary" joined by "or";
- one creature type.

"Historic", "with mana value X", "X cards", "any number" and "from a graveyard" stay unread.

**Who chooses the cards: the engine.** `graveyardCostPlan` uses `graveyardFodder`'s order: cards
with no second life go first. The source is never one of them, which covers "another creature
card". `legalActions` does not offer the ability without enough cards, and `activate` chooses them
before anything is spent and exiles them as the cost is paid.

**Refused on a mana ability.** The rule that limits a mana ability's costs refuses it already, and
the guard beside D610's makes that explicit.

**Tests.** 4 new engine tests:
- The rows read, and the mana and "historic" forms stay refused.
- A creature card is exiled and not the instant beside it; after that the ability is not offered.
- A count is that many cards of any kind.
- "An instant or sorcery card" takes either, and not a creature.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The kind ignored.
- The count read as one.
- The cards never exiled.
- The offer not gated.
- Only the first half of an "or" kind accepted. The test only used an instant at first; a sorcery
  case was added.

The mana-ability guard is the one fault no test can see, because the other refusal stands behind
it.

## D614 — A discard cost with a filter or at random, and the D612 break-run gaps

D580 read "Discard a card" and left its relatives unread on purpose, because the flag could not
carry them. Two of them now have fields:

- **"Discard a creature card"** (and "a land card", "an instant or sorcery card", "an Elf card")
  is `AbilityCost.discardKind`. It narrows the player's choice through D613's `graveyardKind`. The
  offer's `discardOptions`, and the check in `activate`, both list only matching cards. A kind
  that reader cannot say ("a nonland card") stays unread.
- **"Discard a card at random"** is `AbilityCost.discardAtRandom`. Nobody chooses, so nothing
  travels on the action, and a client that sends a card is refused. The card is picked by the
  game's own generator (`mulberry32` over the seed, the state version and `autoSeq`, as
  `bottomPile` does), so a replay of the action log discards the same card. It is offered to any
  hand with another card in it. It is refused on a mana ability, and refused beside a second
  discard in either order.

"Discard two cards" is still refused: a count needs more than one choice from the player, which
neither the table nor the bot asks for yet.

**The D612 break run: 5 faults, 2 caught.** The three misses:
- **Descend keyed by the controller, not the owner.** Now pinned: a Grizzly Bears of seat 0's,
  stolen by seat 1 and destroyed, descends seat 0.
- **A number-label rule wider than "Descend".** No real card changes under it: none of the 97
  corpus cards with "Word N —" compiles differently. It is now pinned with constructed lines:
  "Rampage 2 — Whenever …" and "Suspend 4 — … gets +1/+1 as long as …" stay unread, and "Descend 4
  — Whenever …" reads.
- **Subtypes included in the permanent-type test.** This is vacuous. No subtype on a non-permanent
  card is a permanent type word, so the two readings never differ. A Kindred Instant row is pinned
  anyway, to show that "Kindred" is not counted.

**Tests.** 4 new engine tests:
- Both rows read.
- A creature card only: the Bolt is not offered, and is refused if sent.
- At random: no choice travels, one card goes, a sent card is refused, and an empty hand is not
  offered.
- The random pick is the same on a replay.

Plus 2 D612 pins and 3 refusal rows. Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test
failed:
- The offer filter removed.
- The payment filter removed.
- The random offer gate removed.
- No card discarded.
- The random-beside-chosen guard removed. The row only listed one order at first; the reverse

## D615 — A cost that returns permanents to your hand

Two cost shapes:
- **"Return ~ to its owner's hand"** (12 lines: Attunement, Broken Fall, Gossamer Chains) is
  `returnSelf`. The source goes back as the cost is paid.
- **"Return a land you control to its owner's hand"** (13 lines: Meloku, Floodbringer, Oboro
  Breezecaller), plus "two/three lands", "a Forest", "two Islands", "an artifact" and "an Elf", is
  `returnToHand`. It has a count, a kind (land, artifact, creature or enchantment), and an optional
  basic land type or creature type.

**Who chooses: the engine, with `bouncePlan`.** It takes tapped permanents first, then the cheapest,
and never the source. Tapped first is the point of Quirion Ranger: a land tapped for mana and then
returned is legal (mana abilities come before costs are paid, CR 601.2g–h). So `activate` checks
there are enough before anything is spent, and **chooses after the mana is paid**, from the state
in which those lands are tapped.

"Tapped", "snow", "unblocked attacking" and "Elves" (an irregular plural) stay unread. So does the
cost on a mana ability.

**Tests.** 4 new engine tests:
- The rows read, and the mana form is refused.
- A Forest, the tapped one first, and not a Mountain; with only a Mountain it is not offered.
- Two lands: the Forest just tapped for its {G} goes back and an untapped Mountain stays.
- The card returns itself.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- Untapped first.
- The subtype ignored.
- The offer not gated.
- The choice made before the payment. The first version of the test did not check which lands went
  back; it now forces a {G} from the last land on the battlefield.
- The self-return dropped.
- The mana-ability guard removed.

## D616 — Cast triggers by turn, by zone and by kicker; the D613 break-run gaps

Probing every "Whenever you cast …" subject with a trivial effect showed which subjects themselves
were the gap:
- "a spell during an opponent's turn" (8 cards one line short)
- "your first spell during each opponent's turn" (8)
- "a spell from your graveyard" (3)
- "a spell from anywhere other than your hand" (3)
- "a kicked spell" (4)

The cast event now carries three more facts as it is raised: `activeSeat`, `castFrom` (the zone the
card was cast from, already on the stack object since D607) and `kicked`. The trigger asks for them
with `duringOpponentsTurn`, `fromZone: 'graveyard' | 'not-hand'` and `wasKicked`. "Your first spell
during each opponent's turn" is `onNth: 1` plus `duringOpponentsTurn`, because the per-caster tally
restarts every turn. A face-down cast sets the first two as well.

**Still refused, as rows:** "from a graveyard" (any), "during your turn", and "a kicked creature
spell". So are "your first instant or sorcery spell each turn", "a creature spell that has an
Adventure" and "a spell that targets a creature you control".

**The D613 break run: 5 faults, 0 caught.** D613's tests used only plain kinds, on a battlefield
source, with no card that has a second life. Five pins in their own describe:
- An ability activated from the graveyard ("Exile two other cards") does not count its own card.
- A flashback card goes after a plain one.

- "Another creature card" is one.
- "A legendary card" is a kind.

- Kicked and not unkicked.
