## D617 — Mana in your commander's colour identity; the D614 and D615 break-run gaps

**Command Tower, Arcane Signet and Commander's Sphere** print "{T}: Add one mana of any color in your
commander's color identity". Nearly every Commander deck runs at least one, and they were unread.

**Where the reader belongs.** Mana lines never reach the general line reader. `compile.ts` sends
them to `manaAbilitiesFromLine` in `fromCardData.ts`, and an unreadable mana line is unread outright
(D497). My first version went in `scripts.ts`, was never reached, and was taken back out. The
reader is now a `ManaLine.identity` flag beside `ANY_COLOUR`. `tapAbilities` gives each colour's
ability an `activateOnlyIf` that asks `commanderIdentity`.

**Colour identity, computed** (CR 903.4). Nothing in the engine held it before, and no `CardDef`
carries Scryfall's `color_identity`.
- `colourIdentity(def)` is the card's colours plus every mana symbol in its mana cost and rules
  text, on every face, with hybrid and Phyrexian symbols counting for each colour in them.
  Reminder text in parentheses is left out.
- `commanderIdentity(state, seat)` is the union over every commander that seat **owns**, wherever
  it is. It is empty without one, so the Tower makes nothing (CR 903.4f).

**`manaSources` now honours `activateOnlyIf`**, as the play list and `activate` already did. So
the auto-tapper never pays with a colour the identity forbids.

**D614 break run: 5 faults, 2 caught.** All three misses are pinned:
- The random pick always taking the first card. Twelve seeds must pick more than one card.
- An "or" kind reading only its first half. "An instant or sorcery card" must match a Sorcery.
- A random discard on a mana ability. "Discard a card at random: Add {R}." must stay unread; without
  the guard it reads.

**D615 break run: 5 faults, 1 caught.** All four misses are pinned:
- The source as its own fodder. An Elf returning "an Elf you control" is not offered alone.
- A creature kind read as land. The Llanowar Elves goes back, not the Forest.
- "Plains" read as nothing.
- Self-return written twice. The line stays unread.

**Tests.** 5 new D617 engine tests:
- The line reads.
- Identity counts the cost, the colours and the rules-text symbols, but not reminder text.
- Only the commander's colours, as a source and as plays, and nothing without a commander.
- An opponent's commander lends you nothing.
- A colour outside the identity is refused if activated.

Plus 2 D614 pins and 3 D615 pins. Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The `manaSources` check removed.
- Reminder text counted.
- The owner check removed. Nothing tested an opponent's commander at first; that test was added.
- The identity flag dropped.
- Symbols not read.

The D614 and D615 spec faults were all re-injected against the new pins and all fail.

    engine tests: 4,367, all passing

## D618 — Upkeeps on an opponent's turn and on the enchanted creature's controller's; Auras stay on stolen creatures

D434's step table counted "each opponent's upkeep" (31 lines), "each opponent's end step" (7) and
"the upkeep of enchanted creature's controller" (21, plus 9 for other permanent kinds). It held them
back because no card body could read then. The vocabulary has grown since, so they ship:
- `TriggerDef` `step` gains `of: 'opponent'`: the active player is an opponent of the watcher's
  controller.
- It also gains `of: 'enchanted-controller'`: the active player controls the permanent this Aura or
  Equipment is attached to now. That is answered in `fireTrigger` beside heroic and the attachment
  checks, because `triggerMatches` is not told the holder.
- New rows: each opponent's upkeep and end step, and the upkeep and end step of an enchanted or
  equipped creature, permanent, artifact, land or enchantment's controller.

"That player" already reads on a step event (the active seat is the actor).

### An engine bug found on the way: stealing a creature knocked its Auras off

`relocate` called `detachAllFrom` on every move, including battlefield to battlefield. So
`gainControl` of an enchanted creature left the Aura unattached on the battlefield. A change of
controller is not a zone change, and attachments stay (CR 303.4, 301.5). `relocate` now detaches
only when the permanent really leaves the battlefield. A soulbond pair still breaks on a change of
control (CR 702.95e).

**Break runs pinned here:**
- **D616: 4 faults, 3 caught.** The miss, "from your graveyard" read as "not from your hand", is
  pinned with a commander cast from the command zone: it fires "from anywhere other than your hand"
  and not "from your graveyard".
- **D617: 4 faults, 0 caught.** The test cards printed each colour twice, on `colors` and in a
  symbol, so "hybrid counts one colour" and "colors ignored" hid behind each other. There was also
  no face test and no trailing-text refusal. Four direct pins: a hybrid with empty `colors`, a
  colour indicator alone, a back face's {R}, and "…identity or of the chosen color" staying unread.
  All four faults re-injected now fail.

**Refusal rows updated.** Two compile tables now assert the four new mappings. "Each opponent's draw
step" and "combat on each opponent's turn" stay refused. The `customDeck` unread-line example moved
to "each of your postcombat main phases".

**Tests.** 3 new D618 engine tests:
- Both rows read.
- Each opponent's upkeep: their turn, not yours.
- The enchanted creature's controller, and the new one after a steal. The Aura is asserted still
  attached.

Plus 4 compile mapping rows, the D616 pin and the D617 pins. Each of the following was broken on
purpose and its test failed:
- Opponent read as anyone.
- The host-controller check removed.
- Attachments detached on a control change.
- The opponent end-step row widened.

    engine tests: 4,372, all passing

## D619 — The rest of the step prologues

D434's step table held back nine spellings for want of `of: 'opponent'` or for want of a card. D618
added the field, so they read now. Each is a step the engine has always raised (`raise` sends a step
event for every step, after its turn-based action):

| printed | trigger |
| --- | --- |
| combat on each opponent's turn (either apostrophe) | `begin-combat`, opponent |
| each opponent's draw step | `draw`, opponent |
| each combat | `begin-combat`, any |
| each (player's) draw step | `draw`, any |
| your second main phase / your postcombat main phase / each of your postcombat main phases | `postcombat-main`, you |
| your precombat main phase | `precombat-main`, you |
| each player's precombat / first main phase | `precombat-main`, any |

"Each of your postcombat main phases" is plural on cards that grant extra combats. This engine's
turn has one postcombat main, so the trigger fires on every one there is. "Your next upkeep" is
still refused: it is a delayed trigger that something else schedules.

**Refusal rows.**
- The "'your' is the half that is the rule" table pinned a gap rather than a rule, and it is gone;
  a note says why.
- The step table asserts the seven new mappings.
- The `customDeck` unread-line example is now "your next upkeep".

**Tests.** 3 new engine tests:
- The rows read.
- Over one round from your upkeep, each watcher fires as often as its words say: each combat 2,
  combat on an opponent's turn 1, each draw step 2, an opponent's draw step 1, your second main 1,
  each player's first main 2.
- The second main phase is after combat: no life at begin combat, +1 by the end step.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- The opponent's combat widened to any.
- Each draw narrowed to yours.
- The opponent's draw widened.
- The second main swapped for the first. The round count could not see this one, so the timing test
  was added for it.

## D620 — Statics over a group of creatures; Class, Case and Station lines kept off the card

**The largest family left in one reader.** On the rebuilt corpus, 746 legal lines open with a group
and "get" or "have", and 367 of them were the only thing a card had left. `staticFromLine` read
exactly one of them, the plain anthem "Creatures you control get +1/+1". Lords ("Other Goblin
creatures you control get +1/+1"), tribal keyword grants ("Elves you control have haste"), Slivers
("All Slivers have …") and quoted grants ("Creatures you control have '{T}: Add {G}.'") were all
unread.

**`groupStaticFromLine`** reads the subject into a static scope the engine already had:
- your creatures, and other creatures you control;
- your creatures of a type, optionally "other". The plural goes back to the type with
  `singularCreatureType`: Goblins, Elves, Wolves, Zombies.
- every creature;
- and one new scope: every creature **of a type, whoever controls it**, which is "All Slivers".
  This is `everyone` on the subtype scope; `applyStatics` passes it and `effectApplies` drops the
  controller check for it.

The predicate is the self-static grammar in the plural. It is singularised and read by
`thresholdPredicate`: a size, keywords, protection from a colour, "can't block". A quoted ability
goes through `grantedTriggerFrom` / `grantedAbilityFrom` with the grantor guard on, and the static
carries `grants` / `grantsAbilities`. A quoted mana ability becomes a mana source on every creature
that gets it.

Anything the predicate reader refuses still refuses the line: "until end of turn", a count, a
condition, a non-creature group ("Lands you control", "Artifacts you control") and a quality that is
not a creature type ("Nontoken creatures", "Artifact creatures").

### Three layouts read as the card's own, found by reviewing what newly read

Checking a sample of the 411 newly read lines turned up Barbarian Class: "Creatures you control have
haste" is its **level 3** line. The same is true of every Class line under a level header, for any
reader, and it predates this increment. Wizard Class's level-3 draw trigger had been firing from
level 1. Looking for the same shape found two more:
- **Class levels.** `compile.ts` now reports every line from the first "{cost}: Level N" on a Class
  as unread, the way D572 does for leveler bands. Nothing reads class levels yet.
- **Case cards.** "Solved —" is a state, not a condition the sentence restates, but
  `withoutAbilityWord` stripped it like any label, so Case of the Trampled Garden's attack trigger
  was on from the start. "Solved" and "To solve" are now in `NOT_AN_ABILITY_WORD`.
- **Spacecraft and Planets.** A "STATION 7+" band is a leveler band in another shape, and 58 legal
  Spacecraft had the "Flying" under one read as their own. `LEVEL_BAND_HEADER` now matches station
  bands too, so both the compiler and the printed-keyword reader stop there.

Together these took 79 wrongly counted lines back out of the measurement.

**Tests.** 8 new engine tests:
- The rows read.
- A lord pumps the others of its type you control, not itself and not an opponent's.
- "Elves you control" is the plural of Elf.
- "All Slivers" reaches an opponent's Sliver and not a Goblin.
- A quoted ability is granted to an opponent's Sliver.
- A quoted trigger is granted.
- A granted mana ability makes mana.
- Class, Case and Station lines are not the card's own.

Each of the following was broken on purpose and its test failed:
- `everyone` ignored.
- "Other" dropped.
- Irregular plurals unread.
- The Class guard removed.
- The Case labels removed. At first this fault passed: the test used a static line, which never
  goes through the label stripper. It now uses a trigger line.
- The station header removed.
- Quoted triggers dropped. At first this passed too, with no test for it; one was added.

The Sidewinder Sliver row in `compile.test.ts` asserted the tribal static unread and now asserts its
reading.

## D622 — conditions that compare you with an opponent

Catch-up cards such as Knight of the White Orchid check whether they are behind. Their intervening
"if" clauses were refused, so the whole trigger went unread:
- "if an opponent controls more lands than you"
- "if you control fewer creatures than an opponent" (and the lands/creatures pairs either way round)
- "if an opponent has more life than you"
- "if you have more life than an opponent"

`interveningConditionRows` now reads these. One live opponent who is ahead (or behind) is enough;
eliminated seats are skipped. Lands are counted by type line and creatures by current
characteristics, so an animated land counts as a creature while it is one.

**Still refused, on purpose:** the same comparison with artifacts, enchantments or cards in hand
(e.g. Mardu Hordechief's row in `compile.test.ts` now uses "more artifacts", which is not read).

**Tests.** 3 new engine tests:
- The rows read.
- Enters with more lands behind: the trigger fires (23 life); level on lands: it does not (20).
- Fewer creatures than an opponent (two Bears against the Pup), and less life (25 vs 20).

Three faults were injected by hand (`>=` in place of `>` for the counts, the kind fixed to land, and
`>=` for life). Each one was caught.

### The break harness was not running the tests

The rewritten `break-par.py` (after the container restart) built each working copy without the
repository's root `tsconfig.base.json`. Vitest then failed to load all 16 test files. That non-zero
exit was counted as "caught", so **the break results reported for D618, D619, D620 and D621 are void.**
The hand-injected faults recorded in each of those entries ran in the real tree and still stand.

What changed:
- The harness now copies the root tsconfig files.
- A non-zero exit counts as caught only when tests actually failed. Otherwise the fault is reported
  INVALID.
- A no-op fault is now reported UNCAUGHT, with 4,386 tests passing, as it should be.

The four runs have been queued again on their own snapshots, and their results will be recorded in
the next entry.

## D623 — "Activate only if <condition>", and ability words that restate it

`activationRestriction` read four clauses after "Activate only": "as a sorcery", "once each turn",
and the turn-timing clauses. Any "if" refused the line.

**Now read:** an `if <condition>` clause goes through `interveningConditionFor`, the reader a
trigger's "if" clause already uses. It becomes `AbilityDef.activateOnlyIf`, which three places
already enforce:
- `legalActions`, where the ability is offered (battlefield, graveyard and hand alike);
- `autoActions`, where an activation is applied;
- `manaSources`, for a mana ability (D617).

A second "if" clause, or a condition the reader refuses, still refuses the line.

**Ability words in front of an activated line.** The 28 legal lines below print a label and then
restate it in the trailing sentence:
- "Threshold — {R}, {T}, Sacrifice Barbarian Ring: … Activate only if there are seven or more cards
  in your graveyard."
- Metalcraft, Hellbent, Delirium, Morbid, Ferocious and Corrupted print the same shape.

`abilityFromLine` now takes the label off, but only when what is left reads **with** an
`activateOnlyIf`. Without that sentence the label is the only restriction, and the line stays
unread. The button keeps the printed text, label included.

**A guard came with it.** A labelled mana line ("Metalcraft — {T}: Add …") is not seen as one by
`compile.ts`'s `isManaAbilityLine`, so D497's rule is applied here instead: the result must be a real
mana ability (`produces`) or nothing. Urza's Workshop ("Add {C} for each Urza's land you control")
would otherwise have become a stack ability adding mana, so it stays unread. Mox Opal, Fanatic of
Rhonas and Whisperer of the Wilds are mana abilities that hold back until their condition is met.

**Still unread:**
- "creatures you control have total power 8 or greater" (9 lines).
- The Tainted lands' "Activate only if you control a Swamp" on a plain `{T}: Add` line. The mana
  reader refuses any second sentence it does not know.
- "Activate only if this land entered this turn or if you control a basic land" (5).

The two older refusal rows in `compile.test.ts` that used "seven or more cards in your graveyard"
now use the total-power condition.

**Tests.** 6 new engine tests:
- The rows read.
- An opponent with more lands: the ability is offered and gains life; with as many lands it is
  neither offered nor applied.
- A live count of your artifacts.
- The same restriction on an ability used from the graveyard.
- A Threshold label: off with the sentence, on (unread) without it; the button keeps the label.
- A Metalcraft mana ability is not a mana source with two artifacts, and is one with three. The
  Workshop shape is refused.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- The condition always true.
- The check removed from `legalActions`.
- The check removed from `autoActions`.
- The `activateOnlyIf` requirement removed from the label branch.
- The mana guard removed.
- The printed description dropped.

A regex pre-check I had first written was redundant with the `activateOnlyIf` requirement: each was
enough alone, so a fault in either went uncaught. It was removed.

## D624 — an Aura or Equipment ability aimed at its own creature, and effects that outlive an attachment

29 one-line-short legal Auras and Equipment print an activated ability whose object is their host:
- "{G}: Regenerate enchanted creature" (13: Carapace, Blessing of Leeches, Dark Privilege, …).
- "{1}: Enchanted creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn" (12: Armor of Faith, Briar Shield, …).
- "Equipped creature gains <keyword> until end of turn".

`selfEffect` read these sentences for "~" and "it" only. It now also reads "enchanted creature" and
"equipped creature", resolved through `attachedTo` on the source (D305's attachment). An Aura or
Equipment attached to nothing has no host, and the ability does nothing. The bot is not told a
negative pump on the host is a `selfShrink`, because the creature that changes is not the one paying.

### A rules bug found by a fault that did not fail

The first test, "an Equipment on nothing does nothing", did not fail when the host lookup was made to
fall back to any creature. The cause was not the test. **`removeEffectsFrom` took every effect the
Equipment was the source of**, and the state-based Equipment check called it whenever such an effect
existed. So the fallback's first strike was wiped at once.

The same removal runs on `equipTo`. Equip the Spurs to creature A, give A first strike with the Spurs'
ability, and move the Spurs to B: A lost first strike mid-turn. By CR 611.2a, the effect of a resolved
ability lasts its stated duration whatever happens to its source. An Aura's ability had the same
problem whenever the Aura left the battlefield.

What changed:
- `removeEffectsFrom` now removes only `permanent` effects, which is what an attachment's static
  bonus is.
- The Equipment check in `stateBasedActions` counts only those effects as "the bonus".

That second change has no test, on purpose. Left counting every effect, the check would see a
"bonus" it never removes and set `changed` on every pass. That costs passes (the loop stops at 32),
not correctness, so nothing a test can observe.

**Tests.** 5 new engine tests:
- The rows read.
- The Brace pumps its own creature and not an opponent's.
- The Shell's shield lands on the creature, not on the Aura.
- An Equipment on nothing does nothing; once equipped, it reaches the creature.
- Moving the Equipment leaves the first creature its first strike, and the second does not get it.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- The pump aimed at the source.
- Regeneration on the source.
- The keyword branch refused.
- `removeEffectsFrom` back to removing everything.
- An unattached host falling back to any creature.

    engine tests: 4,404, all passing

**D619's miss** dropped the curly apostrophe from "each opponent['’]s turn". That fault is

## D625 — a power or toughness bound on a target

`targetSpecFrom` knew "with power N or greater" as six exact strings: N of 4–6, "or greater" only,
written for Selesnya Charm and Hidden Dragonslayer. Every other number, every "or less" and every
toughness bound left the line unread. Examples:
- Cruel Cut and Defeat: "Destroy target creature with power 2 or less".
- Gallant Strike: "… with toughness 4 or greater".
- Goblin Tunneler and 10 other tappers: "Target creature with power 2 or less can't be blocked this
  turn".

The bound is now peeled off the end of the phrase, the way D492 peels a mana-value bound, and the
rest is read as before:
- The controller clause is printed on either side of it ("target creature an opponent controls with
  power 3 or less" / "… with power 3 or less an opponent controls"), so a clause after the bound is
  moved back onto the inner phrase.
- The bound is read live from `characteristicsOf`, so a pump in response takes a creature out of
  reach. That is the re-check CR 608.2b makes on resolution.
- It applies to creatures only, which is every printing.
- "With power or toughness N or less" is an or across two bounds, and stays unread.

The six exact cases were unreachable once the peel ran first, so they are gone rather than left as a
second reading of the same phrase.

### A D624 reading that did nothing

The list of newly read lines showed four D624 cards that read but could not work: Briar Shield,
Carapace, Stamina and Thrull Retainer, as in "Sacrifice Carapace: Regenerate enchanted creature".
The cost puts the Aura in the graveyard, `relocate` clears its `attachedTo`, and the ability then

line whose cost sacrifices, exiles or returns the source, and whose effect names "enchanted creature"
or "equipped creature", is now refused.

## D626 — graveyard returns with a mana-value bound, and a card returning itself to the battlefield

The largest family left in the dump has 476 unread lines naming "from your graveyard to the
battlefield", and on 285 cards it is the last unread line. The plain target form ("Return target
creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield") has read since D527. What was left, in two
pieces:

**1. A mana-value bound in front of the zone.** "Return target creature card with mana value 3 or
less from your graveyard to the battlefield" (about 20 legal lines). Two things stood in the way:
- Both graveyard readers, to hand and to the battlefield, required "card from" to be adjacent, so
  the bound never matched.
- They added "in your graveyard" **after** the phrase, while `targetSpecFrom` peels a mana-value
  clause only off the end (D492).

Now the regexes allow the bound, and `graveyardPhrase` puts the zone before it. The bound itself is
D492's, read off the printed mana cost.

**2. A card returning itself to the battlefield as an activated ability.** "{1}{B}: Return Bone
Dragon from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped", Advanced Stitchwing, and Necrosavant (upkeep
only, D509's timing). `graveyardSelfReturn` read only "to your hand"; it now reads the battlefield as
well, tapped or not, under your control. It does nothing if the card has left the graveyard by the
time the ability resolves (CR 400.7). The `fromGraveyard` cost marker that `graveyardSelfReturn`
already produced puts the button on the card in the graveyard and not on a copy on the battlefield.

**Still unread:**
- "With mana value X or less".
- "With total mana value".
- Returns triggered from the graveyard ("At the beginning of your upkeep, return ~ from your
  graveyard to the battlefield"), which need graveyard-active triggers.
- "With a finality counter on it" and "attached to that creature" riders, still refused per D527.

**Tests.** 4 new engine tests:
- To the battlefield: mana value 2 or less takes the Swiftspear and not the Hill Giant, and only
  from your graveyard.
- To your hand with "3 or greater".
- The Stitchwing is offered from the graveyard, not from the battlefield, and comes back tapped.
- Exiled in response, it stays in exile.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- The bound dropped while the zone was moved.
- "Tapped" ignored.
- The graveyard check on resolution removed.

## D627 — "target creature without <keyword>", and the untap symbol {Q}

**Without a keyword.** `parsedTargetPhrase` read "target creature with flying" and refused
"without". The pattern now takes either word, and `permanentFilter` gained `withoutKeyword`. It is
read live as `keyword` is, so a creature granted flying in response is out of reach. Typical
printings:
- "Tap target creature without flying" (Cephalid Retainer, Dromoka Dunecaster).
- "Target creature without flying can't block this turn".

38 legal lines name it, and 26 of them are the last unread line on their card.

**The untap symbol `{Q}`** (CR 107.6). 18 lines print it, 15 of them one line short: Hateflayer,
Farmstead Gleaner, Duergar Mine-Captain. `AbilityCost.untap` is checked in both places a cost is
checked:
- `legalActions` offers the ability only while the permanent is tapped.
- `autoActions` refuses it otherwise, and untaps the permanent as the cost is paid.

On a creature it needs the creature to have been under your control since the turn began, the
same rule as `{T}` (CR 302.6).

Two shapes stay unread on purpose:
- **A `{Q}` mana ability.** The mana planner pays `{T}` and nothing else, so read anyway it would
  be mana from a tapped land for free.
- **`{T}` together with `{Q}`.** No printing has both.

**Tests.** 9 new engine tests:
- Without flying: the Hill Giant and not the Shivan Dragon, and granted flying excludes.
- The same in a disjunction ("artifact or creature without flying").
- "With flying" is unchanged.
- The D625 pin: a power bound on a non-creature target is unread.
- `{Q}` reads as `{ untap: true }`.
- Untapped, it is neither offered nor allowed.
- Tapped, it is offered, untaps as the cost, resolves, and is not offered again.
- On a creature that arrived this turn it is refused, as summoning sickness.
- A `{Q}` mana ability and `{T}` with `{Q}` stay unread.

- "Without" read as "with".
- Each of the two filter spreads dropped. The disjunction one was uncaught until its own test was

- The tapped check removed from the offer path.
- The summoning-sickness check removed from the offer path.
- The "not tapped" refusal removed from the activation path.
- The untap on payment removed.
- `{T}` with `{Q}` allowed.
- A `{Q}` mana ability allowed.

The D625 miss ("bound applied to any kind") is pinned here and checked against its fault.

## D628 — a keyword for the whole team, and graveyard hate

**A keyword with no size.** `massPumpSubject`'s reader (D541) read "Creatures you control get +1/+1
and gain trample until end of turn", but not the same grant without a size. Examples it missed:
- "Creatures you control gain flying until end of turn" (Frostwind Invoker, Nephalia Moondrakes).
- "Other creatures you control gain haste" (Bitter Reunion's family).
- "Attacking creatures gain first strike".

143 legal lines print a mass grant, and 86 of them are the last unread line on their card. Same
subjects, the same frozen list (CR 611.2c), one `pump` with only `keywords`.

Two things are left as they were:
- **The "hold for combat" bot hint stays off.** Haste has to arrive before attackers are declared,
  so holding the card for combat is the wrong advice for the most common grant.
- **Unknown keywords still refuse.** `grantedKeywordList` refuses a keyword the engine does not run
  (banding), and a list of three or more.

**Graveyard hate.** These read now:
- "Exile target player's graveyard" (Bojuka Bog, Angel of Finality).
- "Exile all cards from target player's graveyard" (Tormod's Crypt, Nihil Spellbomb).
- "Exile each opponent's graveyard".
- "Exile all graveyards" and "exile all cards from all graveyards".

The cards go to exile one by one through `exileCard`. The graveyard is read as the effect resolves,
so a card put there in response goes too.

`compile.test.ts`'s example of "a clause with no reader and no near miss" was Rest in Peace's "exile
all cards from all graveyards", which now reads. It moved to "each player shuffles their hand and
graveyard into their library".

### A guard violation shipped in D627

The D627 guide row said "the **untap symbol** ({Q}: Hateflayer, …)". `guards.js` reads "name
({cost}" as a card name followed by a quoted mana cost, and "untap symbol" is no card. The row was
written after the pre-gate checks had run, so the D627 commit (b0f7921) carries one guard violation,
which the gate would have caught had it run after the row. The row is reworded here.

To stop it happening again, the pre-gate checks are now one script, `pregate.sh`, which stops on
the first failure. The gate starts only if it passes, and the guide row is written **before** it
runs. The same mistake had nearly started a gate on a red tree earlier in this increment: the
compile test above was failing and the gate was launched anyway. It was stopped by hand.

**Tests.** 6 new engine tests:
- The rows read, and banding is refused.
- Your creatures gain flying and an opponent's do not.
- "Other creatures you control" leaves out the granter.
- Target player's graveyard goes to exile, and yours stays.
- All graveyards go, and the spell itself lands in your graveyard after.
- Each opponent's graveyard goes, and yours stays.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- The subject replaced by "your creatures".
- "All" shrunk to yours.
- "Each opponent's" widened to everyone.
- The target replaced by everyone.
- The keyword check removed. This one was uncaught until the refusal row was changed from
  "afterlife 1" (which the reader's own pattern already refuses, because of the digit) to banding.

## D629 — tap or untap, and "… and N damage to you"

**"Tap or untap target creature"** (Twiddle, Puppet Strings, Bounding Krasis, Elder Druid,
Trickster Mage): 42 legal lines, 31 of them the last unread line on their card. It reads as one
target and a two-word question, Tap or Untap, asked as the effect resolves (CR 608.2d). "You may"
in front works through `optionalEffect` as before: the inner question is gated on Yes and read at
index 0 after `withoutOurs`. Only a single target; "up to two" stays unread.

The bot's answer comes from the target. `ChoiceDecisionSpec.best` is handed only the state and the
chooser, but while it is asked `pendingDecision.stackId` names the resolving object, which carries
its targets:
- Someone else's permanent: tap it.
- Your own: untap it. This is also the no-op answer when your own untapped creature was targeted
  only to be targeted.

**"~ deals N damage to any target and M damage to you"** (Char, Fireslinger, Brothers of Fire,
Goblin Artillery): 15 lines, 14 the last unread line on their card. `damageEffect` splits the
trailing "and M damage to you" off the destination and deals it through `damageDestination('you')`
with its own printed number, after the first half. If the only target is illegal on resolution,
neither half happens (CR 608.2b); the engine's fizzle already does that.

**The D626 pin.** "Return ~ from your graveyard to your hand tapped" is no printing, and it stays
unread.

**Tests.** 4 new engine tests:
- The rows read.
- Tap or Untap is asked; the bot's preference is Tap on theirs and Untap on yours; each answer is
  applied.
- 2 to the target and 1 to you. The two amounts differ on purpose: with 1 and 1, the fault "the
  first amount used for both" went uncaught.
- The D626 pin.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- Always tap.
- The bot always taps.
- The damage to you dropped.
- "Tapped" accepted on a self-return to hand.
- The first amount used for both halves.

## D631 — "with three or more creatures", and enters triggers that name nobody's side

I ranked the prologues that block one-line-short cards. The method: put each line's effect behind
"When ~ enters," and keep the lines that then read, so the opening is the only blocker. Two of the
largest families need no new machinery.

**"Whenever you attack with two / three or more creatures"** (Chivalric Alliance, Armasaur Guide,
Gallia of the Endless Dance). The `attack-declared` event (D442) now carries `attackers`, the size
of the declaration as it is raised, so a myriad token made afterwards is not counted (CR 508.4). A
trigger's `atLeast` asks it. These stay refused: "with one or more <type>", "a player", "with your
commander", and "while creatures you control have total power 8 or greater".

**"Whenever a creature / an artifact / a land / an enchantment enters"**, with no side named
(Carnival of Souls, Blasting Station), and **"Whenever a creature an opponent controls enters"** /
"… enters under an opponent's control". These are new rows on the `etb` event, which has carried
`of: 'opponent'` since D134:
- "A", not "another": the card's own arrival counts (CR 603.6a). That is the distinction the Soul
  Warden row above it exists for.
- The opponent rows fire only for an opponent's permanent.

Three refusal rows in `compile.test.ts` named these exact sentences, and are now positive
assertions or removed with a note. One had been left unread "for its own row"; it now checks the row
reads `of: 'opponent'`, never `of: 'you'`.

Two families measured and left:
- **"Deals combat damage to a player or planeswalker."** No event is raised for a hit on a
  planeswalker, so reading it would miss half the trigger.
- **"Whenever an artifact is put into a graveyard from the battlefield."** It needs the card's type
  and controller as it left (last known information), about 4 cards.

### The pre-gate script let a red tree through

`pregate.sh` (written in D628 for exactly this) printed PREGATE-OK over four failing tests, and the
gate started. The cause: `echo "$out" | grep -q "failed"` under `set -o pipefail`. `grep -q` exits
at its first match, `echo` takes a SIGPIPE, the pipeline's status is non-zero, and the `&&` that
should have stopped the script never ran.

It now checks vitest's exit status, and matches " failed" in the shell. It was proven by planting a
failing test: the script stopped with exit 1, and the test was deleted. The stray gate was killed
before it finished. Nothing was pushed from that tree.

**Tests.** 4 new engine tests:
- The rows read.
- Two attackers: no life. Three: 3 life.
- "A creature enters" fires for my creature and for theirs; "an opponent controls" only for theirs.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- `atLeast` off by one.
- The count left off the raised event.
- The opponent rows read as "any".
- The any rows read as "you".

## D632 — abilities that work from the graveyard

92 unread trigger lines return their own card from your graveyard, and on 68 cards that is the last
unread line. Examples:
- Bloodghast's family: "Whenever a land you control enters, you may return this card from your
  graveyard to the battlefield".
- Ashen Ghoul's upkeep.
- The Prized Amalgam shapes: "… you may pay {1}. If you do, return ~ from your graveyard to your
  hand".

Until now no trigger could watch from a graveyard, except a card's own death, its arrival there, or
its own cycling.

**The engine.** `TriggerDef.inGraveyard` marks an ability that works only while its card is in its
owner's graveyard (CR 113.6k):
- After the battlefield watchers, `raise` offers every event to each card in each living seat's
  graveyard, for those triggers only.
- The battlefield loop skips them, so they do nothing on the battlefield.
- The card's `zoneSeat` in a graveyard is its owner, so "you" in the trigger is the owner, which is
  who controls such an ability (CR 113.8).

**The compiler.** A trigger whose events all fire on the battlefield, and whose clause returns its own
card from your graveyard, is read by `graveyardSelfReturn` alone (D626, to the hand or to the
battlefield, tapped or not). It may sit behind `optionalEffect`'s "you may" or "you may pay {N}. If
you do,". The trigger is marked `inGraveyard`. The battlefield vocabulary never sees the clause,
because it would read it as a permanent bouncing itself. Death and to-graveyard triggers are not
intercepted; they already fire from there for their own card.

Riders stay unread:
- "It gains haste until end of turn".
- "With a finality counter on it".
- Pay-any-number-of-times shapes.

**Tests.** 6 new engine tests, plus the D630 pin:
- The rows read, each marked as a graveyard ability.
- A land entering returns the card tapped on a yes.
- The same card on the battlefield, or in an opponent's graveyard, does nothing for your land.
- The opponent's graveyard card answers **their** land, and they are the one asked.
- A priced return: paid, and the card goes to the hand.
- The upkeep return from the graveyard.
- The D630 pin: "Monstrosity 2. Activate only as a sorcery." keeps `sorcerySpeed`.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- Graveyard triggers allowed on the battlefield.
- The graveyard loop not firing.
- The compiler not marking `inGraveyard`.
- The priced path dropped.
- The D630 timing dropped.
- Only seat 0's graveyard watched. This went uncaught until the opponent test was added.

## D633 — "one or more +1/+1 counters are put on"

36 legal lines watch counters being put on something, and on 26 cards that is the last unread line.
Examples:
- "Whenever one or more +1/+1 counters are put on ~": Benthic Biomancer, Dreamdrinker Vampire,
  Dusk Legion Duelist (14 lines).
- "… on a creature you control" and "… on another creature you control".
- "Whenever one or more -1/-1 counters are put on a creature".

The engine raised no event for it.

**The event.** It follows the same detect-then-announce pattern as `drew` and `cycled`:
- `addCounters` records a placement in `GameState.countersPut`. Only a +1/+1, -1/-1 or loyalty
  counter is recorded, only on the battlefield, and only when counters were added.
- `settle` drains the list and raises `counters-put`, with the counter, the permanent's controller
  and whether it is a creature.
- One event per placement is the "one or more" every printing says: two counters from one effect
  is one trigger.
- A permanent that enters with counters gets them through `addCounters`, and that counts as putting
  them on (CR 122.6).
- The regeneration shield is stored as a counter but is not one, and removing counters is not
  putting them on.

The new list is optional on `GameState`, so a saved game loads. It is reset in `engine.ts`'s two
initial states and in `settle`, and it keeps `settle`'s loop going like the lists beside it.

**The rows.** On ~ itself; on a creature or permanent you control, with or without "another"; and
-1/-1 counters on any creature. "Whenever **a** +1/+1 counter is put on" counts per counter, which
this event does not, so it stays unread.

`deck coverage` requires every trigger kind to have a pool card or a named exemption (D442).
`counters-put` is exempt, naming its corpus count and the runtime block that drives it.

**Tests.** 6 new engine tests:
- The rows read.
- Two counters at once fire one trigger.
- Your creature fires "a creature you control", and the opponent's does not.
- Counters on another creature do not fire "on ~".
- Removing a counter fires nothing.
- A regeneration shield fires nothing.

Faults injected by hand:
- **Caught:** the "you control" check removed; the drain left out of the loop guard.
- **Caught once their tests were added:** the self check removed; removals recorded.
- **Equivalent, kept:** any counter recorded, regeneration included. Every row names its counter,
  so no trigger can ask for a regeneration event. The key filter is kept so a future row with no
  counter named cannot fire on a shield.

    engine tests: 4,452, all passing

## D634 — "one or more cards leave your graveyard"

13 legal lines watch a graveyard empty out: Fuming Effigy, Garrison Excavator, Hardened Academic,
and "… creature cards …" (Chalk Outline, Desecrated Tomb). No event existed.

**The event.** `relocate`, the one place a card changes zone, records a card leaving a graveyard in
`GameState.leftGraveyard`, to anywhere: exiled, returned to a hand, reanimated, cast from there. It
stores whose graveyard it was and whether it was a creature card, read before the move. `settle`
announces the list as **one** `leaves-graveyard` event per graveyard, which is the "one or more"
every printing says: three cards exiled at once fire one trigger. The list is optional on
`GameState`, initialised in both of `engine.ts`'s states, reset in `settle`, and keeps `settle`'s
loop going. The trigger asks `of: 'you'` and optionally `creatures`.

**The D631 pin.** A creature printing "Whenever a creature enters" gains life for its own arrival.

**Tests.** 6 new engine tests:
- The rows read.
- Three cards exiled at once is one trigger.
- A card returned by an ability, with nothing else happening, still fires it.
- An opponent's graveyard does not count.
- "Creature cards" waits for a creature card.
- The D631 pin.

Faults injected by hand:
- **Caught:** one event per card instead of per graveyard; the "you" check removed; the creature
  check removed; the D631 rows reading `another`.
- **Caught once its test was added:** the drain left out of `settle`'s loop guard. Every earlier
  test cast a spell, and the spell landing in a graveyard started the pass anyway. The
  ability-only return is the case that needs the guard.

    engine tests: 4,458, all passing

## D635 — a tribe attacking, a creature becoming blocked, "When you cast", enters-or-face-up

Four of the prologues the ranking puts next, each an event the engine already raises:
- **"Whenever a Dragon you control attacks"** (Atarka, Kolaghan, Utvara Hellkite): one capitalised
  creature type, checked by `isCreatureType`. `attacks` gained `ofSubtypes`, asked like the board
  events' (D479). It needed one engine change: `raise` never attached subtypes to an attack event,
  only to enters, dies, sacrifices and combat damage. The first test failed at runtime with a
  correctly compiled trigger, which is how this was found. The attacker's live subtypes are now
  added.
- **"Whenever a creature you control becomes blocked"**: `becomes-blocked` with `who: 'any'` and
  `of: 'you'`, already matched by the shared board case.
- **"When you cast a creature spell"**: the cast family now accepts "When" as well as "Whenever",
  the same trigger (CR 603.2). "When you cast this spell" has its own row and is unaffected.
- **"When ~ enters or is turned face up"** (Efreet Weaponmaster): two events, one printed ability.

"Whenever a permanent is turned face up" stays unread: `turned-face-up` is only ever offered to its
own permanent.

**The D632 miss, settled.** "Eliminated seats still watched" was recorded as owed a three-seat pin.
Writing that pin showed the miss is equivalent: elimination empties the player's zones (CR 800.4a)
before any event is raised, so there is no card left to watch. The test stays as the record.

**Tests.** 5 new engine tests:
- The rows read, and the Efreet watches both moments.
- A Dragon attacking fires the row; a Giant does not.
- Your creature becoming blocked fires the row.
- "When you cast a creature spell" fires on the cast.
- The three-seat eliminated-player test described above.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- The subtype check removed.
- The subtype enrichment removed.
- "Becomes blocked" read for the opponent's side.
- Enters-or-face-up read as enters only.
- "When" refused by the cast family.

## D636 — level up, read: bands as the card's abilities in their band

`levelBands` (a size and keywords per band) and `levelUpAbility` have carried the pool's two
levelers since D572, but nothing filled them from printed text. So all 26 legal levelers were
unread from their first `LEVEL` header down. That was D572's deliberate fix: read line by line,
Brimstone Mage had every band's ping from level zero.

**The reader** (`readLevelBands`, in `compile.ts`):
- "Level up {cost}" becomes `levelUp` and `levelUpAbility(cost)`, at sorcery speed.
- Each `LEVEL n-m` or `LEVEL n+` header and its size line becomes a `LevelBand`.
- A band line that is only keywords goes on the band's `keywords`, which is where
  `characteristicsOf` already looks.
- Any other band line is read by the ordinary line reader and **scoped to the band**:
  - an activated ability gets an `activateOnlyIf` on the level count;
  - a trigger gets a level `condition`;
  - a static gets a `source-has-counter` `while`. The condition gained a `below` for the band's
    upper edge, so Kabira Vindicator's +1/+1 (levels 2-4) and +2/+2 (5+) never stack.
- Anything it cannot scope refuses the whole reading, and the tail stays unread exactly as D572
  left it. That includes a line no reader has, a static that already has a condition, and a line
  that grants an ability to something else.

**The definition.** The compiled `def` now carries `levelBands`. `compileSingle`'s `def` became a
`let`, so the reader can attach them.

16 of the 26 legal levelers now read whole. The other ten print a band line nothing reads yet:
Hexdrinker's "protection from everything", Halimar Wavewatch's islandwalk, Lighthouse
Chronologist's extra turn. Spacecraft share the header pattern (`STATION n+`) but also become
creatures at their threshold, which `LevelBand` cannot say, so they stay unread.

Two D572 rows asserted the old "unread" reading. They now assert the scoped one: Brimstone Mage's
1-damage line is its own at every level, its 3 only at 1-2 and its 5 only at 3+; Kargan
Dragonlord's firebreathing only at 8+, and its bands on the definition. A new row checks the
Dragonlord at four counters is a 4/4 that flies.

`guards.js`'s D251 tripwire flagged the band reader for reading `triggers` without
`grantedTriggers`. The reader does handle it, by refusing any fragment that grants; a comment at
the key check now says so.

**The D633 pin.** A -1/-1 counter does not fire "+1/+1 counters are put on ~". It places counters
with `addCounters` directly, because the test card's own "-1/-1 counter" line does not read and the
manual `card:counter` action does not go through `addCounters`. A +1/+1 counter is the control.

**Tests.** 5 new engine tests, 2 changed, plus the D633 pin:
- A Kabira Vindicator-style card reads whole.
- Its anthems apply only in their band, at levels 0, 2, 4 and 5.
- A leveler's attack trigger is not there at level zero, and is after one activation of its own
  "Level up", which also makes it a 3/3.
- The Dragonlord at four counters.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- The band's upper edge ignored on abilities.
- The upper edge left off the static.
- The `below` check removed.
- Triggers not scoped.
- Keywords not put on the band.
- The level-up ability missing.
- Activated abilities not scoped.
- For the D633 pin: the counter type ignored.

    engine tests: 4,468, all passing

### Measurements (rebuilt corpus)

Pod sweep 50301–50340 (D635's build): 40 of 40 finished, no throw and no stall, in 291 s.

**Break run on D635's build:** 4 of 5 caught. The miss is real: with the tribe word unchecked,
"Whenever a Vehicle you control attacks" would read as a creature type that never matches, a trigger

## D637 — Station: Spacecraft, read

67 legal Spacecraft, every one unread, because D620 refuses their `STATION n+` bands for the
reason D572 refused level bands. D636 built the scoping, and this applies it to charge counters,
with the three differences the rules make (CR 721):
- **The station ability.** "Station" builds `stationAbility()`: tap another untapped creature you
  control (D610's `tapUntapped`) to put on charge counters equal to its power, only as a sorcery.
  The power comes from a new `EffectContext.tappedPower`. `activate` sums the tapped creatures'
  power before they tap, and it travels on the stack object as `sacrificedStats` does, into both
  resolution contexts.
- **Cumulative bands.** Each band is "as long as it has N or more charge counters", with no upper
  edge, so scoped abilities ask only the lower edge. Because `levelBandOf` picks one band, each
  band carries every lower band's keywords.
- **The creature threshold.** A Spacecraft's printed size belongs to its last band, "It's an
  artifact creature at N+". That band is marked `LevelBand.creature`, and `characteristicsOf` adds
  the Creature type to the base type line before layer 4: the Spacecraft's own static ability. A
  Spacecraft printed with no size never becomes one.

`LevelBand` gained `counter` (`level` or `charge`) and `creature`, and `levelBandOf` counts the
band's own counter. **"This Spacecraft"** joined `SELF_TYPE_WORDS`, the one list every
self-reference reader uses. On its own that finished lines on most of the 67 ("When this Spacecraft
enters, …").

19 of 67 Spacecraft read whole. The rest print a band line or an ability nothing reads yet.

**The D635 pin.** "Whenever a Vehicle you control attacks" stays unread: Vehicle is not a creature
type, and a row that took it would never fire.

**Tests.** 5 new engine tests:
- The Spacecraft reads whole, with the creature band last and carrying its keywords.
- Tapping a 3-power creature puts three charge counters on it; the 2+ ability arrives and it is not
  yet a creature.
- At six counters it is a 4/4 artifact creature with flying, and the 2+ ability is still there.
- Station is refused outside the main phase. The test asserts the sorcery-speed message, in its own
  beginning of combat where it has priority, and is refused with no other creature to tap.
- The D635 pin.

Faults injected by hand:
- **Caught:** `levelBandOf` counting `level` for charge bands; the creature type not added;
  `tappedPower` replaced by the creature count; the band keywords dropped; the creature mark on the
  first band; the charge check removed; the D635 tribe check removed.
- **Caught once the test was tightened:** sorcery speed removed. The first version asserted only
  "refused", and the refusal it got was "no priority".

    engine tests: 4,473, all passing

## D638 — Class levels; proliferate stops counting markers

**Class levels** (CR 716). D620 left every line from a Class's first "{cost}: Level N" down unread,
because read as the card's own they all worked from level 1. A Class's level is a **designation,
not a counter**, so it is a new instance field, `CardInstance.classLevel`:
- Absent on the battlefield means level 1.
- `relocate` clears it when the card leaves, so the new object starts again (CR 400.7).

`classLevelAbility(cost, N)` gains level N only from level N-1, at sorcery speed (CR 716.2a).
`readClassLevels` scopes each level's lines to "this level or higher", since levels are cumulative,
the way D636 scopes a band:
- activated abilities through `activateOnlyIf`;
- triggers through `condition`;
- statics through a new `source-class-level` condition.

"This Class" joined `SELF_TYPE_WORDS`. Only 1 of the 35 legal Classes reads whole, because their
level-1 lines are mostly abilities nothing reads yet: cost reducers, replacement effects, "you may
play lands from your graveyard". The machinery is in place for when those land.

**Proliferate added to markers.** The engine keeps several per-object facts in `counters`: the
regeneration shield, "unearthed", "evoked", "dashed", "kicked", "myriad", "renowned". Proliferate
adds one of each kind of counter a permanent has (CR 701.27a), and it was adding one of each of
these too: a second regeneration shield, a creature kicked twice. `proliferateCandidates` also
offered a permanent carrying only a marker. Both now skip `MARKERS`, a new set in `effects.ts`.
Found while deciding not to store Class level as a counter, for exactly this reason.

**The D636 pin.** A band static that already has its own condition ("As long as you control a
Plains, ~ gets +2/+2" inside a band) refuses the band, rather than having its condition replaced. A
control shows the same line reads on a plain creature, so the refusal is the band's.

**Tests.** 6 new engine tests, 1 changed:
- The Class reads whole.
- Level 1 is vigilance only; level 2 adds haste; level 3 adds +1/+1 and keeps both.
- A level-2 activated ability is offered only from level 2.
- Level 3 cannot be skipped to, and a Class that leaves comes back at level 1.
- Proliferate adds to +1/+1 and not to a shield, and a shield alone is not a candidate.
- The D636 pin.
- The D620 row now checks the level-2 static is scoped to level 2.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- Level gain allowed from any lower level.
- `classLevel` kept on leaving the battlefield.
- The class-level condition always true.
- Proliferate counting markers.
- The candidate filter counting markers.
- **Caught once its test was added:** the scoping of a Class's activated abilities and triggers.
  The first Class test had only statics past level 1.
- **Caught once its pin was rewritten:** the D636 condition check. The first pin's line did not read
  at all, so it was refused for that reason instead.

    engine tests: 4,479, all passing

## D639 — a free regeneration is not a thing to keep pressing

Sweep 50501's one loop. Seed 50534 played Blessing of Leeches, whose "{0}: Regenerate enchanted
creature" D624 began reading, and the bot pressed it 1,000 times in one main phase. Each press adds
a regeneration shield, which the search sees as a change worth making, and a {0} cost never runs
out.

`AbilityDef.buysNothingIf` (D182, written for adapt) is the field for exactly this: the play stays
legal for a person, and the search stops taking it. Both compiled regenerate readers now set it:
- the host's (D624);
- the creature's own ("Regenerate ~").

The question they ask is "does this creature already have a shield", through one shared predicate,
`ALREADY_SHIELDED`.

`compiled-vs-written.test.ts` then flagged Blight Mamba and Drudge Skeletons: their compiled
readings now carried the hint and the hand-written scripts did not. The four hand-written
regenerators (Drudge Skeletons, River Boa, Blight Mamba, Skithiryx) now carry it too. Their costs
are mana, so they could not loop, but the bot would still pay for a second shield.

`pregate.sh` stopped on that disagreement before a gate ran, which is what D628 and D631 built it
to do.

**Tests.** 2 new engine tests: the hint is false with no shield and true with one, on an Aura's
host and on the creature itself. Seed 50534 replayed alone: finished in 62 turns, no loop.

Faults injected by hand, each caught:
- The self hint removed.
- The host hint always false.

    engine tests: 4,481, all passing

Coverage is unchanged by this increment: 10,683 of 31,653 cards, 29,275 of 59,306 lines.

## D640 — two commanders: partners, Backgrounds and companions

Until now a list with two names under its `Commander` header got one commander. The second name
joined the deck, and the engine had one tax and one 21-damage tally per seat. That is wrong for
every partner deck, and partners are a large share of Commander tables:
- 60 cards print a bare Partner;
- 52 print "Partner with";
- 32 print "Choose a Background";
- 27 are a Doctor's companion;
- 19 print a "Partner—" kind.

**The deck.**
- `DeckSpec.partner` is a second commander. It is placed in the command zone beside `commander`.
- `parseDecklist` reads the second single card under the header as `partner`. A third card, a
  repeated name, or a line of several copies joins the deck as before.
- `customDeck` checks the pair against the printed text with `partnersLegally`, which allows:
  - both print a bare "Partner" (CR 702.124c);
  - "Partner with", each naming the other (702.124j);
  - the same "Partner—" kind on both (Friends forever, Character select, Survivors, Father & son);
  - "Choose a Background" with a Background, either way round;
  - "Doctor's companion" with a Time Lord Doctor.
- An illegal pair keeps the old behaviour: the second card joins the deck. The result carries
  `partnerRefused`, and the realtime ack and the web note say it. The ack's `total` counts that
  card, because it is dealt into the library.
- The realtime pod passes `partner` through: stored list, card warm-up, card data rows, ack.

**The rules.**
- Commander tax (CR 903.8) is per commander when an owner has two. `CardInstance.commanderTax`
  holds it, and `commanderTaxFor` / `withCommanderTaxPaid` read and pay it. A seat with one
  commander still uses `Seat.commanderTax`, so the tabletop tax button and every existing game
  are unchanged.
- Commander damage (CR 903.10a) is per commander. Combat damage now also records
  `Seat.commanderDamageBy`, keyed by the commander's instance id. The state-based check judges
  an owner with two commanders on that record, and skips the per-seat sum, which would add the
  two together. An owner with one commander is judged on the seat tally exactly as before, which
  keeps the tabletop "cmd +1" button working.

**Not done.**
- The tabletop commander-damage button still counts per seat. On a partner deck it can record
  damage, but it cannot knock a player out.
- Colour identity is not checked, for one commander or two.
- The older sandbox route in `apps/api` has its own parser and is unchanged.

**Tests.**
- 2 engine tests:
  - both partners are dealt to the command zone; each pays its own tax; the second still casts
    for its printed cost after the first was taxed;
  - 20 + 20 from two partners is not out, and 23 from one is, through real combat.
- 3 deck tests: the pairing rules, with each kind accepted and refused; a legal pair kept; an
  illegal pair returned to the deck with its reason.
- 2 parser tests, 1 web note test, and 1 realtime test on live Postgres and Redis.

Faults injected by hand, 14 of 14 caught:
- per-commander tax read or paid at seat level;
- the per-seat sum still judged for partners;
- the per-commander check removed;
- the per-commander tally not added;
- the partner not placed;
- "Partner with" one-sided;
- any two kinds pairing;
- the Background only one way round;
- any companion pairing;
- the refused card dropped;
- a "Partner—" kind treated as bare Partner;
- the parser taking any second line;
- the note omitting the partner.

    engine tests: 4,486, all passing

Coverage is unchanged by this increment: 10,683 of 31,653 cards, 29,275 of 59,306 lines.

## D641 — "as it enters, choose a creature type / a color", kept on the permanent

105 legal cards print "As ~ enters, choose a creature type." (58) or "… choose a color." (48),
and a line after it that reads "the chosen type" or "the chosen color". The engine could ask the
question already: Obelisk of Urd and Voice of All were hand-written with a word question and an
`onResolve` that installed their effect. That one-off approach could not be compiled, and it did
nothing for a permanent that arrived without being cast.

**The mechanism.**
- `CardInstance.chosen` holds `{ type }` or `{ color }`, the answer the permanent got as it
  entered. It is cleared when the card leaves (CR 400.7), like `classLevel`.
- `entersChoice` gains `'creature-type'` and `'color'`. The permanent spell's resolution question
  is asked before it moves, the arrangement riot uses since D559. The answer is recorded as the
  permanent arrives.
- A permanent that arrives **uncast** (reanimated, flickered, put onto the battlefield by an
  effect) is answered by the card's own `best`. The rules give its controller the choice; the
  engine has no one to ask in the middle of another effect. This is named in the player guide.
- Statics carry the sentinel `CHOSEN_TYPE` (in a scope's `subtype` or in `addSubtypes`), or
  `chosenColor: 'protection' | 'color'`. `applyStatics` fills them from `chosen` as it installs
  them (`withChosen`). A static whose answer is missing installs nothing.
- `ChoiceDecisionSpec.optionsFor` works out the words when the question is asked.
  `creatureTypeOptions` offers:
  - first, the types on the chooser's own cards, commonest first;
  - then every other type on a battlefield or in a graveyard, alphabetically.
  It never reads anybody's library or hand. The fixed thirteen types remain the fallback for a
  table with fewer than two types.

**The bot's answer** (`enterChoiceDecision`) is aimed by the compiler from the card's other lines:
- **friendly**: the type the controller has most of on the battlefield; ties, and an empty board,
  go to the commonest type in their own cards;
- **hostile**: for a chosen-type static that shrinks or locks creatures (Engineered Plague), the
  opponents' commonest type;
- **protection**: the colour to fear, the Voice of All rule.

**The compiler.**
- `chooseAsEntersFromLine` reads the choice itself.
- `groupStaticFromLine` reads three group forms: "creatures you control of the chosen type",
  "other creatures you control of the chosen type", and "(all) creatures of the chosen type".
- `chosenSelfStaticFromLine` reads three lines about the card itself: "~ is the chosen type in
  addition to its other types", "~ has protection from the chosen color", and "~ is the chosen
  color".
- `compileSingle` refuses a line that reads a choice the card never makes. Chromatic Armor
  chooses with an activated ability, so its line stays unread rather than installing an anthem
  for no type.

Obelisk of Urd and Voice of All now use the shared mechanism. `compiled-vs-written` agrees on
both. `script entersChoice` leaves the compiler-only exemptions, because the pool carries it now.
compile.test's partly-read card moves from Obelisk of Urd to Willbender.

**Not done**, and named in the guide:
- mana of the chosen colour (about 12 lines);
- colour-scoped anthems;
- "whenever you cast a spell of the chosen type/color";
- chosen-type cost reductions;
- "… your opponents control of the chosen type";
- Aura protection from a colour.

**Tests.**
- 4 engine tests on printed text dealt as data:
  - the question on the stack offers this table's types, and the answer makes the Automaton an
    Elf that pumps the other Elves; leaving forgets the answer;
  - an uncast Automaton picks Elf off a two-Elf board although its deck runs more Goblins, and
    picks Goblin off a tied board;
  - Engineered Plague's bot names the opponents' Elves;
  - Order of the Stars gets protection from red.
- 2 compiler tests: the readings, and the refusal.
- The Obelisk options test now asserts table-derived types. The bot test keeps Vampire over Elf
  off a 2-to-1 board.

Faults injected by hand: 18 of 19 caught. The miss is an equivalent mutant: an undefined pick on
an empty board falls back to the first option in both callers, which is the same word.

    engine tests: 4,492, all passing

Coverage: 10,696 of 31,653 cards (+13), 29,399 of 59,306 lines (+124).

## D642 — mana of the chosen colour, and a land that chooses as it is played

The largest group D641 left: about 30 legal lines make "one mana of the chosen color". 20 print
"{T}: Add one mana of the chosen color.", and the ten Thriving lands and Gates print
"{T}: Add {G} or one mana of the chosen color." after "choose a color other than green". Most of
these are **lands**, and a land is played, not cast. No spell resolves for it, so D641's
resolution question never reaches it.

**The mana.**
- `parseManaLine` reads "one mana of the chosen color", optionally after one printed colour.
- It makes five one-colour abilities, the shape "any color" already has. Each colour other than
  the printed one carries `activateOnlyIf: chosen.color === that colour`, the gate Command Tower's
  identity uses since D617.
- So nothing else in the engine needed teaching: about 38 readers of `produces`, the solver and
  the auto-tapper all see ordinary mana abilities. `manaSources` already asked `activateOnlyIf`.
- `potentialMana`, the dimmed pips, did not ask `activateOnlyIf`, and now does. Without it a
  chosen-colour land lit all five colours, and so did a Command Tower outside its identity.
- Only the line-by-line reader may take the line (`chosenOk`), and `compileSingle` refuses it
  unless the card chooses a colour. The new compiler test caught the first draft: a land with
  only the mana line and no choice was read **whole** by `cardFromData`, and would have tapped
  for nothing.

**The choice.**
- "choose a color other than X" leaves X out of the options and out of the bot's pick.
- The two-sentence land line "This land enters tapped. As it enters, choose a color." is
  `entersTapped` plus the choice. "As it enters" alone is refused, because nothing says what
  "it" is.
- **A land is offered once per colour** (`LegalPlay.choose`, `AutoPlayLandAction.choose`): "Play
  Thriving Grove, choosing red". This is the shock-land arrangement from D587; the row is the
  answer. `playLand` checks the word against the land's own options and records `chosen` before
  `settle`.
- A land played without a colour, or put onto the battlefield by an effect, gets the card's own
  pick through D641's uncast path.
- The bot plays the row matching that pick.
- The web client sends `choose` with the row, as it sends `payLife`.

**Also in this commit:** the D640 break run's one miss ("Partner with" ignoring the names) is
pinned. Two "Partner with" cards that each name somebody else are now asserted to be refused, and
the break is caught.

**Tests.**
- 4 engine tests on printed text dealt as data:
  - a Thriving Grove is offered four rows, without green; choosing green is refused; played
    choosing blue (not its own pick), it is tapped, taps for G or U, and lights only those pips;
  - a colour on a land that chooses nothing is refused;
  - the bot names red for a deck whose commonest colour is green, because green is excluded;
  - a cast Coldsteel Heart is asked on the stack and taps only for blue.
- 1 compiler test: the five abilities, the excluded colour, the two-sentence line, an orphan mana
  line unread, and a bare "As it enters" unread.
- 1 web test: the row's colour is sent.

Faults injected by hand: 14 of 14 caught. Two first survived, because the tests chose the default
answer; both tests were strengthened.

    engine tests: 4,497, all passing

Coverage: 10,717 of 31,653 cards (+21), 29,445 of 59,306 lines (+46).

## D643 — "of the chosen color" as a scope, and casts of the chosen type or colour

D641 and D642 left two families behind:
- anthems scoped by the chosen colour: Hall of Triumph, Heraldic Banner (whose mana D642 read),
  and Caged Sun's first line;
- "Whenever you cast a spell of the chosen color / a creature spell of the chosen type":
  Vanquisher's Banner, Chronicle of Victory, Diamond Mare, Prism Ring, Diamond Knight, Curse of
  Wizardry, Jeweled Torque, Paradise Plume.

**A colour scope.**
- `ContinuousEffect` gains `controller-color`: creatures of a colour, yours or (`everyone`)
  anybody's, with `other`.
- The colour is read by `layerFiveColours`: printed colours, then any colour-setting effect, last
  one winning. It does not use `characteristicsOf`, because the scope is helping to compute the
  creature's characteristics, and asking for all of them would come back here.
- A colour-scoped effect never sets a colour, so it is skipped in that pass and the recursion
  cannot start.
- The static entry gains a `{ color }` scope. `CHOSEN_COLOR` is filled from `chosen` by
  `withChosen`, as `CHOSEN_TYPE` is.
- `groupStaticFromLine` reads "(other) creatures you control of the chosen color" and "creatures
  of the chosen color", beside the type forms.

**The cast filter.**
- `spell-cast` gains `ofChosen: 'color' | 'type'`, from the cast tail "of the chosen color/type".
- It is answered in `fireTrigger` beside heroic's `targetsSelf`, because it asks which permanent
  is watching: two Banners naming different tribes each draw for their own.
- The colour is matched against the event's colours. A type is matched against its subtypes,
  case-insensitively, as `ofSubtypes` is.

**The aim.**
- `compileSingle`'s choice guard now reads trigger events as well as statics, so "…of the chosen
  color" on a card that chose a type, or nothing, stays unread.
- A cast trigger that watches **other players'** spells of the chosen colour (`by` not `you`) aims
  the pick at the opponents. Curse of Wizardry would otherwise name its controller's own colour
  and curse them.
- A hostile colour now uses the colour-to-fear reading.

**Tests.**
- 4 engine tests:
  - Hall of Triumph choosing green pumps your green Elf, not your Goblin or the opponent's Elf;
    an Alloy Golem that chose green is green and pumped; a second Hall choosing red pumps the
    Goblin;
  - Vanquisher's Banner on Goblin draws for a Goblin spell and not for an Elf, and pumps it;
  - Diamond Mare on green gains for green only;
  - Curse of Wizardry's bot names the opponent's green over its own red.
- 1 compiler test: the colour scope, the cast trigger, an orphan unread, and a type cast on a
  colour card unread.

Faults injected by hand: 12 of 12 caught, after the test was made to choose two colours. A
hard-coded colour survived each single-colour version of it.
