## D644 — mana that may only be spent on the chosen creature type

"Spend this mana only to cast a creature spell of the chosen type" is printed on Unclaimed
Territory, Pillar of Origins, Secluded Courtyard (which adds "or activate an ability of a creature
or creature card of the chosen type"), Cavern of Souls, Echoing Cavern and Eclipsed Realms. These
are tribal Commander staples. `spendRestriction` refused them explicitly ("no chosen type is kept
yet"), and D641 now keeps one.

**The restriction.**
- `spendRestriction` reads the phrase without "of the chosen type" and marks the restriction
  `chosenType`.
- The only place a restriction is checked is `manaSources`, which knows the source permanent. It
  now also asks that the spell, or the ability's source, has the creature type the source chose.
- "creature card" in the activate half is read as "creature": the type line asked is the same.

**Where it may be read.**
- `parseManaLine` refuses a chosen-type restriction outside the line reader (`chosenOk`), as D642
  does for a chosen colour.
- `compileSingle` refuses "the chosen type" in a mana line on a card that did not choose a type.

**The lands.**
- D642's land rows extend to creature types. A creature-type land is offered once per type in
  `creatureTypeOptions`: the deck's own types first, commonest first.
- `playLand` checks the word against `optionsFor` and records `{ type }`.

**Not done**, and named in the guide:
- Cavern of Souls's "and that spell can't be countered". It needs the spell to remember which
  mana paid for it.
- A changeling creature spell counting as every type for these lands: `PaymentFor` carries the
  printed type line.
- Eclipsed Realms's named-type list.

**Tests.**
- 2 engine tests:
  - an Unclaimed Territory is offered Goblin then Elf (the deck's order); Dragon is refused;
    choosing Elf, it gives any colour to an Elf spell and only colourless to a Goblin or an
    instant;
  - Secluded Courtyard on Goblin pays a Goblin's ability in colour and an Elf's or an artifact's
    only in colourless.
- 1 compiler test: five restricted abilities; the orphan and a colour-choosing card both unread.

Faults injected by hand: 10 of 10 caught.

    engine tests: 4,505, all passing

Coverage: 10,729 of 31,653 cards (+3), 29,460 of 59,306 lines (+3).

## D645 — costs that tap your other permanents: Gates, "and/or", "another", and mana

D610 added `tapUntapped` ("Tap an untapped creature you control:") for creatures, artifacts and a
creature type. Ranking cost blocks after D644 found about 20 cards one line short on its edges:
- a mana ability with the cost: Holdout Settlement, Loam Dryad and Jaspera Sentinel ("{T}, Tap an
  untapped creature you control: Add one mana of any color."), and Birchlore Rangers ("Tap two
  untapped Elves you control: Add one mana of any color.", with no {T});
- a noncreature subtype: Crackling Perimeter's Gate, Dune Diviner's Desert;
- "artifacts and/or creatures": Adaptive Gemguard;
- "another untapped creature": Black Oak of Odunos, Wanderbrine Trapper;
- plural creature types such as "Elves", which the old pattern turned into "Elve".

**One parser.** `tapOthersCost` in `fromCardData.ts` now reads the cost for both readers: the
activated-ability reader in `scripts.ts`, and the mana-line parser, which `scripts.ts` cannot be
imported by. The kinds become:
- `creature`, `artifact`;
- `artifact-or-creature`;
- `permanent` with a noncreature subtype (Gate, Desert, Equipment, Vehicle, Food, Treasure, Clue);
- plus an `other` flag.

Plurals are singularised the way `singularCreatureType` does it. `tapCostPlan` honours the kinds
and never taps the source for `other`.

**Mana abilities.**
- The mana-line parser accepts the cost after `{T}`, and as the whole cost (`tap: false`).
- `sameCost` compares it, so Holdout Settlement's free `{C}` row and its paid colour rows are
  not folded into one cost.
- **These abilities are not mana sources.** `manaSources` skips them, as it skips Overeager
  Apprentice's discard (D580): which creature to tap is the player's answer, and an auto-tapper
  choosing it could tap the attacker they were about to swing with. `potentialMana` skips them
  too, kept in step.
- They stay plays the player presses, and activation already taps the planned permanents before
  the mana branch runs.

The D610 test that asserted the mana-ability refusal now asserts the reading. Its comment says
why the expectation changed.

**Tests.**
- 3 engine tests:
  - Birchlore Rangers is no automatic source and lights no pips; it is offered five rows; pressing
    green taps it and the other Elf (its own summoning sickness is no bar) and adds {G};
  - Holdout Settlement alone taps for {C} only, and with a creature offers the five coloured
    rows;
  - a Gate pays Crackling Perimeter and a Swamp does not; an artifact plus a creature pay the
    Gemguard; "another" refuses the Oak with nobody else to tap.

Faults injected by hand: 10 of 10 caught.

    engine tests: 4,508, all passing

Coverage: 10,755 of 31,653 cards (+26), 29,494 of 59,306 lines (+34).

## D646 — a token for the target's controller, and no maximum hand size

**A new priority list.** The corpus came from Forge and carries no popularity data, and Scryfall
is blocked. So the remaining tail was ranked against **244 Commander staples named from memory**:
Sol Ring, Cultivate, Beast Within, Rhystic Study, Reliquary Tower, and so on.
- Only 127 were fully read.
- An unread staple costs testers far more than an obscure card, so this list now leads the work.
- `$SP/staples.mjs` re-measures it. The list is saved in the repository as `claude/commander-staples.txt`.

**Tokens for somebody else.**
- `tokenEffect` takes a recipient, and the clause reader adds four subjects: "target player
  creates …", "target opponent creates …", "each opponent creates …" and "each player creates …".
- "Its controller creates …" then reads through D537's possessive swap, for which "target player
  creates" is the swapped sentence. That covers Beast Within, Generous Gift, Pongify and Rapid
  Hybridization.
- The controller is captured before the destroy, as D537 does for life loss (CR 608.2h).

**A spell's controller.**
- D537 refused "its controller" on a spell target, believing the controller lived only on the
  stack object.
- A cast puts the card on the stack under the caster's seat, so `withReferent` reads it from the
  instance before the counter moves it.
- `CONTROLLABLE_KINDS` gains `spell`. Swan Song, An Offer You Can't Refuse, and Countersquall's
  family of eight read.
- The D537 test that pinned the refusal now pins the reading, with the reason in its comment.

**The rider mid-line.** "It can't be regenerated" was read only as the last sentence. Pongify
prints the token after it, so the rider is now taken from anywhere after a destroy and the rest is
composed without it. A rider before any destroy is still refused.

**No maximum hand size.**
- `CardScript.noMaxHandSize`, read from "You have no maximum hand size." (23 legal cards).
- `maxHandSize(state, seat)` asks the seat's permanents live: face-down and ability-less ones
  don't count.
- Both cleanup sites use it. `script noMaxHandSize` joins the compiler-only exemptions, with its
  evidence.

**Tests.**
- 5 engine tests:
  - Beast Within gives the Bears' controller the Beast;
  - An Offer You Can't Refuse gives the countered caster two Treasures;
  - Pongify kills a shielded Drudge Skeletons and makes its controller an Ape;
  - each opponent gets the Food and the caster none;
  - the same hand discards to seven without a Tower and keeps every card with one.
- 2 compiler tests.

Faults injected by hand: 8 of 8 caught, after the each-opponent recipient got a runtime test.

    engine tests: 4,515, all passing

Coverage: 10,806 of 31,653 cards (+51), 29,578 of 59,306 lines (+84). Staples: 135 of 244.

## D647 — a search split two ways, and a search by the target's controller

Two staple shapes from D646's list.
- **Cultivate and Kodama's Reach**: "Search your library for up to two basic land cards, reveal
  those cards, put one onto the battlefield tapped and the other into your hand". D455 refused it
  on purpose, as "a split destination".
- **Path to Exile, Assassin's Trophy and Ghost Quarter**: "Its controller may search their
  library for a basic land card, put it onto the battlefield (tapped), then shuffle". Nothing read
  the second person.

**The split.**
- The two destinations are told apart by **the order the cards are chosen in**. The first goes
  onto the battlefield tapped, the second into the hand, and the prompt says so.
- That is the cheapest honest reading: the decision already keeps the order the cards were
  picked, and a second question ("which one goes to your hand?") would ask what the first answer
  already said.
- One card found goes onto the battlefield, which is the land a player wants out of a ramp spell.
- D455's refusal row is gone, with a note saying when and why. The reader's docblock no longer
  lists the split as refused.

**Somebody else's search.**
- "target player/target opponent (may) search(es) their library for …" is read as the
  second-person search. The question goes to `who: 'target-player'` and their library is offered,
  because a decision reads the asked seat's zone. What they find goes to **their** battlefield.
- Under D537's possessive swap, "Its controller may search …" becomes exactly that sentence. The
  question is re-aimed at the referent, whose seat was captured before the exile.
- "may" is the search's own `min: 0`.
- The exile runs before the question, which is the printed order. The test asserts it.

**Tests.**
- 2 engine tests:
  - Cultivate picking Island then Plains: the Island enters tapped and the Plains goes to hand;
    one Plains alone enters;
  - Path to Exile: the opponent is asked, offered only their own library, and their Island enters
    tapped under them; declining leaves them nothing.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught.

    engine tests: 4,516, all passing

Coverage: 10,820 of 31,653 cards (+14), 29,597 of 59,306 lines (+19). Staples: 140 of 244.

## D648 — extra land drops, and lands played from the graveyard

Staples behind it: Azusa, Lost but Seeking; Aesi, Tyrant of Gyre Strait; Crucible of Worlds;
Ramunap Excavator; and the extra-drop half of Oracle of Mul Daya and Dryad of the Ilysian Grove.
The corpus has 22 legal cards printing "You may play an additional land / two additional lands on
each of your turns", and 8 printing "You may play lands from your graveyard".

**Read live from the board.**
- `CardScript.additionalLands` (a count) and `landsFromGraveyard` are statics.
- They are asked of the seat's permanents each time a land drop is counted or offered, through
  `staticsOf`: the seat's own battlefield, face up, abilities intact.
- So an Azusa that dies, or is turned into a Frog, takes her drops with her. Nothing is recorded
  when she arrives.
- `landDropsFor` = 1 + this turn's `extraLands` (Explore) + every `additionalLands`. Both counting
  sites use it: `legalActions` and `playLand`.

**The graveyard is a land drop and nothing else.**
- With a Crucible, the seat's graveyard joins the candidate list as `landOnly` entries. A
  non-land there is skipped before anything else is asked of it, so a sorcery beside the Forest
  is never offered as a cast.
- The row reads "Play Forest from your graveyard".
- `playLand` accepts a graveyard card of the seat's own only while `landsFromGraveyardFor` says
  so.

**Tests.**
- 2 engine tests:
  - three lands with Azusa; one once she is gone; one when she has lost her abilities;
  - with a Crucible a graveyard Forest is offered and played, and a sorcery beside it (with mana
    to pay for it) is not; without one, the Forest is neither offered nor accepted.
- 1 compiler test: the counts and the zone.
- Two exemptions join the mechanic list, with their evidence.

Faults injected by hand: 8 of 8 caught. Two survived at first: no test removed Azusa's abilities,
and the graveyard sorcery could not be paid for. Both tests were tightened.

    engine tests: 4,519, all passing

Coverage: 10,829 of 31,653 cards (+9), 29,622 of 59,306 lines (+25). Staples: 144 of 244.

## D649 — the top of the library, revealed and its lands played

Courser of Kruphix and Oracle of Mul Daya, two Commander staples: "Play with the top card of your
library revealed." and "You may play lands from the top of your library." D648 gave Oracle its
extra land drop; these two lines were what was left.

**Both are statics**, read live by `topRevealedFor` and `landsFromTopFor` (through D648's
`staticsOf`), so they stop the moment the Courser leaves.

**The view.**
- While a seat's top card is revealed, `SeatView.libraryTop` names it.
- The card travels in `cards` without the library's own list, as a scry's cards do.
- `visible` lets every viewer read it. Nothing else of the library is sent.

**The play.**
- The top card joins the candidate list as a `landOnly` entry, D648's land-drop-and-nothing-else
  shape.
- The row reads "Play Forest from the top of your library".
- `playLand` accepts the seat's own top card, and only the top card, only while the permission
  holds.

**The table.** The seat strip shows "top: <name>" beside the deck count for any seat whose top is
revealed. Your own top card gets a "Top of your library" row next to your exile, and tapping it
there is how the land is played.

**Tests.**
- 2 engine tests:
  - an opponent's view holds the top card and its definition while Courser is out, and not the
    second card; without Courser, neither;
  - a land on top is offered and played; a spell on top is not offered; the land beneath it is
    neither offered nor accepted; without Courser, the top land is refused.
- 1 compiler assertion.
- 2 exemptions on the mechanic list.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 5 caught. The miss, `visible`'s top-only clause, is an equivalent
mutant: no other library card ever reaches an opponent's `cards`, and the owner's own search shows
the whole library anyway. It stays as a guard. The second-card offer survived at first and was
pinned.

    engine tests: 4,521, all passing

Coverage: 10,832 of 31,653 cards (+3), 29,639 of 59,306 lines (+17). Staples: 146 of 244.

a negated **card type**, so the whole family was unread: "nonartifact creature", "nonenchantment
permanent", Blinkmoth Well's "noncreature artifact".

- `permanentFilter` gains `notTypes`, checked against the **live** type line beside
  `notColours`. A creature made an artifact by an effect stops being a legal "nonartifact
  creature".
- The qualifier loop reads `non` + any permanent type.
- Blinkmoth Well's refusal row in compile.test retires, with a note.

**Tests.** 1 engine test: Go for the Throat offers the Bears and not an artifact Golem. Bears given
the artifact type stop being offered. The cast destroys them.

Faults injected by hand: 3 of 3 caught, including reading the printed type line instead of the

## D651 — Brainstorm, Ponder and the wheel; and answers read from their own offset

Three staples, three shapes, and one latent defect found on the way.

**Brainstorm.** "Draw three cards, then put two cards from your hand on top of your library in any
order." This is the loot's order problem: the cards put back may be ones just drawn. So it is read
by `lootResolution` beside Faithless Looting: the draw in `beforeDecisions`, a question from the
hand, and the chosen cards put on top **in the order picked**, the first picked being the new top
card.

**Ponder.**
- "Look at the top three cards of your library, then put them back in any order." D584 refused
  this, because the answer is a sequence. It is now a `library-top` question with `min = max = N`
  and the new `chosenGoTo: 'top'`: every card is picked, and they go back in pick order.
- **A reorder is asked even when every card must be picked.** The engine answers a question itself
  when the set is forced (`min === max === candidates`), which for a reorder would answer with the
  order the cards already had. Two or more cards are now asked.
- "You may shuffle" is a yes-or-no that shuffles through the new `shuffleLibrary` (seeded from the
  game).

**The wheel.** "Each player discards their hand" and Wheel of Fortune's "…, then draws seven
cards": every seat's hand goes to the graveyard, then each draws.

`clausesOf` holds ", then put them back in any order" and the wheel's ", then draws" whole, as D602
holds "then shuffle and put that card on top": cut apart, neither half is a sentence.

**The defect: answers were read from index 0.**
- A composed resolution's answers are one list in plan order, and every part read from index 0.
  That was right only while the answer-reading part was the first to ask anything.
- Ponder is the first composition with a question *before* the reader. Its shuffle read the
  reorder's answer, and never shuffled.
- `composeEffects` now hands the reading part the answers from its own offset: the number of plan
  entries before it.
- An `each-player` or `each-opponent` question expands into one entry per seat, so when one comes
  before the reader, the offset is not a fact of the text and the composition is refused.

The D584 refusal row is retired with a note.

**Tests.**
- 3 engine tests:
  - Brainstorm offers the three drawn cards and puts the two picked back, first on top;
  - Ponder is asked the reorder, keeps the order, and draws the card picked first; shuffled, the
    library is the same cards in another order;
  - Wheel of Fortune empties both hands into the graveyards and deals seven each.

Faults injected by hand: 7 of 7 caught, including the offset, the reorder auto-answer, and a
shuffle that does nothing.

    engine tests: 4,523, all passing

Coverage: 10,876 of 31,653 cards (+25), 29,695 of 59,306 lines (+30). Staples: 150 of 244.

## D652 — doubled tokens and replaced counters

Three staples: Anointed Procession, Parallel Lives, Doubling Season. The same table needed
Hardened Scales, Corpsejack Menace, Branching Evolution, Ozolith, Benevolent Hydra, Mowu and
Optimization Annex, about 20 legal cards.

**Read like a printed keyword, not compiled into a script.**
- These lines are replacement effects on events that happen everywhere in the engine. A token is
  made by `addTokens` from dozens of call sites, and counters go on through `addCounters`. A script
  field would have to be reached from each of those.
- So they are **printed parts**, read off the card's oracle text the way protection and landwalk
  are (`printedParts`). The compiler counts the lines as read through `isPrintedAbilityLine`, and
  the two primitives ask the board live:
  - `tokenMultiplier(state, seat)`: ×2 for each token doubler the creating seat controls;
  - `countersAfterReplacement(state, target, key, amount)`: every counter replacement that
    applies.
- `effects.ts` can reach `characteristics.ts`, and could not reach the scripts without an import
  cycle. That decided where these live.

**The counter replacements.**
- One parser reads both wordings. The common one is "If one or more [+1/+1|charge] counters would
  be put on [list] [you control], twice that many / that many plus one … are put on it instead".
  Doubling Season's own is "If an effect would put one or more counters on a permanent you
  control, it puts twice that many …".
- `what` is an any-of list of type words, matched on the target's **live** type line, or `self`
  (Mowu).
- "You control" is required, except for Primal Vigor's "a creature", which is anybody's.
- Order (CR 616.1): every "plus one" before every doubling — the order its controller would choose,
  so Hardened Scales plus Doubling Season makes 1 → 4.

**Exclusions.**
- Never a marker the engine keeps as a counter (a regeneration shield, "kicked").
- Never a removal: costs only remove counters.
- Never a Saga's lore counter, which arrives by turn-based action rather than by an effect.
- A face-down or ability-less doubler does nothing.

**Not done**, and named in the guide: Doubling Season doubling a planeswalker's starting loyalty
(`relocate` writes it directly); Primal Vigor's token half ("If one or more tokens would be
created", anybody's); Winding Constrictor-style "of each of those kinds" on several types; Pir's
"your team".

**Tests.**
- 2 engine tests:
  - one Soldier, two with Parallel Lives, four with Lives and Season; an opponent's Lives does
    nothing; a Lives without abilities does nothing;
  - Scales plus Season: one +1/+1 counter becomes four, a charge counter two; an opponent's
    creature, a regeneration shield and a removal are untouched.

Faults injected by hand: 8 of 8 caught. The ability-loss guard survived at first and was pinned.

    engine tests: 4,525, all passing

Coverage: 10,889 of 31,653 cards (+13), 29,718 of 59,306 lines (+23). Staples: 153 of 244.

## D653 — free if you control a commander

"If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost." is printed on
5 legal cards: Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat, Deadly Rollick, Flawless Maneuver and Obscuring
Haze. The first three are Commander staples.

**An alternative cost of nothing**, the sixth in the family evoke, dash, bestow, spectacle and
overload share.
- `CardScript.freeWithCommander`, read by `spellStaticFromLine`.
- `legalActions` offers a row, "Cast X for its commander bonus (free, because you control a
  commander)", only while `controlsACommander`: a commander instance on the caster's battlefield.
  The command zone does not count.
- `AutoCastAction.commanderFree` is validated with the other five: one alternative cost per cast,
  from the hand, on a card with the line, and refused when the condition fails. It pays `{0}`.
- The bot passes the flag and keys the play on it. A guard test — every field a play and a cast
  share is one the bot passes on — caught the omission before the commit.
- The web client sends it with the row, as it sends `evoked`.

**Not done:** Deflecting Swat's other line, "You may choose new targets for target spell or
ability", which is a different reader.

**Tests.**
- 2 engine tests at a Commander table:
  - with the commander on the battlefield the free row is offered and the cast exiles its target
    with no mana spent;
  - with it in the command zone the row is absent and the flag refused; a card without the line
    is never free.
- 1 web test.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught.

    engine tests: 4,527, all passing

Coverage: 10,892 of 31,653 cards (+3), 29,726 of 59,306 lines (+8). Staples: 155 of 244.

## D654 — death triggers that name a player; the reorder the bot could not answer

**Three Commander staples name a player through the creature that died.** Grave Pact says "each
other player sacrifices a creature", Massacre Wurm "that player loses 2 life" after "a creature an
opponent controls dies", Fecundity "that creature's controller may draw a card". None read.
- `eventRelativeEffect`: a `dies` trigger watching other creatures ("a creature an opponent
  controls", "a creature you control", "a creature") is now about a player. `fireTrigger` already
  raises the event with the dead creature's seat as its actor, so "that player" means that seat.
- "That creature's controller" is the same referent, offered only when every event is a death.
- `readEffect`: "each other player …" is read as "each opponent …". Every table here is a
  free-for-all, where the two are the same seats.

**Not done:** Fecundity itself. Its "may" is asked of another player, and no reader asks a
non-controller an optional question. 289 legal cards print "that player may", "target player may"
or similar, so it is its own increment.

**The sweep found a crash in D651's reorder.** Seeds 52033 and 52036 of sweep 52001 threw
"choose exactly 4" in a pod.
- "Put them back in any order" was not marked as a reorder: `pendingDecision.picksGoTo` carried
  only graveyard and hand.
- The bot therefore gave it the scry answer (the lands it would bottom), two cards where four were
  asked.
- The fix: `picksGoTo` now includes `'top'`. The bot answers it as it answers a dig (all of them,
  best first), and the web bar says "tap all N in order, the first goes on top".
- Both seeds now finish.

**Tests.**
- 4 engine tests in a three-seat pod:
  - Grave Pact makes both other seats sacrifice and spares its controller's second creature;
  - Grave Pact does nothing when an opponent's creature dies;
  - Massacre Wurm drains only the seat that lost the creature;
  - "that creature's controller draws" draws for that seat, not the enchantment's.
- 1 engine test: the reorder is marked `top` and the bot's answer is accepted.
- 1 web test for the reorder's words.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught. One survivor (normalising to "each player") was pinned by
giving the Pact's controller a second creature.

    engine tests: 4,532, all passing

Coverage: 10,898 of 31,653 cards (+6), 29,734 of 59,306 lines (+8). Staples: 157 of 244 (+2).

## D655 — token anthems, team protection, tutors to the top, an exact mana value

Four small readers, chosen from the unread staples. Staples went from 157 to 163 of 244.

**"Creature tokens you control get +1/+1 and have vigilance"** (Intangible Virtue).
- A new static scope, `controller-tokens`, and a matching `ContinuousEffect` scope that requires
  `isToken`. Being a token is a fact about the permanent (CR 111.1), not something on its type
  line, so a scope fits better than a filter.
- `groupStaticFromLine` reads the line. The predicate grammar is the one every other group static
  already uses.

**"Permanents you control gain X until end of turn"** (Heroic Intervention, and a Boros Charm
mode).
- Every permanent on the controller's battlefield, fixed at resolution (CR 611.2c).
- Kept out of `MASS_PUMP_SUBJECTS`, so a size can never be read onto a land.

**Tutors to the top.**
- "…, then shuffle and put that card on top" no longer requires ", reveal it" (Vampiric Tutor).
- "the card" is accepted as well as "that card" (Worldly Tutor).

**"Counter target spell with mana value 1"** (Mental Misstep). `targetSpecFrom`'s mana-value clause
now accepts an exact value as well as "N or less" and "N or greater". On the stack it uses the
announced X, as the bounded forms do.

The D492 refusal row "Destroy target creature with mana value 3." is retired. It assumed Magic
prints only the bounded forms there; Mental Misstep and Spell Snare print the exact one. Its
replacement is a reading test in compile.test.ts.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- Intangible Virtue pumps the token and not the nontoken Bears beside it.
- Heroic Intervention reaches the enchantment and the land and not the opponent's creature; a wrath
  afterwards leaves its controller's side standing.
- Vampiric Tutor puts the chosen card on top and costs 2 life.
- Worldly Tutor offers only creatures.
- Mental Misstep refuses a free spell and a two-drop, and counters a Bolt.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught. One survivor (an exact value read as "or less") was pinned
by adding the free spell to the Misstep test.

    engine tests: 4,537, all passing

Coverage: 10,915 of 31,653 cards (+17), 29,771 of 59,306 lines (+37). Staples: 163 of 244 (+6).

## D656 — lands from hand, graveyard cards to the top, drain and gain

Three readers, picked by how many legal cards each shape reaches. Staples went from 163 to 166.

**"(You may) put a land card from your hand onto the battlefield (tapped)"** (45 cards: Sakura-Tribe
Scout, Arboreal Grazer, Growth Spiral, and Elvish Piper's creature form).
- A question about the hand, with a filter, read by `libraryFilter`.
- "You may" is the empty answer (min 0), not a yes-or-no in front of the question. Without it, the
  bound is one card, clamped to what the hand holds.
- It is not a land play, so the land drop stays.
- The D525 refusal row that used this half as its unreadable example now uses "You may exile a
  creature card from your hand". The sequence reader already judges "if you do" by whether the
  answer named a card.

**"Put target X card from your graveyard on top of your library"** (44 cards: Academy Ruins,
Aphetto Vulture, Bloodwater Entity). The same targets as the return-to-hand reader beside it, moved
to the top of the owner's library.

**"… You gain life equal to the life lost this way"** (20 cards: Gray Merchant, Kokusho).
- `clausesOf` holds the two sentences together.
- The gain is what the first clause actually took, read off every seat's life total before and
  after. A seat that has left the game, or whose life cannot change, gives nothing back.

**Not done:** devotion as X (Gray Merchant's count), and "any number of target … cards" to the top.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the Scout offers only lands, can be declined, and leaves the land drop;
- the mandatory form asks for one card and puts it in tapped;
- Academy Ruins tops the artifact;
- a Merchant in a pod of three gains 4 from two opponents, and 2 once one of them has conceded.

Faults injected by hand: 7 of 7 caught. One survivor (a fixed 2 per opponent) was pinned by the
conceded seat.

    engine tests: 4,541, all passing

Coverage: 10,974 of 31,653 cards (+59), 29,854 of 59,306 lines (+83). Staples: 166 of 244 (+3).

## D657 — devotion, as a count and as the gods' condition

64 legal cards mention devotion (CR 700.5). Staples went from 166 to 168: Gray Merchant and
Purphoros.

**The count.**
- `devotionTo(state, seat, colours)`, in characteristics.ts: mana symbols of those colours in the
  printed mana costs of the seat's permanents. A hybrid symbol counts once if either half matches
  (CR 700.5a); generic, colourless and snow never do.
- Printed costs only, so it can be asked inside `characteristicsOf` without re-entering it.
- "Your devotion to X (and Y)" is a `boardCount`, so it reads everywhere a board count does: "where
  X is", "draw cards equal to", "gain/lose life equal to", "deals damage equal to", and "+X/+X".

**The gods.** "As long as your devotion to red is less than five, Purphoros isn't a creature."
- `staticCondition` reads it as a `controller-devotion` condition with a `below` bound.
- `thresholdPredicate` reads "isn't a creature" as a new layer-4 field, `removeTypes`. It applies in
  effect order with `addTypes`, so a later "becomes a creature" puts the type back.
- `withAddedTypes` returns the printed line untouched unless something was added or removed, so the
  hot path is unchanged.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- a Merchant drains by black symbols, with hybrid counted once;
- a green count beside black permanents counts only the green;
- a two-colour devotion counts each hybrid once and never generic;
- a god is an enchantment below five and a 6/5 creature at five, and stops being one when the
  devotion goes again.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught. One survivor (a count fixed to black) was pinned by the green
count.

    engine tests: 4,545, all passing

Coverage: 10,989 of 31,653 cards (+15), 29,887 of 59,306 lines (+33). Staples: 168 of 244 (+2).

## D658 — a "may" answered by somebody else

"Target player may …", "each opponent may …", and, through the referent readers that swap their
pronoun for "target player", "that player may …", "its controller may …" and Fecundity's "that
creature's controller may draw a card". No reader asked a non-controller an optional question
before; 289 legal cards print one.

**`anotherPlayersMay`**, the last reader in `readEffect`'s chain.
- It is last so that D647's targeted search keeps its reading: one search that may come back empty
  is one question, where this would ask two.
- The clause after "may" is read as if that player had printed it ("their" becomes "your") and run
  with that player as controller.
- "Target player / target opponent": a `target-player` Yes/No. The clause's own questions are
  re-aimed at the same player and gated on Yes (`askOnlyIfChosen`, D450). The referent readers then
  re-aim `target-player` at the acting, hit or referent player, as they already did for other
  questions.
- "Each player / each opponent": one Yes/No per seat. Each answer carries its seat, so each seat
  that says yes gets the effect as its own controller. A clause that asks its own question is
  refused here, because the plan expands a seat at a time and the gate is per question.
- Refused: a clause with targets, or one with work before its questions.

**Measured: +5 cards.** The mechanism is in, but most of the 289 lines fail on the clause after
"may": "cast …", "pay …", "put … onto the battlefield" in shapes nothing reads yet. Those are now
ordinary clause readers away rather than a missing mechanism.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- Fecundity asks the dead creature's controller, who draws on a yes;
- "its controller may draw" is asked of the destroyed creature's controller, and No draws nothing;
- "target player may draw" is answered by the target;
- "each opponent may draw" asks seats 1 and 2 and not the caster, and each answer counts only for
  that seat;
- "target opponent may put a land card from their hand onto the battlefield": the land question
  goes to the same player, from their own hand, and is not asked on a no.

Faults injected by hand: 9 of 9 caught. One survivor (the inner question not gated) was pinned by
giving the declining player lands in hand.

    engine tests: 4,550, all passing

Coverage: 10,994 of 31,653 cards (+5), 29,894 of 59,306 lines (+7). Staples: 169 of 244 (+1,
Fecundity).

## D659 — ward in a keyword list, and a tax that is not a "may"

**Ward in a list.** "Flying, ward {2}" was refused whole, so a warded flier had neither its flying
nor its ward. In a sample of 40 lines printing "unless that player pays", every unread one was ward
in a list or ward granted to something else.
- `printedParts` leaves a ward part out of a list of two or more, so the rest of the list reads as
  printed keywords.
- `compile.ts`, `wardInList`, emits the ward trigger from each ward part. It runs before the
  printed-line check, which would otherwise count the line compiled and emit no ward at all.
- `cardFromData` no longer takes a ward list as keyword-only text. That reading would have been a
  drake with flying and no ward, and the runtime test caught exactly that on its first run.

**"X unless that player pays {N}"** (`punisherEffect`). The mandatory sibling of
`mayUnlessThatPlayerPays`.
- It applies only to triggers whose events are all a player's action, where "that player" is the
  acting player.
- Smothering Tithe's two sentences ("that player may pay {2}. If the player doesn't, you create a
  Treasure token") are rewritten to this form first.
- The question is the acting player's, with the price on the paying answer. A player who cannot
  afford it is not asked, and the effect happens.
- Refused: an X price (Esper Sentinel), a clause that asks or targets, and "counter it" on a cast
  trigger, which nothing reads yet.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- "Flying, ward {2}" has flying, and a removal spell from a seat with no mana is countered;
- Smothering Tithe makes a Treasure when the drawing opponent cannot pay;
- paying {2} prevents it and taps their lands, and declining with the mana available still makes
  one.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught.

    engine tests: 4,553, all passing

Coverage: 10,999 of 31,653 cards (+5), 29,945 of 59,306 lines (+51). Staples: 170 of 244 (+1,
Smothering Tithe).

## D660 — the greatest power among a group, and a target's mana value

Two more counts for `boardCount`, so each reads in all five grammars that take a count ("where X
is", "draw cards equal to", "gain/lose life equal to", "deals damage equal to", "+X/+X").

**"The greatest power (toughness, mana value) among …"** (78 legal cards: Rishkar's Expertise,
Return of the Wildspeaker).
- `greatestAmong` handles these groups: creatures you control, other creatures you control,
  <Type> or non-<Type> creatures you control, creatures your opponents control, and creatures on the
  battlefield.
- Live characteristics are read as the effect resolves, so pumps count.
- An empty group gives 0, and so does a negative maximum, because CR 107.1b makes a negative count 0.

**"Its / that permanent's mana value"** (Feed the Swarm).
- The value is the first card target's printed mana value, which is the same in every zone
  (CR 202.3). The permanent having been destroyed first changes nothing.
- Power and toughness are deliberately not read the same way: they would need last-known
  information.
- The first probe read it everywhere, including "Whenever a creature you control dies, you gain life
  equal to its mana value", where "its" is the dying creature and the gain would have been 0.
- It now reads only while `composeEffects` reads a clause that follows one aiming at a card (the
  `earlierCardTarget` flag, set the way `sacrificeInCost` is).

**Tests.**
- 3 engine tests:
  - the Expertise draws by a pumped Giant's power and not by the opponent's bigger creature, and
    draws none with no creatures;
  - a non-Human group leaves the Human out;
  - Feed the Swarm costs the destroyed enchantment's mana value.
- 4 compile tests: read after a card target; unread with no earlier target, in a death trigger, and
  after a player target ("its" being the discarded card).

Faults injected by hand: 8 of 8 caught. Two survivors were pinned:
- seats beyond the controller, by breaking a tie between the Giant and the opponent's creature;
- the player-kind check, by a two-clause row.

    engine tests: 4,560, all passing

Coverage: 11,016 of 31,653 cards (+17), 29,966 of 59,306 lines (+21). Staples: 171 of 244 (+1, Feed
the Swarm).

## D661 — Ophiomancer's "if you control no Snakes", and Seedborn Muse

Two staples. Staples went from 171 to 173.

**"If you control no X"** (22 legal cards). `interveningConditionFor` already read "you control a/an
X" and "N or more"; "no X" is the same count read in the plural, at zero. Ophiomancer's "At the
beginning of each upkeep, if you control no Snakes, create a 1/1 black Snake …" now reads. The
engine asks the condition both when the trigger fires and when it resolves (CR 603.4).

**Seedborn Muse.**
- New field `CardScript.untapsDuringOthersUntap`. In each untap step `onEnterStep` untaps the active
  seat, then every other living seat that controls a live permanent with the field. Live means not
  face down and not stripped of its abilities, the same rule as `noMaxHandSize`.
- `untapAll` gains `othersStep`: a frozen permanent ("doesn't untap during its controller's next
  untap step") stays tapped and stays frozen through somebody else's untap step, so it is spent in
  its controller's own step and not before.
- No pool deck has the Muse. It is in the mechanic-coverage test's `compilerOnly` set, with a
  pointer to the runtime test.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Ophiomancer makes a Snake when there is none, and not in the next upkeep with one already there;
- the Muse untaps seat 0's lands in seat 1's untap step, and without it they stay tapped;
- a frozen land stays tapped and frozen through the other seat's untap, and the freeze is spent in
  its controller's own untap step.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught.

    engine tests: 4,563, all passing

Coverage: 11,020 of 31,653 cards (+4), 29,970 of 59,306 lines (+4). Staples: 173 of 244 (+2).

## D662 — mana for each thing you control

"{T}: Add {G} for each creature you control" (Gaea's Cradle), "… for each Elf you control" (Elvish
Archdruid), "… for each Elf on the battlefield" (Priest of Titania), "{T}: Add {C} for each charge
counter on ~" (Everflowing Chalice). A mana line had a fixed list of mana until now. Staples went
from 173 to 174 (the Cradle).

**Engine.**
- New field `AbilityDef.producesTimes`, a count read off the board.
- New function `producedBy(state, ability, source, controller)` is the one reader. It returns
  `produces` repeated that many times; a count below zero makes nothing.
- Activation adds `producedBy`'s mana and logs it.
- `manaSources` offers what the source would make now and skips it at zero, so the auto-payer never
  taps a Cradle for nothing.
- `potentialMana` counts it.

**Compiler.** `parseManaLine` reads a single symbol followed by "for each …" as a sum line with a
count (`ManaLine.per`). `manaCount` reads two kinds of phrase:
- permanents by card type or capitalised subtype, "you control" or "on the battlefield", using live
  characteristics;
- a charge, +1/+1 or storage counter on the source itself.

**Not done:** counted mana whose cost starts with mana ("{2}, {T}: Add {B} for each Swamp you
control", Cabal Coffers; the mana-line pattern only takes a cost starting with {T}), and counts of
cards in hand or drawn this turn.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the Cradle shows and makes three green with three creatures, the opponent's not counted;
- it pays for a three-mana spell alone, and with no creatures it offers no mana and is not a
  source;
- the Chalice counts its own charge counters, and an Elder counts its controller's Elves only.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught.

    engine tests: 4,566 at D662's own run (the gate ran with D663, below)

Coverage: 11,033 of 31,653 cards (+13), 29,988 of 59,306 lines (+18). Staples: 174 of 244 (+1).

## D663 — Lotus Cobra's mana of any color, and a choice of tokens

Two clause readers in `untargetedEffect`, for a trigger or a spell (a mana ability's "Add one mana
of any color" is read by the mana-line parser, as before). Staples went from 174 to 176: Lotus
Cobra and Tireless Provisioner.

- **"Add one mana of any color"**: a question with the five colour names, answered as the ability
  resolves, then `addToPool`. The `best` hint names the colour with the most pips among the mana
  costs in the chooser's hand, and none when the hand asks for nothing. The D386-era row in
  compile.test.ts that listed this clause as "mana a pool cannot hold" is retired, because the
  answer is a colour the pool can hold. `{2}` and `{E}` stay refused.
- **"Create a Food token or a Treasure token"**: each half is read as the token clause it is, and
  must ask and target nothing. The choice is the controller's, with the first named token as the
  default.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- a land drop under Lotus Cobra asks for a colour and adds exactly that;
- the bot names blue with a {U}{U} card in hand;
- the Provisioner makes the token named and not the other, both ways.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 4,569, all passing

Coverage: 11,042 of 31,653 cards (+9), 30,001 of 59,306 lines (+13). Staples: 176 of 244 (+2).

## D664 — "Choose two", "Choose one or more", and the modes they needed

The work queue's seventh row was "Choose one" (198 unread lines). The modal reader (`modalScriptFor`)
already read "Choose one" and "Choose one or both". It refused the rest of a card whenever a header
or a single mode did not read. Staples went from 176 to 180: Kolaghan's Command, Farewell, Austere
Command, Return of the Wildspeaker.

**Headers** (`ModalDef` already supported both; only the reader refused them):
- "Choose two —" (31 legal cards) is `min: 2, max: 2`. It needs at least three modes, or it is not
  a choice.
- "Choose one or more —" (18) is `min: 1, max: modes`.

**Modes that blocked staples.**
- `massScope` takes a "with mana value / power / toughness N or less/greater" tail. Mana value is the
  printed cost (CR 202.3, X counted as 0); power and toughness are live. All are read before
  anything moves. This gives Austere Command's two creature modes and "Exile all creatures you
  control with toughness 2 or less".
- `massPumpSubject` takes "(other) (non-)<Type> creatures you control", checked against the
  creature-type list, so "attacking creatures you control" is not mistaken for a type. This gives
  Return of the Wildspeaker's "Non-Human creatures you control get +3/+3" and "Elf creatures you
  control gain trample".

**Not done:** Akroma's Will ("Choose one. If you control a commander as you cast this spell, you may
choose both"), Rakdos Charm's "Each creature deals 1 damage to its controller", and "attacking
creatures you control" as a pump subject.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- "Choose two" offers only pairs, refuses a single mode, and casts a destroy and a burn together;
- Austere Command's artifacts + small creatures sweep spares the 4-drop and the enchantment;
- "Choose one or more" offers 7 combinations of 3 modes, and all three exile everything;
- a non-Human pump leaves the Human alone.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 4,573, all passing

Coverage: 11,076 of 31,653 cards (+34), 30,088 of 59,306 lines (+87). Staples: 180 of 244 (+4).

## D665 — mana abilities that cost mana first

105 legal lines print a mana ability whose cost starts with mana: "{2}, {T}: Add {B} for each Swamp
you control" (Cabal Coffers), "{1}, {T}: Add {R}{R}", and the filter lands' "{U/R}, {T}: Add {U}{U},
{U}{R}, or {R}{R}" (Cascade Bluffs, a staple). The mana-line pattern took only costs starting with
{T}, so every one was unread. (D662 named Coffers as not done for this reason.)

**What changed.**
- `parseManaLine` peels a leading mana run, reads the rest as the {T} line it is, and puts the mana
  on the cost (`ManaAbilityCost.mana`).
- The engine needed nothing new. Activation already pays an ability's mana with `payFrom`, which
  taps other sources, and `manaSources` already leaves out any ability that costs mana. Such
  abilities are therefore pressed by the player, never used by the automatic payer.
- `sameCost` compares the mana too. Without that, the whole-card fold would merge a free colourless
  tap with a paid coloured one into a single free choice.
- The filter lands' choice of equal-sized runs is a new `ManaLine.mode`, `runs`. It gives one
  ability per run on the line path. It is never folded on the whole-card path, which refuses it out
  loud.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Coffers is not a source for the automatic payer; pressed, it taps two Swamps for its {2} and
  leaves three black, the tapped Swamps counted;
- a land with "{T}: Add {C}" and "{1}, {T}: Add {G}" shows one colourless and no free green;
- a filter land turns an Island's blue into {U}{R}.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught. One survivor (`sameCost` ignoring mana) was pinned by the
free-green test.

    engine tests: 4,576, all passing

Coverage: 11,086 of 31,653 cards (+10), 30,098 of 59,306 lines (+10). Staples: 181 of 244 (+1,
Cascade Bluffs).

## D666 — Phyrexian Tower's sacrifice for mana, and Craterhoof's count

Staples went from 181 to 183.

**"{T}, Sacrifice a creature: Add {B}{B}"** (Phyrexian Tower).
- The mana-line parser refuses a sacrifice of another permanent, because which creature to sacrifice
  is a choice it does not model. Then the compiler's rule "a line that promises mana and could not
  be read is unread" made the line unread.
- The general activated-ability reader does model that choice: it is how "Sacrifice a creature: Add
  {C}{C}" has always read.
- The compiler now asks the general reader for a {T}-first line with a typed sacrifice. It takes
  the answer only when every ability returned makes mana and carries the sacrifice, and nothing
  else came back, so the Coliseum failure (D497) cannot recur.
- `manaSources` and `potentialMana` both skip a typed sacrifice. The Tower is pressed by the player
  and never spent by the automatic payer, and a spell is not offered on mana it could only make by
  sacrificing a creature the player did not pick.

**A team pump by a count** (Craterhoof Behemoth, Overwhelming Stampede). "Creatures you control gain
trample and get +X/+X until end of turn, where X is …":
- the count is any `boardCount`, read once as the clause resolves and then fixed (CR 611.2c);
- the keyword may come before or after the size;
- the hold-for-combat hint is set where the subject is your own team.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- the Tower: no black counts as reachable, a {B}{B} spell is not offered, its source entry makes
  only {C}, and pressed with the Bears named it sacrifices them for {B}{B};
- Craterhoof with two Bears: +3/+3 and trample on all three, and a creature arriving afterwards is
  not pumped.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught. One survivor (the `manaSources` skip) was pinned by the
source-entry assertion.

    engine tests: 4,578, all passing

Coverage: 11,093 of 31,653 cards (+7), 30,113 of 59,306 lines (+15). Staples: 183 of 244 (+2).

## D667 — Tectonic Edge's margin, Rakdos Charm's self-damage, Homeward Path

Three small readers, each a staple. Staples went from 183 to 185.

- **"An opponent controls at least four more lands than you"** (Tectonic Edge). It sits beside
  D622's "more lands / creatures than you" comparison, now with a margin: at least N more. The
  existing form is the margin 1, so it reads exactly as before. Being an "Activate only if" clause,
  it is asked when the ability is offered and again when it is activated.
- **"Each creature deals N damage to its controller"** (Rakdos Charm's third mode). Every creature on
  the battlefield as the clause resolves, each the source of its own damage, to the player who
  controls it at that moment.
- **"Each player gains control of all creatures they own"** (Homeward Path). Every creature whose
  controller is not its owner goes back to its owner, using `gainControl`.

**Not done:** Akroma's Will's header ("Choose one. If you control a commander as you cast this
spell, you may choose both."). `ModalDef.max` is fixed, so it needs a conditional maximum in the
combinations `legalActions` offers.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Tectonic Edge is not offered against three lands and is offered against five, its controller
  having one;
- the self-damage clause costs seat 0 two life for two creatures and seat 1 one;
- Homeward Path gives a stolen Bears back.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 4,581, all passing

Coverage: 11,096 of 31,653 cards (+3), 30,120 of 59,306 lines (+7). Staples: 185 of 244 (+2).

## D668 — the Will cycle: both modes while you control a commander

"Choose one. If you control a commander as you cast this spell, you may choose both" (Akroma's Will,
Jeska's Will, Kamahl's Will and about seven more). Staples went from 185 to 186: Akroma's Will.

- New field `ModalDef.maxWithCommander`.
- `modeCombinations` takes the state and the casting seat, and uses that maximum while the seat
  controls a commander on the battlefield.
- Both callers pass them, so the combination is checked as the spell is cast: the offer in
  `legalActions`, and the validation in `autoActions`.

- The modal header accepts the Will wording, with or without "instead", over exactly two modes.
- `grantedKeywordList` reads a list of up to four keywords ("flying, vigilance, and double strike").
- The team grant reads "… and protection from each color" at the end of its list as protection
  from all five colours, as Etched Champion stores it (D83).

the exiled cards this turn). Molten Collapse's "if you descended this turn" header and Disciple of

- without a commander out the Will offers [0] and [1] and refuses both; with one out it also offers

- cast with both modes, a Bears has all five keywords and protection from every colour.

## D669 — mana in words, three of any one colour, and mana by an opponent's hand

**Mana lines.**
- "Add six {G}" (Castle Garenbrig's body): a number word before one symbol is a sum of that many.
- "Add three mana of any one color" (Gilded Lotus, Jeweled Lotus's body): five answers of three
  each, never a mix, read as D665's runs.

**Refused on purpose: a mana cost together with a spending restriction.** Castle Garenbrig's
"{2}{G}{G}, {T}: Add six {G}. Spend this mana only to cast creature spells …" read on the first
pass. But restricted mana is made only by the automatic payer while it pays for something allowed,
and that payer never takes an ability that costs mana. The land would have read and never been
usable, so the line stays unread. A compile test pins this.

**Jeweled Lotus** stays unread for a different reason: "Spend this mana only to cast your commander"
needs the spell's commander status, and `SpendRestriction.allows` sees only type lines.

**Spell-side.** "Add {R} for each card in target opponent's hand" (Jeska's Will's first mode): the
targeted player's hand size as the spell resolves. A mode may now carry `makesMana`; the modal
reader drops that hint with its cost stated (the bot may undervalue a mana mode), where before it
refused the whole card. Jeska's Will now reads in full.

**Tests.**
- 3 engine tests:
  - "Add three {G}" shows and makes three;
  - "three mana of any one color" is exactly WWW/UUU/BBB/RRR/GGG, and the red one makes three red
    and nothing else;
  - the hand-count mode makes one red per card in the target's hand.
- 1 compile test: the Castle's costed, restricted line is unread.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 4,587, all passing

Coverage: 11,113 of 31,653 cards (+14), 30,153 of 59,306 lines (+25). Staples: 186 of 244.

## D670 — deck-construction keywords, and life for every player

**Chosen from a new view of the work queue.** I dumped every unread line (`VERBOSE=1`), took the
cards exactly one line short, and grouped them by that line. The tail is flat. Its biggest rows are
keyword declarations: Backup (16), Banding (10), Enlist, Assist and Devour (9 each), and the partner
family. "Partner" is on 110 lines, "Choose a Background" on 30, "Doctor's companion" on 27.

**Deck-construction keywords** ("Partner", "Partner—<kind>", "Choose a Background", "Doctor's
companion"):
- Each decides which second commander a deck may have and does nothing once the game starts.
- `customDeck`'s `partnersLegally` (D640) already enforces them.
- `compileCard` now counts the line compiled and emits nothing, like a printed keyword.
- "Partner with <name>" is not one of these: its reminder text is a real enter trigger (CR
  702.124j), so it stays unread.
- The bare "Friends forever" wording has no corpus lines, so it is not in the pattern; "Partner—
  Friends forever" is, through the "Partner—<kind>" arm.
- The D583 test that pinned Yasmin Khan's "Doctor's companion" as her one unread line now expects
  none.

**"Each player loses / gains N life"**: every living seat, the controller included. Before, only
"each opponent loses" read.

**Tests.**
- 1 engine test in a pod of three: a conceded seat is untouched, and the caster loses and gains
  with the rest.
- 5 compile tests: four deck-construction lines compile with no script, and "Partner with" stays
  unread.

Faults injected by hand: 3 of 3 caught.

## D671 — Backup N, with keyword abilities to hand on

Backup (CR 702.165): "When this creature enters, put N +1/+1 counters on target creature. If that's
another creature, it gains the following abilities until end of turn." It was the biggest solo
keyword in D670's list, on 16 cards one line short.

**What reads.** Backup, when every line after it is a printed keyword line: Deathtouch, Lifelink,
Vigilance, "Flying, first strike" and so on (about ten legal cards).
- The counters are the ordinary enter trigger, read by the line reader from the sentence the
  keyword stands for.
- The grant is added to that trigger's effect: the keywords, until end of turn, through `pump`.
  This happens only when the target is another creature on the battlefield, because "the following
  abilities" are already the creature's own.
- `printedKeywords`' whole-line rule decides "a keyword line": a list with one unknown word, such as
  "Flying, banding", comes back empty and refuses Backup. A first version also counted the parts
  itself; a fault run showed that check could never change the result, so it was removed.

**Not done:** Backup over a triggered or activated ability (Bola Slinger, Hangar Scrounger, the
Sacrifice-for-damage pair). Handing another creature a trigger until end of turn is a grant of
another kind (`grantedTriggers`), and it needs the following lines' fragments, which this loop has
not built yet when it reaches Backup.

**Tests.**
- 2 engine tests:
  - on another creature: two counters, flying and first strike this turn and not the next;
  - on itself: the counters only, and no extra effect made.
- 3 compile tests: read over Deathtouch; unread over a trigger, and over "Flying, banding".

Faults injected by hand: 2 of 2 caught (the redundant check is gone, not pinned).

    engine tests: 4,598, all passing

Coverage: 11,153 of 31,653 cards (+11), 30,312 of 59,306 lines (+11). Staples: 186 of 244.

## D672 — Transmute

"Transmute {1}{U}{B}" (CR 702.53): "{1}{U}{B}, Discard this card: Search your library for a card with
the same mana value as this card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle. Transmute only as
a sorcery." It was on 8 cards one line short in D670's list, 14 lines in all.

**How it reads.**
- An ability of the card in hand, built the way typecycling is: cost `{ mana, discardSelf: true }`,
  `sorcerySpeed`, a `searchYourLibrary` question and a move to hand.
- It is not marked `cycling`, because transmuting a card is not cycling it (CR 702.53 versus
  702.29f), so "whenever you cycle" does not fire.
- The mana value matched is the printed one of the card being transmuted, looked up by name among
  the card definitions.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- activated from hand, the card goes to the graveyard, and the search offers exactly the mana value
  3 cards (the Ogres and the other Transmuter, never a Bears or a land); the one picked goes to
  hand;
- it is not offered on the opponent's turn.

The first draft of the first test expected only the Ogres. The library's second Transmuter is also
mana value 3, so the engine was right and the test was corrected.

Faults injected by hand: 3 of 3 caught.

    engine tests: 4,600, all passing

Coverage: 11,161 of 31,653 cards (+8), 30,326 of 59,306 lines (+14). Staples: 186 of 244.

## D673 — embalm and eternalize, compiled

25 legal lines print "Embalm {cost}", "Eternalize {cost}" or "Eternalize—{cost}, Discard a card".

**Why this was cheap.** The engine has played both since the hand-written Sacred Cat and Angel of
Sanctions: `embalm` and `eternalize` build the graveyard ability, and `copyAsToken` makes the token
with a replaced type line, colour and (for eternalize) size. A line reader could not use them,
because they need the token's type line: the card's own, with Zombie put in front of its subtypes
(CR 702.128a, 702.129a). `compile.ts` has the card definition, so it builds that line, exports the
two helpers, and calls them.

**Corrections on the way.**
- The printed discard shape ends in a full stop ("Eternalize—{2}{W}{W}, Discard a card."). The first
  pattern refused it; Sunscourge Champion's agreement test found that.
- The test "counts a keyword with no builder apart from a sentence with no reader" used Angel
  of Sanctions' "Embalm {5}{W}" as its example. The Angel now reads whole, so the test uses a
  made-up card with a working enter trigger and Encore (still no builder), and also checks that the
  Angel has nothing unread.

**Tests.**
- 4 compile tests: Sacred Cat, Angel of Sanctions, Adorned Pouncer and Sunscourge Champion each
  compile their embalm or eternalize to the hand-written ability's description. Sunscourge's own
  "gain life equal to its power" line stays unread.
- 2 engine tests: embalm exiles the card and makes a white Zombie Cat with no mana cost that keeps
  lifelink; eternalize makes a black 4/4 Zombie Human Wizard.

Faults injected by hand: 3 of 3 caught.

    engine tests: 4,606, all passing

Coverage: 11,176 of 31,653 cards (+15), 30,353 of 59,306 lines (+27). Staples: 186 of 244.

## D674 — Offspring

"Offspring {N}" (CR 702.175): "You may pay an additional {N} as you cast this spell. If you do, when
this creature enters, create a 1/1 token copy of it." It is on 20 legal lines, 10 of them a card's
only unread line.

**Kicker's machinery, which is what it is.**
- The optional extra cost is `CardScript.kicker`, described as "Offspring {N}". A kicked cast already
  records `KICKED` on the permanent as it arrives (D561).
- The payoff is the card's own enter trigger. Its event shape is taken from the line reader, not
  written by hand; it is conditioned on that record and calls `copyAsToken` with a 1/1 printed-size
  profile, the way eternalize gets its 4/4.
- The token copy has the keyword too, but it was not cast, so it makes no token of its own.

**Known gap, stated:** if the creature leaves the battlefield before the trigger resolves, no token
is made. The rules would make the copy from last-known information.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- paid: the creature plus one 1/1 token copy that keeps vigilance;
- not paid: the creature alone.

Faults injected by hand: 3 of 3 caught.

    engine tests: 4,608, all passing

Coverage: 11,186 of 31,653 cards (+10), 30,373 of 59,306 lines (+20). Staples: 186 of 244.

## D675 — Entwine

"Entwine {2} (Choose both if you pay the entwine cost.)" (CR 702.42), under a "Choose one —" list. It
is on 30 legal lines, 13 of them a card's only unread line.

**How it is built.**
- **Compiler.**
  - `spellScriptFor`'s keyword loop no longer takes an Entwine line out of a modal spell's
    resolution. Before, it filed the line as an unimplemented keyword before the modal reader saw
    it.
  - `modalScriptFor` reads a trailing "Entwine {cost}" (mana only) over two or more modes. It returns
    the modal with `entwine: true`, plus a `kicker` carrying the cost, described "Entwine {cost}".
- **Engine.**
  - `modeCombinations` takes `kicked`. An entwine spell cast kicked has exactly one combination:
    every mode.
  - `autoActions` passes the action's `kicked` when it validates the modes, and already charges a
    kicker's cost.
  - `legalActions`' modal branch offers one more row, kicked and with every mode, only when the
    printed cost plus the entwine cost is affordable (it previously left kicker out of modal spells
    entirely).

**Not done:** non-mana entwine ("Entwine—Sacrifice three lands", Betrayal of Flesh).

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- with one land the spell offers each mode alone; with three it also offers both, kicked;
- unpaid both is refused, paid one alone is refused, and entwined it gains 5 life and draws a card
  with three lands tapped.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 4,610, all passing

Coverage: 11,199 of 31,653 cards (+13), 30,386 of 59,306 lines (+13). Staples: 186 of 244.

## D678 — Esper Sentinel: the first noncreature spell, and a price that is its power

"Whenever an opponent casts their first noncreature spell each turn, draw a card unless that player
pays {X}, where X is Esper Sentinel's power." Staples went from 190 to 191.

**The first of a kind.** "Your first / second spell each turn" (D436) counts every spell the caster
casts. The Sentinel counts noncreature spells only, so a creature cast first does not use it up.
- New field `GameState.spellsCastThisTurnByKind`, keyed `<seat>:creature` and `<seat>:noncreature`.
  It is a separate map because the werewolf conditions iterate `spellsCastThisTurnBy`'s values and
  must see only seats. It is optional (absent counts as zero) and cleared with the rest at each
  turn.
- `countCast` takes the spell's kind. The cast event carries `kindNth` beside `nth`, and a face-down
  morph counts as a creature.
- The trigger's script field is `nthOfKind` (the question) and the event's is `kindNth` (the answer):
  two names for the two directions, as `onNth` and `nth` are.
- New prologue: "Whenever an opponent casts their first noncreature spell each turn".

**The price.** `punisherEffect` reads "… unless that player pays {X}, where X is ~'s power".
- The decision is a function spec, so the price is the source's live power when the question is
  asked; a power below 0 asks for {0}.
- A caster who cannot afford it is not asked, and the card is drawn.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- a creature, then a noncreature spell, then another: only the second draws, the third does not
  trigger;
- the count starts afresh on the opponent's next turn;
- with a land the caster is asked "Pay {1}", and paying stops the draw.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught. One survivor (the per-turn reset) was pinned by the
next-turn test.

    engine tests: 4,617, all passing

Coverage: 11,215 of 31,653 cards (+1), 30,407 of 59,306 lines (+2). Staples: 191 of 244 (+1).

## D679 — "When ~ enters untapped"

Mystic Sanctuary and its cycle: "When this land enters untapped, you may put target instant or
sorcery card from your graveyard on top of your library." Staples went from 191 to 192.

"Enters untapped" is a fact about the arrival, not an intervening-if. A `TriggerDef.condition` is
asked twice (as the trigger fires and as it resolves), so a land tapped for mana in response would
lose its trigger. The fact therefore goes on the event instead:
- the engine sets `subjectTapped` on an entry event, from the instance as it arrived;
- the etb event takes `untapped: true`, compared once, at match time;
- a new prologue reads "When ~ enters untapped, …".

The D587 test that pinned the Sanctuary's trigger line as its one unread line now expects none.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- beside three other Islands the land enters untapped, and the trigger puts the instant from the
  graveyard on top of the library;
- beside one Island it enters tapped and nothing goes on the stack.

Faults injected by hand: 2 of 2 caught.

    engine tests: 4,619, all passing

Coverage: 11,220 of 31,653 cards (+5), 30,412 of 59,306 lines (+5). Staples: 192 of 244 (+1).

## D681 — Fellwar Stone and Exotic Orchard

"{T}: Add one mana of any color that a land an opponent controls could produce." These are read the
way Command Tower is (D617): one ability per colour, each with an `activateOnlyIf`.
`opponentLandColours(state, seat)` in fromCardData.ts answers which colours are possible, following
CR 106.7:
- every land the seat's opponents control counts, tapped or not;
- its script abilities count, and so does the mana its current basic land types give it (a land
  another effect made a Swamp counts for black);
- each land's own colour restriction still holds, so an opponent's Command Tower counts only for
  its own commander's colours;
- abilities of the same kind are ignored, so two Orchards facing each other make nothing;
- colourless is not a colour.

The answer is cached per state object.

- the line reads whole on a land and on an artifact;

  and U;

  lands, or from a table with no opposing land;
- an opponent's Tower counts for its own commander's colours only.

## D682 — "for each permanent destroyed this way", and Gamble

Bane of Progress: "When ~ enters, destroy all artifacts and enchantments. Put a +1/+1 counter on ~
for each permanent destroyed this way." Also the sweepers that gain or lose life, or draw, "for each
creature destroyed this way".

How it is read:
- `clausesOf` glues a "destroy all …" sentence to a following sentence that counts "destroyed this
  way", using ';'. A "can't be regenerated" rider is left out.
- `readEffect` runs the destroy, then gives the second sentence
  `EffectContext.destroyedThisWay`: the card types of each permanent that left the battlefield.
  Indestructible or regenerated permanents are therefore not counted.
- The count phrase "(creature|permanent|artifact|enchantment|planeswalker|land)(s) destroyed this
  way" is read only inside that glue. Anywhere else it would silently count zero.
- The second sentence keeps its immediate reading, so a draw can follow.

Two more readers came with it:
- `selfEffect` reads "put N +1/+1 counters on ~ for each <count>", with the printed number as a
  rate.
- Gamble: "put that card into your hand, discard a card at random, then shuffle" is the same spell
  with the shuffle first, because the shuffle touches only the library.

Staples went from 194 to 196 (Bane of Progress, Gamble).

**Tests.** 7 engine tests:
- every line reads, and a lone "destroyed this way" stays unread;
- Bane counts 3 across both sides, with an indestructible survivor not counted;
- a creature sweep gains 2 life for each of 3 creatures;
- an artifact sweep counts only the artifact creature among what it destroyed;
- the draw counts, including zero;
- the printed counter number is a rate (two counters for each of 2 creatures is 4);
- Gamble discards one card at random from the hand plus the found card.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught.

    engine tests: 4,633, all passing

Coverage: 11,242 of 31,653 cards (+11), 30,440 of 59,306 lines (+13). Staples: 196 of 244 (+2).

How it is read: `revealKeepGroup` sits beside `digGroup` in the composition loop. Nothing is chosen,
so it is an effect and not a question:

The filter is either of:
- card types, read by `graveyardTypeTest` ("creature and land" means either);

  are still what gets reported.

  and flashback's exile still wins.

## D688 — "Creature spells you control can't be countered"

The new `CardScript.spellsCantBeCountered {whose: 'you' | 'all', kind?}`, read in `staticFromLine`
from:
- "(Creature |Noncreature )spells (you control) can't be countered." — Rhythm of the Wild, Prowling
  Serpopard, Allosaurus Shepherd's kin.

How it is enforced:
- `counterSpell` is the one place every counter goes through (scripted counters, ward, the bot). It
  now asks `protectedFromCounters`: does a permanent on the battlefield say so, with "you control"
  meaning the spell's controller, and the kind read from the spell's printed type line?
- A face-down permanent, or one that has lost its abilities, says nothing.
- effects.ts cannot import derive.ts: the import closes a cycle that left scripts.ts reading
  constants before they existed. So derive.ts hands its lookup in as it loads (`useScriptLookup`).
- The mechanic-coverage test lists the field as compiler-only, with a note.

Rhythm of the Wild's second line (granting riot) stays unread.

- both lines read;
- under Rhythm, your creature spell resolves through a counter, while your sorcery and the
  opponent's creature are countered;
- "Spells can't be countered" protects both seats' spells of every kind.

## D689 — a draw at the beginning of the next upkeep

"Draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep." ends 40-odd Mirage and Ice Age spells.
"At the beginning of your next upkeep, <effect>" is its sibling.

How it is read: `spellScriptFor` takes the final sentence off the last resolution line and reads its
body. Provided the body does not target (the spell's targets are gone by then), it becomes a
one-shot `delayed` upkeep trigger appended to the card's `triggers`:
- "the next turn's" upkeep is `of: 'any'`;
- "your next" upkeep is `of: 'you'`.

`withLaterTrigger` wraps the rest of the resolution so the trigger is scheduled once it has
resolved.

A compiled card's trigger index is not known while one line is read (unearth's problem), so the
effect finds the trigger at run time. It looks in the script the card plays by, through effects.ts's
new `scriptOfCard` (the lookup D688 injected), by identity or by description.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- both spells read, each with one delayed trigger;
- "the next turn's upkeep" draws nothing at once, one card on the opponent's upkeep, and never
  again;
- "your next upkeep" waits for your own turn.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught (not one-shot, always "any" seat, never scheduled, trigger
not on the card).

    engine tests: 4,657, all passing

Coverage: 11,298 of 31,653 cards (+17), 30,525 of 59,306 lines (+34). Staples: 203 of 244.

## D690 — the Pacts: pay at your next upkeep or lose the game

"At the beginning of your next upkeep, pay {3}{U}{U}. If you don't, you lose the game." Pact of

Changes:
- D689's delayed reader takes a final line that is entirely "At the beginning of your next upkeep,
  …" whole, with all its sentences.
- `clausesOf` holds "pay {cost}. If you don't, you lose the game" together as "pay {cost} or lose
  the game".
- `readEffect` reads that as one controller question with the price on the paying answer
  (`payIfChosen`). The engine offers "Pay" only when it is affordable and pays it on the answer. The
  bot's `best` always pays.
- Not paying calls the new `loseTheGame`, which eliminates the seat with the new `EliminatedReason`
  `'effect'` (CR 104.3a). The engine's elimination pass then removes the seat's cards.
- The web labels it "out (a card's effect)".

## D691 — a pitch cost: exile a card of the colour instead of the mana

"You may exile a blue card from your hand rather than pay this spell's mana cost." Force of Will
("pay 1 life and …"), Force of Negation ("If it's not your turn, …"), Snapback, Unmask, Vine Dryad,
and the other one-card pitches.

What was added:
- `CardScript.pitch {colour, life?, notYourTurn?}`, read by `pitchFromLine` beside the
  additional-cost reader. A two-card pitch is refused.
- `legalActions` offers a seventh alternative cast, `pitchCast`, at {0}. It is offered while another
  card of the colour is in hand (`pitchOptions`), the life can be paid without ending the game, and,
  for `notYourTurn`, it is not the caster's turn. The choices travel as the play's `discardOptions`
  with `pitchWords`.
- `autoActions` validates the flag with the other alternative costs. The chosen card arrives as
  `discarded` but is held apart from the discard cost, and is **exiled** as the cost is paid, along
  with the life.
- The bot sends `pitchCast` and picks the card the way it picks any discard.
- The web copies the flag and asks "tap a blue card in your hand to exile".
- The mechanic-coverage test lists `script pitch` as compiler-only, with a note.

- it is not offered without another blue card and refuses a red one;

  aim at) it is not offered and is refused;
- the web wording.

## D692 — Mana Drain: colourless mana at your next main phase

spell's mana value."

D689's delayed reader takes one more shape. It is about the spell's target, so:
- `withLaterTrigger` schedules with the first card target as the delayed trigger's subject. The card
  is in the graveyard by then and its object is pinned there (CR 400.7).
- The mana is the subject's printed mana value in {C}.
- "Your next main phase" is chosen when the trigger is scheduled (`nextMainPhase`): this turn's
  postcombat main if the caster's own precombat main or combat is under way, otherwise the
  precombat main of their next turn.

- A spell with no card target leaves the sentence unread.

- countering the opponent's three-drop gives {C}{C}{C} at my next precombat main;

## D693 — an ability word's upgrade: "… instead if …"

"Threshold — Add {B}{B}{B}{B}{B} instead if there are seven or more cards in your graveyard." (Cabal
Ritual). Also Morbid, Metalcraft, Hellbent, Ferocious, Delirium and Raid upgrades on about forty
spells.

How it is read: when a spell's resolution is exactly two lines and the second is "<ability word> —
<effect> instead if <condition>", `insteadIfUpgrade` reads it as follows:
- the condition through `interveningConditionFor`;
- the first line alone;
- the second line rewritten onto the first line's target. "That creature / player / spell / …"
  becomes the first line's "target …" phrase (`TARGET_PHRASE`), and a bare "~ deals N damage" takes
  the first line's destination.

Both readings must ask for the same targets in the same order, and neither may ask a question. The
spell then runs whichever one the condition picks as it resolves. Spell flags (`makesMana`) are
merged.

Staples went from 207 to 208 (Cabal Ritual).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- three upgrades read, while Epicenter (different targets, unreadable second line) and a readable
  second line that drops the target both stay unread;
- Cabal Ritual adds three black with six cards in the graveyard and five with seven;
- Hellbent deals 3 with a card in hand and 5 with none;
- Metalcraft pumps the same creature +4/+4 with three artifacts and +2/+2 with one.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught. The target-equality fault survived at first; it was pinned
with a readable second line that points elsewhere.

    engine tests: 4,671, all passing

## D696 — "Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step"

109 legal lines end with "Sacrifice it / Exile it / … them / … that token at the beginning of the
next end step": Kiki-Jiki, Sneak Attack, Mimic Vat, and the hasty token makers.

What was added:
- **An engine-known delayed ability.** `DelayedTrigger.builtin` and `StackObject.builtin`
  ('sacrifice' | 'exile') sit beside the card-script ones, with `abilityIndex` -1. `fireDelayed`
  marks the stack object, and `abilityOrTrigger` answers it from `BUILTIN_DELAYED` before any script
  is consulted. It goes on the stack like any trigger (CR 603.7). It acts only on its subject, still
  on the battlefield as the same object (CR 400.7, the existing `subjectSeq` pin).
- **The rider.** `clausesOf` joins it to the sentence before, which must create or put something,
  with an optional "It gains haste (until end of turn)." between them. `readEffect` reads the first
  sentence as before. Whatever its effect added to the battlefield gets haste, where printed, and one
  delayed ability each at the next end step.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- three cards read;
- Kiki-Jiki's copy has haste and is sacrificed at the end step, leaving the original and Kiki;
- Sneak Attack's Titan has haste and is in the graveyard after the end step;
- a spell's two Goblins are each scheduled for exile and are gone after the end step, while the Bear
  already on the battlefield is not touched.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught.

    engine tests: 4,682, all passing

Coverage: 11,361 of 31,653 cards (+21), 30,655 of 59,306 lines (+35). Staples: 209 of 244.

## D697 — Jeweled Lotus, and "three mana of any one color" for the auto-tapper

Two parts:

**"Spend this mana only to cast your commander"** (Jeweled Lotus). It is a new `spendRestriction`
phrase. `PaymentFor` gains `commander`, set from the casting card's `isCommander`. It is filled
where a spell's restricted sources are asked for (`payingFor` in legalActions) and where the cast is
paid (autoActions).

**A defect from D669, found while testing it.** "Add three mana of any one color" is five abilities
of three mana each. `manaSources` collapses several rows on one permanent into a single "choose one"
source, and sized that source at **one** mana. So Gilded Lotus paid for one mana in auto-pay, and a
Jeweled Lotus (restricted, so never pressed by hand) could pay for nothing. The fix:
- rows that are each a single-colour run of the same length now become one source with the new
  `ManaSource.chooseRun`;
- `solveTap` sizes it at the run's length and adds the whole run of the colour it picks;
- the source keeps `restricted` when every row is restricted, so mana the payment does not use is
  lost (D595).

Staples went from 209 to 210 (Jeweled Lotus).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the Lotus reads;
- it pays for the commander and refuses a non-commander of the same cost;
- a Gilded Lotus alone pays a three-mana spell;
- for a generic three, the Lotus is tapped and the Forest beside it is not;
- a two-mana commander paid with the Lotus leaves nothing floating.

Faults injected by hand: 7 of 7 caught. The sizing and restricted-flag faults survived at first and
were pinned by the last two tests.

    engine tests: 4,687, all passing

Coverage: 11,362 of 31,653 cards (+1), 30,656 of 59,306 lines (+1). Staples: 210 of 244 (+1).

## D700 — an offered cast pays the offer's own cost, X included

Sweep 56101 threw: "Welcome to the Fold has no X to choose". The card is printed {2}{U}{U} with
Madness {X}{U}{U}.
