  (D460).
- `autoActions` checked X against the **printed** cost on every offered cast, so it refused the X
  the table had just offered.

The fix: an offer with a cost of its own (madness, miracle) is now that cost for the X check. An
empty offer (cascade) still reads the printed cost, as D460 intended. The defect predates this
session's increments; it surfaced because seed 56101 dealt this card.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- an offer of {X}{U} on a card printed without X offers X up to 2 and the cast takes X=2;
- an empty offer still refuses an X.

Seed 56101 now finishes.

Faults injected by hand: 1 of 1 caught (the old printed-cost reading).

## D708 — A free cast from your hand

"You may cast a spell with mana value N or less from your hand without paying its mana cost": the
Expertise cycle, Omnispell Adept ("an instant or sorcery spell"), Maelstrom Archangel ("a spell"),
and the same clause anywhere else an effect prints it.

How it is read:
- A question about the hand: up to one card, filtered by kind and mana value.
  - The kinds are "a spell", "an instant or sorcery spell", "a noncreature spell", "a permanent
    spell" and "a creature spell".
  - Lands are never offered.
- The chosen card then gets cascade's `pendingOfferedCast` with nothing to pay, and `stays` as a
  miracle's does: declined, it stays in hand.
- Choosing nothing is the "may".
- The bot's `pick` takes the dearest eligible card. Without it, the bot answered every optional hand
  question with nothing and wasted the card.
- Not read yet: "mana value X or less" (Electrodominance) and "equal or lesser mana value"
  (Reinterpret, Press the Enemy), which need a number this clause does not have.

Staples went from 220 to 221 (Rishkar's Expertise).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the Expertise and the Adept read;
- the draw happens first, only a nonland spell within the limit is offered, the bot picks it and
  takes the offer, and it resolves with no mana on the board;
- choosing nothing, or declining the offer, leaves the card in hand;
- the Adept's ability offers only instants and sorceries with no mana value limit, and the bot
  takes the dearer one.

## D709 — Myriad Landscape: basic land cards that share a land type

"Search your library for up to two basic land cards that share a land type, put them onto the
battlefield tapped, then shuffle."

How it is read:
- A basic land card has one basic land type, so "share a land type" means "all of one type".
- The type is asked first. Only the types the library's basic land cards have are offered, with all
  five as the fallback for an empty library.
- Then come five library questions, one per type, each asked only if its type was the answer
  (`askOnlyIfChosen`). Their answers are merged and handed to the plain search's effect.
- No engine change was needed.
- The bot's `best` is the type the library holds most of.

Also a D706 follow-up. The D706 break run left one fault uncaught: the plain "Whenever you create a
token" shape counting an opponent's tokens. No test covered that shape, because the hand-run
faults hit only the Mirkwood Bats shape. A new test (Test Witness: yours count, an opponent's do
not) pins it, and that fault was confirmed caught.

Staples went from 221 to 222 (Myriad Landscape).

**Tests.** 3 engine tests for Myriad Landscape, plus the D706 pin:
- the card reads;
- the type question offers the library's types and the bot answers the commonest;
- only that type is offered as up to two, a mixed pair is refused, and the two enter tapped;
- finding nothing is allowed.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught, including the D706 one.

    engine tests: 4,724, all passing

Coverage: 11,389 of 31,653 cards (+1), 30,689 of 59,306 lines (+1). Staples: 222 of 244 (+1).

## D710 — Victimize: sacrifice a creature, and if you do, two back

"Choose two target creature cards in your graveyard. Sacrifice a creature. If you do, return the
chosen cards to the battlefield tapped."

How it is read:
- **The plural reanimation.** "Return two target creature cards from your graveyard to the
  battlefield [tapped]" is the plural return to hand's targets (`TARGET_QUANTIFIER_PREFIX`), each
  put onto the battlefield under the caster's control.
- **The glue.** `clausesOf` joins Victimize's three sentences into "sacrifice a creature and if you
  do return two target creature cards from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped".
- **The composite.** That clause has the return's targets and the sacrifice's question. The return
  runs only if the chosen creature has in fact left the battlefield. With no creature to sacrifice
  there is no answer, and nothing returns.
- A single creature is a forced answer, so the engine answers it.

Staples went from 222 to 223 (Victimize).

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card and the plural return each read;
- the sacrifice question offers creatures only, then both targets return tapped under the caster;
- with no creature to sacrifice nothing returns.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 4,727, all passing

Coverage: 11,391 of 31,653 cards (+2), 30,692 of 59,306 lines (+3). Staples: 223 of 244 (+1).

## D711 — Rhythm of the Wild: "Nontoken creatures you control have riot"

How it is read:
- A new script field, `grantsRiot`, is set by the line.
- `scriptOnStack` hands a nontoken creature spell riot's question and its `entersChoice: 'riot'`
  (the exported `RIOT` piece) while its controller controls an untouched permanent with
  `grantsRiot`. Both the question at resolution and the counter or haste on arrival then come from
  the existing riot code.
- **Not granted:**
  - to a copy (it would be a token);
  - to a spell that already asks a question, or already has riot;
  - to a card the engine cannot play.
- A vanilla creature has no script, and the grant gives it an empty one to carry the question.
- **Limitation.** A creature put onto the battlefield without being cast is asked nothing. Riot's
  question belongs to a resolving spell: D559's limitation, unchanged.

Staples went from 223 to 224 (Rhythm of the Wild).

**Tests.** 3 engine tests, plus the mechanic-coverage entry:
- the card reads;
- a creature cast under it is asked, and enters with a +1/+1 counter or with haste;
- no question without it (another permanent instead), under an opponent's, or for a sorcery.

The D559 refusal row for "Nontoken creatures you control have riot." is retired, since the line
now reads.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught. The fifth (any permanent grants) was caught only after the
"without it" case was given a Forest on the battlefield.

## D712 — Choosing new targets for a spell: Deflecting Swat, Bolt Bend

**"You may choose new targets for target spell or ability"** (Deflecting Swat, Redirect):
- The target is a spell or ability with one target and somewhere else for it to go
  (`redirectable`, as Willbender's).
- The new target is asked as the spell resolves, with the copy effects' `TargetDecisionSpec`
  pointed at the target rather than at a copy.
- `retarget` applies it, and keeps the old target if the new one is not legal for that object.
- Declining is an answer.
- Not offered: a spell or ability with several targets, since choosing new targets for each is a
  question the engine has no shape for.

**"Change the target of target spell or ability with a single target"** (Bolt Bend, Misdirection,
and the printed text of the hand-written Willbender and Swerve):
- Read exactly as those two are written: the spell and where it goes are both targets chosen as it
  is cast, and the effect is `redirect`.
- An earlier draft asked the new target at resolution with a non-declinable question. It gave
  Willbender and Swerve a compiled reading that disagreed with the written one (a new
  compiled-vs-written row). The table's rule is to settle such a row, not add it, and 29 tests plus
  the play-table help describe the cast-time flow. So the compiled reading takes the written shape,
  and the draft's engine and bot changes for a mandatory re-aim were reverted unused.

**Also:** `soleTargetSpecOf` looked spells up only in the hand-written registry, so a **compiled**
spell or ability could not be redirected at all, by these or by Willbender. It now uses the
injected `scriptOfCard` with the registry as fallback, which closes the gap D485 left documented.

`compile.test.ts`'s partly-read example card moves from Willbender (now fully read) to Dragonsguard
Elite. Sigarda was tried first, but its read lines are only printed keywords, so its source is
`printed-only`.

Staples went from 224 to 225 (Deflecting Swat).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- both cards read;
- a compiled Bolt is re-aimed at the opponent by the "may" question;
- declining leaves it where it was;
- "change" takes both targets at cast, with no question, and agrees with the hand-written shape;
- a spell with no target cannot be chosen.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 4,734, all passing

Coverage: 11,400 of 31,653 cards (+8), 30,702 of 59,306 lines (+8). Staples: 225 of 244 (+1).

## D715 — "If this spell was cast from a graveyard": Sevinne's Reclamation and the flashback upgrades

How it is read:
- `EffectContext.resolving` carries the spell's own stack object while it resolves.
- `castFromAGraveyard` reads `resolving.castFrom === 'graveyard'`, which every graveyard cast
  records. It is never true for a copy, which was not cast (CR 707.10).
- The condition is also an intervening-condition row, so "… instead if this spell was cast from a
  graveyard" reads.
- **"X instead."** "If this spell was cast from a graveyard, X instead." as the last sentence of a
  one-line spell is turned around into D693's "X instead if …" second line, and read by
  `insteadIfUpgrade` (Plunder the Trollshaws).
- **An added effect.** "If this spell was cast from a graveyard, <effect>." runs the effect only
  then. One that asks or targets is refused, since it would be asked either way.
- **Sevinne's Reclamation.** "…, you may copy this spell and may choose a new target for the copy":
  - The new target is asked as the spell resolves, about the spell itself, and only when a copy will
    be made.
  - The effect puts the popped object back for `copySpellOnStack` and takes it off again.
  - The copy goes on top and resolves next.
- **Still unread in the family.** Increasing Devotion, Increasing Savagery, Secrets of the Key,
  Increasing Confusion and Ruthless Negotiation fail on their own wording or targets, not on the
  condition.

Staples went from 227 to 228 (Sevinne's Reclamation).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- both cards read;
- cast with flashback, Sevinne's returns the Bear, asks for the copy's target, and the copy returns
  the Relic and copies nothing;
- cast from hand, nothing is asked or copied;
- Plunder draws one from hand and two with flashback.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught. "A copy copies itself" was caught only after the test
checked the stack right after the copy resolved: the extra copy otherwise fizzles silently.

## D716 — Glacial Chasm: life upkeep, no attacking, and no damage to you

How it is read:
- **"Cumulative upkeep—Pay 2 life."** The keyword's age counter and climb, priced in life
  (`cumulativeUpkeepLifeTrigger`, and `cumulativeUpkeep.life` on the script):
  - "Pay N life" is offered only when the life total covers it (CR 119.4), so a player who cannot
    pay sacrifices;
  - paying is `loseLife`;
  - the bot pays while it would be left on 5 or more.
- **"Creatures you control can't attack."** Also "can't block", "can't attack or block", and the
  "other creatures" forms: a static on your creatures with `cantAttack` and/or `cantBlock`. With
  nothing able to attack, the engine skips the declaration.
- **"Prevent all damage that would be dealt to you."** A new script field, `preventsDamageToYou`.
  `dealDamage` prevents damage to the controller of an untouched such permanent before anything
  else reads it: no life lost, no commander damage, no lifelink. Their permanents still take
  damage.

## D717 — Chrome Mox: an imprint from hand, and mana of the exiled card's colours

"Imprint — When Chrome Mox enters, you may exile a nonartifact, nonland card from your hand.
{T}: Add one mana of any of the exiled card's colors."

How it is read:
- **The imprint.** "You may exile a(n) <card> from your hand" is a new clause reader. It asks a
  question about the hand, up to one card; choosing none is the "may". The card chosen is exiled
  and linked to the permanent that exiled it (`CardInstance.imprintedOn`, CR 607.2a). "Imprint —"
  is already stripped as an ability word.
- **The link is to the object, not the card.** It records the Mox's id and its `objectSeq`, so a
  Mox that leaves and comes back has no imprint (CR 400.7). `relocate` clears it when the exiled
  card itself changes zone.
- **The mana.** "One mana of any of the exiled card's colors" reads as five colour abilities, each
  offered only while an imprinted card has that colour (`imprintedColours`). It is taken only by
  the line-by-line reader, as "the chosen color" is (D642), so a card can't be read as having it
  without the line that gives it a card. A colourless imprint makes nothing.
- **"Non" in a card filter.** `cardWordMatch` now reads a `non` prefix as the negation of the word
  ("nonland", "nonartifact"). A comma list made only of "non" words with no "or" is one card that
  is all of them, not a list of alternatives. Guardian Sunmare's "a nonland permanent card with
  mana value 3 or less" reads as a result. Its case in `compile.test.ts` was moved from the unread
  list to the read list.
- **The bot** imprints its dearest coloured card. It never picks a colourless one, which would make
  no mana.
- The same reader takes Isochron Scepter's and Spellbinder's imprint lines ("an instant card with
  mana value 2 or less"). Neither card is finished: "copy the exiled card" doesn't read yet.

Staples went from 229 to 230 (Chrome Mox).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- only nonartifact, nonland cards are offered (the artifact and the land are not), and the Mox
  makes exactly the exiled card's colours: green or white for a green-white creature, red refused;
- with nothing exiled it makes no mana; a Mox bounced and recast has no imprint; and an imprinted
  card that leaves exile and comes straight back no longer counts;
- the bot imprints the dearest coloured card.

Faults injected by script: 8 of 9 caught. The miss, `relocate` keeping the link on a card that left
exile, is pinned by the third test's last case. Re-run: 1 of 1 caught.

How it is read:

  (goad's duration). `playerProtected` is read in two places:

    (attachments aside);
  - `dealDamage` prevents damage to them (CR 702.16b, e).

  counters on the source, read live. That makes "put a burden counter on it, then draw a card for
  each burden counter" count the counter just added. It also reads the upkeep drain, and lines on
  27 cards in all.

    Chasm Skulker test caught: its Squids are counted from the counters it died with.
- **Teferi's Protection** still needs "your life total can't change" and phasing out. The
  protection half is ready for it.

## D719 — Necropotence: no draw step, discards exiled, and a card for 1 life

"Skip your draw step. Whenever you discard a card, exile that card from your graveyard. Pay 1 life:
Exile the top card of your library face down. Put that card into your hand at the beginning of your
next end step."

How it is read:
- **"Skip your draw step."** A new script field, `skipsDrawStep`. While its controller has the
  permanent face up and with its abilities, `advanceStep` goes from upkeep straight to the main
  phase. The draw step doesn't happen at all (CR 614.10): no draw, no priority in it, and nothing
  that triggers "at the beginning of your draw step". The phrase is printed on 15 legal cards (Damia, Solitary
  Confinement, Necrodominance's first line and others).
- **The discard trigger.** The `discards` event now carries the card discarded as its subject, and
  hands it to the ability on the stack. A new clause, "exile that card from your graveyard", exiles
  the subject while it is still in its controller's graveyard.
- **The life ability.** Its two sentences are read as one effect, as impulse draw's are (D583). The
  top card is exiled face down, so only its owner can see it (`view.ts` already hides a face-down
  card in exile). A third engine-known delayed ability, `to-hand`, joins D696's `sacrifice` and
  `exile`. It puts the card into its owner's hand at the beginning of the controller's next end
  step, on the stack like any other trigger. It finds nothing if the card has left exile in the
  meantime (CR 400.7).
- **The bot.** A first probe had the bot pay 19 life in one main phase: a card that arrives later
  scores nothing in its search, and the activation was always legal. The ability now carries
  `buysNothingIf`. It is spent once the bot would drop below 10 life, or once it already has a card
  coming (waiting, or still on the stack) for each 2 life above 10, up to 5 at a time.

Staples went from 231 to 232 (Necropotence).

**Tests.** 6 engine tests, plus the mechanic-coverage entry for `skipsDrawStep`:
- the card reads;
- the draw step is skipped, with no draw and no "beginning of your draw step" trigger, while an
  opponent's Necropotence skips nothing of yours;
- a card its controller discards is exiled, and without Necropotence it stays in the graveyard;
- paying 1 life exiles the top card face down, visible to its owner and not to the opponent, and
  puts it into hand at the next end step, face up;
- a card that left exile first is not fetched back;
- the bot takes between 1 and 5 cards in a main phase and stays at 10 life or more.

Faults injected by script: 11 of 12 caught. The twelfth, the `to-hand` ability's "only from exile"
guard, isn't observable: a card that leaves exile is a new object, so `fireDelayed` already
withholds the subject before the guard is reached. It is kept because the ability means a card in
exile.

    engine tests: 4,764, all passing

## D720 — "Search your library and/or graveyard": Finale of Devastation

"Search your library and/or graveyard for a creature card with mana value X or less and put it onto
the battlefield. If you search your library this way, shuffle. If X is 10 or more, creatures you
control get +X/+X and gain haste until end of turn."

How it is read:
- **Two zones.** Read as Myriad Landscape's search is (D709): the zone is asked first ("Library" or
  "Graveyard"), then one question in that zone, each asked only if its zone was the answer
  (`askOnlyIfChosen`). The plain search does the rest, so the filter, the X bound (D686) and the
  destination are ones it already reads. Hand or battlefield, with or without "reveal it", and
  "you may".
- **"If you search your library this way, shuffle."** `clausesOf` folds it away. A library question
  already shuffles as it is answered (CR 701.19e), and only when the library is the zone searched,
  which is exactly what the sentence says.
- **Simplification, recorded.** The rules let a player look through both zones and then take one
  card from either. Here the zone is chosen first. The graveyard is public, so the only thing lost
  is looking through the library and then settling for a graveyard card.
- **"+X/+X" with no "where X is".** The team-pump-by-a-count reader (D666) now takes it as the X the
  spell was cast with.
- **"If X is N or more, …".** A new condition in front of an effect. The effect runs only when the
  spell's X is at least N. It isn't taken in front of an effect that asks a question or chooses a
  target, for the reason the cast-from-a-graveyard condition gives (D715).
- **The bot** searches its library, and its graveyard only when its library has no card the search
  could find.
- Delivery Moogle reads whole as well. Sanctum of All's and Runeforge Champion's search lines now
  read, though each card has another line that doesn't. Most of the family, 18 legal lines, names
  another card ("a card named Command Tower"), which no filter here reads yet.

Staples went from 232 to 233 (Finale of Devastation).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- Finale and Delivery Moogle read;
- the zone is asked first, and the library offers only creatures with mana value X or less, while
  the graveyard is left alone;
- the graveyard is searched with the same bound;
- with X of 10 the team gets +X/+X and haste, and with X of 9 nothing;
- the bot searches its library, or its graveyard when the library has nothing to find.

Faults injected by script: 8 of 8 caught. The first attempt at this run was cut short by a worker

## D721 — Sylvan Library, and a step of the effect between two questions

"At the beginning of your draw step, you may draw two additional cards. If you do, choose two cards
in your hand drawn this turn. For each of those cards, pay 4 life or put the card on top of your
library."

**The infrastructure: `CardsDecisionSpec.onReach`.** A card's answers were applied together by the
effect at the end. That is right for "each player sacrifices a creature", and it is why Sylvan
Library could not be read: it draws between its two questions, and the second question is about
what was drawn. `onReach` is a step of the effect that runs as the plan reaches that question,
before it is asked, and only if the question isn't skipped (`askOnlyIfChosen`, `askOnlyIf`).
`askOrFinish` reaches each plan entry once, so the step runs once. A resumed resolution starts after
the answered entry. The same hook is what a reveal-then-split card (Fact or Fiction) needs.

**"Drawn this turn": `CardInstance.drawnTurn`.** `drawFromLibrary` stamps it, and `relocate`
clears it when the card changes zone again. Only a card still in the hand it was drawn into
carries it.

How the card is read:
- `clausesOf` joins the three sentences into one clause.
- The first question is the "may". The second is asked only on a yes: it draws the two cards as it
  is reached, then asks which cards drawn this turn go back on top. The turn's own draw counts, as
  printed: it is drained before the trigger resolves.
- The two picks are folded into one. Choosing two cards and then, for each, paying 4 life or
  putting it back is the same as choosing which go back and paying for the rest. Of the two the
  card has the player choose (fewer if fewer were drawn), each one not put back costs 4 life.
- A player can't pay life they don't have (CR 119.4), so the least they must put back is set by
  their life: one at 5 to 7 life, both below 4.
- Two cards put back go on top in the order chosen, the first chosen on top.
- **The bot** always draws. It keeps one card for 4 life at 16 life or more, and puts back the
  cards worth least.

Staples went from 233 to 234 (Sylvan Library).

**Tests.** 8 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- a yes draws two, and offers only the three cards drawn this turn, not the card already in hand;
- putting two back costs nothing, and they go on top in the order chosen;
- each of the two not put back costs 4 life (16 with one kept, 12 with none);
- a no draws nothing and costs nothing;
- at 5 life one card must go back, at 3 both;
- a card that left the hand it was drawn into is no longer "drawn this turn";
- the bot draws, puts back two at 12 life, and keeps one at 20, paying 4.

Faults injected by script: 8 of 9 caught. The miss, `relocate` keeping the stamp, is pinned by the
seventh test. Re-run: 1 of 1 caught.

    engine tests: 4,777, all passing

## D722 — Animate Dead: an Aura that brings its creature back, and takes it away

"Enchant creature card in a graveyard / When Animate Dead enters, if it's on the battlefield, it
loses 'enchant creature card in a graveyard' and gains 'enchant creature put onto the battlefield
with Animate Dead.' Return enchanted creature card to the battlefield under your control and attach
Animate Dead to it. When Animate Dead leaves the battlefield, that creature's controller sacrifices
it. / Enchanted creature gets -1/-0."

How it is read:
- **One mechanic, read as a pair.** In `attachmentScriptFor`'s Aura branch, the enchant line and the
  long arrival line are read together:
  - the target is a creature card in any graveyard;
  - `AuraDef.reanimates` marks the Aura;
  - the bonus line applies to the creature.
- **On resolution.** `completeResolution` puts the targeted card onto the battlefield under the
  Aura's controller, records `animatedBy` (the Aura's id) on it, and attaches the Aura. The card's
  "if it's on the battlefield" check and its change of enchant ability are folded into that one
  step.
- **Its enchant ability on the battlefield.** The state-based attachment check reads "enchant
  creature put onto the battlefield with ~": a host is legal only while it is a creature whose
  `animatedBy` is this Aura. `relocate` clears `animatedBy` on any zone change, so a blinked
  creature is a new object, and the Aura falls off.
- **Leaving.** A leaves trigger sacrifices the creature this Aura animated, if it is still that
  object.
- **Not read yet.** Necromancy, which is not an Aura until it enters, and Dance of the Dead, whose
  other lines are refused.

Staples: +1 (Animate Dead); 235 of 244 with both sessions' work merged.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- an opponent's Giant returns under your control, enchanted, as a 3/4;
- only a creature card in a graveyard can be targeted;
- destroying the Aura sacrifices the Giant into its owner's graveyard;
- a host the Aura did not animate is not legal, and the Aura falls off;
- a blinked Giant is not sacrificed and the Aura falls off.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught. The legality guard was caught only after the direct "only
the creature it animated" test was added.

## D723 — Stun counters, and "it" after a target is the target

The biggest row in `phrase-gap.mjs` is "put a counter on <permanent>" (146 cards one line short),
and its biggest single form is "tap target creature an opponent controls and put a stun counter on
it" (Frostfist Strider, Referee Squad, Fractal Mascot, Splash Lasher and a dozen more).

**Stun counters (CR 122.1d).** "If a permanent with a stun counter on it would become untapped,
instead remove a stun counter from it." One function, `untapPermanent`, and every untap the engine
makes goes through it: the untap step (`untapAll`), an untap effect (`tap(…, false)`), and a {Q}
cost. A permanent that is already untapped would not become untapped, so it keeps its counters. The
tabletop's manual "untap all" is left alone, since a tabletop move means what the player said.
`stun` leaves `RULES_COUNTERS`, so "put three stun counters on it" reads like any other counter,
and the targeted counter reader takes `stun` beside +1/+1 and -1/-1, as a harmful counter.

**A correction found on the way: "it" after a target meant the source.** In "tap target creature
an opponent controls and put a +1/+1 counter on it", the plain clause vocabulary read "put a +1/+1
counter on it" first, where "it" is the trigger's subject or its source. So the counter went on the
creature that entered, not on the one it tapped. On an instant ("Target creature gets +2/+2 … Put a
+1/+1 counter on it", Big Play), "it" was the spell itself, and the counter went nowhere. That is a
wrong card, not an unread one. Now, when an earlier clause aimed at a card and this clause says a
bare "it", the D530 borrow is tried first, and the plain reading only if no borrow reads.
Miraculous Recovery's target is a graveyard card, a kind no pronoun swap reads, so "put N counters
on it" after a single card target is read directly as a counter on that one object. Of the 30
legal cards printing this shape, 3 read before the fix (Big Play, Charge the Sanctum, Miraculous
Recovery), and all 3 lost their counter.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests, plus the D603 test's refused list (stun moved out of it):
- the card reads, and so does a stun counter on the card itself (Ambling Stormshell's shape);
- Big Play's and Miraculous Recovery's counter lands on the target;
- the tapped target gets the stun counter, not the source;
- its untap step removes the counter instead of untapping, and the next one untaps;
- an untap effect is replaced the same way, and an untapped permanent keeps its counter, through
  the untap step and through an untap effect directly.

Faults injected by script: 6 of 7 caught, then 2 of 2 for the Recovery path. The miss, the "only if
tapped" guard in `untapPermanent`, is pinned by the last case above. Re-run: 1 of 1 caught.

fast-forwarded in before this was numbered. The figures below are against its head, 330266d
(11,449 cards, 30,803 lines).

## D724 — "Sacrifice it unless you <do something>"

About fifty legal lines, most of them an entry trigger: the karoo lands' "return a land you control
to its owner's hand", Balduvian Horde's "discard a card at random", Avatar of Discord's "discard two
cards", Mercenary Knight's "discard a creature card", Quickling's "return another creature you
control to its owner's hand". Nothing read them, and D514 and D529 had pinned two of them as
refusals ("a discard price", "a sacrifice price") until there was a reader.

How it is read:
- **The cost is read by the clause vocabulary**, which already knows each cost as an effect. It must
  ask exactly one question about the controller's own hand, battlefield or graveyard and point at
  nothing, or, for a random discard, ask nothing.
- **The choice comes first.** The cost is offered only when it can be done in full: enough cards of
  the kind in that zone (CR 118.3). Choosing it asks which cards pay; choosing "Sacrifice it", or
  having no way to pay, sacrifices the permanent.
- **"Another"** ("return another creature you control"): the cost's question needs the source to
  leave it out, so the choice is worked out against the same source.
- **A mana or energy price** ("sacrifice it unless you pay {1}") is left to D529's upkeep-tax
  reader, which already reads it.
- **New vocabulary on the way:** "discard a creature card", "discard two land cards" — the plain
  discard question with a card filter.
- **The bot pays whenever it can.** Keeping the permanent is what the card was played for.
- Still unread in the family: "sacrifice a Forest" and "return an untapped Mountain you control"
  (their cost clauses don't read yet), "return a non-Lair land" (a hyphenated subtype negation), and
  "unless {U} was spent to cast it".

**Tests.** 6 engine tests, and the D514 and D529 refusal lists lose the cases that now read:
- every shape reads;
- a creature card pays, and the Spark in hand doesn't count;
- with no way to pay, or by choice, it is sacrificed, and declining asks nothing more;
- two cards are chosen, and one is discarded at random;
- "return another creature" never offers itself, and alone it is sacrificed;
- the bot pays.

Faults injected by script: 7 of 8 caught. The miss, the cost question asked after "Sacrifice it",
was invisible because the test hand had only one card that could pay, and a forced answer is taken
without asking. Pinned with a two-card discard over a three-card hand. Re-run: 1 of 1 caught.

## D902 — A size that is a count: the commonest "*" bodies

"~'s power and toughness are each equal to the number of …" (Maro, Dungrove Elder, Crusader of
Odric), and "~'s power is equal to the number of … and its toughness is equal to that number
plus N" (Tarmogoyf).

How it is read:
- **The counts.** `definesSize.count` gains the commonest counts the corpus prints for a `*` body:
  - creatures you control, and creatures on the battlefield;
  - lands you control, and artifacts you control;
  - cards in your hand;
  - creature cards in your graveyard, and cards in your graveyard;
  - card types among cards in all graveyards, and in your graveyard;
  - a land type or creature type you control (`{ subtype }`).
- **The "each equal to" phrasing** is read beside the existing "power is equal to".
- **The compiler** already lets a `*` body through when such a static is present, so these cards now
  compile as single-faced creatures.
- **Limitation, stated.** `cdaCount` runs inside `characteristicsOf`, so permanents are counted by
  their **printed** type line. Asking the live characteristics of the permanents counted (the card
  itself among them) would ask this again. An animated land is therefore not counted as a creature.

`*/*` refusals fell from 134 to 73. About 90 cards are no longer refused outright, which also
raises the denominator.

  creatures;
- the hand count; three Forests make 3/3; the Crusader with a Bear and a Forest is 2/2.

Two compile tests used "cards in your hand" as their example of a count the engine lacks. They

## D725 — Chain Lightning: the player it hit may pay to copy it back

"Chain Lightning deals 3 damage to any target. Then that player or that permanent's controller may
pay {R}{R}. If the player does, they may copy this spell and may choose a new target for that
copy."

How it is read:
- **A new chooser, `target-or-its-controller`.** The seat the spell's first target is, or the
  controller of the permanent it is, read in whatever zone the permanent is now (as
  `referent-player` reads its card). Nobody is asked with no target. `TargetDecisionSpec` takes it
  too, and now accepts `askOnlyIfChosen`, so a new target can be asked only of a player who paid.
- **Two questions to that player.** Pay or decline, with {R}{R} on the paying answer
  (`payIfChosen`, so it is offered only to a player who can pay). Then, only after paying, a new
  target for the copy. `clausesOf` joins the two sentences, since the payment and the copy are one
  offer.
- **The copy is theirs.** It is made from the resolving spell the way Sevinne's Reclamation's is
  (D715) and goes on the stack under the payer's control. It is the same card, so it makes the same
  offer to whoever it hits: the chain the card is named for.
- **The bot pays whenever it can.** Three damage back for {R}{R} is why a player holds the mana.

Staples went from 235 to 236 (Chain Lightning).

- the card reads;
- the player it hit is asked, and declining ends it (17 life, nothing on the stack);
- paying taps both Mountains, and the copy goes on the stack under their control, aimed where they
  choose; it hits the caster, who can't pay to send it back;
- a player who can't pay isn't asked, and the controller of a creature it hit is the one asked;
- the bot pays when it can.

## D726 — Additional phases: extra combats, and Sphinx of the Second Sun

"At the beginning of each of your postcombat main phases, there is an additional beginning phase
after this phase." (Sphinx of the Second Sun.) The same machinery reads the extra-combat family:
"After this phase, there is an additional combat phase" (16 legal lines), "After this main phase,
there is an additional combat phase followed by an additional main phase" (Relentless Assault and
five more), "After this combat phase, …", and "there are two additional combat phases".

**The machinery (CR 500.8).** Two optional state fields:
- `extraPhases`, the queue of phases still to come this turn;
- `extraPhaseRun.resume`, the step the turn goes on to once they are done.

At each phase boundary `advanceStep` runs the first queued phase next: after the draw step (end of
the beginning phase), either main phase, or the end-of-combat step. When the queue is empty it
returns to `resume`.
- An added beginning phase starts at the untap step, so the active player's permanents untap and
  upkeep triggers fire again.
- An added combat starts at beginning of combat, and an added main phase is a postcombat main step.
  So "a combat followed by a main", cast in the first main phase, runs main, extra combat, extra
  main, then the regular combat, the second main and the end step.
- Combat state is already cleared at end of combat, so a second combat starts clean.
- Both fields are cleared when the turn ends.

**"Untap all creatures that attacked this turn"** (Relentless Assault's first sentence) needed a
per-creature record. `attackersThisTurn` holds `id#objectSeq` for each creature declared as an
attacker, cleared with the other turn facts. A creature that left and came back is a new object and
isn't untapped (CR 400.7).

Conditions in front ("if it's your main phase, …") are left to the readers that read conditions.

Staples went from 236 to 237 (Sphinx of the Second Sun).

**Tests.** 7 engine tests:
- the three test cards read;
- the Sphinx adds untap, upkeep and draw after the postcombat main in the same turn: a tapped land
  untaps, an upkeep trigger fires again, a card is drawn, then the end step;
- Relentless Assault cast after attacking untaps the attacker, then a combat and a main phase
  follow before the end step;
- cast in the first main phase, the extra combat and main come first: two postcombat mains;
- an instant in combat adds one combat and no main phase, and the queue is empty afterwards;
- a phase added in the end step dies with the turn, and the next player gets no extra combat;
- a creature that attacked and came back is not untapped.

Faults injected by script: 7 of 8 caught. The miss, the queue surviving the turn, is a real case
(an instant cast in the end step would have handed the next player an extra combat) and is pinned
by the sixth test. Re-run: 1 of 1 caught.

**Two worker restarts, and a fault left in the tree each time.** Both restarts killed a break run
mid-fault. Each time the tree was checked fault by fault against the original text and restored
before anything else ran (D720's shuffle fold, this entry's attacker record). The break-run script
now keeps the original file beside it while a fault is in, and puts back any leftover from a killed
run when it starts.

    engine tests: 4,808, all passing

Coverage: 11,562 of 31,743 cards (+5), 31,052 of 59,509 lines (+8). Staples: 237 of 244 (+1).

## D903 — "That many" after a combat-damage trigger is the damage dealt

"Whenever ~ deals combat damage to a player, draw that many cards", and the rest of the 101 legal
lines where "that many" or "that much" follows a damage trigger.

How it is read:
- **The amount, end to end:**
  - `hit` records how much landed on each combat hit (`dealtCombatDamage[].amount`): life lost, or
    poison for infect, so prevention is already counted;
  - the `combat-damage` event carries it, and `deals-damage` carries its record's amount;
  - `TriggerAbout` → `StackObject.eventAmount` → `EffectContext.eventAmount`.
- **The words.** The trigger reader marks "that many" / "that much" only when every event of the
  shape is a damage event, and only if the clause has no X of its own. Elsewhere the words name
  some other number, and no reader knows the mark.
- **The clauses read with the mark:**
  - draw that many cards (also with "you may");
  - you gain that much life;
  - that player mills that many cards (the player hit);
  - you get that many {E};
  - create that many Treasure tokens;
  - put that many +1/+1 counters on it.
- **Not read yet.** Anything that asks a question, such as "that player discards that many cards";
  "it deals that much damage to each other opponent"; and the non-combat "deals damage to a player"
  self trigger.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- three cards read;
- a 3/3 unblocked draws 3;
- a 2/2 gains 2;
- a 4/1 mills the player it hit 4;
- blocked by a Wall, nothing happens.

Power Fist's granted "put that many +1/+1 counters on it" reads now. Its D511 refusal row moves to
that test's "reads the quote" list. A granted trigger's source is the creature that has it, so
"it" is the equipped creature, as printed.

## D904 — "Deals damage" to anything, and "is dealt damage", with that much

"Whenever ~ deals damage, you gain that much life" (and its enchanted-creature form), and "Whenever
~ is dealt damage, draw that many cards / it deals that much damage to any target / you lose that
much life / create that many 1/1 Insects".

How it is read:
- **"Deals damage" to anything** is `deals-damage` with `to: 'any'`, answered only by the engine's
  `anything` events. The matcher keeps those apart from the player and opponent events, so a hit
  on a player is never counted twice.
  - One event per non-combat hit.
  - One per source for its combat damage in a step, with the total: combat damage is dealt at once
    (CR 510.2), so a trampler that hits a blocker and the player triggers once.
- **"Is dealt damage"** (`damaged`) carries the amount. Combat damage to one creature is summed, as
  the one event it already was: a double block triggers once, for the total.
- **The words.** D903's "that many" mark now applies to `damaged` events too. The new clauses are
  "you lose that much life", "it deals that much damage to <target>" and "… to you", and "create
  that many <token>".

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- both cards read;
- the Drinker gains 3 unblocked and 3 into a Wall;
- a Bolt at the Sponge draws 3, and two Bears blocking it draw 4, once.

## D905 — Afflict, Mobilize and Ingest

Three keywords from the "declaration with no builder" list (1,434 unread lines). Each was the only
unread line on 5 to 8 legal cards.

How each is read:
- **Afflict N** (CR 702.130a): a becomes-blocked trigger. The defending player, read off the
  combat's attack entry for the creature, loses N life.
- **Mobilize N** (CR 702.181a): an attack trigger that creates N 1/1 red Warrior tokens.
  - Each token is tapped and added to the combat attacking what the creature attacks.
  - Each token gets the engine-known delayed sacrifice the end-step riders use (D696).
- **Ingest** (CR 702.115a): a combat-damage trigger. The player hit (`c.attacked.defender`)
  exiles the top card of their library.

## D727 — Necromancy, and a cleanup step that gives priority to a delayed ability

**A correction first.** A delayed ability scheduled for the cleanup step fired there and was then
carried into the next turn: it resolved in the next player's upkeep. CR 514.3a gives the players
priority in the cleanup step when anything triggers there, and then runs the cleanup step again.
The engine already did that for a discard to hand size (`cleanupHolds`, `finishCleanup`). Entering
the step didn't check it, and nothing scheduled a cleanup ability until Necromancy, so nothing had
shown it. `advanceStep` now hands out priority in the cleanup step when `cleanupHolds` says so.

"You may cast Necromancy as though it had flash. If you cast it any time a sorcery couldn't have
been cast, the controller of the permanent it becomes sacrifices it at the beginning of the next
cleanup step. When Necromancy enters, if it's on the battlefield, it becomes an Aura with 'enchant
creature put onto the battlefield with Necromancy.' Put target creature card from a graveyard onto
the battlefield under your control and attach Necromancy to it. When Necromancy leaves the
battlefield, that creature's controller sacrifices it."

How it is read:
- **The flash line** is a new script field, `castAsThoughFlash`. It is a permission to cast at any
  time a player has priority, not the keyword, so "creatures with flash" don't see it. A cast when a
  sorcery couldn't have been cast is recorded on the stack object (`castOutsideSorceryTiming`). As
  the permanent arrives, an engine-known delayed `sacrifice` is scheduled for the next cleanup step.
- **The entry** is D722's Animate Dead mechanism by a different road:
  - Necromancy is cast as an enchantment with no target, so it is never an Aura spell;
  - the target is the trigger's, a creature card in any graveyard, and the trigger asks "if it's on
    the battlefield" (an intervening if);
  - as it resolves, the card comes back under Necromancy's controller (recorded as `animatedBy`),
    Necromancy becomes an Aura (a static adding the subtype to itself), and it is attached;
  - when Necromancy leaves, the creature is sacrificed;
  - as an Aura with no `script.aura`, the state-based check bins it when its host leaves.
- **With no creature card in any graveyard**, the trigger has no target and Necromancy stays an
  enchantment that does nothing, as the rules leave it.

Staples went from 237 to 238 (Necromancy).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests, plus the mechanic-coverage entry for `castAsThoughFlash`:
- the card reads;
- cast in a main phase, it takes a creature from an opponent's graveyard, controls it, and becomes
  its Aura, with nothing scheduled;
- when it leaves, the creature is sacrificed, and when the creature leaves, it goes too;
- cast in the end step, both are sacrificed in that turn's own cleanup step (turn 3, step cleanup),
  and the creature ends in its owner's graveyard;
- with no creature card in any graveyard, it stays a plain enchantment.

Faults injected by script: 8 of 8 caught, including the cleanup correction.

    engine tests: 4,827, all passing (on the tree merged with the other session's D906)

session's D904 and D905). Staples: 238 of 244 (+1).

## D906 — Scavenge and Reinforce

Two more keyword builders, both activated abilities that pay with the card itself.

How each is read:
- **Scavenge {cost}** (CR 702.97a) is embalm's shape:
  - activated from the graveyard (`fromGraveyard`), exiling the card as part of the cost
    (`exileSelf`), at sorcery speed;
  - it puts as many +1/+1 counters on target creature as the card's printed power.
- **Reinforce N—{cost}** (CR 702.77a) is cycling's shape:
  - activated from the hand, discarding the card (`discardSelf`), at instant speed;
  - it puts N +1/+1 counters on target creature.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- both cards read;
- scavenge exiles the card and puts 3 counters on the Bear, and is refused on the opponent's turn
  even with priority;
- reinforce, on the opponent's turn, discards the card for 2 counters.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught. The sorcery-speed fault was caught only after the
opponent's-turn case gave seat 0 priority first: without it, the refusal came from priority.

## D907 — Devour and Amplify

Two "as this enters, choose some, and it enters with N counters for each" keywords. Each blocked
about 7 to 9 legal cards on its own.

How they are read:
- **The shared machinery.** A new script field, `entersCounting: { kind, n }`, plus the card's one
  question, asked as the spell resolves (riot's and Mox Diamond's path, so only a cast creature is
  asked: D559's limitation). As the creature arrives, `completeResolution` counts the chosen cards
  and adds N +1/+1 counters for each.
- **Devour N** (CR 702.82a):
  - any number of your creatures may be chosen, and they are sacrificed;
  - the bot devours nothing.
- **Amplify N** (CR 702.38a):
  - any number of creature cards in your hand that share a creature type with the spell may be
    chosen;
  - they are only revealed, and stay in hand;
  - the bot reveals everything it may, since revealing costs nothing.
- **Still unread.** Skullmulcher's "draw a card for each creature it devoured".

Also: two earlier mechanic-coverage notes (D714, D716) had been joined onto the line before them by
a missing newline. They are inside a comment, so nothing ran differently; they are fixed.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests, plus the mechanic-coverage entry:
- both cards read;
- devour 2 eats two Goblins for four counters and leaves the Dragon;
- amplify offers the Dragon and not the Goblin, and the card stays in hand.

Faults injected by hand: 3 of 4 caught. The fourth, a zone re-check at resolution, cannot be
reached: the question's candidates already come from the right zone. It is kept as a belt.

    engine tests: 4,825, all passing

Coverage: 11,660 of 31,743 cards (+16), 31,200 of 59,509 lines (+28). Staples: 237 of 244.

## D909 — "Reveal a <type> card from your hand or pay", and behold

"As an additional cost to cast this spell, reveal a Merfolk card from your hand or pay {3}"
(Silvergill Adept and the Lorwyn tribal cycle), and "… behold a Goblin or pay {2}" (the newer form,
where a permanent you control also counts).

How it is read:
- A `selfCostChange` adds the printed generic amount only when nothing qualifies:
  - another card of that creature type in hand (never the card being cast);
  - for behold, also a permanent of that type you control (by its live type line).
- Revealing costs nothing and paying buys nothing, so the engine reveals for the caster, which is
  the only answer a player would give. The offer and the payment agree because `costChangeFor`
  answers both.
- **Refused:** a type that is not a creature type, such as Countersculpt's "behold a Jace".

- both cards read;
- castable for {1}{U} with a Merfolk card in hand, not without one, and with {3} more it is;
- a Goblin does not count for the Merfolk;
- behold accepts a Goblin on the battlefield or in hand.

## D910 — "If a creature dealt damage this way would die this turn, exile it instead"

Anger of the Gods, Magma Spray, Red Sun's Zenith, Pillar of Flame, Yamabushi's Flame and their
cousins. The second sentence is about what the first one damaged, so `clausesOf` now holds the two
together, and `exiledIfDamagedThisWay` wraps the damage.

How it is read:
- The creatures dealt damage this way are those whose marked damage the first sentence raised, read
  off the battlefield around it. A creature whose damage was prevented is not one of them and dies
  normally.
- Each one gets D539's `exiledInsteadOfDying` until end of turn, scoped to that creature. It is
  exiled whether it dies to the damage or to something else later in the turn.
- "A permanent dealt damage this way" (Spikefield Hazard, Underworld Fires) adds planeswalkers,
  where damage is loyalty removed.
- The X form (Demonfire, Red Sun's Zenith) is wrapped in `xSpellResolution` the same way.
- The compile.test row that refused Anger of the Gods "until a channel is built" now asserts the
  line reads.
- **Not counted:** damage that is not marked (wither, infect). No card of this family deals it.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the four printings read;
- a sweep exiles what it kills, and a survivor is exiled when it dies later that turn;
- a creature the spell missed dies normally;
- a creature already damaged and not damaged again is not counted;
- X damage is wrapped;
- "a permanent" takes a planeswalker and "a creature" does not.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught. A sixth, an end-of-turn duration spelled out, changes
nothing and passes, as it should.

Coverage: 11,696 of 31,743 cards (+10), 31,250 of 59,509 lines (+11).

  ~ trains".

## D913 — Blocking requirements: Lure, provoke, "must be blocked if able"

CR 509.1c: the defending player's declaration must obey as many blocking requirements as it can
without breaking a restriction. The engine had restrictions on blocks and no requirements, so 135
printed sentences could not be played. Four requirements are now characteristics, set by printed
statics or by `PumpOptions`:
- `mustBlock`: "~ blocks each combat if able", and "target creature blocks this turn if able";
- `mustBlockAttackers`: provoke, and "target creature blocks ~ this turn if able";
- `mustBeBlocked`: "~ must be blocked if able", and "target creature must be blocked this turn if
  able";
- `lure`: "All creatures able to block ~ do so", and its targeted until-end-of-turn form.

How the declaration is held to them (`combat.ts`):
- `obeyed` counts the requirements a declaration meets. Lure is one requirement per creature able
  to block the lured attacker.
- `betterBlocks` looks for a legal declaration that meets more, by moving one creature (two together
  for a menace attacker). `declareBlockers` refuses a declaration that has one, naming what has to
  block what.
- `meetBlockRequirements` applies those moves to the computer's own plans, so its blocks are
  always legal.
- When no requirement is in play, which is nearly every combat, the check returns before building
  its table of who may block whom.
- **The approximation, stated:** CR 509.1c asks for the global maximum. This is the local form, one
  or two creatures moved at a time. That covers every board a printed requirement makes in practice;
  a board where only a three-creature rearrangement does better would be accepted as declared.
- A restriction beats a requirement: a creature that cannot block that attacker (flying, can't
  block) is never required to.

Read by the compiler:
- the printed statics above;
- provoke, an optional target chosen from the defending player's creatures, which untaps and must
  block the provoker;
- the four targeted "this turn" forms;
- the Aura riders "blocks each combat if able" and "must be blocked if able".

`printedCombatStatics` keeps its four-field answer (D495's tests pin it). The new flags come from
`printedCombatFlags`.

Not read yet:
- "gets +N/+N until end of turn and must be blocked this turn if able" (Compelled Duel);
- "target creature defending player controls blocks it this combat if able" on an attack trigger;
- the Aura and Equipment sentences that grant Lure to the creature;
- "you choose how those creatures block".

The table has no "must block" hint yet. The refusal reason says what has to block what.

**Tests.** 10 engine tests:
- seven printed cards and two spells read;
- Lure, refused short of every able creature;
- a flier's Lure binds only the creature that can block it;
- Lure with menace moves two creatures;
- "must be blocked if able";
- "blocks each combat if able";
- provoke: the target untaps, must block, and only a defending creature can be targeted;
- the activated taunt;
- the granted "must be blocked" and Lure;
- the computer obeys every requirement at once.

Faults injected by hand: 17 of 17 caught. Two of them, the granted Lure and "must be blocked",
were missed at first and pinned by the spell test.

    engine tests: 4,860, all passing

Coverage: 11,745 of 31,743 cards (+37), 31,348 of 59,509 lines (+65). Staples: 238 of 244.

## D915 — Exert

"You may exert ~ as it attacks. When you do, <effect>." (CR 701.39): Glorybringer, the Amonkhet
cycle and others. 21 legal cards print it.

How it is read (`triggerFromLine`):
- **First, as D472's "you may X. If you do, Y":** the line becomes the attack trigger "you may exert
  ~. If you do, <effect>". The new clause "exert ~" asks nothing and is `freezeNextUntap` on the
  card, so the effect happens only if it did. An effect that asks its own question (a scry) rides
  the same gate.
- **A targeted "when you do"** (Glorybringer, Ahn-Crop Crasher), which D472 refuses. The effect is
  read as the plain attack trigger and an Exert / Don't exert question goes in front of it. The
  targets are chosen as the trigger goes on the stack, and the effect runs only after "Exert". This
  is taken only when the effect asks nothing itself.
- **The timing, stated:** the rules exert as the attack is declared and then put the reflexive
  trigger on the stack. Here the choice is made as the trigger resolves. Nothing in the family can
  tell the two apart except a response in between.

Not read:
- "Whenever you exert a creature" (no exert event yet);
- "If ~ hasn't been exerted this turn";
- the activated "Exert ~" cost;
- "When you do, you may …", a second "may".

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- three printings read;
- exerted, the pump happens and the creature stays tapped through its next untap step;
- not exerted, nothing happens and it untaps;
- the targeted form affects the target only if the creature was exerted;
- the scry is asked only after exerting, and the exert lands with it.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught. The D472 path was missed at first: the new wrap covers
every effect that asks nothing. The scry test pinned it.

    engine tests: 4,870, all passing

Coverage: 11,766 of 31,743 cards (+15), 31,369 of 59,509 lines (+15). Staples: 238 of 244.

## D917 — Colours of mana spent: sunburst and converge

Sunburst (CR 702.44a) and converge both count the colours of mana spent to cast a spell. The engine
did not record that, so 53 printed sentences could not be played.

The engine:
- `payFrom` reports `coloursSpent`: the colours the pool holds less of after the payment than before.
  Mana left floating does not count, and neither does colourless.
- `castSpell` records it on the stack object. A copy, or a spell cast without paying its mana cost,
  has none.
- **The approximation, stated:** which mana pays the generic part is `payCost`'s choice, and which
  lands tap is `solveTap`'s. Neither aims at more colours. A player who wants every colour counted
  floats the mana first, and the guide says so.

Read:
- **Sunburst**: the keyword, as the new `CardScript.sunburst {counter: 'auto', n: 1}`. It gives
  +1/+1 counters on a creature and charge counters otherwise, decided as it enters.
- **"~ enters with a (two) +1/+1 counter(s) on it for each color of mana spent to cast it"**
  (converge creatures), as `sunburst {counter: '+1/+1', n}`.
- **"where X is the number of colors of mana spent to cast this spell"**, a count read off the
  resolving spell.
- **Ability words on spells now come off** before the resolution is read. "Converge — Draw X cards,
  …" is the sentence after the dash. An ability word has no rules meaning (CR 207.2c), and the
  permanent path has always dropped them. This added a few cards beyond converge, and every
  existing test still passes.

Not read:
- "Modular—Sunburst";
- spells that gain sunburst (Lux Artillery, Solar Array);
- other kinds of counter per colour (Prism Array's crystal counters);
- the converge spells whose other sentences don't read yet ("discards X cards").

**Tests.** 8 engine tests:
- the printings read;
- sunburst gives 3 counters for three colours and 1 for one colour;
- a noncreature gets charge counters;
- a converge creature gets its counters;
- a converge draw draws 3 or 1;
- a pool with a colour left over, or with colourless, counts only the colours spent;
- "two counters for each color" doubles;
- put onto the battlefield without being cast, it has none.

Faults injected by hand: 7 of 8 caught. The miss is converge's +1/+1 against sunburst's automatic
choice, which differs only on a noncreature printing +1/+1 converge, and no card does.

    engine tests: 4,883, all passing

Coverage: 11,790 of 31,743 cards (+19), 31,404 of 59,509 lines (+29). Staples: 238 of 244.

## D918 — Annihilator, and the edict widened

"Each player/opponent sacrifices a creature" was the only edict read. Now:
- "**each player | each opponent | defending player** sacrifices **a | two | … | N**
  **creature | permanent | artifact | land | enchantment | nonland permanent**(s)";
- each sacrificing player chooses, in turn order, out of their own permanents of that kind;
- the choice goes through `sacrifice`, so whatever watches a sacrifice sees it;
- "Defending player" is `hit-player`, the attack's defender, which a trigger off an attack carries.

**Annihilator N** (CR 702.86a) is read as the printed sentence: "Whenever this creature attacks,
defending player sacrifices N permanents."

- in a three-player pod, annihilator 2 asks only the attacked player, offers their three
  permanents, and leaves the third player's board alone;
- "each player sacrifices a land" takes a land from both players, and offers only lands;
- "each opponent sacrifices a nonland permanent" offers no land.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught. The type filter was missed at first and pinned by asserting
only lands are offered.

Coverage: 11,811 of 31,743 cards (+21), 31,440 of 59,509 lines (+36). Staples: 238 of 244.

## D919 — Historic and subtypes in a card filter

`graveyardTypeTest` is the one test that turns "a creature card", "an instant or sorcery card" and
the like into a predicate. The dig, the reveal-and-keep, the chosen discard and the graveyard
targets all share it. It read card types only. Now it also reads:
- **historic**: an artifact, a legendary card, or a Saga (CR 700.6);
- **a subtype by its printed capital**, only when it is real: a creature type (`isCreatureType`) or
  one of `CARD_SUBTYPES_READ` (Aura, Equipment, Vehicle, Saga, Curse, Shrine). This is the
  validation #341 asked for, so "Blorp" and the plural "Rebels" are still refused;
- **a mix**: "Human or artifact", "creature or Vehicle".

The test now takes the card definition as well as its type line. A creature type then goes through
`cardHasSubtype`, so a changeling card has every creature type (CR 702.73a). All four callers pass
it. D683's reveal-and-keep test caught the changeling the first version lost.

Compile tests retired, each now asserting the line reads:
- D527: "creature or Vehicle" and "Rebel";
- D584: historic, Elf, and "Aura, creature, or planeswalker".

New refusal rows: "Blorp", "Rebels", and "a shiny card".

Not read: "colorless" (a colour, not a type-line fact), and lists of more than three kinds.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the printings read;
- historic offers the artifact, the legendary card and the Saga, and nothing else;
- a creature type offers the Hero and the changeling;
- "Goblin or artifact" offers either;
- a Goblin card can be targeted in the graveyard, and a Bear cannot.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6. Four were caught as written; the plural guard was a redundant
check and was removed (it would have refused real types such as Cyclops), and the "or" mix was
pinned by a new test.

    engine tests: 4,895, all passing

Coverage: 11,843 of 31,743 cards (+32), 31,499 of 59,509 lines (+59). Staples: 238 of 244.

"{T}: Add {C}. / {T}: Add {B} or {R}. Cinder Marsh doesn't untap during your next untap step." — the
Tempest lands and their kin, ten legal cards.

  rider beside the pain land's damage.
  - It is part of the same mana ability's effect (CR 605.3a): `freezeNextUntap` on the land as the
    mana is made.
  - The sentence must be about the land itself, by its name, short name or "this land".

  a line beside another is refused there and read line by line, where each line keeps its own
  rider.
- **Compile test retired:** D497's refusal row for the sentence. A row for "Target land doesn't
  untap …" now stands in its place.
- **Not modelled:** the auto-tapper does not yet weigh the cost of a frozen land when it chooses
  sources.

- the land reads;
- tapped for black: the mana arrives, the land stays tapped through its next untap step, and it
  untaps the turn after;
- tapped for colourless: no rider;
- the rider about another land is refused.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught. One first ran against the wrong file, and was re-run once
the subject test existed.

## D921 — A mana line with "Activate only if …"

The second sentence after a mana ability can be a condition. The new `ManaLine.onlyIf` reads it as
the ability's `activateOnlyIf`, so it is neither offered nor tapped automatically while false. It
is read live, from characteristics. Conditions read:
- "you control a Swamp or a Mountain" (the Duskmourn Verges) and "you control a Swamp" (the Tainted
  lands): a land of that basic land type;
- "this land entered this turn or if your control a basic land" (the Dominaria lands; the typo is
  Scryfall's own text);
- "you control an artifact" (Spire of Industry) or a creature type (Mox Jasper);
- "you control five or more lands" (Temple of the False God), and the same count for artifacts and
  creatures;
- "~ entered this turn" (Mirrex).

Both builders carry it: a single mana and a sum (Temple's {C}{C}). The colour fold leaves such a
line to the per-line path, as D920 does. D497's refusal row for "you control a Swamp" now names a
condition this does not read.

Not read:
- conditions behind an ability word (Formidable, Corrupted, Metalcraft);
- counters on the card (Pyramid of the Pantheon, Tablet of Compleation);
- "an Elf card in your graveyard";
- "~ is a creature".

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the printings read;
- a Verge's second colour needs a Swamp or a Mountain;
- the Dominaria land works when it entered this turn or with a basic land, and not with a nonbasic
  one;
- Temple needs five lands;
- Spire's colour needs an artifact, and its colourless line does not.

Faults injected by hand: 7 of 7 caught.

    engine tests: 4,904, all passing

Coverage: 11,876 of 31,743 cards (+23), 31,534 of 59,509 lines (+25). Staples: 238 of 244.

## D922 — Plot

"Plot {cost} (You may pay {cost} and exile this card from your hand. Cast it as a sorcery on a later
turn without paying its mana cost. Plot only as a sorcery.)" (CR 702.170). The Outlaws of Thunder
Junction mechanic: 14 legal cards were held back by the keyword alone.

How it is built, on what was there:
- **`CardScript.plot {cost}`**, read from the keyword line.
- **The special action `auto:plot`**, suspend's sibling. It is offered from hand at sorcery speed,
  for the card's own cost, beside its cast. The card goes to exile **face up**. No stack, nothing
  to respond to.
- **The wait in exile is D583's `playFromExile`** with a new deadline kind, `through: 'plotted'`.
  No cleanup expires it, and `relocate` clears it if the card leaves exile. What it adds:
  - the cast is offered and allowed only on a turn after the plot;
  - only at sorcery speed, an instant included ("cast it as a sorcery");
  - with no mana cost, so X is 0.
- **The computer** is offered the plot like a suspend, and drops it by the same rule
  (`specialIsSpareMana`): it plots only when the mana had nothing better to do. It casts a plotted
  card like any other cast on offer.
- **The web table:** `arena.ts` maps the `plot` play to `auto:plot`, the play sheet gives it its own
  row id, and the table's help lists it.

Not read: "Whenever you plot a card", and the cards that plot something else ("exile … it becomes
plotted").

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- both printings read;
- plot is offered from hand and the card goes face up into exile, paid by the Island;
- it is not castable the turn it was plotted;
- on the next turn it is cast with every land tapped and draws its three;
- an instant plotted is still cast only as a sorcery;
- plot itself is refused, and not offered, outside a main phase, an instant with plot included.

Faults injected by hand: 9 of 9 caught. The plot offer's own timing was pinned by the instant case.

    engine tests: 4,910, all passing

Coverage: 11,891 of 31,743 cards (+15), 31,567 of 59,509 lines (+33). Staples: 238 of 244.

## D728 — Fact or Fiction: an opponent splits the top five, the caster takes a pile

"Reveal the top five cards of your library. An opponent separates those cards into two piles. Put
one pile into your hand and the other into your graveyard."

**The infrastructure.**
- **Revealed cards, `AutomationState.revealed`** (CR 701.20a). Cards a resolving spell reveals to
  the table. Every seat and spectators see them (`view.ts` sends them as cards without their
  library's list). A question may be asked about them, `DecisionZone` `revealed`, which unlike a
  search or a scry moves nothing and shuffles nothing when answered. The spell clears it as it
  finishes.
- **A new chooser, `an-opponent`.** The next opponent in turn order after the controller. Exact at
  two players. **Known limitation:** at a pod the caster would choose which opponent separates, and
  this doesn't ask.
- **D721's `onReach` hook now receives the answers so far, and a choice question may carry one.**
  That is how the opponent's split becomes two named piles (`AutomationState.piles`) before the
  caster is asked, so the caster's two answers can list the cards in each ("First pile: Island",
  "Second pile: …", either of which may be "nothing").

How the card is read:
- `clausesOf` joins the three sentences.
- The top N cards are revealed before anything is asked.
- The opponent chooses the first pile from them; the rest are the second.
- The caster chooses a pile. It goes to hand, and the other goes to the graveyard.
- **The bot**, as separator, puts the card worth most alone in the first pile. As caster it takes
  the pile worth more, counting each card as one plus its mana value.
- Sphinx of Uthuun prints the same lines and reads whole as well.

**The web client** shows revealed cards in a row for the player choosing among them, with the hint
"tap the revealed cards below". Typecheck and its 270 tests pass.

Staples went from 238 to 239 (Fact or Fiction).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- the top five are revealed to both seats, and the opponent is the one asked, from them;
- the caster takes the pile they choose and the other goes to the graveyard (four to hand and one
  binned; or, with an empty first pile, all five binned);
- the bot splits off its best card and answers as caster.

Faults injected by script: 9 of 9 caught.

**A slip, caught by its own test.** The effect first read the caster's answer with `chosenOption`,
which reads the *first* answer, here the opponent's split, which has no option. So choosing the
empty first pile was taken as choosing the second. It reads the caster's answer by position now.

    engine tests: 4,914, all passing (merged with the other session's D920–D922)

Coverage: 11,894 of 31,743 cards (+2), 31,572 of 59,509 lines (+3), against 82ce488. Staples: 239
of 244 (+1).

## D923 — Casualty, and a copied permanent spell becomes a token

"Casualty N (As you cast this spell, you may sacrifice a creature with power N or greater. When you
do, copy this spell.)" (CR 702.153a), from Streets of New Capenna: A Little Chat, Make Disappear,
Rooftop Nuisance, Join the Maestros and others.

How it is read:
- **`CardScript.casualty N`** and a self cast trigger, `CASUALTY_COPY`, which copies the spell
  when `StackObject.casualtyPaid` says the cost was paid. It is replicate's shape (copy with
  `copySpellOnStack`, keeping the original's targets, CR 707.10).
- **A second cast play** (`casualty: true`) is offered beside the printed one when the caster
  controls a creature of power N or greater. Its `sacrificeOptions` are those creatures, so the
  table asks for the sacrifice as it does for any sacrifice cost, and the creature is gone as the
  spell is cast.
  - It is not offered beside a spell whose own additional cost already sacrifices.
  - The cast refuses a creature that is too small or not yours.
- **The plumbing:** the computer passes the flag on, and the shared-fields test caught the first
  version that did not. The web table forwards it among its cost flags.
- **New engine rule:** a copy of a permanent spell resolves into a **token** that is a copy of it
  (CR 707.10f). Before, a copy had no card and a permanent copy resolved into nothing. Every copied
  spell takes this path. Rooftop Nuisance with casualty is two Nuisances.

Not read: "Casualty X" (Ob Nixilis), and the copy's printed exceptions ("The copy isn't legendary").

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- both printings read;
- the casualty play is offered only with a creature of power N or greater, and offers only those;
- paid, the creature is sacrificed and the copy draws two more;
- not paid, no sacrifice and no copy;
- a creature too small is refused;
- a creature spell's copy is a token of it.

Faults injected by hand: 7 of 7 caught.

    engine tests: 4,916, all passing

Coverage: 11,898 of 31,743 cards (+7), 31,581 of 59,509 lines (+14). Staples: 238 of 244.

## D929 — Emerge

"Emerge {cost} (You may cast this spell by sacrificing a creature and paying the emerge cost reduced
by that creature's mana value.)" (CR 702.119a), from Eldritch Moon and Doctor Who: Elder
Deep-Fiend's cousins, Decimator of the Provinces, Wretched Gryff and others.

How it is read:
- **`CardScript.emerge {cost}`** and a cast play `emerged: true`. Its `sacrificeOptions` are the
  creatures whose mana value, taken off the emerge cost's generic part, leaves a cost the seat can
  afford (`emergeOptions`). So the table asks for the creature as it asks for any sacrifice cost,
  and offers only those that work.
- **`reducedCostText`** reduces the generic part and writes the cost back in its printed form, so
  delve and convoke, which rebuild the cost from the text, see the reduced cost too.
- **The cast** refuses a sacrifice that is missing, not a creature, not yours, or the card itself.
  It sacrifices the creature as the spell is cast and pays the reduced cost.
- **The plumbing:** the computer and the web table forward the flag.

Not read: "if its emerge cost was paid" (Adipose Offspring), and Herigast's emerge for every
creature spell.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- the reduction is generic only, never below zero;
- the play is offered only with the creature that makes it affordable;
- cast, the Fodder is sacrificed, the Emerger resolves, and the three Islands pay;
- refused with no creature and with a land.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught. The creature check was pinned by the land refusal.

  one-each splits is legal;
- the copies are gone after the end step.

## D932 — Awaken

"Awaken N—{cost} (If you cast this spell for {cost}, also put N +1/+1 counters on target land you
control and it becomes a 0/0 Elemental creature with haste. It's still a land.)" (CR 702.113a), from
Battle for Zendikar: Coastal Discovery, Ruinous Path, Planar Outburst, Scatter to the Winds and
others.

How it is read:
- **`CardScript.awaken {cost, n}`** and an alternative-cost play `awakened: true`, validated with
  the other alternative costs (one per cast, from hand).
- **The land is a target.** The play's target specs are the spell's own followed by `AWAKEN_LAND`
  ("target land you control"), so the table asks for it like any target.
  - The cast checks it against that spec and moves it onto `StackObject.awakenOn`, out of the
    spell's own targets. Nothing the spell does to "target creature" or "each target" can touch it.
  - **The approximation, stated:** a spell whose only target is the land does not fizzle when the
    land becomes illegal; it resolves without awakening.
- **After the spell's own effect,** if the land is still a land its caster controls, it gets N +1/+1
  counters and a permanent effect: Creature, Elemental, base 0/0, haste. The land itself is the
  effect's source. The first version used the spell, and a permanent effect leaves with its source,
  so the animation vanished as the spell went to the graveyard. The test caught it.
- **The plumbing:** the computer and the web table forward the flag.

Not read: Encircling Fissure, Ondu Rising and Part the Waterveil, whose other sentences don't read.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- both printings read;
- the play's last target is "target land you control", offering only the caster's Island;
- awakened, the spell draws its two and the Island is a 2/2 Elemental creature land with haste;
- a destroy spell kills its creature and leaves the land, at 1/1;
- refused with no land or the opponent's land, and cast normally no land changes.

Faults injected by hand: 7 of 7 caught.

## D935 — Prowl and freerunning

"Prowl {cost} (You may cast this for its prowl cost if you dealt combat damage to a player this turn
with a [creature type].)" (CR 702.76a), from Morningtide, and "Freerunning {cost} (... with an
Assassin or a commander.)" (CR 702.181a), from Assassin's Creed. Nine legal cards now read whole.

How it is read:
- **A new turn fact, `combatHitsThisTurn`.** Written where combat damage to a player lands (the
  place toxic and `dealtCombatDamage` are written), keyed by the seat that controlled the creature,
  with its creature types and whether it was a commander as the damage was dealt. Cleared with the
  other turn facts. A changeling records every creature type.
- **Spectacle's play a third and fourth time**, after surge (D928): `CardScript.spectacle` gained
  `prowl` and `freerunning`. The four conditions now live in one function, `spectacleRefusal`,
  which the offer and `castSpell` both ask, so the two cannot disagree. Prowl compares the
  recorded types with the spell's own (`cardHasSubtype`, so a Kindred spell and a changeling card
  both work); freerunning looks for an Assassin or a commander.
- **The riders are surge's**: "If this spell's prowl (freerunning) cost was paid" on the spell, and
  "When ~ enters, if its prowl cost was paid" on the `surged` marker, which the arrival now writes
  for all three keywords (a card has only one of them).

**Tests.** 7 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- a Rogue's hit is recorded with its types, and the record clears with the turn;
- prowl is offered after a Rogue's or a changeling's hit, and not after a Bear's or none, and is
  refused then;
- the spell rider happens only when prowled;
- the enters rider happens only when prowled;
- freerunning is offered after an Assassin's or a commander's hit and not a Rogue's or a Bear's;
- a commander's hit is recorded as one.

Faults injected by hand: 10 of 10 caught.

## D936 — Cipher, and casting a copy of a card

"Cipher (Then you may exile this spell card encoded on a creature you control. Whenever that
creature deals combat damage to a player, its controller may cast a copy of the encoded card
without paying its mana cost.)" (CR 702.99), from Gatecrash. Ten legal cards now read whole.

How it is read:
- **A copy of a card** (CR 707.12) is new: `copyCardInExile` makes an instance marked `cardCopy`
  in exile, owned by the seat that will cast it, and the existing free-cast offer
  (`pendingOfferedCast`) offers it. `relocate` ends a copy as it moves anywhere but the stack
  (after it resolves, or when a declined offer moves it), and turns a permanent copy that resolves
  into a token. A cast copy counts as a spell cast. This is the base the other "cast a copy" cards
  (about 130 in the corpus) can use.
- **Encoding is the spell's last question**, appended after its own so their answer indexes are
  unchanged. As the spell leaves the stack, `completeResolution` exiles it with `encodedOn` (the
  creature and the object it was) if that is still a creature its controller controls, and a copy
  is never encoded. The question is asked with the spell's others, at the start of the resolution
  rather than at the end; the creature is checked again at the end, so one the spell itself
  removed is not encoded on.
- **The ability is the card's**, in its `grantedTriggers`, handed to the creature by a permanent
  pump whose source is the creature (so it ends as the creature leaves, CR 702.99c) and whose new
  `encodedCard` names the card as the grantor. The grant also stops as soon as the card is no longer
  exiled encoded on it, and any move clears `encodedOn`.

**Tests.** 9 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- encoded, the spell resolves and the card is exiled on the creature chosen;
- with its own question, each answer goes where it belongs;
- not encoded, it goes to the graveyard;
- the creature connects: a free copy is offered, cast, counted, resolved and gone, and the card
  stays encoded;
- declined, the copy is gone and nothing moves;
- only that creature, and not once it has left and come back;
- the card leaves exile: it is no longer encoded and the creature loses the ability;
- a cast copy leaves the stack and stops existing, and is never encoded.

Faults injected by hand: 9 of 11 caught. The first round missed five. Two were redundant code,
