## D937 — "Can't be blocked by more than one creature", and the sea creatures

Two combat restrictions from the corpus tally of single unread lines:
- "~ can't be blocked by more than one creature." (CR 509.1b): 9 cards with it as their only
  unread line, and Aura and Equipment riders.
- "~ can't attack unless defending player controls an Island." (CR 508.1c): 12 cards, the sea
  creatures, and one each for Swamp, Mountain and Forest.

25 legal cards now read whole.

How it is read:
- **`blockedByOne`**, a printed combat static beside lure (`COMBAT_STATICS`). It is also a
  continuous-effect field, so the attachment rider "… and can't be blocked by more than one
  creature" hands it out. `singleBlockSatisfied`, menace's opposite, refuses a declaration with two
  blockers on it.
- **The blocking-requirement search (D913) keeps it as a restriction**: a lure on such a creature is
  met by exactly one blocker, as CR 509.1c asks (the most requirements obeyed without breaking a
  restriction).
- **The computer's gang block** skips such an attacker, so its gang goes on the next one worth
  killing instead of on a plan the engine would refuse.
- **`attacksOnlyIfDefenderHas`**, a basic land type read off the printed line. `attackAimIssue`
  refuses an attack at a player without one, so `legalDefenders` offers only the others.
  `canAttack` refuses the attacker outright when no opponent has one, so it is neither offered nor
  forced. The test is the land's live subtype, so a land that became an Island counts.
- Losing all abilities clears both.

**Tests.** 10 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- one blocker is legal, two are not;
- the computer never gangs it;
- with a second big attacker, the gang goes on that one;
- against a lure, exactly one blocks;
- an Aura hands it out;
- the Serpent attacks only a player with an Island;
- in a pod, only the players with one;
- losing all abilities loses both.

Faults injected by hand: 10 of 10 caught. The first round missed four:
- the ability-loss reset and the per-defender check: pinned by new tests;
- the gang guard: illegal plans are dropped when scored, so it only matters when another attacker
  can take the gang, which is now tested;
- a separate land-type check: removed (a basic land type is only ever a land's).

Pod sweep, seeds 62001–62010 on the D931 build: 520 pods, all decided.

    engine tests: 4,995, all passing

Coverage: 12,046 of 31,743 cards (+25), 31,839 of 59,509 lines (+50). Staples: 239 of 244.

## D938 — "You control enchanted creature"

Control Magic's family (CR 613.1b): 40 legal Auras print "You control enchanted creature"
(permanent, artifact, land, enchantment). 18 now read whole.

How it is read:
- **The compiler** reads the line on an Aura as `AuraDef.controls`. Such an Aura is never marked
  friendly, whatever else it does to its host, and it is marked `removesACreature`, so the computer
  aims it at the other side. Hypnotic Siren's "+1/+1 and flying" does not make it a card for your own
  creature.
- **Control here is which battlefield a permanent is on**, so this is a move that must be undone,
  not a modification. A new pass in `settle`, `auraControl`, keeps it true. Each control Aura that
  takes a permanent leaves a `permanent` effect sourced on itself with `controlRevertTo`, the seat
  it took it from.
- **Several such effects on one permanent are a chain in timestamp order** (CR 613.7), and the
  newest Aura's controller has the permanent:
  - an effect whose Aura has left, been moved onto something else or lost its abilities is dropped;
  - if that effect was the newest, the permanent goes back; if not, the next one up inherits its
    seat, so the last to go still returns the permanent to the right player;
  - an attached Aura whose controller does not control its permanent takes it, unless a newer one
    holds it.
- **One pass, before effects expire**, which covers every way an Aura arrives or leaves, an Aura
  that changes hands, and a creature an end-of-turn steal hands back while it is enchanted. The
  control change makes the permanent summoning sick for its new controller, as `relocate` already
  does for any change of control.

**Tests.** 12 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- the creature is the Aura controller's, and summoning sick;
- the Aura leaves: it goes back;
- the creature leaves: the Aura goes and nothing is owed;
- the Aura changes hands, twice, and the creature follows and finally goes home;
- the Aura is moved onto another creature;
- the Aura loses its abilities;
- two control Auras, the newer leaving first;
- two control Auras, the older leaving first;
- the older Aura never takes it back from the newer one, whichever seat is asked first;
- a helpful rider does not make it friendly;
- the computer aims it at the other side.

Faults injected by hand: 11 of 12 caught. The first version let the first Aura's hold stand, which
is not the rule (the newer one wins). The two-Aura tests showed it, and the pass was rewritten as
the chain above. The one fault left is equivalent: skipping the hand-back when a newer Aura remains
gives the same end state, because the take step in the same pass hands the permanent straight to
the newer Aura.

    engine tests: 5,007, all passing

Coverage: 12,064 of 31,743 cards (+18), 31,872 of 59,509 lines (+33). Staples: 239 of 244.

## D940 — Printed cost modifiers

"Instant and sorcery spells you cast cost {1} less to cast." (Goblin Electromancer's line, 15 legal
cards), "Noncreature spells cost {1} more to cast." (Thalia's), "Dragon spells you cast cost {1}
less", "Spells your opponents cast cost {1} more", "Treefolk spells and Shaman spells you cast …"
(CR 601.2f). 173 legal cards print a line of the family. The engine has had `costModifiers` since
the hand-written Electromancer and Thalia, and `costChangeFor` serves the offer and the charge alike,
but the compiler had no reader for the line. 78 of the cards now read whole.

How it is read (`costModifierFromLine`):
- **Who it applies to**: "you cast" is the controller, "your opponents cast" the others, and nothing
  named is everyone, its controller included, as Thalia is.
- **The kind of spell**, as a test of the card being cast:
  - nothing ("Spells …");
  - "instant and sorcery";
  - words that must all hold ("white creature", "noncreature"): a colour, a card type, "legendary",
    "multicolored"/"colorless", a "non-" of any of those, a creature type (through
    `cardHasSubtype`, so a changeling card counts), or Aura, Equipment, Vehicle, Lesson or Arcane;
  - two kinds joined by "… spells and … spells" apply to either.
- **Only generic mana moves**, so a coloured change ("cost {B} more") stays unread, and so do a
  counted one ("for each …"), a conditional one ("As long as it's not your turn"), and
  "face-down creature spells". An ability word in front is only a name.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the cards read, and the coloured and face-down lines stay unread;
- instant and sorcery spells, its controller's only;
- cast for less: the play shows the change, and one Mountain pays the rest;
- everyone, and opponents only;
- a creature type, a changeling, and two kinds joined by "and".

Faults injected by hand: 10 of 10 caught.

    engine tests: 5,016, all passing

attacks or has the counter. "Other creatures you control with flying" is left out: a filter on a

## D942 — Blocking more than one attacker

"~ can block an additional creature each combat." (17 legal lines), "~ can block any number of
creatures." (8), and "an additional seven / ninety-nine creatures" (CR 509.1a). 15 legal cards now
read whole.

How it is read:
- **`extraBlocks`**, a printed characteristic: 1, the spelled-out N, or Infinity for any number.
  Losing all abilities clears it.
- **The declaration** lets such a creature be named as the blocker of that many attackers, each
  once. The refusal names the limit ("can block only 2 creatures"), and an ordinary creature keeps
  its one-attacker refusal.
- **Its damage is split** (CR 510.1d). A creature blocking several attackers divides its combat
  damage among them: lethal to each in the order the attacks were declared (1 with deathtouch), and
  the rest to the last. The blocking player does not choose the split; this is the order most often
  picked, and it is stated here rather than asked. A blocker of one attacker deals its power as
  before.
- **Not done**: the table's blocking screen still assigns one attacker per blocker, and the
  computer still blocks one attacker each. The engine accepts the larger declarations from either.
  The activated "can block an additional creature this turn" (2 cards) is not read.

**Tests.** 8 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- one more: two attackers, not three, each once, and an ordinary creature still one;
- any number, and a spelled-out number;
- the split: lethal to the first, the rest to the next;
- what is left all goes to the last;
- lifelink shows the whole split (2 and 3, not 2 and 2);
- deathtouch kills two with two points;
- nothing left for the second: it is dealt no damage.

Faults injected by hand: 8 of 8 caught, after the second round. The first missed three:
- the remainder rule and deathtouch: pinned with a lifelink blocker and a deathtouch one;
- a guard against a zero share: a no-op, removed.

    engine tests: 5,029, all passing

Coverage: 12,239 of 31,743 cards (+15), 32,170 of 59,509 lines (+20). Staples: 239 of 244.

## D943 — Activation caps, stronger-only blockers, and Arrest

Three shapes from the corpus tally of single unread lines.

**"Activate no more than twice each turn."** (CR 602.5f, 5 cards with it as their last unread line,
"three times" alongside). `AbilityDef.timesEachTurn` is the once-each-turn rule with a number:
- the activation records a count on the new `CardInstance.abilityUseCount`, beside the turn
  `abilityUsedTurn` already keeps;
- one function, `usesLeftThisTurn`, answers both limits for the offer and for the activation, so
  the two cannot disagree;
- the count starts again on a new turn, because it only counts while the recorded turn is the
  current one.

**"Creatures with power less than ~'s power can't block it."** (5 cards): a printed combat static,
`weakerCantBlock`. `canBlock` compares the two powers as they are now, and equal power may block.

**Arrest's rider**, "Enchanted creature can't attack or block, and its activated abilities can't be
activated." (CR 602.5a). A new continuous-effect field, `cantActivate`:
- it is read as the Aura rider and is harmful, so the computer aims it at the other side;
- the permanent is skipped in every activation offer and refused in the activation path;
- its mana abilities are switched off too: `manaSources` and the potential-mana count skip it, so
  the Elf under Arrest pays for nothing.

Six Arrest-family Auras now read. "… unless they're mana abilities" (Faith's Fetters) and detain,
which is the same effect until your next turn, are not read yet.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- twice, then neither offered nor accepted, and again on another turn;
- a Bear cannot block the 4-power creature and an Ogre can;
- Arrest stops attacking, blocking, the mana ability and its activation.

Faults injected by hand: 13 of 13 caught. Two assertions in the first draft read a field that does
not exist (`legalActions(...).abilities`) and passed vacuously. They now read `plays` and fail when
they should.

    engine tests: 5,033, all passing

## D729 — Path of Ancestry: a trigger for how its mana is spent

"{T}: Add one mana of any color in your commander's color identity. When that mana is spent to cast
a creature spell that shares a creature type with your commander, scry 1."

How it is read:
- **The mana** is the line before the rider, read by the mana-line reader as Command Tower's is
  (D617): one ability per colour in the commander's identity.
- **The rider is a new kind of trigger, `TriggerDef.whenManaSpent`.** It is flagged `delayed`, so
  no event fires it. The cast does:
  - `payFrom` already reports which sources it tapped to pay for the spell;
  - when one of them has the rider, and the spell is a creature sharing a creature type with a
    commander of its caster, the trigger goes on the stack above the spell;
  - its "scry 1" is the existing scry reader (`manaSpentScryTrigger`).
- `compile.ts` reads a mana line followed by this rider as the mana abilities plus the trigger.
- The rider is also found when another card grants it (`grantedTriggers`, D251), pushed with its
  grantor as automation pushes any granted trigger. The guards caught the first draft reading only
  the printed list.
- **Known limitation.** Mana tapped from Path by hand and left floating has lost its source by the
  time it is spent, so it doesn't trigger. Only mana the payment taps Path for does. The
  automatic payer does that whenever Path is the source it uses, which is how the bot and the
  "cast" button pay.

Staples went from 239 to 240 (Path of Ancestry).

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- paying for an Elf with an Elf commander taps Path and puts "scry 1" on the stack above the
  spell, which asks the scry question when it resolves;
- a Bear (no shared type) triggers nothing, and neither does mana tapped from Path by hand first.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught.

    engine tests: 5,039, all passing (merged with the other session's D943 and D944)

Coverage: 12,270 of 31,743 cards (+1), 32,214 of 59,509 lines (+1), against 958aade. Staples: 240
of 244 (+1).

## D948 — Reflexive triggers: "When you do, …"

The clause tally of single-unread-line cards put "you may pay {M}. When you do, …" near the top:
178 legal cards had a "When you do" sentence as their only unread line. "When you do" is a reflexive
triggered ability (CR 603.12). It triggers when the first half has been done, and chooses its
targets then, after the payment and not before. The engine had no such trigger.

How it is read:
- **A new trigger kind, `reflexive`**, raised by nothing on the board. Its `key` is the printed text
  of its effect.
- **The compiler** (`optionalEffect`, from the trigger reader only) reads "you may X. When you do,
  Y" as the existing "you may X. If you do, Y", with Y replaced by an effect that queues the
  reflexive trigger. Y's own reading, with its targets and questions, becomes the trigger and is
  added to the card's triggers. So every "may" shape already read (a price, a sacrifice, a discard,
  a plain yes) can be the first half.
- **The engine**: the queue is `GameState.reflexive`. `settle` drains it with the other event lists
  and hands each entry to `fireTrigger`, with the trigger found on its card by key. Targets are
  asked as for any trigger, after the payment, and the first half's subject is carried, so "it"
  means the same in both halves.
- **Refused**: every other caller of `optionalEffect` still refuses "When you do", because only the
  trigger reader adds the second trigger to the card. A "When you do" with no "may" in front ("sacrifice
  it. When you do, …") is not read yet, nor is one whose second half does not read on its own (29
  of the "you may pay" lines).

24 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the card reads, its second half is a trigger of its own, and a "when you do" with no "may" stays
  unread;
- paid: asked to pay with nothing aimed, then the reflexive trigger asks for its target, and the
  effect lands;
- declined: nothing is aimed and nothing happens;
- two on one card: each "when you do" fires its own half;
- a "may" that asks a question: discarded, then the draw.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught, after one redundant check (the key compared again in
`triggerMatches`, where the trigger was already chosen by key) was simplified away and the
two-trigger test added.

    engine tests: 5,055, all passing

Coverage: 12,325 of 31,743 cards (+24), 32,290 of 59,509 lines (+31). Staples: 240 of 244 (the
other session's Path of Ancestry, merged in D947's merge).

## D730 — Torment of Hailfire and Perforating Artist: a punisher in rounds

"Repeat the following process X times. Each opponent loses 3 life unless that player sacrifices a
nonland permanent or discards a card." Perforating Artist prints the same sentence once, behind a
raid end-step trigger.

How it is read (`punisherRounds`):
- **Three questions per opponent per round**, in turn order:
  - lose the life, sacrifice, or discard, offering only what that player can do (losing the life
    is always offered);
  - which nonland permanent;
  - which card.
  The second and third have no candidates for anyone who didn't choose them, and an empty question
  is answered without asking.
- **A round takes effect as the next round is reached** (the D721 hook, with D728's answers), so
  each round sees the board and the hand the last one left. The last round takes effect with the
  spell. `AutomationState.punisher` holds the round bookkeeping and is cleared by the spell.
- **Rounds past X are not asked.** The rounds are a fixed list of questions, so there is a ceiling
  of 40. X above it repeats only 40 times, a known limit no realistic game reaches.
- `clausesOf` joins "Repeat the following process X times." to the sentence it is about. "Of their
  choice" (the Artist's wording) is read too.
- **The bot**, as the player choosing, loses the life while it has more than 9, then discards while
  it has cards, then sacrifices; it gives up the cheapest card or permanent.

Staples went from 240 to 241 (Torment of Hailfire).

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- Torment and the Artist read;
- two rounds against one opponent: the sacrificed Rock is gone before round two is asked, round
  two offers only the life and the discard, and the discard is chosen from hand;
- with nothing to sacrifice or discard, the life alone is taken every round, unasked (X = 3,
  9 life); and choosing the life twice costs 6;
- at a table of three, each opponent answers for themselves every round (one discards then has
  nothing left; the other loses the life then discards);
- X of 0 asks nothing;
- the bot loses life above 9 and discards at 6.

Faults injected by script: 9 of 9 caught.

    engine tests: 5,061, all passing (merged with the other session's D948)

Coverage: 12,328 of 31,743 cards (+2), 32,294 of 59,509 lines (+2), against 5e56eeb. Staples: 241
of 244 (+1).

## D949 — "You may sacrifice another creature", and "sacrifice it. When you do"

Two first halves D948 could not take.

**"You may sacrifice another creature"**, with "If you do" or "When you do" after it. The sacrifice
reader asks its question through a function, because "another" needs the source and a filter is
not handed one. `optionalEffect` refused any function-shaped question, because it gates a question
by adding `askOnlyIfChosen` to it and could not see inside a function. It now wraps the function, so
what it returns carries the gate, and declining still asks nothing. The same change covers every
other "another" question behind a "may".

**"Sacrifice it. When you do, …"**: the one first half without a "may", on the enchantments that
sacrifice themselves as they enter (the tri-colour land fetchers) or on their last plan counter. The
reflexive trigger is queued only if the permanent was on the battlefield to be sacrificed.

Still unread: "that creature's power" in the second half (Bolg's and others' sacrificed creature),
which needs the sacrificed creature remembered into the reflexive trigger.

18 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- sacrifice another creature: never itself, and then the reflexive target is destroyed;
- declined: with two candidates the sacrifice is never asked about, and nothing is aimed;
- "If you do" with sacrifice another creature: the draw comes with the sacrifice;
- "sacrifice it. When you do": it goes, and then the draw.

Superseded row: D465's "still cannot read 'you may return another'" (#337, Aviary Mechanic) now asserts the
reading.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught. The gate on the wrapped question was missed until the
decline test had two candidates: with one, the engine answers the question itself, which hid
whether it was ever asked.

    engine tests: 5,060, all passing

Coverage: 12,343 of 31,743 cards (+18), 32,315 of 59,509 lines (+25). Staples: 240 of 244.

## D950 — "That creature's power" after a sacrifice, in a reflexive trigger

"You may sacrifice another creature. When you do, ~ deals damage equal to that creature's power to
any target." "That creature" is the one sacrificed, as it last was on the battlefield (CR 608.2h).

How it is read:
- With a sacrifice in the first half, "that creature's power / toughness / mana value" in the second
  is read as D586's cost phrase, "the sacrificed creature's power". That phrase is answered from the
  stack object's `sacrificedStats`, which a cost sacrifice already fills.
- The first half's effect records, before it runs, what each candidate was: the source (for
  "sacrifice it") and every card an answer named, with live power and toughness, counters included,
  and printed mana value. The one that left the battlefield is written onto the queued reflexive
  entry (`sacrificed`), and `settle` puts it on the stack object as the trigger goes on the stack.

1 legal card now reads whole. Most lines of this shape stop elsewhere (Bolg's amass, for one), but
the reading is the machinery they need.

**Tests.** 1 engine test: the card reads; an Ogre with a +1/+1 counter is sacrificed, and the
reflexive trigger deals 4 (not its printed 3) to the chosen player.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught (the record never written, printed instead of live power,
never put on the stack object, and the phrase read without the sacrifice context).

    engine tests: 5,061, all passing

Coverage: 12,344 of 31,743 cards (+1), 32,316 of 59,509 lines (+1). Staples: 240 of 244.

## D951 — "You may exile it. If you do / When you do", from the graveyard

The listing of "When you do" lines still unread showed second halves the reader already reads
("return target creature card from your graveyard to your hand"); the first halves were the gap.
The commonest is a card exiling itself from where its trigger left it: "When ~ dies, you may exile
it. If you do, …" (18 legal lines with it as their only unread line).

How it is read:
- **"Exile it" / "exile this card" / "exile ~"**, a clause beside D466's "return it to its owner's
  hand", with that reader's zone guard: the card is exiled only if it is still where the trigger's
  subject zone says. A card that moved on is a new object and stays (CR 400.7).
- **"If you do" may now point at something** when the first half asks nothing. The ability's
  targets are chosen as it goes on the stack (CR 603.3d), before the yes or no, which is when a
  trigger chooses them here. With a first half that asks a question, the order of the two still
  cannot be stated, so that stays refused.
- **"If you do" means it was done.** A question-less first half used to count as done the moment
  "yes" was given. Now it counts only if it changed the board. "You may exile it" when the card has
  already left returns the board untouched, and then the second half does not happen either
  (CR 608.2c). No earlier test relied on the old meaning.

16 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- yes: exiled and the draw follows; no: it stays and nothing is drawn;
- gone from the graveyard before it resolves: nothing exiled, so nothing drawn;
- "If you do" with a target: the target is asked as it triggers, before the yes or no, and comes
  back.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 5,071, all passing

Coverage: 12,360 of 31,743 cards (+16), 32,341 of 59,509 lines (+25). Staples: 241 of 244 (the
other session's Torment of Hailfire, merged after D950).

## D952 — "You may X. If you do, Y" in the middle of a spell

"~ deals 3 damage to any target. You may discard a card. If you do, draw a card." `optionalEffect`
reads "you may X. If you do, Y" when it is a whole trigger body, but a spell's sentences are cut
apart by `clausesOf`, and "If you do, draw a card" alone has nothing to refer to.

How it is read:
- `clausesOf` holds a "You may X." sentence and the "If you do, Y." after it together as one clause,
  wherever they stand in the line.
- `composeEffects` hands such a clause to `optionalEffect` when the plain reading refuses it. The
  "may" is then one part of the sequence, its question the resolution's own. The composer's rule
  that at most one part reads its own answers still applies.
- A modal bullet is such a line, so Witherbloom Charm's "You may sacrifice a permanent. If you do,
  draw two cards" now reads as a mode. D525 had left it out as untried, and the engine test below
  plays all three answers inside the mode.

8 legal cards now read whole. "You may put a card from your hand on the bottom of your library"
(Fiery Temper's kin) is not a clause the reader has yet.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read, the modal bullet included;
- the damage, then the may: yes discards and draws, no does neither, and the damage lands either
  way;
- in a mode: yes sacrifices and draws two, no does nothing, and the other mode still draws one.

Superseded row: D525's "refuses a modal bullet" now asserts the reading.

Faults injected by hand: 3 of 3 caught (the glue removed, restored as the wrong punctuation, and the
composer's route switched off).

    engine tests: 5,074, all passing

Coverage: 12,368 of 31,743 cards (+8), 32,354 of 59,509 lines (+13). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D953 — Two targeting sentences in one line

"Target creature gets +2/+2 until end of turn. Another target creature gets -2/-2 until end of
turn." "Destroy target creature. ~ deals 2 damage to target player or planeswalker." "Target
player draws two cards. Put a +1/+1 counter on up to one target creature you control." 154 legal
lines print two targeting sentences, and `composeEffects` refused every one. The reason was sound:
a resolution has one `targets` list, and two parts reading it would act on the same object.

How it is read:
- **The specs are concatenated**, and each targeting part reads its own slice of the targets,
  counted from the specs before it.
- **A target that has gone keeps its place.** `resolveTop` drops targets that are no longer the
  object chosen (CR 608.2b), which shifts every position after it, so the second sentence would have
  acted on the first sentence's slot. It now also records `StackObject.targetSlots`, the targets as
  chosen with `null` for the gone ones, and the context carries it (through `aboutNow`). A part
  slices from there, so the -2/-2 still lands on its own creature when the +2/+2's was blinked.
- **Positions are a fact of the text only when every spec but the last asks an exact number**, so
  an "up to" anywhere but last is refused. So is a targeting part that asks a question (its "target
  player" would be read off the whole list), one that divides, a possessive borrow, and a blink.
  The engine's existing rule that one object is never chosen twice in a resolution keeps "another
  target creature" apart.

39 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read, and an "up to" before the last spec stays unread;
- each sentence acts on its own target;
- the first target blinked before it resolves: the second still gets its own -2/-2;
- "up to one" last: chosen gets the counter, left out the draw alone.

Superseded rows: three refusals in `compile.test.ts` now assert the two-spec reading. They are
Two Targets, the "destroy target creature and destroy target enchantment" conjunction, and D454's
Consume Strength pair.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught.

    engine tests: 5,078, all passing

Coverage: 12,407 of 31,743 cards (+39), 32,414 of 59,509 lines (+60). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D954 — A card from your hand to the bottom of your library

"You may put a card from your hand on the bottom of your library. If you do, draw a card" (Fiery
Temper-style sorceries and their cycle-mates). "Draw two cards, then put a card from your hand on
the bottom of your library." "Draw three cards, then put two cards from your hand on the bottom of
your library." There was no clause for the sentence, so each of these lines was unread.

How it is read:
- **One clause reader, beside the discard.** It asks the same question from the same zone,
  "a / one / two / three cards", and moves the cards picked to the bottom of the owner's library.
  A new `putOnBottomOfLibrary` in `effects.ts` is the sibling of `putOnTopOfLibrary`.
- **Nothing special for the draw first.** `composeEffects` already splits a chain at its first
  question and runs what comes before it in `beforeDecisions` (D418). So the cards just drawn are
  in the hand the question is planned against. A test pins it: the two cards drawn are among the
  candidates, and the one picked ends at the bottom.
- **Two or more go in the order picked**, each to the bottom, so the last one picked is the bottom
  card. The owner orders them (CR 401.4).
- **The "may … If you do" form** goes through `optionalEffect`, as the discard does (D952).

5 legal cards now read whole, the enters-trigger form ("When this creature enters, draw two cards,
then put two cards …") among them. Still unread: the one with a condition in the middle ("Then if
you don't control a legendary creature, put …"), "put any number of cards … then draw that many
plus one", and the digital-only seek line.

Pod sweep on D953 (seeds 63001–63005; the worker restarted after two passes, so the last three
were re-run as 63003–63005): 260 pods, all decided, none threw.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the three cards read;
- the may: yes puts the picked card on the bottom and draws, no does neither;
- draw first: the drawn cards are offered, and the one picked goes to the bottom;
- two cards go in the order picked.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught.

    engine tests: 5,082, all passing

Coverage: 12,412 of 31,743 cards (+5), 32,421 of 59,509 lines (+7). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D955 — A mode whose first half comes before its question

A fix, found while reading D954's chain split. `composeEffects` puts everything before a chain's
first question into `beforeDecisions` (D418), and spells, abilities and triggers all carry that
half. A **mode** did not: `ModeDef` had no such field, and `modalScriptFor` built each mode from
`targets`, `decisions` and `effect` only. So a bullet like "~ deals 2 damage to target creature.
Scry 1." read whole and did only the scry, and "Draw two cards, then discard a card" discarded from
a hand that never drew. Nothing reported it, because the card counted as read.

The fix:
- **`ModeDef.beforeDecisions`**, carried by `modalScriptFor`. `beforeDecisionsFor` in
  `automation.ts` runs the chosen mode's half when exactly one mode was chosen.
- **Only where exactly one mode can be chosen.** With two chosen, the second mode's first half
  would have to run after the first mode's questions, and the engine plans every question before
  anything runs. So "choose two", "one or both", "one or more", the Will cycle's commander clause
  and entwine all refuse a mode that has such a half, rather than reorder it.

That refusal costs 2 legal cards that had been reading whole and playing wrong:
- Artistic Refusal: "Draw two cards, then discard a card" as one of "one or both", so it discarded
  without drawing.
- Avengers Disassembled: "Destroy target land. Its controller may search …", whose destroy was
  dropped, so the land stayed.

Both are now honestly unread. Reading them needs the chosen modes split at their first question at
resolution time, which is not done yet.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- reads whole as "choose one", and stays unread as "one or both" or entwined;
- the damage mode deals its damage, then scries;
- the draw mode draws before the question, so a card just drawn can be the one discarded.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught. The entwine refusal was missed at first and is now pinned
by its own assertion.

    engine tests: 5,085, all passing

Coverage: 12,410 of 31,743 cards (−2), 32,415 of 59,509 lines (−6): the two cards above, now
counted as what they are. Staples: 241 of 244.

## D956 — "You may gain N life"

"At the beginning of your upkeep, you may gain 1 life." "When this creature enters, you may gain 3
life." `optionalEffect` strips "you may" and reads the rest, and "gain 3 life" alone is not a
sentence any reader takes: the life reader reads "you gain 3 life", which is how the indicative is
printed. So every one of these lines was unread, while "you may draw a card" read, because the draw
reader accepts a bare "draw".

The fix is one line: an inner clause that does not read is tried once more with "you" in front.
Putting back the printed subject cannot change what a clause means, so it is not limited to the
bare "may". A first version was limited to it, but no test could tell the limit was there, so it
was removed. Logged across the whole corpus, every clause that now reads this way is a life gain:
"gain N life", "gain life equal to the number of charge counters on …", "gain life equal to the
number of Allies you control".

25 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests: the card reads; it asks, and gains the life only on a yes.

Faults injected by hand: 2 of 2 caught.

    engine tests: 5,087, all passing

Coverage: 12,435 of 31,743 cards (+25), 32,443 of 59,509 lines (+28). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D957 — "You may have X get / discard / lose …"

"When this creature enters, you may have target creature get -2/-2 until end of turn." "… you may
have target opponent discard a card." "… you may have target player lose 2 life." D574 read the
causative for one verb: "you may have it deal 1 damage" becomes "it deals 1 damage" behind a
yes-or-no. Every other verb after "have" stayed unread.

The fix widens that rule to the verbs whose third person is a plain "-s": deal, get, discard,
lose, mill, gain and sacrifice. "Have target creature get -2/-2" is read as "target creature gets
-2/-2", and the question is still asked in the card's own words. Logged across the corpus, what
now reads this way:
- "have target creature get -N/-N / +N/+N / +N/-N until end of turn";
- "have target opponent / target player / that player discard a card";
- "mill a card", "lose N life", "sacrifice a creature";
- "have target creature gain / lose flying until end of turn";
- "have each opponent lose N life".

Every one means what the card says. "Draw" was in the first list and no card used it, so it was
taken out.

Still unread: "you may have it fight target creature you don't control" (5 lines). "It fights …"
does not read on its own yet, only "target creature you control fights …". The "~'s base power
becomes" family is unread too.

18 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read, and so do the discard, mill, sacrifice and gain-flying forms;
- -2/-2 on a yes kills a 2/2, and on a no it lives;
- the target player loses the life only on a yes.

Faults injected by hand: 6 of 6 caught, across two rounds.

    engine tests: 5,090, all passing

Coverage: 12,453 of 31,743 cards (+18), 32,461 of 59,509 lines (+18). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D958 — A creature fighting from its own trigger

"When this creature enters, it fights up to one target creature you don't control." "When ~ enters,
you may have it fight target creature you don't control." The fight reader (D542) read two targets
fighting each other. When the first creature is the permanent printing the trigger, there is one
target, and the line was unread.

How it is read:
- **A self reader beside "sacrifice it"**, in `selfEffect`: "it" or the card's own name fights one
  target creature. It uses the same `fight` helper as Prey Upon, so both powers are read before
  either damage is dealt (CR 701.12a), and the damage comes from the creatures, not the trigger.
- **The battlefield only, checked again as it resolves.** If the creature has left by then, it is
  not on the battlefield to fight, so neither creature deals damage (CR 701.12b). A gone target is
  dropped by the targeting rules already.
- **"Have it fight"** comes through the causative (D957), with "fight" added to its verbs.

Still unread:
- the spell form where "it" is an earlier target ("Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you
  control. Then it fights target creature an opponent controls"), which is D542's open referent
  case;
- "chosen at random";
- "have ~ fight that creature".

10 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- a 3/3 and a 2/2 deal their power to each other;
- the creature gone before the trigger resolves means no fight, and the bear is unharmed;
- "you may have it fight": a no fights nothing, a yes fights.

Faults injected by hand: 5 of 5 caught.

    engine tests: 5,094, all passing

Coverage: 12,463 of 31,743 cards (+10), 32,479 of 59,509 lines (+18). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D959 — "Then it fights / that creature deals damage equal to its power to"

"Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control. Then it fights target creature an opponent
controls." "… Then that creature deals damage equal to its power to target creature you don't
control." D542 left every such referent unread: the second sentence borrows the first's target and
also declares one of its own, and `referentEffect` supplies exactly one object. D608 then read one
spelling of it whole: a pump, then "it fights / bites".

How it is read now:
- **In `composeEffects`, as its own targeting part.** After exactly one earlier targeting part that
  aims at exactly one creature, the clause "(then) it / that creature fights / deals damage equal to
  its power to <target>" declares its target, and its first creature is slot 0 of the full target
  list. D953's slicing gives each part its own targets. The slicing wrapper now also passes the full
  list as `targetSlots`, so this part can see the earlier one.
- **The first creature gone means nothing happens.** If it has left by resolution, its slot is
  empty, so there is no fight and no bite (CR 701.12b). The other creature is not taken in its
  place.
- **Damage from the creature**, credited to its controller, as `selfBite`'s is.
- **D608's `pumpThenBiteResolution` deleted.** Two readers for one sentence is what D441
  collapses, and the general one is also more correct. D608 read its targets with `cardTargets`,
  which shifts when the first target has gone, so the creature it meant to fight would have been
  taken as the one it pumped. D608's own tests pass on the composed reading. Its compile row's
  "Then that creature …" refusal now asserts the reading.
- **Two earlier targets stay unread**: "it" then means the later one, not slot 0.

10 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests, plus D608's existing ones on the new path:
- the cards read, and a line with two earlier targets stays unread;
- the counter, then the fight: a 3/3 kills a 0/3 and takes nothing back;
- the first creature gone before resolution: no fight, and the second is not taken for it;
- the bite is one way and from the creature; with "up to one" left out, the counter still goes on.

Faults injected by hand: 7. 6 were caught. The seventh was a zone check that a gone target's empty
slot already covers, and it was removed. One of the six, the one-earlier-target guard, was missed
at first and is now pinned.

    engine tests: 5,098, all passing

Coverage: 12,473 of 31,743 cards (+10), 32,489 of 59,509 lines (+10). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D960 — "Target … that player controls" after combat damage, and "defending player controls"

"Whenever ~ deals combat damage to a player, destroy target artifact that player controls."
"Whenever ~ attacks, tap target creature defending player controls." Neither target phrase read.
`parsedTargetPhrase`'s docblock gave the reason: a filter could not know which attack it was
about. But the filter is handed the source, and D913's provoke and D914's "blocks it if able"
already read the attacker's own attack off it.

How it is read:
- **A "defending player controls" suffix** on any target phrase: the phrase without it, narrowed
  to permanents the defending player controls.
- **"Defending player"** comes from `defendersOf`, shared with D914. It is the player the source's
  own attack is aimed at. For an Equipment or Aura, it is the attack of the creature the source is
  attached to. When neither is attacking (a spell, or an attacker already gone), it is each player
  a creature of the controller is attacking.
- **"That player controls" on "Whenever ~ deals combat damage to a player"** is rewritten to
  "defending player controls" in `triggerFromLine`. The player it hit is its attack's defender.

The stale note in `parsedTargetPhrase` is struck through.

Logged across the corpus, the new readings are each what the card says:
- attack triggers that tap, damage, bounce or shrink "target creature defending player controls",
  and the Equipment forms (Thunder Lasso, Heart-Piercer Bow, Greatsword of Tyr);
- "becomes blocked" (Rust Scarab), and Ancient Hellkite's activation while attacking;
- the combat-damage family: Caustic Wasps, Trygon Predator, Throat Slitter, Mistblade Shinobi,
  Schema Thief, Skirk Commando and Spark Mage through the D957 causative, and Blind Zealot's
  "sacrifice it. If you do".

Pod sweep on D959 (seeds 64001–64004): 208 pods, all decided.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read, with the attack and causative forms;
- at a table of three, only the artifacts of the player it hit can be chosen. That rules out its
  own, the third player's (another attacker of ours went there), and an enchantment on the hit
  player's side;
- an Equipment's trigger offers the equipped creature's defender only.

Superseded row: D469's list of refused target phrases had "destroy target creature defending
player controls"; it is taken off the list, with a note saying when.

Faults injected by hand: 5. 3 were caught at once. Two were missed and are now pinned: the
artifact filter, and "its own attack" rather than every defender.

    engine tests: 5,101, all passing

Coverage: 12,506 of 31,743 cards (+33), 32,529 of 59,509 lines (+40). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D961 — "… to a player or planeswalker", and "you mill"

"Whenever ~ deals combat damage to a player or planeswalker, draw a card": 9 legal lines print
the planeswalker form. The engine recorded a combat hit only when it landed on a player, so the
trigger had no event to hear.

How it is read:
- **A planeswalker hit is recorded**, in `hit` (combat.ts), on the same `dealtCombatDamage` list
  with a `planeswalker` flag, the walker's controller as `defender`, and the loyalty it lost as
  the amount. "Landed" means loyalty went down, so damage prevented by a shield records nothing.
- **Only "… or planeswalker" hears it.** The combat-damage event carries the flag, and
  `triggerMatches` refuses it unless the trigger has `orPlaneswalker`. The other readers of the
  list skip it: the one-or-more batch ("whenever one or more creatures you control deal combat
  damage to a player") and the monarch's crown (CR 720.5 is about a player).
- **The trigger form** is the existing self combat-damage prologue with "or planeswalker" and the
  flag.
- **Edge, stated:** a trampler that hits a planeswalker and its controller in one damage step
  would fire twice. The rules fire it once per damage event. It is rare enough to leave.
- **"You mill two cards"**: the self-mill reader now takes the printed subject.

The "player or battle" form (8 lines) stays unread, because battles are not in the engine.

6 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- a hit on a planeswalker: "or planeswalker" draws, "a player" does not, and loyalty goes 5 to 3;
- a planeswalker hit fires no "one or more … to a player" and takes no crown;
- damage to the planeswalker prevented: nothing landed, nothing drawn;
- a hit on the player: both draw, once;
- "you mill two cards" mills its controller.

Faults injected by hand: 7. 4 were caught at once. Three were missed and are now pinned: the batch
skip, the crown, and the prevented hit.

    engine tests: 5,107, all passing

Coverage: 12,512 of 31,743 cards (+6), 32,535 of 59,509 lines (+6). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D962 — One damage sentence, several targets

"~ deals 2 damage to target creature and 2 damage to target player or planeswalker." "~ deals 2
damage to any target and 1 damage to any other target" (Arc Trail). "~ deals 3 damage to any
target, 2 damage to another target, and 1 damage to a third target" (Cone of Flame). "~ deals 1
damage to each of two targets." "~ deals 2 damage to each of two target creatures." The two-sentence
spelling of each already read (D953). The one-sentence spelling did not.

How it is read:
- **`splitDamageClauses`**, run on the clause list before `composeEffects` reads it, turns
  "X deals A damage to P, B damage to Q, and C damage to R" into one damage sentence per target.
  D953's slicing gives each sentence its own target.
- **"Any other target", "another target" and "a third target" become "any target".** Every target
  of one resolution is already a different object (`checkTargets` refuses the same target twice),
  which is all those words add.
- **"Each of two targets"** becomes two "any target" sentences. **"Each of two / three target
  creatures"** is a new quantifier with an exact count, and the whole amount goes to each, through
  `damageEveryTarget`.

Logged across the corpus, the new readings are each what the card says:
- Arc Trail, Cone of Flame, Cunning Strike, Punish the Enemy and Reckless Rage;
- Chandra's Outrage, Neonate's Rush and Unleash Shell, through the possessive "that creature's
  controller";
- Jagged Lightning and Swelter;
- Furious Reprisal;
- the enters triggers "it deals 3 damage to target opponent and 1 damage to up to one target
  creature" (Burning Sun's Avatar, Rakdos Firewheeler).

22 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- "each of two targets": one damage to a player and one to a creature;
- each amount goes to its own target, and the same target cannot be chosen twice;
- "each of two target creatures": the whole amount to each;
- "… and 2 damage to that creature's controller", and three amounts to three targets.

Faults injected by hand: 5. 3 were caught at once. "Each of two targets" was missed and is now
pinned. A check that every split piece opens "N damage to" was redundant by construction, and was
removed.

    engine tests: 5,112, all passing

Coverage: 12,534 of 31,743 cards (+22), 32,559 of 59,509 lines (+24). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D963 — "Defending player" as the subject of an attack trigger

"Whenever ~ attacks, defending player loses 1 life and you gain 1 life." "… defending player
discards a card." "… defending player mills ten cards." "Whenever a creature you control attacks,
defending player loses 1 life." A combat-damage trigger's "that player" has read the player it hit
since D530, through `c.attacked`. An attack event hands down the same seat (its `attacked`). The
words "defending player", on an attack, were simply not a referent.

How it is read: **"defending player" is a referent pronoun** on a trigger whose events are all
attacks, attacks-unblocked or combat-damage hits. It is supplied from `c.attacked.defender`, and
its questions are re-aimed to the hit player (`'hit-player'`), so a discard or a "may" is asked of
the player attacked. "Becomes blocked" is not included: no `attacked` travels with it, and its one
printed edict already reads through D918's reader.

Logged across the corpus, the new readings are Agate-Blade Assassin, Campaign of Vengeance,
Leeching Sliver, Nemesis of Reason, Shrieking Specter, Silent Skimmer, Nefarox and Thraximundar's
edicts, and Harbor Guardian and Sibilant Spirit's "defending player may draw a card". Each means
what the card says.

10 legal cards now read whole.

- the cards read;
- the attacked player loses the life, not the other opponent;
- "defending player may draw": the attacked player is the one asked, and draws on a yes;
- the attacked player discards, not the other opponent.

## D964 — "That creature" on a trigger about another creature

"Whenever another creature you control enters, that creature gets +1/+1 until end of turn."
"… put a +1/+1 counter on that creature and it gains haste." The same clause with "it" already
read, and on these triggers "it" is the event's creature (`itMeans`). "That creature" was not
read as the same thing.

How it is read: on a trigger whose events are all about **another** creature (`who` any or
another), `triggerFromLine` reads the clause with "it" in place of "that creature". The printed
clause stays the description. Three limits:
- **Not on a trigger about its own creature.** On "Whenever ~ blocks a creature, that creature gets
  -1/-1", "that creature" is the one blocked and "it" would be ~. That line already reads
  correctly by its own path, and a test pins it.
- **No guard for a target earlier in the clause.** After a target, a bare "it" is that target
  (D723), which is what "that creature" meant. A first draft had such a guard, and fault injection
  showed it changed nothing.
- **Not where "that creature deals" damage.** This increment's own tests found that the "it deals
  …" readers deal from the watching card, not the event's creature. A lifelink creature entering
  under "that creature deals 1 damage to each opponent" gained nothing, and "damage equal to its
  power" read the enchantment's power. Those lines stay unread, and the tests assert it.

Logged across the corpus, every line that reads this way is right:
- counters and pumps on the entering or attacking creature;
- one "you may pay {1}. If you do, put a +1/+1 counter on that creature";
- one fight through D958's reader, which uses the event's creature;
- one "put a +1/+1 counter on target creature. That creature gains flying", where "it" is the
  target.

4 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the pump card reads, and the two "that creature deals" cards stay unread;
- the pump goes on the creature that entered;
- a target before it: the counter and haste go to the target, not the creature that entered;
- on a block trigger, the -1/-1 goes to the creature blocked, not the blocker.

Faults injected by hand: 7, across two rounds. The first round missed three: Banner's counter line
already read by another path (it is now a pump), the target guard was redundant (removed), and the
own-creature check was unpinned (now pinned by the block test). The second round caught 3 of 3.

    engine tests: 5,120, all passing

Coverage: 12,548 of 31,743 cards (+4), 32,582 of 59,509 lines (+5). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D965 — "It deals …" on a trigger about another creature: from that creature

A fix, found by D964's tests. The general damage reader (`damageEffect`) read its subject, "~" or
"it", and then dealt from `c.source`, the watching card, and took "its power" from it too. On a
trigger about another creature, "it" is that creature. So Warstorm Surge ("Whenever a creature you
control enters, it deals damage equal to its power to any target") read whole and dealt the
enchantment's power, 0, every time. A lifelink or deathtouch creature dealing "1 damage to each
opponent" this way would not have applied its keyword either. Warstorm Surge is the one legal card
printed that way. Nothing reported it, because the card counted as read.

How it is read now:
- **"It" is `itMeans`:** the event's creature where there is one, the source otherwise. It is both
  the damage source passed to the destination and the creature whose power "its power" reads.
- **The card's own name is always the source**: "this creature deals damage equal to its power"
  is its own power, even on a trigger about another creature.
- **D964's "that creature deals" exclusion is lifted.** It was there only because of this.

2 more legal cards now read whole, and Warstorm Surge now plays correctly.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests, and D964's "that creature deals" test:
- the damage is from the creature that entered, so its lifelink gains the life;
- "this enchantment deals": the source is still the enchantment, so no lifelink;
- "this creature deals damage equal to its power": its own 1, not the entered 3/3's;
- "damage equal to its power" is the entered 3/3's;
- on its own death trigger, "it" is still the card itself;
- D964's: "that creature deals", with the lifelink and the power.

Faults injected by hand: 4. 3 were caught at once. The named-subject case was missed twice: the
first pin exercised the source but not the power. The own-power test now catches it.

    engine tests: 5,126, all passing

Coverage: 12,550 of 31,743 cards (+2), 32,585 of 59,509 lines (+3). Staples: 241 of 244.

## D967 — "Exile a creature card from your graveyard" as an additional cost

"As an additional cost to cast this spell, exile a creature card from your graveyard"
(Headless Skaab, Cobbled Lancer and four more), and "… exile two creature cards …" (Skaab
Goliath). The same cost on an activated ability has read since D613. On a spell it was unread.

How it is read:
- **A new `additionalCost` variant, `exileFromGraveyard`**, with exactly D613's shape and its
  grammar ("a / one … five", an optional kind read by `graveyardKind`).
- **Offered only when it can be paid** (CR 601.2h). `legalActions` asks `graveyardCostPlan`, and
  a spell whose graveyard holds too few is not offered. The reason says how many of what.
- **Paid as the spell is cast**, in `castSpell`, after any delve: the cards are exiled before
  anybody may respond, and never the spell itself. The engine chooses them with D613's plan, which
  keeps cards with flashback or escape back where it can, as it does for abilities.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- with no creature card in the graveyard it is not offered, and refused if tried;
- cast: the creature card is exiled as it is cast, the artifact stays, and it draws two.

Superseded row: `compile.test.ts` listed "exile a creature card from your graveyard" among the

## D969 — "Destroy that creature at end of combat": the basilisks

"Whenever ~ blocks or becomes blocked by a creature, destroy that creature at end of combat"
(Tangle Asp, Venomous Dragonfly), "… by a non-Wall creature …" (Cockatrice, Rock Basilisk and one
more), and "… by a nonblack creature …" (Deathgazer, Dread Specter and one more). Thicket Basilisk
is hand-written this way. The compiler had no clause for it.

How it is read:
- **A fourth engine-known delayed ability, `destroy`** (D696's family, beside sacrifice, exile and
  to-hand). It destroys its subject at end of combat if it is still on the battlefield, and does
  nothing to a creature that has left.
- **"Destroy that creature at end of combat"** in `eventRelativeEffect`, on the block events, where
  "that creature" is `c.blocked`. It schedules the other creature for that ability.
- **The filtered forms** in `triggerFromLine`: the same two block triggers, with the filter asked
  of the other creature live as the trigger resolves, as the hand-written card's Wall check is. A
  negated creature type ("non-Wall") is read directly. Any other filter goes through the target
  reader ("nonblack"). "Green or white" (one card) is not a filter it reads, and stays unread.

- **Thicket Basilisk, hand-written, now uses the same factory** (`basiliskTriggers`). Its compiled
  reading appeared in `compiled-vs-written` as a new disagreement: its old three triggers, one of
  them a delayed one of its own, against the compiled two. That table is kept empty, so the
  difference is settled rather than listed: both are now the same two triggers and the same
  engine-known ability. Its existing tests pass unchanged, including the two Cloudshift cases
  where a blinked blocker is a new object and is not destroyed. So do the stack labels "destroy
  the non-Wall creature blocking it at end of combat" and "destroy Grizzly Bears".

8 legal cards now read whole.

- the cards read;
- the creature it blocks is still there at combat damage and destroyed at end of combat;
- a non-Wall basilisk spares a Wall, and a nonblack one spares a black creature and not a green
  one.

## D970 — A chosen discard or exile with a mana value, a type list, or several exclusions

"Target player reveals their hand. You choose a nonland card from it with mana value 3 or less.
That player discards that card." "… You choose an artifact, instant, or sorcery card from it and
exile that card." "… You choose a noncreature, nonland card from it. That player discards that
card." (Duress's wording, also Mardu Charm's and Elspeth's Nightmare's.) D531's chosen discard and
D916's exile read the plain qualifier only. These spellings were unread.

How it is read, all in `chosenDiscardPrefix`:
- **A mana value** on either side of "from it" ("… card with mana value N or less from it", "…
  card from it with mana value N or greater"), asked of the printed card's mana value. "X or less"
  stays unread, because the question is asked before X could be looked at.
- **A comma list of types** is the "or" list `graveyardTypeTest` already reads.
- **Stacked negations** ("noncreature, nonland", "nonlegendary, nonland") exclude each: a card
  type, or the legendary supertype.

A first draft dropped the negation branch as unused. The measurement disagreed: Duress and its
siblings use it. It stays, and is pinned.

- the cards read;
- "a noncreature, nonland card": the artifact is taken, the creature and the land stay;
- "a nonlegendary, nonland card": the legendary artifact stays, the creature is taken;
- "with mana value 3 or less": the one card that fits is taken, and the 5-drop stays;
- "an artifact, instant, or sorcery card": the artifact is exiled, the creatures stay.

## D971 — Connive

"When ~ enters, it connives." "Whenever this creature attacks, it connives." "{2}: ~ connives."
"Whenever you cast a noncreature spell, ~ connives." The keyword action (CR 701.50a): draw a card,
then discard a card, and if a nonland card was discarded, put a +1/+1 counter on the creature. It
was not in the engine.

How it is read: before `composeEffects` reads a chain, "it / ~ / he / she connives" becomes two
clauses. The first is "draw a card". The second is a private connive clause (`CONNIVE`, read in
`selfEffect`): a discard question from the controller's hand, then the counter if any card
discarded was not a land, on the conniving creature if it is still on the battlefield. Because the
chain splits at its first question (D418), the draw happens before the discard is asked, so the
card just drawn can be the one discarded. "It" is the event's creature and "~" the card itself, as
`itMeans` has it.

Still unread: "connives X", "whenever a creature you control connives", and "you may have it
connive".

15 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the enters and activated forms read;
- the draw comes first: the card drawn is one of the cards it may discard;
- a nonland card discarded puts a +1/+1 counter on it, and a land discarded does not.

Faults injected by hand: 4 of 4 caught. They were the order of the two clauses, the nonland test,
the discard itself, and the land check.

and its pattern ended at "you control", so a second sentence left the line unread.

How it is read: the pattern now takes one more sentence. That sentence is read by `composeEffects`
with "that creature" as "target creature you control". It must come back with exactly one creature
target, no questions and no `beforeDecisions`. It then runs after the attach, with the same

## D731 — Spells cast from the top of the library, and Bolas's Citadel's life

"You may cast <kind> spells from the top of your library." is on 43 legal cards (Future Sight,
Mystic Forge, Vizier of the Menagerie, Garruk's Horde, Sigarda, Font of Blessings, Melek…).
Bolas's Citadel adds "If you cast a spell this way, pay life equal to its mana value rather than
pay its mana cost." Courser's land permission (D649) was the only part the engine already had.

How it is read (`spellsFromTopFromLine`, `CardScript.spellsFromTop`):
- **The kinds are D940's spell kinds**, joined by "and", "or" and commas, any of which lets the
  card be cast: "artifact spells and colorless spells", "Cleric, Rogue, Warrior, and Wizard
  spells", "instant and sorcery spells". "Play lands and" in front also sets `landsFromTop`.
- **Left unread:** a kind with a condition ("with flying", "with mana value 4 or greater", "of the
  chosen type", "historic"), and any rider sentence except the Citadel's (Elsha's flash, Thundermane
  Dragon's haste, Mikey & Don's counter).
- **"You may look at the top card of your library any time."** is `lookAtTop`: the controller's own
  view gets the top card and `libraryTop`; nobody else's does.

How it plays:
- **One library entry for lands and spells.** A land on top is a land drop only under a land
  permission. A spell is offered only when a permission of its kind applies, at its ordinary timing.
- **The printed cost only under a printed permission.** Under the Citadel alone the only row is the
  life cast. It costs `{0}` plus life equal to the mana value of the face cast, and is offered while
  that leaves the caster alive (D585's line). Cost increases still apply, paid in mana.
- **Not from the top:** the hand's alternative costs (evoke, dash, pitch and the rest), morph,
  foretell, suspend and emerge. Each of those is paid from the hand.
- **Refused on a life cast:** X other than 0, the kicker, buyback and replicate. There is no mana
  cost left for them to add to.
- **The action.** `auto:cast` with `payLifeFromTop` carries the life cast. The bot and the table
  client send it as one more cost flag. A plain cast of the top card is refused unless a printed
  permission of its kind applies.

The Citadel's third line ("{T}, Sacrifice ten nonland permanents") needs a cost that sacrifices
several permanents, which the engine does not have. That is D732.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the family reads, and conditioned kinds stay unread;
- the Citadel casts the top card for 3 life, taps nothing, and offers no mana row;
- a land on top is the land drop; the life row is withheld at 6 life against a 6-mana spell;
  nothing is offered without the Citadel; the second card from the top is refused;
- the controller sees the top card and the opponent does not;
- a creature permission casts a creature at its printed cost and in its own main phase only;
  a sorcery and a land are not its kind;
- a permission naming two kinds casts either.

Faults injected by script: 16 of 17 caught. The miss removes the own-side check before the look
permission, and nothing observable changes: another seat's library top is never put in an
opponent's view to be shown.

    engine tests: 5,151, all passing (merged with the other session's D970 and D971)

Coverage: 12,590 of 31,743 cards (+8), 32,691 of 59,509 lines (+62), against 700bd75. Staples:
241 of 244 (Bolas's Citadel waits on D732).

## D732 — A counted sacrifice: "Sacrifice two creatures", and Bolas's Citadel's ten

Activated abilities that sacrifice several permanents as their cost: "Sacrifice two creatures",
"Sacrifice three Foods", "Sacrifice two other creatures", Bolas's Citadel's "Sacrifice ten
nonland permanents". About 80 lines in the legal corpus print one. The engine's sacrifice cost was
one permanent.

How it is read (`countedSacrifice`):
- **The count is two to ten.** "Sacrifice X …" stays unread.
- **The kind is a single sacrifice's kind in the plural**: creatures, artifacts, lands,
  enchantments, tokens, permanents, "artifacts and/or creatures". "Other" maps to the "another"
  kind, and a kind with no "another" form ("two other lands") stays unread.
- **"Nonland permanents" is a new kind**, `nonland-permanent`.
- **Plural subtypes narrow the kind:** Foods, Treasures, Clues and Blood tokens are artifacts; the
  basic land types are lands; anything else is a creature type ("Goblins", "Elves", "Eldrazi"),
  read live as the single sacrifice's subtype is.
- **`AbilityCost.sacrificeCount`** holds the count. Absent means one.

How it plays:
- **Offered only with enough fodder.** The play carries `sacrificeCount` beside the usual
  `sacrificeOptions`.
- **The activation sends `sacrifices`**: exactly that many, all different, each one the cost can
  take. A single `sacrifice` is refused on a counted cost, and a list is refused on a
  single-sacrifice cost.
- **They are sacrificed together**, so each death trigger sees the others gone.
- **The source is fodder unless the cost says "other".** The Citadel can be one of its own ten.
- **The table** collects the picks one tap at a time; a second tap on a picked permanent takes it
  back. The bar says "tap 10 nonland permanents to sacrifice (3 of 10 chosen)", and the picks are
  ringed as chosen.
- **The bot leaves counted sacrifices to a person.** Which ten permanents is a judgement the
  single-sacrifice sort can't make.

Staples went from 241 to 242 (Bolas's Citadel, with D731).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests and 1 table test:
- the family reads; "Sacrifice X" and "two other lands" stay unread;
- the Citadel's options are every nonland permanent and no land, itself included; activated with
  ten, they all go and the opponent loses 10;
- not offered with nine; refused for nine, a repeat, a land, a single `sacrifice`, and a list on a
  single-sacrifice outlet;
- "two other creatures" never offers its source and is not offered with one other; "two creatures"
  sacrifices both and draws;
- the table: picks one at a time, a second tap takes one back, the second pick sends `sacrifices`.

Faults injected by script: 15 of 15 caught (12 in the engine, 3 in the table).

    engine tests: 5,158, all passing (merged with the other session's D972)

Coverage: 12,637 of 31,743 cards (+25), 32,759 of 59,509 lines (+40), against 50f4683. Staples:
242 of 244. Left: Teferi's Protection, and Castle Garenbrig (blocked by D669).

## D733 — Teferi's Protection: phasing, and a life total that can't change

"Until your next turn, your life total can't change and you gain protection from everything. All
permanents you control phase out. Exile Teferi's Protection." Protection from everything was
already there (D718). This adds the other three pieces: phasing, the life lock, and the self-exile.

**Phasing** (CR 702.26):
- **A zone of its own, `phased`.** It isn't a zone in the rules. Keeping phased permanents in
  their own list means every reader of the battlefield passes over them without being told: they
  can't be targeted, counted, attacked with, destroyed by a wrath, or seen by a static. A stored
  target that phased out is illegal on resolution.
- **`phaseOut` and `phaseIn` move them without `relocate`.** Phasing changes no zone, so nothing
  triggers, and counters, damage, tapped state, attachments and tokens stay. `phased` is not in
  `ZONE_IDS`, so no tabletop move can name it.
- **Phasing out removes from combat.** What is attached phases out with it, indirectly
  (`phasedIndirectly`), however deep the chain goes. An indirectly phased permanent phases in only
  with its host, even when another seat controls it, so an opponent's Aura on your creature waits
  for your untap step.
- **Phase-in is the first thing in the untap step** (CR 502.1), before anything untaps.
- **A static stays put while its source is phased** (CR 702.26d). It is off while phased and on
  again after; before this, a phased Aura's static was expired. Effects that last "for as long as"
  still end, which is CR 702.26e.
- **The table** draws phased permanents in their battlefield row, dimmed, with a "phased out"
  badge and no plays.

**Your life total can't change** (`lockLife`, `lifeLocked`, CR 119.7–119.8):
- no life is gained or lost, so nothing triggers on it;
- damage is still dealt and tallied, commander damage included, and the life stays;
- no life can be paid: `canPayLife` replaces the eleven "life above the cost" checks in the offer
  list and the actions;
- it lasts until the controller's next turn. Platinum Emperion's static is the same lock, read

## D734 — Emblems: "You get an emblem with …"

79 legal planeswalker abilities give their controller an emblem (CR 114): an object in the command
zone with the abilities quoted. The engine had nothing to hold one.

How it works:
- **An emblem is a `CardInstance` with `emblem: true`** in its controller's command zone, made by
  `createEmblem` with a card definition built at the time from the quoted text ("<walker> emblem",
  type line "Emblem"). Its script is compiled from that text like any card's.
- **Its abilities work from the command zone:**
  - statics are installed as it arrives and kept while it exists, so an anthem outlives the
    planeswalker and reaches creatures that come later;
  - triggers are watched from the command zone (`raise`);
  - the seat-level statics ("no maximum hand size", "can't change", "prevent all damage to you",
    "skip your draw step", riot, Seedborn's untap) read emblems beside permanents.
- **It is never cast.** It is shown in the command zone, which everybody sees.
- **"This emblem"** is a self-reference, like "this creature".

How it is read (`emblemClause`):
- "You get an emblem with "A"" or ""A" and "B"", each quoted ability on its own line.
- **Read only if every ability reads** (`lineScriptFor`), and none is activated, since nothing
  offers an activation from the command zone. Two emblems with one ("Tap an untapped artifact …",
  "{1}{B}, Sacrifice a creature: …") stay unread.
- **The quoted punctuation is hidden from the clause splitter**, so an emblem's own ", then" stays
  inside it. Four real emblems need that.

26 of the 79 emblem abilities read; the rest quote abilities the engine can't read yet. Five legal
cards now read whole; most emblem walkers have another unread loyalty ability.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the walkers read; an unreadable emblem, an activated one, and one with ", then" inside it;
- the anthem emblem is in the command zone, is never offered as a cast, everyone sees it, it
  outlives the walker, and it pumps a creature cast afterwards;
- an emblem's cast trigger deals its damage from the command zone;
- an emblem's "no maximum hand size" keeps ten cards through cleanup.

Faults injected by script: 11 of 11 caught, two of them after pinning (the quote hiding, and
refusing activated emblems).

    engine tests: 5,176, all passing (merged with the other session's D973)

Coverage: 12,668 of 31,743 cards (+5), 32,819 of 59,509 lines (+27), against 7699a9b.

## D975 — A */* from more measures: colours, zones, life, devotion

A creature printed "*/*" is refused whole unless its size line is read, because a 0/0 dies before
anyone has priority. D902 read "… are each equal to the number of <count>" for eleven counts and a
subtype. The measurement showed 73 legal "*/*" cards still refused. The commonest missing measures
were these:
- "green / black / … permanents you control" (Drove of Elves, Crowd of Cinders, Kithkin Rabble);
- "artifacts your opponents control" (Gaea's Avenger, with "1 plus");
- "<type> cards in all graveyards" (Cognivore, Cantivore, Magnivore, Terravore, Slag Fiend), and
  "cards in all graveyards" (Lord of Extinction);
- "your life total" (Soul of Eternity);
- "your devotion to <colour>" (Anax and the other Theros gods' heroes print it for power).

How it is read:
- **Three serializable count kinds** in `definesSize.count`, because the count runs inside
  `characteristicsOf` and travels in state, so it is data, not a closure:
  - `your-life-total`;
  - `{ devotion: [colours] }`, which counts the coloured symbols in the printed costs of your
    permanents, hybrid and Phyrexian included;
  - `{ zone, whose, anyType?, colour? }`, a count of printed cards in a zone.
- **`cdaCountFor`** reads the general zone phrases. **`definesSizeFromLine`** reads a measure that
  is "the number of …", "N plus the number of …" (through the existing `powerPlus` and
  `toughnessPlus`), "your life total" or "your devotion to …". Power-only is read the same way,
  with the printed toughness kept.

Logged across the corpus, all 18 newly read lines name the count they say. Refused "*/*" cards
went from 73 to 58.

14 legal cards now read whole.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- green permanents you control: itself and a green bear, not the forest;
- your life total, 20/20;
- 1 plus the artifacts your opponents control, not yours;
- power is your devotion to red ({2}{R} and {R}{R} make 3), and the printed toughness stays;
- instant cards in all graveyards, both players'.

Faults injected by hand: 8 of 8 caught.

    engine tests: 5,184, all passing

Coverage: 12,691 of 31,764 cards (+14), 32,867 of 59,553 lines. Staples: 241 of 244.

## D735 — Anthems by colour and kind: "Other green creatures you control get +1/+1"

The group statics of D620 covered your creatures, other creatures, a creature type, tokens, and
since D941 attacking or countered creatures. They didn't cover a colour or a kind, so a whole
shelf of lords stayed unread:
- "Other green creatures you control get +1/+1" (the colour lords, 35 lines);
- "Artifact creatures you control have flying";
- "Legendary creatures …", "Multicolored creatures …", "Untapped creatures …", "Land creatures …".

How it is read (`groupStaticFromLine`):
- **A run of colour and kind words before "creatures you control"**, with or without "other", then
  "get" or "have" and the predicate the other group statics read.
- **A colour is the existing colour scope** (`controller-color`), the one "of the chosen color"
  uses. A run names at most one colour; "white and blue" isn't a run, so it stays unread.
- **Every other word is a new data filter, `onlyKind`**, beside D941's `onlyAttacking` and
  `onlyWithCounter`: artifact, legendary, land, enchantment, colorless, multicolored, monocolored,
  untapped, tapped, token, nontoken, nonartifact, nonlegendary, snow. Every word must hold. It is
  read live in `effectApplies`: types after layer 4 (an Artifact-ised Bear joins the artifact
  lord), colours after layer 5, tapped state as it is.
- **Data, not a function**, because effects are part of the persisted game state.

One older compile test pinned "Black creatures you control have wither" as unread, because nothing
read it then. It now reads correctly, so that case is gone from the refusal list.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the family reads; two colours stay unread;
- a green lord pumps its controller's other green creatures, not itself, not a red one, not the
  opponent's; recoloured, the two swap places;
- an artifact lord gives flying to artifact creatures, itself and a Bear made an artifact included,
  and not to a plain Bear;
- untapped creatures get the bonus only while untapped;
- both words must hold: an untapped artifact creature only;
- multicolored and legendary, the Prism being both.

Faults injected by script: 9 of 9 caught, one after pinning (any word instead of every word). A
tenth fault was on a two-colour check no text can reach; the check was removed.

## D736 — Ward and goad granted by a static or an attachment

Two grants the static readers didn't have:
- **"Has ward {N}"**: "Equipped creature gets +1/+1 and has ward {2}", "Other creatures you control
  have ward {1}", "Legendary creatures you control get +1/+1 and have ward {1}", about 30 lines;
- **"Is goaded"**: "Enchanted creature gets +1/+1 and is goaded", 11 lines.

And one combination the attachment reader refused: "gets +N/+N and has "…"", a size and a quoted
grant together (Equipment and Auras with "Whenever this creature attacks, …").

How it is read:
- **Ward is a triggered ability** (CR 702.21a), so "has ward {N}" at the end of a predicate is
  rewritten to `has "Ward {N}"` (`wardAsQuoted`). It is then granted by the readers that already
  grant quoted triggers: the attachment reader and the group statics (D620, D735). The granted ward
  counters a spell or ability an opponent aims at the creature unless they pay, as a printed one does.
- **"Is goaded"** on an attachment is goad's two halves for as long as it is attached: attacks each
  combat if able, and not the attachment's controller while there is another player to attack
  (CR 701.38). After another predicate it is read with it.
- **"Gets +N/+N and has "…""** reads each half on its own and joins them.

Still unread: a goad after two predicates ("gets +2/+2, has deathtouch, and is goaded"), ward with a
condition or a count, and ward on a single named permanent.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- an Equipment's ward {2}: the opponent's removal waits for the trigger, the opponent is asked to
  pay {2}, and declining counters it;
- a lord's ward reaches its other creatures and not itself;
- a goading Aura in a pod of three: its host must attack, may not attack the Aura's controller, and
  may attack the third player;
- an Equipment's "gets +1/+1 and has "Whenever this creature attacks, draw a card."": both.

Faults injected by script: 7 of 7 caught.

    engine tests: 5,194, all passing (merged with the other session's D975)
