## D737 — Board conditions: "as long as you control another artifact"

The static condition reader (D605) answered "you control a Plains" and metalcraft's "you control
an artifact". It didn't answer "another", an opponent's board, a colour, or a count of a type, so
"~ gets +1/+1 as long as …" stayed unread across a family of about 50 lines:
- "you control another artifact";
- "an opponent controls an Island";
- "you control a blue creature";
- "an opponent controls a nontoken white permanent";
- "you control two or more Wizards";
- "you control ten or more lands".

How it is read (`boardCondition`, a new `board-has` condition):
- **Whose board:** yours, or any one opponent's.
- **"Another":** not the source. It is yours only; "another" on an opponent's board is refused.
- **The count:** "a"/"an" is one, "N or more" is N.
- **What each counted permanent must be:**
  - an optional "nontoken", on either side of the colour;
  - an optional colour;
  - then a card type with "creature" or "permanent" after it, "permanent" alone, or a capitalised
    subtype (creature types singularised, basic land types, Equipment, Aura, Vehicle, Gate, Desert).
- **Answered off printed type lines and colours,** the compromise the metalcraft count states,
  because it is asked from inside `characteristicsOf`.

Triggers share the reader: an intervening "if you control another Wizard" is asked with the
trigger's own source, so it doesn't count the creature asking. Two older tests pinned these as
refusals. The D563 row ("another Wizard") is removed. The D605 row moves to a condition still out
of reach: "an opponent controls a creature with flying".

**Tests.** 7 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- "another artifact": the source doesn't count, a Rock does, a non-artifact creature doesn't;
- "an opponent controls an Island": the opponent's counts, your own doesn't;
- a blue creature of yours gives flying, the opponent's doesn't;
- "a nontoken white permanent": a white card counts, a white token doesn't;
- the intervening "if you control another Wizard" on entering, with and without one;
- "two or more Wizards" needs two.

Faults injected by script: 9 of 9 caught, one after pinning (card types ignored).

    engine tests: 5,205, all passing (merged with the other session's D976)

Coverage: 12,841 of 31,764 cards (+62), 33,127 of 59,553 lines (+75), against 1af49a9.

## D738 — "Prevent all damage that would be dealt to / by …" this turn

Fog's "Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt this turn" was the only one of its family the
engine read. The rest stayed unread:
- "Prevent all damage that would be dealt to target creature this turn";
- "… combat damage that would be dealt by target attacking creature this turn";
- "… dealt by creatures this turn";
- "… dealt this turn to creatures you control";
- "… to you and creatures you control this turn";
- "… combat damage … to players this turn".

How it works:
- **Four effect flags, checked in `dealDamage`** before anything is marked, beside protection and
  the shields (CR 615.1):
  - `preventsDamageTo` and `preventsDamageFrom`, for the damaged permanent and for the source,
    each over the effect's scope (`effectReaches`);
  - `preventsDamageToPlayers`, the controller or every player;
  - `preventsCombatOnly`, which lets non-combat damage through.
- **Prevented damage is never dealt:** no life lost, no damage marked, no deathtouch, no lifelink.
- **"This turn" is the duration;** the line has to say it. The static "Prevent all damage that would
  be dealt to creatures" is left unread.
- **The subjects read:** a target creature (any target creature phrase), creatures, creatures you
  control, creatures your opponents control, you, players, and you and creatures you control.

The first version special-cased "combat damage by" as a Fog over a scope. The break run showed it
behaves the same as the general combat-only flag, so the special case was removed.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- to target creature: a Bolt does nothing to it, and still kills another;
- combat damage by target creature: its attack deals nothing;
- by creatures: a creature's ping is prevented, a Bolt is not;
- combat damage to players: the attack is prevented, a Bolt to the face is not, and the effect is
  gone by the opponent's turn;
- to you and creatures you control: both spared from the opponent's Bolts; the caster's Bolt still
  hits the opponent and the opponent's creature.

Faults injected by script: 8 of 8 caught, one after pinning ("to you" stopping damage to everyone).
A ninth was on the removed special case.

    engine tests: 5,218, all passing (merged with the other session's D977)

## D978 — Prepare: a creature that casts a copy of its spell

The "prepare" layout is a creature with a spell printed beside it: "While it's prepared, you may
cast a copy of its spell. Doing so unprepares it." The compiler refused all 71 legal cards as "more
than one face".

Of those 71, 50 carry both faces in the data. The other 21 carry only the creature face, so they
have no spell to copy and stay refused.

**How it is built:**
- **The faces.** `CardFaces.kind` gains `prepare`, and the compiler builds the layout the way it
  builds an adventurer's. From the hand only the creature is offered, and a cast of the spell face
  is refused ("cast only as a copy").
- **Prepared.** A designation on the permanent, `CardInstance.prepared`:
  - set by "This creature enters prepared" (`entersPrepared`, applied at arrival like
    `entersTapped`);
  - set by "~ becomes prepared" / "it becomes prepared" (an effect clause), so every trigger and
    activated ability the compiler already reads can prepare a creature;
  - cleared by casting the copy and by leaving the battlefield (CR 400.7).
- **The copy.** `preparedCopyOf` makes a card copy of the spell face in its controller's exile,
  with the D583 permission to cast it this turn, and unprepares the permanent in the same step.
  `castSpell` (`preparedCopy: true`, `half: 0`, `card` the permanent) casts it from there. So the
  cost, the timing, the targets and the copy leaving the game as it resolves (CR 707.12) are the
  ordinary ones.
- **The offer.** `legalActions` asks the same state `castSpell` will make for its plays of that
  copy, so the offer and the cast cannot disagree. The recursion ends because the permanent is
  unprepared in that state. The row reads "Cast a copy of <spell> (prepared)".
- **The condition.** "If this creature isn't prepared" is read, as a `source-prepared` condition.
- **The view, the bot and the web table** carry the flag. The board shows a "prepared" badge.

21 legal cards now read whole, plus the cards whose other lines were already readable.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the three shapes read, with a `prepare` face, and a one-face prepare row stays refused;
- from the hand the creature is the only cast, and a half-0 cast from the hand is refused;
- it enters prepared, then the copy is offered for the spell's cost, cast, unprepares the creature,
  resolves (+3 life) and leaves no object behind, and a second copy is refused;
- a sorcery copy is not offered with something on the stack, it is not another seat's, and a
  bounced creature is not prepared;
- "if this creature isn't prepared, it becomes prepared": on its own upkeep, not the opponent's;
- an attack prepares the Duelist, and its instant copy is cast in combat.

Faults injected by script: 16. 14 were caught at once. The two misses were the leave-the-battlefield
reset and the controller check; both are now pinned with a real bounce and a check against the
other seat.

    engine tests: 5,224, all passing (merged with the other session's D738)

Coverage: 12,887 of 31,845 cards (+23), 33,278 of 59,749 lines (+100).

restriction, the ban form (`spendBan`): the mana pays for any ability, and for a spell only if it

Map, Junk and Gold are still not written, and the compile test that pins that now names them.

## D979 — Omen: an adventurer whose spell goes back into the library

The "omen" layout (16 legal cards, the Dragons of Tarkir Dragonstorm) is a creature with an instant
or sorcery beside it. The compiler refused all of them as "more than one face".

It is the adventurer's shape with a different destination, so it is built the same way:
- `CardFaces.kind` gains `omen`, and the compiler builds it like an adventure. From the hand both
  faces are offered.
- A cast of the spell face marks its stack object `omen`.
- `spellLeavesStack` shuffles a **resolved** omen into its owner's library ("Then shuffle this
  card into its owner's library"). A countered one goes to the graveyard, as a countered adventure
  does. Flashback's exile still wins (CR 702.33a).

## D741 — Lands described by type and state: "a non-Lair land", "an untapped Island", "two Swamps"

`permanentDescribed` reads the permanents a choice, a bounce or a sacrifice is about. It knew types,
colours and "nonland". It didn't know these, which the "sacrifice it unless you …" costs (D724) and
their kin print:
- **A basic land type as the noun:** "an Island", "two Forests", "a Swamp". It is a land with that
  subtype. The type is a fixed word, so a lower-cased phrase is still safe.
- **"Untapped" / "tapped":** the permanent's state now.
- **"Basic" / "nonbasic":** the supertype.
- **"Non-<Subtype>":** "a non-Lair land" (the Lairs), "a non-Zombie creature", off the printed
  capitals.

The sacrifice reader also takes "four" and "five" ("sacrifice five lands").

Two older pins move. "Sacrifice a Forest" and "sacrifice a non-Zombie creature" (D471) read now,
correctly. The refusal is pinned on "sacrifice a Goblin" (a creature type as the noun) and a
keyword filter instead.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- a Lair returns a land that isn't a Lair, never itself or another Lair, and with only another Lair
  it is sacrificed;
- "an untapped Island": a tapped one doesn't pay, an untapped one does;
- "two Swamps": one isn't enough, and with three, two are chosen and sacrificed.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 5,236, all passing (merged with the other session's D979)

## D980 — "Whenever ~ deals damage to a player", and "… to a creature"

Two trigger sentences that the event model could nearly say already:

- **"Whenever ~ deals damage to a player"** (and "equipped / enchanted creature deals damage to a
  player"). `deals-damage` has meant `to: 'player'` since D566, but only "to an opponent" had a
  row. Now any player is heard, its own controller included, and "that player" is the seat that
  was hit.
- **"Whenever ~ deals (combat) damage to a creature"**: a new `deals-damage` event with
  `to: 'creature'`.
  - The engine raises one per creature a permanent dealt damage to. Combat damage is summed per
    pair, because it is dealt at once (CR 510.2).
  - The creature travels as `blocked`, the channel the block events use for "that creature".
  - Whether it was a creature is asked of the snapshot, so a creature the damage killed still
    counts and a planeswalker never does.
  - No player row hears these events, and no creature row hears a player's.

The block referents (D480/D969) now read under the new event as well: "destroy that creature",
"destroy that creature at end of combat", and "~ deals N damage to that creature". A new clause,
"(tap that creature and it | that creature) doesn't untap during its controller's next untap step",
reads under both the block and the damage events.

Two D566 refusal rows ("deals damage to a player", "… to a creature") are now reads rows.

**Not yet:** a creature that dies in the same combat damage step does not get its "deals damage"
trigger. The watcher has left by the time triggers are collected. That is a look-back question
shared with D904's "deals damage", and it is left for its own increment.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- a ping at a creature fires the creature row and not the player row, and a ping at a player fires
  the player row (the hit player discards) and not the creature row; a ping at its own controller
  is "a player" too;
- combat damage to its blocker taps and freezes the blocker, not the attacker, and an unblocked
  hit freezes nothing;
- a ping at a planeswalker is not damage to a creature, and a prevented ping is not dealt.

Faults injected by script: 9. 6 were caught at once. Of the 3 misses, two (a player row narrowed to
opponents, and the creature check) are now pinned by tests. The third, a source-in-play and
zero-amount guard, was unreachable and is removed.

    engine tests: 5,240, all passing (merged with the other session's D741)

Coverage: 12,986 of 31,858 cards (+55), 33,434 of 59,790 lines (+82).

## D981 — A creature that dies dealing its damage still triggers

D980 left a gap that D566 had already written down. A creature's "whenever ~ deals (combat)
damage …" did not fire when the same damage step killed it, under either `deals-damage` or
`combat-damage`. Two cases:
- a 2/2 with "deals combat damage to a creature" that trades with its blocker;
- a trampler that dies to its blocker while trampling over.

The damage was dealt while it was on the battlefield, so the ability triggered then. State-based
actions only buried the creature afterwards (CR 603.2, 704.3).

The fix is the one `damaged` has had since D566: the event's own subject may fire from its
last-known state (`lastKnown`), now for `deals-damage` and `combat-damage` too. The two sentences
change together, as the gap they shared was kept together.

The watcher list needed nothing. The board-wide list already carries the subject with its
controller, wherever it is (D566's arrangement for deaths). The fault run showed that a second
addition there was redundant, and it was removed before commit.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- a 2/2 trades with a 2/2 blocker and still gains its 3 life;
- a 3/1 trampler dies to a 1/1 blocker, the opponent takes 2, and it still gains its 4 life.

Faults injected by script: 4. 3 were caught. The miss was the redundant watcher addition, which is
removed.

    engine tests: 5,243, all passing

Coverage is unchanged (a rules fix, not a new reader).

## D742 — "If {U} was spent to cast it", and a spell's "If <condition>, <effect>"

Eventide's hybrid cards and their kin check which colours paid for them: "When ~ enters, if {R}
was spent to cast it, …", "If {U} was spent to cast this spell, draw a card", "sacrifice it unless
{U} was spent to cast it". 45 legal lines, nearly every one its own shape.

How it works:
- **The payment records which colours it spent** (`colorsSpent`, beside sunburst's count from
  D917): a colour counts when the pool holds less of it after paying, generic mana included. The
  stack object carries the list.
- **The permanent keeps it.** As a permanent spell resolves, the colours go into its
  `castPermanents` record with "you cast it" (D607), under the same object-sequence check. A
  permanent that was bounced and replayed by other means, or never cast, spent nothing.
- **"{C} was spent to cast it / this spell / ~"** is a new intervening condition. For a resolving
  spell it reads the spell's own list; otherwise it reads the permanent's record.

Two readers take any condition the intervening-if reader answers, not only this one:
- **A spell's "If <condition>, <effect>"**: the effect happens only while the condition holds as the
  spell resolves. This is for spells only (`where` is null). On a trigger the "if" is intervening
  and asked as it triggers too, so `interveningIfFromLine` keeps reading those. The first version
  applied it to triggers as well, and 46 tests caught it.
- **"Sacrifice it unless <condition>"**, beside D724's "unless you <cost>".

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- a spell with a generic {1} draws two when an Island paid and one when a Forest did;
- "sacrifice it unless {U} was spent": kept when cast with blue, sacrificed when cast with green,
  and sacrificed when bounced and put back by hand;
- an intervening "if {R} was spent to cast it": life with a Mountain, none with a Forest, and a
  permanent put onto the battlefield without being cast spent nothing.

Faults injected by script: 6 of 6 caught, one after pinning (a stale cast record trusted).

    engine tests: 5,244, all passing (merged with the other session's D980)

Coverage: 13,027 of 31,858 cards (+37), 33,480 of 59,790 lines (+45), against 397e7d8.

## D743 — Pumps by X, and pumps of several targets

Two shapes the targeted pump reader (D544) refused:
- **X in the size:** "Target creature gets +X/+0 until end of turn", "… -X/-X …", "+X/+X". X is the
  spell's own, settled as it resolves (`c.x`). The aim follows the printed signs as the numbered
  form's does, so a -X/-X points at somebody else's creature.
- **Several targets, each pumped:** "Up to two target creatures each get +1/+1 until end of turn",
  "Two target creatures each get +2/+0 and gain first strike until end of turn". Every chosen
  creature gets the same bonus, and "up to" may take fewer. A true shrink with a granted keyword
  stays refused, as in the single form.

Still unread here: X from a count ("where X is …"), a pump with a second sentence, and type-changing
pumps ("becomes a blue Serpent with base power and toughness 5/5").

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- +X/+0 for X = 3 makes a 2/2 a 5/2, and -X/-X for X = 2 kills a 2/2;
- up to two each get +1/+1: two Bears both 3/3, and with one target only that one;
- two each get +2/+0 and first strike, both creatures, and it is gone once the turn ends.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 5,251, all passing (merged with the other session's D981)

## D982 — Flip cards, comma names in costs, and an ability that outlives its face

**Flip cards** (CR 710; 20 legal cards, the Kamigawa flip creatures). The compiler refused them all
as "more than one face".
- `CardFaces.kind` gains `flip`.
- The flipped half keeps the card's one mana cost and mana value (CR 710.2a).
- From the hand only the upright half is cast; a cast of the flipped half is refused.
- `flipPermanent` is "flip ~" / "flip it". It is transform's one-field move (`defKey` to the other
  half, `printedDefKey` remembering the card, and `relocate` putting it back on the way off).
  The differences:
  - it is one-way (CR 701.29c);
  - it records nothing for "transforms into" to hear;
  - it refuses a permanent already holding a copy's memory in the same field.
- `transformPermanent` now refuses anything but a transforming card. A flip card, an adventurer or
  a prepare card has no back to turn to (CR 701.28c). Before this, "transform it" on such a card
  would have turned it into its spell.

**A legendary name with a comma, in a cost.** "Remove a ki counter from Ichiga, Who Topples Oaks:"
was cut in two by the cost's comma split, so every activated ability whose cost names its own
comma-bearing card stayed unread: "Sacrifice X, Y:", "Exile X, Y from your graveyard:", and the
rest. The full name is now read as its short form before the split.

**An ability that outlives its face.** An activated ability is put on the stack after its costs are
paid, and its `cardKey` was read from the source as it was by then. A flipped card that sacrifices
itself is its upright half again by then, so ability 0 of the wrong face resolved. A Clone that
sacrifices itself had the same bug. `pushAbility` now takes the face the ability was activated
from, read before the costs (CR 113.7a).

4 of the 20 flip cards read whole. Most of the rest wait on their flip conditions.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads whole, with the flipped half's mana cost and mana value;
- only the upright half is cast, and a cast of the flipped half is refused;
- it flips to a flying 3/3 that does not flip back. A flip card does not transform, flipping records
  no transform, and a copy is not flipped over its memory. The flipped half's "Sacrifice <its full
  name>:" resolves (+5 life), and the card leaves as the card it was printed as.

Faults injected by script: 10. 9 were caught at once. The copy guard was missed and is now pinned.

    engine tests: 5,254, all passing (merged with the other session's D743)

Coverage: 13,052 of 31,878 cards, 33,535 of 59,841 lines (with the other session's D742 merged).

## D983 — A */* from a general zone count

D975 to D977 read the "*/*" counts one phrase at a time. This increment adds a general grammar
(`zoneCountFrom`) behind the fixed readers, in `cdaCountFor`. It reads a list of words in front of a
noun, each word one filter the zone count asks of printed or instance data. Everything stays
serialisable, as `definesSize` requires.

- **Words:**
  - `other`, `untapped`, `face-down`, `nonbasic`, `snow`, `legendary`, `colorless`;
  - a colour;
  - `nonX` for a card type;
  - a card type ("permanent" means any permanent type);
  - a capitalised subtype ("Elf cards in your graveyard").
- **Joining:** types joined by "and", "or" or a comma are **any** of them ("instant and sorcery",
  "artifacts, creatures, and lands"). Types side by side are **all** of them ("artifact creatures").
- **Nouns:**
  - `cards in` your graveyard, all graveyards, your opponents' graveyards, your hand, or all
    players' hands;
  - on the battlefield, a type, "permanents", or a subtype plural ("other Rats on the
    battlefield"), with "you control", "your opponents control" or "on the battlefield";
  - "creatures named ~ on the battlefield" (Plague Rats), matched against the card's own name.
- **Counters:**
  - "+1/+1 counters on creatures you control" sums those counters on what the count finds;
  - "fade counters on it" is the permanent's own counters.
- **Also:**
  - "the highest / greatest mana value among cards in your graveyard";
  - "the total number of …".
  - An unknown word refuses the phrase.

The count now receives the permanent whose size it is (`effect.source`), for "other" and "named ~".
The new zone filter is `ofSubtype` rather than `subtype`, because `'subtype' in kind` already tells
the `{ subtype }` kind apart.

Refused "*/*" cards: 39 to 26 (and the "*/N" ones 9 to 7).

Two older refusal rows used "face-down creatures on the battlefield" as the count the engine
did not have. They now use "cards you've drawn this turn".

**Tests.** 7 engine tests, all on real boards:
- the 14 cards read;
- "other creature cards" (not the sorcery or the land), "noncreature, nonland cards", and
  "nonbasic land cards in your opponents' graveyards" (not yours, not their Swamp);
- "artifact creatures" is both types; "untapped artifacts, creatures, and lands" is any of them and
  drops by one when a Swamp taps;
- "creatures named ~" counts both sides; "legendary creatures"; and the highest mana value in the
  graveyard;
- +1/+1 counters on your own creatures summed (not the opponent's, not -1/-1), and fade counters on
  itself;
- all players' hands;
- "other Rats" (everyone's, not itself, not a Bear), face-down creatures, and colorless creatures.

Faults injected by script: 16. 12 were caught at once. The 4 misses (subtype, "other", face-down,
colorless) are now pinned by the last test.

    engine tests: 5,264, all passing (merged with the other session's D744)

Coverage: 13,098 of 31,900 cards (+46), 33,611 of 59,888 lines (+76).

## D745 — "Exile up to N target cards from graveyards"

Graveyard hate (D527) read "Exile target card from a graveyard". The "up to" forms didn't read,
about 45 legal lines: "Exile up to one target card from a graveyard", "… up to two target cards
from graveyards", "… from an opponent's graveyard", "… up to one target creature card …".

They read now as the single spec with a count and `optional`, so fewer may be chosen, none
included, and the spell still resolves. Every card chosen that is still in a graveyard is exiled.

**"From a single graveyard" stays unread**, on purpose. The targets must share an owner, which a
per-target filter can't check, and exiling across graveyards would be a different card.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read; "from a single graveyard" stays unread;
- up to one: the target is offered as optional, a chosen card is exiled, and with none chosen the
  spell still resolves and draws;
- up to two from graveyards: one card from each player's graveyard, both exiled.

Faults injected by script: 2 of 3 caught. The miss was a malformed fault: reading "a single
graveyard" takes two coordinated edits, and a one-edit fault leaves it as unread as before, which
the test above pins.

Pod sweep 59001 (D740–D744): every game finished.

## D985 — Ravenous, and the X a permanent was cast with

**Ravenous** (CR 702.156a; 4 legal cards it alone blocked): "This creature enters with X +1/+1
counters on it. If X is 5 or more, draw a card when it enters." It is read as those two sentences,
by the readers that already had each. Both are merged in, or neither.

It found a latent bug in the second sentence's reader. "When ~ enters, if X is 5 or more, …" read
cleanly, but its X was the **trigger's** X, which is always 0, so it never fired. CR 107.3m says an
enters ability's X is the X of the spell that became the permanent. So:
- `CardInstance.castX` is set as a permanent spell resolves, when X was more than 0, and cleared
  when the permanent leaves the battlefield;
- a triggered ability with no X of its own resolves with its source's `castX` (`triggerX`).

The intervening-if and before-decisions contexts are left at 0. No condition reads X yet, and the
fault run showed both unreachable.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- cast for X = 3 it has three counters and draws nothing; for X = 5, five counters and a card. The
  X stays on the permanent and goes when it is bounced.

Faults injected by script: 6. 4 were caught at once. Of the misses, the reset on leaving is now
pinned, and the intervening-if context's X is reverted as unreachable.

    engine tests: 5,277, all passing (merged with the other session's D746)

## D986 — Searching for "a card named …"

The planeswalker-deck creatures (Gideon's, Chandra's, Ajani's and the rest) print "When ~ enters,
you may search your library and/or graveyard for a card named <their walker>, reveal it, and put it
into your hand. If you search your library this way, shuffle." D720 had read that sentence since
it was written. What it could not read was **"a card named …"**: the library search's filter
(`libraryFilter`) had no named-card form, so every printing stayed unread.

- `libraryFilter` reads "a card named <name>" as the printed name, compared exactly. A name with
  a comma in it ("Gideon, Battle-Ready") is kept whole: the phrase ends where the search
  sentence's own ", reveal it" begins.
- "…, reveal it, **then** put it into your hand" (two printings) is folded into "… and put it", the
  form D720 reads. The clause splitter would otherwise have cut it at ", then".

The plain library search reads the same name: "Search your library for a card named …, reveal it,
put it into your hand, then shuffle."

D449's row that refused a name other than the card's own now reads it. Its reason was that a search
for a name not in the library finds nothing, which is what the search does at a table.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads, with the comma name and "then put it";
- from the library only cards with exactly that name are offered (not "Test Gideon"), and the one
  chosen goes to hand;
- from the graveyard, the same, and the other card stays.

Faults injected by script: 4. 3 were caught. The miss was a "then" alternative in D720's regex,
which the fold makes unreachable, and it is removed.

    engine tests: 5,284, all passing (merged with the other session's D747)

## D988 — Cast triggers on what the spell targets, and on two colours at once

Grouping the cards one line short by their opening (D987's probe) showed a family under "Whenever
you cast …" whose effects already read ("put a +1/+1 counter on ~", "draw a card"). The spell
filter in front of them is what stayed unread:

- **"… a spell that targets a creature / a creature you control / an opponent or a creature an
  opponent controls"**: `targetsWhat` on the `spell-cast` event.
  - It is answered in `fireTrigger`, beside heroic's `targetsSelf` and for its reason: "you" is
    the watching permanent's controller.

  beside `ofColours` in `triggerMatches`.

- "a creature you control" fires on yours and not on theirs;

## D989 — "You may pay N life. If you do / When you do, …"

The "may" with a price (D448) read mana and, since D451, energy. A life price stayed refused:
"When ~ enters, you may pay 2 life. When you do, target creature gets -1/-1 until end of turn"
(19 cards one line short opened that way), and "… If you do, draw a card".

- `payIfChosen.life` is the third currency, beside `cost` (mana) and `energy`.
  - It is offered only when `canPayLife` says the seat can pay, which is the test every other life
    payment in the engine uses.
  - It is paid with `loseLife` before the effect runs. Paying life is losing it (CR 119.4).
- `optionalEffect` reads "you may pay N life. If you do, …" (N a numeral or a word) into that
  price. Its "When you do" form (D948) is read through the same path, so the reflexive trigger's
  target is chosen after the payment.
- A life price that is not a number ("X life") refuses the line.

Two older rows refused this price: D448's "life, which has no field here", retired as D451 retired
energy's, and D472's "pay 2 life", which now uses "pay X life".

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read, and "pay X life" does not;
- "Pay 2 life" pays 2 and draws, and "Decline" pays nothing and draws nothing;
- at 2 life the payment is not offered;
- "When you do": paid, the reflexive trigger shrinks the target creature.

Faults injected by script: 5. 4 were caught at once. The non-number guard was missed and is now
pinned.

## D750 — A trigger whose targets are gone before it is aimed is removed

**Found by the 100-game pod sweep at seed 59203.** Schema Thief's "Whenever ~ deals combat damage
to a player, create a token that's a copy of target artifact that player controls" triggered with
candidates. By the time its controller aimed it, that player had left the game, and with them the
attack, so "that player" (read as "defending player", D960) named nobody. `chooseTargets` refused
every answer, including none, and the game threw.

The rule is CR 603.3d: a triggered ability with no legal target is removed. The engine already did
that as a trigger goes on the stack; now `chooseTargets` does it too, when a required target has
nobody left to point at. A trigger whose target is "up to one" still resolves the rest of its
effect with no target.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- two artifacts gone before the trigger is aimed: the trigger leaves the stack and the game goes on;
- "destroy up to one target artifact … You gain 2 life" with nothing left: the life is still gained.

Faults injected by script: 2 of 2 caught, one after pinning (an optional target counted as
unaimable). Seed 59203 replays to a finish.

    engine tests: 5,306, all passing (merged with the other session's D988 and D989)

## D990 — Trigger openings with an event already behind them

A new probe (`prologue-gap.mjs`) asks which cards are one line short only because of the trigger's
opening. It compiles the opening with a trivial effect ("you gain 1 life") and keeps the lines where
that fails: 1,686 of them. The commonest openings had events the engine already raised:

  raised once every defender has declared blockers. Only the hand-written Ophidian used it.

  spelling of three rows that read only "Whenever". It is the same event (CR 603.2), as the
  combat-damage row has read both since D592.

  step entered.
- **"Whenever a creature attacks"**: anybody's attacker, as "… a creature you control attacks"
  reads yours.

The rest of the list stays for later. It needs events or fields the engine lacks: scry and surveil,
discarding, "becomes monstrous", "a source deals damage to ~", "an artifact is put into a graveyard
from the battlefield" (no type on `to-graveyard`). "Whenever you crank ~" is an un-set mechanic.

  end-of-combat step, yours);
- "attacks and isn't blocked" gains unblocked, and nothing when blocked;
- "When this creature attacks" fires on the attack;
- "At end of combat" fires once, with an attack and without one;
- "Whenever a creature attacks" fires for your attacker and for the opponent's.

## D991 — "Whenever you scry / surveil / scry or surveil"

Next on D990's list of unread trigger openings: 17 lines one card short begin "Whenever you scry",
"Whenever you surveil" or "Whenever you scry or surveil".

- `CardsDecisionSpec.keyword`: `scry` and `surveil` (the two spec builders) say which keyword their
  question is. The other `library-top` questions ("look at the top N…") are not scries and carry
  none.
- A new `scries` event is raised in `answerDecision` once the scry or surveil question is answered
  and the cards are placed: once per scry, whatever was picked, with the seat that scried and
  `did` naming the keyword.
- Matching is in `triggerMatches`. `what` is `scry`, `surveil` or `either`, and `by` (default
  `you`) is whose scry, as `cycles` asks it.
- Three prologue rows read the three openings.

**A fall-through, caught by the pregate.** The new `case 'scries'` was first written between
`case 'discards':` and `case 'cycles':`. `discards` falls through into `cycles` on purpose, so it
then fell into the scry case instead, and every discard trigger stopped firing. 7 existing discard
tests and the cleanup-step tests went red. The case now sits above the pair. `scries` is also on
the deck-coverage list of compiler-only mechanics: no pool deck plays one.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the three cards read;
- a scry fires "scry" and "scry or surveil" and not "surveil";
- a surveil fires "surveil" and "scry or surveil" and not "scry";
- an opponent's scry fires none of yours.

Faults injected by script: 6 of 6 caught.

    engine tests: 5,317, all passing (merged with the other session's D751)

## D992 — Monstrous as a designation, and two more damage openings

Three more openings from D990's list:

**"When ~ becomes monstrous"** (10 lines). Monstrosity used to be its +1/+1 counters: "is it
monstrous" was "does it have one". D182 wrote down the visible edge of that: a creature that lost
its counters became monstrous-able again. Now:
- `MONSTROUS` is a marker counter, a designation kept as `RENOWNED` is (CR 701.32b), and it is in
  `MARKERS` so proliferate and counter replacement leave it alone.
- Monstrosity puts its +1/+1 counters **and** the marker. It does nothing if the creature is
  already monstrous or has left (CR 701.32a), which covers two activations in response to each
  other.
- "Activate only if it isn't monstrous", Fleecemane Lion's static and the compiled "as long as ~
  is monstrous" all ask the marker.
- Putting the marker is recorded as counters put on the permanent, so "When ~ becomes monstrous"
  is a `counters-put` trigger on it.

**"Whenever a source deals damage to ~"** (5): the "is dealt damage" sentence the other way round,
the same row.

**"Whenever ~ is dealt combat damage"** (4): `damaged` with `combatOnly`. The engine now sets
`combat` on the `damaged` event it raises for combat damage.

- the cards read;
- monstrosity puts two counters, gains 3 life (the trigger) and gives trample (the static), is not
  offered again, and is still monstrous with its +1/+1 counters removed;
- activated twice in response to itself it grows once and triggers once, and a real proliferate
  adds a +1/+1 counter without making it monstrous again;
- a ping fires "a source deals damage to ~" and not "is dealt combat damage";
- a blocked attacker's damage fires "is dealt combat damage".

Faults injected by script: 9. 7 were caught at once. The 2 misses (the marker's place in `MARKERS`,

## D755 — Spell copies: "Copy target instant or sorcery spell", and cast triggers that copy

"You may choose new targets for the copy." ends 131 unread lines. The engine has had
`copySpellOnStack` and the new-targets question since the hand-written Twincast; the compiler read
neither.

- `copyTargetSpell`, a group reader in `composeEffects`: "Copy target instant or sorcery spell [you
  control]. You may choose new targets for the copy." is Twincast's hand-written reading, on a
  spell (Reverberate) or an ability (Lithoform Engine's first). The two sentences are read
  together because the second is the question, not an effect. A copy of only an instant, or only
  a sorcery, is not read.
- A `triggerFromLine` pre-reader: "<cast prologue>, [you may] copy it / that spell. You may choose
  new targets for the copy."
  - The prologue is read by the trigger table with a stand-in effect, so every cast filter the
    table knows works here.
  - The copy is made of `answering`, the spell the cast event saw, as casualty and replicate make
    theirs.
  - Only when every event is a cast: an activation or a death has no spell to copy.
  - "You may copy" asks first, and the new-targets question is asked only after "Copy it"
    (`askOnlyIfChosen`, D725).
- Not read: copying abilities, "your next instant or sorcery spell this turn" (Doublecast), and
  cast filters the table cannot read ("from your library", "with hybrid mana").

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the cards read; a death trigger's "copy it" and a copy of an instant only stay unread;
- an opponent's Bolt is copied by Reverberate's shape and both copies hit;
- copy target spell is refused a creature spell;
- "spell you control" on an ability copies my own Bolt and is refused the opponent's;
- the cast trigger copies my spell and not the opponent's;
- "you may copy": declined, there is no copy and no target question; accepted, both hit.

Faults injected by script: 7. 3 were caught at once. The 4 misses were test gaps, all fixed and
now caught:
- the opponent still held priority when "you control" was checked;
- no test aimed the copy at a creature spell;
- the non-cast refusal used a prologue that did not parse anyway;
- the instant-only refusal was printed on an Enchantment, where a spell line never reads.

    engine tests: 5,357, all passing (merged with the other session's D996)

Coverage: 13,449 of 31,900 cards (+16), 34,087 of 59,888 lines (+21), against 5565d3e.

## D756 — Named modes

225 unread bullets on 97 cards print a name in front of the mode: "• Attack — Create a 2/2 white
Knight creature token." (Battle Menu), "• Surgical Separation — Destroy target creature. …"
(Impossible Choice). `modalScriptFor` read the whole bullet, name and all, and no effect reader
knows a sentence that begins with a name.

Under a "Choose …" header the name has no rules meaning, the role an ability word has (CR
207.2c). So the effect after the dash is read, and the mode's description keeps the name for the
table. The name must start with a capital letter or digit and hold no sentence punctuation.
Sieges ("choose Khans or Dragons"), whose names are the choice itself, have another header and
never reach this reader. Tiered spells ("• Fire — {0} — …") and modal triggers stay unread for
the same reason.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read, with the names in the descriptions; a Siege and a lower-case "name" stay unread;
- each mode of a named "Choose one" does what follows its name;
- "Choose one or both" with named modes, both chosen.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught. The first gate stopped at the test typecheck: a
`compileCard` script read without the optional chain it needs.

    engine tests: 5,360, all passing

Coverage: 13,471 of 31,900 cards (+17), 34,150 of 59,888 lines (+53), against aaaceb1.

## D998 — "When enchanted creature becomes the target …" and "Whenever ~ blocks a creature with flying"

Two openings from D990's prologue list: the Aura that watches its host being targeted (7 lines:
Ice Cage, Illusionary Armor, Sleeping Potion, Spectral Prison, Crystallization) and the reach
creature that rewards blocking a flier (7 lines: Netcaster Spider, Skystinger, Woolly Spider).

- **Targeted host.** `raiseTargeted` now carries what is attached to the targeted permanent, and
  `targeted` takes `who: 'self' | 'attached'` the way D994's damage and tapping events do. The
  event also says whether the targeting object was a spell, so "the target of **a spell**" (Spectral
  Prison) keeps to spells and an activated ability does not break it.
- An Aura's own "this enchantment becomes the target" still means the Aura, and targeting the Aura
  is not targeting its host.
- Casting a second Aura on the host is a spell that targets it, so an Ice Cage on that creature goes.
  That is the printed rule, and a test holds it.
- **Blocked flier.** The `blocks` event carries the attacker's live keywords at the block, and
  `blocks` takes `blockedKeyword`. "Blocks a creature with <word>" reads only when the word is a
  keyword the engine knows.
- "Destroy / exile **that creature**" and "that spell or ability's controller gains control" after
  the targeted host are not read yet.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the cards read; a non-keyword refuses; "an opponent controls" keeps `by: 'opponent'`;
- targeting the Aura itself does not fire its host trigger;
- a spell at the host fires the Aura, and the Aura's own "this enchantment" trigger stays quiet;
- casting a second Aura on the host sacrifices the first;
- an ability at the host fires "a spell or ability" and not "a spell"; targeting a player fires
  nothing;
- blocking the flier fires "blocks a creature with flying"; blocking the bear does not.

Faults injected by script: 11 of 11 caught (three after the pins above).

    engine tests: 5,372, all passing

## D757 — Modal triggered abilities

"When ~ enters, choose one —" and its kin ("When ~ dies", "Landfall — …", "At the beginning of your
end step, …") were 193 unread trigger headers, each with its bullets unread under it. Triggers had
no modes at all: only spells did (`ModalDef`, D664).

**The engine.**
- `TriggerDef.modal` holds the modes. Only "choose one".
- **The mode is chosen as the ability goes on the stack, before its targets (CR 700.2b).**
  `fireTrigger` pushes the ability and asks a `pendingDecision` with `options` (one per mode) and
  `modeChoice` (the mode index each option stands for). This is the word question the table and
  the bot already answer, so neither needed a new prompt.
- Only modes that can be aimed are offered. With none, the ability is not put on the stack, as a
  trigger with no legal target is not (CR 603.3c). With one, it is chosen for its controller.
- The answer, in `answerDecision`, records `modes` on the stack object, as a modal spell's are.
  The stack object's description becomes the chosen mode, which is public from then on. The
  ability is then aimed as `fireTrigger` aims any other (`aimModalTrigger`): by the engine where
  the targets are obvious, otherwise through `pendingChoice`. With no answer (its controller left
  the game) the ability is removed.
- `abilityOrTrigger` returns, for a modal trigger with its mode chosen, a reading built from that
  mode (`modalReading`): its targets, questions and effect, run by `runModes` as a modal spell's
  are. The fizzle check, the questions and the resolution all go through it unchanged.
  `abilityTargetSpecs` gives the chosen mode's targets, for `chooseTargets` and the table's offer.

**The compiler.** `modalTriggerFor` reads the header and the bullets under it as one group, called
from the permanent loop in compile.ts before lines are offered one by one.
- The prologue is read by `triggerFromLine` with a stand-in effect, so every event the trigger
  table knows works here.
- Each bullet is read by `composeEffects`, a name stripped as D756 strips one.
- A bullet that does not read, or reads with a reflexive trigger, refuses the group, as one
  unreadable mode refuses a modal spell.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the cards read with three modes, and one unreadable bullet refuses all three lines;
- the mode is asked as the trigger goes on the stack ("Test Channeler: choose one"), the stack then
  shows the chosen mode, and it is done;
- a mode with targets is offered only when it can be aimed, and is then aimed by its controller;
- one aimable mode is chosen for its controller and its obvious target taken;
- with no aimable mode the ability never reaches the stack;
- the bot answers the mode question and play goes on.

Faults injected by script: 8 of 8 caught.

    engine tests: 5,372, all passing (with the other session's D997 merged)

Coverage: 13,540 of 31,900 cards (+69), 34,377 of 59,888 lines (+227), against 99812fd.

choice". The words say what an edict always meant, since the sacrificing player chooses (CR
701.21a), but none of the edict readers knew them: 42 unread lines in the corpus. Live Scryfall
data, which is what a pasted deck brings, uses the new wording throughout. `readEffect` now reads

three words. "Target player sacrifices two creatures" stays unread in either wording; that is a
gap in the edict reader, not in this change.

**The bottom of the library.** "Put target creature on top of its owner's library" read (D546) and
"… on the bottom of …" did not. The same reader takes both now, with `putOnBottomOfLibrary`
(D954).

- an opponent's edict: the opponent is asked, the creature they pick goes, and nothing of the
  caster's;
- "two creatures of their choice": two go;
- the tucked creature is last in its owner's library, not first.

## D759 — "… that was dealt damage this turn"

28 unread lines aim at a creature "that was dealt damage this turn": the red-black finishers
("Destroy target creature that was dealt damage this turn") and their creature and mode cousins.

- **A turn fact, not marked damage.** `permanentsDamagedThisTurn` lists, as `id#objectSeq`, every
  permanent damage landed on this turn. `recordDamage` writes it, whatever dealt the damage; the
  older `damagedBy` record keeps only sources on the battlefield. It is cleared with the other turn
  facts. Marked damage would be the wrong fact: regeneration removes it, and the creature was
  still dealt the damage. The object sequence keeps a creature that left and came back from
  counting as damaged (CR 400.7). `wasDealtDamageThisTurn` asks it.
- **`targetSpecFrom` peels the phrase**, as it peels mana value, power and creature types: the inner
  phrase must point at a permanent, and the filter asks the record.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- an undamaged creature is refused; pinged for one, the same creature is taken and destroyed;
- the record is empty again next turn;
- damage that was prevented was never dealt, so the target is still refused.

Faults injected by script: 4. 3 were caught. The miss is equivalent: it dropped the `amount > 0`
guard, and prevented damage never reaches `recordDamage`, so the guard is only defensive.

The first gate failed four older tests that held the phrase as unreadable. D611's cost reduction
"if it targets a creature that was dealt damage this turn" now reads through the same peel, so
Bitter Downfall is whole. Two refusal rows now use "… combat damage this turn", which still does
not read, and D469's refusal list drops the phrase.

    engine tests: 5,386, all passing (merged with the other session's D998)

Coverage: 13,582 of 31,900 cards (+19), 34,442 of 59,888 lines (+27), against 20fdb27.

## D760 — Gaining control, for good and until end of turn

Two gaps in one family. 149 unread lines print "gain control".

**For good.** "Gain control of target <permanent>." had no reader: Agent of Treachery's enters
trigger, the sorcery cousins of Treachery, and "Gain control of target artifact". `readEffect` now
reads it with `gainControl`, which moves the permanent to the new controller's battlefield
(control is which battlefield a permanent is on here), and nothing moves it back. A phrase with
"until end of turn" or "for as long as" is not taken by this reader.

**Until end of turn, more widely.** D516's `stealPrefix` (the Act of Treason sentence) took only
the bare "target creature".
- The target now goes through `targetSpecFrom`, so "… an opponent controls" and "… with mana value
  3 or less" read. That also reads the creatures' and planeswalkers' steals, which print the
  narrower phrase.
- Any permanent, with "Untap that permanent" (Zealous Conscripts); `stealUntilEndOfTurn` already
  works on one.
- Threaten's order, "Untap target creature and gain control of it until end of turn. That creature
  gains haste until end of turn.", is read as the three-sentence form.

Zealous Conscripts reading whole completes the Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker combo's pieces, both
compiled.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the cards read, and a bare "until end of turn" steal with no untap stays unread;
- for good: the creature is the caster's, and still is two turns later;
- an enters trigger takes a land for good;
- Threaten's order: untapped, hasty, and back with its owner as the turn ends;
- Conscripts' form on a land: taken, and back next turn;
- "an opponent controls" on the steal refuses the caster's own creature.

Faults injected by script: 5. 4 were caught. The miss is equivalent: it dropped the duration guard
on the lasting reader, and `targetSpecFrom` refuses "target creature until end of turn" anyway.

    engine tests: 5,392, all passing

Coverage: 13,617 of 31,900 cards (+26), 34,489 of 59,888 lines (+38), against 676129d.

## D761 — "~ can be your commander."

35 unread lines are this sentence, on the planeswalkers and the few other cards that may lead a
deck (CR 903.3d). It is a deck-construction statement with no effect once the game starts, and
nothing here restricts which card a deck names as its commander. So, like D670's "Partner" and
"Choose a Background", the permanent loop in compile.ts counts it compiled and emits nothing. The
subject must be the card's own name or its short name ("Svega can be your commander."). The one
sorcery that prints it (Ashaya's Enduring Bond) takes the spell path and still shows it unread.

**Tests.** 2 compile tests through `compileCard`:
- the line reads with the full name and with the short name;
- naming another card leaves it unread.

## D762 — Ascend and the city's blessing

29 unread "Ascend" lines, and 29 more that ask "if / as long as you have the city's blessing". The
engine had neither the keyword nor the designation.

- **`Seat.citysBlessing`** (CR 702.131c): a player designation, got once and kept for the rest of
  the game, so it outlives the card that gave it. `SeatView.citysBlessing` carries it to the
  table, which shows a "city's blessing" badge beside the monarch's.
- **`CardScript.ascend`**, compiled from the bare keyword.
  - On a permanent it is a static ability (CR 702.131b). `ascendBlessings`, in the state-based
    loop beside `auraControl`, blesses a player who controls ten or more permanents, one of them
    with ascend and its abilities on.
  - On an instant or sorcery it is checked once, first, as the spell resolves (CR 702.131a).
- **The condition**: `controller-citys-blessing` for statics ("~ gets +2/+2 as long as you have
  the city's blessing"), and a row in `interveningConditionRows` for triggers, spells and "Activate
  only if".
- Not read: the "If you have the city's blessing, <X> instead" sentence on spells, which is the
  reversed form of D693's "instead if" and has no reader yet.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- a permanent with ascend: the tenth permanent (a land played) brings the blessing and the +2/+2;
  taken back to nine, the blessing and the bonus remain next turn;
- nine permanents with ascend are not enough, and an opponent with twelve and no ascend is not
  blessed;
- an ascend sorcery blesses at ten and not at nine;
- "if you have the city's blessing" on an attack trigger, without and with the blessing.

Faults injected by script: 8 of 8 caught. The first gate stopped at the deck-coverage test: no
pool deck plays ascend, so `ascend` joins its list of mechanics only the compiler reads.

    engine tests: 5,404, all passing

## D1002 — Expend: "Whenever you expend N"

From the refreshed prologue list (9 lines unread for this reason alone, Bloomburrow's Raccoons and
Muerra, Trash Tactician). "You expend 4 as you spend your fourth total mana to cast spells during a
turn."

- `payFrom` now reports how much mana a payment spent in all (`manaSpent`), beside D917's colours.
- `GameState.manaSpentOnSpellsThisTurn`, per seat, counts what casting spells spent. It is cleared at
  the end of each turn and by a table reset. Mana spent on activated abilities is not counted.
- Casting a spell adds its payment to the seat's total and raises one `expend` event for each
  threshold the total crosses, so a three-mana spell after a two-mana one raises 3, 4 and 5.
- `expend` takes `n` and fires only for its own seat.

  the opponent's "expend 2" stays quiet;
- mana spent on an activated ability is not expended;
- the count starts again each turn;
- a table reset clears it.

## D1004 — State triggers: "When you control no Islands, sacrifice ~" (CR 603.8)

The old sea creatures' drawback (Dandân, Sea Serpent, Pirate Ship, Island Fish Jasconius), its
Swamp, Forest and artifact cousins (Bog Serpent, Gorilla Pack, Covetous Dragon), Emperor
Crocodile's "no other creatures", and "When there are no creatures on the battlefield" (Drop of
Honey, Porphyry Nodes). 26 legal lines.

- A new `state` trigger with `none: { whose, type | subtype, other }`. At the end of every `settle`,
  each permanent carrying one is offered a `state` event, and `fireTrigger` asks two things: does the
  state hold, and is this ability already on the stack. It triggers whenever the state matches and
  not again while it waits (CR 603.8).
- **Read only with a sacrifice after it**, which is every legal card that prints one. A state
  trigger triggers again as soon as its ability leaves the stack if the state still holds, so an
  effect that did not end the state would trigger forever. The sacrifice removes the watcher.
- Basic land types and card types only. "Snow lands", "permanents with … counters" and "the chosen
  color" are not read.

- the cards read; "When you control no Islands, you gain 1 life" stays unread;
- losing the last Island sacrifices the Serpent; losing one of two does not;
- the trigger is on the stack once, and casting another spell over it does not add a second;

- "no creatures on the battlefield" counts everybody's: one Bear left on the other side keeps it,

23 lines, and the Pest's "token with "When this creature dies, you gain 1 life."" beside it. Three
things kept them unread.

- **Toxic on a token.** `tokenFrom` checks that every keyword it names can be read back from the
  token's text. "Toxic 1" is a number, not a `Keyword`, so it never counted. It now counts the
  "toxic N" parts, which `printedToxic` reads off any card's text, combat included.
- **The quoted ability inline.** "… token with "X"" and "… token with <keywords> and "X"" are split
  in `tokenEffect` and handed on as the quoted rider D536 reads after "It has", so the same check
  applies.
- **A printed static as the quoted ability.** The quoted text had to compile to a script, and "This
  creature can't block." is a static the characteristics layer applies with no script behind it.
  The check now also accepts a line `isPrintedAbilityLine` reads. A sentence neither reads ("Fly over
  the moon.") is still refused.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read; an unreadable quoted sentence still refuses;
- the Mite is a 1/1 Phyrexian Mite artifact creature token and cannot block;
- its unblocked hit deals 1 damage and gives 1 poison counter;
- the Pest token's own quoted "When this creature dies, you gain 1 life" fires.

The compile.test refusal row for the Pest token now reads, so it became a reads test.

Faults injected by script: 6 of 6 caught. A `printedToxic` check in the read-back was folded away
after it survived a fault: the digits the regex requires are exactly what that reader accepts.

    engine tests: 5,437, all passing

Coverage: 13,729 of 31,900 cards (+49), 34,709 of 59,888 lines (+83).

## D1009 — Exile from a hand until ~ leaves: Tidehollow Sculler

From the "When ~ leaves the battlefield, …" tails: Tidehollow Sculler (a Legacy staple) and Mesmeric
Fiend print the hand version of the exile-until-it-leaves pair. "When ~ enters, target opponent
reveals their hand and you choose a nonland card from it. Exile that card." and "When ~ leaves the
battlefield, return the exiled card to its owner's hand."

- A whole-card shape, beside the battlefield one (Journey to Nowhere, Banisher Priest), because the
  two triggers are one effect and neither line is a unit. Both lines must be present; the exile line
  alone stays what it was.
- The chosen card is exiled with `exiledBy` set to the Sculler, and the leave trigger hands back what
  points at it. `returnExiledBy` now takes where it goes back to: the battlefield, or the owner's hand.
- If the Sculler leaves before its entry trigger resolves, the leave trigger finds nothing and the
  card stays exiled, which is the printed rule (and a well-known play).

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads; without the return line there is no leave trigger;
- the opponent's two spells are offered and their land is not; the chosen card goes to exile, and
  returns to that player's hand when the Sculler dies;
- killed in response to its own entry trigger, the Sculler gives nothing back and the card stays
  exiled.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught (one after the exile-line-alone pin).

## D1010 — "Other than ~" and two-colour targets

Two target phrases that kept exile-until-it-leaves cards (Faceless Butcher, Slithery Stalker) and
about 30 other lines unread, both read at the front of `targetSpecFrom` so every reader that uses
it gets them.

- **"Target creature other than ~"** (and "permanent", "nonland permanent", "other than this
  creature"): the same rule as "another", that the target is not the permanent whose ability this is. The
  phrase is read without the clause and the filter refuses the source. The name is taken by its
  printed capital; "other than a Wall" is not a name and stays unread.
- **"Target green or white creature"**, "target black or red permanent": the colour list on a target
  filter is already an any-of, so the two colours read side by side. The description keeps the
  printed "or".

- The pair reads for permanent nouns only. A spell phrase reads adjacent words as "both" (D490's
  "blue instant"), so "white or blue spell" keeps its own grammar; the first pregate caught the
  rewrite reaching it.
- An Aura's "Enchant red or green creature" now reads too, through D939's narrower-creature host;
  the compile.test refusal row for it became a reads test.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the cards read; "other than a Wall" stays unread;
- "target green or white creature" takes the green Bear or the white Knight, and refuses the black
  Zombie;
- "other than this creature": alone it kills nothing and survives; with a Zombie on the other side it
  kills the Zombie;
- "nonland permanent other than this creature" never takes a land.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught (one after the land pin).

    engine tests: 5,453, all passing

## D1013 — Conjunctions in a card filter: "legendary creature card", "noncreature, nonland card"

A tally of the graveyard-card target phrases inside unread lines, each tried as "Return target <X>
card from your graveyard to your hand.", found the refused ones were all conjunctions: "noncreature,
nonland card" (6), "legendary creature card" (4), "artifact creature card", "Zombie creature card",
"enchantment creature card", "nonlegendary creature card", "multicolored card", "black card".

- `graveyardTypeTest` reads several words with no "or" as a conjunction: each word is a test the card
  must pass. The words are a card type, its negation, a real subtype (by its capital), legendary or
  nonlegendary, a colour, multicolored or colorless. They are read off the printed card, like the
  rest of the function. Any other word refuses the phrase.
- D919's subtype branch now takes single-word parts only, so "Zombie creature" reaches the
  conjunction instead of being refused there.
- Every reader of the helper gets it: graveyard targets, the dig's "you may reveal a … card", and the
  hand-reveal choices.

- **A wrong reading caught by the pregate.** D1010's colour-pair rewrite also reached graveyard phrases
  ("target white or black creature card from your graveyard"). With this increment that became "white
  black creature", read as a conjunction: white and black. D527's refusal row failed on it. The pair
  rewrite now leaves card phrases alone, so the line is unread again, as it should be.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- the cards read; an unknown word refuses;
- with a legendary creature, a Bear, an artifact, an artifact creature, a Zombie, a two-colour
  creature and a land in the graveyard, each spell can target exactly the one card that passes every
  word.

## D1014 — "If ~ is in your graveyard, …": Bridge from Below and the upkeep returners

From a tally of the intervening-if conditions inside unread lines: "if ~ is in your graveyard" was
17 lines (Bridge from Below, Ghastly Remains, Gigapede, Genesis, Blood Operative). These are
abilities that work only from the graveyard. D632 built that machinery (`TriggerDef.inGraveyard`);
these lines spell the zone out instead of implying it.

- **The condition.** "<prologue>, if ~ is in your graveyard, <effect>" is read as a graveyard-only
  trigger with that intervening-if (CR 603.4), checked as it triggers and again as it resolves. A
  card exiled from the graveyard in response does nothing. "Return ~ to your hand" in such a line is
  the card returning itself from there. Read for any event, because the condition names the zone
  itself.
- **Bridge from Below's prologues.** "Whenever a [nontoken] creature is put into your / an opponent's
  graveyard from the battlefield": a death with `owner`. That is the owner's graveyard (CR 400.3), not
  the controller's.
- **A fact the death event lacked.** A dying token has ceased to exist when its death is announced,
  so nothing could say whose graveyard it went to. The event now carries `subjectOwner`, read from
  the last-known card. The first fault run found this: with "nontoken" removed, a token's death still
  made no Zombie.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- from the graveyard, your nontoken creature dying makes a Zombie, and a token dying does not;
- exiled from the graveyard in response, the Bridge makes nothing;
- an opponent's creature dying exiles the Bridge;
- the Bridge in hand hears no death;
- the upkeep returner comes back from the graveyard and does nothing on the battlefield.

Faults injected by script: 7 of 7 caught (two after the response pin and the owner fix).

    engine tests: 5,468, all passing

Coverage: 13,831 of 31,900 cards (+8), 34,872 of 59,888 lines (+11).

## D763 — Turn facts: life lost, no spell cast, no attack

End-step triggers were the second shape in the re-measured beta queue (40 four-player pods, seed
59701: 51.1% of the cards players met had an unread line, down from 70.2% at D518). Their bodies
mostly fail on a turn fact. Several of those facts the engine already records, and only the
words were missing. New rows in `interveningConditionRows`, so they serve triggers, spells and
activation restrictions alike:
- "if you lost life this turn", and "if you gained or lost life this turn", off `lifeLostThisTurn`
  (life paid counts; damage turned into poison does not, as that record keeps);
- "if an opponent / a player lost N or more life this turn";
- "if you didn't cast a spell this turn", the existing "haven't" row in the other tense;
- "if you didn't attack with a creature this turn", raid's record read the other way.

Not read: "a creature died under your control this turn", which needs a per-seat death record.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests, each an end-step draw checked with and without its fact:
- the cards read;
- "lost life" and "gained or lost life": nothing on a quiet turn, both after paying 2 life;
- "an opponent lost 3 or more": not after 2, yes after 3;
- "didn't cast a spell": a quiet turn draws, a spell turns it off;
- "didn't attack with a creature": declaring no attackers draws, an attack turns it off.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught. The first gate failed a D563 refusal row that held "if
you lost life this turn" unread; it reads now, as the controller's own record, so the row uses the
per-player death count instead.

    engine tests: 5,479, all passing (with the other session's D1016 merged)

Coverage: 13,842 of 31,900 cards (+4), 34,888 of 59,888 lines (+7), against 5309345. Most of
these triggers have a second unread clause.

## D1018 — Spell targets: whose spell, and what it targets

A tally of the spell-target phrases inside unread lines, each tried as "Counter target <X>.", found
two clauses D490's spell grammar did not take after the noun:

- **Whose spell**: "target instant or sorcery spell you control" (7), "target spell an opponent
  controls", "creature spell you control", "noncreature spell an opponent controls". Read off the
  spell's controller on the stack.
- **What it targets**: "target spell that targets you", "… that targets a permanent you control",
  "… a creature [you control]" (about 12). Read off the spell's own targets on the stack.

Both read the spell's stack object; a card on the stack has exactly one. "Target spell" with only a
clause and no kind word reads too.

  its "spell an opponent controls" may not; after seat 0 passes, seat 1's are the other way round;
- a Bolt at seat 1 may be countered by seat 1's "that targets you" and not by "that targets a
  permanent you control", and a Bolt at seat 1's Bear the reverse. A Bolt at its own caster, or at

Faults injected by script: 6 of 6 caught (two after the own-caster pins).
