## D1019 — Increment

"Increment (Whenever you cast a spell, if the amount of mana you spent is greater than this
creature's power or toughness, put a +1/+1 counter on this creature.)" A keyword printed on 10
legal creatures (Hungry Graffalon, Cuboid Colony, Textbook Tabulator, Pensive Professor and the rest
of the set). It needs the mana a cast spent, which D1002 started counting.

- The `spell-cast` event carries `manaSpent`, from the payment's own count.
- The keyword reads as a "whenever you cast a spell" trigger with `manaSpentOverSelf`. `fireTrigger`
  compares the mana spent with the creature's live power and toughness as it triggers, and the trigger
  puts a +1/+1 counter on it.
- The second ask of the "if" at resolution is not made: the event's amount does not travel to the
  stack object. It only matters if the creature's size changes while the trigger waits, and then the
  counter still arrives.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- on a 2/3, a three-mana spell adds a counter; a two-mana spell (not more than 2 or 3) and a free
  spell do not;
- the opponent's three-mana spell does not.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 5,487, all passing

Coverage: 13,858 of 31,900 cards (+4), 34,915 of 59,888 lines (+9).

## D1020 — a measure of the event's creature: "life equal to its toughness"

"Whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to a player, you gain life equal to that
creature's toughness" (Ikra Shidiqi), "Whenever a creature you control dies, you gain life equal to
that creature's toughness" (Proper Burial), "When Bottle Golems dies, you gain life equal to its
power", "Whenever a creature you control enters, you gain life equal to its toughness" (Angelic
Chorus, Verdant Sun's Avatar), "When Champion of Wits enters, you may draw cards equal to its power.
If you do, discard two cards."

- `eventRelativeEffect` reads "[you] gain life / [you] draw cards equal to its | that creature's
  power | toughness". It only does so on triggers whose every event is an entry, a death, an attack
  or a combat hit: the four events that are about one creature and carry its size. "Its" and "that
  creature's" are both the event's subject; on the card's own trigger that is the card itself.
- Measured live while that creature is still on the battlefield, so a pump in response counts.
- Once it has gone, it is measured as it last was (CR 608.2h). That covers a death, and a blink in
  response, which makes a new object (CR 400.7). The size comes from a new snapshot:
  - `StackObject.subjectStats` (`{power, toughness}`) is taken in `fireTrigger` from the event's
    `subjectPower`/`subjectToughness`;
  - it is carried through `TriggerAbout`;
  - it is handed to the resolution and to `beforeDecisions` as `EffectContext.subjectStats`.
  The dead creature's counters are still part of its size, which the printed numbers would miss.
- Lose-life and each-opponent drains with the same measure are not read. Nothing legal prints them on
  these events.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- a 1/4 entering gains 4;
- the same 1/4 with a +1/+1 counter dying gains 5, not the printed 4;
- the card's own death gains its own power;
- a 1/4 connecting gains 4;
- an entry draws its power;
- with "If you do, discard a card" the draws come before the discard.

Faults injected by script: 8 of 8 caught. The draw-before-discard fault was missed at first and is
now pinned by the looter test.

Coverage: 13,872 of 31,900 cards (+14), 34,935 of 59,888 lines (+20).

## D1021 — one of yours becoming a target

"Whenever a creature you control becomes the target of a spell or ability an opponent controls, you
may draw a card" (Shapers' Sanctuary, Battle Mammoth's permanent version). The same prologue appears
on:
- MACO Strike Team;
- "a Dragon you control … deals 3 damage to that player" (Thunderbreak Regent);
- "a Cleric creature you control" (Daru Spiritualist);
- "a creature you control with a +1/+1 counter on it" (Swarm Shambler);
- "a Wolf or Werewolf you control … of an instant or sorcery spell" (Silverfur Partisan);
- "… that creature gets +3/+3" (Wild Defiance);
- "another permanent you control … return that permanent to its owner's hand" (Cloud Cover);
- "a creature you control becomes the target of a spell, ~ fights up to one target creature you
  don't control" (Gargos);
- "~ or another Spirit you control" (King of the Oathbreakers' prologue).

Until now `targeted` was offered only to the targeted permanent itself and to its attachments (D998).

- **Engine.**
  - `raise` offers `targeted` to every permanent, as it does entries and deaths.
  - `raiseTargeted` puts the targeted permanent's controller, live types, subtypes and counters on
    the event, and whether an instant or sorcery did the targeting (an Aura spell targets too, and
    is neither).
  - The matcher's new `who: 'any' | 'another'` arm asks `of: 'you'`, `what` (creature, or creature
    or planeswalker), `ofSubtypes`, `withCounter` and `instantOrSorcery`. `orSelf` passes ~ itself
    whatever its types.
  - On those triggers the event's permanent is the trigger's subject, so "that creature" is the
    one targeted.
- **Compiler.**
  - One parsed prologue row reads the family. It refuses a tribe that is not a creature type and
    any `with` filter but a counter.
  - `targeted` joins the player-action events: "that player" is the controller of the spell or
    ability that targeted, which the engine already passes as the actor.
  - "That permanent" joins D964's "that creature" rewrite to "it" on triggers about another
    permanent.

**Tests.** 7 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and a non-creature-type tribe does not;
- an opponent's spell at your creature fires, your own spell does not, and their spell at their
  own creature does not;
- a Dragon fires and "that player" is the caster, while a Bear does not fire;
- "~ or another Spirit" fires for itself (a Giant) and for a Spirit, but not for a Bear;
- an instant pumps "that creature" and an Aura spell does not;
- "that permanent" is returned to hand;
- "another" leaves the watcher out, "a creature" leaves an enchantment out, and the counter filter
  is asked.

Faults injected by script: 16 of 16 caught. Of the first 16, 14 were caught and 2 survived:
- Naming `targeted` among the board events was redundant: anything outside `selfOnly` already walks
  the board. It was folded away, and its replacement fault, putting `targeted` back in `selfOnly`,
  is caught.
- The creature-type refusal is now pinned by a "Whenever a Vehicle you control …" row that stays
  unread.

Coverage: 13,884 of 31,900 cards (+12), 34,950 of 59,888 lines (+15).

## D1022 — poison counters from an effect

"Target opponent gets two poison counters", "Each opponent gets a poison counter" (Infectious Bite),
"each player gets a poison counter" (Ichor Rats), "you get a poison counter" (Phyrexian
Vatmother). "Defending player gets a poison counter" (Crypt Cobra) and "that player gets …" on a hit
or on a player's action also read, because the referent swap turns them into "target player". The
same goes for D1021's "a creature you control becomes the target of a spell, target opponent gets a
poison counter" (Venerated Rotpriest).

- `givePoison` in effects.ts adds the counters (CR 122.1f). It is not damage and not life loss, so
  nothing that watches those fires. The ten-poison loss is the state-based check that already reads
  `poison` for toxic and infect.
- `readEffect` reads "(target player | target opponent | each opponent | each player | you)
  get(s) (a | one … five | N) poison counter(s)". "Each player" skips eliminated seats.
- "Its controller gets a poison counter" after a target is a separate reader and is not this one.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- the target gets two, each opponent and each player one, and "you" yourself;
- "defending player" is the one attacked;
- 8 + 2 poison eliminates the seat and seat 0 wins.

Faults injected by script: 6. 5 were caught; the 6th was a guard against a non-positive amount
that no printed line can reach, and it was folded away.

Coverage: 13,899 of 31,900 cards (+15), 34,967 of 59,888 lines (+17).
## D764 — "If a creature died under your control this turn"

The condition D763 left out because it needed a record the engine did not keep. Morbid's
`creaturesDiedThisTurn` counts every creature that died; this one counts only the creatures its
controller controlled as they died.

- `creaturesDiedThisTurnBy`, keyed by the seat that **controlled** the creature as it died. It is
  written where morbid's count is written (`relocate`, asked of the permanent as it was on the
  battlefield, so last-known information decides; CR 700.4) and cleared with the other turn
  facts in all three places they are reset.
- `turnFacts.creaturesDiedUnder`, and a row in `interveningConditionRows` for "if a creature died
  under your control this turn" and "… you controlled died this turn".

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- my creature destroyed: the record holds one and the end step draws. An opponent's creature
  destroyed: morbid's count is one, and the end step does not draw;
- the record is empty next turn.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught. The first gate failed the D563 refusal row that D763 had
moved to this very phrase; it now holds "… died under an opponent's control", which is not read.

    engine tests: 5,500, all passing (with the other session's D1021 merged)

Coverage: 13,875 of 31,900 cards (+2), 34,940 of 59,888 lines (+3), against c721e9e. Of the 8 lines
that print it, the rest have another unread clause.

## D1023 — phasing

"Phasing" (CR 702.26a): "As the untap step begins, all phased-in permanents with phasing that the
active player controls phase out, and simultaneously all phased-out permanents that had phased out
under that player's control phase in." Printed on Teferi's Drake, Sandbar Crocodile, Merfolk
Raiders, Breezekeeper, Tolarian Drake, Teferi's Isle and the rest of the Mirage block. D733 had
already built phasing out and in for Teferi's Protection.

- `phasing` joins `KEYWORDS`. The keyword line reads, and so does a grant ("creatures you control
  have phasing").
- The untap step in `onEnterStep` gathers the active seat's battlefield permanents that have
  phasing before anything phases in, phases in, then phases those out. The two halves are one
  moment, so a permanent that comes back this step stays until the next one.
- "All lands / creatures / artifacts / enchantments you control phase out" (Taniwha), and "it
  phases out" as the event's permanent. With D1021 that reads "whenever a creature you control
  becomes the target of a spell an opponent controls, it phases out", and the spell then has no
  target.
- Not read: "whenever ~ phases in / out" triggers (Teferi's Imp, Warping Wurm, Shimmering Efreet).
  Phasing raises no event.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and so does "gains phasing until end of turn" (compile.test's refusal row now stands on banding);
- out at its own untap step, unchanged on the other seat's turn, in at its next own untap step,
  and out again at the one after;
- a granted phasing takes the creature and not the enchantment granting it;
- Taniwha's lands go out at upkeep, come back at the untap step, and go out again;
- a targeted creature phases out and the spell does nothing.

Faults injected by script: 8 of 8 caught. One of the first run's mutations did not compile, so it
was rerun as a well-formed one (always reading seat 0's battlefield) and is caught.

Coverage: 13,908 of 31,900 cards (+7), 34,984 of 59,888 lines (+14). Both are measured against
13,901 / 34,970, the merged tree with the other session's D764 and without this increment.
## D765 — Curses: Auras that enchant a player

"Enchant player" was refused outright: an Aura here could only be attached to a permanent. 45
legal cards print it, and the Curses are a Commander theme of their own.

**The engine.**
- `CardInstance.enchantedSeat` (CR 303.4): an Aura cast at a player records that player as it
  resolves; `attachedTo` stays null. `relocate` clears it when the Aura leaves the battlefield.
- The state-based check (CR 704.5m) keeps a Curse while that player is in the game, and puts it
  into its owner's graveyard when they leave. Before this an Aura attached to nothing was always
  binned.
- The first ask of a trigger's condition now carries `attacked` for an attack event, as the
  second ask (off the stack object) always did.
- `GOLD_TOKEN`, "Sacrifice this token: Add one mana of any color." from its makers' reminder text, joins the named tokens: Curse of Opulence makes them.

**The compiler.**
- `attachmentScriptFor`: "Enchant player" is a player-targeting Aura with no bonus of its own. Its
  triggers come through the line path, and any it cannot read stay flagged (D456's rule).
- `triggerFromLine` reads a Curse's three common openings, as conditions on events the trigger
  table already knows:
  - "At the beginning of enchanted player's upkeep / draw step / end step, …" is that step of
    each player's, when the active player is the enchanted one. "That player" and "they" read
    as on "each player's upkeep".
  - "Whenever a creature attacks enchanted player, …" is the per-attacker attack, aimed at that
    player and not at a planeswalker of theirs.
  - "Whenever enchanted player is attacked, … [Each opponent attacking that player does the
    same.]" is once per declaration that reaches that player. The effect is the Curse
    controller's, and with the second sentence each other player attacking that player does it
    too, as its own controller. These are the Commander 2017 Curses: Opulence, Verbosity,
    Vitality, Disturbance.
- Not read: Curses that change the enchanted player's creatures or what they can do (statics with
  a player scope), "that attacking player may …", and replacement effects (Curse of
  Bloodletting).

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the Curses and a Gold token read;
- cast at a player, a Curse attaches to that player and stays;
- in a three-player pod, an attack on the enchanted player gives the Curse's controller a Gold
  and the attacking opponent a Gold, and nothing to the enchanted player;
- an attack on somebody else gives nothing;
- of two attackers, the one aimed at the enchanted player gets the counter and the other does not;
- the enchanted player's upkeep mills that player, and the next player's upkeep mills nobody.

Faults injected by script: 8. 7 were caught at once. The miss (the upkeep condition dropped) was a
test that never reached another player's upkeep; it does now and catches it.

The first gate failed two older compile tests, both for the right reason:
- D456's "refuses enchant player" recorded the refusal and its cause (an Aura could attach only
  to a card), which this increment removes. It now asserts the player Aura and a still-unread
  Curse line.
- The undefined-token test held Gold in its list. Gold's text was first written from memory as
  "Sacrifice this artifact", the slip that test's note records for Food. Its makers print
  "Sacrifice this token", and the definition now says so.

    engine tests: 5,509, all passing (with the other session's D1022 merged)

Coverage: 13,894 of 31,900 cards (+7), 35,008 of 59,888 lines (+53), against 8ced5e3.

## D1024 — "one or two target creatures"

"One or two target creatures each get +2/+1 until end of turn" (Heroic Teamwork, Appeal to Eirdu),
"One or two target creatures gain flying" (Wind Sail), "Return one or two target creatures to
their owners' hands" (Counterintelligence), "Return one or two target creature cards from your
graveyard to your hand" (Infernal Rebirth), "Tap one, two, or three target creatures", "One or two
target creatures can't block this turn". 51 legal cards print "one or two target" and 17 print "one,
two, or three target". These are "up to" with a floor of one (CR 601.2c, 115.1).

- **`TargetSpec.min`.** With `optional`, it is the fewest that may be chosen. It is asked in the
  three places that read `optional`:
  - `checkTargets` refuses an announcement with fewer than the minimum;
  - `hasAnyLegalTargets` needs that many legal targets before a spell is castable or a trigger is
    put on the stack;
  - D750's removal of a trigger whose targets have gone before it is aimed counts them against it.
- **Compiler.**
  - `TARGET_QUANTIFIERS` gains "one or two", "one or two other" and "one, two, or three", with
    `min: 1`, through both spec builders and `targetSpecFrom`'s quantifier group.
  - Two readers that spelt their own quantifiers now use `TARGET_QUANTIFIER_PREFIX`: "… can't
    block / be blocked this turn" (so "two target creatures can't block" reads too) and "… each get
    +N/+N".
  - A plural keyword grant, "[quantifier] target creatures gain <keywords> until end of turn", has
    the singular reader's three-way hint.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- one target is a cast, two is the most, three is "too many", and none is refused;
- with an empty graveyard the spell is not castable, and one card is enough;
- an entry trigger with nothing to aim at is not put on the stack;
- a trigger whose only card leaves before it is aimed is removed;
- the plural grant, the three-target tap and the plural "can't block" all work.

Faults injected by script: 8. 7 are caught, two of them after tests added for that purpose. A
spawned trigger with no targets resolves to nothing, so the castability rule is now asserted
directly. The 8th was a plural-only guard that nothing printed could reach, and it was folded away.

## D1025 — the edict that takes the biggest

These edicts take the biggest permanent:
- "Each opponent sacrifices a creature with the greatest power among creatures that player
  controls" (Crackling Doom, and Myrkul's Edict's 20 row);
- "… a creature or planeswalker with the highest / greatest mana value among creatures and
  planeswalkers they control" (Soul Shatter, Flare of Malice);
- Szat's Will's "a creature they control with the greatest power";
- the same aimed at "target opponent" (Break Under Pressure, Riveteers Charm, Consumed by Greed).

13 legal cards print one.

- `readEffect` reads each opponent or one target opponent / player. Each sacrificing player chooses
  from their own permanents that are tied for the most, as the spell resolves.
- The filter is measured against the chooser's own board: a bigger creature of yours does not make
  their 5/5 safe. A tie is their choice, and nothing smaller can be given up.
- Power is live, mana value is printed, and a token's is 0. Both forms really sacrifice, so
  sacrifice triggers fire.
- Not read: the second sentences some of these cards add ("You gain life equal to the greatest
  power among creatures sacrificed this way", Will of the Abzan's "any number of target opponents
  each … and lose 3 life").

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- the 5/5 goes rather than the 1/1 that costs 6, even with your own 7/7 on the table, and yours
  stays;
- the highest mana value goes and a mana-value-9 artifact stays;
- aimed at one opponent;
- with two tied 2/2s both are offered and the 1/1 is not.

Faults injected by script: 7. 6 are caught, two of them after the tests above were added for them.
The 7th was a battlefield check that nothing could reach (the candidates and the comparison both
come from the battlefield), and it was folded away.

## D766 — Phyrexian mana

`parseManaCost` refused `{B/P}` outright (`unsupported`). So **33 legal cards with a Phyrexian
symbol in their mana cost could not be cast at all**: Dismember, Gitaxian Probe, Gut Shot, Mental
Misstep, Birthing Pod, Mutagenic Growth and the rest, several of them Commander staples. 38
activated abilities print one in a cost and were unread. Found by grouping the unread lines that
end "Activate only as a sorcery." (the Phyrexian transform creatures).

**One mana of that colour, or 2 life (CR 107.4f).**
- `parseManaCost` counts each Phyrexian symbol in `colors` and notes it in `ManaCost.phyrexian`.
  Every check that knows nothing of life therefore reads the cost as payable with mana only,
  which is never cheaper than the card; none of the 62 call sites had to change to stay correct.
- `phyrexianWays` lists the ways to pay: each subset of the symbols paid with 2 life apiece,
  fewest life payments first. `phyrexianPayment` picks the first way the pool and the sources
  can cover within a life budget. `canAfford` takes that budget as an optional argument, default
  none.
- `payFrom`, the one payer, pays mana first and 2 life for each symbol the mana cannot cover,
  within `canPayLife`'s line (never the last life point; nothing while life can't change). The
  life is paid as part of the cost.
- `legalActions` passes the same budget (`phyrexianLife`) to the spell, activated-ability and
  tapped-cost affordability checks. The side options (kicker, buyback, entwine) stay mana-only,
  the conservative side: such a play is not offered rather than charged wrongly.
- Not done: choosing to pay life while holding the mana, so a player can keep mana open, which
  needs a choice on the cast; and hybrid Phyrexian `{G/U/P}`, which stays refused.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- `{1}{B/P}{B/P}` parses as two black noted Phyrexian, mana value 3, and the cards read;
- three Swamps: Dismember kills the 3/3 for no life;
- a Swamp and a Mountain: one symbol in mana, the other for 2 life;
- a Mountain alone: offered, and paid with 4 life. At 4 life it is not offered, and sent anyway
  it is refused by the payment itself; at 5 it is offered;
- an ability's `{1}{R/P}` off a Swamp alone: the Swamp and 2 life, and the pump resolves.

Faults injected by script: 7. 6 were caught at once. The miss (the payer allowed the last life
point) was hidden behind the offer's own refusal; the direct cast at 4 life now catches it.

The first gate failed three mana.test.ts rows that pinned `{R/P}` as unsupported. They now assert
the new reading: its colour, noted, payable by life only with a budget. The "refuses rather than
guessing" and "first unsupported symbol" rows use snow, monocoloured hybrid and hybrid Phyrexian,
which are still refused.

Pod sweeps 59901, 60001 and 60101 (300 games on this build, D765 and D766): every game finished,
with no throw and no stall.

    engine tests: 5,525, all passing (with the other session's D1023 and D1024 merged)

Coverage: 13,923 of 31,900 cards (+14), 35,051 of 59,888 lines (+26), against fe4462f. The cards
that become castable are not in the line count: their lines were already read.

## D1026 — a trailing "if"

"At the beginning of your upkeep, draw a card if you control an artifact", "You gain 3 life if you
attacked this turn", "Draw two cards if you control an artifact, then discard a card". The leading
form ("If you control an artifact, draw a card") has been read on spells since D742. The trailing
one was unread everywhere, on spells and triggers alike.

- `readEffect` splits on the last " if " and reads the condition with the leading form's vocabulary
  (`interveningConditionFor`). The clause happens only if the condition holds as it resolves.
- A trailing "if" is never intervening: CR 603.4 is the "if" straight after a trigger condition.
  So on a trigger it is asked once, on resolution, unlike D742's leading form, which triggers read
  as intervening.
- Conditions about the clause's own action ("if able", "if you do", "if they don't") are left to
  their readers. A clause that asks a question is refused, as the leading form refuses it, because
  the question would be asked whatever the condition.
- **`guardedBy`, and a fix to the leading form.** A guarded reading now wraps `immediate` as well as
  `effect`. `immediate` is the form `composeEffects` uses for a clause that something follows. D742
  spread the unguarded `immediate`, so "If you control an artifact, draw two cards, then discard a
  card" would have drawn whatever the condition.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and a clause that would ask its question regardless does not;
- the upkeep draw comes only with an artifact out;
- the spell gains only with one;
- the first clause of "draw two cards if …, then discard a card" draws only when the condition
  holds.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught. The question refusal was missed at first and is now pinned
by the unread row.

Coverage: 13,958 of 31,900 cards (+14), 35,109 of 59,888 lines (+18), measured against the merged
tree with the other session's D766 (13,944 / 35,091).
## D767 — Monocoloured hybrid: {2/W}

The other refused cost symbol worth reading. **21 legal cards print `{2/X}` in their mana cost and
could not be cast**: Spectral Procession, Beseech the Queen, Flame Javelin, Reaper King,
Advice from the Fae and the rest. Found by asking `parseManaCost` of every legal mana cost what it
refuses. The tail of that list is 4 hybrid-Phyrexian planeswalkers (`{G/U/P}`) and 2 snow costs,
which stay refused.

- `parseManaCost` counts a `{2/W}` as one white in `colors`, the cheaper half, and notes it in
  `ManaCost.monoHybrid`. So, as with D766, a check that knows nothing of the field never
  undercharges.
- `costValue` adds one for each, since a `{2/W}` is 2 towards mana value (CR 202.3f).
- `phyrexianWays` also enumerates each monocoloured symbol paid as its colour or as two generic:
  fewest life payments first, then the fewest paid as two. `canAfford` and `payFrom` take the
  first way that can be covered, so the colour is spent where there is one and generic mana
  covers the rest.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests (one is a parse test):
- `{2/W}{2/W}{2/W}` parses as three white, noted, mana value six, and the card reads;
- three Plains pay it as white, tapping three lands;
- six Mountains pay it as generic;
- one Plains and four Mountains: one white and two twos, five lands;
- five Mountains are not enough, and it is not offered.

D766's mana.test.ts row that still held `{2/W}` as refused now asserts that it reads, and the
"first unsupported symbol" row uses snow and hybrid Phyrexian.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught.

    engine tests: 5,534, all passing (merged with the other session's D1025)

Coverage: unchanged at 13,941 of 31,900 cards and 35,085 of 59,888 lines against 6db1f99. These
cards' lines were already read; what changed is that they can be cast.

## D1027 — "if you don't control an Ogre" and "the creature with the greatest power"

"At the beginning of your upkeep, you lose 2 life if you don't control an Ogre" (Scourge of Numai,
and the Oni's "… a Demon"), "draw a card if you control the creature with the greatest power or tied
for the greatest power" (Triumph of Ferocity), "… toughness" (Abzan Beastmaster), and "… a creature
with the greatest power among creatures on the battlefield" (High Score). These are conditions that
D1026's trailing "if" found unread.

- `interveningConditionFor` reads "you don't control a(n) X" as the negation of "you control a(n)
  X". It reads exactly what that form reads, and nothing else.
- A new row, "you control the / a creature with the greatest power | toughness [or tied for the
  greatest … | among creatures on the battlefield]", measures every creature on the battlefield
  live. One of yours at the most is enough, ties included. With no creatures at all it is false.
- **A fix to the exclusion that kept "if you do" out.** D742's leading reader refused any condition
  starting with "you don't", and so did D1026's trailing one. That refused "if you don't control an
  Ogre" along with the bare "if you don't" it was written for. Both now refuse only the whole phrase.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- the Ogre-less upkeep loses 2 and the upkeep with an Ogre loses nothing;
- the leading spell form gains only without an Ogre;
- the greatest-power draw comes on a tie, not when their 6/6 is bigger, and not with no creatures.

Faults injected by script: 6. 5 are caught; the 6th was an empty-board check that `some` already
answers, and it was folded away.

## D1028 — half a life total, "that much life", and an aimed edict with a count

"Whenever equipped creature deals combat damage to a player, that player loses half their life,
rounded up" (Quietus Spike, Scytheclaw, Radioactive Man), "you lose half your life, rounded up",
"each opponent loses half their life, rounded down", "that player loses that much life" on a damage
trigger, and "that player sacrifices two permanents" (Greater Harvester).

- `readEffect` reads "(target player | target opponent | each opponent | each player | you) lose(s)
  half (their | your) life, rounded (up | down)". The half is taken from the life total as the
  clause resolves; at 0 or less there is nothing positive to lose. "That player" on a combat hit
  reaches this as "target player" through the referent swap (D530).
- D1007's damage-amount readers gain "that player loses that much life": the hit player loses the
  damage dealt.
- The aimed edict gains a count: "target player / target opponent sacrifices two | three … <noun>s".
  The player chooses that many of their own; it is a real sacrifice.
- Not read: "that player discards that many cards" (Dreamstealer, Needle Specter). Its question
  would need a size that is the event's amount, which a decision does not yet carry.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- a 3-power hit leaves 20 - 3 = 17, then half rounded up, 9, leaves 8;
- "that much life" doubles a 2-power hit;
- at 15, half rounded up takes 8 and half rounded down takes 7;
- "each player" halves both;
- the hit player is asked to choose two of their three permanents;
- the target sacrifices both creatures.

Faults injected by script: 7 of 7 caught, one of them after the "each player" row was added. One
more guard (life 0 or less) duplicated `loseLife`'s own refusal and was folded away.

## D768 — The bot stops buying regeneration shields it has no use for

Found while re-measuring the beta number. One pod (seed 60212) ran more than 25 minutes: two
seats at 34 and 47 life, turn 104 and still going, and one creature activated 85 times. Jace's
Mindseeker had no ability of its own; Molting Snakeskin gave it "{2}{B}: Regenerate this creature",
and the bot bought a shield in every upkeep, its own and the opponent's. A shield lasts the turn,
so each one was three mana spent on nothing, and in its own upkeep the bot tapped out of its main
phase. Two bots doing that cannot finish a game, and a tester playing beside one would see a
seat that never casts anything.

D639's `buysNothingIf` hint stopped a **second** shield. It now also stops the first one when
nothing could destroy the creature before the shield wears off: an empty stack and the creature
in no fight. `shieldBuysNothing` answers both, for the creature's own regenerate (hand-written
and compiled) and for an Aura's "Regenerate enchanted creature". A player may still press it any
time; the hint only steers the bot. Regenerating in answer to a removal spell on the stack, or
with the creature attacking or blocking, is still worth it to the bot.

**Tests.** D639's two tests now give the board a spell on the stack, so an unshielded creature
still has a reason to regenerate. A new one: with nothing threatening, neither the creature's
own regenerate nor an Aura's is worth a shield, and in a fight it is again.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught.

Game 60212 replayed on this build: finished at turn 88 in 1,175 moves, against the 20,000-move cap
it was heading for.

    engine tests: 5,541, all passing (merged with the other session's D1027)

## D1029 — phase triggers

"Whenever Teferi's Imp phases out, discard a card. Whenever Teferi's Imp phases in, draw a card",
"Whenever Shimmering Efreet phases in, target creature phases out", "When Ertai's Familiar phases
out or leaves the battlefield, mill three cards", "Whenever Warping Wurm phases in, put a +1/+1
counter on it". These complete D1023's phasing.

- `phaseOut` and `phaseIn` record what phased in `GameState.phased` (id and direction), indirect
  phasing included (CR 702.26g). `settle` drains it and raises `phases-in` / `phases-out` to the
  permanent itself, in the order it happened. They live below the module that can `raise`, as
  `transformed` does.
- A "phases out" trigger looks back in time (CR 603.10a), so the permanent hears it from the
  phased-out zone, as a creature hears its own death from a graveyard.
- Prologue rows read "Whenever ~ phases in", "Whenever ~ phases out" and "When ~ phases out or
  leaves the battlefield".
- Still unread on these cards: Warping Wurm's "phases out unless you pay {2}{G}{U}", Ertai's
  Familiar's "can't phase out", and King of the Oathbreakers' "or another Spirit … phases in".

**Tests.** 3 engine tests, plus the two kinds added to the deck-coverage test's compiler-only list:
- the rows read whole;
- the Imp phasing out at its untap step loses 1 from the phased-out zone, and a Familiar beside it
  does not hear it;
- phasing back in, the gain is on the stack in the upkeep, before any draw, then 3 is gained;
- out again loses 1;
- "phases out or leaves the battlefield" fires for a phasing spell.

Faults injected by script: 9 of 9 caught. Two were caught only after the test above was extended: the
settle loop's condition (a phase event would otherwise wait for an unrelated event to be announced)
and the self-only watcher list (the matcher trusts it for these kinds).

Coverage: 13,978 of 31,900 cards (+2), 35,138 of 59,888 lines (+5).

## D1030 — a keyword granted to any one target creature

"Whenever ~ attacks, another target attacking creature gains flying until end of turn", "another
target creature you control gains deathtouch until end of turn", "target attacking creature gains
first strike", "target creature with a +1/+1 counter on it gains …", "target legendary creature
gains …", "up to one target creature gains haste". Until now the single-target keyword grant read
only "target creature [you control]". The size pump with the same target phrases already read.

- The grant's target is any single target phrase `targetSpecFrom` reads ("another", "up to one",
  attacking, blocking, with counters, with a power, a tribe), as long as it is a creature: "target
  land gains shroud" stays unread.
- The bot hints are the reader's own: hexproof or shroud protects, haste or infect helps the
  attack, and the rest waits for blockers.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and the land grant does not;
- the attack trigger gives the other attacker flying, not itself, and when it attacks alone it has
  nothing to aim at and is not put on the stack;
- "target attacking creature" accepts the attacker and refuses the creature at home.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught. A count check was folded away: a plural target prints
"gain", not "gains", and never reaches this reader.

## D1032 — keyword counters

"Put a flying counter on target creature", "put a deathtouch counter on target creature you
control", "When ~ enters, put a lifelink counter on it", "~ enters with a first strike counter on
it". A permanent with a keyword counter has that keyword (CR 122.1b). Until now these lines were
refused on purpose, because nothing applied the keyword.

- `characteristicsOf` seeds the keywords of any counters with a positive count beside the printed
  keywords. The counters are flying, first strike, double strike, deathtouch, hexproof,
  indestructible, lifelink, menace, reach, trample, vigilance and haste. A count below one (a
  hand-adjusted counter) gives nothing.
- **An approximation, recorded:** seeded with the printed keywords, a counter's keyword is cleared
  by any "loses all abilities" effect. By the rules a counter put on after such an effect keeps its
  keyword (its timestamp is the placement). Nothing in the pool tests the difference, and the
  "loses all abilities" spell form is not read yet.
- The readers:
  - the counters-on-a-target reader takes the keyword kinds, aimed as a gift as a +1/+1 counter is;
  - the self-counter reader stops refusing them, and takes "first strike" / "double strike";
  - the enters-with reader takes a keyword kind.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and the flying counter's target is marked friendly; D603's refusal row for a flying counter is now a reads assertion;
- a flying counter gives flying and a first strike counter gives first strike;
- both last past end of turn, and a −1 count gives nothing;
- a creature that enters with a lifelink counter has lifelink.

Faults injected by script: 6. 5 are caught, two of them after the tests were extended (the friendly
hint, and the positive-count check). The 6th was a two-word guard that the regex already enforces,
and it was folded away.

Coverage: 14,056 of 31,900 cards (+12), 35,255 of 59,888 lines (+25).

## D1033 — shield counters

"Put a shield counter on target creature" (Boon of Safety), "~ enters with a shield counter on it"
(Dapper Shieldmate, Disciplined Duelist), "When ~ dies, put a shield counter on target creature you
control" (Brokers Veteran). The rule (CR 122.1c): "If a permanent with a shield counter on it would
be dealt damage or destroyed, instead remove a shield counter from it." 28 legal cards print one.
Until now the counter was refused, as a kind with a meaning of its own.

- `spendShieldCounter` in effects.ts is the replacement.
  - `dealDamage` asks it after the "prevent all" checks: damage that was prevented never touches the
    counter. The damage is then never dealt: nothing is marked and no deathtouch applies.
  - `destroy` asks it after indestructible and before regeneration and umbra armor. The order of
    replacements is the controller's choice; this one keeps a regeneration shield for later.
- The lethal-damage check does not ask it. Spending a counter there would leave the damage marked,
  and the next pass of the same check destroys the creature anyway (CR 704.3), so the counter would
  only be lost.
- **Compiler.**
  - Shield leaves `RULES_COUNTERS`.
  - It joins the target-counter reader's kinds (aimed as a gift) and the enters-with reader's.
  - The self-counter reader takes it now that it is no longer refused.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and the target is marked friendly;
- the Shieldmate enters with one: the first burn removes the counter and marks no damage, and the
  second kills it;
- a destroy spell is replaced once per counter.

Faults injected by script: 8 of 8 caught, the friendly hint after the read test asserted it. Two
checks were folded away: the battlefield check inside `spendShieldCounter` (both callers already ask
it), and the lethal-damage hook described above.

Coverage: 14,065 of 31,900 cards (+9), 35,278 of 59,888 lines (+23).

## D1034 — mana kept until end of turn

"Whenever Savage Ventmaw attacks, add {R}{R}{R}{G}{G}{G}. Until end of turn, you don't lose this mana
as steps and phases end." (Savage Ventmaw, Grand Warlord Radha, Klauth and the rest). The 16 legal
lines whose "Until end of turn, …" sentence was unread are the biggest single group of that kind.

- **Engine.** `GameState.keptMana` is how much of each type a seat keeps this turn.
  - `emptyPools` leaves the smaller of that and what is in the pool, and shrinks the record to
    what stayed: what was spent is gone, and mana added since is not kept.
  - The cleanup step clears the record with the other until-end-of-turn facts.
  - Spending takes the ordinary mana first, which is the player's best order.
- **A fix found here.** `advanceStep` can walk from the end step into the next turn's upkeep in one
  call, and it emptied the pools only once, at its start. With mana kept, that left a seat's kept
  mana in its opponent's upkeep. The pools are now emptied again as the turn ends inside that loop.
- **Compiler.**
  - `clausesOf` joins "Add …. Until end of turn, you don't lose this mana …" into one clause.
  - `readEffect` reads it: the add as it is, and whatever it added (the pool's difference)
    recorded as kept on top of anything already kept. Mana already in the pool is not the
    trigger's to keep.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the row reads whole;
- the three red survive into the second main phase;
- with two spent, one survives;
- two more added later are not kept;
- the turn ends them, and nothing is left by the next upkeep;
- two triggers keep six, and a red already in the pool empties.

Faults injected by script: 9. 7 are caught, three of them after the tests were extended (the record
shrinking, the sum of two triggers, the difference against the pool). The other 2 were empty-case
shortcuts, folded away.

Coverage: 14,070 of 31,900 cards (+5), 35,285 of 59,888 lines (+7).

## D769 — Snow mana: {S}

The last cost symbol in a printed mana cost or ability cost that the engine refused, apart from
hybrid Phyrexian. **46 legal cards print `{S}`**: Arcum's Astrolabe, Faceless Haven, Icehide
Golem, Boreal Griffin, Frost Raptor and the rest. A `{S}` is one mana that must come from a
**snow** source (CR 107.4h).

- `parseManaCost` counts the symbols in `ManaCost.snow`, and `costValue` adds one for each.
- A pool cannot tell snow mana from other mana, so `payCost` refuses a cost that still has `{S}`
  in it, and **floating mana never pays `{S}`**. The offer can be smaller than the rules allow,
  never larger.
- `manaSources` marks a permanent whose live type line says snow (`ManaSource.snow`).
- `solveTap` sets aside snow sources for the `{S}` symbols, then solves the rest of the cost as
  before with the other sources. It prefers snow sources whose colours the rest of the cost does
  not ask for, least flexible first, so a snow Mountain pays the `{S}` of a `{G}{S}` spell and the
  only green land is left for the `{G}`. If the rest cannot be paid, it tries other sets of snow
  sources, up to 200 tries. The picks record which mana went to `{S}` (`ManaPick.snowPaid`).
- `payFrom` turns the `{S}` symbols into exactly that mana (`snowAsColours`) before paying, so the
  payment is the one the plan made.
- Two readers that came with the cards. `targetSpecFrom` peels "snow" and "nonsnow" ("target snow
  creature", Ohran Yeti) the way D754 peels a creature type. The mass pump reads a kind word in place
  of a creature type: snow, artifact, legendary or a colour ("Snow creatures you control get +1/+1
  until end of turn", Diamond Faerie).

Still unread: "the amount of {S} spent to cast this spell" (Graven Lore, Rime Transfusion's
family) and "if {S} of any of that spell's colors was spent" (Boreal Outrider). Both need the
snow mana spent to be recorded, and nothing records it yet.

**Tests.** 2 mana.test.ts rows:
- `{1}{S}` is paid only by a snow source, and `snowAsColours` names the mana;
- `{G}{S}` with a snow Forest and a snow Mountain sets the Mountain aside; with the snow Forest the
  only snow source and the only green, it cannot be paid.

6 engine tests:
- the cost parses as one snow, mana value two, and both test cards read;
- a Forest and a snow Mountain cast it;
- three plain lands do not, and it is not offered;
- the only green is kept for `{G}`;
- a snow Forest alone cannot be both the green and the snow;
- an activated `{1}{S}` is paid and pumps only the snow creatures.

The D766/D767 mana.test.ts rows that held `{S}` as refused now assert that it reads, and the
"refuses rather than guessing" rows use hybrid Phyrexian.

Faults injected by script: 7 of 8 caught. The fault no test catches removes the retry over other
sets of snow sources. The preference order gets every case tried right, so the retry is a safety
net that no test reaches.

    engine tests: 5,572, all passing (merged with the other session's D1034)

Coverage: 14,066 to 14,096 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 35,280 to 35,316 of 59,888
lines, against 8852c43.

## D1036 — the top card, if it is of a kind

"Look at the top card of your library. If it's a land card, you may put it onto the battlefield
tapped" (Explorer's Scope), "… If it's a creature card, you may reveal it and put it into your hand"
(Archghoul of Thraben), "Reveal the top card of your library. If it's a creature card, put it onto
the battlefield" (Call of the Wild), "… If it's a land card, put it into your hand". 57 legal
sightings of the opening; the forms read here are the 36 that end at the move.

- `clausesOf` joins the two sentences: the second is about the card the first looked at.
- `readEffect` reads the kind with the search vocabulary (`cardFilterBody`).
- With "you may" it is a question over the top card (`library-top`, `look: 1`): only a card of
  that kind can be chosen, and the engine moves a chosen card where `chosenGoTo` says (the hand, the
  battlefield, the battlefield tapped). When the top card is of another kind the question has no
  candidates and answers itself, and nothing moves.
- Without "may" the effect moves it when it qualifies, and leaves it on top otherwise.
- Not read: the follow-ups some cards add ("If you don't put the card into your hand, you may put it
  into your graveyard", "… repeat this process", the Deceivers' riders).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- a land on top is offered, and enters tapped on a yes and stays on top on a no;
- a creature on top asks nothing and stays;
- without "may", a creature goes onto the battlefield, a land stays, and a land goes to hand for
  the "into your hand" row.

Faults injected by script: 6. 5 are caught, the hand destination after its row was added. The 6th
was an `askOnlyIf` that the empty candidate list already provides, and it was folded away.

Coverage: 14,110 of 31,900 cards (+8), 35,332 of 59,888 lines (+9), measured against the merged tree
with the other session's D769 (14,102 / 35,323).
## D770 — Combat damage assigned as though it weren't blocked

"You may have ~ assign its combat damage as though it weren't blocked": Thorn Elemental, Lone Wolf,
Rhox, Pride of Lions, Deathcoil Wurm, Tornado Elemental, Wolf Pack, Spinebiter and Imaryll, nine
legal cards that print it of themselves. It was unread, so these creatures played as vanilla bodies.

- The line is a printed combat static (`assignsAsUnblocked`), read by `printedCombatLine` the way
  "can't be blocked" is, and cleared by "loses all abilities" like the others.
- The choice is made by the attacking player when combat damage is assigned (CR 510.1c), which is
  the moment the damage order is asked (CR 509.2). So it is asked with the order:
  `damageOrdersOwed` also lists every blocked attacker with the ability, marked `mayGoUnblocked`,
  even behind a single blocker.
- `auto:order` entries take `unblocked: true`, refused where it was not offered. The attack is
  marked `asUnblocked`, and `dealCombatDamage` sends all of its damage to the player or
  planeswalker it attacked. It is still blocked: the blockers deal their damage to it, and nothing
  that cares about being unblocked fires.
- The bot adds one more plan to its order search, with every such attacker going as though
  unblocked, and the playout chooses.
- The table: the order prompt shows an "As though unblocked" toggle beside each attacker the engine
  offered it for. A toggled attacker needs no order, and the button sends the blockers as listed.

Not yet: the same choice granted by other cards (Garruk, Savage Herald; Predatory Focus; Indomitable
Might; Proud Wildbonder; Siege Behemoth; Ruxa) and Gurzigost's activated version. Each needs a grant
of the flag, which `ContinuousEffect` does not carry yet.

**Tests.** 7 engine tests:
- the line reads, and a blocked one is asked even behind a single blocker;
- as though unblocked: all five damage to the player, none to the wall, and the wall still deals
  its damage;
- declined: the wall dies and the player takes nothing;
- a creature without the ability is not asked;
- two blockers: the order is still asked, with the choice beside it;
- the bot sends it through when that is lethal;
- "unblocked" is refused for an attacker that was not offered it.

2 web tests: the toggle sends `unblocked: true` with no order needed and the other attacker still
owes its order; the toggle does nothing for an attacker the engine did not offer it for.

Faults injected by script: 7 of 7 caught.

    engine tests: 5,583, all passing (merged with the other session's D1035)

Coverage: 14,101 to 14,110 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 35,323 to 35,332 of 59,888
lines, against 5d43a1a.

## D1037 — counters on each of a set, and on the host

New shapes read:
- "Put a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control with a +1/+1 counter on it";
- "… on each creature target player controls";
- "Put two +1/+1 counters on each other creature you control";
- "Put a -1/-1 counter on each creature";
- "When ~ enters, put two +1/+1 counters on each other Elf you control";
- "At the beginning of your upkeep, put a +1/+1 counter on enchanted creature" and the same on
  equipped creature.

- **Counters on each.** "each <creature or Tribe> [you control | target player controls | your
  opponents control]" is the plural set the team pump already reads (`massPumpSubject`, D769's
  kinds included), so the sets are the same ones, taken as the clause resolves. "with a <kind>
  counter on it" narrows them. Any count, and the kinds the target reader knows: +1/+1, -1/-1, stun,
  shield and the keyword counters. The single +1/+1 or -1/-1 counter over a board scope is read
  earlier, by the older `eachCounter` reader; this one adds counts above one, the other kinds, the
  counter filter and "target player controls".
- **On the host.** "Put <count> <kind> counter(s) on enchanted / equipped creature": the permanent
  the source is attached to, or nothing if it is attached to nothing.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- "with a +1/+1 counter on it" reaches only your creatures that have one;
- two counters on each other creature of yours and none of theirs;
- a -1/-1 counter on each of the target player's creatures;
- "each other Elf" leaves out the creature itself and the non-Elf;
- the Aura's upkeep trigger puts the counter on the enchanted creature.

Three refusal rows in compile.test.ts (D453's "a condition on the permanents" and "a controller said as a target", and the Aura-host row) are now notes pointing at these tests.

Faults injected by script: 6 of 6 caught. The "other" fault was caught only after the creature row
was moved to the plural count, because the single-counter form is the older reader's.

Coverage: 14,142 of 31,900 cards (+23), 35,376 of 59,888 lines (+35), measured against the merged

## D1038 — a pick from what was just milled

"Mill three cards. You may put a land card from among them into your hand" (Ainok Wayfarer), "… a
permanent card from among the cards milled this way" (Cache Grab), "… an artifact, creature, or land
card from among the milled cards" (Dredger's Insight). 37 legal cards print the shape.

- `clausesOf` joins the two sentences.
- The cards really are milled first, so everything watching a graveyard sees all of them and the
  pick comes back from there. A look-at-the-top with the rest going to the graveyard would have been
  a different card.
  - The mill runs before the question (`beforeDecisions`) and records what it milled in a new
    `GameState.milledThisWay`, keyed by source.
  - The question, built from its source (the thunk form of a decision), offers only those cards
    in the graveyard, of the kind the search vocabulary reads (`libraryFilter`). Without "may" it
    asks for exactly one.
  - The effect moves the pick to hand and clears the record.
- Gain is small (+2 cards): most of the 37 have another unread line.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- all three are milled, and only the milled land is offered, not the Forest already there;
- on a yes it goes to hand and the record is cleared, and on a no it stays;
- without "may" the question asks for exactly one, and a Bear is taken.

Faults injected by script: 6. 5 are caught, the minimum after the test asserted it. The 6th was a
graveyard check on the milled cards that the question's own zone already makes, and it was folded
away.

Coverage: 14,144 of 31,900 cards (+2), 35,382 of 59,888 lines (+6).
## D771 — Sweeps end a runaway board instead of hanging

Sweep 60301 (100 pods) never finished. Seed 60315 was the game: one player cast Troubling Tribbles
("At the beginning of your upkeep, create a token that's a copy of this creature"), and each copy
copies itself too. That player had 128 at turn 45, 512 at turn 53, 2,048 at turn 58 and 2,900 at
turn 60. The engine played the card correctly and kept pace, about 50 moves a minute at 1,000
permanents. But nothing threatened a 0/1 that cannot block or deal damage. Nobody attacked that
player (still at 37 life), and the board doubles for as long as the game lasts.

Two things were tried and one was kept:

- **Not kept: attack plans aimed at every opponent.** The bot's search gets one plan aimed at the
  lowest life total. Adding a plan for each other opponent did not change the replay: the bots
  still went for the low-life player, which is defensible, since 0/1s that cannot block are no
  danger to anyone. Each extra plan is a playout on every attack in a pod, so the change cost
  speed and bought nothing. Reverted.
- **Kept: a board cap in `corpus-decks.mjs`.** `BOARD=<n>` (default 1,000) ends a game as
  `runaway-board` once any battlefield holds more than n permanents. The report names the
  commonest card on that board: "seat 2 has more than 1000 permanents, 1010 of them Troubling
  Tribbles". The move cap could not catch this, because the doubling happens in a handful of moves.
  TRACE lines now also show the biggest board's commonest names, which is how this was found.

For the beta: a human table meets the same board and decides for itself. The engine handled several
thousand permanents at a usable speed, but a game that keeps doubling will eventually be too slow to
play. Players with a Tribbles deck will need to finish the game or concede, as they would at a real
table.

Sweep 60301 rerun with the cap: 99 of 100 games finished, and seed 60315 is reported as
`runaway-board` (1,010 Troubling Tribbles). 60.3 turns and 344 moves on average.

    engine tests: 5,589, all passing (merged with the other session's D1037; the engine is unchanged here)

## D1039 — a spell's own trigger from the graveyard

"Whenever a Dragon you control enters, you may pay {R}. If you do, return Spit Flame from your
graveyard to your hand." An instant or sorcery whose second line is a triggered ability that works
from the graveyard (Spit Flame, Unconventional Tactics, Killian's Confidence, Punishing Fire).

- `spellScriptFor` hands a line that opens "When/Whenever/At" and returns or puts the card itself
  "from your graveyard" to the trigger reader. The line is kept only when every trigger it reads
  works from the graveyard (`inGraveyard`) and nothing else came with it; otherwise it stays
  unread as before. The card's resolution is read from its other lines as it always was.
- "Whenever an opponent gains life" and "Whenever a player gains life" are new `life-gained`
  prologue rows. `life-gained` gains `by: 'opponent'`, and its matcher answers it the way
  `life-lost` does (D999). This is what Punishing Fire needed.
- The D487 test that pinned Punishing Fire's recursion as unread now pins it as read: both lines
  compiled, the trigger a graveyard `life-gained` watcher for an opponent.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests, plus the D487 engine test converted and its compile row swapped to a trigger that still does not read ("Whenever a Vehicle you control attacks"):
- the rows read whole, and the opponent and any-player rows read to the right `by`;
- a Dragon entering asks; paying {R} brings the instant back to hand, declining leaves it;
- an opponent's life gain asks and returns it; your own life gain does not ask.

Faults injected by script: 5, all caught (the dropped bookkeeping of the read line by the
converted D487 test).

Coverage: 14,150 of 31,900 cards (+6), 35,388 of 59,888 lines (+6).

## D1040 — control for as long as the terms hold

"Gain control of target creature for as long as Sower of Temptation remains on the battlefield",
"… for as long as you control Dragonlord Silumgar", "… for as long as ~ remains tapped", "… for as
long as you control ~ and ~ remains tapped". 42 legal lines print a "for as long as" control
change; this reads the four sets of terms that are about the source itself.

- `ContinuousEffect.controlWhile` holds the terms: the source on the battlefield, and as printed
  still controlled by the effect's controller (`controlled`) and still tapped (`tapped`).
- `stealWhile` (effects.ts) moves the permanent and leaves a `permanent` effect with
  `controlRevertTo` and the terms. If the terms are already false as it resolves (the Sower
  bounced in response) nothing changes hands (CR 611.2b). A take-and-give-back would also have
  marked the permanent for echo.
- `auraControl` already keeps control Auras true of the board as a timestamp chain (D938). Its
  `holds` now answers a `controlWhile` effect by its terms (`controlTermsHold`), so the newest
  change on a permanent holds it, and the permanent goes back when the terms fail. A phased-out
  source is not on the battlefield, so its steal ends too.
- Other terms ("as long as that creature is enchanted", "as long as they're the monarch", a power
  that "remains" less) stay unread.
- Sower of Temptation, Dragonlord Silumgar, Master Thief, Roil Elemental and Mind Flayer read whole.
  Helm of Possession, Willow Satyr and their kin still need "You may choose not to untap ~", which
  is next.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- the Sower holds the Bear while it stays and gives it back when it dies;
- the Lord killed with its trigger on the stack takes nothing, and does not hand it back either
  (no echo mark);
- the Lord taken by the opponent's Sower gives the Bear back, and the Sower's own steal stays;
- a stolen Bear that dies takes the effect with it;
- "remains tapped", alone and with "you control", holds through the turn and ends at its
  controller's next untap step.

Faults injected by script: 8. 7 are caught, the 611.2b check after the echo assertion pinned it. The
8th was a host-on-the-battlefield check that the leave-the-battlefield cleanup already makes, and it
was folded away.

Coverage: 14,159 of 31,900 cards (+7), 35,405 of 59,888 lines (+14).

## D1041 — "You may choose not to untap ~"

"You may choose not to untap Helm of Possession during your untap step." 46 legal lines print it,
mostly on cards whose other line lasts "for as long as ~ remains tapped".

- `CardScript.mayStayTapped`, read by `keywordScriptFor`.
- In its controller's own untap step (CR 502.3), the table keeps the permanent tapped while it holds
  a control change that lasts "as long as ~ remains tapped" (D1040), and untaps it otherwise.
  `untapAll` takes the set to `keep`. That is the one reason to keep such a permanent down that the
  engine models, so the table answers the choice the way its controller wants it answered. Seedborn
  Muse's untap in another player's step offers no choice and untaps it.
- What this does not do: ask. A player who wants to end a Helm's steal early cannot. Storage lands
  (Bottomless Vault and the rest) keep themselves tapped for counters, a choice the table cannot
  make. A tripwire test pins Bottomless Vault as not fully read, so whoever reads its storage mana
  ability has to turn this into a real question first.
- Helm of Possession and Willow Satyr read whole. Rubinia Soulsinger and Hivis of the Scale print a
  short name the compiler cannot derive, Seasinger and Vedalken Shackles a target condition.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests (and `script mayStayTapped` added to the deck-coverage `compilerOnly` list):
- the row reads whole, with the flag;
- the Satyr holding the Bear stays tapped through its own untap step, and keeps the Bear;
- with the Bear dead it untaps as usual;
- Bottomless Vault is not claimed.

Faults injected by script: 5, all caught (the script-flag check by D1040's Shackles test, which has
no such line and so untaps).

Coverage: 14,161 of 31,900 cards (+2), 35,451 of 59,888 lines (+46).

## D1042 — a token's quoted ability of two sentences

"Create a 1/1 red Mercenary creature token with "{T}: Target creature you control gets +1/+0 until
end of turn. Activate only as a sorcery."" is the Mercenary token Outlaws of Thunder Junction prints
on a dozen cards. The quote holds two sentences, and `clausesOf` split the line at the first
period inside it, so neither half was a token.

- The quoted ability after "token(s) with" has its punctuation hidden from the splitter, as an
  emblem's already was (D734, `hideEmblemText`). The inline reader in `tokenEffect` puts it back
  before the token's own text is read and checked (`showEmblemText`).
- Prickly Pair, Wanted Griffin, Nezumi Linkbreaker, Lassoed by the Law and Brimstone Roundup read
  whole. Form a Posse ("Create X …") does not, because the count is X.

**Tests.** 1 engine test: the row reads whole, and the token's text is both sentences restored. A
turn later the Mercenary is refused once combat has begun and pumps the Bear in a main phase.

Faults injected by script: 2, both caught.

Coverage: 14,167 of 31,900 cards (+6), 35,464 of 59,888 lines (+13).

## D1043 — discover

"Discover N" (CR 701.57a): exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card
with mana value N or less, then cast it without paying its mana cost or put it into your hand; the
rest go to the bottom in a random order. 31 legal cards print it, most as the last clause of a
trigger or an activated ability (Trumpeting Carnosaur, the Hidden lands, Chimil, Etali's Favor).

- `cascadeFrom` takes the number. Cascade's walk with two differences: a card of exactly N is a
  hit, so the limit is N + 1 with cascade's "less than" comparison; and the offer carries a new
  disposition.
- `pendingOfferedCast.toHand`: the decline path (`auto:pass` on the offer) moves the hit to its
  owner's hand and bottoms the pile. Cascade sends it to the bottom, madness to the graveyard, and
  miracle leaves it where it is.
- Read for a number only. "Discover X, where X is …" (Monstrous Vortex, Hurl into History, Dinosaur
  Egg) and Hit the Mother Lode's follow-up about "the discovered card" stay unread.
- Like cascade, the cast is offered when the effect finishes. Every discover in the pool ends its
  ability except Hit the Mother Lode's, which is unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the row reads whole;
- the walk passes a Mountain and a three-drop to a two-drop for "discover 2", which casts for
  nothing and deals its damage, with the other two at the bottom;
- declined, the hit goes to hand and the other two to the bottom.

Faults injected by script: 4, all caught.

Coverage: 14,183 of 31,900 cards (+16), 35,485 of 59,888 lines (+21).

## D1044 — a card filter by power or toughness

"Search your library for a creature card with power 2 or less" and "You may reveal a creature card
with power 2 or less from among them" (Kinship digs, Recruiter-style searches). 12 legal cards print
a power or toughness bound in a card filter.

- `cardMeasureTest`: "with mana value / power / toughness N or less|greater" of a card outside the
  battlefield. Mana value is the printed `cmc`, as before. Power and toughness go through
  `characteristicsOf`, so a star answers with its characteristic-defining value (CR 208.2a).
- `libraryFilter`'s mana-value clause becomes this one clause with three measures.
- The dig reveal ("you may reveal a(n) … card from among them and put it into your hand") takes the
  same measure after "card", and its prompt says it.
- Not read: "a noncreature, nonland card" (a list of negations), and the measure on the
  several-card and onto-the-battlefield digs.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests, and the D584 compile row "a filter with a number in it" moved from unread to read:
- the rows read whole;
- a search for power 2 or less offers the Bear and a 0/4 Wall, and one for toughness 3 or greater
  offers the Giant and the Wall;
- a dig offers the Bear and not the Giant beside it, and the prompt says the bound.

Faults injected by script: 5. All are caught, the power-for-toughness swap after a 0/4 Wall
joined the deck.

Coverage: 14,191 of 31,900 cards (+8), 35,493 of 59,888 lines (+8).

## D1045 — negations in a series

"Destroy target nonartifact, nonblack creature" (Terror), "target noncreature, nonland permanent"
(Vindicate's cousins), "target nonland, nontoken permanent". The comma in a series of negated
qualifiers means "and", and the same words without the comma already read. 33 such target phrases
are printed on legal cards.

- `targetSpecFrom` reads a phrase with "nonX, nonY" again as "nonX nonY". Card filters already took
  the comma form (searches, graveyard returns, hand picks).
- Terror, Vindicate, Dismember and Ravenous Chupacabra read whole.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- Terror is refused at a black creature and an artifact creature, and destroys a green one;
- "noncreature, nonland permanent" is refused at a land and a creature, and exiles an artifact.

Faults injected by script: 2, both caught (refusing the phrase, and dropping the second negation).

Coverage: 14,199 of 31,900 cards (+8), 35,508 of 59,888 lines (+15).

## D1046 — enters with counters if something happened this turn

"Raid — ~ enters with two +1/+1 counters on it if you attacked this turn", "… if a creature died
this turn" (morbid), "… if an opponent lost life this turn", "… if a permanent you controlled left
the battlefield this turn" (revolt). About 30 legal lines.

- `CardScript.entersWith.if`: a condition asked as the permanent arrives, by the arrival pass, of
  the table and under its new controller. The context it gets has no event, no targets and no X.
- `entersWithFromLine` reads "<enters with …> if <condition>" with the enters trigger's own
  condition reader (`interveningConditionFor`). Only conditions that end "this turn" are taken:
  they are facts of the table, where a condition about "it" would ask about an event a replacement
  does not have.
- A printed number only. X is applied where the cast is known, and no condition rides on it, so an
  X with a condition stays unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and an X with a condition does not;
- raid: no counters when cast before combat, two when cast after an attack;
- morbid: none on a quiet turn, one after a creature died.

Faults injected by script: 4. All are caught, the X refusal after the test asserted it.

Coverage: 14,217 of 31,900 cards (+18), 35,527 of 59,888 lines (+19).

## D1047 — enters with a counter for each

"~ enters with a +1/+1 counter on it for each other creature you control", "… for each creature card
in your graveyard", "… for each creature that died this turn", "… for each other Human you
control". 41 legal lines print a per-thing count on an "enters with".

- `CardScript.entersWith.per`: the count, from `forEachCount`, asked by the arrival pass in the
  same context as D1046's condition and multiplied by the printed amount.
- Only a count the permanent itself cannot be in: "other", a graveyard, a death this turn, an
  opponent's permanents. The rule counts before the permanent arrives (CR 614.1c), and the arrival
  pass runs with it already there, so "for each creature you control" would count one too many.
  It stays unread.
- Not read: multikicker ("for each time it was kicked", 8 lines), convoke and spent-mana counts,
  and "exiled this way".

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and the self-including count does not;
- the Captain counts the two other creatures, not itself and not the opponent's;
- the Scavenger counts the two creature cards in the graveyard, not the land.

Faults injected by script: 4, all caught.

Coverage: 14,223 of 31,900 cards (+6), 35,538 of 59,888 lines (+11).

## D1048 — a land turned into a creature by a target

"Target land you control becomes a 4/4 Elemental creature with haste until end of turn. It's still a
land." (Clan Guildmage, Elemental Uprising, Skarrg Guildmage, Llanowar Loamspeaker) and "Until end
of turn, target land becomes a 3/3 creature that's still a land" (Animate Land, Lifespark
Spellbomb). About 25 legal lines.

- `animateSelf` takes a land target as its subject as well as the card itself: a "target … land"
  phrase read by `targetSpecFrom`, with the same layers on the land chosen (addTypes, base size,
  colours, subtypes, keywords). The bot's `animates` hint stays on self-animation only; a land it
  points at is chosen as any target is.
- The one-sentence ending "creature that's still a land" reads as the two-sentence one.
- Spells and triggers: `clausesOf` holds "… becomes … creature …. It's still a land" together as one
  clause, and `readEffect` hands that clause, or a "creature that's still a land" clause, to
  `animateSelf`. Activated abilities already went there.
- Until end of turn only, as before. Mishra's Groundbreaker's permanent animation stays unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole; an unreadable land phrase and a creature target both stay unread, and
  neither animates the card itself;
- refused at a creature; on a Forest, a 4/4 Elemental with haste that is still a land, and not a
  creature on the next turn;
- "a 3/3 creature that's still a land" on the opponent's land.

Faults injected by script: 5. All are caught, two after the unread-phrase assertions.

Coverage: 14,237 of 31,900 cards (+14), 35,555 of 59,888 lines (+17).

## D1049 — a creature land with a quoted ability

Raging Ravine: "Until end of turn, this land becomes a 3/3 red and green Elemental creature with
"Whenever this creature attacks, put a +1/+1 counter on it." It's still a land." The creature lands
that grant an ability while animated (Raging Ravine, Lavaclaw Reaches, Restless Spire, Wandering
Fumarole, Den of the Bugbear, Hall of Storm Giants, and more) were all unread on the quote.

- `animateSelf` reads the quoted text as the card's own line would be read (`lineScriptFor`), and
  takes exactly one trigger or one activated ability. The grant is held on the card
  (`grantedTriggers` / `grantedAbilities`) and handed over by index (`grants: [0]`) on the
  animation's own continuous effect. It lasts as long as the animation and is erased with it, the
  way an Aura's grant is (`grantedTriggersOn`).
- `ReadEffect.cardFields`: card fields an activated ability brings with it, merged by the ability
  path only. `merge` in compile.ts refuses a second line that sets the same field, so a card with
  two such lines leaves the second unread and an index cannot point at the wrong grant.
- A grant on a land the card points at (D1048's target form) is refused, because spells and
  triggers do not carry `cardFields`.
- Raging Ravine reads whole. The other cards' quoted abilities do not read yet: an X pump on "this
  creature", a tapped-and-attacking token, and switching power and toughness. Den of the Bugbear and
  Hall of Storm Giants also need "If you control two or more other lands, ~ enters tapped".

**Tests.** 2 engine tests, and the D754 refusal row of a quoted "{T}: Draw a card." swapped for one that does not read:
- the row reads whole with one granted trigger; a second quoted grant on another line, a quoted
  ability that does not read, and a grant on a target land all stay unread;
- animated, it attacks and the trigger puts a counter on it (a 4/4), and a turn later the grant is
  gone.

Faults injected by script: 5. All are caught, two after the unread assertions.

Coverage: 14,239 of 31,900 cards (+2), 35,557 of 59,888 lines (+2).

## D1050 — a creature land with a sentence after the animation

Creeping Tar Pit: "Until end of turn, this land becomes a 3/2 blue and black Elemental creature.
It's still a land. It can't be blocked this turn."

- `animateThen`, on the activated-ability path after `animateSelf`: the animation as `animateSelf`
  reads it, then the rest of the line with "it" as the land itself, applied to the animated land.
- The rest may not aim at anything or ask anything. Such a line falls through to the ordinary
  reading, which already joins the animation to a targeted sentence (D1048's clause) and keeps the
  target.
- Creeping Tar Pit reads whole.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the row reads whole;
- a 3/2 that is still a land and cannot be blocked this turn, and can be blocked again on the next;
- the same animation followed by "Tap target creature." taps the Bear it is aimed at.

Faults injected by script: 4, all caught.

Coverage: 14,240 of 31,900 cards (+1), 35,558 of 59,888 lines (+1).

## D1051 — a count of counters

"Put X +1/+1 counters on target creature" (the spell's or the ability's X), "…, where X is the
number of lands you control", and "Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature for each creature card in
your graveyard". Even the bare X form was unread: the counter reader took printed numbers only.

- The counter reader takes the tail `countTailOf` reads ("where X is …" counts and "for each …"),
  and reads the body as the fixed-count sentence would be. The number is computed as it resolves:
  the paid X for a bare X, the count for "where X is", and the printed rate times the count for
  "for each".
- A printed number with an X to define ("two counters …, where X is …") and an X with "for each"
  are not sentences and stay unread. A fixed count with no tail is read as before.
- Infuse with the Elements and Nova Flame read whole. Counts `countTailOf` does not have (your
  life total, domain, "noncreature, nonland cards") stay unread, and so do the Fractal token forms
  ("Create a 0/0 Fractal … Put X +1/+1 counters on it").

**Tests.** 4 engine tests, and the compile refusal row "Put X +1/+1 counters on target creature." turned into a note:
- the rows read whole;
- X is the X paid, a printed two is two, and a two with "where X is" stays unread;
- "where X is the number of lands you control" counts 2, and 0 with none;
- "for each creature card in your graveyard" counts the two creatures and not the land.

Faults injected by script: 4. All are caught, two after the fixed-count and refusal assertions.

Coverage: 14,248 of 31,900 cards (+8), 35,567 of 59,888 lines (+9).
## D773 — Combat damage by a kind of creature you control

"Whenever a <kind> you control deals combat damage to a player, …" read a tribe, an artifact
creature and a plain creature (D602). A survey of unread combat-damage lines found twelve that end
in a plain "draw a card" and were unread only because of their subject. Read now:

- "a **legendary** creature" (Vraska Joins Up);
- "a **modified** creature" (SP//dr, Piloted by Peni): CR 700.9, a counter on it, an Equipment
  attached, or an Aura its controller controls;
- "an **enchanted** creature" (Ellivere of the Wild Court): any Aura on it;
- "a creature **token**" (Curiosity Crafter);
- "a **land** creature" (Jolrael, Voice of Zhalfir);
- "a **Wolf or Werewolf**" (Tovolar, Dire Overlord): either tribe.

The `combat-damage` event now carries `subjectIsToken`, `subjectLegendary`, `subjectEnchanted` and
`subjectModified`, read off the creature as it hits, and the trigger asks for them with `token`,
`legendary`, `enchanted`, `modified` and `what: 'land'`. The prologue's subject group admits
"creature token" and "<Tribe> or <Tribe>".

Still unread in this family: "~ or equipped / enchanted creature" (Acquisition Octopus, Thassa's
Emissary), "with a legendary Equipment attached" (Kassandra), "that was turned face up this turn"
(Kaust), and the batched "each with power greater than its base power" (Kutzil).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests: all six subjects read; a legendary creature (only the legend draws); a
modified creature (the one with a counter draws, the plain one does not); a Wolf or Werewolf (each
tribe draws, an Ox does not); an enchanted creature (only the one wearing an Aura draws).

Faults injected by script: 6 of 6 caught.

D602's row that held "a modified creature" as refused now holds "a face-down creature".

    engine tests: 5,638, all passing (on 760997f)

Coverage: 14,241 to 14,248 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 35,560 to 35,571 of 59,888
lines, against 760997f.

## D1052 — counters on the token just made

"When this enchantment enters, create a 0/0 green and blue Fractal creature token. Put three +1/+1
counters on it." Additive Evolution and Recon Craft Theta were counted as read and were wrong. "It"
fell back to the source, so the counters went on the enchantment or the Vehicle, and the 0/0 token
died to the state-based actions.

- `clausesOf` holds "create a(n) … token(s). Put N / X +1/+1 counters on it/them[, where X is …]"
  together as one clause.
- `readEffect` reads the token clause as it always did. It then puts the counters on exactly the
  instances that effect created, which are the tokens, since nothing else arrives during one effect
  (a trigger they cause waits for the stack).
- N is printed. X is the X paid (Fractal Summoning), or a count `countTailOf` reads (Leyline
  Invocation's lands, Manifestation Sage's hand).
- A fix for two misread cards as well as new ones: Additive Evolution and Recon Craft Theta now do
  what they print. Counts the vocabulary does not have (cards in your library, differently named
  lands) stay unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- the Fractal is a 3/3, and the enchantment that made it has no counters;
- X paid makes a 2/2; a second Summon puts its counter on the new Fractal only; and X counted from
  three lands makes a 3/3.

Faults injected by script: 4. 3 are caught, one after the second-Summon assertion. The 4th was a
token-and-battlefield filter on the new instances that nothing else can be, and it was folded away.

Coverage: 14,262 of 31,900 cards (+7), 35,590 of 59,888 lines (+12).

## D1053 — combat damage prevented both ways

"{T}: Untap target attacking creature. Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt to and dealt by
that creature this turn." (Maze of Ith, Ith, Maze of Shadows, Ebony Horse), "{U}: Prevent all combat
damage that would be dealt to and dealt by ~ this turn." (Urborg Phantom, Deftblade Elite, Moonlight
Geist), "… by target creature you control this turn" (Soratami Cloud Chariot, Cephalid
Illusionist).

- A reader for "prevent all combat damage that would be dealt to and dealt by <~ | target
  creature …> this turn": `preventCombatDamage` on those cards, the hand-written Maze of Ith's own

- the Phantom blocks a Bear after activating, and neither is hurt.

Faults injected by script: 4. All are caught, two after the second attacker and the player row; the friendliness one by `compiled-vs-written.test.ts`.
