## D1054 — searches for exactly N, or for one of two kinds

"Search your library for an instant or sorcery card with mana value 1" (Micromancer), "an Equipment
card with mana value 2" (Maximus), and "a basic land card or Gate card" / "… or a Gate card"
(District Guide, Gatecreeper Vine).

- `libraryFilter`'s measure clause takes a bare number as "exactly", beside "N or less" and "N or
  greater". The D1044 measure test answers it for mana value, power and toughness. A bare number
  was left unread before only for want of a reading, and equality is the reading.
- Two whole card phrases joined by "or" are read as either one, each by `libraryFilter`. The split
  needs both halves to end in "card", so "an artifact or creature card" (one phrase whose type words
  take the "or") keeps its own reading. For the same reason neither half can carry a "with mana value
  X" bound.
- Dig and hand-pick readers that use `libraryFilter` take both shapes too.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests, and three compile refusal rows (two filters, Shefet Monitor's two filters, a bare mana value) turned into notes:
- the rows read whole;
- "mana value 2" offers the Bear and not the one-drop or the three-drop;
- "a basic land card or Gate card" offers Islands and the Gate, not a nonbasic land or a creature.

Faults injected by script: 4. 3 are caught. The 4th, an X-bound guard on the two halves, cannot be
reached because both halves end in "card", and it was folded away.

Coverage: 14,287 of 31,900 cards (+14), 35,618 of 59,888 lines (+16).

## D1055 — a bare X, as the X paid

"Target player loses X life", "You gain X life", "Target player mills X cards", "Target player gains
X life", "… deals X damage to any target. You gain X life." (Death Grasp, Stream of Life, Psychic
Drain, Damnable Pact, Swallowing Plague). These readers take a number and not the letter, and the X
is the spell's or the ability's own (`EffectContext.x`, which an enters trigger takes from the cast
X).

- `xAsPaid`, the last reader `readEffect` tries: the clause read with 2 for X, and read again at
  resolution with the X paid. It refuses:
  - "where X is", an X in a target count, a bound or a cost, and "half X";
  - a reading that asks anything (`decisions`, `beforeDecisions`, `immediate`, `reflexive`), since
    those are built at compile time and would keep the 2 ("Scry X");
  - targets that differ between X = 2 and X = 3, since a divided amount lives in the target spec
    (Fire Covenant).
  An X of 0 that a reader refuses does nothing.
- **"Where X is" anywhere in the sentence turns it off** (`xAnnounced`, set by `readEffect` and by
  `composeEffects` for the whole clause group). Without this, "Tendrils of Corruption deals X damage
  to target creature and you gain X life, where X is the number of Swamps you control" split on
  "and": the damage half read as the X paid (nought) while the life half read the count. An audit of
  every newly read card whose X is not in a cost found ten such sentences. All are unread again,
  and a test pins the sentence-level and the clause-split forms.
- **Only an X that something pays** (`xPayable`): the card's mana cost for a spell and for a
  permanent's triggers (the cast X), and the ability's own cost for an activated ability.
  `compileCard` sets the flag from the mana cost and `abilityFromLine` from the ability's cost.
  Without it, "{T}: Prevent the next X damage …" read X as nought. "+X/+X … for each" is a rate and
  is refused too.
- **Morph, megamorph, disguise and echo costs with {X} are refused.** Turning a card face up pays
  no X and keeps none, so Warbreak Trumpeter's "Morph {X}{X}{R}" cost {R} and its "create X Goblins"
  made none. That was a misread already counted as read.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- loses 3, and deals 2 and gains 2, with the X paid;
- X = 0 mills nothing, and X = 2 mills two;
- "where X is" in the sentence, whole or split into clauses, leaves it unread;
- "Scry X", a divided X, a morph X, an X on a card with none in its cost, an ability whose own cost
  has no X (on an X card), and "+X/+X … for each" stay unread. Twin Spend's "X damage … You gain X
  life" compile row now reads.

Faults injected by script: 13. All are caught except one check folded away, an X = 1 / X = 12
read-through that no clause failed. A target check folded alongside it was restored when an audit
found Fire Covenant reading with a divided amount fixed at 2, and that fault is caught. Three
gating faults needed the pins above before they were caught.

Coverage: 14,320 of 31,900 cards (+33), 35,669 of 59,888 lines (+51). The net includes Bane of the
Living and Warbreak Trumpeter, removed from the read count because their morph X was misread.
## D774 — Bestow from the printed text, and "~ or enchanted / equipped creature" hits

Two readers that one card needed: Thassa's Emissary.

**Bestow.** The engine has played bestow since Boon Satyr's hand-written script (`CardScript.bestow`:
an Aura for its bestow cost, a creature again when its host leaves). The compiler never produced
it, so every other bestow card was a creature with an unread keyword and an unread "Enchanted
creature gets …" line. `bestowShapeFor` reads the pair as one: the "Bestow {cost}" line and the
bonus line, through `attachmentBonus`, into `bestow: { cost, effect }`. **31 of the 42 legal bestow
cards** now read both lines. The 11 left are refused, not guessed:
- a bonus with a drawback ("can't block", "attacks each combat if able"), which `attachmentBonus`
  marks harmful;
- a bonus that grants an ability or a trigger, which `bestow.effect` cannot carry;
- X costs and counted bonuses (Nyxborn Hydra).

**"Whenever ~ or enchanted creature deals combat damage to a player"** (Thassa's Emissary), and the
equipped form (Acquisition Octopus): one row with both events, the card's own hit and its host's.
Each fires once. Acquisition Octopus is still partly read for its Reconfigure line.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests: the card reads whole; as a creature it draws when it connects and an Ox
beside it does not; bestowed, the creature it enchants is +3/+3 and draws once when it connects.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 5,650, all passing (on bdad2c5)

Coverage: 14,288 to 14,310 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 35,620 to 35,685 of 59,888
lines, against bdad2c5.

## D775 — Reconfigure

21 legal cards print Reconfigure (CR 702.151), the Kamigawa Equipment creatures: Lion Sash, Lizard
Blades, Acquisition Octopus and the rest. The engine had no notion of it, so each was a creature with
an unread keyword and an unread bonus line.

- `attachmentScriptFor` reads "Reconfigure {cost}" as the equip line, so the attach ability and the
  bonus are the ones every Equipment already uses. The card must be a creature.
- The equip ability's target filter now excludes the Equipment itself, which only a reconfigure
  creature could ever have targeted.
- An unattach ability for the same cost, also sorcery speed, offered only while it is attached
  (`activateOnlyIf`).
- `characteristicsOf`: an attached permanent printing Reconfigure is not a creature and has no
  creature types (`reconfiguredTypeLine`, beside `bestowTypeLine`). Unattached, whether by its
  ability or because its host left (CR 301.5c), it is a creature again.
- **The bot never unattaches** (`buysNothingIf`). A test caught it attaching and unattaching in one
  main phase, spending mana twice to end where it started. A person can still press it.

**18 of the 21** now read their Reconfigure and bonus lines (8 more cards read whole: some print other lines this does not read). The other three: a bonus that sets base power and toughness and
adds types, a quoted "can't lose the game" grant, and a cost paid in mana or energy.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests: the card reads and cannot attach to itself; attached, the host gets +2/+2
and the Equipment is not a creature, with only "Equipment" left in its subtypes; unattached for the
same cost it is a creature again and the bonus is gone; the unattach is not offered while it is
unattached; when the host dies it comes unattached and is a 2/2 creature again; the bot does not
attach and unattach in one turn.

Faults injected by script: 6 of 7 caught. The miss leaves the bonus effect in place when the ability
unattaches; the CR 301.5c check in the state-based actions removes an unattached Equipment's bonus
anyway, so the card behaves the same.

## D1056 — drawing X, now and owed

"Target player draws X cards" (Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius, Blue Sun's Zenith), "You gain X life
and draw X cards" (Sphinx's Revelation), "Each player draws X cards" (Prosperity). D1055's bare-X
reader refused them, because a draw's reading carries an `immediate` part: the same draw done now,
which `composeEffects` uses when something comes after it (a draw is otherwise owed, for dredge).

- `xAsPaid` keeps refusing a question (`decisions`, `beforeDecisions`, `reflexive`), which would keep
  the number it was read with. `immediate` is a function of the resolution like `effect`, so it is
  re-read with the X paid in the same way and passed through.
- Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius, Blue Sun's Zenith, Sphinx's Revelation and Prosperity read whole.
  "Target player discards X cards at random" (Mind Twist) is still unread, because its reader takes
  no number at all.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests. The compile test "will not read the same sentence on a permanent" turns
round: its premise, a trigger with no X, has not held since D985 gave enters triggers the cast X
(`castX`), so Hopeful Drake's "draw X cards" reads now.
- the rows read whole;
- a creature cast for X = 2 draws two when it enters;
- the target draws 3;
- Revelation gains 2 and draws 2. "Draw X cards. Discard a card." with X = 3, not the 2 the reading
  was made with, has all three in hand when the discard asks.

Faults injected by script: 3. 2 are caught. The 3rd, re-reading through `composeEffects` instead of
`readEffect`, was a change made while finding the cause and turned out unneeded, so it was
reverted.

Coverage: 14,358 of 31,900 cards (+8), 35,770 of 59,888 lines (+10), over a baseline that includes
the other session's D774 and D775.
## D776 — Saddle

32 legal Mounts print "Saddle N" (CR 702.171): tap any number of other untapped creatures you control
with total power N or more, as a sorcery, and the Mount becomes saddled until end of turn. Nearly
every one pays off with "Whenever ~ attacks while saddled, <effect>". The keyword had no builder, so
none of the 32 could be saddled.

- `keywordScriptFor`: "Saddle N" is an ability with crew's cost (`cost.crew`, so `crewPlan` picks
  the creatures to tap and never the Mount itself), sorcery speed, offered once a turn
  (`activateOnlyIf`). It marks `CardInstance.saddledTurn` with the turn; the Mount is saddled while
  that is the current turn, and `relocate` clears it when the card changes zones.
- `triggerFromLine`: "Whenever ~ / this creature attacks while saddled, <effect>" is its attack
  trigger read as usual, with the condition that it is saddled.
- The bot: `animates` is crew's rule (press it only with an attack to make), and
  `crewBuysMoreThanItCosts` applies as it does to a Vehicle. In practice the bot saddles with
  creatures that could not have attacked this turn. Conservative, never wasteful.

All 32 read their Saddle line; **16 read whole**. The rest print payoffs whose bodies are unread
("put a +1/+1 counter on target creature that saddled it", "becomes saddled for the first time each
turn", "seek a land card").

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- saddled by tapping another creature, it gets +2/+2 when it attacks;
- unsaddled, the attack does nothing extra;
- only as a sorcery (not in our own end step with priority and an untapped Ox), once a turn (not
  again though a second Ox could pay), and not saddled on the next turn, whose attack gets nothing.

Faults injected by script: 6 of 6 caught, three of them after the last test was extended (instant
speed, a second saddle, saddled into the next turn).

Sweep 60601 (100 pods, on D775 with Bestow and Reconfigure in play): every game finished, 61.8 turns
and 354 moves on average.

    engine tests: 5,665, all passing (merged with the other session's D1055)

## D1058 — "that player or that planeswalker's controller"

Blightning: "~ deals 3 damage to target player or planeswalker. That player or that planeswalker's
controller discards two cards." The subject is the player aimed at, or the controller of the
planeswalker aimed at.

- A referent pronoun with a new supply, `'player-or-controller'`. It is offered only after a
  "player or planeswalker" target, and swapped before any of its parts.
- Without a question, the referent seat is the target player, or the planeswalker's controller read
  before the damage (`withReferent`, which now answers a player target as its own referent).
- A question in the clause (a discard) asks `target-or-its-controller`, the engine's existing
  answer to the same question.
- Blightning reads whole. Rakdos's Return ("discards X cards") stays unread, because the discard's
  question would keep the number it was read with (D1055). The "each creature that player or that
  planeswalker's controller controls" form (Flame Wave, Bonfire of the Damned) is a different
  sentence and stays unread.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the row reads whole, and the sentence after a creature target stays unread;
- aimed at a player: 3 damage, and that player is asked to discard two;
- with no question ("loses 2 life"), the player aimed at loses 2 more;
- aimed at a planeswalker: its controller is asked.

Faults injected by script: 4, all caught.

Coverage: 14,392 of 31,900 cards (+1), 35,837 of 59,888 lines (+1).
## D777 — "Untap it" on a permanent's own trigger

"Whenever ~ attacks, untap it and put a +1/+1 counter on it" (Brightfield Mustang), "Whenever ~
attacks, untap it": a permanent's own trigger untapping itself. `selfEffect` read "untap ~" and
not "untap it", so the line was unread wherever the card did not print its name.

`selfEffect` now reads "untap it" as the card itself, **only on a permanent** (`where ===
'battlefield'`). An "it" that names a target is read before this by the referent readers ("Put a
+1/+1 counter on target creature. Untap it."), and a bare "Untap it." on a spell names nothing and
stays refused.

**D533's refusal row moved.** It held "Whenever Probe Card attacks, untap it. Tap target creature."
as refused, because "untap it" had no self-reading and so could only compile by binding forward to
the later target, which is the wrong card. It now has its own reading, the attacker, which is what
the card means, so the line reads correctly. The row now uses "tap it", which still has no
self-reading, and D777's tests check the "untap it" line plays: the attacker untaps and only the
target is tapped.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests: both cards read and a bare "Untap it." on a spell is refused; the attacker
untaps itself and gets its counter; before a target, "untap it" is the attacker and the target is
only tapped; on a spell, "it" is still the target.

Faults injected by script: 2 of 2 caught (one after the test was extended with the bare-spell
refusal).

## D778 — Leylines begin the game on the battlefield

"If ~ is in your opening hand, you may begin the game with it on the battlefield" (CR 103.6): Leyline
of the Void, of Sanctity, of the Meek and the rest, 17 legal cards and Modern and Commander staples.
The line was unread, so a Leyline in an opening hand stayed there.

- `lineScriptFor` reads the line as `CardScript.beginsInPlay`.
- `beginFirstTurn` (`autoActions.ts`), after every player has kept and before the first turn: each
  player in turn order, starting with the first, puts the ones in their opening hand onto the
  battlefield. Their statics apply from there.
- **Always taken.** The rule says "may", and there is no decline yet. A deck holding a Leyline wants
  it in play; the case for keeping one in hand is narrow.

Several Leylines print a second line the engine does not read yet (Leyline of Sanctity's "You have
hexproof", Leyline of Punishment's "Players can't gain life"), so they begin on the battlefield and
carry a badge for that line.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests: the card reads; in an opening hand it is on the battlefield before the
first turn and its +0/+1 applies; each player puts their own, two at once included; drawn later it is
an ordinary card in hand.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught.

The deck-coverage test lists `script beginsInPlay` with the other compiler-only fields.

## D1059 — damage to a player and each creature they control

"Flame Wave deals 4 damage to target player or planeswalker and each creature that player or that
planeswalker's controller controls", Chandra's Fury's "… and 1 damage to each creature …",
Lavalanche's and Bonfire of the Damned's X, Chandra, Pyrogenius's -10.

- A `damageEffect` reader for "<~> deals N|X damage to target player|opponent [or planeswalker] and
  [M damage to] each creature that player [or that planeswalker's controller] controls".
- The creatures are listed before any damage is dealt: those of the player aimed at, or of the
  planeswalker's controller. The damage is dealt at once, and the planeswalker may not survive it.
- The referent must match the target ("that player" after a player, the planeswalker form after a
  player or planeswalker). X is used only when a cost pays it (`xPayable`, D1055).
- `splitDamageClauses` no longer cuts "… and 1 damage to each creature that player … controls" into
  two clauses, since the second piece is about the first piece's player.
- Flame Wave, Chandra's Fury, Lavalanche, Bonfire of the Damned and Chandra, Pyrogenius read whole.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and a mismatched referent and an unpaid X stay unread;
- aimed at a player: 4 to the player, the Bear dies, the Wall takes 4, and the caster's Bear lives;
- "1 damage to each creature" puts one on each;
- aimed at a planeswalker: it loses 4 loyalty and its controller's creatures are hit;
- X = 3 hits the player and each creature for 3.

Faults injected by script: 6. All are caught, the guard after the unread assertions.

## D1060 — the delayed blink: back at the beginning of the next end step

"Exile target creature. Return it to the battlefield under its owner's control at the beginning of
the next end step." Turn to Mist, Voidwalk, Mistmeadow Witch, Glimmerpoint Stag, Galepowder Mage,
Roon of the Hidden Realm, Liberate. The self form is "Exile ~. Return it …", printed on Argent
Sphinx, Ghost Council of Orzhova, Fleeting Spirit, Saltskitter and Hikari, Twilight Guardian.

- Two new engine-owned delayed abilities, `return-to-owner` and `return-to-you`, next to D696's
  `sacrifice`, `exile`, `to-hand` and `destroy`. Each puts its subject onto the battlefield, under
  its owner's control or under the delayed ability's controller's.
- The D543 clause reader for "return target creature to the battlefield under its owner's|your
  control" takes "at the beginning of the next end step". Instead of returning the card at once, it
  schedules the return about the card in exile. That is anybody's next end step (`of: 'any'`).
- A self reader beside D951's `exilesItself` reads "return ~|it to the battlefield under … control
  at the beginning of the next end step". It reads only on a battlefield ability, so a dies
  trigger's "return it" (from the graveyard) stays unread. It schedules only when the card did
  reach exile, so a Sphinx that died in response leaves no "coming back" row on the table.
- No zone check on the return itself. The subject pin (CR 400.7) already drops a card that left
  exile in between: every zone change goes through `relocate`, which makes a new object, and a
  token is deleted as it leaves the battlefield. A fault that removed such a check went uncaught,
  and the check was folded away.
- Flickerwisp's hand-written card uses `return-to-owner` instead of a second delayed trigger. That
  is what the compiler builds from the same words, and `compiled-vs-written.test.ts` now finds the
  two readings equal.
- compile.test's refusal row for Flickerwisp's wording now asserts that the wording reads (D516).
  The tapped return, the counter rider and the plural are still refused.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, while the tapped return (spell and self) and a dies trigger's return stay
  unread;
- an opponent's Bear is exiled, one delayed ability is scheduled, and the Bear returns under its
  owner at the end step;
- "under your control" gives the caster the Bear;
- a card moved out of exile in between stays where it went;
- the self blink exiles the Sphinx, which comes back at the end step;
- a Sphinx moved to the graveyard before its ability resolves schedules nothing and stays there.

Faults injected by script: 8. All are caught. Two earlier faults went uncaught, and each pointed at
a zone guard that cannot fail; both guards were removed.

Coverage: 14,440 of 31,900 cards (+29), 35,915 of 59,888 lines (+43).

## D1061 — back from the graveyard: a death trigger returns the card

"When enchanted creature dies, return that card to the battlefield under your control" (False
Demise, Fool's Demise, Shade's Form, Minion's Return, Unhallowed Pact, Abduction's owner's-control
form), "… tapped …" (Ferocity of the Hunt), "Whenever a creature dealt damage by ~ this turn dies,
return that card …" (Soul Collector), and the delayed form "… at the beginning of the next end step"
(Avacyn, Angel of Horror; Resurrection Orb).

- A `selfEffect` reader for "return ~|it|that card to the battlefield [tapped] under its owner's|your
  control [at the beginning of the next end step]". It reads only where the trigger's event leaves
  the card in a graveyard (`where === 'graveyard'`: `dies` and `to-graveyard`).
- "It" and "that card" are the card the event put there (`itMeans`). On an Aura, that is the
  creature that died, not the Aura, which went to the graveyard by the same death. A test checks
  this.
- It acts only while the card is still in the graveyard (CR 400.7): a card exiled in response stays
  exiled, and a token is gone. "Your control" is the trigger's controller: a False Demise on an
  opponent's creature takes it.
- The delayed form schedules D1060's `return-to-owner` / `return-to-you` about the card in the
  graveyard. The subject pin holds it there, and the tapped delayed return stays unread because that
  return does not tap.
- D1060's unread row for a dies trigger now reads, which is correct. It becomes a "leaves the
  battlefield" row, which neither reader can place.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, while a tapped delayed return and a return off an enters trigger stay unread;
- an Aura on the opponent's Bear: the Bear is killed and returns under the Aura's controller, and the
  Aura stays in the graveyard;
- its own death: it returns tapped under its owner;
- a card exiled from the graveyard before the trigger resolves stays exiled;
- the delayed form on an opponent's creature: it waits in the graveyard and returns under its owner
  at the end step.

Faults injected by script: 9. All are caught. Two were caught only after the delayed test was moved
to an opponent's creature, the only place "its owner's" can differ from "your", and reworded with
"it".

Coverage: 14,454 of 31,900 cards (+14), 35,932 of 59,888 lines (+17).

## D1062 — a quoted ability granted to a target until end of turn

"Until end of turn, target creature gets +2/+0 and gains "When this creature dies, return it to the
battlefield tapped under its owner's control."" (Supernatural Stamina, Return to Action, Pain 101,
Demonic Gifts, Abnormal Endurance), "Until end of turn, target creature gains "{T}: Return target
nonland permanent to its owner's hand."" (Banishing Knack, Retraction Helix), and the activated
form: Herd Heirloom, Dragon-Cursed Halls, Greater Stone Spirit. Hunter's Prowess too.

- `quotedGrantUntilEndOfTurn` reads "[until end of turn,] target creature … [gets +N/+N and] gains
  [keywords and] "<quotation>" [until end of turn]", with "until end of turn" exactly once.
- The quotation goes through the readers an Aura's grant uses (`grantedTriggerFrom`, then
  `grantedAbilityFrom`, D511 and D512). It is held in the card's `grantedTriggers` or
  `grantedAbilities` and handed to the creature by index, through an end-of-turn effect.
- The ability belongs to the creature, so "this creature" and "it" mean the creature, and its
  controller controls the trigger. A granted dies trigger fires from the creature's last state, so
  Supernatural Stamina's creature comes back, as a new object without the pump.
- **Two callers only.** The table lives on the card and the index lives in a closure, so every place
  that builds a script from this reading has to carry the table, or the creature is handed index 0
  of nothing. A spell whose whole resolution is this one sentence merges it (`granting`), and so does
  an activated ability (`cardFields`, D1049). A trigger, a mode, or a composition with another
  sentence stays unread rather than dropping the grant.
- The target is `friendly`: an ability is its holder's to use, so a grant is a gift.
- compile.test's row "does not read a 'this creature' inside a quoted granted ability as the card's
  own" asserted that Abnormal Endurance's line reads to nothing. It now asserts that the line reads
  whole, the spell has no trigger of its own, and the quotation is its one `grantedTriggers` entry
  (D516).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the rows read whole and the target is friendly; a quotation with no "until end of turn", with two,
  or with another sentence after it stays unread;
- the pump and the dies trigger: 4 power, then killed, back tapped at 2 power;
- an activated ability on the creature: offered after the spell, used to gain 3 life with the
  creature tapped for it, and no longer offered next turn;
- an artifact's activated grant: trample and one granted trigger on the creature.

Faults injected by script: 9. All are caught. The `friendly` hint was caught only after the test
asserted it.

Coverage: 14,467 of 31,900 cards (+13), 35,946 of 59,888 lines (+14).

## D1063 — "you may <a targeted action>. If you do, …"

"Whenever a player cycles a card, you may exile target creature. If you do, return that card to the
battlefield under its owner's control at the beginning of the next end step" (Astral Slide), "you
may exile target creature card from a graveyard. If you do, you gain 2 life" (Carrion Imp, Mardu
Woe-Reaper, Boneclad Necromancer), Lagonna-Band Storyteller, Niambi, Esteemed Speaker, Soldevi
Golem.

- `optionalEffect`'s "you may X. If you do, Y" refused any X with a target. It now reads that X
  when the two sentences read as one composition.
- Y very often names X's object ("that card", "its mana value", "that creature's mana value"), and
  only `composeEffects` can answer that: the referent swap (D533) and the blink rule (D543). So the
  targets are the composition's, and Wisp's exile-and-return target carries `blinks`.
- "If you do" is learnt as for a question-less X (D951): X is run alone, and a board it left
  untouched means it did not happen (CR 608.2c), so nothing does. Otherwise the composition runs from
  the same board.
- A question in Y splits the composition and the line is refused. No targeted X asks one of its own,
  so the composition's questions are carried, not guarded; that guard and a target-count guard went
  uncaught by faults and were folded away.
- **Tapping a creature that is already tapped no longer rebuilds the board** (`tap` in effects.ts,
  CR 701.26a). It used to, so "you may tap target creature. If you do, you gain 2 life" gained life
  off a tapped creature. Nothing else depended on it, and the whole suite stays green.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the rows read whole; a tapped delayed return and a question after the yes stay unread; the
  target blinks;
- yes: the opponent's Bear is exiled and back under its owner at the end step; no: nothing;
- a card exiled out of a graveyard, then 2 life;
- tapping a creature already tapped gains no life;
- the enchantment put on top of the library is the "its mana value" of the life gained.

Faults injected by script: 6. All are caught after two guards were folded and the blink flag was
asserted.

Coverage: 14,474 of 31,900 cards (+7), 35,953 of 59,888 lines (+7).

## D1064 — "target … you own"

"Exile another target creature you own. Return it to the battlefield under your control at the
beginning of the next end step" (Charming Prince), "Whenever ~ deals combat damage to a player,
exile up to one target creature you own, then return it …" (Meneldor, Swift Savior), "{T}: Destroy
target permanent you own" (Despotic Scepter, Staff of Compleation), "Return target creature you own
to your hand" (Saving Grasp), "{T}: Put target permanent you own on the bottom of your library"
(Tel-Jilad Stylus).

- A `targetSpecFrom` wrapper for "<permanent phrase> you own", beside D1010's "other than ~" and
  D1011's counter wrapper. The candidate's `owner` must be the controller choosing, and ownership is
  not control (CR 108.3): a creature you own that an opponent took may be chosen, and one you took
  may not. Only on a phrase that points at a permanent, because "counter target spell you own"
  would otherwise read as a target nothing can be.
- "To your hand" and "of your library" after "target … you own" read as the owner's hand and
  library, which they are, through the bounce reader (D751) and the library reader (D546, D758). On
  any other target they stay unread, so an opponent's card is never put into your hand.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole; "to your hand", "of your library" on an ordinary target, and "counter target
  spell you own" stay unread;
- an opponent's Bear is refused; after the two Bears trade controllers, the one you took is still
  refused and the one you own is returned to your hand;
- the Stylus puts a permanent you own on the bottom of your library.

Faults injected by script: 4. All are caught. The permanent guard was caught only after the spell
row was added.

Coverage: 14,480 of 31,900 cards (+6), 35,965 of 59,888 lines (+12).

"Until end of turn, creatures you control gain "{T}: This creature deals 1 damage to any target.""

## D1066 — a new body for the turn: base size, lost abilities, a new type

"Until end of turn, target creature loses all abilities and has base power and toughness 0/1"
(Humble, Ovinize), "Target creature has base power and toughness 1/1 until end of turn" (Diminish,
Multiply by Zero, Gigantomancer's 7/7, Creeperhulk's 5/5 and trample), "… becomes a Dragon with
base power and toughness 4/4 and gains flying" (Mordenkainen's Polymorph, Dance of the Skywise,
Gift of Tusks), Turn to Frog's own words, and Merfolk Trickster's "It loses all abilities until end
of turn" through the referent.

- A targeted clause reader: one target, "until end of turn" exactly once, and predicates joined by
  "," or "and". Each predicate is one of:
  - "loses all abilities" (layer 6);
  - "has base power and toughness N/N" (layer 7b, so a pump on top still counts);
  - "becomes a [colours] [creature types] [with base power and toughness N/N] [in addition to its
    other types]". The colour is replaced, and the types are replaced unless the card says "in
    addition" (CR 205.1b). Every word must be a real creature type.
  - "gets +N/+N" (layer 7c);
  - "gains <keywords>".
- All of it is one end-of-turn effect, so the abilities are cleared before the keywords it grants
  (CR 613.1f), which is how Turn to Frog's hand-written script has always worked.
- A body made small (1 or less in either number) or with no abilities is removal for the turn:
  `removesACreature` and a hostile aim. A bigger one is a gift and the target is friendly. Either
  way it wears off (`expiresAtEndOfTurn`).
- It must set something (a base size, a type, or the abilities), or the line belongs to the pump
  readers, including what they refuse on purpose: "gets -2/-2 and gains menace" is a shrink with a
  grant that no card prints (D454). The guard was folded away once, when a fault run over this
  increment's tests alone missed it. The pregate's full suite failed on that compile.test row, so
  the guard is back and the fault script runs that row too.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the rows read whole; no duration and a word that is not a creature type stay unread; Humble and
  Diminish are hostile removal, Grower is a friendly gift, and "gains hexproof" keeps the pump
  reader's `protectsACreature`;
- Humble: the flying 2/2 is a 0/1 without flying, and a 2/2 flier again next turn;
- a +3/+3 cast before Humble still counts: 3/4;
- Polymorph: a 4/4 whose only subtype is Dragon, with trample;
- base 5/5.

Faults injected by script: 10. All are caught. Three were caught only after Diminish's flag, the
hexproof row and a trample grant were asserted.

Coverage: 14,518 of 31,900 cards (+31), 36,017 of 59,888 lines (+45).

## D1067 — a new body for itself

"{4}{G/U}: ~ has base power and toughness 5/5 until end of turn" (Brokers Initiate), "{8}: ~ has base
power and toughness 10/10 until end of turn. Activate only if you control an Oko planeswalker"
(Bramblefort Fink), "{W}{U}{B}{R}{G}: Until end of turn, ~ becomes a Dragon, gets +5/+3, and gains
flying and trample" (Dragonsoul Knight).

- D1066's predicates are now one helper, `newBodyFrom`, shared by the target's reader and a new
  `selfEffect` reader for "[until end of turn,] ~ <predicates> [until end of turn]".
- The self reader takes the permanent's own name only, because "it" on a trigger is the event's
  subject. It reads only on a battlefield ability or trigger (`where`): a dies trigger that gives
  the dead card a body stays unread.
- It has to set something, as D1066 does, so lines that only add stay with the pump readers.
- No zone check at resolution. A permanent that left in response and came back is a new object, and
  the engine already keeps the effect off it (CR 400.7). A fault that removed such a check went
  uncaught, so it was folded away and the case is a test.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the rows read whole; no duration and a dies trigger's body stay unread;
- a 1/1 is 5/5 until the turn ends, then 1/1;
- bounced in response and played again, it is a 1/1;
- the Knight is a 3/3 Dragon (its only subtype) with flying.

Faults injected by script: 5. All are caught, including D1066's `sets` guard against compile.test's
shrink row.

Coverage: 14,524 of 31,900 cards (+6), 36,025 of 59,888 lines (+8).

## D1068 — an artifact that animates itself

"{W}{U}: ~ becomes a 2/2 white and blue Bird artifact creature with flying until end of turn" (the
ten Keyrunes), "{4}{R}{G}: ~ becomes a 4/4 red and green Dragon artifact creature with flying until
end of turn" (the Monuments), Darksteel Brute, Guardian Idol, Fountain of Ichor, Gruul War Plow,
Ensouled Scimitar, Chimeric Idol, Firdoch Core, and the trigger form, Eye of Malcator's.

- `animateArtifactSelf` gives D754's land animation the sentence these cards do not print. "It's
  still a land" is what tells that reader the card keeps its types. An artifact that becomes an
  *artifact* creature keeps being an artifact by the words themselves, so the animation is the
  same: Artifact and Creature added, the size set, and the colours, creature types and keywords as
  printed.
- Only for a phrase ending "artifact creature [with …] [until end of turn]" with no land sentence of
  its own. Only the card itself, because the land reader aims only at land phrases: Alloy Animist's
  "target noncreature artifact you control" stays unread.
- One hook, in `readEffect`, so an activated ability and a trigger read it alike. A second hook on
  the ability path, a pre-check on the readEffect hook and a target refusal each went uncaught by
  faults, because each repeated something already enforced, and all three were removed.
- Process note: this increment was first written while D1067's gate was running, against the
  standing rule. That ship was stopped before it committed, the D1068 hunks were set aside, D1067
  was gated and pushed alone, and only then were they restored.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole; a target, and a "Bird creature" that is not an artifact creature, stay unread;
- the Keyrune is a 2/2 white and blue Bird artifact creature with flying, and not a creature next
  turn;
- the "until end of turn" first spelling: a 3/3 whose only subtype is Golem.

Faults injected by script: 3. All are caught after the three redundant checks were folded.

Coverage: 14,552 of 31,900 cards (+28), 36,060 of 59,888 lines (+35).

## D1069 — damage to "that land's controller"

"Whenever a land enters, ~ deals 2 damage to that land's controller" (Ankh of Mishra, Zo-Zu the
Punisher), "Whenever enchanted creature becomes tapped, ~ deals 3 damage to that creature's
controller" (Insolence, Lust for War), and Psychic Venom's land.

- An `eventRelativeEffect` reader for "~ deals N damage to that creature's / land's / artifact's /
  enchantment's / permanent's controller". The player is whoever controls the event's own object
  as the ability resolves.
- It reads only on an entry, a tap or a block, never on the watcher's own event (`who: 'self'`,
  where "that creature" would be the card itself).
- A death or a move to the graveyard is not this reader's. "Whenever a creature dies, ~ deals 2
  damage to that creature's controller" already reads through the actor path (D654), whose seat is
  the controller as the creature last existed (CR 608.2h).
- "Enchanted creature becomes tapped" carries no subject on the event, so the creature is the Aura's
  host.
- Battle Strain, Heat of Battle and Tetsuko Umezawa wait on their opening, "Whenever a creature
  blocks", which does not read yet.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and the card's own entry stays unread;
- Ankh: your land costs you 2, and on the opponent's turn their land costs them 2;
- an Aura on the opponent's Bear: it attacks, becomes tapped, and its controller takes 2, not the
  Aura's.

Faults injected by script: 3. All are caught.

Coverage: 14,557 of 31,900 cards (+5), 36,067 of 59,888 lines (+7).

## D1070 — "whenever a creature blocks"

"Whenever a creature blocks, ~ deals 1 damage to that creature's controller" (Battle Strain, Heat of
Battle, finished by D1069's reader), "Whenever a creature you control blocks", "Whenever a creature
an opponent controls blocks", and "Whenever another creature [you control] blocks".

- A trigger-opening row beside D990's "Whenever a creature attacks", read into `blocks` with `who`
  (`any`, or `another` for "another creature") and `of` (`any`, `you`, `opponent`).
- The engine already matched `who` and `of` on blocks, as on attacks: the blocker is the subject,
  once per blocking creature.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- seat 1 blocks: Battle Strain deals 1 to seat 1, the blocker's controller; seat 1's "a creature you
  control blocks" gains it 2; seat 0's "a creature an opponent controls blocks" gains it 1; and seat
  1's copy of that watcher hears nothing;
- a creature whose trigger is "another creature you control blocks" gains nothing when it blocks
  itself.

Faults injected by script: 3. All are caught. The `another` fault was caught only after the third
test was added.

Coverage: 14,560 of 31,900 cards (+3), 36,070 of 59,888 lines (+3).

## D1071 — clash with an opponent

"When ~ enters, clash with an opponent. If you win, put a +1/+1 counter on ~" (Adder-Staff Boggart,
Bog Hoodlums, Nath's Elite, Oaken Brawler, Paperfin Rascal, Springjack Knight), "When ~ dies, clash
… If you win, return ~ to its owner's hand" (Ringskipper), Lash Out, Spring Cleaning and Broken
Ambitions. The first support for the mechanic (CR 701.23).

- `clausesOf` keeps "Clash with an opponent. If you win, Y. [Otherwise, Z.]" together as one clause,
  as D952 does for "you may X. If you do, Y".
- `readEffect` asks two questions: keep the revealed top card, or put it on the bottom. The first
  goes to you (`controller`) and the second to the next opponent in turn order (`an-opponent`). That
  is exact with two players; in a pod the caster would choose the opponent, which is the limitation
  D728 already records.
- As the ability resolves, the two top cards are compared where they are. You win only if yours has
  the greater mana value (CR 701.23b), so a tie loses and an empty library cannot win. Then the cards
  move as answered, and then Y happens, or Z when you lose.
- Y and Z are any clauses the reader reads, but with no question of their own and with at most one
  of the two aiming at something. A target is the whole ability's, chosen as it goes on the stack.
- The computer puts a revealed land on the bottom once it has five lands, and keeps anything else.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the rows read whole; an outcome with its own question, and two outcomes that each aim, stay
  unread;
- a 6 against a 0: the counter goes on, your card goes to the bottom as chosen, and theirs stays;
- a 0 against a 6, and a tie, lose;
- "otherwise": the loss costs 2 life;
- Lash Out's shape: 3 to the target Bear, then after the win 3 to its controller.

Faults injected by script: 9. All are caught. Two were caught only after the question and two-target
rows were added.

Coverage: 14,571 of 31,900 cards (+11), 36,082 of 59,888 lines (+12).

## D1072 — kinship

"Kinship — At the beginning of your upkeep, you may look at the top card of your library. If it
shares a creature type with ~, you may reveal it. If you do, each opponent loses 2 life" (Nightshade
Schemers). Also Ink Dissolver, Kithkin Zephyrnaut, Mudbutton Clanger, Pyroclast Consul, Sensation
Gorger, Wandering Graybeard, Winnower Patrol and Wolf-Skull Shaman.

- `clausesOf` marks the three sentences as one clause. A `readEffect` reader asks the reveal as a
  yes-or-no for the controller.
- The reveal is offered only when the top card shares a creature type with the permanent.
  Changeling counts, because `characteristicsOf` gives it every type. When the card does not share
  a type, the question has one option and answers itself, so nothing is asked.
- The look is private and costs nothing, so it is not asked.
- The payoff is any clause the reader reads with no question or target of its own, because the
  reveal is answered as the ability resolves, after targets would have been chosen.
- Leaf-Crowned Elder, Squeaking Pie Grubfellows and Waterspout Weavers stay unread: their payoffs
  play the card, ask a question, or grant flying to the team.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads whole, while a payoff that aims and one that asks stay unread;
- with a Faerie on top: asked, and "Reveal it" costs the opponent 2 life while "Keep it hidden" does
  nothing;
- a changeling on top is asked about; with a Bear on top nothing is asked and nothing happens.

Faults injected by script: 5. All are caught. The payoff guard was caught only after the aim and ask
rows were added.

Coverage: 14,580 of 31,900 cards (+9), 36,091 of 59,888 lines (+9).

## D1073 — the top card, and where it goes when it is not taken

"Whenever ~ or another Elemental you control enters, look at the top card of your library. If it's
a land card, you may put it onto the battlefield tapped. If you don't put the card onto the
battlefield, put it into your hand" (Risen Reef), N'Yami-Class Mother Ship, Skyclave Aerialist,
Wickerfolk Thresher.

- D1036's top-card reader takes a third sentence: "If you don't put the card into your hand / onto
  the battlefield, put it into your hand / on the bottom of your library". `clausesOf` joins it to
  the clause.
- It reads only after "you may". An answer that picks nothing leaves the card on top, and the effect
  then moves it. A card of another kind is never offered, so it goes the same way.
- The optional form, "you may put it into your graveyard" (six cards), needs a second question asked
  only when the first picked nothing, and stays unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and the third sentence without a "may" stays unread;
- a land taken goes onto the battlefield and nothing else moves; declined, it goes to your hand;
- a creature on top for a land question goes straight to your hand, and a land on top for a creature
  question goes to the bottom of your library.

Faults injected by script: 4. All are caught. The taken check was caught only after the hand-size
assertion was added.

Coverage: 14,585 of 31,900 cards (+5), 36,097 of 59,888 lines (+6).

## D1074 — a second question only if the first took nothing

"Landfall — Whenever a land you control enters, look at the top card of your library. If it's a
creature card, you may reveal it and put it into your hand. If you don't put the card into your
hand, you may put it into your graveyard" (Territory Culler). Also Sarinth Steelseeker, Traveling
Botanist, Archghoul of Thraben, Cabaretti Ascendancy, and the "you may put it on the bottom" form.

- **Engine:** `CardsDecisionSpec.askOnlyIfNonePicked`. The question is asked only when the one
  before it picked nothing; otherwise it is skipped as `askOnlyIfChosen` skips, with an empty answer
  in its place.
- D1073's "otherwise" now takes "you may", and the graveyard as a destination. The optional form is
  a second look at the same card, with `chosenGoTo` the destination, so the engine moves it on a yes.
  The mandatory form is still moved by the effect.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the card reads whole;
- a creature taken into the hand: the graveyard question is never asked;
- declined: the graveyard question comes, and the card goes to the graveyard or stays on top;
- a land on top: no hand question, straight to the graveyard question.

Faults injected by script: 4. All are caught.

Coverage: 14,592 of 31,900 cards (+7), 36,104 of 59,888 lines (+7).

## D1075 — revealing the top cards and putting one into your hand

"Reveal the top five cards of your library. You may put a creature or land card from among them into
your hand. Put the rest into your graveyard" (Grisly Salvage), Commune with the Gods, Malevolent
Rumble.

- `digGroup` takes "reveal the top N cards" as well as "look at". The cards are seen by everyone
  rather than by one player; what is chosen from them, and where the rest go, is the same question.
- A new pick sentence: "you may put a <kind> card from among them into your hand", at most one card,
  using the same kind test as D973's forms.
- "A creature card and/or a land card" means one of each, which one question with one filter cannot
  hold. It stays unread because the kind test does not read the phrase. A separate guard went
  uncaught by faults and was folded away.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- the card reads whole, and the "and/or" form stays unread;
- the five cards revealed: creatures and lands are offered (the artifacts are not), at most one is
  taken, and it goes to the hand while the other four go to the graveyard.

Faults injected by script: 2. Both are caught.

Coverage: 14,598 of 31,900 cards (+6), 36,111 of 59,888 lines (+7).

## D1076 — the total power of creatures you control

"This spell costs {X} less to cast, where X is the total power of creatures you control" (Ghalta,
Primal Hunger), and the same measure wherever a count is read: "draw cards equal to …", "you gain
life equal to …", "… where X is …", "with flying", "other creatures".

- `totalAmong`, beside D660's `greatestAmong`, reads "the total power|toughness of [other] [<Type>]
  creatures you control|your opponents control|on the battlefield [with <keyword>]". It sums the
  live values as the effect reads them, so a creature with negative power takes from the sum. The
  result is never below 0 (CR 107.1b).
- `boardCount` asks it, and the five readers that pre-filter their measure ("where X is", "draw
  cards equal to", "gain or lose life equal to" and two more) now let it through.
- Ghalta and Stonehoof Chieftain's cost line read. The corpus has few other cards with this measure
  outside lines unread for other reasons, so the gain is mostly the vocabulary.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the rows read whole;
- 4 power on the battlefield makes a six-drop cost {2}, and 3 power leaves it uncastable with two
  lands;
- "with flying": two 1/2 fliers beside a 3/1 give 2 life;
- "other creatures": a 5/5 whose ability it is counts only the 3/1, for 3 life.

Faults injected by script: 4. All are caught. Two were caught only after power and toughness were
made to differ and the "other" row was added.

Coverage: 14,600 of 31,900 cards (+2), 36,115 of 59,888 lines (+4).

## D1078 — entering with counters of its own

"~ enters with three oil counters on it" (Gitaxian Raptor, Glistener Seer, Furnace Strider and the
rest of the oil cards), "~ enters with two -1/-1 counters on it", and the other counters a card keeps
for its own lines: wish, net, omen, gem, study, javelin.

- `entersWithFromLine`'s allow-list (`+1/+1`, charge, ice, shield, and the keyword counters) now
  admits any one-word counter that is not in `RULES_COUNTERS`, plus -1/-1. A card-local counter is
  read by another line of the same card ("Remove an oil counter from ~: …"), exactly as charge
  always was, so that line decides whether the card is read.
- Still refused: a counter whose rule the engine applies by name (time and fade without their
  keyword, loyalty, lore, finality, age, level and the rest of `RULES_COUNTERS`), and any size
  counter but +1/+1 and -1/-1. Finality is on that list because the engine does not apply it yet.
- -1/-1 needed its "-" admitted to the counter-name pattern. `characteristicsOf` already reads -1/-1
  counters.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the rows read whole; time, finality, +1/+0 and lore counters stay unread;
- three oil counters on arrival, and the card's own "Remove an oil counter" ability spends one for
  +1/+1;
- two -1/-1 counters make a 4/4 a 2/2.

Faults injected by script: 3. All are caught.

## D1080 — "its power" after the clause that aimed at it

"Destroy target attacking creature. You gain life equal to its power" (Chastise), "Destroy target
nonblack creature. It can't be regenerated. You gain life equal to its toughness" (Sever Soul),
Exile, Heal the Scars, Sheltering Word, Brightmare.

- A `boardCount` measure: "its|that creature's power|toughness", only after a clause that aimed at a
  card (`earlierCardTarget`). Live while the creature is on the battlefield.
- Once the clause before has destroyed or exiled it, it is read as it last was (CR 608.2h). That
  value comes from a new `EffectContext.targetStats`, which `composeEffects` fills with each card
  target's power and toughness as the composed resolution begins. The `boardCount` docblock had left
  this unread "for want of last known information"; this is that information.
- The five readers that pre-filter their measure now let the phrase through.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the rows read whole, and "its power" with nothing aimed at before it stays unread;
- a Bear pumped +3/+3 and then destroyed gives the power it last had, 5;
- "+2/+2, then its toughness" on a creature still there gives the value now, 6, not the snapshot;
- a regenerated creature that is still there gives its toughness.

Faults injected by script: 4. All are caught. The live-value fault was caught only after the
pump-then-measure row was added.

Coverage: 14,650 of 31,900 cards (+10), 36,239 of 59,888 lines (+11).

## D1081 — "that creature's toughness" after an edict

"Target opponent sacrifices a creature. You gain life equal to that creature's toughness" (Tribute
to Hunger), Consuming Vapors, and Doomgape's own upkeep sacrifice.

- **`EffectContext.composedChosen`**: every card a question of the composed resolution chose, in
  order. A part's own slice of the answers does not include an earlier part's, so this is how a
  later part finds the creature the edict took.
- D1080's snapshot (`targetStats`) now includes those chosen cards as well as the targets, taken as
  the resolution begins.
- A flag beside `earlierCardTarget`, set when an earlier part's question picks from the battlefield,
  lets "that creature's power|toughness" read the last card chosen: live if it is still there, as it
  last was otherwise (CR 608.2h).
- A context built by hand (some compile tests) carries neither targets nor decisions, so both lists
  are optional in the snapshot. The full suite found that on its first run.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- the row reads whole, and the phrase with no question before it stays unread;
- a 0/5 Wall pumped +3/+3 is sacrificed to the edict, and the caster gains its last toughness, 8.

Faults injected by script: 4. All are caught.

Coverage: 14,654 of 31,900 cards (+4), 36,243 of 59,888 lines (+4).

## D1082 — an additional land this turn, and a permanent that tucks itself

Two lines from the top of the EDHREC-ordered queue the D7xx session relayed.

- "You may play an additional land this turn" (Explore, Growth Spiral, Urban Evolution, Broken Bond)
  is a clause reader using `allowExtraLand`, the permission Explore's hand-written script has used
  since D648. It takes one, two or three lands.
- "Put ~ on top of its owner's library" (Sensei's Divining Top's "{T}: Draw a card, then put ~ on
  top of its owner's library") is a `selfEffect` reader. It works only from the battlefield and only

- the rows read whole;
- after the spell, a second land may be played this turn and a third may not;
- the Top draws a card and is then the top card of its owner's library;
- a Top moved to hand in response stays in hand.

Faults injected by script: 4. All are caught.

Coverage: 14,660 of 31,900 cards (+6, Explore among them), 36,255 of 59,888 lines.
## D779 — Most-played first: Chromatic Lantern, Frantic Search, and two questions in one spell

**A new priority order, from Nick: automate cards from the most played down.** Ranked by EDHREC
(Scryfall's `oracle_cards` bulk file, `edhrec_rank`), fully automated today: top 100 96%, top 250
88%, top 500 77%, top 1,000 65%, top 2,500 50%, top 5,000 41%. The work queue is the unread cards
in rank order. This increment takes two from near its top.

- **Chromatic Lantern** (rank 85): "Lands you control have "{T}: Add one mana of any color."" A
  granted activated ability on the `controller-lands` scope, through the same grant table the
  creature lords use. `manaSources` already reads granted mana abilities, so a Forest pays a blue
  cost with the Lantern out.
- **Frantic Search** (rank 97): "Untap up to three lands." Asked as it resolves, from your own tapped
  lands. The rules allow any land; an opponent's is never worth untapping, so only yours are offered.
  Snap and Cloud of Faeries' kin read too.
- **Two questions in one resolution.** Frantic Search asks two (what to discard, what to untap), and
  `composeEffects` refused any composition with more than one answer-reading part (D467), because
  every part read its answers from index 0. D651 gave each part its own offset into the answers, so
  that hazard is gone, and this allows more than one, **with one condition**: every part from the
  first question to the last must itself be a question. Every question is planned before the
  resolution runs and only the parts before the first question run first, so a draw between two
  questions would have the second one planned against the hand before that draw.
  "Target player discards a card. Draw two cards, then discard two cards." is refused for that
  reason; the loot-first order reads.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests: the Lantern reads; with it a Forest pays for a blue spell, which resolves;
without it the spell is not offered; Frantic Search draws two, asks for two discards from the new
hand, asks for up to three lands, and untaps them. The compile test that held Greedy Rummage refused
now holds its reversed order refused and its loot-first order read.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught.

    engine tests: 5,771, all passing (merged with the other session's D1081)

Coverage: 14,641 to 14,655 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 36,230 to 36,246 of 59,888
lines, against 9143dbc.

## D780 — An attack tax: Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Windborn Muse

Most-played order: Propaganda (rank 110) and Ghostly Prison (160), Windborn Muse after them. "Creatures
can't attack you unless their controller pays {2} for each creature they control that's attacking
you." Unread, so these cards did nothing, and in Commander they are among the most played defences.

- `lineScriptFor` reads the line as `CardScript.attackTax` (the number).
- `attackTaxFor` (`legalActions.ts`): what a declaration costs its player. For each creature
  attacking a player (not a planeswalker), the sum of that player's taxing permanents. Face-down and
  ability-less permanents tax nothing.
- `declareAttackers` pays it before anything is tapped for the attack (CR 508.1h), from the attacking
  player's mana and never with the attackers' own mana abilities. Unpayable, the declaration is
  refused ("attacking there costs {4}, and you cannot pay it") and nothing is spent.
- A creature that must attack is not owed when every player it could attack charges a tax
  (CR 508.1d).
- The bot: `legalDeclaration` ends with `affordableAttack`, which drops the weakest attacker aimed at
  a taxed player until the rest can be paid for. Without it the bot's search threw the whole plan
  away as illegal and attacked with nothing; with it, it attacks with what it can afford.

Not yet: the table does not show the cost before you declare; an attack you cannot pay for is
refused with the amount, and you declare again. "Or planeswalkers you control" variants are not read.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests: the card reads; one attacker is paid for from the lands and attacks; two
need {4}, and with two lands the declaration is refused with the amount; no tax without the
enchantment or for declaring nothing; the bot at a 4-life player with three 2/2s and two lands
attacks with exactly one. The deck-coverage test lists `script attackTax`.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 5 caught, one after the bot test was sharpened (one attacker, not at
most one). The fifth rebuilt the seats from the state before the payment; mana is held in
`state.pools`, not on the seats, so a mana-only tax changes nothing it could lose.

    engine tests: 5,780, all passing (merged with the other session's D1082)

Coverage: 14,669 to 14,672 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 36,261 to 36,265 of 59,888
lines, against 7e3780f. Small in count and large in play: these are two of the most-played defences
in Commander.

## D1083 — mana and life from one ability

"{T}: Add {G}{G}. You gain 2 life." (The Great Henge) and the other mana lines with a life sentence
after the mana.

- A mana line's tail may now be "You gain N life" (`ManaLine.gains`), beside a pain land's damage
  (D497) and the depletion-free duals' freeze (D920).
- It is part of the mana ability's effect, so it resolves immediately with no stack and no window
  (CR 605.3a). `painEffect` applies all three. Every return of the mana-line parser carries it, and
  the sum path passes it too.

**Tests.** 1 engine test: the line reads whole, and tapping adds {G}{G} and gains 2 life with
nothing on the stack.

Faults injected by script: 3. All are caught.

Coverage: 14,684 of 31,900 cards (+2 over the baseline measured after merging D780), 36,283 of
59,888 lines.
## D781 — Channel lands: Boseiju and Otawara (and an ability that costs less)

Most-played order: Boseiju, Who Endures (rank 78) and Otawara, Soaring City (89), with Eiganjo after
them. Channel itself has read since D582; four smaller readers stood between these cards and a full
reading.

- **"Nonbasic" in a target list.** "Target artifact, enchantment, or nonbasic land an opponent
  controls": each part of a listed target was one word. A part may now be several words that must
  all hold, each read by `permanentWordMatch`, which now also reads "non" plus a supertype
  (nonbasic, nonlegendary, nonsnow). A qualifier outside that vocabulary still refuses the list
  ("target tapped Goblin or Elf"). And only supertype words may stand before a part's noun:
  "target Cleric or Wizard creature" shares its trailing noun (a creature that is a Cleric or a
  Wizard), and the first draft, which let any words combine, read it as "a Cleric, or a Wizard
  creature". The gate caught it on D488's refusal row.
- **"That player" after a permanent aimed "… an opponent controls"** is that permanent's controller,
  a new row in the referent table beside "its controller". After a player target the old row is the
  one used.
- **"A land card with a basic land type"**: a land with Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain or Forest
  among its subtypes, typed duals included.
- **"This ability costs {N} less to activate for each <thing>."** 74 legal cards print an ability
  cost reduction; 6 of them with "for each legendary creature you control". `abilityFromLine` takes
  the sentence off the end, reads the rest, and carries the count on the ability
  (`AbilityDef.costLess`), counted by `forEachCount` as the spells' "costs less for each" is.
  `abilityManaText` is the cost as paid now: the generic part reduced, never below zero. It is what
  `legalActions` offers and shows, and what `activate` pays.

Takenuma and Sokenzan still need their effects ("mill three, then return a creature or planeswalker
card", "two 1/1 Spirits that gain haste").

**Tests.** 4 engine tests: both cards read whole; Otawara is not offered off two Islands with no
legend, and with two legendary creatures it is offered at {1}{U}; at that cost it returns the
creature and goes to the graveyard; Boseiju cannot target a basic Forest, destroys a nonbasic dual,
and its controller is asked for a land with a basic land type and gets it. (Two different legends:
two of one name would lose one to the legend rule, which the first draft of the test found.)

Faults injected by script: 7 of 7 caught (the trailing-noun guard's after the gate found it).

    engine tests: 5,784, all passing (on 6c20ae0)

Coverage: 14,683 to 14,709 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 36,283 to 36,313 of 59,888
lines, against 6c20ae0.

## D1084 — "if you created a token this turn"

"{T}: Draw a card. Activate only if you created a token this turn." (Idol of Oblivion), one of the
EDHREC-queue cards this session claimed.

- **Engine:** `GameState.tokensCreatedThisTurn`, per seat. `addTokens` counts every token it makes
  for the seat that created them, and the record is cleared with the rest of the turn's facts.
  `turnFacts.tokensCreated` reads it.
- The intervening-condition vocabulary reads "you created a token this turn" and "you've created a
  token this turn", so activation limits, trigger conditions and cost conditions all have it.

**Tests.** 1 engine test: the Idol reads whole; activating it is refused before a token, allowed
after a Soldier token is made, and refused again on the next turn.

Faults injected by script: 3. All are caught.

of 59,888 lines.
## D782 — Return a card from your graveyard, chosen; and Command Beacon

Most-played order: Takenuma, Abandoned Mire (rank 246) and Command Beacon (183).

- **An untargeted return from your graveyard**: "(You may) return a / an / up to one <kind> card from
  your graveyard to your hand". 44 not-yet-automated cards print it. Chosen as it resolves, from the
  cards of that kind (the search vocabulary, `libraryFilter`). Without "may" or "up to" one is taken
  if any can be, and with exactly one the engine takes it without asking. In "Mill three cards, then
  return …" the composition runs the mill first, so a card milled by the same resolution can be the
  one returned. Takenuma, Grapple with the Past and Corpse Churn read whole.
- **"Put your commander into your hand from the command zone"**: Command Beacon. Every commander of
  yours in your command zone (both, with partners).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests: both cards read; the spell mills three and returns the creature from the
graveyard; a creature milled by the same spell can be the one returned; with nothing of the kind it
still resolves; Command Beacon puts the commander from the command zone into the hand.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught.

    engine tests: 5,790, all passing (merged with the other session's D1083)

## D783 — Mana that makes a spell uncounterable: Cavern of Souls, Delighted Halfling

Most-played order: Cavern of Souls (rank 113), Delighted Halfling (146). "Spend this mana only to cast
<…>, and that spell can't be countered."

- `spendRestriction` reads the rider: the restriction before it as it always was, marked
  `uncounterable`.
- `payFrom` now returns its `picks`, what each source tapped for the payment made.
- `castSpell`: the spell can't be countered when a source tapped for it made a type its
  uncounterable row makes, and that row's restriction allows this spell (Cavern's chosen creature
  type included). A source whose unrestricted row made the mana does not count: Cavern's {C}, or a
  free {G} paying for a nonlegendary spell. The stack object carries `cantBeCountered`, the flag
  "This spell can't be countered" already sets. Mana tapped by hand earlier and left floating is not
  traced back to its source.

**A bug found on the way.** `foldManaLines` (`fromCardData.ts`) merges a card's mana lines into one
set of rows for a card it reads whole, and kept only the first line's details. A restricted line
after a free one (Delighted Halfling's "{T}: Add {C}" then its restricted "any color") came out with
no restriction: mana that pays for anything. A line with a spending restriction now sends the card
to the line-by-line reader, which keeps it, as it already did for the pain lands' damage (D497).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests: both cards read; a legendary spell paid with the Halfling's any-color mana
can't be countered; its {C} paying for an artifact does nothing of the kind; a free {G} paying for a
nonlegendary spell does not make it uncounterable, while the same source paying for a legendary one
does; Cavern with Elf chosen makes an Elf uncounterable and its {C} paying for an artifact does not.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught, one after the free-{G} test was added.

    engine tests: 5,795, all passing (on 48cefc1)

Coverage: 14,721 to 14,723 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 36,327 to 36,329 of 59,888
lines, against 48cefc1. Few in count; the fold fix also stops a restricted line paying for anything.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught.

## D785 — "That much life", the additional card, everyone's extra land

Most-played order: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose (rank 490), Sanguine Bond (507), Howling Mine (719),
then Rites of Flourishing (1527), Kami of the Crescent Moon (1808), Dictate of Kruphix (1864), Font of
Mythos (2181) and Ghirapur Orrery (2613), which share their lines.

- **"Whenever you gain life, target opponent / each opponent loses that much life."** The life-gained
  event now carries how much (`amount`): what the gain added to the turn's record of gains, or the
  rise in the life total where nothing was recorded. "That much" reads it the way Exquisite Blood's
  life-lost trigger does (D999). Exquisite Blood plus either one is the familiar two-card loop; it
  runs through the stack one trigger at a time, so each lap is visible and the table can stop it.
- **"That player draws an additional card"** (and "two additional cards"): a draw-step trigger whose
  draw is ordinary. The referent swap hands the reader "target player draws …", so the reader takes
  that form too. Howling Mine's "if ~ is untapped" was already read.
- **"Each player may play an additional land on each of their turns."** `CardScript.additionalLandsEach`,
  added to every seat's land drops by `landDropsFor` while the permanent is on any battlefield with its
  abilities.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests: the cards read; gaining 3 makes each opponent lose 3, and with the
enchantment gone the opponent loses nothing; the targeted version takes 3 from the chosen opponent;
the opponent draws 2 in their draw step with the Mine out, 3 with the Font, 1 with neither; with
Rites out both players get a second land drop on their own turns, and without it one.

Faults injected by script: 6 of 6 caught.

## D786 — The reveal lands

Most-played order: Choked Estuary (rank 293), Foreboding Ruins (317), Frostboil Snarl (332), Port
Town (333), Game Trail (400), Shineshadow Snarl (420) and the rest of their cycles, with Lorwyn's
tribal lands ("you may reveal a Goblin card") after them: 18 legal printings.

"As ~ enters, you may reveal an Island or Swamp card from your hand. If you don't, ~ enters tapped."
is read as `entersUntappedIf` (D587), asking whether a card of either kind is in its controller's
hand as the land arrives. The reveal is taken whenever it can be: it costs nothing and shows a card
that was going to be seen anyway. The land row says why when it would enter tapped ("enters tapped:
no Island or Swamp card in your hand to reveal"), and the bot's land choice, which already asks the
same question of check lands, prefers the land that will arrive untapped.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests: the cards read; with an Island in hand the land enters untapped and its
row says nothing extra, with only a Mountain it enters tapped and the row says why, and a second copy
of itself is not an Island; a Goblin in hand untaps the Goblin land and a Mountain does not; put onto
the battlefield by an effect, it asks the hand all the same.

Faults injected by script: 2 of 3 caught. The miss removes the guard that skips the land itself; it
is an equivalent fault, since none of these lands has a land type of its own to reveal.

## D787 — An opponent's permanents enter tapped

Most-played order: Authority of the Consuls (rank 299), Blind Obedience (511), Thalia, Heretic
Cathar (1485), Urabrask the Hidden (1815), Archon of Emeria's second line (2153), Manglehorn (2405),
Kinjalli's Sunwing (3400) and the rest: "Creatures your opponents control enter tapped", "Artifacts
and creatures …", "Creatures and nonbasic lands …", "Artifacts, creatures, and lands …".

`CardScript.opponentsEnterTapped` lists the kinds. As any permanent arrives, every other seat's
battlefield is asked for a permanent that still has its abilities and names one of its kinds; if one
does, it arrives tapped, by the same replacement and at the same moment as "enters tapped" (CR
614.1c). Its controller's own permanents are untouched, and a basic land is not a nonbasic land.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests: the cards read; the opponent's creature enters tapped, the controller's
own does not, an artifact does not under "creatures", and with no Authority nothing does, nor with
an Authority that has lost its abilities; a creature cast and resolved arrives tapped; under Thalia a
nonbasic land played enters tapped and a basic does not; "artifacts and creatures" taps both, and
nothing once it has left.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught (the lost-abilities test was added after the first run
missed that fault).

    engine tests: 5,812, all passing (on e906c2b)
