## D788 — Casting limits: Grand Abolisher, Teferi, Rule of Law, Deafening Silence, Dosan

Most-played order: Grand Abolisher (rank 254), Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar's first line (397), Voice of
Victory (481), Teferi, Time Raveler's static (1129), Myrel (1541), Dragonlord Dromoka (1886),
Deafening Silence (1959), Rule of Law (3465), Eidolon of Rhetoric (3600), Dosan (6273), High Noon,
Moderation and the rest: 20 legal printings across seven lines.

`CardScript.castLimits` names the limit; `castProhibition` asks every live one on the table where a
cast is offered and again where it is made, so the two cannot disagree, and the refusal names the
permanent ("Test Rule: no more than one spell each turn").

- **One spell each turn** for each player (Rule of Law, Eidolon of Rhetoric, High Noon), for its
  controller only (Moderation, Yawgmoth's Agenda), and **one noncreature spell** (Deafening
  Silence), counted from the turn's cast record the storm count already keeps.
- **Spells only during your own turn** (Dosan), for every player.
- **Opponents only at sorcery speed** (Teferi, Time Raveler). A cast an effect makes mid-resolution
  (cascade) is not timed by its caster, so Teferi does not stop it; the one-spell limits still count
  it.
- **Opponents cast nothing during your turn** (Dragonlord Dromoka, Voice of Victory, Kutzil), and
  Grand Abolisher's and Myrel's second half: **no abilities of the opponents' artifacts, creatures
  or enchantments** during its controller's turn, mana abilities included, refused where offered and
  where activated (`abilityProhibition`). Lands' abilities are untouched, as printed.

Not done: the payment tapper is not yet told about Grand Abolisher, so paying for a land's ability on the Abolisher's turn could still tap an artifact for mana (the only thing left the opponent can pay for then). Also not done: Ethersworn Canonist's "nonartifact" count (the turn's record counts creature and
noncreature, not artifact), Fires of Invention's two-spell limit, and Teferi's +1.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests: the cards read; under Rule of Law a second spell of any kind is neither
offered nor accepted, and without it two are; under Deafening Silence creatures keep coming after
the one noncreature spell; under Teferi the opponent's instant is refused in our main phase and
accepted without him, while his controller's is offered, the opponent casts it in their own main
phase, and his controller casts an instant on the opponent's turn; under Grand Abolisher the opponent can neither cast nor use an artifact's ability on our turn,
can do both without it, and on their own turn the artifact works again and the spell is accepted; under Dosan the opponent is
refused on our turn and we are not.

Faults injected by script: 9 of 9 caught. The first run missed two (Teferi reaching his own
controller, and Abolisher's spell half reaching the opponent's own turn); a test for each was added
and both were then caught.

    engine tests: 5,818, all passing (on 4f909e1)

Coverage: 14,768 to 14,780 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 36,386 to 36,406 of 59,888
lines, against 4f909e1.

## D1085–D1087 — Reflecting Pool, Mox Amber, Mithril Coat

Three EDHREC-queue cards this session claimed, each a small extension of a shape the engine
already had.

- **D1085, "one mana of any type (or color) that a land you control could produce":** Reflecting
  Pool, Naga Vitalist, Incubation Druid, Horizon of Progress, Cactus Preserve, Harvester Druid.
  `ownLandTypes` asks the Fellwar Stone question (D681) of your own lands, colourless included.
  Each type's ability is offered only while a land you control could make that type; the "color"
  wording leaves out {C}. The land scan both directions use is now one function, `landManaInto`.
  Abilities of the same kind are skipped (CR 106.7), so a Reflecting Pool beside nothing but
  another Reflecting Pool makes nothing.
- **D1086, "one mana of any color among legendary creatures and planeswalkers / legendary
  permanents you control":** Mox Amber, Plaza of Heroes. `legendaryColours` reads live
  characteristics. Colourless legends give nothing, so a Mox Amber alone makes no mana.
- **D1087, "When ~ enters, attach it to target legendary creature you control":** Mithril Coat,
  Mjolnir. This is the D972 attach-on-arrival with its target filter narrowed to legendary
  creatures you control.

**Tests.** 9 engine tests:
- D1085: Pool and Harvester read whole. Tapped lands count, and {C} counts only for "type".
  Nothing comes from an opponent's lands, from a mana creature, or from another Pool.
- D1086: both wordings read whole. A legendary enchantment's colour counts for the Plaza and not
  the Mox. Nothing comes from an opponent's legend, or with no legend.
- D1087: the Coat reads whole. It attaches to the legend with its bonus, and with only a
  non-legendary creature it stays unattached.

Faults injected by hand: 2 (the legendary filter dropped; the Mox's creature/planeswalker
restriction dropped). Both are caught.

Coverage: 14,716 of 31,900 cards (+6 over D1084's 14,710), 36,319 of 59,888 lines (+9).

## D1088 — mana added when a permanent is tapped for mana: Wild Growth, Crypt Ghast

"Whenever enchanted land is tapped for mana, its controller adds an additional {G}" (Wild Growth,
Wolfwillow Haven; Overgrowth's {G}{G}; Utopia Sprawl's "one mana of the chosen color"), and
"Whenever you tap a Swamp / Forest / creature / land for mana, add an additional {B}" (Crypt Ghast,
Nirkana Revenant, Nissa, Who Shakes the World, Leyline of Abundance, Badgermole Cub, Autumn
Willow). Wild Growth was the last of this session's EDHREC claims.

- **Engine:**
  - `CardScript.tapManaExtra` records what is watched (the enchanted permanent, or a kind of
    permanent its controller controls) and what is added (fixed mana, or the chosen colour).
  - `tapManaExtras(state, tapped)` is the one reader. Its watchers are found once per state.
  - A triggered mana ability resolves with the tap (CR 605.3b), so the mana is folded into the tap
    on every path: the auto-tapper's sources, an ability pressed by hand, and the dimmed pips.
- **Solver:** `ManaSource.extra` carries mana a choice source adds beside its choice, so a dual
  land under Wild Growth is one of its colours plus {G}, and one land pays {U}{G}. A colour that
  only the extra makes still makes the source useful for that colour.
- **Not taken:**
  - "An additional one mana of any color" (Fertile Ground and five more). It is a second choice on
    the tap, which the solver does not make, so the line stays unread rather than guessed.
  - "One mana of any type that land produced" (Zendikar Resurgent, Mirari's Wake, Vorinclex).
  - Gauntlet of Power's and Rikala's conditional extras.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- Each wording reads whole, and "any color" stays unread.
- A Forest under it is {G}{G} in the sources, the pips, and when pressed by hand. Overgrowth makes
  {G}{G}{G}.
- A dual under it is a choice plus {G}: it pays {U}{G} and {2} but not {U}{B}.
- Crypt Ghast doubles your Swamps, not a Forest and not an opponent's Swamp.
- An Aura on an opponent's land gives you nothing.

The chosen-colour branch (Utopia Sprawl) is read and covered by the reading test only. It adds
nothing until the Aura has chosen a colour.

Faults injected by hand: 2. The first drops the extra mana from a choice source's pick in the solver; the second drops it from an ability pressed by hand. Both are caught.

Coverage: 14,722 of 31,900 cards (+6 over D1085–D1087's 14,716), 36,330 of 59,888 lines (+11).

## D1089 — the Backgrounds: "Commander creatures you own have …"

The Background enchantments (Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur's Gate) all print one static:
"Commander creatures you own have "<ability>"" or "… get +N/+N and have …". 28 legal cards are a
single line short on it.

- **Engine:**
  - A new static scope, `commander-creatures`. It reaches a creature that is a commander and that
    the Background's controller **owns**, whoever controls it now. A commander an opponent has
    stolen keeps the gift, and your other creatures get nothing.
  - `effectApplies` reads it live, like every other group scope.
- **Reader:** the line joins the group-static reader beside "Creature tokens you control …". Its
  predicate goes through the existing grammar: a pump, keywords, a quoted trigger or a quoted
  activated ability.

Four Backgrounds now read whole: Flaming Fist, Candlekeep Sage, Far Traveler and Clan Crafter. The
other 24 are short only because their quoted ability does not read on its own yet. Examples are
"Whenever this creature attacks a player, if no opponent has more life than that player …" (five
of them) and a quoted static such as "Creature tokens you control get +2/+2".

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both shapes read whole.
- The quoted trigger reaches your commander, but not your other creature or an opponent's
  commander.
- The pump reaches your commander only, and still does once an opponent controls it.

Faults injected by hand: 2 (the owner test changed to a controller test; the commander test
dropped). Both are caught.

Coverage: 14,796 of 31,900 cards and 36,429 of 59,888 lines, measured after merging D782–D788 (that merge's own baseline was not measured separately; the four Backgrounds above are the cards this reads whole).

Two pieces that five Backgrounds share inside their quoted grants: "Whenever this creature attacks
a player, if no [other] opponent has more life than that player, …".

- **Trigger:** a new prologue row, "Whenever ~ attacks a player,". It sets `atPlayer` on the
  `attacks` event, and `triggerMatches` refuses an attack declared against a planeswalker.
- **Condition:** the intervening if "no (other) opponent has more life than that player". It is
  read off `c.attacked`, which both asks of an intervening if already carry (CR 603.4). The
  attacked player must have at least as much life as every opponent still in the game, and an
  attack on a planeswalker answers no.

Guild Artisan and Sword Coast Sailor now read whole. Veteran Soldier, Hardy Outlander and Agent of
the Shadow Thieves still have effect clauses that do not read.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- The line reads whole on a creature and inside a Background's grant.
- In a three-player pod, attacking the richer opponent makes two Treasures, and attacking the
  poorer one makes none.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the life comparison always true). It is caught.

Coverage: 14,798 of 31,900 cards (+2 over D1089's 14,796), 36,431 of 59,888 lines (+2).

## D1091 — "Partner with <name>": the enter trigger that fetches the partner

"Partner with <name>" is two things (CR 702.124j). The deck-construction half has been
`partnersLegally`'s since D640. The game half is the reminder text's enter trigger: "When this
creature enters, target player may search their library for a card named <name>, reveal it, put
it into their hand, then shuffle." D670 left the line unread because nothing read that trigger.

- **Reader:** `compileCard` gives that sentence, with the card's name and its partner's, to the
  line reader. The line reader reads every word of it already (D986's search by name), so the
  keyword and its printed reminder cannot disagree. It is the backup and embalm pattern: a keyword
  read as the sentence it stands for.
- 52 legal lines print it (26 pairs). Partner was the commonest unimplemented keyword among cards
  one line short: 16 of them.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The pair reads whole, reminder text included.
- Aimed at yourself, only the named partner is offered from your library, and it goes to your hand.
- Aimed at the opponent, the question is theirs.

The D670 compile row that pinned "Partner with" as unread is retargeted (the D516 way). It now
asserts that the line reads as one enter trigger.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the card's own name searched for instead of its partner's). It is
caught.

Coverage: 14,814 of 31,900 cards (+16 over D1090's 14,798), 36,483 of 59,888 lines (+52).

## D1092 — typed equip: "Equip legendary creature {3}", "Equip Human {1}"

"Equip [quality] {N}" (CR 702.6e) is an equip ability whose target must have the quality. It is
usually printed beside an ordinary, dearer equip: Blackblade Reforged's "Equip legendary creature
{3}" and "Equip {7}". 20 legal cards print one. Before this, the ordinary line was read and the
typed one left unread.

- **Reader:** each typed line becomes its own equip ability, the main one's twin with its own cost
  and quality. A card that prints only a typed equip (Excalibur, Sword of Eden) has it as its one
  equip ability.
- **Qualities:** "legendary creature" (the live supertype), "commander", "creature token", and one
  or more creature types ("Human", "Shaman, Warlock, or Wizard"). Mjolnir's "worthy" is not a
  quality the engine has, so it stays unread.
- `equipFragment` takes the quality. It narrows the target filter and names the quality in the
  description.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The cards read whole, with two equip abilities on the card that prints two.
- The Human equip reaches a Human for {1} and refuses the Bear, and the ordinary equip takes
  either.
- A card with only a legendary equip refuses non-legendary creatures and equips a legend.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the legendary test always true). It is caught.

Coverage: 14,825 of 31,900 cards (+11 over D1091's 14,814), 36,503 of 59,888 lines (+20).

## D1093 — graft, and moving a +1/+1 counter

Graft N (CR 702.58a): "This creature enters with N +1/+1 counters on it. Whenever another creature
enters, you may move a +1/+1 counter from this creature onto it." 13 legal lines, 10 of them on
cards that were a single keyword short.

- **Engine:** `moveCounter(state, from, to, key)`. It does nothing unless the source has such a
  counter and both are on the battlefield. **Moving is not putting** (CR 122.6), so the counters
  are edited directly, not through `addCounters`. Hardened Scales and Doubling Season, which
  replace counters being put on a permanent, do not change how many arrive.
- **Reader:** the event-relative sentence "move a +1/+1 counter from ~ onto it", on "whenever
  another creature enters", where "it" is the creature that entered. The graft keyword reads as
  its two sentences, as "Partner with" does (D1091).

Five graft cards now read whole: Aquastrand Spider, Cytoplast Manipulator, Cytospawn Shambler,
Simic Initiate and Plaxcaster Frogling.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Graft reads whole, with its reminder text.
- It enters with two counters, and a creature that enters after it takes one.
- Under Hardened Scales it enters with three, and the moved counter is still just one.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the move made through `addCounters`, so Scales adds to it). It is
caught.

Coverage: 14,835 of 31,900 cards (+10 over D1092's 14,825), 36,516 of 59,888 lines (+13).

## D1094 — champion

"Champion a Goblin" (CR 702.72a): "When this enters, sacrifice it unless you exile another Goblin
you control. When this leaves the battlefield, that card returns to the battlefield under its
owner's control." 12 legal cards, 10 of them a single keyword short.

- **Engine:** `championTriggers(kinds, words)` returns two triggers.
  - The enter trigger asks for up to one other creature of the kind you control. It is a
    **choice, not a target**, so a hexproof creature may be championed. The chosen card is exiled
    with `exileUntilLeaves`, the link Banisher Priest uses. Choosing nothing, or having nothing to
    choose, sacrifices the champion.
  - The leave trigger is the same `returnExiledBy`.
  - The computer champions its weakest candidate.
- **Reader:** "Champion a creature", "Champion a Goblin" and "Champion a Treefolk or Warrior". A
  word that is neither "creature" nor a creature type stays unread.

Seven now read whole: Boggart Mob, the three Changelings, Wren's Run Packmaster, Lightning Crafter
and Unstoppable Ash. Mistbind Clique's own "when a Faerie is championed" trigger is still unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- It reads whole, with its reminder text.
- Only another Goblin is offered, a hexproof one included. It is exiled, and it comes back when
  the champion leaves.
- With no other Goblin, or choosing none, the champion is sacrificed.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the return removed). It is caught.

Coverage: 14,845 of 31,900 cards (+10 over D1093's 14,835), 36,528 of 59,888 lines (+12).

## D1095 — kicked halves with targets of their own, and "if this spell wasn't kicked"

D562 read a kicker spell's two halves when they shared one list of targets. It refused a kicked
half with targets of its own ("If this spell was kicked, tap target creature an opponent
controls") and an "instead" that points elsewhere ("instead return target nonland permanent"),
because "a script has one list of targets whether it was kicked or not".

The kicker is announced before targets (CR 601.2b-c), and modes already make the target list
depend on an announced choice. So such a spell is now **two modes the kicker picks**:

- `ModalDef.kickerModes`. With `instead`, the unkicked cast is mode 0 and the kicked cast is
  mode 1. With `also`, the kicked cast is both modes, in printed order.
- `modeCombinations` returns the one combination the kicker allows. `legalActions` offers the
  kicked cast through the row entwine already uses, so the plain and kicked casts each ask for
  their own targets.
- A half becomes a mode only when it holds nothing but targets, questions and an effect, so
  nothing either half read is dropped.
- "If this spell wasn't kicked, <effect>" (Nocturnal Hunger, Archival Whorl): the effect runs only
  on the unkicked cast, after the base. It must be an effect only.

This is the groundwork for gift (D1096). Rewritten as kicker, seven of the 27 gift cards read once
this is in.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- All three shapes read whole.
- "Instead": the plain cast reaches only creatures, the kicked cast any nonland permanent, and the
  artifact is returned.
- "Also": the kicked cast asks for and taps the extra target, and the plain cast only draws.
- "Wasn't kicked": the life is lost only on the plain cast.

Two rows of D562's refusal table now read and are retargeted (the D516 way) into a positive test:
the Tear Asunder shape and the "different restriction" shape. It asserts two modes with different
targets, picked by the kicker.

Faults injected by hand: 1 ("also" given only the kicked mode). It is caught.

Coverage: 14,850 of 31,900 cards (+5 over D1094's 14,845), 36,538 of 59,888 lines (+10).

## D1096 — gift, on the kicker's machinery

Gift (CR 702.174, Bloomburrow): "Gift a card (You may promise an opponent a gift as you cast this
spell. If you do, they draw a card before its other effects.)". The spell's text then asks "if the
gift was promised". 27 legal cards. To the rules of casting it is a kicker: a choice announced
with the spell that its text reads later.

- **Reader:** `giftSpellFor`, on instants and sorceries. The declaration becomes a free kicker
  (`{0}`) marked `gift`, "the gift was promised" becomes "this spell was kicked", and the whole
  card must then read through the kicker readers (D562, D1095). The gift is given first, as the
  spell resolves: before the effect, or before the mode the promised cast runs first.
- **Gifts:** a card (they draw), a tapped 1/1 blue Fish, a Food, a Treasure, an 8/8 blue Octopus.
  "An extra turn" and the rest stay unread.
- **The opponent:** with one opponent there is nothing to choose. In a pod the caster is asked as
  the spell resolves, and only when the gift was promised (`askOnlyIf`, now on choice questions
  too). The rules ask at casting; nothing between the two can change the answer, since the gift is
  not a target.
- **Not a kicker:** the cast event's `kicked` is false for a promised gift, so cards that watch
  "a kicked spell" do not fire for it.

Seven gift cards now read whole: Consumed by Greed, Into the Flood Maw, Long River's Pull, Mind
Spiral, Nocturnal Hunger, Peerless Recycling and Wildfire Howl. Permanents with gift (Scrapshooter,
Starforged Sword, Kitnap) need the gift given on the permanent's side and are not read yet.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The card reads whole and is offered as two casts.
- Promised, the opponent draws and no life is lost. Not promised, you lose 2 life.
- On an "instead" spell, the gift comes with the kicked mode: the opponent draws and the artifact
  is returned.
- In a pod the caster names the opponent, and only that one draws.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the gift dropped from the modal path). It is caught.

Coverage: 14,857 of 31,900 cards (+7 over D1095's 14,850), 36,552 of 59,888 lines (+14).

## D1097 — impending: the Duskmourn Overlords

"Impending 4—{2}{W}{W} (If you cast this spell for its impending cost, it enters with four time
counters and isn't a creature until the last is removed. At the beginning of your end step, remove
a time counter from it.)" (CR 702.176a). The five Overlords are Commander staples, and three of
them were short only this keyword.

- **Engine:** an alternative cost, `impended`, on prototype's path (D934): offered as its own row
  in `legalActions`, validated with the other alternative costs, and carried on the stack object.
  As the permanent arrives, it gets N time counters and the `IMPENDED` marker, where evoke writes
  its marker.
- **The type:** a self static with `removeTypes: ['Creature']`, the Theros gods' layer-4 removal
  (D657). Its condition is `source-has-counter` on time counters with the new `alsoCounter:
  IMPENDED`, so only an impended permanent with a time counter is not a creature. One that was
  cast for its full cost never is, whatever counters it later gets.
- **The countdown:** the keyword's own trigger, "at the beginning of your end step, remove a time
  counter from it", skipped when there is none.

Overlord of the Mistmoors, Floodpits and Boilerbilges now read whole. Hauntwoods and Balemurk are
short on their enters-or-attacks lines.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- It reads whole, and both casts are offered.
- Impended, it has two time counters and is not a creature. It has one after your end step, and
  after your next one it has none and is a creature.
- Cast for its printed cost, it is a creature at once, with no counters.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the marker not written, so it stays a creature). It is caught.

Coverage: 14,860 of 31,900 cards (+3 over D1096's 14,857), 36,557 of 59,888 lines (+5).

## D1098 — land tokens, and "a non-Avatar creature card"

The last two Overlords after D1097: Overlord of the Hauntwoods ("create a tapped colorless land
token named Everywhere that is every basic land type") and Overlord of the Balemurk ("… you may
return a non-Avatar creature card or a planeswalker card from your graveyard to your hand").

- **Land tokens**, in the three printed shapes:
  - "create a Forest land token" (Generated Horizons);
  - Everywhere;
  - "create a tapped Planet land token named New Planet with "{T}: Add one mana of any color."",
    the Doctor Who Anomalies.

  A basic land type gives the token its mana (CR 305.6), and a quoted ability is the token's text,
  read the way a Treasure's is. 12 legal lines.
- **"Non-<Subtype>" in a card filter:** "a non-Avatar creature card", "a non-Human creature card".
  The battlefield readers have read this shape since D453, and the card-filter reader now does
  too. 10 legal lines.

Overlord of the Hauntwoods, Overlord of the Balemurk, Generated Horizons and Stable Wormhole now
read whole, so all five Overlords do. The other Planet cards are short on other lines.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- All four read whole.
- Everywhere arrives tapped as a land with all five basic land types, and taps for any colour once
  untapped.
- A Planet token taps for any colour, and a Forest token is a Forest token.
- From the graveyard, the Bear is offered and the Avatar is not.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the subtype not negated). It is caught.

Coverage: 14,869 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1097's 14,860), 36,566 of 59,888 lines (+9).

## D1099 — a double kicker, and two target questions at once

**Double kicker** (CR 702.32b): "Kicker {B} and/or {R}". Either, both or neither may be paid, and
the card asks which. 18 legal cards. Archangel of Wrath is the Commander one.

- **Engine:**
  - `kicker.second` holds the second cost.
  - The cast offers three kicked plays (either kicker, or both) beside the printed one, and the
    choice travels as `kickedWith` on the play, the action and the stack object. The cost is the
    printed one plus the kickers chosen.
  - As the permanent arrives, it gets `KICKED` as before, plus `KICKED_FIRST` and/or
    `KICKED_SECOND`.
  - `kickerEntersWith` adds each paid kicker's counters and keywords.
- **Reader:** `doubleKickerShapeFor`. Every kicker line must be one of:
  - "When ~ enters, if it was kicked with its {X} kicker, …" (the Battlemages);
  - "If ~ was kicked with its {X} kicker, it enters with N +1/+1 counters on it and with …" (the
    volvers);
  - "When ~ enters, if it was kicked [twice], …" (Archangel of Wrath).

  Each condition is an intervening if on the markers.

Archangel of Wrath, Sunscape, Thornscape, Thunderscape, Stormscape and Nightscape Battlemage, and
Cetavolver now read whole. The other volvers grant quoted abilities the keyword list does not read.
Spells with a double kicker (Illuminate, Temporal Firestorm), Wastescape's cast trigger and "for
each time it was kicked" are not read yet.

**A fix, found by this increment's test.** When two triggers that each want targets went on the
stack together, the second's `pendingChoice` **replaced** the first's. The first then resolved
aimed at nothing, silently. Archangel of Wrath kicked twice dealt 2 damage, not 4. Now
`pendingChoice.queued` keeps the waiting questions: `withTargetQuestion` puts a new question in
front of them, and `nextTargetQuestion` asks the next one once an answer is given (or once an
unaimable one is removed). It applies to any card with two targeted enters triggers, not only
kicker.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- Three cards read whole, and four casts are offered.
- "Kicked" and "kicked twice": no hit unkicked, one for either kicker, two for both.
- "With its {W} kicker" runs only that kicker's line.
- The volver gets each paid kicker's counters and keyword.
- Two targeted enters triggers each get their question.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the queue never asked). Two tests catch it.

The D561 compile row that pinned "Kicker {2} and/or {1}{R}" as unread is retargeted (the D516 way). It now asserts that the line reads as a double kicker with its second cost.

Coverage: 14,876 of 31,900 cards (+7 over D1098's 14,869), 36,587 of 59,888 lines (+21).

## D1100 — multikicker, and "for each time it was kicked"

Multikicker (CR 702.33a): "Multikicker {2}" may be paid any number of times, and the card counts
the kicks. 19 legal lines. Everflowing Chalice is the Commander one.

- **Engine:** `kicker.multi`.
  - The cast offers one kicked play per count the mana covers ("multikicker x1", "x2", …), the way
    replicate offers its rows.
  - The count travels as `kickCount` on the play, the action and the stack object.
  - The `KICKED` marker the arrival writes is now the **count**: a multikicker's, two for both
    kickers of a double kicker (D1099), or one.
- **The count:** "for each time it was kicked" and "the number of times this spell was kicked" are
  in the counting vocabulary. A spell reads its own count off the stack; a permanent reads it off
  `KICKED`. The counted enters-with reader (D1047) no longer excludes the phrase, so "enters with a
  +1/+1 counter on it for each time it was kicked" reads too.
- **The keyword:** "Multikicker {cost}" reads on its own, unlike a kicker (D561). Every printed
  multikicker counts its kicks on another line, and a payoff line that does not read keeps the
  card's badge.

Ten now read whole: Apex Hawks, Enclave Elite, Everflowing Chalice, Flametongue Yearling, Gnarlid
Pack, Lightkeeper of Emeria, Quag Vampires, Skitter of Lizards, Spell Contortion and Wolfbriar
Elemental. "Up to X targets, where X is the number of times …" (Voyager Drake, Comet
Storm) is not read yet.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The cards read whole, and each count the mana covers is offered, no more.
- The Chalice gets a charge counter per kick and taps for that much; unkicked, none.
- A Wolf per kick, and a spell that draws a card per kick.

The D561 row that pinned "Multikicker {1}{G}" as unread is retargeted (the D516 way). It now
asserts that the multikicker reads, while an "if it was kicked" line it does not pair with stays
unread.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the marker written once, not per kick). Two tests catch it.

Coverage: 14,886 of 31,900 cards (+10 over D1099's 14,876), 36,619 of 59,888 lines (+32).

## D1101 — wider Aura hosts, and an Aura that exiles until it leaves

D469 kept an Aura's host to the exact phrases of `targetSpecFrom`'s switch, so that a change to
target phrases could not widen the attachment machinery by accident. These are widened on
purpose, by name (`WIDER_HOSTS`):

- "land you control" and "basic land you control" (Ossification, Dimensional Exile);
- a basic land type, "Enchant Forest" (Utopia Sprawl);
- "artifact you control", "Equipment", "planeswalker";
- compounds of the card types and Vehicle: "artifact or creature" (22 legal lines), "creature or
  Vehicle" (10), "creature or planeswalker", "creature or land".

Each is a kind of permanent an Aura is written onto by `attachedTo` and policed by CR 704.5m
through the same spec, as "Enchant land" always was. It is read with the printed capitals, which
are what make "Forest" a subtype.

**And two shapes on one card.** `wholeCardShapeFor` returned its first match, so an Aura that also
exiles until it leaves (Ossification, Dimensional Exile, Hardlight Containment) had its exile pair
sent to the per-line loop. No single line of that pair is a unit, so it was never read. The exile
shape now reads what the Aura shape left, and the two join with their triggers side by side.

Utopia Sprawl, Ossification, Dimensional Exile, Hardlight Containment and Aether Meltdown now read
whole. Many other Auras with these hosts are short on lines of their own ("As long as enchanted
permanent is a creature, …").

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both cards read whole.
- Only a basic land you control is offered as Ossification's host. Cast, it attaches, the
  opponent's creature is exiled, and it comes back when the Aura goes.
- "Artifact or creature" offers the artifact and the creatures, not a land.

Retargeted (the D516 way):
- D456's four refusals: planeswalker, "artifact or creature", "creature or Vehicle" and "land you
  control" now read as wider hosts.
- D469's exact-phrase row now asserts that "Enchant token", a phrase off both lists, is still
  refused.

Faults injected by hand: 1 (the two shapes not joined). Two tests catch it.

Coverage: 14,907 of 31,900 cards (+21 over D1100's 14,886), 36,709 of 59,888 lines (+90).

## D1102 — kicked halves that refer back to the base

D562 read a kicked clause alone, then joined it to the base. A clause that names the base's
things again ("that creature", "those creatures", "they") does not read alone, so these were
refused:

- "If this spell was kicked, that creature also gains hexproof until end of turn" (Shell Shield;
  the gift's Crumb and Get It).
- "Blooming Blast also deals 3 damage to that creature's controller".
- "those creatures get +2/+1 until end of turn instead" (Dauntless Unity, Marsh Casualties) and
  "they get +1/+1 until end of turn" (Savage Offensive), "those creatures also gain trample"
  (Heroic Charge).
- Gift of Growth: "Untap target creature. It gets +2/+2 until end of turn. If this spell was
  kicked, that creature gets +4/+4 until end of turn instead."

**Read together.** The kicked half is now read with the base, as one text, when it does not read
alone: the base and "That creature gains hexproof until end of turn." The kicked cast runs that
text, the unkicked cast the base. The reading is kept only when it has the base's shape (the
same targets, nothing asked), so one set of targets is announced either way, as the kicker is
announced before targets (CR 601.2b-c). The "also" is dropped first; it says only that the base
still happens.

**"Instead" replaces the sentence before it.** For a base of several sentences, the kicked text is
the base without its last sentence, then the new half. Before this the whole base was replaced, so
a kicked Gift of Growth would have lost its untap; it was refused for a different reason (below),
so no card played that way.

**"Those creatures" and "they"** after a mass effect are named again as the base's subject
("creatures you control", "creatures target player controls").

**Hints out of the shape.** Two halves were compared with the bot's hints included
(`expiresAtEndOfTurn`, a target's `friendly`, `blinks`, `helpsInCombat`), so Colossal Growth's
"+4/+4 and gains trample and haste" did not match its "+3/+3", and the modal fallback refused the
hint. The comparison leaves them out, and a kicker mode carries `expiresAtEndOfTurn`.

Ten cards checked by hand read whole: Colossal Growth, Gift of Growth, Dauntless Unity, Marsh
Casualties, Heroic Charge, Shell Shield, Savage Offensive, Crumb and Get It, Blooming Blast and
Valley Rally. Still refused: Vines of Vastwood ("can't be the target" then "that creature gets"),
and kickers that cost a sacrifice ("Kicker—Sacrifice a creature.", 6 cards).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- All four test spells read whole.
- Gift of Growth's shape, kicked: still untaps, and +4/+4 in place of +2/+2. Unkicked, +2/+2.
- "Those creatures … instead" reaches only the caster's creatures; "they get" adds +1/+1 to the
  first strike.
- "That creature also gains hexproof": one target asked either way, and hexproof only when kicked.

Retargeted (the D516 way): D562's row "a kicked half that refers back without replacing" ("that
creature gets +7/+0") now reads, with one target, in a new test beside the refusals.

Faults injected by hand: 2. The multi-sentence "instead" path turned off (caught by the Gift of
Growth test), and the shape check on the joined reading turned off (caught by D562's "a target of
its own, chosen only when kicked").

Coverage: 14,918 of 31,900 cards (+11 over D1101's 14,907), 36,731 of 59,888 lines (+22).

## D1103 — kickers paid in a sacrifice or in life

Every kicker reader declared "Kicker {cost}" in mana. Eighteen legal cards print a kicker in
something else, after an em dash: "Kicker—Sacrifice a creature." (Vicious Offering),
"Kicker—Sacrifice an artifact or creature." (Final Flourish, Eject the Warp Core, Vayne's
Treachery, Stomped by the Foot), "Kicker—Sacrifice a land." (Rushing River),
"Kicker—{2}{R}, Sacrifice a land." (Dwarven Landslide), "Kicker—Pay 3 life." (Phyrexian Scuta).

**The cost.** CR 702.33a makes a kicker an optional additional cost, so the rest is read by
`additionalCostFromLine`, the reader of "As an additional cost to cast this spell, …". A kicker
can eat exactly what an additional cost can. It rides the kicker as `kicker.additional`, and only
a sacrifice or a life payment is taken.

**The reading.** The declaration is swapped for one of its mana part (`{0}` when there is none)
and the card goes through the kicker readers as before: `costKickerSpellFor` at the start of
`spellScriptFor`, after the gift, and `costKickerPermanentShapeFor` after
`kickerPermanentShapeFor` for a permanent. The printed declaration stays the kicker's
description, so the table's row says "Cast Vicious Offering with kicker—sacrifice a creature".

**The offer and the cast.** A kicked row is offered only when the sacrifice has a permanent to
eat, or the life can be paid (CR 601.2h), and it carries the permanents on `sacrificeOptions`,
the field an additional cost's victims travel on. The bot reads them the way it already does. The
cast takes the kicker's sacrifice and life as the additional cost of the kicked cast only: the
permanent is gone as the spell is cast, before anybody can respond. A card with an additional cost
of its own and a cost kicker is not offered kicked, since one cast carries one sacrifice.

Read whole: Vicious Offering, Final Flourish, Eject the Warp Core, Vayne's Treachery, Stomped by
the Foot, Dwarven Landslide, Rushing River, Primal Growth and Phyrexian Scuta. Still unread:
"Sacrifice two lands" (Bog Down, Magma Burst), "Return a creature you control to its owner's hand"
(Arctic Merfolk), "Discard a creature card" (Dralnu's Pet), "Tap an untapped Vampire you control"
(Blood Tribute), "an artifact or Goblin" (Goblin Barrage), and the cards whose kicked halves do not
read (Falling Timber, Pollen Remedy).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both test cards read whole.
- The kicked cast is offered only with a creature to sacrifice, and it lists that creature.
- Kicked, the creature is in the graveyard as soon as the spell is cast and the target gets
  -5/-5. Unkicked, nothing is eaten and the target gets -2/-2. A kicked cast that names no victim
  is refused.
- A life kicker costs 3 life, and the permanent enters with its counters. Unkicked, neither.

Retargeted (the D516 way): D561's refusal of "Kicker—Sacrifice a land." now reads, in a new test
that checks `additional`. The refusal row keeps two costs nothing can pay ("Return a land you
control to its owner's hand", "Sacrifice two lands").

Faults injected by hand: 2. The offer's sacrifice check turned off (caught by the offer test), and
the cast ignoring the kicker's cost (caught by both cast tests).

Coverage: 14,927 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1102's 14,918), 36,749 of 59,888 lines (+18).

## D1104 — abilities granted in quotes to artifacts and enchantments

A quoted grant ("Creatures you control have "…"") reached creatures (the lord scopes) and, since
D779, lands ("Lands you control have", for Chromatic Lantern). Nothing reached an artifact or an
enchantment that is not a creature, so these were unread:

- Kataki, War's Wage: "All artifacts have "At the beginning of your upkeep, sacrifice this artifact
  unless you pay {1}.""
- Energy Flux: the same at {2}.
- Aura Flux: "Other enchantments have "… sacrifice this enchantment unless you pay {2}.""
- Galazeth Prismari: "Artifacts you control have "{T}: Add one mana of any color. Spend this
  mana only to cast an instant or sorcery spell.""

**Four scopes.** `artifacts-you-control`, `all-artifacts`, `all-enchantments` and
`other-enchantments`, on a static's `scope` and on the continuous effect's, answered by
`effectApplies` off the printed type line: on the battlefield, of the type, and the controller's or
not the source where the words say so. The grant machinery is the creature lords' (`grants` and
`grantsAbilities`, indices into `grantedTriggers` and `grantedAbilities`). `grantedTriggersOn` and
the trigger loop were already asked of every permanent, so nothing else changed.

**Whose ability.** CR 113.6 makes a granted ability the holder's, which is what Kataki needs: "your
upkeep" in the quote is the upkeep of the artifact's controller, so each player pays for their own
artifacts, and "this artifact" is the holder. The upkeep tax is D529's, with its rule that a seat
who cannot pay is not asked.

The reader is `lineScriptFor`'s, beside the land grant. A trigger is tried first, then an
activated ability. Still unread: Food Fight's quote, which names its grantor (D511's guard), and
Mm'menon's "spend this mana only to cast a spell from anywhere other than your hand".

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both test cards read whole.
- An opponent's Kataki taxes your artifact in your upkeep. Paid, it stays.
- With no mana the artifact goes, and the creature beside it is never asked.
- "Artifacts you control have "{T}: Add {C}."": your artifact is a mana source, the opponent's is
  not.

Faults injected by hand: 2. `artifacts-you-control` not checking the controller (caught by the
mana test), and `all-artifacts` matching nothing (caught by both Kataki tests).

Coverage: 14,931 of 31,900 cards (+4 over D1103's 14,927), 36,754 of 59,888 lines (+5).

## D1105 — upkeep taxes priced in life, and taxes whose forfeit is a tap

D529 read "sacrifice ~ unless you pay {N}" (and energy) as a choice whose unpaid answer is the
sacrifice, with `payIfChosen` doing the paying and leaving an unpayable price unasked. It refused
two neighbours:

- A price of **life**: "sacrifice ~ unless you pay 2 life" (Season of the Witch; Vile
  Consumption's grant).
- A **tap** as the forfeit: "At the beginning of your upkeep, tap Carnophage unless you pay 1 life"
  (Carnophage, Sangrophage), "tap ~ unless you pay {3}" (Heavyweight Demolisher), "tap ~ unless you
  pay {E}" (Electrozoa).

**Life.** `payIfChosen.life` has been the price of "you may pay N life" since D989, so the same
question takes it as its price: "Pay N life", refused at the life that would end the game, the
rule every life cost here keeps.

**Tap.** The same question with "Tap it" first instead of "Sacrifice it". Declined (or unpayable),
the permanent is tapped and stays. It is not sacrificed, and nothing is done if it has already
left the battlefield.

Read whole: Carnophage, Sangrophage, Heavyweight Demolisher, Vile Consumption and Electrozoa.
Season of the Witch is still short its end-step line.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- All three test cards read whole.
- A life tax. Paid, the life goes and the creature stays untapped. Declined, it is tapped and kept.
- A life tax whose forfeit is the permanent.
- A mana tax whose forfeit is a tap. With no mana it is not asked and the creature is tapped; with
  mana it is asked and paid.

Retargeted (the D516 way): D529's row "a price of life, which is a cost and not mana" now reads, in
a new test that checks its `payIfChosen`.

Faults injected by hand: 2. The life forfeit sacrificing instead of tapping (caught by the life
test), and the mana forfeit doing nothing (caught by the tap test).

Coverage: 14,936 of 31,900 cards (+5 over D1104's 14,931), 36,760 of 59,888 lines (+6).

## D1106 — one mana of any type that land produced

D1088 read mana a permanent adds when something is tapped for mana, in two forms: a fixed list
(Wild Growth's {G}, Crypt Ghast's {B}) or "one mana of the chosen color". The doublers were unread:

- "Whenever a player taps a land for mana, that player adds one mana of any type that land
  produced": Mana Flare, Heartbeat of Spring, Dictate of Karametra, Zhur-Taa Ancient.
- "… a basic land" (Lavaleaper); "… a Mountain, Forest, or Plains" (Keeper of Progenitus).
- "Whenever you tap a land for mana, add one mana of any type that land produced": Zendikar
  Resurgent, Mirari's Wake.

**The watcher.** `tapManaExtra.watches` gains `anyone`: any player's land, a basic land, or one of
a list of subtypes. The mana goes to the player who tapped the land, which every tap path already
does, since the mana is part of the tap (CR 605.1b). `watcherSees` is now the one check for all
three kinds of watcher.

**The mana.** `adds: 'produced'` is one more mana of what the tap made: one mana, whatever the land
made (Ancient Tomb's {C}{C} gets one {C} more, CR 106.12), so it is counted separately by
`tapManaEchoes`, not listed by `tapManaExtras`.
- In the auto-tapper's sources, a fixed source lists it in `produces`. A choice source carries
  `echo`, and the solver adds that many more of the colour it picks, so a dual land under a Mana
  Flare pays {B}{B} alone.
- The pips add one more of each kind the permanent's taps make, optimistic like the rest of
  `potentialMana`.
- A tap by hand adds one more of the first mana it made.

Still unread: Overabundance ("…, and ~ deals 1 damage to the player"), Winter's Night ("snow
land", and its untap clause), Barbflare Gremlin ("if ~ is tapped"), and "one mana of any color"
extras (Fertile Ground), which are a second choice on the tap.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- All three test cards read whole.
- A Mana Flare doubles every player's lands, in the sources, the pips and by hand.
- A dual land makes two of the colour it is tapped for and pays {B}{B} alone.
- "You tap" covers only the controller's lands, and a subtype list only those subtypes.

Faults injected by hand: 2. "Anyone" narrowed to the watcher's own lands (caught by the Mana Flare
test), and the solver leaving out a choice source's echo (caught by the dual land test).

Coverage: 14,944 of 31,900 cards (+8 over D1105's 14,936), 36,770 of 59,888 lines (+10).

## D1107 — a card that names itself in the plural

A card that is two characters or a crowd names itself with a plural verb: "When Cloak and Dagger
enter", "Whenever Bebop & Rocksteady attack or block", "When The Duras Sisters die", "Whenever
Falcon and Redwing deal combat damage to a player". Every reader spells the self reference with a
singular verb ("enters", "attacks"), so 16 legal cards had a line unread for the grammar alone.

**Put in the singular before the lines are read.** `singularSelf` in `compileSingle` rewrites the
verb straight after the card's name or short name:
- enter, attack, die, deal, block, get, have, gain, become and leave take an "s";
- "are" becomes "is" and "aren't" becomes "isn't";
- a second verb joined by "or", "and" or "and/or" changes too.

The rules are the same for one permanent whatever its name says it is (CR 201.5). It runs only for
a name that is plural ("and", "&", or "The …s"), so "When Test Solo enter" on a card with a
singular name is still refused. An unread line is reported in the singular.

Read whole now: Falcon and Redwing, The Duras Sisters, David and Carol Marcus and The Immortal
Weapons. Most of the rest print "enters or attacks", "they're not a token" or other lines that are
short for other reasons.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both test cards read whole, with the plural prologues in the singular ("attack or block" is two
  triggers).
- The pair enters and draws a card.
- A singular name is left alone.

Faults injected by hand: 2. The rewrite turned off (caught by both reading tests), and the plural
guard removed (caught by the singular-name test).

Coverage: 14,948 of 31,900 cards (+4 over D1106's 14,944), 36,777 of 59,888 lines (+7).

## D1108 — "whenever one or more … enter": one trigger for the batch

D1000 batched deaths ("whenever one or more creatures die" fires once for a board wipe). The
arrivals had no batch, so "Whenever one or more other creatures you control enter" (24 legal lines)
was unread: Welcoming Vampire, Tocasia's Welcome, Woodland Champion, Ingenious Artillerist and
others.

**The event.** `permanents-entered`, raised once per settle pass, after the arrivals loop, with
everything that arrived on the battlefield in it. Each entry is read as it now is: its controller,
whether it is a token, its card types, creature types, power and mana value. A spell that makes
three tokens is one event (CR 603.2c), so the trigger goes on the stack once.

**The trigger** is asked in `fireTrigger`, which knows the watcher, as `creatures-died` is. At least
one of the batch has to fit:
- the kind: creatures, artifacts, enchantments, lands, tokens, artifact creatures, creature tokens,
  or a creature type ("other Elves", "Merfolk"; the plurals Elves, Dwarves and Wolves by name, the
  rest by their "s", validated as a creature type);
- `other`, which leaves the watcher out;
- `nontoken`;
- whose they are ("you control", "your opponents control");
- "with power N or less" and "with mana value N or less".

The watcher arriving in the same batch counts itself unless the line says "other".

Read whole now: Welcoming Vampire and Tocasia's Welcome (with "This ability triggers only once each
turn", D532). Still short: "that many" and "that much" counted off the batch (Woodland Champion,
Ingenious Artillerist), "Humans and/or Warriors", and "if they entered from a graveyard".

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both test cards read whole.
- Three tokens made at once are one trigger: 1 life, not 3.
- The filters. A 3-power creature does not draw and a 1-power one does, and the watcher entering
  alone does not count itself as "other".

Faults injected by hand: 2. One event per arrival instead of one per batch (caught by the token
test), and the power filter dropped (caught by the filter test).

Coverage: 14,957 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1107's 14,948), 36,793 of 59,888 lines (+16).

## D1109 — an animation beside another clause keeps its bot hint

**Pod sweep 61101** (100 four-player Commander games on the D1107 build, random decks from the whole
legal pool): 99 finished, 59.0 turns and 343 moves on average, no throw. One looped. In seed 61157 a
bot pressed Chimeric Idol's "{0}: Tap all lands you control. Chimeric Idol becomes a 3/3 Turtle
artifact creature until end of turn." a thousand times in one precombat main phase, and the harness
ended the game.

**Why.** `AbilityDef.animates` is the bot's rule for an animation: press it only when there is an
attack or a block to make with it, and not when the permanent is already a creature or the
animation is already on the stack (`animationCouldMatter`). The "becomes a creature" reader sets
it, as `abilityFlags`. Chimeric Idol's ability is two clauses, though, and `composeEffects` carried
`spellFlags` outwards but not `abilityFlags`. So the composed ability had no hint, and to the search
a free activation that taps already-tapped lands and re-animates a creature always looked worth one
more press.

**The fix.** A composition carries `animates` when any part has it. Other ability flags are left
alone. `untapsOnly` and `selfShrink` each describe an ability whose whole effect is that one
clause, which a composition is not.

Seed 61157 rerun on this build: finished, 71 turns, no throw and no stall.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- The Idol's ability reads whole, with `animates` on the composed ability.
- Driven by the bot through its main phase, the Idol is animated at most once.

Faults injected by hand: 1. The carry removed: both tests fail.

Coverage: 14,957 of 31,900 cards (+0 over D1108's 14,957), 36,793 of 59,888 lines (+0).

## D1110 — "that many" off a batch of arrivals or deaths

"That many" and "that much" after a damage or life event have been the event's amount since D903:
the trigger reader marks the words and `readEffect` reads them as `eventAmount`. A batch trigger
had no amount, so Woodland Champion's "Whenever one or more tokens you control enter, put that many
+1/+1 counters on Woodland Champion" and Ingenious Artillerist's "Whenever one or more artifacts you
control enter, Ingenious Artillerist deals that much damage to each opponent" were unread.

**The count.** `batchCount` counts the members of a batch event that fit a batch trigger's filters,
as seen by its watcher: the deaths for `creatures-died` (D1000) and the arrivals for
`permanents-entered` (D1108). Both triggers now match on it (zero is no trigger), and it is the
trigger's `eventAmount`. So the number is what the trigger names. Three Saprolings entering beside
an Artillerist are not artifacts, and deal no damage.

**The words.** Both batch kinds are marked for "that many" by the trigger reader, and the reader
gains "~ deals that much damage to each opponent".

Read whole now: Woodland Champion and Ingenious Artillerist. Every legal card printing "one or more
… enter" or "… die" with "that many" or "that much" now reads.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both test cards read whole.
- Three tokens at once are one trigger and three counters.
- Two Treasures deal 2 damage to each opponent, and three Saprolings deal none.

Faults injected by hand: 2. The amount fixed at 1 (caught by both count tests), and the batch
kinds not marked (all three fail).

Coverage: 14,959 of 31,900 cards (+2 over D1109's 14,957), 36,796 of 59,888 lines (+3).

## D1111 — a battle named where nothing can be one

**Pod sweep 61201** (100 four-player Commander games on the D1109 build): all 100 finished, 57.0
turns and 321 moves on average, with no throw and no stall. This follows D1109's fix of the
Chimeric Idol loop found by sweep 61101.

Cards printed since battles (March of the Machine) name them beside players and permanents:
"Whenever ~ deals combat damage to a player or battle", "{T}: ~ deals 2 damage to target
opponent, battle, or planeswalker", "target creature, planeswalker, or battle". The readers do not
know the word, so 18 legal cards were a line short on it alone or with something else.

**The word names nothing that can exist.** Battle cards are refused (D591, CR 310), because their
defense counters come from card data the production import does not have yet. So no battle is ever
on the battlefield. `withoutBattles` in `compileSingle` takes "battle" out of such a list before
the readers see the line:
- "A, B, or battle" and "A, battle, or B" become "A or B";
- "A or battle" becomes "A".

No game changes: the choices were only ever players and the other permanents. A **battle card**
("an instant, sorcery, or battle card from your graveyard") is left alone, since a battle card is a
card in a hand, library or graveyard whether battles are played or not.

The rewrite is behind `BATTLES_PLAYED = false`. When battles are played (after the Scryfall import,
Nick's decision), the switch goes and the readers learn the word.

Read whole now: Aetherblade Agent, Beamtown Beatstick, Jeska and Kamahl, Onakke Javelineer and
Thorin, Company's Leader, among others.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- Four battle wordings read.
- A battle card line is left as printed.
- "Target player or battle" offers the two players, and the ping deals 2.

Faults injected by hand: 2. The switch turned on (all four wordings fail), and the battle-card guard
removed (caught by the battle-card test).

Coverage: 14,964 of 31,900 cards (+5 over D1110's 14,959), 36,802 of 59,888 lines (+6).

## D1112 — an entry named with subject words

The board prologue (D477, D478, D484) reads "Whenever a[nother] [nontoken] <type> you control
[with power N or greater] enters". The words in front of the type, and a mana value, were refused:

- a colour: "Whenever another white creature you control enters" (the Denizens);
- "colorless": Eldrazi Mimic, Flayer Drone;
- "legendary": Hero's Blade, Crown of Gondor;
- "a creature token you control enters": Anointer Priest;
- "a creature with mana value 6 or greater enters": Dragon Breath's cycle;
- "another artifact enters" with nobody's side named: Arcbound Crusher.

**The event carries them.** An entry now carries the subject's live colours, whether it is
legendary, and its mana value (off the card's printed cost, which is what mana value is on the
battlefield, CR 202.3). They are asked as the size filters are: a missing fact fails the filter,
never passes it.

**One row for the words** (`richEntryTrigger`), after the plainer rows so it reads only what they
refused:
- one colour or "colorless";
- "legendary" and "nontoken";
- "token" after the type;
- "you control" or "an opponent controls", or neither (anybody's);
- "with mana value N or greater / less".

Two colours ("white and blue") are still refused.

Read whole now: Court Street Denizen, Foundry Street Denizen, Anointer Priest, Arcbound Crusher and
Flayer Drone among them. Eldrazi Mimic, Hero's Blade and Dragon Breath are short on their effects.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Three test cards read whole.
- A colour: a white creature entering gains life, a green one does not.
- A creature token: the token gains life, a card does not.
- A mana value: 3 gains life, 1 does not.

Faults injected by hand: 2. The colour check and the mana value check each removed (caught by
their tests).

Coverage: 14,981 of 31,900 cards (+17 over D1111's 14,964), 36,825 of 59,888 lines (+23).

## D1113 — death triggers with subject words, and the look-back in a wipe

**Subject words on a death**, D1112's twin (`richDeathTrigger`, after the plainer death rows). These
were refused, and now read:
- "Whenever a nontoken creature an opponent controls dies" (Harvester of Souls, Fire Nation
  Sentinels);
- "another nontoken creature dies" (Ogre Slumlord);
- "a creature token dies" (Grismold);
- "a legendary creature you control dies";
- "a white creature you control dies";
- "a creature you own dies";
- "a creature with power 4 or greater dies" with nobody's side named.

A death now carries the creature's colours and whether it was legendary, as it last was. A "token"
filter is asked of the death as `nontoken` already was.

**The look-back (CR 603.10a), which was wrong.** A leaves-the-battlefield ability looks back in
time: a permanent that leaves in the same event as others still "sees" them leave. D1000 gave that
to the batched "one or more creatures die" trigger. The per-creature death events did not have it.

A watcher destroyed in the same wipe was by then in a graveyard, so only its own death reached it:
- "Whenever another creature dies" in a wipe saw nothing.
- "Whenever ~ or another creature dies" (Blood Artist) saw only itself.
- "Whenever a creature you control dies" (Zulaport Cutthroat, Grim Haruspex) likewise.

A Blood Artist in a Wrath with four other creatures drained once instead of five times.

A death event now carries the other permanents that died in the same settle pass (`alongside`).
Each is asked about it from wherever it went, as an Aura from the creature it was on (D994) or a
Morbid Opportunist from its own batch (D1000) already is. Pinned by a wipe test: itself, my Bear
and their Bear is three; the Harvester still sees the opponent's Bear; the Mourner still sees my
Hero.

The new row steps aside for a line with no subject words at all ("Whenever another creature dies"), so the plainer rows keep reading those with their own shapes. The first pregate caught that row being taken.

Read whole now: Harvester of Souls, Grismold, Fire Nation Sentinels, Ogre Slumlord, Overseer of the
Damned.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both test cards read whole.
- An opponent's nontoken creature counts and mine does not.
- A legendary creature of mine counts and a non-legendary one does not.
- The wipe look-back test.

The full rules-engine suite ran on this change, 5,922 tests. The only failures were D565's two
rows below, both expected.

Retargeted (the D516 way):
- D565's refusal "a narrower death" ("Whenever a nontoken creature dies") now reads with its filter,
  in a new test.
- "Whenever a creature dies" keeps D565's exact shape: no `of` when nobody's side is named.

Faults injected by hand: 2. The look-back removed (caught by the wipe test), and the legendary check
removed (caught by the legendary test and the wipe test).

Coverage: 14,991 of 31,900 cards (+10 over D1112's 14,981), 36,839 of 59,888 lines (+14).

## D1114 — "your first instant or sorcery spell each turn"

"Whenever you cast your first spell each turn" has counted per caster since D436, and Esper
Sentinel's "their first noncreature spell" among noncreature spells since D678 (`nthOfKind`).
"Whenever you cast your **first instant or sorcery** spell each turn" had no count of its own, so
it was unread (Arcane Bombardment, Aquatic Alchemist, Baral and Kari Zev, and "second" on others).

**The count.** `countCast` keeps a third tally per caster, `<seat>:instant-or-sorcery`, raised for
an instant or a sorcery only. The cast event carries that spell's ordinal among them
(`instantOrSorceryNth`). `nthOfKind` with `spell: 'instant-or-sorcery'` counts on it, so a creature
cast first does not use the trigger up, and the second instant of the turn does not fire it again.
"First" and "second" are read.

Read whole now: Aquatic Alchemist and Storm-Kiln Artist. Arcane Bombardment and Baral and Kari Zev
are short on their effects.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- The test card reads whole.
- A creature cast first does not count. The first instant gains life and the second does not.

Faults injected by hand: 2. The count taken from all spells (caught: the creature used it up), and
the tally never raised (caught: the second instant fired it again).

Coverage: 14,993 of 31,900 cards (+2 over D1113's 14,991), 36,841 of 59,888 lines (+2).

## D1115 — a player dealt damage by any source, and "one or two" down to its minimum

**Pod sweep 61301** (100 four-player Commander games on the D1113 build, which carries D1113's
look-back for deaths): 99 finished, 58.6 turns and 345 moves on average, no stall. One threw (seed
61396): a bot cast **Wind Sail** ("One or two target creatures gain flying until end of turn") with
no creature on the battlefield, and the cast refused it.

**The fix.** D1024 made "one or two target creatures" one spec with `count: 2`, `optional`, `min: 1`.
The cast honoured the minimum. The offer (`playableTargets`) and the bot (`chooseTargets`) took
`optional` to mean "none will do". Both now stop at the minimum. Seed 61396 rerun on this build:
finished, 65 turns, no throw.

**A player dealt damage, by any source.** `deals-damage` is raised only for a permanent's damage
("whenever ~ deals damage" is an ability of a permanent), so a burn spell to the face raised nothing
a "source you control" could see. A new event, `player-damaged`, is raised once per landing on a
player, whatever dealt it. It carries:
- how much was dealt, and whether it was combat damage;
- who was dealt it;
- who controlled the source: the damage record now keeps the controller `dealDamage` was given (a
  spell's caster), falling back to the source's seat.

Triggers ask from the watcher's side:
- "Whenever a source you control deals [noncombat] damage to an opponent" (Niv-Mizzet, Visionary;
  Virtue of Courage; Chandra's Pyreling);
- "Whenever a source an opponent controls deals damage to you" (Farsight Mask, Retaliator Griffin);
- "Whenever an opponent is dealt [noncombat] damage" (Chandra's Spitfire, Wildfire Elemental);
- "Whenever you're dealt damage" (Darien, King of Kjeldor).

"That many" and "that much" are the damage. "That player" is the one hit, unless that was the
watcher's own controller, and then the one whose source hit them (Michiko Konda's "that player
sacrifices a permanent").

Read whole now: Niv-Mizzet, Visionary; Chandra's Pyreling; Chandra's Spitfire; Darien, King of
Kjeldor; Farsight Mask; Retaliator Griffin; Wildfire Elemental; Asgardian Inspiration; Stick,
Fearless Mentor.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both test cards read whole.
- A burn spell of mine to an opponent draws that many, and to myself draws nothing.
- An opponent's Shock to me triggers my Mask, and my own does not.
- "One or two target creatures" is not offered with no creature, and is offered with one.

The bot, compile, automation, playout and combat suites pass (2,074 tests).

Faults injected by hand: 2. The old offer rule restored (caught by the Wind Sail test), and the
"an opponent controls" check removed (caught by the Mask test).

Coverage: 15,002 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1114's 14,993), 36,856 of 59,888 lines (+15).

## D1116 — a card put into a graveyard from anywhere, and the Colossus shuffle

D569 gave the `to-graveyard` event a `self` and a "from the battlefield", read for Rancor. Three
neighbours were unread.

**"When ~ is put into a graveyard from anywhere"**: the Eldrazi titans' "its owner shuffles their
graveyard into their library" (Kozilek, Butcher of Truth; Ulamog, the Infinite Gyre), and Serra
Avatar's and Worldspine Wurm's "shuffle it into its owner's library". It is the card's own arrival
from any zone (destroyed, milled, discarded, countered), fired from the graveyard it reached.
"Your graveyard" says the same, since a card always goes to its owner's. The two effects are new
readers:
- the card back into its owner's library, then a shuffle, only while it is still in the graveyard;
- the owner's whole graveyard back, the card with it, then a shuffle.

**The Colossus replacement**: "If ~ would be put into a graveyard from anywhere, reveal ~ and
shuffle it into its owner's library instead" (Blightsteel Colossus, Darksteel Colossus, Progenitus,
Legacy Weapon). The card's own `replaces` entry on `to-graveyard`, the widest wording, so it covers
a death, a mill and a discard alike. `replaceZoneChange` asks the card's own replacement first and
from wherever it went (CR 616.1). The card never reaches the graveyard, so no death or graveyard
trigger sees it.

**"Whenever a land card is put into your graveyard from anywhere"** (Skola Grovedancer, Slogurk),
"a Desert card" (Yuma) and "another card". The event now carries the card's printed types and
subtypes, as a card in a graveyard has them. A trigger can ask for a card type or a subtype, and
"your" for whose graveyard.

Read whole now: Kozilek, Butcher of Truth; Ulamog, the Infinite Gyre; Serra Avatar; Worldspine
Wurm; Blightsteel Colossus; Darksteel Colossus; Progenitus; Legacy Weapon; Skola Grovedancer;
Slogurk, the Overslime; Yuma, Proud Protector.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Three test cards read whole.
- The titan destroyed shuffles the whole graveyard (itself and the spell) back.
- The Colossus destroyed goes into the library, and only the spell is in the graveyard.
- A creature card reaching my graveyard gains life, and the instant does not.

Faults injected by hand: 2. The replacement never applying (caught by the Colossus test), and the
card-type filter removed (caught by the creature-card test).

Coverage: 15,015 of 31,900 cards (+13 over D1115's 15,002), 36,878 of 59,888 lines (+22).

## D1117 — "for the first time each turn" in the prologue

**Pod sweep 61401** (100 four-player Commander games on the D1115 build): all 100 finished, 57.3
turns and 314 moves on average, no throw and no stall.

  Leech Collector);

  card …".

`triggerRestriction` now reads "<event> for the first time each turn, <effect>" as the event with
`onceEachTurn`: one firing a turn, on the first such event. Only where no "if" follows the comma.
With a condition, a later event could fire it after the first one failed the condition, which the
flag would not allow.

## D1119 — "whenever a creature you control explores"

Explore has been an effect since D590 ("When ~ enters, it explores"), but it raised no event, so
"Whenever a creature you control explores" (Lurking Chupacabra, Wildgrowth Walker, Shadowed Caravel,
Merfolk Cave-Diver) was unread.

**The event.** The explore effect records its explorer on the state (`explored`) as it explores,
whether the revealed card is a land or not, and whether or not the question is asked. `settle`
drains that list as it drains `countersPut` (D633), raising one `explores` event per explore with
the explorer as its subject. A creature that has left the battlefield still explored (CR 701.44c),
so the event is raised for it too, read from `vanished` if need be.

**The trigger.** `explores` takes `who` (self, another, any) and `of` (you, any), asked as the board
events ask them. Rows: "Whenever a creature you control explores", "Whenever another creature you
control explores", "Whenever ~ explores".

Read whole now: Lurking Chupacabra, Wildgrowth Walker and Shadowed Caravel. Jadelight Ranger's
"explores, then it explores again" is still the D590 refusal.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- Both test cards read whole.
- The Scout explores (its question answered if asked) and the Walker gains 3 life.

Faults injected by hand: 1. The event not raised (caught).

Coverage: 15,029 of 31,900 cards (+3 over D1118's 15,026), 36,898 of 59,888 lines (+3).

## D1121 — the board's "becomes tapped" and "leaves the battlefield"

Both events were offered only to the permanent they happened to (`selfOnly` in `raise`), since a
tap is raised for every land tapped for mana. About 50 legal lines watch the board for them:

- "Whenever a creature an opponent controls becomes tapped" (Gideon's Avenger, Palliation Accord,
  Verity Circle, and Rhoda with "if it isn't being declared as an attacker"), "a Dwarf / Merfolk you
  control" (Magda, Judge of Currents), "a Mountain / Forest / Island an opponent controls"
  (Lifeblood, Lifetap, Thoughtleech).
- "Whenever another creature you control leaves the battlefield" (Ninth Bridge Patrol, Flaming Fist
  Officer), "a token you control" (Nadier's Nightblade), "a creature token" (Twilight Drover),
  "another nontoken creature you control" (Tokka & Rahzar), "another permanent" (Super Shredder),
  "without dying" / "if it didn't die" (Imperial Cosmographer, Taeko), "if it had counters on it"
  (Leader's Talent, Nikara, Angelic Sleuth).

`BoardSubjectFilter` (who, of, what, subtype, token or nontoken, a counter, without dying, not
attacking) is shared by the two events. `raise` asks `boardWatched` first, which looks for a
printed `any`/`another` trigger on a permanent or an emblem; only then is the event enriched and
offered to the whole board. A leave is read as it last was, from the `vanished` snapshot. The leave
event carries `died`, and the tap carries `declaredAttacking`.

A rules fix rides along: the plain "when ~ leaves the battlefield" matcher returned true for any
leave it was offered. That was harmless while only the subject was asked. It now asks for its own
leave.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The watchers read whole, and the shape is correct.
- An opponent's creature tapping gains life, and one's own does not.
- Another creature of one's own leaving gains life, and an opponent's does not. A self-leave watcher
  on the same board stays its own: 1 life, not 4. Its own leave still pays.
- "Without dying": a bounce gains life, and a death does not.

Retargeted (the D516 way): the compile refusal "Whenever another creature you control leaves the
battlefield" reads now, in a new test.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- The self check on the plain leave removed (caught).
- The without-dying check removed (caught).

Coverage: 15,053 of 31,900 cards (+21 over D1120's 15,032), 36,940 of 59,888 lines (+32).

## D1124 — "whenever ~ becomes untapped", and enchantment creature tokens

This adds a new trigger event, `becomes-untapped`. It is found the way a tap is (D994): `settle`
compares each battlefield permanent before and after. So the untap step, an untap effect and a
Seedborn Muse all raise it without knowing the event exists. A trigger from the untap step waits for
the upkeep, where the first player gets priority (CR 502.4).

It reads:
- Inspired (Born of the Gods and Journey into Nyx; its ability word is stripped first), Key to the City and
  Hollowsage, which are the permanent's own untap.
- The board's untap, on D1121's filter: "whenever a permanent you control becomes untapped" (Wake
  Thrasher).

The token reader now takes "enchantment" as it took "artifact": "a 2/2 blue Bird enchantment
creature token with flying" (the Inspired payers, Fated Intervention, the gods' tokens).

26 tail cards read whole with the two together, among them Deepwater Hypnotist, Felhide
Spiritbinder, Key to the City, King Macar, Pheres-Band Tromper, Siren of the Silent Song, Wake
Thrasher, Aerie Worshippers, God-Favored General, Forlorn Pseudamma and Satyr Nyx-Smith.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The watchers and the token read whole.
- Its own untap in the untap step pays at the upkeep, and another creature's untap does not.
- "A permanent you control becomes untapped" counts the Forest that paid and the creature that was
  tapped. On that watched board, a self watcher stays its own.
- An enchantment creature token is an enchantment and a creature.

The deck-coverage test exempts 'trigger becomes-untapped': no pool deck plays one.

Faults injected by hand: 2. Both were caught, the first only after the test gained its
watched-board case.
- The self check removed.
- The untap raise removed.

## D1126 — keyword anthems, and a player with hexproof or shroud

Two static shapes from the D1125 survey.

**"Other creatures you control with flying get +1/+1"** (Empyrean Eagle, Thunderclap Wyvern, Spirit
of the Spires, Windstorm Drake, Alela, and Stalwart Shield-Bearers' "with defender"). The group
static takes a new filter, `onlyWithKeyword`, which reads the creature's live keywords. A creature
given flying by a spell is grown while it flies.

That is a keyword read in the middle of the effect loop that makes keywords. So `effectApplies`
computes the creature's characteristics with a guard that leaves keyword-filtered statics out. The
reader only accepts a size change ("get +N/+N"), so leaving such a static out cannot change a
keyword, and the inner answer equals the outer one. `characteristicsOf` has no cache that could
keep the inner result.

**"You have hexproof." / "You have shroud."** (Leyline of Sanctity, Aegis of the Gods, Ivory Mask,
Crystal Barricade, Solitary Confinement, Spirit of the Hearth, True Believer, Teyo, Metropolis
Reformer) is `CardScript.controllerHas`. Targeting checks a player against it beside D718's
protection:
- Hexproof refuses spells and abilities an opponent controls.
- Shroud refuses everyone's.

The reader lives in `effects.ts`, which can read scripts, and is registered with `targeting.ts`
through a hook, since targeting importing effects would be a cycle.

Read whole now: those 15 cards.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The statics read whole.
- The fliers grow, and the Eagle itself and the ground creature do not.
- A creature given flying grows while it flies.
- Hexproof keeps an opponent's burn off its controller, while their own still aims at themselves;
  shroud keeps even its controller's own off.

The deck-coverage test exempts 'script controllerHas': no pool deck plays one.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- The shield check in targeting removed (caught).
- The keyword test in `effectApplies` removed (caught).

Coverage: 15,125 of 31,900 cards (+18 over D1125's 15,107), 37,031 of 59,888 lines (+26).

## D1127 — replacements on gaining life

"If you would gain life, …instead" had no reading. It is now `CardScript.lifeGainReplacement`,
applied in `gainLife`, the one path every gain takes, lifelink included, while the permanent is on
the battlefield with its abilities (CR 614.1a):

- "you gain twice that much life instead" (Boon Reflection, Rhox Faithmender, The Wind Crystal);
- "you gain that much life plus 1 instead" (Angel of Vitality, Heron of Hope, Honor Troll, Knight of
  Dawn's Light, Bilbo);
- "If an opponent would gain life, that player loses that much life instead" (Tainted Remedy);
- "If a player would gain life, that player gains no life instead" (Sulfuric Vortex).

The gaining player orders replacements (CR 616.1), and the engine takes the order that gains the
most:
1. "Gains no life" ends it.
2. "Loses that much life" turns it into a loss.
3. Otherwise every "plus N" comes before every "twice".

Read whole now: Angel of Vitality, Bilbo, Birthday Celebrant, Boon Reflection, Heron of Hope, Honor
Troll, Knight of Dawn's Light, Rhox Faithmender, Sulfuric Vortex, Tainted Remedy, The Wind Crystal.
Plague Drone's "Rot Fly —" is a flavour label the line reader does not strip, so it is still unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The replacements read whole.
- Twice, plus one, and both: 3 life is 6, 4 and 8. An opponent's Boon is not "you".
- An opponent's Remedy turns the gain into a loss of 3, and one's own does not. A Vortex stops the
  gain even with a Boon out.

The deck-coverage test exempts 'script lifeGainReplacement': no pool deck plays one.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- "Twice" before "plus" (caught).
- The whose check removed (caught).

Coverage: 15,135 of 31,900 cards (+10 over D1126's 15,125), 37,047 of 59,888 lines (+16).

## D1128 — "~ can't attack or block alone"

`CardScript.cantAlone` (CR 506.5): a creature that may attack only if another creature also attacks,
and block only if another creature also blocks, in the same declaration.

- `combat.ts` `aloneIssue` is the one test: a declaration of exactly one distinct creature that says
  so, and still has its abilities.
- `declareAttackers` refuses a lone attacker. A creature that must attack is not owed when it could
  only have attacked alone.
- `declareBlockers` refuses a lone blocker.
- The bot's two declaration filters respect it: `legalDeclaration` sends a lone one home, and
  `withoutLoneBlock` takes a lone block out. They feed the simulated playouts, which otherwise stop
  short when a declaration is refused.

Read whole now: Bonded Construct, Bonded Horncrest, Craven Hulk, Ember Beast, Jackal Familiar, Loyal
Pegasus, Militia Rallier, Mogg Flunkies, Pet Sehlat, Raging Kronch, Trusty Companion, Wojek
Bodyguard. Pipsqueak's "unless he has a +1/+1 counter on him" is not read.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- It reads whole.
- A lone attack is refused, and an attack beside another creature is fine.
- A lone block is refused, and a block beside another blocker is fine.
- The bot leaves it home alone, where a Bear in the same spot attacks.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- The engine's attack check removed (caught).
- The bot's attack filter removed: **not caught**. The bot's final choice already drops a plan the
  engine refuses, so the outcome is the same. The filter is there for the playouts inside the
  search, which no test isolates.

Coverage: 15,147 of 31,900 cards (+12 over D1127's 15,135), 37,061 of 59,888 lines (+14).

## D1129 — bolster, and counters on a creature you choose

**Bolster N** (CR 701.39a): "choose a creature with the least toughness among creatures you control
and put N +1/+1 counters on it". It had no reader: 18 single-unread legal lines, across the Khans
block's Abzan cards and their reprints.

It is read now as a question asked as the effect resolves, of the controller's own battlefield, with
a filter for the least live toughness:
- A tie is the controller's choice.
- One candidate is answered by the engine.
- No creature means nothing happens (CR 701.39b).

The same question without the filter reads "put a +1/+1 counter / two +1/+1 counters on a creature
you control", which is not targeted (Humiliate's tail and its kin). The engine's own seat puts the
counters on its strongest candidate.

18 of the 27 tail cards that print either read whole now: Abzan Skycaptain, Anafenza, Kin-Tree
Spirit, Aven Tactician, Abzan Advantage, Enduring Victory, Honor's Reward and more.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both read whole.
- Bolster's single candidate is the least toughness: no question, and the counters land there.
- A tie is offered and the controller's pick gets them.
- "A creature you control" offers every one.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- The least-toughness filter removed (caught).
- The count fixed at 1 (caught).

## D1130 — suspend spells that exile themselves with time counters

"Exile ~ with three time counters on it." as a suspend spell's last sentence (Arc Blade, Inspiring
Refrain, Reality Strobe and the rest of the Time Spiral / Modern Horizons cycle) is where the card
goes as it resolves, not something the resolution does. It extends D733's "Exile ~.":
- The same reader takes the count, as `CardScript.exilesWithTimeCounters`.
- The resolution exiles the card and puts that many time counters on it.

That is all "suspended" means here. The owner's upkeep already takes a counter off any exiled card
with time counters and offers the cast at zero (CR 702.62b–c), so the card loops as printed.

Read whole now: Arc Blade, Cyclical Evolution, Festering March, Inspiring Refrain, Reality Strobe,
Rousing Refrain, Suspended Sentence. Charnel Serenade, Chronomantic Escape and Venture Forth are
short on other sentences.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- It reads whole.
- It resolves into exile with three time counters (two cards drawn), and the owner's next upkeep
  takes one off.
- A plain "Exile ~." gets none.

The deck-coverage test exempts 'script exilesWithTimeCounters': no pool deck plays one.

Faults injected by hand: 1. The counters not put on (caught).
