## D1131 — "It gains haste." and an end-step exile after a return, and a fix to "it"

**Grants with no duration.** "It gains haste." after "Return target creature card from your
graveyard to the battlefield" (Grave Upheaval, Whip of Erebos, Haunted House), and "Target
creature gains haste." on its own, last as long as the object does (CR 611.2a). The effect's source
is the creature itself with `duration: 'permanent'`, so the sweep in `settle` ends it the moment
the creature leaves.

**The end-step rider for returned cards.** D696's "Sacrifice / Exile it at the beginning of the next
end step" joined only a "create" or "put" sentence. It now joins "return" too (Kami of Industry,
Postmortem Lunge, Footsteps of the Goryo). "Your next end step" schedules the delayed ability for the
controller's own end step, where "the next" is anybody's.

**A fix found on the way.** In a spell, the self reader took a bare "it" as the spell itself. So the
long-standing reading of "Return target creature card … It gains haste until end of turn" (Scrap
Welder's kin) gave the haste to a card on its way to the graveyard, and the creature came back
without it. A bare "it" after a clause that aimed at a card is now that card.

Read whole now: Dawn of the Dead, Footsteps of the Goryo, Grave Upheaval, Harried Dronesmith, Kami
of Industry, Stone Idol Trap.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- All read whole.
- "It gains haste." outlasts the turn.
- "Until end of turn" gives the haste to the returned creature, and it is gone a turn later.
- The returned creature is exiled at the next end step.
- "Your next end step", cast on an opponent's turn, waits past that turn for its controller's own.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- "It" back to the spell (caught, two tests).
- The lasting grant's source back to the spell (caught).

Coverage: 15,179 of 31,900 cards (+7 over D1130's 15,172), 37,099 of 59,888 lines (+11).

## D1132 — extra turns

"Take an extra turn after this one" had no mechanism (65 legal cards print an extra turn). Now:

- `GameState.extraTurns` is a stack of seats owed a turn: the most recently created is taken first
  (CR 500.7).
- When a turn ends, `advanceStep` takes the newest one whose player is still in the game. An
  eliminated player's extra turn is dropped.
- `extraTurnResume` remembers whose regular turn they followed, so the order resumes after that
  seat. Time Warp aimed across a three-player table does not skip the player in between.
- Readers: "take an extra turn after this one" and "you take …" (the controller's, e.g. Time Walk,
  Temporal Manipulation, Temporal Mastery), "target player / opponent takes an extra turn" (Time
  Warp, Beacon of Tomorrows), "two extra turns" (Time Stretch).

Read whole now (16): Alrund's Epiphany, Beacon of Tomorrows, Capture of Jingzhou, Karn's Temporal
Sundering, Magistrate's Scepter, Mu Yanling, Part the Waterveil, Second Chance, Teferi, Timebender,
Temporal Manipulation, Temporal Mastery, Temporal Trespass, Time Sieve, Time Stretch, Time Walk,
Time Warp. Final Fortune's and Last Chance's "at the beginning of that turn's end step, you lose
the game" is not read.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- All read whole.
- "Take an extra turn": turns go 0, 0, 1 after the cast.
- "Two extra turns" at oneself: 0, 0, 1, 0, counting the turn after the cast.
- Aimed at seat 2 of three: 2, 1, 2, 0. The order resumes after the caster.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- The resume seat ignored (caught).
- The extra turn never taken (caught, three tests).

Pod sweep 61801 (100 games, D1131 build): 100 finished, no throw, no stall.

Coverage: 15,195 of 31,900 cards (+16 over D1131's 15,179), 37,126 of 59,888 lines (+27).

## D1133 — exhaust and "Activate only once"

Exhaust (CR 702.177a) is an activated ability that may be activated only once. Since D612 the label
has been deliberately kept on, so the remainder could never read as an unrestricted ability. Now it
reads *with* the restriction:

- `AbilityDef.onceEver` marks the ability.
- `abilityFromLine` takes "Exhaust — " off and sets it.
- The activation restriction reader sets it for the plain sentence "Activate only once."

The use is recorded at activation (CR 602.5f, like once-each-turn) on
`CardInstance.abilityExhausted`, against the permanent's `objectSeq`. So a permanent that leaves
and returns is a new object and may use it again (CR 400.7). `usesLeftThisTurn` answers 0 while
that object has spent it, and both the offer and the activation path ask it.

Read whole now (11): Camera Launcher, First Little Pig, Greenbelt Guardian, Hazard of the Dunes,
Hog-Monkey, Keen Buccaneer, Mai, Jaded Edge, Pacesetter Paragon, Prowcatcher Specialist, Skystreak
Engineer, Stampeding Scurryfoot.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests and 1 compile test:
- Both forms read whole.
- For each form: offered once and used, not offered or accepted again, and offered again after a
  blink.
- Retargeted (the D516 way): the compile refusal "a keyword that is the restriction (exhaust)"
  reads now, asserting `onceEver`.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- The object binding ignored (caught: the blinked permanent stays spent).
- The record never written (caught).

Coverage: 15,207 of 31,900 cards (+12 over D1132's 15,195), 37,146 of 59,888 lines (+20).

## D1134 — boast

Boast (CR 702.142a): "Activate only if this creature attacked this turn and only once each turn."
D612 kept the label on so the remainder could never read without its restriction. D1133 did this for
exhaust; now boast reads the same way:
- `abilityFromLine` takes "Boast — " off and sets `onceEachTurn`.
- It adds an `activateOnlyIf` that asks whether this object was declared as an attacker this turn.

The record is D726's `GameState.attackersThisTurn` (an id with its `objectSeq`), so a creature put
onto the battlefield attacking never attacked (CR 508.4), and one that left and came back is a new

## D1135 — bloodrush from the hand, renew from the graveyard

Two labels in front of an activated ability that D612 kept on, for D582's reason. Read
remainder-only, each would be offered from the battlefield. Each now comes off exactly when the
remainder's cost says where the ability is used from:

- **Bloodrush** joins channel's branch: "Bloodrush — {R}, Discard ~: Target attacking creature gets
  +4/+4 until end of turn." The cost discards the card itself (`discardSelf`), which is what
  `legalActions` and `activate` read as "used from the hand" since cycling (#45).
- **Renew** (Tarkir: Dragonstorm) is the graveyard's twin: "Renew — {B}, Exile this card from your
  graveyard: …". It comes off only when the cost left exiles the card from the graveyard
  (`fromGraveyard` with `exileSelf`). A "Renew —" whose cost did not would stay unread.

Read whole now (17):
- Bloodrush: Ghor-Clan Rampager, Pyrewild Shaman, Rubblebelt Maaka, Rubblehulk, Scab-Clan Charger,
  Scorchwalker, Skarrg Goliath, Skinbrand Goblin, Slaughterhorn, Viashino Shanktail, Wasteland
  Viper, Wrecking Ogre, Zhur-Taa Swine.
- Renew: Adorned Crocodile, Agent of Kotis and two more.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both read whole, and a stray "Renew —" with no graveyard cost stays unread.
- Bloodrush is used from the hand on an attacker (+4/+4), and the card is discarded.
- Renew is used from the graveyard (a counter on the target), and the card is exiled.
- Neither is offered from the battlefield.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- Bloodrush taken out of the branch (caught, two tests).
- Renew's cost check removed: caught only after the stray probe was added, since every printed
  Renew line has the graveyard cost.

## D789 — {X} in an activated ability's cost

Most-played order: Kessig Wolf Run (rank 412), Treasure Vault (463), Blast Zone's counter line
(1682), Folio of Fancies' draw (2774), Helix Pinnacle's counters (4474), Fiend Artisan (4496), and
the rest of the 143 legal cards whose unread lines included an ability with {X} in its cost.

The cost reader refused `{X}` outright ("announcing X on an activated ability is machinery this
reader does not reach"). The machinery was mostly there: the effect side has read the X its own cost
pays since D1055 (`xPayable`, `xAsPaid`), and resolution already hands `object.x` to the effect for
any stack object. What was missing, now added:

- **The cost**: `{X}` reads as part of the mana component, `{X}{X}` as one number paid twice.
- **The offer**: an ability whose cost has X carries `xMax`, the most the rest of the cost leaves
  room for, with the source's own {T} and anything crewed or tapped for the cost kept out of the
  mana (a Kessig Wolf Run does not count itself).
- **The action**: `AutoActivateAction.x`, refused on a cost without an X and when it is not a whole
  number of zero or more; absent on a cost with one, it is zero. Paid with the rest of the cost and
  carried on the stack object; the log line says `(X=2)`.
- **The table**: the web client's X picker, which spells already used, now opens for an ability too
  and sends `x` with the activation.
- **The bot** activates with the most X it can pay, as it casts a Fireball.

Coverage: 25 of the 143 cards are now fully read, and the X line of 31. The rest stop on a word the
effect vocabulary does not have yet ("X target lands", "mana value X" as an exact match, "Spend only
black mana on X", base power and toughness X/X).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests and 1 web client test: the cards read; a Kessig Wolf Run with five lands
is offered with X up to 3 (the Run itself does not count), and activated for 2 it taps four lands and
gives +2/+0 and trample; `{X}{X}` for 2 takes four mana and makes two Treasures; an X too large, an X
on a cost without one, and a negative X are refused, and no X is zero; "mana value X or less" searches
with the X paid. In the client, the X picker opens on an ability's `xMax` and the chosen X goes out
with the activation and its target.

The hand-written compile test that pinned "{X} in an ability cost is refused" now pins the opposite:
the cost reads and keeps `{X}` in its mana. The first gate run caught it.

Faults injected by script: 7 of 7 caught.

    engine tests: 5,993, all passing; web: 275 (on 94f589d)

Coverage: 15,196 to 15,222 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 37,128 to 37,164 of 59,888
lines, against 94f589d.

## D1136 — domain, formidable and cohort

- **Domain's count**: "for each basic land type among lands you control", "the number of basic land
  types among lands you control". Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain and Forest, each counted once off
  the lands' live subtypes, so a dual land counts twice. "Lands they control" is the targeted
  player's (Allied Strategies).
- **Formidable's condition**: "Activate only if creatures you control have total power 8 or
  greater". The condition reader asks D1076's total-power count, so D623's label branch takes the
  "Formidable —" off as it does threshold's.
- **Cohort**: "Cohort — {T}, Tap an untapped Ally you control: …". The ability word names the cost
  the remainder prints, so the label comes off when that cost is there.

Dragon-Scarred Bear, Gaea's Might, Tribal Flames, Might of Alara, Evasive Action, Briar Hydra and
Drana's Chosen.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- All three read whole.
- Domain counts each basic land type once: Forest, Forest and Island make +2/+2.
- Formidable is offered only with total power 8 or greater.
- Cohort taps itself and another Ally, and pays.

Retargeted (the D516 way): two compile rows used formidable's condition as their unreadable board
condition. They now use "three or more creatures with different powers".

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- Domain counting lands rather than types (caught).
- The formidable threshold ignored (caught).

## D1138 — firebending, and mana kept until end of combat

Firebending N (Avatar: The Last Airbender): "Whenever this creature attacks, add N {R}. This mana
lasts until end of combat." It is read as the attack trigger it stands for, which needed one new
fact: mana kept **until end of combat**.

`GameState.keptManaCombat` sits beside D1034's `keptMana`. `emptyPools` keeps it through the combat
steps and drops it as the end of combat step ends, then shrinks the record to what stayed. It is
also cleared in the cleanup step with the turn's record. "Until end of combat, you don't lose this
mana as steps and phases end" joins its "add" sentence the way D1034's does.

Read whole now (9): Azula, On the Hunt; Fire Sages; Loyal Fire Sage; Tundra Tank; Uncle Iroh;
Vindictive Warden; Zhao, Ruthless Admiral; Zuko, Exiled Prince, and one more. Not read:
- "Firebending X, where X is …" (Firebending Student, Sun Warriors) waits on an "add an amount of
  {R} equal to …" reader.
- Avatar Roku's "add six {R}" waits on a number word in an add.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- It reads whole.
- An attacking Firebending 2 adds {R}{R}, still there in the end of combat step, and gone in the
  second main phase.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- The combat mana never lost (caught).
- Never kept (caught).

## D798 — Counter thresholds, and any static line under a condition

Most-played order: Beastmaster Ascension (rank 575), Voice of the Blessed (2932), Quest for the
Goblin Lord (7672), Vadmir, Angelic Cub, and every conditional anthem the general form below reaches.

- **"As long as ~ has seven or more quest counters on it"**: a `staticCondition`, read as the
  permanent's own counters (`source-has-counter`, the level band's condition), for any counter name.
  A creature that grows into a keyword ("… it has flying and vigilance") reads through D605's general
  form as before.
- **Any static line under a condition**: "As long as <condition>, <line>" and "<line> as long as
  <condition>", where the line is anything that reads on its own as static entries only ("creatures
  you control get +5/+5", "… get +1/+1"). Each entry takes the condition as its `while`, asked live.
  A line that reads as anything else (a trigger, an ability), or whose entries already carry a
  condition, is refused, so nothing is read with half its meaning.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests: the cards read; Beastmaster Ascension gives +5/+5 at seven quest counters
and nothing at six; a creature has trample at three +1/+1 counters and not at two; "creatures you
control get +1/+1 as long as you control an artifact" pumps only with an artifact out.

## D1142 — "Choose a creature type." spells

D641 asked "As ~ enters, choose a creature type" for a permanent and kept the answer on it. A spell
that opens "Choose a creature type." asks the same question as it resolves (CR 205.3m), and the
rest of its text names "the chosen type" or "that type". That rest is read with the type written in:
- "permanents you control of that type" becomes "Elfs you control";
- "creatures that aren't of the chosen type" becomes "non-Elf creatures";
- "creature cards of the chosen type" becomes "Elf creature cards";
- "creatures you control of the chosen type" becomes "Elf creatures you control".

The plural is the type and an "s". That isn't English, but every plural reader here singularises
it back by dropping the "s" (D620), so "Elfs" and "Merfolks" read as Elf and Merfolk.

The rest is read twice:
- with a stand-in type when the card is compiled, which says whether it reads and which targets it
  takes as it is cast;
- with the chosen type as it resolves.

The targets are the same in both, because only the type's words differ. A rest that asks a question
of its own is refused: the type is already the spell's question. The bot names its own deck's
tribe, as D641's friendly choice does.

Read whole now (10): And They Shall Know No Fear, Coordinated Barrage, Distant Melody, Harmonized
Crescendo, Kindred Dominance, Kindred Judgment, Luminescent Rain, Pack's Disdain, Raise the
Palisade, Roar of the Crowd. Not read:
- Crippling Fear ("Non-Elf creatures get -3/-3" opening a sentence is not read);
- Bloodline Bidding (the mass return from a graveyard by type);
- Pact of the Serpent, Peer Pressure, Tsabo's Decree, and the "other than Wall" type changers.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The three test spells read whole.
- Naming Elf with two Elves and a Goblin draws two.
- Naming Goblin destroys both sides' Elves and keeps both Goblins.
- Naming Goblin with three Goblins and an Elf deals 3 to the target chosen as it was cast.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- The stand-in type used as it resolves instead of the chosen one (caught: 2 tests).
- "Creatures that aren't of the chosen type" read as the chosen type's creatures (caught).

Coverage: 15,437 of 31,900 cards (+35 over D1141's 15,402), 37,436 of 59,888 lines (+54). The difference also counts the D7xx
session's D798, merged in after D1141 was measured; D1142's own share is the 10 cards above.

## D1143 — decayed, and "You create"

Decayed (CR 702.147a) is the Innistrad: Midnight Hunt Zombie token's keyword: "This creature can't
block. When this creature attacks, sacrifice it at end of combat." It was in the list of keyword
names (so a printed "Decayed" was a declaration) but not a keyword, so every "create a 2/2 black
Zombie creature token with decayed" was refused by the token reader's read-back of its keywords.
It is now a keyword, and both halves are the engine's:
- can't block: `cantBlock`, set by the keyword where defender sets `cantAttack`;
- the sacrifice: the end of combat step sacrifices every attacker that has decayed, before
  combat is cleared (where myriad's tokens are exiled).

The sacrifice reads the keyword at end of combat rather than as a trigger on attacking. That differs
only for a decayed creature that lost its abilities mid-combat, which would stay.

"You create …" after a clause about another player (No Way Out, Taste of Death, Rat Out) is now
read as "Create …": the subject is the controller either way.

Read whole now (26 by the measure below; these are the ones probed by hand): Falcon Abomination, Flip the Switch, Ghoulish Procession, Rotten Reunion (decayed),
and Hornswoggle, No Way Out, Path to the World Tree, Rat Out, Send in the Pest, Supplant Form,
Taste of Death, Volatile Fault ("You create"). Not read:
- Diregraf Horde ("When you do" after the tokens);
- Jadar ("creatures with decayed" as a filter);
- Wilhelt ("if it didn't have decayed");
- Hobbling Zombie ("a 2/2 black Zombie creature", printed without "token").

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The token-maker reads whole, and its token has decayed.
- The token can't block.
- The token attacks, deals 2, and is gone after combat.
- A decayed token that does not attack stays.
- "Target opponent discards a card. You create a … token" makes the token for the caster, not the
  opponent.

Faults injected by hand: 3.
- Decayed without the block restriction (caught).
- No sacrifice at end of combat (caught).
- "You create" not rewritten (caught).

Coverage: 15,463 of 31,900 cards (+26 over D1142's 15,437), 37,472 of 59,888 lines (+36).

## D1144 — the Ring tempts you

"The Ring tempts you" (CR 701.54) is printed on 53 legal cards and was read on none. Now:
- **State.** `GameState.ring` holds, per seat, how many times the Ring has tempted that player and
  which creature they chose as Ring-bearer.
- **Ring-bearer.** `ringBearerOf` returns the chosen creature only while it is on the battlefield
  under that seat's control (CR 701.54c). One that leaves or changes control stops being the
  Ring-bearer without anything clearing it.
- **The emblem.** The first temptation gives the seat an emblem named The Ring in its command zone
  (CR 701.54a). Its printed text is the four abilities; its script is hand-written
  (`theRingScript`).
- **The clause.** "The Ring tempts you" asks the controller to choose a creature they control as
  it resolves, then calls `temptWithRing`.

The Ring's abilities by level:
1. "Your Ring-bearer is legendary and can't be blocked by creatures with greater power." This is a
   characteristic of the bearer: Legendary joins its supertypes, and the blocking half is skulk's
   rule word for word (CR 702.118a), so the bearer gets skulk.
2. "Whenever your Ring-bearer attacks, draw a card, then discard a card."
4. "Whenever your Ring-bearer deals combat damage to a player, each opponent loses 3 life."

Abilities 2 and 4 are triggers on the emblem. Each is read by the line reader from its sentence,
with "a creature you control" for "your Ring-bearer", plus a condition: the creature is the seat's
bearer and the Ring has tempted the seat often enough. Ability 3 (the blocker is sacrificed at end
of combat) is not done yet; D1145 adds it.

Read whole now include Bilbo, Retired Burglar, Enraged Huorn, Fiery Inscription, Claim the Precious,
Birthday Escape and Bombadil's Song. Not read yet:
- "Whenever the Ring tempts you" (7 cards);
- "your Ring-bearer" on cards (12 cards);
- "Whenever you choose a creature as your Ring-bearer" (Call of the Ring).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test Hobbit reads whole.
- One temptation choosing a Bear: level 1, the emblem in the command zone, and the Bear is a
  legendary Ring-bearer with skulk, while the Hobbit is not.
- A Ring-bearer that is sacrificed is no longer one, and the level stays.
- At level 1 an attack does not loot (nothing reaches the graveyard); at level 2 it loots (hand
  size the same, one more card in the graveyard).
- At level 4 an unblocked 2/2 Ring-bearer costs the opponent 5.

Faults injected by hand: 3.
- The level check dropped. This was caught only after the level-1 check was changed from hand size
  (which a loot leaves unchanged) to the graveyard.
- No skulk (caught).
- A bearer that left still counted (caught).

Coverage: 15,488 of 31,900 cards (+25 over D1143's 15,463), 37,503 of 59,888 lines (+31).

## D1145 — "Whenever the Ring tempts you", the third ability, and comma names before an "if"

Three pieces, finishing what D1144 started and fixing a reader gap it exposed.

**The event.** `ring-tempted` is raised once for each time the Ring tempted a seat, read in
`settle` off the difference in `GameState.ring` (the way life lost is read off its record). "Whenever
the Ring tempts you" is the trigger for it, matching only the tempted seat's own permanents.
"If you chose a creature other than ~ as your Ring-bearer" is an intervening condition (CR 603.4):
the seat's Ring-bearer is not the source.

**The Ring's third ability** (CR 701.54a): "Whenever your Ring-bearer becomes blocked by a
creature, that creature's controller sacrifices it at end of combat." It is done at the end of
combat step, beside decayed's sacrifice (D1143): every creature still blocking a seat's Ring-bearer,
once the Ring has tempted that seat three times, is sacrificed. The printed trigger fires at the
block and schedules the sacrifice. Reading the blocks at end of combat gives the same sacrifice,
and differs only for a Ring that reached three during the combat, after the block.

**Comma names before an "if".** The intervening-if trigger reader splits "When …, if …, …" on
commas, so a card whose own name has a comma failed whenever its name was in the prologue or the
condition: "When Tymna, the Weaver enters, if …", and "if you chose a creature other than Gandalf,
Friend of the Shire as your Ring-bearer". The name is now masked before the split and put back in
each part.

Read whole now include Faramir, Field Commander and Dúnedain Rangers. Others are one line short:
- Gandalf, Friend of the Shire: its flash grant, which is the D7xx session's D800;
- Nazgûl: the deck-construction line;
- Aragorn: the counter choice.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests, on a test Gandalf named with a comma:
- Its "Whenever the Ring tempts you, if you chose a creature other than ~ …, draw a card" reads
  whole.
- Choosing another creature as Ring-bearer draws.
- Choosing itself does not.
- At level 3 a 1/4 that blocks the Ring-bearer, and survives its damage, is sacrificed at end of
  combat; at level 2 it stays.

Faults injected by hand: 4.
- The event never raised (caught).
- The condition always true (caught).
- The third ability never reached (caught).
- The name mask off (caught: 2 tests).

Coverage: 15,495 of 31,900 cards (+7 over D1144's 15,488), 37,516 of 59,888 lines (+13).

## D1147 — "If damage would be dealt to ~, …"

Seventeen legal cards replace damage dealt to themselves (CR 615), and none was read. Now
`CardScript.damageToSelf` holds the replacement, and `dealDamage` applies it to each damage event
on its own, right after a shield counter, before anything is marked. Five shapes:
- "prevent that damage. Remove a +1/+1 counter from ~" (seven Phantoms): one counter per event, so
  three blockers cost three counters, and none to remove still prevents;
- "… while it has a +1/+1 counter on it, prevent that damage and remove a +1/+1 counter from it"
  (Oathsworn Knight, Undergrowth Champion): with no counter, the damage is dealt as normal;
- "… and remove that many +1/+1 counters" (Ugin's Conjurant);
- "put that many +1/+1 counters on it instead" (Phytohydra);
- "prevent that damage. Put a -1/-1 counter on ~ for each 1 damage prevented this way" (Phyrexian
  Hydra).

Undergrowth Champion. Not read:

- Phyrexian Vindicator (a reflexive damage trigger);
- Dralnu ("sacrifice that many permanents instead").

  is still there.
- A Knight with one counter loses it and takes no damage; with none it takes the 3.
- The Conjurant with five counters hit for 3 keeps two.
- Phytohydra hit for 4 gets four counters and no damage, and is a 5/5.

## D1148 — "Whenever you attack while …"

greater, …", and The Chief Warg prints "… while you control a creature with power 4 or greater".

"if", through the same reader and the same conditions (D1136's total power).

The difference is accepted and recorded. The printed "while" is a trigger condition, asked only as
the ability triggers (CR 603.2). An intervening "if" is asked again as it resolves (CR 603.4). The

## D1149 — goad

Goad (CR 701.38) is printed on 83 legal cards, and the engine had the effect, `goad`, since
Disrupt Decorum was hand-written. But the line reader read none of the printed forms except an
Aura's "is goaded" (D736). It now reads:
- "goad target creature" with any target phrase `targetSpecFrom` reads: "an opponent controls",
  "defending player controls", "up to one target creature";
- "goad each/all <scope>" through `massScope`: "each creature your opponents control", "all
  creatures you don't control". This form carries Disrupt Decorum's bot hint (`goadsOpponents`):
  in a duel a mass goad only sends the creatures at the caster.
- "goad it" and "goad that creature" after a clause that targeted it, through the borrowed
  referent (D530): "Tap target creature and goad it".

Until the goading player's next turn, a goaded creature attacks each combat if able, and attacks a
player other than the goader if able. These are the two halves `goad` sets, which combat already
enforces.

Read whole now: 13 of the 83 goad cards. The rest are short of something else:
- "for each opponent, goad target creature that player controls";
- "goad each creature that player controls" after a combat-damage trigger;
- "goad them" after "up to three target creatures";
- "goaded creatures" as a filter, and suspect.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests, in a three-player pod:
- Both test spells read whole.
- "Goad target creature. Draw a card." goads the target for the caster only, draws, and on its
  controller's turn the Bear must attack, may not attack the goader, and may attack the third
  player.
- A mass goad takes both opponents' creatures and not the caster's.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- A goad that only forces the attack, without "a player other than the goader" (caught).
- A mass goad that also takes the caster's own creatures (caught).

Coverage: 15,565 of 31,900 cards (+27 over D1148's 15,538), 37,612 of 59,888 lines (+41). The difference also counts the D7xx
session's D803 and D804, merged in after D1148 was measured; D1149's own share is the 13 goad cards.

## D1150 — amass

Amass (CR 701.47a) is printed on 66 legal cards and was read on none. "Amass Orcs 2": if you control
no Army creature, create a 0/0 black Orc Army creature token; then choose an Army creature you
control and put two +1/+1 counters on it; if it isn't an Orc, it becomes an Orc in addition to its
other types. War of the Spark's "Amass 2" is the same with Zombies.

`amass` in effects does exactly that. The token's counters go on before anything checks its
toughness, so the 0/0 never dies. Two choices are made for the player:
- **Which Army.** With several Armies the largest is chosen; there is no question asked. A player
  nearly always wants the biggest grown, and almost every board has one Army.
- **The new type.** It is a permanent subtype effect sourced at the Army itself. A `permanent`
  effect is removed when its source leaves (`removeEffectsFrom`), and the amass spell leaves the
  stack at once. A first version sourced it at the spell, and the Orc type vanished as the spell
  resolved; a test caught it.

Read whole now: 32 of the 66 amass cards. The rest are short of:
- "amass … X, where X is …";
- "When you do" after the amass;
- "the amassed Army";
- other lines.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The three test spells read whole.
- With no Army, "Amass Orcs 2" makes a 2/2 Orc Army, and "Amass Orcs 3" then grows the same Army
  to 5/5 without a second token.
- "Amass 2" makes a Zombie Army, and amassing Orcs onto it keeps it Zombie and makes it an Orc,
  at 4/4.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- A new Army made every time (caught: 2 tests).
- One counter instead of N (caught: 2 tests).

Coverage: 15,609 of 31,900 cards (+44 over D1149's 15,565), 37,681 of 59,888 lines (+69). The difference also counts the D7xx
session's D805, merged in after D1149 was measured; D1150's own share is the 32 amass cards.

## D1151 — populate

Populate (CR 701.36a) is printed on 26 legal cards and was read on none: "Choose a creature token
you control, then create a token that's a copy of that creature token." It is now a clause:
- **The question.** It is asked as the effect resolves, from the creature tokens you control.
- **The copy.** It is made with `copyAsToken` off the token's own definition, which is its
  copiable values, so counters, damage and effects on it are not copied.
- **With no token, nothing happens.** A nontoken creature is never offered.

"Create a 1/1 green Saproling creature token, then populate" makes the first token before the
question is asked: the split at a chain's first question (D418) runs the clauses before it first.

Read whole now: 18 of the 26 populate cards. Not read:
- "populate X times";
- "The token created this way gains haste" and "The token enters tapped and attacking";
- "Whenever you attack with one or more Elves";
- modal and other lines.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both test spells read whole.
- "Create a 1/1 Saproling, then populate" leaves two Saprolings, both tokens.
- With only a nontoken Bear, "Populate." does nothing.

Faults injected by hand: 1.
- A nontoken creature offered (caught: the Bear is copied).

## D1152 — flip a coin

"Flip a coin. If you win the flip, X. [If you lose the flip, Y.]" (CR 705) is printed on 66 legal
cards and was read on none. Three pieces:
- **The flip.** `flipCoin` uses the game's seeded generator, as every shuffle does, so a replay
  flips the same. Each flip is recorded in `GameState.coinFlips`.
- **The log.** The action's log line reads the new flips off that record: "Nick wins a coin flip"
  sits beside what the flip did. A coin flip is the one random event a player has to see the
  result of to follow the game.
- **The reader.** `coinFlipGroup` reads the sentences as one group. Each branch goes through
  `composeEffects` on its own. A branch's targets are chosen as the ability is put on the stack, and
  the losing branch does nothing with them. It is refused when both branches target, when either
  asks a question, or when anything follows the branches.

Not done: flips a player may choose the outcome of (Krark's Thumb) and "flip until you lose".

Read whole now: 13 of the 66, among them Boompile, Goblin Archaeologist, Frenetic Efreet, Orcish
Captain, Skyclaw Thrash, Stitch in Time and Winter Sky. The rest have riders this group refuses:
- "and you decide whether to flip again";
- "for each flip you win";
- the "next time that source would deal damage" replacements.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- The test spell reads whole.
- Across twenty seeds the flip is both won and lost. Each time the life change is that branch's
  (+5 or -2), the flip is recorded for the caster, and the log line says the result.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- The branches swapped (caught).
- Every flip won (caught).

Coverage: 15,660 of 31,900 cards (+27 over D1151's 15,633), 37,739 of 59,888 lines (+31). The difference also counts the D7xx
session's D807, merged in after D1151 was measured; D1152's own share is the 13 coin-flip cards.

## D1153 — manifest

Manifest (CR 701.40) is printed on 54 legal cards and was read on none. The engine already played
face-down creatures for morph: a 2/2 with no name, text or mana cost, and a special action to turn
it face up. Manifest is that, put onto the battlefield from the top of the library instead of
cast:
- **The effect.** `manifestTop` moves the top card face down onto the battlefield and marks it
  `manifested`.
- **Turning up.** `turnUpCostOf` is now the one answer to "what does turning this face up cost",
  for the offer and the action alike:
  - a morph or megamorph cost, as before;
  - for a manifested creature card, its mana cost (CR 701.40b).
  A manifested land or other noncreature card has no cost and stays a 2/2. The flag is cleared as
  it turns up.
- **The reader.** "Manifest the top card of your library", and "the top two / three cards".

Read whole now: 9 of the 54, among them Mastery of the Unseen, Qarsi High Priest, Soul Summons,
Sultai Emissary and Wildcall. Not read:
- "manifest dread" (look at two, manifest one);
- "manifest the top card of target player's library";
- "manifest X cards", and riders after the manifest.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test spell reads whole.
- With a 4/4 Bear on top, it arrives face down as a 2/2, the only turn-up offered is its own, and
  turning it up pays {1}{G} and makes it the named 4/4.
- With a Forest on top, it stays face down and nothing offers to turn it up.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- Any manifested card turnable (caught: the Forest is offered).
- The manifest mark never set (caught: the Bear is not offered).

The existing morph tests (20) pass unchanged on the shared `turnUpCostOf`.

## D1154 — roll a d20, with its table

The Forgotten Realms cards print a die roll on one line and its results on the lines under it:
"Roll a d20." then "1—9 | …", "10—19 | …", "20 | …" (CR 706.2). Each printed line was read alone, so
none of the 37 table cards was read. The table is now read as one:
- **The group.** `dieTableFor` finds the roll line and claims the rows beneath it. It requires that
  they cover every result from 1 to the die's size once, with no gap and no overlap.
- **The marker.** The roll is replaced by a marker clause, "roll a die for table N", and the line
  around it is read as usual: a spell's line, a trigger's "When ~ enters, …", an ability's
  "{T}: …". A first marker was a control character, which the clause readers drop before any
  reader sees it, so nothing read; the plain-words marker does.
- **The rows.** Each row is read by `composeEffects`. A row that targets or asks a question is
  refused: a table's targets depend on the result, and this engine chooses targets on the stack.
- **The roll.** `rollDie` uses the seeded generator, and the log says "Nick rolls 14 on a d20".
- **Line counts.** The printed lines are reported compiled together, or unread together.
- **The table store.** Tables are kept by their own text, so compiling a card again does not grow
  the store.

Read whole now: 8 of the 61 die-roll cards (Chaos Channeler, Farideh's Fireball, Hoarding Ogre,
Lightfoot Rogue, Nothic, Overwhelming Encounter, Recruitment Drive, Sylvan Shepherd). Not read:
- rows that target;
- "roll a d20. When you do …", and "… equal to the result";
- "roll two d8 and choose one result".

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- A three-row d20 spell reads, with all four printed lines compiled.
- A table with a gap stays unread, and a whole table on an enters trigger reads.
- Across thirty seeds each roll gains the life of the row it lands in (1, 3 or 10), and the log
  line says the number.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- The row bounds off by one (caught).
- The coverage check skipped (caught: the table with a gap reads).

Coverage: 15,715 of 31,900 cards (+41 over D1153's 15,674), 37,832 of 59,888 lines (+73). The difference also counts the D7xx
session's D809, merged in after D1153 was measured; D1154's own share is the 8 die-roll cards.

## D1155 — incubate

Incubate N (CR 701.53a) is printed on 30 legal cards and was read on none: "Create an Incubator token
with N +1/+1 counters on it and '{2}: Transform this artifact.' It transforms into a 0/0 Phyrexian
artifact creature." Two pieces:
- **The effect.** `incubate` makes the colorless Incubator artifact token and puts the counters on
  it.
- **The token's script.** `INCUBATOR` is hand-written, as Clue's is, and found by the token's name.
  It is looked up in `scriptFor` beside the Ring, not listed in `ALL`, because no starter deck makes an
  Incubator and the registry test requires each listed script to name something in the pool. Its one
  ability, {2}, transforms it.

A transforming permanent stays the same permanent with its counters (CR 712.18). So the transform
is a permanent effect on the token itself: it becomes a creature and a Phyrexian, base 0/0, and the
counters make it N/N. The ability is offered only while it is not a creature, which is the front
face.

Read whole now: 12 of the 30 (Compleated Huntmaster, Converter Beast, Eyes of Gitaxias, Gift of
Compleation, Ichor Drinker, Infected Defector, Injector Crocodile, Marauding Dreadship, Merciless
Repurposing, Phyrexian Awakening and two more). Not read:
- "incubate X, where X is …";
- "If they do, you incubate 2" after a counter-unless.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test spell reads whole.
- "Incubate 3" makes an Incubator artifact, not a creature, with three counters, and its transform
  is offered.
- Paying {2} makes it a 3/3 Phyrexian artifact creature, and the transform is not offered again
  even with mana left.

Faults injected by hand: 2.
- No counters (caught).
- The transform offered again (caught). It was missed the first time because the test spent the
  only two lands on the transform, so no further offer was affordable either way; the test now has
  four lands.

session's D810, merged in after D1154 was measured; D1155's own share is the 12 incubate cards.

## D1156 — suspect

Suspect (CR 701.60) is printed on 26 legal cards and was read on none. A suspected
creature has menace and can't block for as long as it is on the battlefield. `CardInstance.suspected`
holds it and `characteristicsOf` turns it into menace and `cantBlock`.

Three printed forms:
- **"Suspect target creature"** and "suspect up to one target creature".
- **"Suspect it"** with no earlier target is the source (Barbed Servitor, Person of Interest), and
  "suspect enchanted creature" is the Aura's host (Convenient Target, Incriminating Impetus).
- **"Suspect it" after a target.** After a creature target the D530 borrow reads it. After a
  graveyard card target (It Doesn't Add Up: "Return target creature card from your graveyard to the
  battlefield. Suspect it.") it is read beside D723's counter: the returned card is suspected, and
  a card that never arrived is not. The plain reading of "it" as the source is refused after a card
  target: the spell would have suspected itself, a wrong card that the first version of this test
  caught.

**A fix to D1153.** `relocate` now clears `manifested` and `suspected` when a card leaves the
battlefield. Before, a manifested card that died and came back face up still carried the flag, so
it would have been offered a turn-up for its mana cost.

Read whole now: 9 of the 26 (Barbed Servitor, Caught Red-Handed, Convenient Target, Incriminating
Impetus, It Doesn't Add Up, J. Jonah Jameson, Person of Interest, Presumed Dead, Reasonable Doubt).
Not read:
- "if it's suspected" and "if it's not suspected" (Agrus Kos, Repeat Offender, Rubblebelt Braggart);
- "suspected creature" as a filter (Deadly Complication, Rune-Brand Juggler);
- "no longer suspected" (Absolving Lammasu, Eliminate the Impossible);
- suspect counters (Investigator's Journal).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "Suspect it" on an arrival: the creature has menace and can't block.
- Destroyed, it is no longer suspected.
- "Suspect it" after a graveyard target suspects the returned creature, not the spell.
- A manifested, suspected card moved to the graveyard has neither flag.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- No menace and no can't-block.
- No reset in `relocate`.
- No graveyard-target reading: the card is then unread rather than misread.

Coverage: 15,742 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1155's 15,733), 37,871 of 59,888 lines (+13).

## D1157 — "if it's suspected", and "If …, A. Otherwise, B."

Two pieces:
- **The condition.** "If ~ is suspected", "if it's suspected", "if ~ isn't suspected" and "if it's not
  suspected" are a new static condition, `source-suspected`, beside D978's `source-prepared`. Any
  reader that asks a static condition can ask it: intervening-if triggers, "as long as" statics, and
  the branch below.
- **"If <condition>, A. Otherwise, B."** `ifOtherwiseGroup` reads the two sentences as one effect.
  The condition is anything `interveningConditionFor` reads. It is checked as the ability resolves,
  and then one branch runs. It is refused when both branches target, when either asks a question, or
  when anything follows. Comma names are masked before the split, as in D1145.

Read whole now: Rubblebelt Braggart ("Whenever ~ attacks, if it's not suspected, you may suspect
it") and Repeat Offender ("{2}{B}: If ~ is suspected, put a +1/+1 counter on it. Otherwise, suspect
it."). So 11 of the 26 legal suspect cards read whole. The other 6 legal "If …, A. Otherwise, B."
lines ask conditions or effects that are not read (day and night, seek, "has toughness 5 or
greater").

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- The first activation suspects the creature and adds no counter; the second adds a counter.
- The attack trigger suspects it; once it is suspected, the attack puts nothing on the stack and
  asks nothing.

Faults injected by hand: 2, both caught.
- The condition inverted.
- The branch always taking the first half.

Coverage: 15,752 of 31,900 cards (+10 over D1156's 15,742), 37,885 of 59,888 lines (+14). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D811, merged in after D1156 was measured; D1157's own share is the 2 cards above.
## D813 — Ward at the end of a keyword list: Sheltered by Ghosts

Most-played order: Sheltered by Ghosts (rank 1206), and the Equipment and lords that print ward
last in a list: Falcon's Wing Harness, Lavaspur Boots, Winged Boots, Super Strength, Giant Ankheg,
One, Borg Evolved, and Shelob's "Other Spiders you control have deathtouch and ward {2}".

D736 turned "has ward {N}" into the quoted ward trigger the grant readers know, but only when ward
was the whole predicate. `wardAsQuoted` now also takes a keyword list in front of it ("has lifelink
and ward {2}", "have trample, lifelink, and ward {2}"), keeps the list under its verb and gives the
ward a verb of its own: `has lifelink and has "Ward {2}"`. The static grant reader already split on
`and has "…"`. The attachment's quoted reader now accepts the second "has" too. Nothing new in the
engine: the keywords go through `grantedKeywords` / `thresholdPredicate` and the ward through
`grantedTriggers`, as before.

Still unread: The Tarrasque ("… and ward {10} as long as it was cast": a condition about how it
entered) and the "exactly one creature" and "during your turn" wrappers on Solitary Defiance and Yuna.

equipped creature, and an opponent's removal on it asks for {1}; an anthem's trample, lifelink and

## D1158 — collect evidence

Collect evidence N (CR 701.59a) is printed on 25 legal cards and was read on none. To collect
evidence N, a player exiles cards from their graveyard whose mana values total N or more.
`evidencePlan` (effects.ts) picks the cards:
- the biggest first, so the fewest leave;
- cards with a flashback or escape of their own last, as D613's graveyard costs order them;
- never the ability's own card.

It returns `null` when the graveyard totals less, which is when evidence cannot be collected (CR
701.59b). The player does not choose the cards, as with D613's graveyard costs.

Two forms are read:
- **As an ability cost**: "{T}, Collect evidence 3: …" (Forensic Researcher). It is a new
  `totalManaValue` on D613's `AbilityCost.exileFromGraveyard`, so the existing offer check,
  refusal and payment all apply. The ability is not offered when the graveyard totals less, and a
  request is refused with "the cards in your graveyard total less than mana value 3". A mana
  ability with this cost stays unread, as every other graveyard cost on a mana ability does
  (Cryptex).
- **As an effect**: `collectEvidence` exiles the plan, or leaves the board unchanged. So "you may
  collect evidence 4. If you do, …" (Izoni) and "When you do, …" (Sample Collector) go through
  `optionalEffect`, where an X that changed nothing did not happen. With too little in the
  graveyard the yes does nothing and the rest does not follow.

Read whole now: Forensic Researcher, Izoni, Center of the Web, Sample Collector. The cost also reads
on Hedge Whisperer, Kylox's Voltstrider, Polygraph Orb and Tenth District Hero, which stay unread
on their effects. Not read:
- "As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may collect evidence N" with "if evidence was
  collected" (8 cards; next, modelled on kicker);
- "Whenever you collect evidence";
- ward and bestow paid by collecting evidence;
- collect evidence X.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- The cost exiles two 2-mana-value cards for 3 and leaves the third; the ability resolves.
- A graveyard totalling 2: no offer, and the refusal names collect evidence 3.
- "You may collect evidence 4. If you do, you gain 3 life": the yes exiles both cards and the life
  follows.
- With a graveyard totalling 2, nothing is exiled and no life is gained.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- No total check.
- The effect collecting nothing.
- The cost not exiling.

Coverage: 15,761 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1157's 15,752), 37,901 of 59,888 lines (+16).
## D814 — A bonus while the host is legendary, a colour or a creature type: Champion's Helm

Most-played order: Champion's Helm (rank 1219), and the attachments that print "As long as
enchanted/equipped creature is X, it …", usually beside a plain bonus line: Butcher's Cleaver,
Gimli's Axe, Hero's Heirloom, Bladed Bracers, Heavy Mattock, Silver-Inlaid Dagger, True-Faith Censer,
Sharpened Pitchfork, Equestrian Skill, and the Shadowmoor and Eventide colour Auras (Edge of the
Divinity, Clout of the Dominus, Runes of the Deus, Steel of the Godhead, Shield of the Oversoul and
others). 18 of the 31 printings read in the probe; the rest of the corpus total below is the legal-card count.

**Engine.** An attachment's one bonus became one effect on its host. A `PumpOptions` can now carry
`alsoParts`: further effects from the same source on the same scope, each with its own filters.
`staticEffect` (the Equipment's equip) and `addAuraEffect` push them. `removeEffectsFrom` already
removes everything from a source, so they leave with the attachment. Two host filters join the
D735/D941 ones on `ContinuousEffect`: `onlySubtypes` (any one of them) and `onlyColours` (any one,
after layer 5). Legendary, tapped and untapped use `onlyKind`; attacking uses `onlyAttacking`.

**Reader.** `hostConditionalParts` reads each "As long as <host> creature is <legendary | tapped |
untapped | attacking | a colour | a Human[ or an Angel]>, it <predicate>" through `attachmentBonus`.
"An additional +1/+1" is read as "+1/+1": the word only says the plain bonus still applies. It
reads only parts that help and only a size or a keyword. Grants, harmful parts (Ray of Frost) and
"has defender" / "has vigilance" / "is attacking alone" / "is face down" stay unread. Conditional
lines are not taken beside a plain bonus line that did not read, so a card never claims a line
it does not give.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- the Helm's +2/+2 reaches any host, and its hexproof only a legendary one. Re-equipping moves both;
- "a Human or an Angel" covers an Angel and not a Bear;
- "an additional +1/+1" makes a Human +2/+2;
- an Aura's two colour lines give a white host one bonus, a black host the other, and a green
  host neither.

Faults injected by script: 10 of 10 caught. They cover both engine filters, the subtype
disjunction, `modsFrom`, the Equipment and Aura paths that push the parts, and the reader's
legendary, "additional", second-type and filter handling.

- engine tests: 6166, all passing (on 1824f47)
- Coverage: 15,766 to 15,772 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 37,907 to 37,919 of 59,888 lines, against 1824f47.

## D1159 — "you may collect evidence N" as an additional cost

"As an additional cost to cast this spell, you may collect evidence N." is printed on 8 legal cards
and was read on none. It is an optional cost announced with the spell, and the text asks about it
as "if evidence was collected" (CR 701.59, 601.2b).

It is read on the kicker's machinery, the way D1103's "Kicker—Pay 3 life" is:
- The declaration becomes a free kicker whose `additional` is D1158's graveyard cost (`totalManaValue`).
- "Evidence was collected" becomes "this spell was kicked" on a spell and "it was kicked" on a
  permanent, so the kicker readers read the rest.
- `kicker.additional` now also holds a graveyard cost. The kicked cast is offered only when
  `graveyardCostPlan` finds enough, and the cards are exiled as the spell is cast.
- The description is the printed sentence.

Read whole now:
- Extract a Confession: "If evidence was collected, instead each opponent sacrifices a creature
  with the greatest power".
- Vitu-Ghazi Inspector: "When ~ enters, if evidence was collected, put a +1/+1 counter on target
  creature and you gain 2 life".

Not read: the cards whose other half is unread, and Bite Down on Crime's "costs {2} less to cast if
evidence was collected".

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- The evidence cast is offered beside the plain one with 4 in the graveyard, and not with 2.
- A spell: collected, it exiles both cards and takes the bigger branch; not collected, neither.
- A creature's "When this creature enters, if evidence was collected" fires only on the evidence
  cast.
- Asked for with too little in the graveyard, the evidence cast is refused.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The offer not checking the graveyard.
- The cost not exiling.
- "Evidence was collected" not rewritten: the cards are then unread.

Coverage: 15,770 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1158's 15,761), 37,914 of 59,888 lines (+13). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D813, merged in after D1158 was measured; D1159's own share is the 2 cards above.
## D815 — "~ can't attack or block unless <condition>": Topiary Stomper

Most-played order: Topiary Stomper (rank 1208), and the drawbacks printed the same way on the
card itself, wherever the condition is one the static reader already knows: "unless you control
seven or more lands", "unless you control another artifact", "unless there are N or more cards in
your graveyard", "unless you control another Giant", "unless it's equipped" (Training Drone) and
others. 14 cards in the probe, among them Bast, Panther Goddess, Gorilla Pack, Felhide Brawler,
Mindless Null and Slumbering Dragon.

**Engine.** `ContinuousEffect.while` gains `{ kind: 'not', of }`: any other condition, negated,
asked in `conditionMet` like the rest. That is the whole engine change: the restriction is a
self static (`cantAttack` / `cantBlock`) whose condition is the printed one negated, asked live.
The creature can attack the moment the seventh land arrives, and stops if one leaves.

**Reader.** In `conditionalStaticFromLine`, after the D798 general wrapper: "<self> can't (attack
or block | attack | block) unless <condition>". The subject must be the card's name, its short
name or "this creature". The condition goes through `staticCondition`, which also learns "you
have N or fewer cards in hand" (Hazoret the Fervent's line; the card still has an unread
activated ability) and "it's equipped".

Not read, as before: conditions about combat ("unless a creature with greater power also
attacks"), payments and sacrifices as attack costs, "defending player is the monarch / poisoned",
"more creatures than defending player", and "another creature with power 4 or greater" (Rhonas,
which needs a power filter on `board-has`).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- with six lands the Stomper can neither attack nor block, and with seven it can and an attack
  is accepted;
- the seventh land played in the main phase lifts the restriction at once;
- a creature whose condition is "one or fewer cards in hand" is held home by a hand of two and
  freed by a hand of one, and its blocking is never restricted;
- "unless it's equipped" restricts the Drone bare and frees it once equipped.

And in compile.test, D502's pin "leaves a line unread: an 'unless' restriction" (Deep-Sea Terror's
line) moved from the unread table to a positive test: the line reads as `cantAttack` under
`{ kind: 'not', of: controller-graveyard 7 }`. The first gate caught it; the move is deliberate.

Faults injected by script: 7 of 7 caught. They cover the negation in the engine and in the
reader, each half of "attack or block", "or fewer" read wrongly or not at all, and "it's
equipped".

- engine tests: 6176, all passing (on 9eb329f)
- Coverage: 15,786 to 15,803 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 37,939 to 37,961 of 59,888 lines, against 9eb329f.

## D1160 — the initiative and Undercity

"You take the initiative" (CR 722) is printed on 23 legal cards and was read on none. The engine
had `GameState.initiative` as a tabletop marker only, with no dungeon behind it. Now:

- **Dungeons** (CR 309). `DUNGEONS` holds each dungeon's rooms, top first, with each room's text and
  the rooms below it. A dungeon card is made in the seat's command zone the way the Ring is (D1144),
  and `GameState.dungeon` holds the seat's marker: the dungeon, the room, and the card.
  `dungeonScript` gives the card one reflexive trigger per room, keyed by the room's name. Each
  room's ability is read from its text by the ordinary clause readers, so it goes on the stack and
  chooses its targets there (CR 309.4c).
- **Venture** (CR 701.49). `ventureInto` moves the marker into the top room, or into the room chosen
  below the current one, and queues that room's trigger. When two rooms are below, the player is
  asked "Venture into which room?"; the bot takes the first. The bottom room completes the dungeon
  once it has resolved: the card leaves the command zone and `dungeonsCompleted` records it (CR
  309.7).
- **The initiative.**
  - `takeInitiative` sets the seat and moves The Initiative's card into that seat's command zone,
    or makes it.
  - The card's "At the beginning of your upkeep, venture into Undercity" is an ordinary step
    trigger (CR 722.3).
  - A creature that deals combat damage to the seat with the initiative takes it for its controller
    (CR 722.4). That venture goes on the stack as the card's "taken" trigger, because it asks which
    room.
- **Undercity**'s nine rooms all read. Throne of the Dead Three is built on the dig reader, with
  the three +1/+1 counters, hexproof until your next turn and the shuffle added after it. It reads
  "Put a creature card from among them" as "You may put …", so a player may take none; that is the
  one difference from the printed room.
- The view carries each seat's dungeon and room.

TODO(scryfall-dungeons): the room text is written from the printed card. Dungeons are not legal
cards, the local corpus has none, and this environment's proxy refuses api.scryfall.com. Check the
text against the Scryfall import.

Read whole now: Aarakocra Sneak, Avenging Hunter, Feywild Caretaker, Goliath Paladin, Passageway
Seer, Underdark Explorer. Not read:
- "venture into the dungeon" and the other three dungeons (next);
- "if you've completed a dungeon";
- "whenever you complete a dungeon".

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test card reads whole.
- Taking the initiative: the seat has it, The Initiative and Undercity are in its command zone, and
  the marker is on Secret Entrance.
- At the next upkeep the player chooses Lost Well over Forge and the marker moves there.
- Combat damage to the seat with the initiative: the attacker's seat takes it, the card moves, and
  that seat ventures into its own Undercity.
- From Catacombs, a venture into Throne of the Dead Three completes Undercity: the card leaves and
  the completion is counted.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- No upkeep venture.
- No steal on combat damage.
- No completion.
- The room choice ignored.

Coverage: 15,793 of 31,900 cards (+23 over D1159's 15,770), 37,957 of 59,888 lines (+43). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D814, merged in after D1159 was measured; D1160's own share is the 6 initiative cards above, plus lines on cards that stay unread for other reasons.
## D816 — Dark Confidant compiled: the card put into the hand, and its mana value in life

Most-played order: Dark Confidant (rank 1225), with Dark Tutelage, Darkstar Augur and Pain Seer,
which print the same two sentences.

Dark Confidant has had a hand-written script since the first pool, and that script used `draw`.
The card says "reveal the top card of your library and put that card into your hand", which is
not a draw (CR 121.1). So the hand-written Confidant was seen by "whenever an opponent draws a
card" and counted toward the turn's draws, and the printed card is not. The compiled reading now
covers all four printings. The hand-written script still wins in play (`scriptForCard` prefers it),
so the Confidant in the pool keeps drawing until that script is corrected; that is the next
increment (D817).

**Reader.** `clausesOf` joins the two sentences into one clause ("… put it into your hand and lose
life equal to its mana value"), since the second is about the card the first moved. `readEffect`
reads that clause: take the top card of the controller's library, move it to the hand with
`moveToHand`, and lose life equal to its printed mana value (`cmc`, the same in every zone, CR
202.3). An empty library puts nothing and costs nothing; it is not a draw from an empty library,
so it does not lose the game.

Still unread: Ad Nauseam's "You may repeat this process any number of times", and Sorin the
Mirthless's "you may reveal that card … If you do".

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- with a three-mana card on top, the upkeep puts it into the hand, takes three life, and does not
  count as a draw;
- a land on top costs nothing;
- with an empty library nothing is put, nothing is lost, and the seat has not lost the game.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught. They cover the joiner, a draw in place of the move (the
first version of the test read `drew`, which is cleared when announced, and missed it; it now
reads `cardsDrawnThisTurn`), no life loss, the bottom card instead of the top, and a fixed
amount.

- engine tests: 6180, all passing (on 5c4bad1)
- Coverage: 15,806 to 15,810 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 37,966 to 37,970 of 59,888 lines, against 5c4bad1.

## D1161 — "until your next turn"

"Until your next turn" (CR 611.2b) is on 195 legal cards with these shapes. On most of them it was
the one thing unread: "target creature gets -4/-0 until your next turn", "until your next turn,
creatures you control get +1/+0", "up to two target creatures can't attack or block until your next
turn".

`readEffect` now reads such a clause as the same clause with "until end of turn" ("this turn" for a
"can't" restriction). Every continuous effect that reading makes and that would end with the turn
lasts until its controller's next turn instead. That is `until-controllers-next-turn`, goad's
duration since D623, which ends in that player's untap step. This applies only to a clause about
what something is or may do ("gets", "gains", "has", "loses", "can't") and not to one about playing
or casting. Those are the readings made of continuous effects; a permission or a delayed effect
"until end of turn" is bounded some other way, and lengthening its continuous half would end the
rest too soon.

Also read now:
- "target creature can't attack this turn";
- "target creature can't attack or block this turn".

They sit beside D528's "can't block this turn", aimed at somebody else's creature.

Read whole now: 41 of the 195, among them Hag of Inner Weakness, Azorius Arrester, Lyev Skyknight,
Martial Law, Inaction Injunction and Netter en-Dal. Some were read before through goad's and the
life lock's own readers. Two rooms of the other dungeons now read: Fungi Cavern and Twisted
Caverns.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- -4/-0 until your next turn holds through the opponent's turn and ends as yours begins.
- "Can't attack until your next turn" stops the attack on the opponent's next turn, and not on the
  one after yours.
- "Can't attack this turn" is a can't-attack effect that ends with the turn.

Faults injected by hand: 2, both caught.
- The duration not lengthened.
- "Can't attack" read as "can't block".

Coverage: 15,826 of 31,900 cards (+33 over D1160's 15,793), 38,009 of 59,888 lines (+52). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D815, merged in after D1160 was measured.
## D817 — The hand-written Dark Confidant puts the card into the hand rather than drawing it

D816 noted it: the hand-written `DARK_CONFIDANT` script, which `scriptForCard` prefers over the
compiled reading, used `draw`. The card puts the revealed card into its owner's hand, which is
not a draw (CR 121.1). As a draw:
- an opponent's "whenever an opponent draws a card" (Orcish Bowmasters, Notion Thief) saw it;
- it counted toward the turn's draws, which decides "the first card you draw each turn" and
  miracle;
- with an empty library it was a draw from an empty library.

The effect is now the compiled one's move: the top card of the library, `moveToHand`, then life
equal to its printed mana value. Ashen Rite, the built-in deck that runs two Confidants, plays it
correctly now. No new reading, so no coverage change.

**Tests.** 1 engine test beside the original "Dark Confidant charges you for the card it just
drew", which passes unchanged: in Ashen Rite, the Confidant's upkeep puts the library's top card
into the hand and leaves the turn's draw count where it was.

Faults injected by script: 2 of 2 caught (a draw in place of the move, the bottom card in place of
the top). The first run missed both because the new test's name did not contain the filter; it
was renamed and both are caught.

- engine tests: 6181, all passing (on 963849a)
- Coverage: unchanged, 15,810 of 31,900 cards and 37,970 of 59,888 lines, against 963849a.

## D1162 — a punisher, once

"Each player loses 2 life unless they discard a card" (Veils of Fear's room) and its kin were
unread: "each opponent loses 3 life unless they discard a card", "each player loses 4 life unless
they sacrifice a nontoken creature", "target opponent loses 2 life unless that player sacrifices a
creature", "… unless they sacrifice an artifact, a creature, or a land" (Sandfall Cell's room).
D730's `punisherRounds` read only Torment of Hailfire's three-way form.

`punisherOnce` asks each player it names, in turn order:
1. to lose the life, or to do the other thing, which is offered only to a player who can;
2. then, only of those who chose it, which card or which permanent.

The choice is recorded as the second question is reached, in D730's `AutomationState.punisher`, so
that question is empty for everyone else. A player with nothing to give is offered only the life,
and a one-answer question is not asked at all. `sacrificeKinds` reads what may be sacrificed: "a",
"an", "nontoken", and a list joined by commas and "or". The bot loses the life while it has more
than 9, otherwise gives up its cheapest card or permanent.

Read whole now: Bellowing Mauler, Hag of Ceaseless Torment, Nicol Bolas, the Deceiver and Painful
Quandary. Two rooms of Tomb of Annihilation read too: Veils of Fear and Sandfall Cell. Three dungeon
rooms remain unread before "venture into the dungeon" can be read: Oubliette, Runestone Caverns and
Mad Wizard's Lair.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- One player discards, so the card goes and the life stays; the other refuses and loses 2.
- A player with nothing to discard is not asked, and loses the life; the player who can is offered
  both.
- The sacrifice: a land goes instead of the life; a player with no permanent loses the life.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- Every choice costing the life.
- The other choice always offered.
- A land not counted for "an artifact, a creature, or a land".

Coverage: 15,832 of 31,900 cards (+6 over D1161's 15,826), 38,015 of 59,888 lines (+6). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D816, merged in after D1161 was measured.
## D818 — "Whenever a permanent you control enters tapped": Amulet of Vigor

Most-played order: Amulet of Vigor (rank 1266). It is the corpus's one printing of the sentence.
Tiller Engine prints the same prologue on a modal trigger and stays unread.

**Engine.** The entry trigger gains `tapped?: true`, the mirror of D679's `untapped` (Mystic
Sanctuary). It is asked of the arrival through the `subjectTapped` the engine already sets on an
entry: a land that entered tapped and was then tapped or untapped by something else is still a
tapped arrival.

**Reader.** In `lineScriptFor`, "Whenever <a/an/another/one or more> … you control enters tapped,
<effect>" is read as the same line without "tapped", and each trigger it makes takes `tapped`. That
happens only when everything it makes is an entry trigger. "Untap it" in that sentence is the
permanent that entered. The general "untap it" reader (D777) is a permanent's own trigger ("Whenever
~ attacks, untap it") and would untap the Amulet, so this reader untaps the trigger's subject
instead. No other card prints "… enters, untap it" about a board entry, so nothing else had that
misreading.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- a land that enters tapped triggers the Amulet once and is untapped when the trigger resolves;
- a Forest entering untapped triggers nothing, and without the Amulet the tapped land stays
  tapped.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught (no matcher, an inverted matcher, the flag not set, and
the untap aimed at the Amulet).

- engine tests: 6184, all passing (on b54095c)
- Coverage: 15,810 to 15,811 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 37,970 to 37,971 of 59,888 lines, against b54095c.

## D819 — "Other enchantments / artifacts you control have …": Sterling Grove

Most-played order: Sterling Grove (rank 1254). The same reader covers "Other artifacts you control
have …" (Inspirit, Flagship Vessel prints it under a station threshold, so that card stays
unread for other reasons) and "Enchantments you control have …".

**Engine.** Three static scopes join D801's `permanents-you-control` pair:
- `enchantments-you-control`;
- `other-enchantments-you-control`, which excludes the source;
- `other-artifacts-you-control`.

Each is answered in `effectApplies` off the live type line and the controller, like the rest.
`automation.ts`'s static mapping passes them through. The older `other-enchantments` (Aura Flux's
"Other enchantments have …") is everyone's enchantments, and stays as it was.

**Reader.** D801's "(other )?(permanents|artifacts|lands) you control have <keywords>" also takes
"enchantments", and "other" now also applies to artifacts and enchantments. Still only
indestructible, hexproof and shroud.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- under a Grove our other enchantment has shroud, while the Grove itself, the opponent's
  enchantment and our artifact do not;
- under "Other artifacts you control have indestructible" our other artifact has it, while the
  source, the opponent's artifact and our enchantment do not.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught. They cover the source not excluded, any controller,
any card type, the mapping dropping the scope, and "other artifacts" read as all artifacts.

- engine tests: 6187, all passing (on 3661d19)
- Coverage: 15,811 to 15,812 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 37,971 to 37,973 of 59,888 lines, against 3661d19.

## D1163 — venture into the dungeon

"Venture into the dungeon" (CR 701.49a) is printed on 38 legal cards and was read on none. D1160 built
the dungeons, the venture and Undercity for the initiative. This increment adds the other three
dungeons and the reader:

- **The dungeons.** `DUNGEONS` gains Lost Mine of Phandelver (7 rooms), Dungeon of the Mad Mage (9)
  and Tomb of Annihilation (5), each read room by room as Undercity is. The room text is written from
  the printed cards, with the same TODO(scryfall-dungeons) as D1160.
- **The reader.** A seat in no dungeon is asked which of the three; Undercity is not offered (CR
  309.3). A seat in a dungeon, Undercity included, moves down in that one and is asked which room
  when two are below. The bot takes the first dungeon and the first room.
- **The rooms that needed more than the readers had.**
  - Fungi Cavern and Twisted Caverns: D1161's "until your next turn".
  - Veils of Fear and Sandfall Cell: D1162's punisher.
  - Oubliette: "Discard a card and sacrifice an artifact, a creature, and a land" reads as its four
    sentences.
  - Runestone Caverns: "You may play them" with no deadline is a new `playFromExile.through`,
    `while-exiled`, which nothing clears but the card leaving exile. "For as long as they remain
    exiled" reads to it too.
  - Mad Wizard's Lair: built by hand. The three cards are drawn before anything is asked and shown
    to the table as `AutomationState.revealed`. The question is which of them, if any, to cast, a
    land never offered. The cast is D708's free-cast offer on that card.
- **"You've completed a dungeon"** and "you haven't completed Tomb of Annihilation" are a static
  condition, `controller-completed-dungeon`, read off `dungeonsCompleted`.

Read whole now: 19 of the 38 venture cards, plus Cloister Gargoyle and Nadaar, Selfless Paladin on
the completed-dungeon condition. Not read: "whenever you complete a dungeon", "venture into the
dungeon more than once each turn", and the cards' other unread lines.

**A pin moved.** D583's `compile.test.ts` listed "You may play that card for as long as it remains
exiled" among the shapes left unread, because then nothing could hold a permission without a
deadline. It is now a positive test, with the bare "You may play them", that both read.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests and the moved compile pin:
- The test cards read whole.
- The first venture asks which dungeon (Lost Mine of Phandelver) and enters Cave Entrance; the next
  asks which room, and Mine Tunnels makes a Treasure.
- Tomb of Annihilation can be chosen, and Trapped Entry costs each player a life.
- Runestone Caverns exiles two cards playable while exiled, and the permission outlasts two turns.
- Mad Wizard's Lair draws three and completes Dungeon of the Mad Mage; a creature with "as long as
  you've completed a dungeon, gets +3/+0" gets it.
- In Undercity, a venture into the dungeon moves down Undercity.

Faults injected by hand: 6. Caught:
- The dungeon choice ignored.
- The Lair not completing the dungeon.
- The condition always false.
- Runestone Caverns' permission ending this turn.
- `ventureInto` starting a new dungeon over one in progress.

Survived, as designed: the reader's own in-dungeon check removed. `ventureInto` reads the dungeon in
progress itself, so the two checks guard each other.

Coverage: 15,855 of 31,900 cards (+23 over D1162's 15,832), 38,055 of 59,888 lines (+40). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D817 and D818, merged in after D1162 was measured.
## D820 — "Whenever an opponent discards a creature / land / noncreature, nonland card": Waste Not

Most-played order: Waste Not (rank 1268), whose three lines are each a discard trigger about one
kind of card. The same row reads Bone Miser, Surly Badgersaur and Wharf Infiltrator.

**Engine.** The per-card `discards` event now carries `subjectTypes`: the discarded card's printed
card types, lowercased and read as it is raised. The trigger gains `cardTypes` (any of them) and
`notTypes` (none of them), and the matcher asks them only when a trigger has them, so every
existing discard trigger means what it did. The batch event (D993) carries no types and is not
asked.

**Reader.** A trigger row "Whenever (you | an opponent | a player) discard(s) a(n) <kind> card,
…". The kind is either one card type ("a creature card") or a list of card types each printed
with "non" ("a noncreature, nonland card"). A list of positive types and mixed lists stay unread.
"When you discard a land card" (Green Goblin) prints "When" and stays unread too.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests (Waste Not's controller makes the opponent discard their one card):
- the card reads;
- a creature card makes one Zombie and nothing else;
- a land adds {B}{B} and nothing else;
- an instant draws a card and nothing else;
- its own controller discarding a creature card fires none of them.

And in compile.test, D567's pin "leaves a discard narrowed by card type unread" ("Whenever you
discard a creature card, you gain 1 life") is retargeted, the way that table already records its
others: the line now reads as `{ kind: 'discards', by: 'you', cardTypes: ['creature'] }`. The first
gate caught it; the change is deliberate.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught. They cover the positive filter, the negative filter,
the types not raised, "non" read as the type itself, and whose discard ignored.

- engine tests: 6192, all passing (on 2672538)
- Coverage: 15,812 to 15,816 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 37,973 to 37,985 of 59,888 lines, against 2672538.
