## D1165 — "for each opponent"

"For each opponent" was not a count any reader knew: "create a 1/1 black Rat creature token for each
opponent you have", "draw a card for each opponent", "you gain 2 life for each opponent". It is now
one in `countOfThing`: the seats still in the game other than the controller's, counted as the
effect resolves. So every reader that takes a "for each" count takes it, as they take "for each
creature you control".

The prefix form, "For each opponent, you create a 1/1 black and green Pest creature token with
'When this token dies, you gain 1 life.'", is the clause read without its prefix and done once per
opponent. It applies only to a clause that targets nothing, asks nothing and does not name the
opponent. A clause about each opponent in turn ("that player", "they") is a different reading and
stays unread, as do the per-opponent targets ("for each opponent, return up to one target nonland
permanent that player controls").

Read whole now: Darksteel Splicer, Eccentric Pestfinder, Inspired Sphinx and Big Apple, 3 a.m.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests, in a four-player pod:
- The test cards read whole.
- Three opponents: three Rats, three Pests, six life.
- An opponent who has left the game is not counted: two Rats.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The count always 1.
- The prefix form done once.
- Eliminated seats counted.

Coverage: 15,866 of 31,900 cards (+8 over D1164's 15,858), 38,078 of 59,888 lines (+18). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D820, merged in after D1164 was measured.
## D821 — Prevention for attacking creatures you control (Dolmen Gate, Iroas), and combat damage between creatures counted as combat damage

Most-played order: Dolmen Gate (rank 1348) and Iroas, God of Victory (rank 1446), the corpus's two
printings of "Prevent all [combat] damage that would be dealt to attacking creatures you
control".

**Reader.** D752's `preventionStaticFromLine` takes "attacking creatures you control" as the
`controller-creatures` scope with D941's `onlyAttacking` filter, read live. A creature is shielded
exactly while it attacks. "You and attacking creatures …" is not printed and is refused.

**An engine bug, found by Dolmen Gate's test.** `dealDamage` decides "is this combat damage?" for
the combat-only prevention flag from `combatFrom`. `combat.ts` passes `combatFrom` only for damage
to a player or a planeswalker, because that is what makes commander damage count. So damage between
an attacker and its blockers was never combat damage to the prevention check. A combat-only
shield on creatures ("Prevent all combat damage that would be dealt to creatures you control",
D752's own family) let a blocker's damage straight through, and an attacker's damage to a blocker
too.

The fix: a separate `combat: true` option on `dealDamage`, set by the two creature-to-creature
calls in combat (attacker to blocker, blocker to attacker) and read beside `combatFrom` by the
prevention check. `combatFrom` keeps its one meaning, so commander damage is unchanged.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- under the all-damage shield, a Bolt kills our Bear at home but not while it attacks, and blocked
  by a 3/3 it lives;
- under Dolmen Gate (combat only), blocked by a 3/3 it lives, but a Bolt while it attacks still
  kills it;
- the opponent's attacker is not shielded by our Gate;
- under a combat-only "creatures you control" shield, the opponent's blocker survives our 3/3
  attacker. This one is the bug's other half.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught. They cover the attacking filter dropped, the attacking
subject unread, the `combat` option ignored by the prevention check, and each of the two combat
calls left unmarked.

- engine tests: 6197, all passing (on a7c7c64)
- Coverage: 15,816 to 15,818 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 37,985 to 37,987 of 59,888 lines, against a7c7c64.

## D822 — "For each land you control, create a Treasure token": Brass's Bounty

Most-played order: Brass's Bounty (rank 1364). "Create a Treasure token for each land you control"
already read. The card prints the count first.

**Reader.** A `clausesOf` rewrite: a sentence "For each <thing>, create <tokens>" becomes "Create
<tokens> for each <thing>", where the counted-token reader looks for the count. "For each of …"
(target lists) is excluded, and whether <thing> is countable is still the counted reader's
decision. So the rest of the corpus's 37 printings stay unread for their own reasons: copies of
"that creature", "destroyed this way", dice and coin results, and second sentences about "those
tokens".

**Tests.** 2 engine tests: the card reads; with three lands of ours and two of theirs it makes
three Treasures, all ours.

Faults injected by script: 2 of 2 caught (the rewrite off, and the count dropped from it).

- engine tests: 6199, all passing (on 64e9800)
- Coverage: 15,818 to 15,821 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 37,987 to 37,991 of 59,888 lines, against 64e9800.

## D1166 — delayed sacrifice of the source or a target, and a token's keyword list

"Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step" was read only after a clause that puts a
creature onto the battlefield (D696's Kiki-Jiki and Sneak Attack rewrite). After anything else it
was unread. The single-unread list holds 89 lines that end "at the beginning of the next end step",
21 of them "sacrifice it" or "exile it".

Two readers now schedule the same engine-known delayed ability that D696 does (`scheduleDelayed`
with a `builtin`). It goes on the stack at the next end step and acts only on the object as it is
now (CR 400.7):
- **The source**: "sacrifice / exile / destroy ~ (or it, or this creature) at the beginning of the
  next end step". It is refused after a card target, where "it" is that card, as D1156 refuses.
- **A target**: "sacrifice / exile / destroy target … at the beginning of the next end step". Through
  the pronoun borrow it also reads "Sacrifice it …" after an earlier target (D530).

A token fix found alongside: "with trample, lifelink, and haste" was split into "trample",
"lifelink" and "and haste". The Oxford comma is now part of the separator. Three lines in the list
have the shape.

Read whole now: Deathknell Kami, Krovikan Elementalist, Slave of Bolas and Hungry for More. Not
read: the rest of the 89, which fail on other clauses (Chimeric Coils' "becomes an X/X", Dark Maze's
defender line, Fatal Frenzy's "+X/+0, where X is its power").

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "Sacrifice it" with no target sacrifices the source at the next end step, not before.
- After a target, "Sacrifice it" sacrifices the target and leaves the source.
- The token has trample, lifelink and haste, and is gone after the next end step.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The source exiled instead of sacrificed.
- No target reader: the card is then unread.
- The old keyword split.

Coverage: 15,885 of 31,900 cards (+19 over D1165's 15,866), 38,100 of 59,888 lines (+22). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D821 and D822, merged in after D1165 was measured.
## D823 — Tokens counted by the dying creature's power: Elenda, Goldvein Hydra

Most-played order: Elenda, the Dusk Rose (rank 1301) and Goldvein Hydra (rank 1425), with
Elenda's Hierophant. The same reading now covers Murder Investigation, Nested Shambler,
Stratagem Emulator and Threefold Thunderhulk.

D1020 measured "its power" off the event's creature for life gained and cards drawn, but not for a
token count: "create a number of tapped Treasure tokens equal to its power", or "create X 1/1 …
tokens with lifelink, where X is Elenda's power".

**Reader.** In the same block, on the same four events (entry, death, attack, combat hit),
"create (a number of | X) <tokens>[ with <keywords>] (equal to its/that creature's power |,
where X is its/that creature's/<self>'s power)" is read. The count is measured the way D1020
measures: live while the creature is on the battlefield, and as it last was once it is gone,
never below 0. `tokenEffect` gains an optional `countOverride` that takes the place of its own
count tail. The clause then prints X, and a count tail of its own alongside one is refused.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- a 3/3 Hydra destroyed makes three tapped Treasures, and pumped to 5 power before it dies, five;
- an Elenda referred to by its short name, pumped to 4 power and destroyed, makes four 1/1
  lifelink Vampires.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught. They cover the override ignored, a fixed count in place
of the last-known power, keywords before the count refused, and the short name refused.

- engine tests: 6202, all passing (on 85113d1)
- Coverage: 15,821 to 15,828 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 37,991 to 37,999 of 59,888 lines, against 85113d1.

## D1167 — graveyard card filters: colours joined by "or", and a comma list with "legendary"

`graveyardTypeTest` reads what kind of card a graveyard target, a search or a dig may take. Every
graveyard clause family asks it. It refused two printed shapes:
- **Colours joined by "or" in front of the type**: "target blue or red creature card", "a white or
  black creature card". The colours are now one test, any of them, ANDed with what follows.
- **A comma list with "or" that includes "legendary"**: "target artifact, enchantment, or legendary
  card". Each part is an alternative: a card type, a real subtype, or "legendary".

Still refused: the "with …" suffixes after "card" ("with infect", "with power 2 or less"). Each
caller reads those itself, and they are a change across several readers.

**A pin moved.** D527's `compile.test.ts` listed "Return target white or black creature card from your
graveyard to the battlefield" as a colour run the vocabulary did not read. It is now a positive test.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests and the moved compile pin:
- The test cards read whole.
- "Blue or red creature card": the blue creature returns; the green one is refused as a target.
- "Artifact, enchantment, or legendary card": the legendary creature returns; a plain creature is
  refused.

Faults injected by hand: 2, both caught.
- The colours ignored.
- The list matching anything.

Coverage: 15,900 of 31,900 cards (+15 over D1166's 15,885), 38,118 of 59,888 lines (+18). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D823, merged in after D1166 was measured.
## D825 — "Double target creature's power [and toughness]": Bulk Up

Most-played order: Bulk Up (rank 1378). The same reader covers Unleash Fury and the other
"double target creature's power …" and "double the power … of target creature …" printings.

**Reader.** In `readEffect`: "double target <creature>'s power[ and toughness] until end of turn",
and "double the power[ and toughness] of target <creature> until end of turn". To double a
creature's power is to give it +X/+0, where X is its power as the spell resolves (CR 701.10e),
so the effect reads the target's live characteristics and pumps it by that much until end of
turn, toughness too when the sentence says so. A negative power gets +0. "Double its power"
(own abilities, six lines) stays unread: "its" can be the source or an earlier target, and
nothing here tells which.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests (a 3/2):
- the cards read;
- doubled power makes a 6/2 that is a 3/2 again next turn;
- doubled power and toughness makes a 6/4;
- +3/+3 first and then doubled makes a 12/5. The double reads the creature as it is, not as
  printed.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught. They cover printed values in place of current ones,
toughness always or never doubled, and a permanent effect in place of until end of turn.

- engine tests: 6209, all passing (on ea1f103)
- Coverage: 15,829 to 15,837 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 38,000 to 38,013 of 59,888 lines, against ea1f103.

## D1168 — domain as a static count, and any line read without its ability word

Domain cards (CR 207.2c's "Domain —" label) were 16 single-unread lines, for two reasons:
- **The static count.** "~ gets +1/+1 for each basic land type among lands you control" is a static
  size, read by `staticCountedSizeFromLine` through `staticCountOf`, whose vocabulary had no domain.
  It is now a `StaticCountable`, `basic-land-types`: the distinct Plains, Island, Swamp, Mountain
  and Forest subtypes among the controller's lands, off their printed type lines (D604's compromise,
  as metalcraft's count is).
- **The ability word.** Several readers never strip the label: the static counted size, the cost
  reduction ("This spell costs {1} less to cast for each …") and the attachment bonus. So:
  - `lineScriptFor` now reads a line whole and, failing that, once more without its ability word.
    The label has no rules meaning, so the sentence after the dash is the whole ability.
  - The retry skips activated abilities. A cost line under a label ("Threshold — {1}: …",
    "Metalcraft — {T}: Add …", "Bloodrush — {R}, Discard this card: …") stays D623's and D1135's
    to read: the label comes off only when the line restates its condition, and a mana line stays a
    mana line. The first version retried those too, and the pregate's D623 and D1135 tests caught
    it.
  - The attachment reader finds and reads its static line without the label, and still claims the
    printed line.

Read whole now: Wayfaring Giant, Kavu Scout, Strength of Unity, Exotic Curse, Manaforce Mace,
Leyline Binding, Stratadon and Yavimaya Sojourner, and any other line that failed only on its label.
Not read: "all creatures get -1/-1 until end of turn for each …" and "target player discards a card
for each …" (Planar Despair, Voices from the Void), which fail without the label too.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole, each under "Domain —".
- The size counts basic land types, not lands: Plains and two Islands is +2/+2; Plains, Island and
  Swamp is +3/+3.
- The cost: three types take {3} off, so three lands cast a {4}{G} spell; three Forests cannot.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- No retry without the ability word.
- The count always 0.
- Lands counted instead of their types.


Coverage: 15,927 of 31,900 cards (+27 over D1167's 15,900), 38,158 of 59,888 lines (+40). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D824 to D826, merged in after D1167 was measured. Eight are the domain cards above; the split of the rest between the ability-word retry and D824 to D826 was not measured.

## D1169 — a colour, a keyword or a counter on a mass scope

`massScope` reads the scope of "Destroy all …", "Tap all …", "Return all …", "each …" and the
board counts ("draw a card for each …"). It knew types, subtypes, supertypes, the state words, a
size bound and "with no counters". It now also reads:
- **A colour word** as the permanent's live colours, not its type line: "Destroy all green
  creatures" (Perish), "nonblack creatures", "colorless", "multicolored" and "monocolored". A colour
  alone is not a scope: "all green" without a type word stays unread.
- **"With <keyword>"**, the creature's live keywords: "Destroy all creatures with flying"
  (Whirlwind), "for each creature you control with flying" (Aven Gagglemaster, Aerial Assault).
  Only a single keyword the engine knows; "with flying and vigilance" stays unread.
- **"With a +1/+1 counter on it" / "with +1/+1 counters on them"**, a counter of that kind
  (Armorcraft Judge, Avatar of the Resolute), and "with a counter on them" with no kind named, any
  counter at all. An article is never read as a counter kind.

The mass pump ("… get +N/+N / gain <keyword> until end of turn") had its own subject list. Its
subjects now fall back to `massScope` for any creature scope with a colour or a "with" filter:
"Creatures you control with flying get +1/+1", "All creatures with flying get -1/-1", "Nonblack
creatures get -1/-1". Creatures only: every id is checked to be a creature. The sentence's capital
is lowered first, because `massScope` reads a capitalised word as a subtype.

The compile pin "a count qualified past the vocabulary" was "… with a +1/+1 counter on it"; it is
now "… with flying and vigilance", which is still refused. D600's refusal row "Destroy all white
permanents" (caught by the pregate) is now "Destroy all white": a colour alone is still not a scope.

**Tests.** 7 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- A colour: green creatures die on both sides, the white flier stays.
- Colorless: the artifact creature dies, the coloured ones stay.
- A keyword: only the flier dies.
- A keyword on a pump: the flier grows, the bear does not.
- A counter as a count: one card for each creature with a +1/+1 counter.
- A counter with no kind named: only the creature with an oil counter dies.

Faults injected by hand: 6, all caught.
- The colour test inverted.
- The counter test accepting zero.
- The keyword test always true.
- The sentence capital left on.
- Colorless accepting any colour count.
- A kindless counter test always true.

Coverage: 15,981 of 31,900 cards (+54 over D1168's 15,927), 38,230 of 59,888 lines (+72).

## D828 — A lord of two tribes: Death Baron

Most-played order: Death Baron (rank 1652), with Caterwauling Boggart ("Goblins you control and
Elementals you control have menace").

**Reader.** At the top of `lineScriptFor`: "<[other] Tribe> you control and <[other] Tribe> you
control <get/have …>" is read as two lines, each with the shared predicate. Each must come back
as a single subtype-scoped static, or the line stays unread.

**Engine.** Two static effects would give a creature of both tribes the bonus twice. A Zombie
Skeleton under Death Baron would be a 4/4, and Death Baron is itself a Zombie Skeleton. The
printed sentence is one effect. So `ContinuousEffect` gains `notSubtypes`, beside D814's
`onlySubtypes`: none of these subtypes, read live after layer 4. The second static carries the
first one's subtype in it, so the two scopes do not overlap.

Death Baron is a Skeleton, so it gets its own bonus, once. "Other" belongs to the Zombies, and the
Skeleton half has no "other".

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- under a Baron our Skeleton, our other Zombie and our Zombie Skeleton are each 3/3 with
  deathtouch, the last one once and not twice;
- the Baron (a Zombie Skeleton) is a 3/3 with deathtouch, while our Bear and the opponent's
  Zombie are unchanged.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught. They cover the engine filter unchecked, `modsFrom`
dropping it, the reader not excluding the first tribe, and the first half dropped.

- engine tests: 6218, all passing (on 19bc115)
- Coverage: 15,840 to 15,842 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 38,016 to 38,018 of 59,888 lines, against 19bc115.

## D1170 — another player's count, blockers counted, and a rate aimed at one player

Three gaps in the "for each" grammar (D520), each seen on a run of single-unread lines:
- **A rate aimed at one player.** `countScaledEffect` read "you gain / you lose / each opponent
  loses / draw N for each …" but not a targeted player. It now reads "target player / target
  opponent loses N life for each …" and "… mills N cards for each …": Bishop of the Bloodstained,
  Ishkanah's ability, Burden of Greed, Liliana, Death Mage's −7. Through the existing referent swap
  the same clause reads as "that player loses …" after a combat hit (Emissary of Despair) and as
  "defending player loses …" on an attack (Guiltfeeder).
- **Another player's things.** `countOfThing` counted only the controller's board, graveyard and
  hand. It now reads "<scope> they control" / "that player controls" and "cards in their graveyard /
  hand" (with a card type) as the targeted player's, which is also the player a referent swap hands
  the clause. "<scope> defending player controls" is the targeted player if there is one, else the
  defender of the source's attack (`defendersOf`, D960): Coastline Marauders, Killmonger's shape.
  The scope is anything `massScope` reads.
- **Blockers.** "For each creature blocking it" (Elvish Berserker, Gang of Elk, General Marhault
  Elsdragon), "… beyond the first" (Jungle Wurm, Johtull Wurm), and "for each creature it's
  blocking" (Guardian of the Gateless). "It" is the creature the trigger is about, else the source.
  Read off the combat as the trigger resolves.

Still unread here: a discard "for each …" (the discard question's size is a fixed number today),
"for each Blood token defending player controls" (tokens by subtype under another controller),
Berserk Murlodont's "a Beast" subject, and the second sentences of Last Stand and Foul-Tongue Shriek.

**Tests.** 7 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- Blocked by two, it gets +2/+2.
- Beyond the first: blocked by two, -1/-1; by one, nothing.
- The defending player loses one life for each card in their graveyard, not the attacker's.
- "Defending player controls" with no target: the lands of the player attacked.
- A rate aimed at an opponent counts your creatures.
- "They control" is the target's: three lands there, one here.

The blocker tests order the blockers when the engine asks (CR 509.2 as this engine runs it): a 6/6
blocked by two 0/5 walls waits for the attacker's damage order before the trigger resolves, a 2/2
does not.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- "Beyond the first" ignored.
- "They control" counting every player's.
- "Defending player" read as the controller (caught only once the Marauder test was added).
- The aimed loss taken from the controller.
- The blocker count fixed at one.

Coverage: 16,032 of 31,900 cards (+51 over D1169's 15,981), 38,285 of 59,888 lines (+55). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D827 and D828, merged in after D1169 was measured.
## D829 — Losheel's attacking artifact creatures, and annihilator granted by an Aura (Eldrazi Conscription)

Most-played order: Eldrazi Conscription (rank 1595) and Losheel, Clockwork Scholar (rank 1607).

The static keeps the `controller-creatures` scope and the `onlyAttacking` filter and adds D735's
`onlyKind: ['artifact']`.

**Eldrazi Conscription.** An attachment's "has trample and annihilator 2" now reads annihilator as
the quoted attack trigger it stands for (CR 702.86a: "Whenever this creature attacks, defending
player sacrifices N permanents"), the way D736 reads "ward {N}". The existing size-and-grant reader
then takes it, so the host gets the trigger through `grantedTriggers`. "Has menace, deathtouch,
annihilator 1" (a comma list ending in annihilator) is not rewritten, and stays unread.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- both cards read;
- under Losheel, an attacking artifact creature blocked by a 3/3 lives and an attacking Bear does
  not;
- the Conscription's host is a 12/12 trampler, and when it attacks the defending player
  sacrifices two of their three permanents.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught (the artifact filter dropped, the annihilator rewrite
off, and the count fixed at one).

- engine tests: 6222, all passing (on 76a6c8a)
- Coverage: 15,842 to 15,844 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 38,018 to 38,020 of 59,888 lines, against 76a6c8a.

## D1171 — that spell's mana value, and the mana spent to cast it

About 60 legal lines measure "that spell": a cast trigger's spell ("Whenever you cast a noncreature
spell, … where X is that spell's mana value") or a counterspell's target ("Counter target spell.
Create X Treasure tokens, where X is that spell's mana value"). None read.

- **The measures.** `SPELL_MEASURE`: "that spell's mana value", "the mana value of that spell" and
  "the amount of mana spent to cast that spell". It rides on `SACRIFICED_MEASURE` (D586), so every
  "equal to …" and "where X is …" reader that takes one takes the other, and `boardCount` reads it
  through `spellMeasure` first.
- **Which spell.** The one a cast trigger answers (`EffectContext.answering`, the channel the copy
  and counter-on-cast readers use), else the spell this effect targets.
- **Mana value** counts X as chosen (CR 202.3e, `manaValueOnStack`). **Mana spent** is new engine
  state: the cast records `manaSpent` on the stack object beside `coloursSpent`.
- **A spell already countered.** "Counter target spell. Create X …" measures a spell the first
  sentence took off the stack. `counterSpell` now records the spell's mana value and mana spent as
  it leaves (`GameState.counteredSpellsThisTurn`, cleared each turn), and the measure reads that
  when the spell is gone. A spell that left the stack any other way measures 0; nothing printed
  needs that yet.

Read whole now, among others: Bounteous Kirin, Cloudhoof Kirin, Erratic Cyclops, Manaplasm, Jamie
McCrimmon, Livaan, Aberrant Manawurm, Uncover the Moon-Letters, Dancing from Dark to Dawn, Kaervek
the Merciless, Keeper of Secrets, The Frightful Four, Spell Swindle, Overwhelming Intellect, Access
Denied, Imp's Mischief. Still unread: incubate X, X/X tokens with a where-X, "with that spell's
mana value" as a filter (Celestial Kirin, Skyfire Kirin), and a countered spell's X/X Ooze.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- The mana value of a {2}{U} spell: three life.
- X counts on the stack: {X}{U} for X=3 is mana value four.
- The mana spent: four for X=3, read off the spell as cast.
- A countered spell is measured as it was countered: X=3 still counts, and the countered spell's
  own effect never happens.

Faults injected by hand: 6, all caught.
- Mana spent always 0.
- Mana value read off the printed card (X as 0).
- Mana spent not recorded at the cast.
- No `spellMeasure` in `boardCount`.
- The countered record written as zeros.
- Only the answered spell looked at, not the target.

The first draft took the spell only from `answering`, so a counterspell would have measured 0. It
was found by probing Spell Swindle before any test was written; the last fault above is that draft.

Coverage: 16,052 of 31,900 cards (+20 over D1170's 16,032), 38,308 of 59,888 lines (+23). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D829, merged in after D1170 was measured.
## D830 — "Historic" as a scope word: Desynchronization

Most-played order: Desynchronization (rank 1614).

**Reader.** The scope-word classifier `massScope` uses (D781's supertypes, card types and
subtypes) learns "historic" (CR 700.6): an artifact, a legendary permanent or a Saga, read off
the printed type line. "Nonhistoric" needed no branch of its own: the mass reader's "non" already
negates any word it knows. A first version had one, and a fault that broke it went uncaught, so it
was removed. A `clausesOf` rewrite turns "all/each [nonland] permanent(s) that's not / is not /
isn't / are not / aren't historic" into "all nonhistoric …", as D827 does for "aren't legendary".

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- Desynchronization returns the Bear and the enchantment on both sides and leaves the legend,
  the artifacts and the land;
- "Destroy all historic permanents" takes the legend and the artifacts and leaves the rest.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught on the code that remains (artifacts dropped from
historic, legends dropped, and the rewrite off).

- engine tests: 6225, all passing (on 342e819)
- Coverage: 15,844 to 15,846 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 38,020 to 38,022 of 59,888 lines, against 342e819.

## D1172 — an X/X token, where X is a measure

"Create an X/X green Ooze creature token, where X is …" was 26 single-unread legal lines. The token
reader (`tokenFrom`) took only a printed power and toughness, and the "where X is" grammar
(`tokenEffect`, D520) only as the number of tokens.

`tokenEffect` now reads "create a/an X/X <token>, where X is <measure>" as one token whose power and
toughness are the measure as the clause resolves. The token's definition is the 0/0 the rest of
the sentence describes, so colours, subtypes, "artifact" and keywords read as they do on any token;
`addTokens` (D810) keeps two Oozes of different sizes as two definitions. X of 0 still makes the
token, which the state-based check then removes (CR 704.5f).

Any measure `boardCount` reads works: a count, "the greatest power among …", a devotion, and
D1171's "that spell's mana value" (Mystic Genesis measures the spell it countered).

Read whole now, among others: Miming Slime, Tumbleweed Rising, Kin-Tree Invocation, Seed Guardian,
Oviya Pashiri's ability, Spoils of Blood, Abzan Monument, Grakmaw, Manaform Hellkite, Mystic
Genesis. Still unread: "~'s power" on a dies trigger (Flesh Carver), "the sacrificed creature's
power" on abilities with other restrictions (Ooze Garden, Geralf), and lines with a second sentence
of their own (Experimental Overload, Phyrexian Rebirth).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- The greatest power: a 5/3 on the board makes a 5/5 Ooze.
- A graveyard count, and the keyword: two creature cards make a 2/2 with trample.
- X of 0: no 0/0 is left on the battlefield.
- The countered spell's mana value: X=3 on a {X}{G} spell makes a 4/4.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- Toughness fixed at 1.
- Size fixed at 1/1.
- The keywords dropped from the token.

Coverage: 16,066 of 31,900 cards (+14 over D1171's 16,052), 38,333 of 59,888 lines (+25). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D830, merged in after D1171 was measured.

## D1173 — sacrifice "X or Y", a token, a subtype

`permanentDescribed` (D465, D741) is the description reader behind "sacrifice a …", "return a …
you control to its owner's hand" and "target player sacrifices a …". It read one type with colour
and state adjectives. On the ETB "you may sacrifice …" lines alone, about 20 single-unread legal
lines failed on three shapes:
- **A disjunction of whole descriptions:** "another creature or artifact", "a creature or land",
  "an artifact or creature", "a creature, artifact, or enchantment". Read only when every part is a
  description of its own. Otherwise the "or" is the colour list's ("a red or green creature"), read
  as before.
- **A token:** "a token", "a creature token", and the adjective "nontoken".
- **A subtype as the noun**, off the printed capital: "a Vehicle", "a Goblin", "an Equipment". A
  phrase that reaches the reader lower-cased still refuses, as D471 required, so a subtype is never
  widened to its type.

Read whole now, among others: Harvester Troll, Undercity Eliminator, Gastal Blockbuster, The
Sackville-Bagginses, Glorifier of Suffering, Boilerbilges Ripper. Still unread: "sacrifice a
creature or discard a creature card" (Crypt Lurker, K'un-Lun Warrior) and Shire Shirriff's "until
~ leaves the battlefield".

D471's pin "sacrifice a Goblin stays unread" (caught by running the file) now reads, and is moved
to the reads list.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "Another creature or artifact": the Golem and the Relic are offered; the Swamp and the creature
  itself are not. The chosen one goes, and a card is drawn.
- "Another creature or Vehicle": the Vehicle and the Golem, not the plain artifact.
- "A token": only the token can go, and the Golem stays.
- "A nontoken creature": the token stays, the Golem goes.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The disjunction read as a conjunction.
- The token requirement ignored.
- "Nontoken" inverted.
- The subtype noun ignored (caught once the Vehicle test was added).

Coverage: 16,091 of 31,900 cards (+25 over D1172's 16,066), 38,370 of 59,888 lines (+37).
## D831 — "Deals N damage to each opponent. You gain life equal to the damage dealt this way"

Most-played order: Creeping Bloodsucker (rank 1566), with Syphon Soul ("each other player", which
is each opponent in a pod).

**Reader.** `clausesOf` joins the two sentences, and `readEffect` reads the joined clause: the
source deals N to each opponent in turn, and its controller gains the damage that was dealt. That
is measured on each opponent as life lost plus poison gained by the hit, so prevented damage
gains nothing. The other three printings in the corpus aim the damage elsewhere ("any target",
"each creature that shares a color", "target player or planeswalker") and stay unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- in a pod of three, Syphon Soul takes 2 from each opponent and gains its caster 4, and with one
  opponent shielded by "Prevent all damage that would be dealt to you" it gains 2;
- the Bloodsucker's upkeep drains one.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught (the joiner off, the printed amount gained in place of
the damage dealt, and one opponent's worth gained).

- engine tests: 6228, all passing (on 2a4f236; the first gate run was lost to a container restart and re-run)
- Coverage: 15,846 to 15,848 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 38,022 to 38,024 of 59,888 lines, against 2a4f236.

## D1174 — an edict of any description

"Each player / each opponent / defending player sacrifices a …" read a fixed list of kinds:
creature, permanent, artifact, land, enchantment, nonland permanent and the nontoken pair. Any
other description stayed unread. It now falls back to `permanentDescribed`, which since D1173
reads disjunctions, tokens and subtypes: "each opponent sacrifices a creature token", "each
opponent sacrifices an artifact or creature", "… a creature or planeswalker", "… an untapped
creature", "each player sacrifices a Goblin". One each, each player choosing from their own, as the
fixed kinds do. A description with "with", "that", "they control", "of their choice", "unless" or
"for each" is left to its own readers.

Prankster; Tribute to the Wild. Still unread: keyword filters ("a creature with flying") and the
greatest-power edicts that name another shape.

- "A creature token": the Soldier goes, the Golem stays.
- "An artifact or creature": the Relic is the only one, so it goes; the Swamp stays.

Faults injected by hand: 2, all caught.
- The description ignored (anything offered).
- Nothing sacrificed.

Coverage: 16,102 of 31,900 cards (+11 over D1173's 16,091), 38,394 of 59,888 lines (+24). The difference also counts the D7xx session's D831, merged in after D1173 was measured.

`massScope` (D600, D1169) read "nontoken" but not "token". It now reads "token" and "tokens" as a

## D1176 — a counter on each permanent of any scope

"Put a +1/+1 (or -1/-1) counter on each …" read its scope with `boardScope` (D453), which knows
types, subtypes, supertypes, "other", the controller clause and the state words. It now falls back
to `massScope` for anything else, which since D1169 and D1175 reads colours, keywords, counters
and tokens, and splits a comma list before it classifies a word: "each creature token you
control", "each creature you control with flying", "each white creature you control", "each
nonblack creature", "each Pest, Bat, Insect, Snake, and Spider you control" (Blech, Loafing Pest).
The set is frozen before the first counter lands, as before.

Four of D453's refusal rows (caught by running compile.test.ts) now read, and each reading is the
printed one: a subtype list is a union, "with lifelink" is the keyword, "white" is the colour. They
move to the reads list. The punctuation-guard row ("each Pest, Bat you control") reads as a union
of two subtypes, because `massScope` splits at the comma first; the test now pins that no word
reaches a subtype test with its comma on. Still refused: "with modular" placed before "you
control", "that convoked it", "named …", "and/or", "each of those creatures", a second clause.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "Each green creature you control": your Bear, not your Bird, not their Bear.
- A list of subtypes is a union: "each Bird and Bat you control", not the Bear.
- "Each nonblack creature": both sides, the black Bat spared.

## D1177 — tokens in a static count

A static size "~ gets +1/+1 for each … you control" counts through `staticCountOf`, which may not
read live characteristics (`ContinuousEffect.sizePerCount`: a size that reads sizes recurses). It
read printed types and subtypes but not tokens. Whether a permanent is a token is a fact about the
object, not a characteristic, so it is as safe to read there as a printed type line. Now:
- "for each token you control": a new `StaticCountable`, `tokens-you-control`;
- "for each artifact token you control" (and enchantment or land, with "and/or"): `permanents-of-type`
  with `token`;
- "for each Officer token you control": `permanents-of-subtype` with `token`.

"Creature token" stays refused, for D523's reason (whether a permanent is a creature now is what a
printed line cannot say).

Read whole now: Academy Instructor. Still unread: the same count on an anthem ("Other Dwarves you
control get +1/+0 for each artifact token you control", Thorin), which is the anthem reader's.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "Each token": the Soldier and the Treasure, not the nontoken Golem.
- "Each artifact token": the Treasure only; the Golem is an artifact but not a token.
- "Each Soldier token": the Soldier token only; the Golem Soldier is not a token.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- `tokens-you-control` counting every permanent.
- The token flag ignored on `permanents-of-type`.
- The token flag ignored on `permanents-of-subtype`.

Coverage: 16,123 of 31,900 cards (+1 over D1176's 16,122), 38,425 of 59,888 lines (+1).

## D1178 — an anthem with a count

`staticCountedSizeFromLine` read "~ gets +N/+N for each …" (a size on the permanent itself) and
nothing with a team in front of it. It now also reads the same count on an anthem:
"Creatures you control get +1/+1 for each Gate you control", "Other creatures you control …",
"Creature tokens you control …", "Other Elf creatures you control …", "Other Dwarves you control
…". The scope is the one the plain anthems use (`controller-creatures`, `controller-tokens`, a
subtype with `other`), the effect is `sizePerCount` as on the self size, and the count is the
source's: `staticCount` is handed the static's source and controller, so every creature gets the
same bonus.

`staticCountOf` also reads a named counter on the permanent itself: "for each unity counter on ~",
"… blessing counter on ~". An article is never a kind ("a counter on ~" is any kind, still unread).

Read whole now: Call for Unity, Boon of the Spirit Realm, Joraga Warcaller, Thorin, King of Durin's
Folk. Still unread: a count with a second predicate ("… and have vigilance", Hold the Gates),
"each counter on ~" of any kind (Kyler), "Equipment attached to ~" and commander-cast counts.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "Other Elf creatures … for each +1/+1 counter on ~": two counters make the Elf +2/+2. The Bear,
  and the Warcaller itself, are not other Elves.
- "For each unity counter on ~": the counters on the enchantment, for every creature you control
  and none of theirs.
- "For each artifact you control": two Relics give +2/+0.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The subtype scope dropped to every creature you control.
- The named counter read as +1/+1.
- "Creatures you control" read as every creature.

Coverage: 16,138 of 31,900 cards (+15 over D1177's 16,123), 38,447 of 59,888 lines (+22).

## D1179 — a sentence that starts with "Then"

"Put a +1/+1 counter on ~. Then draw a card." did not read: no clause reader takes a leading
"Then", and 450 single-unread legal lines contain ". Then ". The sentences of a group already
happen in the printed order (CR 608.2c), so the word says nothing a reader needs: `composeEffects`
now drops a leading "Then" (or "Then,") from each sentence before reading it. "Then if …" becomes
"If …", the condition checked when that sentence's turn comes, after the sentences before it.

One reader needs the word: Chain Lightning's "then that player or that permanent's controller may
pay …" keeps it.

Read whole now (25 of the 450, the rest failing on something else in the same line): Aligned
Heart, Altar of Shadows, Assemble the Legion, Become the Avalanche, Brilliant Spectrum, Caldera
Pyremaw, Calming Verse, Cantankerous Captain, Carrion Cruiser, Deadly Embrace, Experimental
Overload, Hour of Promise, Mayael's Aria, Recoil, Survival Cache, Undercity Uprising, and others.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- In order: the counter first, then damage equal to the new power (3, not 2).
- Both sentences of a spell happen: two life and a card.
- "Then if …" is checked after the first sentence: at 20 life against 20, gaining 2 first makes the
  draw happen.

Faults injected by hand: 1, caught: the "Then" left on.

Coverage: 16,161 of 31,900 cards (+23 over D1178's 16,138), 38,473 of 59,888 lines (+26).

## D1180 — a trailing "unless" over a condition

"Draw two cards. Then discard a card unless you attacked this turn." (Chart a Course) did not read.
`readEffect` now reads "<clause> unless <condition>" as the negation of D1026's trailing "if", over
the same condition vocabulary (`interveningConditionFor`): "unless you attacked this turn",
"unless you control an artifact", "unless this enchantment has three or more quest counters on it"
(Anthropological Mission). Only a condition about the game reads; "unless you pay", "unless they
discard" and the other choices start with a player and a verb, have their own readers, and are
excluded.

Unlike the "if" form, this one takes a clause that asks a question, because here the question is
the clause: the discard is asked only when the condition fails, through the decision's
`askOnlyIf`, checked as the clause resolves. The effect is guarded by the same condition.

Read whole now: Chart a Course, Anthropological Mission. Still unread: conditions the vocabulary
lacks ("there are three or more Lesson cards in your graveyard", Chakra Meditation) and "unless you
discard an artifact card" (Alpharael), which is a choice.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test card reads whole.
- No attack this turn: two cards, then the discard is asked.
- After an attack: two cards, and nobody is asked to discard.

Faults injected by hand: 2, all caught.
- The discard always asked.
- The condition inverted.

Coverage: 16,168 of 31,900 cards (+7 over D1179's 16,161), 38,482 of 59,888 lines (+9).

- **"You have a full party"** (CR 700.8): `partySize` at four.

## D832 — A token with a name of its own: Kher Keep

Most-played order: Kher Keep (rank 1582). 62 corpus lines create "a … creature token named <Name>"
(Kobolds of Kher Keep, Cadet, Sky Cadet, Ajani's Pridemate, Wood…). The reading now covers the
named line on 26 cards. The rest are unread for other reasons: modes, quoted abilities after the
name, "a number of", dice and coins.

**Reader.** `tokenFrom` takes " named <Capitalised Name>" off the end of the clause before
reading the rest. The name is printed last, after any keywords. The token's `name` is then that
name instead of its subtype, and its type line, colour, size and keywords are read as before. Two
tokens with one name and different definitions are already kept apart by D810's `name#n` key.

- "two 1/1 white Soldier creature tokens with flying named Sky Cadet" makes two flying Soldiers

## D1182 — "for as long as ~ remains tapped" on any continuous effect

D1040 read the duration on a control change. About 33 single-unread legal lines print it on
something else: a pump ("Target creature gets +1/+1 for as long as ~ remains tapped", Tawnos's
Weaponry, the Couriers, Thran Weaponry), or a freeze ("Tap target land. It doesn't untap during its
controller's untap step for as long as ~ remains tapped", Mana Leech, Rust Tick, Sand Squid, Amber
Prison). Also "for as long as you control ~" (Dungeon Geists).

- **The reader.** The clause is read as it would be until end of turn (or "has" as "gains", or with
  no duration), and every effect it makes becomes `permanent` with `lastsWhile`, the same terms
  D1040's `controlWhile` holds: the source on the battlefield, still tapped, or still yours.
- **The engine.** The settle drops an effect whose `lastsWhile` fails, with nothing to send home.
  It does not come back if the terms hold again. D1041's "you may choose not to untap ~" now also
  keeps a permanent tapped while it holds such an effect.
- **The freeze.** "Tap target X. It doesn't untap during its controller's untap step for as long
  as …" is joined into one clause and read as the tap and a `doesntUntap` effect on that permanent.
  The join happens only when the target phrase reads, so a reader that splits the clause again
  cannot loop (the first draft did, on Entrancing Lyre).

Read whole now (22 of the 33), among others: Tawnos's Weaponry, Thran Weaponry, Ashnod's Battle
Gear, Endoskeleton, Spirit Shield, the five Couriers, Hisoka's Guard, Mana Leech, Mole Worms,
Rust Tick, Phyrexian Gremlins, Sand Squid, Amber Prison, Deserter's Quarters, Thalakos Dreamsower,

## D1183 — tokens that enter tapped and attacking

"Create two 1/1 white Soldier creature tokens that are tapped and attacking" (Hero of Bladehold)
did not read; 83 single-unread legal lines print "tapped and attacking". Mobilize (D905) did it for
one keyword's own Warriors. Now any token clause does, in the three printed orders: "… token tapped
and attacking", "… token that's tapped and attacking" / "… tokens that are tapped and attacking",
and "create two tapped and attacking 1/1 …" (`attackingTokenEffect`, in front of the token reader).

Each new token is tapped and joins the combat (CR 508.4) against the player, or planeswalker, the
creature the ability is about is attacking: the trigger's subject ("whenever a creature you control
attacks"), else the source; with neither attacking, the first opponent. It was never declared as an
attacker, so "whenever … attacks" does not see it, and a noncreature token is only tapped.

Read whole now (11), among others: Hero of Bladehold, Captain's Claws, Carefree Swinemaster,
Skyknight Vanguard, War Effort, Inexorable Blob, Pugnacious Pugilist. Still unread: the riders
"exile / sacrifice that token at end of combat" (a handful) and "whenever a nontoken creature you
control attacks" as a trigger.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- Two Soldiers, tapped, in the attack against the same player, and their damage lands (3 + 2).
- On another permanent's trigger, the token attacks alongside the creature the trigger is about,
  and does not fire the trigger again.

Faults injected by hand: 2, all caught.
- The tokens left out of the combat.
- The tokens left untapped.

Coverage: 16,255 of 31,900 cards (+11 over D1182's 16,244), 38,583 of 59,888 lines (+15).

  Ascendancy) did not read: the `attacks` event had no token filter. It now has `nontoken`, the

- **The rider.** "… token that's tapped and attacking. Exile that token at end of combat." (and
  "Sacrifice that token / those tokens / it at end of combat") is joined by `clausesOf` to the

Read whole now: Militia's Pride, Mardu Ascendancy, and three more attacking-token cards with the
end-of-combat rider.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- A nontoken attacker draws, a token attacker does not; the token that joins the attack does not
  fire the trigger either.
- The Spirit token is exiled at end of combat.

Faults injected by hand: 2, all caught.
- The nontoken filter ignored on `attacks`.
- The rider scheduled at the end step instead.

Coverage: 16,259 of 31,900 cards (+4 over D1183's 16,255), 38,590 of 59,888 lines (+7).

## D1185 — sacrifice triggers: "X or Y", "nontoken", a land, a creature type

"Whenever you sacrifice a …" (D570) read creature, artifact, token, permanent and the token
subtypes (Clue, Food, Treasure and the rest). It now also reads:
- **"A land"**: a new `what`, matched off the event's card types.
- **"A nontoken creature / permanent"**: `nontoken` on the `sacrifices` event.
- **A creature type**: "another Eldrazi", "a Goblin", as a subtype filter.
- **Two kinds joined by "or"**: "another creature or artifact", "an artifact or creature", "a
  Clue or Food". One event with any of them (`whatAny`, or the subtype list), so an artifact
  creature fires it once, not twice. Types with types and subtypes with subtypes; a mix refuses.

Three of D570's refusal rows (caught by running compile.test.ts) now read, each the printed reading,
and one more ("a nontoken creature") reads. Those rows are replaced by "an enchantment", which the
event still has no answer for; "a creature token" (two filters on one noun) and a batch still
refuse.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "An artifact or creature": an artifact creature draws once, not twice; a plain artifact draws; a
  land draws nothing.
- "A land": the Swamp draws, the Golem does not.
- "A nontoken permanent": the Golem draws, a Treasure token does not.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The land filter ignored.
- The nontoken filter ignored.
- "Any of" read as "all of" (caught once the plain artifact was added).

Coverage: 16,265 of 31,900 cards (+6 over D1184's 16,259), 38,604 of 59,888 lines (+14).

## D1186 — the board's "is dealt damage"

"Whenever ~ is dealt damage" (D566) was the permanent's own only, offered to one permanent because
the event is raised for every landing of damage. Two shapes were left out:
- **The board's:** "Whenever a creature you control is dealt damage", "… a creature an opponent
  controls …", "… a creature …", "… a permanent you control …", "… a Dragon you control …". The
  `damaged` event now takes the `BoardSubjectFilter` filters, and `raise` offers it to the whole
  board only while something there watches for it (`boardWatched`), with what the permanent was as
  the damage landed: its controller, types, subtypes, token or not, counters. The same mechanism
  D1121 gave "becomes tapped".
- **"Whenever equipped creature is dealt damage"**, an Equipment's host, read as an Aura's (D994).
  D566's pin said the host may be dead and unattached by the time the trigger is asked; D994's
  event carries what was attached as the damage was dealt, so the pin (caught by running
  compile.test.ts) now reads, and a test shows the trigger firing when the damage kills the host.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "A creature you control": your Bear draws a card; their Bear does not.
- "Equipped creature is dealt damage": fires even when the damage kills the host.
- "A Dragon you control": the Dragon gains life, the Bear does not.

Faults injected by hand: 2, all caught.
- The board filter ignored.
- The event not offered to the board.

Coverage: 16,269 of 31,900 cards (+4 over D1185's 16,265), 38,608 of 59,888 lines (+4).

## D1187 — playing a land as an event

"Whenever an opponent plays a land" (Burgeoning, Dirtcowl Wurm, Pangosaur, Infernal Sovereign,
Horn of Greed) had no event to listen to: a land played was only seen entering (`etb`,
landfall's). Playing a land is a special action (CR 305.1) and is now its own event,
`land-played`, raised by `playLand` with the seat that played it. A land put onto the battlefield
by an effect is not played and does not raise it.

- "Whenever you / an opponent / a player plays a land" reads, with `by` as for a cast.
- "That player" after it is the player who played the land: `land-played` joins the events whose
  acting seat is "that player" (`PLAYER_ACTION_EVENTS`), so Horn of Greed's "that player draws a
  card" draws for them.
- "Whenever you play a land or cast a spell" is the two events with one effect.

Read whole now: Burgeoning, Dirtcowl Wurm, Infernal Sovereign, Pangosaur, Horn of Greed. Still
unread: Flubs's "Otherwise" and Pia Nalaar's "from exile".

The deck-coverage test (caught by the pregate) lists `trigger land-played` as a mechanic no
built-in deck plays, like D1164's `trigger dungeon-completed`.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "An opponent plays a land": their land gains you a life; yours does not.
- "That player draws": the player who played it draws, and a land put onto the battlefield by an
  effect is not played.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The event never raised.
- Whose play ignored.
- "That player" not bound to the player who played it.

Coverage: 16,274 of 31,900 cards (+5 over D1186's 16,269), 38,614 of 59,888 lines (+6).

## D1188 — nine more "as long as" conditions

`staticCondition` turns "as long as …" into data (`PumpOptions['while']`), since the state is
serialised and a closure would not survive. Nine common conditions had no row:
- **New kinds:** "you've drawn two or more cards this turn" (`controller-drew`, off
  `cardsDrawnThisTurn`), "you're the monarch" (`controller-monarch`), "you have more cards in hand
  than each opponent" (`controller-most-cards-in-hand`), "~ entered this turn"
  (`source-entered-this-turn`, off the instance's `enteredTurn`).
- **Graveyards:** "there are N or more creature cards in your graveyard" (`controller-graveyard`
  with `creatures`, printed type lines), and "an opponent has N or more cards in their graveyard"
  (`whose: 'an-opponent'`).
- **The board:** "you control a token" (`board-has` with `token`), "you control another
  multicolored permanent" (`multicolored`: two or more printed colours), "you control exactly one
  creature" (`atMost` beside `atLeast`).

Every one answers without a live characteristic, as the union requires (it is asked inside
`characteristicsOf`).

Read whole now (28 of the 40 lines that print these), among others: the Alara blades (Bant
Sureblade, Esper Stormblade, Grixis Grimblade, Jund Hackblade, Naya Hushblade), Jace's Phantasm,
Thieves' Guild Enforcer, Dawnglade Regent, Keldon Strike Team, Spinehorn Minotaur, Secretkeeper,
Gnarled Sage, Messenger Hawk, Okina Nightwatch.

D502's pin "a count of a kind of card" (caught by running compile.test.ts) used creature cards,
which read now; it uses instant cards instead, still unread.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- Cards drawn this turn (one, then two), the monarch (theirs, then yours), the bigger hand.
- Their graveyard at seven and eight; two creature cards in yours, artifacts not counted.
- Entered this turn or the turn before; a token; exactly one creature; another multicolored
  permanent.

Faults injected by hand: 6, all caught.
- The monarch read as anybody being the monarch.
- "An opponent's graveyard" read as yours.
- The token filter ignored.
- "Exactly" read as "at least".
- The multicolored filter ignored.
- "Entered this turn" ignored.

Coverage: 16,309 of 31,900 cards (+35 over D1187's 16,274), 38,652 of 59,888 lines (+38).

## D1189 — "This effect doesn't remove ~": the Ward Auras

White Ward and its cycle print "Enchanted creature has protection from white. This effect doesn't
remove White Ward." Protection from white makes every white Aura on the creature an illegal
attachment (CR 702.16d), the Ward included, which is why the second sentence exists: this
effect's protection does not remove its own source.

- **The reader.** `attachmentBonus` reads the protection sentence as before and marks the effect
  `protectionSparesSource`.
- **The engine.** `characteristicsOf` records which sources' protection spares them
  (`protectionSpares`) and the protection from everything else (`protectionUnspared`: the printed
  card and every other effect). The CR 704.5m attachment check (`isLegalAttachment`) asks a sparing
  source only against that, so the Ward stays on while another white Aura falls off, and
  protection from white given by anything else still removes the Ward.

Read whole now: White Ward, Blue Ward, Black Ward, Red Ward, Green Ward. Still unread: the "chosen
color" Wards (Cho-Manno's Blessing, Ward of Lights, Pentarch Ward, Flickering Ward), since an
Aura's protection from a chosen colour is not read yet, and Spectra Ward, Tattoo Ward and Pledge
of Loyalty, whose protection is not a single colour.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- The test card reads whole.
- The Ward stays on its own protection; another white Aura on the same creature falls off.

Faults injected by hand: 1, caught: the source never spared.

Coverage: 16,314 of 31,900 cards (+5 over D1188's 16,309), 38,657 of 59,888 lines (+5).

## D1190 — an Aura's protection from the chosen color

"As ~ enters, choose a color. Enchanted creature has protection from the chosen color." (Ward of
Lights, Cho-Manno's Blessing, Pentarch Ward, Flickering Ward) did not read: the attachment reader
took a printed colour only, and D641's chosen-colour fill is for a permanent's own statics.

- **The reader.** `attachmentRider` reads "has protection from the chosen color" as a new
  `protectionFromChosen` on the effect, and D1189's "This effect doesn't remove ~" accepts it.
- **The engine.** `characteristicsOf` adds the colour the effect's source chose as it entered
  (`CardInstance.chosen.color`), read live, so the effect is the same whether the Aura's effect
  was installed before or after the choice was recorded. With no colour chosen, none is given.

Read whole now: Ward of Lights, Cho-Manno's Blessing, Pentarch Ward, Flickering Ward.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test card reads whole.
- Choosing white: the creature has protection from white, the white Halo falls off, the Aura
  stays.
- Choosing red: protection from red and not from white, and the Halo stays.

Faults injected by hand: 2, all caught.
- The chosen colour always white.
- The chosen colour's protection not sparing its source.

Coverage: 16,318 of 31,900 cards (+4 over D1189's 16,314), 38,662 of 59,888 lines (+5).

## D1193 — compound X

68 legal cards print a measure with arithmetic in it: "where X is 2 plus the number of …",
"where X is twice the number of …", "… equal to the number of creatures you control plus the
number of Foods you control". None read: the measure readers took one measure.

`boardCount` now reads three compound forms, each part a measure it already reads: a number plus a
measure, twice a measure, and the sum of two measures. The five "where X is" and "equal to" readers
(`countTailOf`, draw, life, damage) accept a leading "N plus" or "twice" on "the number of"; the sum
already matched there and failed in the count.

15 of the 68 read whole after this change: An-Havva Constable, Artillery Blast, Aysen Crusader,
Bloodtithe Harvester, Deathforge Shaman, Gaea's Avenger, Jovial Evil, Liliana, the Last Hope,
Masumaro, First to Live, Price of Progress, Road Rage, Sky Cycle, Territorial Maro, Welding Sparks
and Wing Storm. The rest fail on a part this does not read, such as "cards named ~ in all
graveyards".

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- Two artifacts and a creature: 3 plus 2 is five life, twice 2 is four, 2 plus 1 is three.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- "Twice" read once.
- The fixed part of "N plus" dropped.
- Only the first part of a sum counted.

Coverage: 16,345 of 31,900 cards (+13 over D1192's 16,332), 38,696 of 59,888 lines (+14).

## D1195 — a discard of a count: "a card for each", "X cards", "cards equal to"

A discard whose size is a count, not a number printed on the card: "Target player discards a card
for each Swamp you control" (Mind Sludge), "Target opponent discards a card for each Shrine you
control" (Honden of Night's Reach), "Target player discards X cards, where X is one plus the number
of cards named ~ in all graveyards" (Mind Burst), and "Target player discards X cards" with the X
paid. The discarding player still chooses, as in every discard that does not say "at random", and
the count is clamped to the hand.

The engine change underneath: a question the card works out as it is asked (`DecisionSpecOf`, a
function since cumulative upkeep) now also gets the resolution's own context: its controller,
targets and X (`askingContext` in `automation.ts`). Until now it saw only the board and the
source, so it could not know the X paid or whose Swamps to count. The two compiler wrappers that
put a "you may" or an "unless" around a computed question pass the context through.

"Each player/opponent discards …" reads only over a count that does not name the player
discarding ("for each card in their hand" would be a different count for each of them).

Read whole now (8 of the 26 such lines in the unread list): Mind Sludge, Mind Burst, Arcane Omens,
Enthrall, Honden of Night's Reach, Voices from the Void, Bloodhusk Ritualist, and Rakdos's Return
(its "that player or that planeswalker's controller" is D1058's rewrite).
Still unread: "that player discards that many cards" after a hit (Dreamstealer, Needle Specter),
counts of things that died or were devoured this turn (Ashen-Skin Zubera, Tar Fiend), and the
draw-then-discard-that-many chains (Laquatus's Creativity, Horrid Shadowspinner, Varina).

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "A card for each Mountain you control": three Mountains, a question of three cards to the
  player targeted.
- "X cards": the X paid (2) is the size of the question.
- "Each opponent discards X cards, where X is …": four Mountains, four cards.
- "That player or that planeswalker's controller discards X cards": the player dealt the damage
  discards.
- A count larger than the hand takes the whole hand without asking.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The count fixed at one.
- The engine not passing the context (the count reads nought).
- The X read one high.

Coverage: 16,361 of 31,900 cards (+7 over D1194's 16,354), 38,713 of 59,888 lines (+8).

## D1196 — "that player discards that many cards", and a fix for counted questions about "that player"

"Whenever ~ deals combat damage to a player, that player discards that many cards" (Dreamstealer,
Needle Specter). The player hit chooses the cards; the count is the damage dealt, read as the
question is asked from the context D1195 hands a computed question (`eventAmount`).

**A fix found on the way.** "That player …" is read by rewriting it as "target player …", reading
that, and re-aiming the result at the player the event was about (`referentEffect`, D530). The
re-aim looked only at questions that are plain objects. A question the card works out as it is
asked (a function) went through untouched, still aimed at a target nobody had chosen, so it asked
nobody and the clause did nothing. Since D1195 such questions exist for "discards a card for each
…", so "that player discards a card for each Island you control" would have resolved silently. Now
the function is wrapped: what it returns is re-aimed, and the context it reads has the referent in
place of the target. On a clause about a creature it is refused, since what it would ask cannot be
known when the card is read.

Read whole now: Dreamstealer, Needle Specter. Whispering Specter needs "you may sacrifice it. If you
do, …" around the same clause, and stays unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- Three combat damage: the player hit is asked to discard three cards, and does.
- "That player discards a card for each Island you control": asked of the player hit, counting the
  attacker's controller's Islands.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- A computed question not re-aimed (the old behaviour).
- The count fixed at one.
- The question asked of the controller instead of the player hit.

Coverage: 16,363 of 31,900 cards (+2 over D1195's 16,361), 38,715 of 59,888 lines (+2).

## D1197 — "create a number of … tokens equal to …", and "~'s power"

"Create a number of 1/1 white Soldier creature tokens equal to your devotion to white" is the same
sentence as "Create X 1/1 white Soldier creature tokens, where X is your devotion to white", which
already reads (D1172 and before). So `readEffect` reads the first as the second, unless the clause
has an X of its own. 38 lines in the unread list start this way; the measure decides the rest.

And a measure: **"~'s power" / "~'s toughness"**, the source's own size. Live while it is on the
battlefield (Jacked Rabbit's attack, Krenko after its own +1/+1 counter). Once it has left, as it
last was, from the size the event recorded (Termagant Swarm and Flesh Carver dying, CR 608.2h).

Read whole now (16): Abhorrent Overlord, Chittering Witch, Evangel of Heliod, Master of Waves,
Reverent Hoplite, Goblin Gathering, Royal Talon Fighter Jet, Silverwing Squadron, Tyranid Invasion,
Underworld Hermit, Jacked Rabbit, Krenko, Tin Street Kingpin, Termagant Swarm, Flesh Carver,
Elemental Mastery, Dragon Throne of Tarkir. Still unread in the family: die rolls ("equal to the
result"), excess damage, "this creature" for "~", and counts this engine does not keep (nontoken
creatures that entered this turn, opponents attacked this turn, colors among permanents).

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- An enters trigger: three Mountains, three Soldier tokens.
- "Equal to two plus the number of …": five Goblins.
- "Equal to ~'s power" as it attacks: three Rabbits from a 3/3.
- "Equal to ~'s power" once it has died: two Tyranids from a 2/2 killed by 3 damage.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The power of a source that has left read as 0.
- The power of a source on the battlefield read as 1.
- The measure replaced by a different count.

Coverage: 16,379 of 31,900 cards (+16 over D1196's 16,363), 38,739 of 59,888 lines (+24).

## D1198 — "the amount of life you gained this turn"

A measure, in `boardCount` and the five where-X / "equal to" lists: Fortifying Draught's "+X/+X …
where X is the amount of life you gained this turn", Defiling Daemogoth, Midnight Snack, Nightmare's
Thirst, Gumdrop Poisoner, Blossoming Bogbeast. The engine has kept the amount per seat since "if
you gained life this turn" (`lifeGainedThisTurn`), so it is read from there; "you" is the controller
of what is resolving. Life gained earlier in the same resolution counts, so "You gain 2 life.
Target creature gets -X/-X …" includes the 2 (in order, as printed).

The D520 compile pin "a quantity that is not a count of the board at all" used this very phrase as
its example; it now uses "the amount of damage dealt to you this turn", which the engine does not
keep.

Read whole now (6 of the 19 such lines): Blossoming Bogbeast, Defiling Daemogoth, Fortifying
Draught, Gumdrop Poisoner, Midnight Snack, Nightmare's Thirst. The rest are unread for other parts
of their text (mills X for each opponent, mass -X/-X, cost reduction, "pay X life").

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- 3 life gained earlier and 2 by the spell itself make -5/-5, which kills a 4/4 that either alone
  would not.
- None gained is no life lost; 3 gained is 3 lost.

Faults injected by hand: 2, all caught.
- The opponent's life gained read instead of yours.
- The amount read 2 short.

Coverage: 16,385 of 31,900 cards (+6 over D1197's 16,379), 38,746 of 59,888 lines (+7).

## D1199 — colours among a scope, differently named, and the highest mana value among any scope

Three measures, each over any scope `massScope` reads:
- **"The number of colors among permanents you control"**, and "for each color among …" (both
  grammars, so it is in `countOfThing`): the colours of everything in the scope, each colour once.
  Colorless is not a colour, so lands and colorless artifacts add none.
- **"The number of differently named lands you control"** and "for each differently named …":
  each name once.
- **"The greatest / highest power, toughness or mana value among …"** beyond creatures:
  "the highest mana value among permanents you control", "… among artifacts you control".
  "Highest" is read as "greatest" in the five where-X and "equal to" lists too. Power and toughness
  skip a noncreature in the scope; mana value counts it.

Two compile pins used these phrases as their examples of "a count the engine cannot make" (D511's
Idolized row and D520's "a countable nothing can count"). They now use "the amount of damage dealt
to you this turn" and "for each card type among cards in your graveyard", which the engine does not
count.

## D1200 — "each [other] creature [you control] gets …" as the plural it is

"Each creature gets -2/-2 until end of turn", "each other creature you control gets +1/+1 and gains
trample until end of turn", "Until end of turn, each creature you control gets +2/+2 and gains
trample": the singular of the plural sentence the mass pump reads. `readEffect` now reads it as that
plural ("all creatures get …", "other creatures you control get … and gain …"), with the verbs
made plural too. The mass pump's subject list gains any other creature scope `massScope` reads
("all other creatures", "all untapped creatures"), and `massPumpSubject` still refuses what it
cannot read.

Not where the rest of the sentence says "it" or "its" ("+1/+1 for each of its colors", "if it has
flying", "unless it's tapped"): that is each creature in turn, and the plural has no such word. The
same point needed a guard in D1180's trailing "unless": it took "unless it's tapped" off "Each
creature you control gets +1/+1 until end of turn" and read "it" as the source, which before this
increment was harmless because the body never read. Now a condition about "it" after a body about
"each …" is refused there too.

Read whole now (15): Avacyn and Griselbrand, Demon of Dark Schemes, Festercreep, Harvester of
Misery, Kodama of the South Tree, Moonveil Dragon, Phalanx Tactics, Renegade Warlord, Shefet
Archfiend, Smogsteed Rider, The Meathook Massacre, Thundercloud Elemental, Waterspout Weavers, Wild
Beastmaster, Zhang He, Wei General.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole, and "each creature you control gets +1/+1 until end of turn unless
  it's tapped" is refused.
- "Each creature gets -2/-2": the 2/2s on both sides die and the 3/3 is 1/1.
- "Each other creature you control gets +1/+1 and gains trample": your other creature is 3/3 with
  trample, the source and the opponent's creature are unchanged.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- "Other" dropped from the subject.
- The "it" guard removed (caught once the refused sentence was one that would otherwise read).
- "You control" dropped from the subject.
- The D1180 guard removed.

Coverage: 16,447 of 31,900 cards (+37 over D1199's 16,410), 38,829 of 59,888 lines (+48).

## D1203 — "A. If …, B instead."

Court of Ire's "~ deals 2 damage to any target. If you're the monarch, it deals 7 damage instead",
Frost Bite's "… If you control three or more snow permanents, it deals 3 damage instead", Court of
Grace's tokens, Scute Swarm's copy. The condition is anything an intervening-if can ask, checked as
the ability resolves; B runs in place of A when it holds, A otherwise (`insteadGroup`, beside
D1157's "If …, A. Otherwise, B.").

B is read on its own, or, when it is "it deals N damage" after A's "~ deals M damage to …", as A
with the new number at the same target. A B that refers back ("put two +1/+1 counters on it
instead", "that creature gets …") is refused: read on its own it would name something else. Not a
replacement effect ("if … would …, … instead"), which is a different family, and not a kicker,
which has its own readers. Refused when either half asks a question.

Gangrenous Zombies; Jace's Triumph; Life Goes On; Scute Swarm; Secrets of the Golden City;

- "Draw two cards instead": one card without a Wizard, two with one, never three.

- The halves swapped.
- The damage substitution removed.

## D1204 — "A. If …, B instead." where B refers back to A's target

D1203 refused a B that says "it" or "that creature", since read on its own it would name something
else. When A has exactly one target and B has exactly one such pronoun, the pronoun now becomes A's
target phrase: "Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature. If …, put two +1/+1 counters on it instead"
reads B as "put two +1/+1 counters on target creature", and "Target creature gets +2/+2 until end
of turn. If …, that creature gets +4/+4 until end of turn instead" likewise. The check D1203 already
makes, that both halves aim the same way, is what keeps the substitution honest: a B aimed at a
different kind of target ("target creature you control") is refused.

D1203's refusal test moved to a B whose "it" has nothing in A to be ("Draw a card. If …, put a
+1/+1 counter on it instead").

Read whole now (6): For the Family, Galvanize, Huatli's Spurring, Tezzeret's Simulacrum, The
Destined White Mage, You're Not Alone.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests (and D1203's refusal moved):
- The test cards read whole, and a B aimed at a different kind of target than A is refused.
- "Put two +1/+1 counters on it instead": one counter on the target without a Wizard, two with one.
- "That creature gets +4/+4 instead": +2/+2 without a Wizard, +4/+4 with one, never both.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The substitution removed.
- A pronoun with no target in A read on its own.
- The same-target check removed (caught once a test named a B aimed elsewhere).

Coverage: 16,477 of 31,900 cards (+6 over D1203's 16,471), 38,866 of 59,888 lines (+7).

## D1205 — a grant of protection from a colour

"Target creature gains protection from red until end of turn", "Target creature you control gains
indestructible and protection from white until end of turn", "Creatures you control gain flying and
protection from black and from red until end of turn". Until now a grant read only keywords, and
"protection from red" was refused on purpose (D966's pin): the engine stores protection as colours
(`PumpOptions.protectionFrom`), not as a keyword. `grantedWithProtection` reads the keywords before
it and the colours after "protection from", including "from black and from red" and "from each
color". The single-target grant and the team grant use it; a protection grant counts as protective
for the bot, as hexproof does.

"Protection from creatures", "from instants" and "from the chosen color" in a spell stay unread.
D966's compile pin moved to "protection from creatures".

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.

## D1206 — "Choose a color." spells

"Choose a color. Creatures you control gain protection from the chosen color until end of turn"
(Brave the Elements, Akroma's Blessing), "Choose a color. ~ deals X damage to each creature of the
chosen color" (Sudden Demise), Searing Rays' count of "creatures of the chosen color that player
controls". Read as D1142's "Choose a creature type." spells are: the colour is asked as the spell
resolves, and the rest is read with the colour written in ("red creatures", "protection from
red"), once with a stand-in colour for whether it reads and what it targets, and again with the
colour chosen. The bot names the colour it most fears for protection and damage, its own deck's
colour otherwise. D1205's protection grants are what make the first shape read.

Not a mana ability that chooses a colour (Astral Cornucopia, "{T}: Choose a color. Add one mana of
that color …"): read here it would go on the stack, and a mana ability never does (CR 605.3). It
stays unread.

## D1207 — a return from the graveyard on another card's death

Nether Traitor: "Whenever another creature is put into your graveyard from the battlefield, you may
pay {B}. If you do, return ~ from your graveyard to the battlefield". D632 reads a card returning
itself from its graveyard only when the event's subject is on the battlefield, because a card's own
death already fires from the graveyard. That also refused another card's death, whose subject is in
a graveyard too but is not this card: this card hears it from its own graveyard like any other
event. A death or a trip to the graveyard of **another** card now takes D632's reading.

Read whole now (1): Nether Traitor. The others with "return ~ from your graveyard" are unread for
other parts (tapped and attacking, "while ~ is in your graveyard", perpetual).

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both test cards read whole, each as a graveyard ability.
- Another creature dies: {1} paid, and the card returns from your graveyard to the battlefield.
- "Whenever another creature dies, you may return ~ … to your hand": on a yes it goes to your hand.

Faults injected by hand: 2, 1 caught.
- Another card's death not taken: caught.
- "Put into your graveyard" counted as another card only when the event says so explicitly: not

## D1211 — switching power and toughness

"Switch target creature's power and toughness until end of turn" (About Face, Transmutation, the
Thaumaturgists), "Switch ~'s power and toughness until end of turn" (Aquamoeba, Windreaver, Crag
Puca), "switch its power and toughness" on Valakut Fireboar's attack, and Mannichi's "each
creature's". The engine had no way to say it: a new continuous-effect flag,
`switchPowerToughness`, is applied in layer 7d (CR 613.4d), after every other change to power and
toughness, counters and pumps included, whatever order they arrived in. Two switches cancel, so the
count's parity decides.

## D1212 — damage that can't be prevented, and players who can't gain life

Skullcrack's turn: "Players can't gain life this turn. Damage can't be prevented this turn." Two new
facts about the turn on the game state, cleared with the others when it ends:
- `damageUnpreventableThisTurn`: `dealDamage` skips every prevention (protection's included, CR
  702.16e, and a shield counter's, CR 122.1c), while a redirect still applies, since it is not a
  prevention.
- `lifeGainBlockedThisTurn`, by seat: `gainLife` gains nothing for them. "Players", "your
  opponents", "each opponent", "target player" and "target opponent" read.

And Combust's "~ deals 5 damage to target creature. The damage can't be prevented.": the sentences
before it resolve with `damageUnpreventableNow` set, and it is put back as it was straight after,
so only the spell's own damage is unpreventable.

Not yet: "Damage that would be dealt by ~ can't be prevented" as a static (Excruciator), "Combat
damage can't be prevented" (Frenzied Baloth), Lava Burst's "can't be prevented or dealt instead".
The Phantoms' "prevent that damage. Remove a +1/+1 counter" (D1147) is left as it was under
unpreventable damage; its ruling (the counter is still removed and the damage dealt) is a later
refinement.

Read whole now (7): Call In a Professional, Combust, Flaring Pain, Impractical Joke, Pinpoint
Avalanche, Pyrewood Gearhulk, Skullcrack.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- A prevention shield stops an ordinary 3 damage, but not "the damage can't be prevented".
- Only Combust's own damage: a Bolt after it is prevented as usual.
- "Damage can't be prevented this turn" and "players can't gain life this turn" last for the
  turn: a shielded creature dies to a Bolt, and 3 life gained is no life gained.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The prevention shields still spent.
- Combust's flag left set after it.
- The life-gain block ignored.

Coverage: 16,566 of 31,900 cards (+10 over D1211's 16,556), 38,988 of 59,888 lines (+18).

## D835 — "When you play another land": City of Traitors

Most-played order: City of Traitors (rank 1137), the corpus's one printing.

**Engine.** The `land-played` event (D1187) now carries the land as its subject. `raise` copies
the subject onto it, as it does for an entry or a discard, and the trigger gains `other`: not when
the watcher is the land that was played. So the City's own play does not sacrifice it, and the
next land does.

**Reader.** D1187's "Whenever you/an opponent/a player play(s) a land" also takes "When" and
"another land".

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- playing the City itself leaves it;
- playing a Forest with the City out sacrifices it;
- an opponent's land does not.
D1187's tests pass unchanged.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught (`other` ignored by the matcher, the land not passed as
the subject, and "another" unread).

- engine tests: 6436, all passing (on a9f8fce, D835 and D836 gated together)
