## D836 — "Double the number of +1/+1 counters on …": Kalonian Hydra

Most-played order: Kalonian Hydra (rank 1150), with Mossborn Hydra, Bristly Bill and Ornery
Tumblewagg.

**Reader.** In `readEffect`: "double the number of +1/+1 counters on (each creature you control |
target creature [you control] | this creature | <self>)". To double them is to put that many more
(CR 122.7), so the effect goes through `addCounters`, and anything that changes how many counters
are put applies. "On it" (nine lines) and "on that creature" (five) stay unread: which creature
"it" is depends on the sentence before.

- the cards read;
- "each creature you control" turns our 2 counters into 4, leaves our creature with none at none,
  and leaves the opponent's 3;
- "target creature" aimed at the opponent's creature turns 3 into 6.

Faults injected by script: 2 of 2 caught (one counter added in place of doubling, and the
opponent's creatures included).

**Two test tables moved, as they say to.** The first gate failed twice, both on purpose:

- compiled-vs-written now lists Dragonsguard Elite in DISAGREE: the compiled ability does what

## D837 — "When ~ dies, if it was a creature, return it … It's an enchantment": the Enduring cycle

Most-played order: Enduring Vitality (rank 432), Enduring Innocence (738), Enduring Tenacity (791),
Enduring Curiosity (834) and Enduring Courage (1161). Each was one sentence short of finished.

**Reader.**
- "When ~ dies, if it was a creature, …" is read as the line without the condition, with the
  death trigger narrowed to a creature (`what: 'creature'`, asked of the snapshot as it died).
- `clausesOf` joins "return it to the battlefield under its owner's control. It's an enchantment"
  into one clause, and D1061's back-from-the-graveyard reader takes "as an enchantment".

**Engine.** The card comes back not a creature, as itself otherwise. That is a flag on the object,
`CardInstance.returnedNoncreature`, set as it is put back: `characteristicsOf` takes the creature
type and creature subtypes off its type line while it is on the battlefield, and `relocate` clears
it on the way out, so the card in a graveyard is a creature card again. The first version used a
continuous effect sourced from the card. That effect ended as the card left, so the snapshot of its
next death said "creature" and the card came back again; the test caught it.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- destroyed as a 3/3 it returns as an enchantment that is not a creature; destroyed as that
  enchantment it stays in the graveyard; moved back onto the battlefield as a new object, it is a
  creature again.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught (the flag not set, the death not narrowed to a creature,
`characteristicsOf` ignoring the flag, and `relocate` keeping it).

- engine tests: 6438, all passing (on d581153)
- Coverage: 16,561 to 16,566 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 38,978 to 38,983 of 59,888 lines, against d581153.

## D838 — "Put a +1/+1 counter on ~ and it …": the "it" is the card (Kappa Cannoneer)

Most-played order: Kappa Cannoneer (rank 888), with Infernal Pet.

"Whenever an artifact you control enters, put a +1/+1 counter on Kappa Cannoneer and it can't be
blocked this turn." The second half did not read, and the shape had a worse problem beside it. On
a trigger about another permanent, a bare "it" is read as the event's subject (the docblock above
`selfEffect` explains why: Armory of Iroas's "put a +1/+1 counter on it" is the equipped creature).
So "… on ~ and it gains flying" would have given the entering artifact flying, not the card. In
this sentence "it" is the card the first half named.

**Reader.** In `conjoinedEffect`, when the first part ends "on <the card's name>", a later part
that begins with "it" has the name put in its place. "It can't be blocked this turn" then reads as
the card's own restriction.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- both cards read;
- an artifact creature entering puts a counter on the Cannoneer, which also can't be blocked, and
  on a second watcher, which also gains flying. The artifact gets neither.

Faults injected by script: 1 of 1 caught (the name not carried into "it").

- engine tests: 6440, all passing (on f2b4851)
- Coverage: 16,566 to 16,567 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 38,983 to 38,984 of 59,888 lines, against f2b4851. Infernal Pet already read before, with "it" resolved through the cast event, whose subject is unset, so it was not counted twice.

library." Mnemonic Nexus: "Each player …". Every card goes to its owner's library, the library is

sentence when the line is cut into clauses, as Wheel of Fortune's is (D651), because cut apart
neither half is a sentence.

## D839 — Attaching an Equipment as it enters: Sigarda's Aid, Hammer of Nazahn

Most-played order: Hammer of Nazahn (rank 721) and Sigarda's Aid (rank 844).

An Equipment's own "When this Equipment enters, attach it to target creature you control" was
already read, in `attachmentScriptFor`, where the card's bonus line is at hand. These two attach a
**different** Equipment, the one the entry event is about, and its bonus is printed on that card.

**Reader.** On a battlefield trigger, "[you may] attach it / that Equipment to target creature you
control" targets a creature you control and attaches the event's subject. Only if it is an
Equipment on the battlefield, and with that Equipment's own `equipBonus`, read from its script
through `scriptOfCard` (compiled or hand-written, as `derive.ts` injects it). An Equipment whose
bonus nothing reads is not attached: that would be an Equipment that gives nothing with no badge
to say so. Hammer of Nazahn's own entry ("Hammer of Nazahn or another Equipment") attaches the
Hammer itself.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- both cards read;
- with Sigarda's Aid out, an Equipment cast for free attaches to our Bear with its +1/+1;
- the Hammer's own entry attaches it, making the Bear a 4/2 with indestructible.

**D972's pin, retargeted.** The first gate failed on one test: D972 pinned "When this Equipment
enters, attach it to target creature you control. Destroy target artifact." as unread, because its
whole-card path would have handed the second target the host creature. The line now reads through
the trigger's own composition instead. A test run showed the reading is right: the Equipment
attaches to the first target with its bonus, and the second target is destroyed. So the pin is now
a positive test of exactly that.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught (the Equipment's bonus not carried, the Hammer's own
entry refused, and the reader off).

- engine tests: 6444, all passing (on 94287f0)
- Coverage: 16,567 to 16,571 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 38,984 to 38,991 of 59,888 lines, against 94287f0.

## D1216 — targets "from a single graveyard"

"Exile up to two target cards from a single graveyard" (Rapid Decay, Decompose, Scarab Feast,
Arashin Sunshield, Carrion Beetles). "From graveyards" already read; "a single graveyard" adds that
every target the spell takes has the same owner. A new target-spec flag, `sameOwner`, is checked
across the chosen targets in `checkTargets` (the only place that sees them together), so one card
from each of two graveyards is refused. The bot's two target pickers take the rest from the first
pick's graveyard.

Ghoul, Feral Deathgorger, Griffnaut Tracker, Rag Dealer, Rapid Decay, Scarab Feast, Shred Memory.

D745's test that pinned "from a single graveyard" as unread now asserts it reads, with the flag.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test card reads whole, and its spec says one graveyard.
- Two from the opponent's graveyard are exiled; one from each graveyard is refused.
- The bot, with one card in the opponent's graveyard and two in its own, never mixes the two.

Faults injected by hand: 2, both caught.
- The one-graveyard check removed from `checkTargets`.
- The bot's same-owner filter removed (caught once the graveyards were uneven).

## D1217 — an Aura that exiles its host, and "target opponent gains control of ~"

Two small readers:
- **"Exile enchanted creature"** as an Aura's ability (the Pacifism upgrades: Dreadful Apathy,
  Cooped Up, Redemption Arc, Sigarda's Imprisonment), and "destroy" or "return … to its owner's
  hand" the same way. The host is the Aura's `attachedTo`, as "tap enchanted creature" reads it
  (D939).
- **"Target opponent gains control of ~"** (Jinxed Idol, Jinxed Ring, Humble Defector, Avarice
  Amulet): for good; the card moves to that player's battlefield.

A new flag, `costSacrificesSource`, is set from an activated ability's cost as `xPayable` is
(D1055): an Aura that sacrifices itself to pay ("{3}{W}{W}, Sacrifice ~: Exile enchanted
creature", Choking Restraints) is in the graveyard and attached to nothing by the time the ability
resolves, so the host reader refuses there rather than doing nothing. Today the cost parser already
refuses an Aura sacrificing itself, so the flag is a safeguard for when it does not.

Read whole now (12): Act of Authority, Avarice Amulet, Cooped Up, Dreadful Apathy, Drooling Ogre,
Humble Defector, Jinxed Idol, Jinxed Ring, Measure of Wickedness, Redemption Arc, Sigarda's
Imprisonment, Starke of Rath.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The Aura and the Idol read whole, and the Aura that sacrifices itself stays unread.
- "{0}: Exile enchanted creature": the opponent's creature the Aura is on is exiled.
- "Target opponent gains control of ~": the Idol is on the opponent's battlefield.

Faults injected by hand: 3, 2 caught.
- Exile read as a bounce: caught.
- The control change dropped: caught.
- The sacrifice guard removed: not caught, because the cost parser refuses the line first (see

## D841 — "Whenever one or more [land] cards are put into your graveyard from anywhere": The Gitrog Monster

Most-played order: The Gitrog Monster (rank 910). The corpus prints the batched form on about 18
lines; this reads "from anywhere" with no type or with land, creature, artifact or enchantment.

**Engine.** The `to-graveyard` event had only one event per card. Now, after those, `settle`
raises one batch per graveyard per move, carrying each card's printed types (`batch`,
`batchTypes`, and the owner as `subjectSeat`). As discards do (D993), a trigger hears only its own
kind: a per-card trigger ignores the batch and a batch trigger ignores the cards. A batch trigger
matches if its graveyard is the right one and any card in the batch is of its type.

**Not read:** "from your library" (9 lines), which needs to know where each card came from.
`cameFrom` records only the battlefield.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- two lands and an Ox milled at once draw one card, not two;
- three Oxen draw nothing;
- lands milled into the opponent's graveyard draw nothing;
- a per-card watcher ("a card is put into your graveyard") still gains one life per card, four
  for three milled cards and the spell, and does not hear the batch.

Faults injected by script: 4 of 4 caught. They cover the batch not raised, per-card triggers
hearing the batch (missed at first; the per-card watcher test was added for it), the type ignored,
and whose graveyard ignored.

- engine tests: 6468, all passing (on 97a76ef, D840 and D841 gated together)
- Coverage, both together: 16,636 to 16,641 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 39,091 to 39,096 of 59,888 lines, against 97a76ef.

## D842 — One subject, several verbs: Archon of Cruelty

Most-played order: Archon of Cruelty (rank 951). The same reading finishes about twenty cards
across the corpus, among them Mind Drain, Mental Agony, Geth's Verdict, Funeral Rites, Arbiter of
Woe, Atrocious Experiment and Hopeless Nightmare.

"Target opponent sacrifices a creature or planeswalker, discards a card, and loses 3 life. You draw
a card and gain 3 life." Each verb read alone, as its own sentence, with "That player" for the
targeted player, the same words for "each opponent / each player" and "you". The shared subject
was what nothing read.

**Reader.** `distributeSubject` gives each later verb its subject back. "That player" after a
targeted player keeps it one target; the same words after "each …" and "you". It splits only where
the next word is one of a fixed list of player verbs (discards, loses, gains, draws, sacrifices,
mills, creates, reveals, scries, surveils, exiles, shuffles, and their "you" forms), so a list of
objects like "a creature, an artifact, and a land" is never cut.

**A fallback, and why.** The first version split every line in `clausesOf`. A card-by-card diff
against the pushed build found it lost 11 cards while gaining 20. Lines like "you gain 1 life and
scry 1", "you gain X life and draw X cards, where X is …" and "target player draws two cards and
loses 2 life" read as one clause already, and cut apart they did not. So `composeEffects` now reads
the clauses as printed first (`composeEffectsAsPrinted`, the old body), and only if that fails
retries once with the subject distributed. The diff afterwards: 0 lost, 20 gained.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- Archon's line as a sorcery: the targeted opponent sacrifices their creature, discards and loses
  3, and we draw and gain 3, with one target throughout;
- "each opponent discards a card and loses 2 life" in a pod of three takes a card and two life
  from each opponent and nothing from us.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught (the target repeated instead of "That player", the
fallback off, and the "you" verbs off).

- engine tests: 6477, all passing (on 4e24061)
- Coverage: 16,670 to 16,690 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 39,139 to 39,165 of 59,888 lines, against 4e24061.

## D1220 — "that spell's controller" on a targeted trigger, and "a spell or ability you control"

Bonecrusher Giant: "Whenever ~ becomes the target of a spell, ~ deals 2 damage to that spell's
controller." The `targeted` event is raised with the targeting object's controller as its actor, so
on a trigger whose every event is `targeted` the possessive "that spell's controller" (and "that
spell or ability's controller") is the acting player, read through the same referent swap as "that
player" on a cast or discard trigger. When the spell was the Giant's own controller's, the trigger
carries no actor (it drops the watcher's own seat) and the damage goes to that controller, which is
what the card does. On any other event the possessive still names nobody and stays unread.

And the self-named targeted prologue with "a spell or ability you control" (`by: 'you'`), which
D1117's "for the first time each turn" leaves behind on the Valiant cards that name themselves.
Beta Ray Bill, Flowerfoot Swordmaster and Whiskervale Forerunner now read their trigger and wait on
their effects.

Read whole now (10): Bonecrusher Giant, and the self-named Valiant cards Emberheart Challenger,
Heartfire Hero, Lava Runner, Mouse Trapper, Nettle Guard, Retromancer, Seedglaive Mentor, Veteran
Guardmouse, Whiskerquill Scribe. (Corrected after the measurement: the first draft of this entry
said 1.)

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- Every test card reads whole; the possessive on an attack trigger stays unread.
- An opponent's spell aimed at the Giant: the opponent takes 2.
- Its controller's own spell: the controller takes 2.
- "That spell or ability's controller" reads the same player.
- Valiant: two of its controller's spells in a turn give one counter; an opponent's spell gives none.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The damaged player always the trigger's controller.
- `by: 'you'` widened to anybody.
- The possessive offered on every event, not only `targeted`.
- The once-a-turn flag dropped from "for the first time each turn".

Coverage: 16,714 of 31,900 cards (+30 over D1219's 16,684), 39,190 of 59,888 lines (+37).
The +30 includes the other session's D842, merged in after D1219 was measured; D1220's own gain
is the 10 cards above.
## D843 — A modal activated ability as one ability per mode: Cankerbloom

Most-played order: Cankerbloom (in the top 2000), with Breya, Etherium Shaper, Breya's
Apprentice, Balm of Restoration, Insidious Fungus, Phoenix Down, Disciple of the Ring and Tea,
Earl Grey, Hot. About 36 legal lines print "<cost>: Choose one —" over bullets.

`ModalDef` is a spell's (and since D757 a trigger's); an activated ability had no modes, so these
lines did not read.

**Reading.** `modalAbilityFor`, a whole-card reader beside D757's `modalTriggerFor`: the header
"<cost>: Choose one —" and its bullets become one ability per mode, each with the whole cost
(`lineScriptFor("<cost>: <mode>")`, which must give exactly one ability). To activate a "choose
one" ability is to pay its cost and choose a mode as it goes on the stack (CR 602.2b, 700.2), and
that is what choosing one of these abilities is. The client shows a button per mode, and the bot
weighs them as it weighs any abilities, so nothing changes in the engine.

**Only where that is the same card.**
- "Choose one" alone: "choose two", "one or more", escalate and entwine stay unread.
- No activation limit: "Activate only once each turn", after the bullets or in one, would become
  a limit per mode, so the line is refused.
- A bullet that does not read refuses the whole line.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- the Bloom reads as three abilities with the whole cost, and a modal ability with "Activate only
  once each turn" keeps its header unread;
- the enchantment mode, activated alone, destroys the opponent's enchantment, sacrifices the
  Bloom, and leaves their artifact.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught. They cover the limit ignored (missed at first: the
limit line is unread on its own either way, so the test now asserts the header itself is unread),
the reader not registered, and the cost dropped from the modes.

- engine tests: 6483, all passing (on 946f080)
- Coverage: 16,705 to 16,713 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 39,181 to 39,228 of 59,888 lines, against 946f080. The line count rises by more than the card count: the modal header and its bullets are claimed on cards still short of another line, Umezawa's Jitte among them.

## D1221 — "Look at target player's hand and choose N cards from it"

The older printing of the chosen discard: Thrull Surgeon ("… choose a card from it. That player
discards that card"), Extortion ("… up to two cards from it. That player discards those cards"),
and the two that put the cards back on top: Painful Memories ("Put that card on top of that player's
library") and Agonizing Memories ("Put them on top of that player's library in any order"). One
sentence where the newer cards print two, and the same question as D531's: the caster picks out of
the target's hand, which the question shows them. A count of one, two or three, or "up to" one of
those; the second sentence must agree with it ("that card" after one, "those cards" or "them" after
more), or the card stays unread. "In any order" is the order picked, the last one picked ending on
top. The type words are D970's, now in one function both readers share (`handCardTypeTest`).

Not read: X ("choose X cards", Mind Warp, Abandon Hope, Discordant Dirge), because the question's
size is fixed before X could be looked at.

Read whole now (4): Agonizing Memories, Extortion, Painful Memories, Thrull Surgeon.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- Every test card reads whole; "choose a card … discards those cards" stays unread.
- "Up to two": the caster is asked, for 0 to 2, and both cards picked are discarded.
- "A nonland card": the only nonland card is taken and the land stays.
- On top: the card picked is the top of the library.
- Two on top "in any order": the last picked on top, the first under it.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- "Up to" asked as exactly N.
- The type filter dropped.
- The cards put on top in reverse.
- The pronoun no longer required to agree with the count.
- Discards put on top instead.

## D844 — "Whenever equipped creature deals combat damage": Umezawa's Jitte, and the Equipment that sees it even when its creature dies

Most-played order: Umezawa's Jitte. D843 read its modal ability; this reads its trigger. The same
rows finish Lost Jitte, Banshee's Blade, Drinker of Sorrow and Sunhome Enforcer.

**Reader.** Two rows beside D904's "Whenever ~ / equipped creature deals damage" (to anything):
"deals **combat** damage", on the same events with `combatOnly`. D904 raises one event per source
for its combat damage in a step, so a creature that hits a blocker and a player triggers it once.

**An engine bug, found by the test.** A Jitte on a creature that died in the combat it dealt damage
in got nothing. The trigger asked "is the Jitte attached to the source?" when the event was raised,
after state-based actions had killed the creature and `relocate` had detached the Jitte. The
damage happened while it was attached, and that is the moment the rules ask about (CR 603.10a's
look-back for leave-the-battlefield abilities is the same idea, and a trigger on the damage event
sees the game as the damage was dealt).

The fix follows D994, which solved the same problem for "enchanted creature is dealt damage":
- each damage record notes what was attached to its **source** as it was dealt (`sourceHosted`,
  in `recordDamage`, before state-based actions);
- the "deals damage to anything" events carry that as `attachments`;
- `wasAttached` already prefers the event's answer to the board's.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- the equipped creature's noncombat ping puts no counters, and its combat damage to a blocking
  wall puts two;
- blocked by a 3/3, the equipped creature dies, and the Jitte still gets its two counters;
- a counter pays for a mode (you gain 2 life) and is gone.

Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught (`combatOnly` dropped, `sourceHosted` not recorded, and
the combat raise not carrying it).

- engine tests: 6492, all passing (on 3c56540)
- Coverage: 16,723 to 16,730 of 31,900 cards with every line read, and 39,239 to 39,247 of 59,888 lines, against 3c56540.

## D1222 — "When that creature dies this turn, …"

A Good Day to Die, Make Your Mark, Felonious Rage, Searing Blood, Virulent Wound, Burn Away: a
spell aims at a creature and leaves a watch on it for the rest of the turn. Delayed triggers had
only ever fired at a step; this one fires on an event, so `DelayedTrigger` gained `onDeath`. The
spell schedules the watch as it finishes (on the creature it aimed at, if that creature is still on
the battlefield), `raise` fires it when that creature dies (`fireDeathWatches`), and `fireDelayed`
drops it on the next turn's first step if it never did. Only the object the watch was made about
counts (CR 400.7): a creature blinked after the spell is a new object, and its death fires nothing.

The effect may name the dead creature's controller ("its controller", "the creature's
controller"): the watch fires with that player as its actor, taken from the snapshot `relocate`
keeps of what left the battlefield. For a token that snapshot's seat is where it went, its owner's,
which differs from its controller only for a stolen token.

The view shows the watch under "later" as "When it dies this turn".

Not read: the same sentence on abilities (Grim Javelineer, Sandals of Abdallah), in the middle of
a spell (Time to Feed), or with an effect that refers to the creature itself (Rushed Rebirth's
"lesser mana value", Scintillating Encore's "return it").

Read whole now (9): A Good Day to Die, Blessed Defiance, Burn Away, Felonious Rage, Make Your Mark,
Otherworldly Outburst, Scarblade's Malice, Searing Blood, Virulent Wound.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- The creature dies two spells later: the watch fires then, and draws.
- The spell kills it: the creature's controller takes 3, not the caster.
- "Its controller gets a poison counter."
- A creature that survives: the watch is gone by the next turn's upkeep.
- A creature blinked after the spell, then killed: nothing is drawn.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The watch never fired on a death.
- The object check dropped.
- The watch kept past the turn.
- No actor passed, so the caster took the damage.

Not covered by a test: the watch skipped when the aimed-at creature has already left the battlefield
as the spell finishes.

The coverage below includes the other session's D844, merged in before this was measured.

Coverage: 16,742 of 31,900 cards (+16 over D1221's 16,726), 39,259 of 59,888 lines (+17).

## D1223 — "those creatures", "they" and "them" after a clause that aimed at several

Sparkmage's Gambit and Wrap in Flames ("~ deals 1 damage to each of up to two/three target
creatures. Those creatures can't block this turn."), Coronation of Chaos ("Up to three target
creatures can't block this turn. Goad them."), Leo's Guidance ("Put a +1/+1 counter on each of up to
three target creatures. Untap them."), Bretagard Stronghold ("… They gain vigilance and lifelink
until end of turn."). The singular referent (D530) supplies one object, and D946's plural freeze
read one sentence; this is the plural for any clause. The clause is read with "target creature" in
the pronoun's place, the verb made singular to agree, and must then ask for exactly that one target
and no question; its effect is run once for each object the one earlier targeting clause chose, with
that object as its target. Nothing new is targeted.

Refused where the rest of the clause has a pronoun of its own ("they", "their", "it", "its"), since
it could mean the group or one of them, and where more than one earlier clause aimed at something.

Read whole now (5): Bretagard Stronghold, Coronation of Chaos, Leo's Guidance, Sparkmage's Gambit,
Wrap in Flames.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole; a mixed sentence ("until their controller's next turn") stays unread.
- "Those creatures get -2/-0": each of the two chosen, and not the third creature.
- "They gain flying": both chosen, after their own pump; the third does not.
- "Goad them": all three chosen with three targets, only the one with one target.

Faults injected by hand: 4, 2 caught.
- The effect done to the first object only: caught.
- The object not handed to the effect as its target: caught.
- The rest-of-clause pronoun guard dropped: not caught. The mixed sentence in the test is refused
  by the reader it is handed to as well, and no printed line was found that only the guard refuses.
- The verb left plural ("gain"): not caught, because the grant reader already reads "gain" as
  "gains"; the agreement matters for the other verbs.

Coverage: 16,747 of 31,900 cards (+5 over D1222's 16,742), 39,264 of 59,888 lines (+5).

## D1224 — counters of two or three kinds in one sentence

"Put a +1/+1 counter and a lifelink counter on target creature" (Unexpected Fangs), "Put a flying
counter, a deathtouch counter, and a lifelink counter on target creature" (Qarsi Revenant), "Put a
+1/+1 counter, a reach counter, and a deathtouch counter on target creature. Untap it." (Gift of the
Viper), Champion of Dusan's renew. `clausesOf` splits the sentence into one per kind, the first on
what was printed and the rest on the same object: "it" after a target, so no second target is
asked for and the referent machinery hands each the one creature; the printed words again for
anything else ("~", "that creature"). Each kind is then read by the counter readers that already
exist, keyword counters (D1032) among them.

Read whole now (4): Champion of Dusan, Gift of the Viper, Qarsi Revenant, Unexpected Fangs.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole, with one target.
- Two kinds on the one target, and the keyword counter grants its keyword.
- Three kinds and the untap after them, all on the same creature.
- "On ~", on an activated ability: both kinds on itself.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The printed object repeated for every kind (a second target asked for).
- The middle kinds dropped.
- The first kind replaced by the last.

Pod sweep 82001 (100 games, D1221 build): 100 finished, no throw, no stall.

## D1225 — "Copy target triggered ability you control", read from the card

Strionic Resonator has been written by hand since the stack could hold an ability; the compiler
could not read its text, nor its kin. Now it does: "Copy target triggered ability you control"
(Strionic Resonator, Kirol), "activated or triggered" (Peter Parker's Camera), and the source
named, "from an artifact source" (Tawnos, Urza's Apprentice; Scientist Supreme of A.I.M.), "a
creature source" (Echo, Perceptive Prodigy), "an enchantment source" (Weaver of Harmony), "a
colorless source" (Abstruse Archaic), "another legendary source that's not a commander" (The
Peregrine Dynamo). The source is read live where it is still on the battlefield, and as printed
where it has gone. The copy and its retarget sentence are held together by `clausesOf` and read as
one ability with the hand-written card's question (`NEW_TARGETS_FOR_THE_COPY`) and the same
`copyAbilityOnStack`.

Not read: "twice" and "X times" (Mister Fantastic, Gogo), because each copy may be pointed
somewhere else and one question cannot say where both go.

Read whole now (9): Abstruse Archaic, Echo, Perceptive Prodigy, Kirol, Attentive First-Year, Peter
Parker's Camera, Scientist Supreme of A.I.M., Strionic Resonator, Tawnos, Urza's Apprentice, The
Peregrine Dynamo, Weaver of Harmony.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole; "twice" stays unread.
- A copied enter trigger gains its life twice.
- "Triggered" refuses an activated ability as its target; "activated or triggered" takes it, and
  the copy resolves.
- "From an artifact source" refuses a creature's trigger and copies an artifact's.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The triggered or activated filter dropped.
- The source filter dropped.
- The copy never made.

Not covered by a test: an opponent's ability refused as a target (the "you control" check).

Coverage: 16,762 of 31,900 cards (+8 over D1224's 16,754), 39,282 of 59,888 lines (+11).

## D1226 — "Activated abilities of artifacts can't be activated"

Null Rod, Stony Silence and Collector Ouphe ("of artifacts"), Cursed Totem ("of creatures"), Linvala,
Keeper of Silence ("of creatures your opponents control"), Karn, the Great Creator ("of artifacts
your opponents control"), Clarion Conqueror ("of artifacts, creatures, and planeswalkers"), and
Damping Matrix and Sharkey ("… unless they're mana abilities"). Arrest's flags (D943, D944) as a
static over each kind named; three scopes were added for them (`opponent-artifacts`,
`opponent-lands`, `all-planeswalkers`). A mana ability is an activated ability (CR 605.1a), so under
a Null Rod a Sol Ring taps for nothing and the mana-source list leaves it out; under a Damping
Matrix it still does.

Not read: "sources with the chosen name" (Pithing Needle, Phyrexian Revoker, Sorcerous Spyglass),
which needs a card name chosen as the permanent enters.

Read whole now (7): Clarion Conqueror, Collector Ouphe, Cursed Totem, Damping Matrix, Linvala,
Keeper of Silence, Null Rod, Stony Silence. Karn and Sharkey read this line and wait on others.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- "Of artifacts": an artifact's ability is refused and its mana is gone; a creature's ability and
  mana are not touched.
- "Of creatures": the other way round.
- "Creatures your opponents control": the opponent's creature is refused, the controller's is not.
- "Unless they're mana abilities": both kinds' other abilities are refused, both kinds' mana stays.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- Every reading taken as "unless they're mana abilities".
- "Your opponents'" creatures widened to every creature.
- "Your opponents'" creatures read as a scope that matches nothing.
- Only the first kind of a list kept.

## D847 — "Until end of turn, creatures you control get +X/+X, where X is …": Overwhelming Stampede

Most-played order: Overwhelming Stampede. The same rewrite finishes Elspeth, Undaunted Hero
as well.

**Reader.** A leading "Until end of turn," moves to the end of its sentence when the sentence
ends in a "where X is …" count, so "Until end of turn, creatures you control gain trample and get
+X/+X, where X is the greatest power among creatures you control" reaches the pump reader as
"Creatures you control gain trample and get +X/+X until end of turn, where X is …". X is counted
once, as the spell resolves.

**Tests.** 1 engine test: Overwhelming Stampede makes a 2/2 Bear 6/6 and a 4/4 Ogre 8/7 (the
Ogre's power, counted once), both with trample. The opponent's creature is unchanged.

Faults injected by script: 1 of 1 caught (the rewrite removed).

## D848 — A bite at any target, and at everything: Chandra's Ignition

**Reader.** D546's bite ("target creature you control deals damage equal to its power to target
creature …") now also takes "any target" and "target player" as the second target. The damage
goes to whatever was chosen, player or permanent, from the creature. "Target creature you control
deals damage equal to its power to each other creature and each opponent" (Chandra's Ignition),
and either half alone, is new. The power is read once, before any damage is dealt. The damage
comes from the creature, so deathtouch and lifelink apply. "Any other target" stays unread,
because the target reader cannot yet exclude the biter.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the cards read;
- Ignition with a 4-power Ogre kills both players' Bears, takes 4 from the opponent, and
  leaves the Ogre undamaged and our life unchanged;
- the "any target" bite can hit the opponent for the creature's power.

Faults injected by script: 5 of 5 caught. These were: "any target" refused, the biter hitting
itself, no opponents, every player treated as an opponent, and only our own creatures hit. A
sixth fault changed nothing and was dropped.

Most-played order: Commander's Plate (rank 474).

the colours outside the effect controller's commander identity (`commanderIdentity`, CR 903.4),

color identity", after the +3/+3.

- with a black commander: green is shielded, black is not;

## D850 — Weaker creatures can't block yours: Champion of Lambholt

Most-played order: Champion of Lambholt (rank 592).

**Engine.** A new printed combat static, `weakerCantBlockYours`, beside D943's `weakerCantBlock`.
`canBlock` refuses a blocker whose power is less than that of a creature with it controlled by
the attacker's controller, compared as they are now. Losing all abilities clears it, like D943's.

- with the 3-power Champion out, a 2-power Bear cannot block our attacking 1/1, and a 4-power

- without the Champion, the Bear blocks;

## D1227 — "Creatures entering don't cause abilities to trigger"

Torpor Orb, Tocatli Honor Guard and Hushwing Gryff; Doorkeeper Thrull ("Artifacts and creatures
entering …"); Hushbringer ("Creatures entering or dying …"). Two new script fields,
`entriesDontTrigger` (the kinds) and `deathsDontTrigger`, read live off every permanent on the
battlefield that still has its abilities. `raise` checks them before anything else, and an entry
or a death of a silenced kind is not announced at all: not to the permanent's own "when this
enters", not to the board's "whenever a creature enters", not to a death watch (D1222). A batch of
arrivals ("one or more creatures enter") keeps only the arrivals that are not silenced, and is
dropped if none are left. Replacement effects and "enters with" are not triggers, so they are
untouched.

Not read: Elesh Norn's "Permanents entering don't cause abilities of permanents your opponents
control to trigger", which waits on its other line (an extra trigger, next).

Read whole now (5): Doorkeeper Thrull, Hushbringer, Hushwing Gryff, Tocatli Honor Guard, Torpor Orb.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- Without a silencer, a creature's own enter trigger, a board watcher and a batch watcher all fire.
- Torpor: none of the three fire for a creature; an artifact's enter trigger still does.
- "Artifacts and creatures": the artifact's is silenced too.
- "Or dying": a death fires nothing where, without Hushbringer, it did.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- An entry never silenced.
- A death never silenced.
- The batch not filtered.
- The artifact kind ignored.
- Every entry silenced, not only creatures'.

Pod sweep 83001 (100 games, D1223 build): 100 finished, no throw, no stall.

The two new fields are listed among the mechanics the compiler reads that no built-in deck plays
(the deck-coverage test), with the runtime block above as their evidence.

**And the gate's `Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"`, found and fixed.** Five gate and pregate runs in
a row failed with that error beside every test passing. Running files on their own found it:
`scripts.test.ts` alone reproduces it, and `playout.test.ts` alone does not. Every test in
`scripts.test.ts` is synchronous, and vitest runs synchronous tests one after another without
returning to the event loop, so the file is one unbroken stretch of work; once that passed 60
seconds (76 now), the worker's pending reporter call timed out before it could read the reply already
waiting for it. A file-level `afterEach` now yields to the event loop every hundred tests, and the
file alone runs clean. Two smaller changes made on the way are kept, since both shorten unbroken
stretches: the file's decks are built on first use rather than as the file is collected (a getter
wrapper over `customDeck` in the test file only; collection went from 25 seconds to 8), and the long
`playout.test.ts` games yield every few hundred moves and once a game, as `vitest.config.ts` asks.
No assertion changed.

## D853 — Thassa's Oracle

Most-played order: Thassa's Oracle (rank 464).

**Engine.** `CardsDecisionSpec.lookCount`: a `library-top` question whose number is counted live
for the seat asked, in place of the printed `look`. It is used everywhere `look` was read: the
candidates, the cards shown, and the put-back.

to one of them on top of your library and the rest on the bottom of your library in a random

This is one question: up to one card is kept on top, and the rest go to the bottom at random.
Then the win is asked of X counted again and of the library as it then is.

- the card reads;
- devotion 2 over a two-card library wins;
- devotion 2 over a three-card library does not win;
- the top two are asked, the picked one stays on top, and the other goes to the bottom.

## D865 — Double and triple damage: Fiery Emancipation, City on Fire, Twinflame Tyrant

Most-played order: Fiery Emancipation (rank 873), City on Fire (924), Twinflame Tyrant (757).

**Engine.** `CardScript.damageMultiplier` (`factor`, and `opponents` for Twinflame's "to an
opponent or a permanent an opponent controls"). It is asked by `dealDamage` of the source
controller's permanents, live, as the damage is about to be dealt and before any prevention. Two
of them multiply together. A redirect is a new event and is not multiplied again.

- the cards read;

- their Shock at us is not tripled by our City;

- combat damage too: an unblocked 2/2 under the City deals 6.

controller when none is passed. No test path reaches it, because combat and spells both pass a

## D1228 — "That ability triggers an additional time", and Elesh Norn

Panharmonicon ("If an artifact or creature entering causes a triggered ability of a permanent you
control to trigger, that ability triggers an additional time."), and the same sentence with "a
permanent entering" (Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines; Virtue of Knowledge; Starfield Vocalist), "a
land entering" (Ancient Greenwarden), "a creature dying" (Teysa Karlov, Drivnod), "a creature
attacking" (Isshin, Two Heavens as One) and "a creature you control attacking" (Wulfgar of Icewind
Dale). A new script field, `extraTriggers`. When a permanent's printed trigger fires for one of
those events, its controller's live doublers whose event and kinds fit each fire it once more: two
Panharmonicons, three times. A batch of arrivals or deaths counts when any of it fits. A dying
creature's own death trigger is a permanent's (it was one as it triggered), so Teysa doubles it.

And Elesh Norn's second line, "Permanents entering don't cause abilities of permanents your
opponents control to trigger": D1227's silence for the watchers of its controller's opponents
only (`opponentsEntriesDontTrigger`).

Not doubled: a modal trigger, whose mode question would be asked over the first copy's; a granted
trigger (only printed ones are fired again); an emblem's. A trigger that "triggers only once each
turn" triggers once. Not read: the other doubling sentences ("If a triggered ability of a Ninja you
control triggers", Veyran's casting, Krang's drawing), each its own event.

Read whole now (8): Ancient Greenwarden, Drivnod, Carnage Dominus, Elesh Norn, Mother of Machines,
Isshin, Two Heavens as One, Panharmonicon, Starfield Vocalist, Teysa Karlov, Virtue of Knowledge,
Wulfgar of Icewind Dale.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- An entry: twice with one doubler, three times with two, and an opponent's doubler does nothing
  for you.
- A death: twice under the dying doubler, once under the entering one.
- An attack: twice.
- Elesh Norn: an entry fires nothing for her controller's opponent, and still does for her
  controller.
- A land: the land doubler doubles landfall; the artifact-or-creature one does not.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- No extra trigger ever.
- The kinds ignored.
- Every player's doublers counted, not the controller's.
- Norn's silence dropped.
- Norn silencing her controller instead of the opponents.

The three new fields are listed among the mechanics the compiler reads that no built-in deck plays,
with the runtime block above as their evidence.

Coverage: 16,867 of 31,900 cards (+78 over D1227's 16,789), 39,413 of 59,888 lines (+97).

## D1229 — Grand Arbiter Augustin IV's three cost lines, and Reality Shift

Grand Arbiter Augustin IV prints three cost changes on three lines ("White spells you cast cost
{1} less to cast", "Blue spells …", "Spells your opponents cast cost {1} more to cast"). Each line
read, and the second and third were refused as a conflict with the first, because `costModifiers`
is a list but was not one of the fields the compiler lets several lines add to. It is now. A tally
of every refused merge across the legal pool found this the only card it held up.

And "Target player manifests the top card of their library", which is how Reality Shift's "Exile
target creature. Its controller manifests the top card of their library." reads once the referent
has been swapped for a target (D537): the exiled creature's controller gets the face-down 2/2.

Read whole now (2): Grand Arbiter Augustin IV, Reality Shift.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both test cards read whole.
- All three lines apply: white and blue spells cost one less for the Arbiter's controller, a red
  one does not, and every spell costs one more for the opponent.
- Reality Shift: the creature is exiled, and its controller (not the caster) has a face-down
  permanent.

Faults injected by hand: 2, both caught.
- `costModifiers` not accumulated.
- The manifest made for the caster.

## D1230 — "Players can't untap more than one land during their untap steps"

Winter Orb ("As long as Winter Orb is untapped, players can't untap more than one land during their
untap steps"), Static Orb ("… two permanents"), Damping Field and Imi Statue ("… one artifact"),
Smoke and Stoic Angel ("… one creature"), Winter Moon ("… one nonbasic land"), and Mungha Wurm's
"You can't untap more than one land during your untap step". A new script field, `untapLimit`,
read live off every permanent as each untap step begins; "as long as ~ is untapped" holds only if
the Orb is untapped at that moment. For each limit that reaches the active player, their tapped
permanents of the kind beyond the first N stay tapped.

**The engine chooses which permanents untap, for every player**: mana sources first, then the
highest mana value, then board order. The rules give that choice to the player (CR 502.3); asking
a person is not built yet, and this is the reading that costs a player least in nearly every game.

Read whole now (8): Damping Field, Imi Statue, Mungha Wurm, Smoke, Static Orb, Stoic Angel, Winter
Moon, Winter Orb.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- Without a limit, all three lands untap.
- An opponent's untapped Orb: one land untaps, and the creature still does.
- A tapped Orb limits nothing.
- "Two permanents": two of the four, lands first.
- "You can't": its controller is limited, its opponent is not.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- The limit never applied.
- "As long as ~ is untapped" ignored.
- "You" read as every player.
- Mana sources chosen last.
- One permanent too many untapped.

The new field is listed among the mechanics the compiler reads that no built-in deck plays, with the
runtime block above as its evidence.

Most-played order: Peer into the Abyss (rank 1307).

The hit trigger rewrites "that player" to "defending player", and the rewritten line is refused
before the trigger reader is reached. The refusal was not found within the time this increment
allowed.

## D891 — An opponent's extra draws are ours: Notion Thief

Most-played order: Notion Thief (rank 1231).

**Engine.** `CardScript.stealsExtraDraws`, asked by `draw` (CR 614.1a). Each card an opponent of
the Thief's controller would draw, except the first in their own draw step, is skipped, and the
Thief's controller draws one instead. "The first in their draw step" is the first card they
actually draw this turn while it is their draw step; replaced draws were not theirs and do not
count. The stolen card is drawn as it is and is not offered to another Thief. Two Thieves on
opposite sides would otherwise pass one card back and forth without end, so this is a deliberate
simplification.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- the card reads;
- under our Thief, their draw-step card is theirs, and their Divination draws two cards for us;
- our own draws are untouched by our Thief.

Faults injected by script: 2 of 2 real faults caught. A third, letting the Thief take its own
controller's draws, gives the same cards to the same player, so it is equivalent and not counted.

  permanent (the Mountain that entered), or less the source when there is no event. A subtype in
  the plural ("Mountains", "Plains", "Goblins") is counted by its singular.
- "You may have ~ deal 3 damage" already read, so a causative reader written for it was dead code
  and was removed when its fault went uncaught.

**Found on the way.** Before this, "you control N or more other Mountains" read as a count of
nothing, so it was always false. It was silent, because the line was marked read.

**Tests.** The card reads. With five other Mountains the sixth deals 3, and with four it does
nothing. Faults injected by script: 2 of 2 caught.

## D1232 — Stranglehold, Mindlock Orb and Aven Mindcensor

"Your opponents can't search libraries." (Stranglehold), "Players can't search libraries." (Mindlock
Orb), and "If an opponent would search a library, that player searches the top four cards of that
library instead." (Aven Mindcensor). A new script field, `searchLimit`, asked as a library search
finds its candidates: nothing under a Stranglehold or an Orb, or only the cards among the top N of
their library under a Mindcensor (the smallest N if there are several). The rest of the effect still
happens, so a fetch land is still sacrificed and the library still shuffled, which is the ruling. A
search stopped this way raises no "searches" event (the other session's D863), since nothing was
searched.

And Stranglehold's second line, "If an opponent would begin an extra turn, that player skips that
turn instead." (`opponentsSkipExtraTurns`): the extra turn is dropped where the next turn is chosen.

Read whole now (3): Aven Mindcensor, Mindlock Orb, Stranglehold.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- An opponent's Stranglehold: the search finds nothing; with none, or with the searcher's own,
  it finds the land.
- Aven Mindcensor: a land fourth from the top is found, one fifth is not.
- An opponent's extra turn is skipped under Stranglehold, and taken without it.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- No limit ever.
- "Your opponents" read as every player.
- The top five searched instead of four.
- The extra turn taken anyway.

Not covered by a test: a player's own Stranglehold leaving their own extra turn alone.

The two new fields are listed among the mechanics the compiler reads that no built-in deck plays,
with the runtime block above as their evidence.

## D1236 — Ragavan: the top card of that player's library, to cast this turn

"Whenever Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer deals combat damage to a player, create a Treasure token and
exile the top card of that player's library. Until end of turn, you may cast that card." Three
pieces the impulse draw (D583) did not have:
- **Another player's library.** `exileTopToPlay` takes whose library, and the card goes to its
  owner's exile, as every exiled card does.
- **Offered from any exile zone.** The impulse offers read only the player's own exile, so a card
  taken from an opponent was never offered. They now read every exile zone for cards this player
  has been given.
- **"Cast", not "play".** `playFromExile.castOnly`: a land taken this way is never a land drop.

The trigger's whole sentence is read for a combat-damage trigger, with the player it hit from the
event; "you may play that card" is the same without the land restriction.

Read whole now (1): Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test card reads whole.
- It connects: a Treasure, and the defender's top card in the defender's exile, offered to and cast
  by the attacker in the second main phase.
- A land taken this way is offered as nothing.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The attacker's own library taken from.
- Only the player's own exile offered.
- The land offered as a land drop.

## D1237 — "As ~ enters, choose a card name", and Pithing Needle

Pithing Needle ("As Pithing Needle enters, choose a card name. Activated abilities of sources with
the chosen name can't be activated unless they're mana abilities.") and Phyrexian Revoker ("…
choose a nonland card name. … can't be activated."). A third kind of entry choice beside a creature
type and a colour (D641): the answer is kept on the permanent (`chosen.name`), and a static whose
scope is `CHOSEN_NAME` is filled in with it as it is installed, over every permanent with that name
(a new `named` scope; a face-down permanent has no name).

**Which names are offered** is the decision worth recording. The game state holds every card in
every deck, and offering all of them would tell a player what an opponent's library contains. So
the question offers the cards anybody can see: on the battlefield face up, in a graveyard, face up
in exile, on the stack. A name nobody has seen yet cannot be chosen, which is this reading's one
limit. The bot names the opponents' permanent with an activated ability and the highest mana value.

Also: only permanents are stopped, so a named card's ability from another zone (cycling from a
hand, say) is not; the abilities a Needle usually meets are on the battlefield.

Read whole now (2): Phyrexian Revoker, Pithing Needle. Voidstone Gargoyle reads this line and waits
on "Spells with the chosen name can't be cast"; Sorcerous Spyglass waits on its look at a hand.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- The question offers the cards on the table, and the answer is kept on the Needle.
- The named card's ability is refused; a named mana rock still taps; an unnamed card is untouched.
- Revoker's version stops the named rock's mana, and offers no land name.
- The bot names the opponent's permanent with an ability and the highest mana value.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- The named scope matching nothing.
- Every reading stopping mana abilities too.
- Land names offered for "a nonland card name".
- The bot naming the first card in the list.
- The answer not kept.

Coverage: 16,951 of 31,900 cards (+2 over D1236's 16,949), 39,535 of 59,888 lines (+19).

**Tests.** The card reads. A Bear entering gains 1, and its death gains another 1. Faults injected
by script: 2 of 2 caught.

## D1239 — "Exile it instead", from any permanent, of a graveyard or a death

Rest in Peace, Leyline of the Void and the "a creature an opponent controls would die" family, read
off the card rather than written out by hand. The replacement pass these need has existed since D576
(`replaceZoneChange`); what was missing was the reader. Two lines:
- "If a card [or token] would be put into (a | your | an opponent's) graveyard from anywhere, exile
  it instead", and "an instant or sorcery card" (Dryad Militant). Whose graveyard is the card's
  owner's, which is where a card goes (CR 404.1).
- "If a [nontoken] creature an opponent controls would die, exile it instead", and "a Warlock you
  control" (Lorcan). Who controlled it is read off the snapshot `relocate` takes as it leaves the
  battlefield, not off the graveyard it reached.

One engine fix with it. A token has ceased to exist by the time a replacement is asked, and the token
branch of the pass never asked the rule's own test: it treated every "or token" rule as
unconditional, which was true of Rest in Peace and nothing else. With "your graveyard" (Necrodominance,
Festival of Embers, Emet-Selch) that would have exiled an opponent's tokens as well, so their deaths
would never have triggered anything. The test is now asked of the token's last state.

Read whole now (5): Rest in Peace, Leyline of the Void, Dryad Militant, Stone of Erech, Misery's
Shadow. The line is read on ten more that each have another line left (Vren, Gisa, Liesa, Garruk,
Veiled Butcher, Lorcan, Yawgmoth's Agenda, Necrodominance, Festival of Embers, Emet-Selch, Forbidden
Crypt).

Not read, and why: lines that exile with a counter (Dauthi Voidwalker, Draugr Necromancer, Rayami),
because the counter is what a later ability reads; "When you do, create …" after the exile (Head of
the Hunt, Nemata), a reflexive trigger; Abandoned Sarcophagus's "and it wasn't cycled"; and the
spells' "this turn" form (Gaea's Will, Yawgmoth's Will).

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- An opponent's graveyard: their creature is exiled and mine is not.
- A creature an opponent controls: exiled, and a "whenever a creature dies" watcher gains nothing;
  my own creature dies and the watcher gains 1.
- A Warlock you control: my Warlock is exiled, my Bear and their Warlock are not.
- "A card or token … your graveyard": my token does not die, theirs still does.
- An instant or sorcery card: a discarded Bolt is exiled and a discarded Bear is not.

Faults injected by hand: 6, all caught.
- The token branch asks no test (the old behaviour).
- "An opponent's" not checked.
- "You control" read as "an opponent controls".
- "Instant or sorcery" not checked.
- The creature type not checked.
- "Your" not checked.

Not covered by a test: a stolen creature (the snapshot's controller rather than the owner).

Coverage: 16,969 of 31,900 cards (+15 over D1238's 16,954), 39,564 of 59,888 lines (+26).

## D1240 — "Look at an opponent's hand, then choose any card name": Sorcerous Spyglass

D1237's card-name choice, with a look first. The name question for a Spyglass also offers the names
of the cards in the hand looked at, and the bot weighs those cards alongside the opponent's
permanents when it picks the dearest one with an activated ability. So a Spyglass can name what is
coming as well as what is already on the table. Pithing Needle's question is unchanged.

The hand looked at is the next opponent's in turn order, which is the only opponent in a two-player
game. In a pod the printed card lets its controller pick the opponent; this does not ask. "Any card
name" is still the names a player could know (D1237), now with that hand added.

A correction to D1239's coverage line: its +15 was counted from D1238's figure, which was measured
before the other session's D3005–D3011 were merged in. Five of the fifteen are D1239's own (the
five it lists).

Read whole now (1): Sorcerous Spyglass.

- The test card reads whole.
- The Spyglass question offers a card in the opponent's hand; a Needle's question does not.
- The bot names the dearest card with an ability in that hand for a Spyglass, and the dearest one on
  the battlefield for a Needle.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.

## D3012 — "Players can't gain life" and "Damage can't be prevented" as statics

Erebos, God of the Dead, Leyline of Punishment, Rampaging Ferocidon, Sunspine Lynx, Havoc Festival,
Tibalt, Rakish Instigator and Giant Cindermaw.

**Readers.** "Players can't gain life." and "Your opponents can't gain life." are the D1127
"gains no life instead" row (`lifeGainReplacement`, becomes `none`), with whose as printed. The
rules call it a prohibition rather than a replacement (CR 119.7), but at the table they are the same:
a gain that cannot happen gains nothing and triggers nothing, and the row already wins over every
other life-gain replacement. "Damage can't be prevented." is a new `CardScript.damageUnpreventable`,
which `dealDamage` checks across every seat's battlefield next to Skullcrack's turn flag. So every
prevention is skipped, protection's included.

**Tests.** A "each player gains 3 life" spell: both gain with nothing out, neither gains with
"players" on either side, and only the controller gains with "your opponents". A red sweep leaves a
protection-from-red Knight alive, and kills it while either player has the Leyline out. Faults
injected by script: 4 of 4 caught.

**Not counted.** An "enters or attacks" joiner was written and then removed. Every such line it
read already read through the existing self-trigger path, and the non-self ones ("another creature
you control of the chosen type") fail on their halves, so it gained nothing.

## D1241 — Grafdigger's Cage and Containment Priest

Three graveyard-hate statics.
- **"Creature cards in graveyards [and libraries] can't enter the battlefield"**: Grafdigger's Cage,
  Kunoros, Weathered Runestone ("Nonland permanent cards") and Soulless Jailer ("Permanent cards").
  The card stays where it is. A reanimation spell resolves and does nothing, and a search that would
  put a creature onto the battlefield leaves it in the library.
- **"Players can't cast spells from graveyards [or libraries]"**: two new casting limits beside the
  others (D788), checked against the zone the card is cast from, so flashback and escape are refused
  under a Cage and still offered without one.
- **"If a nontoken creature would enter and it wasn't cast, exile it instead"**: Containment Priest.
  A creature card arriving from anywhere but the stack goes to exile instead: reanimated, put in
  from a hand or a library, or coming back from a blink.

Both arrival rules are asked in `relocate`, the one place a card changes zone, so no reanimation path
can miss them. `cardActions` cannot read card scripts without an import cycle, so `automation`
registers the check with `setArrivalBan`. Only on an automated table; a tabletop move means what the
player said. Each refusal or redirect goes into the replacement log, so the player sees why the card
did not arrive.

Read whole now (4): Grafdigger's Cage, Containment Priest, Kunoros, Hound of Athreos, Weathered
Runestone. Soulless Jailer's first two lines read; its "noncreature spells from graveyards or exile"
does not yet.

Not done: printed types decide the kind, so a manifested noncreature card is not seen as a creature
by the Priest. Worms of the Earth's "Lands can't enter the battlefield" and Ashes of the Abhorrent's
"or activate abilities of cards in graveyards" are not read.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- Under the Cage, a creature card stays in a graveyard and in a library, and an artifact card does
  not; without it the creature enters.
- "Permanent cards in graveyards" stops an artifact, and not a library.
- Flashback is refused under the Cage and allowed without it.
- Under the Priest, a creature put in from a graveyard is exiled, and one that was cast enters.

Faults injected by hand: 6, all caught.
- The Cage never stops anything.
- "And libraries" dropped.
- Every ban read as creatures only.
- The cast check not told the zone.
- The Priest exiling a creature that was cast.
- A graveyard-only ban read as libraries too.

Coverage: 16,983 of 31,900 cards (+13 over D1240's 16,970), 39,595 of 59,888 lines (+29).

**Damn (rank 349).** "Destroy target creature. A creature destroyed this way can't be regenerated."

the counted group in the clausesOf chain, so both sentences read with the readers they already had.
The draw moves no counters, so it is the same set. Tests: one Bear with a counter and one without;
the Call draws one, and a wipe after it kills only the unmarked Bear. Faults injected by script:

## D1242 — "Exile it instead", and something done as well: Kalitas and kin

D1239's "a creature an opponent controls would die" line, with a second half the permanent's
controller does as the creature is exiled:
- "instead exile that card and create a 2/2 black Zombie creature token" (Kalitas);
- "instead exile it and you gain 2 life" (The Darkness Crystal);
- "exile it instead. When you do, create a 2/2 green Wolf creature token" (Head of the Hunt, and
  Nemata's Saproling).

The second half is read as any other effect is. It is accepted only when it aims at nothing and asks
nothing: "When you do" is a reflexive trigger (CR 603.12) and strictly goes on the stack, and done at
once it could only be wrong if somebody could have answered it or a choice was owed. Valentin's
"you may pay {2}. If you do" asks one, and is refused.

Not done: a creature token is not exiled by these when the line says "a creature" rather than "a
nontoken creature". It dies as usual and nothing follows. A token has ceased to exist by the time
the replacement is asked, so there is no exile for the second half to follow, and Head of the
Hunt's Wolf for an opponent's token is the case this misses.

Read whole now (2): Head of the Hunt, Nemata, Primeval Warden. The line is read on Kalitas and The
Darkness Crystal, each of which has an activated ability left (Kalitas has a hand-written script).

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- An opponent's creature is exiled and leaves a Zombie; mine dies and leaves nothing.
- "And you gain 2 life" gains 2, and "When you do, create a Wolf" makes one.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The second half never done.
- The "When you do" form not read.
- The second half run on the state before the exile.

## D3014 — "Look at target player's hand.": Gitaxian Probe, Peek

**Reader.** The sentence on its own, ahead of the composer loop with the other hand readers
(`handLookPrefix`). It is a hand question over the target's hand with `max: 0`. The caster is shown
the cards and picks none, and nothing on the board changes.

**Engine.** A question with nothing to pick used to be answered by the engine itself, which would
make the look silent. A target-hand question with `max: 0` is now asked anyway while the hand has
cards, for the same reason D584 asks a dig with nothing to take: what the cards are is the point of
looking. An empty hand is not asked. A bot answers it with no cards, like any other show-only question.

**Tests.** The Probe at an opponent holding two cards asks seat 0, shows exactly those two, and
takes none. The bot answers it the same way, the opponent keeps both cards, and the caster draws one.
At an empty hand nothing is asked. Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught (answered silently,
asked over an empty hand, the caster's own hand shown).

## D1243 — Tergrid: an opponent sacrifices a nontoken permanent or discards a permanent card

Tergrid, God of Fright's front face, in three pieces:
- **"A permanent card"** in a discard trigger: any of the permanent types, beside D820's card types.
- **One line, two events**: "Whenever an opponent sacrifices a nontoken permanent or discards a
  permanent card" is one trigger that fires on either.
- **"Put that card from a graveyard onto the battlefield under your control"**, in either word
  order: the card the event was about, taken from whichever graveyard it reached, only while it is
  still there (CR 400.7).

One engine fix with it. A sacrifice trigger never carried the sacrificed permanent onto the stack as
the ability's subject, so no effect of one could name "that card". Discards had carried theirs since
D719; sacrifices now do too. The rest of the sacrifice triggers in the pool are unchanged (204
sacrifice tests).

Read whole now: Tergrid's front face. The card is not whole yet, because its back face, Tergrid's
Lantern, has "loses 3 life unless they sacrifice a nonland permanent or discard a card", a three-way
punisher. That is D1244.

- The test card reads whole.
- An opponent's sacrificed creature comes over on a yes, and stays in their graveyard on a no.
- A discarded permanent card comes over; a discarded instant does not trigger.
- My own sacrifice does not trigger it.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The sacrifice's subject not carried.
- The discard's permanent filter dropped.
- "An opponent" read as anyone.
- The card put onto the battlefield under its owner's control.

Not covered by a test: "nontoken" (a token sacrificed has ceased to exist, so there is nothing to
take either way).

permanent, or to discard a card. Each way is offered only when they can take it, and the card for the
chosen way is asked from the battlefield or from the hand. "A nonland permanent" joins the kinds a
punisher's sacrifice may be. The bot, as the player choosing, loses the life while it has more than

## D1245 — Orcish Bowmasters

"Whenever an opponent draws a card except the first one they draw in each of their draw steps": the
opponent-draw trigger with a flag, `exceptDrawStepFirst`. The engine answers it as it raises each
draw event. A draw counts as the draw step's own card when it is the seat's first card this turn,
drawn in its own draw step. That is the reading Notion Thief's exemption uses (D891), so the two
cards agree on which draw is exempt. The rest of the card (the enter trigger, 1 damage to any target,
amass Orcs 1) was already read, and "When ~ enters and whenever …" already made two triggers of it
(D882).

Not exact: a card drawn earlier in the same turn (in the upkeep, say) makes the draw step's card the
second of the turn. Bowmasters then fires on it, where the printed card would not.

Read whole now (1): Orcish Bowmasters.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The test card reads whole.
- An opponent's draw on my turn triggers it.
- The first card of their own draw step does not; a second card in that step does.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The exception never checked.
- Every draw in their draw step treated as exempt.
- The first draw of the turn treated as exempt in any step.

Coverage: 17,004 of 31,900 cards (+3 over D1244's 17,001), 39,626 of 59,888 lines (+3).

## D1246 — Land types set: Blood Moon, Spreading Seas, Song of the Dryads

A continuous effect can now set a permanent's land types (CR 305.7), `ContinuousEffect.setLandTypes`.
Every land type it had (basic or not, from a closed list of the land types in CR 205.3i) is
replaced, in effect order like creature types. The rule also takes away the land's rules-text
abilities, so the readers set `losesAllAbilities` beside it. The new type's own mana ability still
works: `landTypesSet` lets the mana-source walk keep a land that lost its abilities when its land
types were set, and offer only the mana its types give.

Readers:
- "Nonbasic lands are Mountains" (Blood Moon, Magus of the Moon), on a new static scope,
  `nonbasic-lands`.
- "Enchanted land is an Island / a Swamp / …" (Spreading Seas, Evil Presence, Sea's Claim).
- "Enchanted permanent is a colorless Forest land" (Song of the Dryads): its other card types and
  creature types gone, its colour gone, a Forest and nothing else.

Two fixes found on the way:
- **The mana pips never counted a type an effect added.** `potentialMana` walks the board on its own
  and had never included the mana a basic land type gives a land that is the type only because an
  effect says so. `manaSources` has done this since D699. A Forest under Urborg tapped for black when
  paying, but lit no black pip. Both walks now agree.
- **Activation never refused a lost ability.** The play list has never offered an ability of a
  permanent that has lost them all, but the activate action itself did not refuse one. A Frogged
  creature's printed ability could be activated by an action the table did not offer. A grant that
  landed after the loss is still allowed.

Not done: Imprisoned in the Moon ("a colorless land with '{T}: Add {C}'") grants a quoted ability
after the loss, and is left for the attachment grant path. A land whose types were set taps for its
new colour through the payer, and its printed mana ability is refused if pressed by hand, which is
right. A UI that taps lands by printed ability index will not see the new colour as a button.

Read whole now, by the probe: Blood Moon, Magus of the Moon, Spreading Seas, Evil Presence, Sea's
Claim, Song of the Dryads.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The test cards read whole.
- Under the Moon, a nonbasic land taps for red and nothing else, both in the pips and in the
  auto-payer. Its other ability is refused, and a basic Swamp is untouched.
- A Forest Island under the Moon is only a Mountain.
- The enchanted land is an Island: blue, not green.
- The enchanted creature is a colorless Forest land with no abilities, and taps for green.

Faults injected by hand: 6, all caught (two after tests were added for them).
- The old land types kept.
- The auto-payer reading the printed abilities.
- The pips skipping a retyped land.
- Basic lands caught by the Moon.
- The lost ability's activation allowed.
- Song's colour left on.

Coverage: 17,013 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1245's 17,004), 39,636 of 59,888 lines (+10).

## D1247 — Demonic Consultation

"Choose a card name. Exile the top six cards of your library, then reveal cards from the top of
your library until you reveal a card with the chosen name. Put that card into your hand and exile all
other cards revealed this way." The name is asked as the spell resolves, on D1237's card-name
question with a third aim, `own-library`. A player knows their own deck, so the options are the names
anyone can see plus every name in the caster's library. The bot names the dearest nonland card left
in its library. Nobody knows which cards are in the top six.

A name that is not found (or is only in the top six) exiles the whole library. That is how the card
is played with Thassa's Oracle; the caster loses only when they next draw (CR 704.5b).

Read whole now (1): Demonic Consultation.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The test card reads whole.
- The named card below the top six comes to hand. The six and the card revealed before it are
  exiled, and the rest of the library stays.
- A name in the top six (or nowhere) exiles the whole library.
- The bot names the dearest nonland card left in its library.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The caster's library missing from the options.
- The top six not exiled.
- The named card exiled instead of put into the hand.
- The bot's library choice skipped.

Coverage: 17,015 of 31,900 cards (+2 over D1246's 17,013), 39,638 of 59,888 lines (+2).

shares one of those types" (Legerdemain) are not read. Gilded Drake's "If you don't or can't make an

nothing reads. It reads now, so they use Mindslaver's "You control target player during that
player's next turn." instead. The property they pin is unchanged.

"When ~ enters, exchange control of ~ and up to one target creature an opponent controls. If you
don't or can't make an exchange, sacrifice ~. This ability still resolves if its target becomes

can happen when the creature it was aimed at is removed in response. The effect then checks the
target itself. The older printed wording ("can't be countered except by spells and abilities") is
read too, as asking nothing.

## D3015 — "{B}{B}: Attach ~ to target creature you control": Cranial Plating, Felidar Umbra

**Reader.** The permanent moved onto a creature you control as an ability of its own, at whatever
speed it is printed with (Cranial Plating's is instant speed, where equip is sorcery speed). An
Equipment moves the way equip moves it, with its own `equipBonus`. An Aura is moved with the new
`moveAura` (effects.ts). An Aura's grant is installed as it resolves, scoped to the creature it
enchanted, so every effect from that Aura scoped to the old host is re-pointed at the new one, its
conditional parts with it. Anything that is neither does nothing.

**Tests.** An Equipment with "+2/+0" goes onto one Bear and then the other, and the bonus moves
with it. An Aura with "+2/+2" is cast onto one Bear and moved to the other by its ability, and the
bonus follows. Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught (the Aura moved without its grant, the
Equipment moved without its bonus, the Aura treated as nothing).

## D1251 — A printed alternative of mana or life: Snuff Out, the Bringers

"You may pay X rather than pay this spell's mana cost", where X is mana or life, with "If you control
a <basic land type>," in front where printed. `CardScript.altCost` holds it. It is offered as an
alternative-cost cast beside the pitch (D691) and the others, while the caster controls the land type
named and has the life to pay without losing. It is checked again as the cast is made, and validated

returned is the trick these cards are played for. It is offered only while there are enough of

player would choose almost always, and a choice can be added where it matters.

## D3016 — "~ gets +2/+2 for each Aura attached to it": Kor Spiritdancer, Graceblade Artisan, Rabid Wombat

**Reader.** A new static count kind, `attached-to-self`, which counts the permanents on any
battlefield whose `attachedTo` is the source and whose printed type line has the subtype: "Aura",
"Equipment", or "Aura and Equipment". It reads printed type lines, for the reason the other static
counts do: it never re-enters `characteristicsOf`.

"It" is the creature the line is about. On a creature that is the source; on an Aura or Equipment
(Golem-Skin Gauntlets, Auramancer's Guise, Thran Power Suit: "Equipped creature gets +1/+0 for each
Equipment attached to it") it is the host the source is attached to. The first card-by-card diff
caught this: the first version counted on the Equipment, which made the Gauntlets a wrong card.

**Tests.** A 0/2 with the line: an Equipment on it adds only its own +1/+0, an Aura on a different
creature adds nothing, and one and then two Auras of "+1/+1" on it make it 4/5 and then 7/8. A
Gauntlets-shaped Equipment on a Bear gives +1/+0, and +2/+0 once a second Equipment joins it.
Faults injected by script: 3 of 3 caught. A fault that fixed the count at one went uncaught
until the test put a second Aura on it.

## D1266 — A flavour word in front of an activated ability comes off

"Magical Tinkering — {W}, {T}, Sacrifice an artifact: Search your library …" (Oswald Fiddlebender).
D623 took an ability word off an activated ability only when what was left carried an "Activate
only if" sentence, so a label was never the one thing restricting it. That requirement is dropped:
an ability word has no rules meaning (CR 207.2c), nor has a flavour word (CR 207.2d), so the ability
is exactly what follows the dash. A keyword in the same position *is* a restriction ("Max speed —",
"Exhaust —", "Boast —", "Channel —", "Cycling—"), and those were never labels, by
`withoutAbilityWord`'s list; they stay as they were.

Measured before the change: of the labelled activated lines in the legal corpus whose remainder
reads on its own, 50 carry a true ability or flavour word (Imprint, Domain, Ferocious, and one-card
flavour words from the Universes Beyond and Alchemy sets) and 15 a keyword. No legal card prints a
condition ability word (Threshold, Metalcraft, Hellbent …) in front of an activated ability without
restating the condition. Two of the newly read lines cost "Discard this card", which the engine
already activates from the hand (`discardSelf`).

The D623 pin that kept a made-up "Threshold — {1}: You gain 4 life." unread now pins it read as
printed, with no activation condition.

- A flavour-labelled ability reads whole; "Max speed —" in the same place stays unread.
- The labelled ability activates and does what follows the dash; the button keeps the label.

Faults injected by hand: 2, all caught.
- The "Activate only if" requirement restored.

(`DecisionSpecOf`, D1195) with X counted from the board at that moment — the most cards that may be
taken, or the highest mana value one may have. The prompt shows the X it was asked with. With no
context to count from, X is 0.

## D1269 — Five more counts: life total, permanent cards in a graveyard, different powers, players with more lands, a commander's mana value

`boardCount` (and through it every "where X is …" reader) takes five more measures, each counted
from the board as the effect runs (`moreMeasures`):
- "your life total" (Storm Herd, Ajani, Caller of the Pride, Death's Shadow);
- "the number of permanent cards in your graveyard", by the printed type line;
- "the number of different powers among creatures you control" (Celebrate the Harvest);

  Surveyor's Scope), opponents only, eliminated seats not counted;

  with none there.

`countTailOf`'s list of announced measures gains the two that do not begin "the number of".

- A commander's mana value: a 5 and a 2 as commanders give 5, none gives 0.

- Different powers counted with duplicates.
