## D1270 — Power/toughness counters other than +1/+1 and -1/-1

"+2/+2", "+1/+2", "+1/+0", "-0/-1", "-0/-2" (CR 122.1a): Baron Sengir, the Chimeras, Fungus
Elemental, Armor Thrull, Shield Sphere, Spirit Shackle and their kin. `characteristicsOf` now sums
every power/toughness counter in layer 7c, each adding what its name says; only +1/+1 and -1/-1
cancel as a state-based action (CR 704.5q), as before. The counter readers (on ~, on a target, on
each of a set, on the enchanted or equipped creature, a counted number) take any such counter
(`PT_COUNTER`) and keep the kind as printed. Before this, a "+" counter was normalised to "+1/+1"
wherever it was read. A counter that lowers power and toughness on balance is aimed at somebody
else's creature, as a -1/-1 counter is (`ptCounterHelps`).

**A fix on the way.** `addCounters` refuses to put a +1/+1 or -1/-1 counter on a card that has left
the battlefield (D566, CR 400.7). That guard now covers every power/toughness counter. Without it a
+2/+2 counter would have stayed on a graveyard card and come back with it.

**Pins changed.**
- D453 refused "put a +2/+2 counter on each creature you control" because nothing sized the
  counter. It now reads.
- D475's table kept "Whenever a creature you control dies, put a -1/-1 counter on that creature"
  unread. It reads now, as the +1/+1 and stun versions of the same sentence already did: "that
  creature" is the one that died, and the counter is not placed on the card in the graveyard. The
  row became an engine test here.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- Three forms read; the +2/+2 counter is aimed as a gift and the -0/-1 counter is not.
- A +2/+2 counter makes a 2/2 a 4/4, kept under its printed name.
- A -0/-1 counter takes toughness only.
- A +1/+2 counter on itself; beside it a +1/+1 and a -1/-1 cancel and a +2/+2 does not.
- No power/toughness counter lands on a card in a graveyard, and the dies sentence reads.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- Characteristics summing only +1/+1 and -1/-1.
- Every power/toughness counter aimed as a gift.
- "+2/+2" normalised to "+1/+1" again.
- The graveyard guard back to +1/+1 and -1/-1 only.

Coverage: 17,154 of 31,900 cards (+12 over D1269's 17,142), 39,849 of 59,888 lines (+16).

## D1271 — "That many" counters: a batch of discards, any counter kind, a target

- **A batch of discards carries its count.** "Whenever you discard one or more cards, put that many
  +1/+1 counters on this creature" (Marauding Mako, Scrounging Skyray). The batch event already
  knew how many cards (D993). It now hands that number to the trigger as the event's amount, and
  "that many" after it is marked as D903 marks it after damage.
- **Any counter kind on the card itself**: "that many charge counters on ~" (Angelheart Vial),
  "… incubation counters on it" (Drake Hatcher), and the power/toughness counters D1270 sizes. A
  counter the rules give a meaning of their own (`RULES_COUNTERS`: lore, time, loyalty …) is
  refused, as it is with a printed number.
- **On a target**: "put that many +1/+1 counters on target Halfling or Treefolk" (Treebeard,
  Gracious Host), aimed as a gift when the counter helps.

**A fix on the way.** A "you may" around a "that many" clause asked the player in the reader's own
mark for "that many" (an unprintable character) instead of the printed words. The question is now
put as printed: "Put that many charge counters on Angelheart Vial?".

Read whole now: Marauding Mako, Scrounging Skyray, Drake Hatcher, Angelheart Vial, Treebeard,
Gracious Host. Voracious Brood's "one or more creature cards are put into your graveyard from
anywhere" is an event not read yet.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Three forms read; "that many lore counters" stays unread.
- Two cards discarded at once give two +1/+1 counters.
- Three life gained gives three charge counters (after a "may" asked in the printed words) and three
  +1/+1 counters on the creature targeted.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- A discard batch's amount always 1.
- A rules counter let through.
- One counter on the target instead of that many.
- The prompt left with the mark in it.

Coverage: 17,162 of 31,900 cards (+8 over D1270's 17,154), 39,859 of 59,888 lines (+10).

## D1272 — Two counters in one sentence

"Put a +1/+1 counter on that creature and a +1/+1 counter on Juniper Order Ranger." `clausesOf`
does not split on "and" (D387). `conjoinedEffect`, tried only when nothing reads the whole clause,
splits it. The second half ("a +1/+1 counter on ~") had no verb and read as nothing. A later part
that is only the next counter and where it goes now takes "put" back, as the next token takes
"create" back (D810). Each half is then read on its own, and the composition is all or nothing.

- Brokers Ascendancy and Ajani, the Greathearted: loyalty counters on each planeswalker.
- Sagu Pummeler: two counter kinds before one "on".

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both test forms read.
- A creature entering gets a counter, and so does the Ranger.
- One counter on itself and one on the target.
- Two targets in one sentence get three counters each, not six on one (Evolutionary Escalation).

Faults injected by hand: 2, all caught.
- The second half's destination rewritten to "it".
- The verb restored only from the third part on.

Coverage: 17,170 of 31,900 cards (+8 over D1271's 17,162), 39,868 of 59,888 lines (+9).

## D1274 — "… if it's <colour>": the colour asked as it resolves

Pyroblast's and Hydroblast's "Counter target spell if it's blue" / "Destroy target permanent if it's
red", Burnout's "Counter target instant spell if it's blue", and the Ring cycle's "put a +1/+1
counter on equipped creature if it's green". Unlike Red Elemental Blast's "target blue spell", the
target may be anything. The colour is asked as the effect resolves, of what "it" is then
(CR 608.2b), and the effect does nothing if it is not that colour. "It" is the single target, or,
with no target, the enchanted or equipped creature a counter is put on. The rest of the sentence
is read as it would be without the tail.

Statics that print the same words stay unread: Hobble's "can't block if it's black" and Scion of
Draco's keyword list.

Read whole now: Pyroblast, Hydroblast, Burnout, and the five Rings (Evos Isle, Kalonia, Thune,
Valkas, Xathrid).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both forms read; a two-target sentence with the tail stays unread.
- It destroys a blue permanent, and does nothing to a red one it may still target.
- It counters a blue spell, and not a red one.
- The Ring adds a counter to a green creature wearing it at its controller's upkeep, and not to a
  red one.

Faults injected by hand: 3; 2 caught.
- The colour check dropped: caught.
- "It" read as the Ring itself rather than the creature wearing it: caught.
- A separate "two targets" guard removed: not caught, because a sentence with two targets already
  reads to two targets and is refused by the one-target check. The guard was redundant and is gone.

Coverage: 17,191 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1273's 17,182), 39,901 of 59,888 lines (+15).

## D1275 — The Confluences: choose three, and a mode may come again

"Choose three. You may choose the same mode more than once." (CR 700.2d): Mystic Confluence, Fiery
Confluence and the rest of the cycle, and Planewide Celebration's "Choose four". `ModalDef` gains
`repeats`. `modeCombinations` then counts combinations with repetition, three modes giving ten,
and no longer caps the picks at the number of modes. The engine already resolved chosen modes by
index, each with the next targets in the list, so a mode picked twice resolves twice with its own
target each time. The header reads the bullets as "Choose one" would and sets exactly that many
picks. A mode with a first half before its question is refused, as under any header that picks
more than one (D955).

Read whole now: Mystic Confluence, Fiery Confluence, and other Confluences whose modes read.
Still unread:
- Brokers Confluence: a phasing mode.
- Planewide Celebration: a mode not read yet.
- Doomsday Confluence: "Choose X".
- The Seasons: "{P} worth of modes".

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- It reads as three picks with repeats: ten combinations of three modes, including the same mode
  three times; two modes with three picks give the four combinations.
- The damage mode twice, each with its own target, then the life.
- Three draws, and two picks are refused.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- No repeats in the combinations.
- The picks capped at the number of modes again.

## D1276 — Finality counters

"If a permanent with a finality counter on it would be put into a graveyard from the battlefield,
exile it instead" (CR 122.1i). 44 legal cards print finality counters and nothing applied the rule.
`replaceZoneChange` now asks it first in the to-graveyard pass, the engine's rule rather than any
permanent's. It looks at the permanent as it last was (`vanished`, whose counters survive the move
that wiped the card's), and only at what left the battlefield in this move (`left`). Exiled
instead, the permanent did not die, so death triggers do not see it. That holds for a token too:
its last state is recorded after its move, which is why the check reads `left` and not the
snapshot's zone.

Readers:
- `finality` leaves `RULES_COUNTERS`, so "enters with a finality counter" and "put a finality
  counter on ~" read.
- The targeted counter reader takes finality, aimed at somebody else's creature.
- "Return target … card … to the battlefield with a finality counter on it" reads, and
  "… to the battlefield tapped with …" too.
- The graveyard self-return ("Return this card from your graveyard to the battlefield [tapped] with
  a finality counter on it", Grim Repriser's shape) reads, the counter on the card that came back.

Read whole now: Balustrade Wurm, Resurrected Cultist, Soulcoil Viper, Uchbenbak, Wolfbat, U.S.S.
Reliant, and other finality cards whose other lines read.

**Pins changed.**
- D527 refused "Return target creature card … with a finality counter on it" as a rider the move did
  not carry. It now reads.
- D1078 kept "enters with a finality counter" unread among the rules counters. It now reads.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both forms read.
- A card comes back from the graveyard with a finality counter, and is exiled rather than dying: no
  death trigger.
- A finality counter put on an opponent's creature: exiled when destroyed; one without the counter
  dies and triggers.
- A token with a finality counter does not die: no death trigger. This test found a bug on the way:
  the first check read the snapshot's zone, which for a token is recorded after its move.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The finality check never true.
- The snapshot's zone used again instead of `left`.
- The self-return's counter dropped.

Coverage: 17,205 of 31,900 cards (+8 over D1275's 17,197), 39,936 of 59,888 lines (+11).

## D1278 — "A Blood token": a subtype before "token"

"Sacrifice a Blood token", "… a Map token": the subtype is the noun, and "token" says what kind of
object it is. `permanentDescribed` read "token" first and, with no card type before it, put
"permanent" in its place. The subtype branch then took that "permanent" off instead of the
subtype, and the phrase read as nothing. A capitalised subtype before "token" is now left for the
subtype branch, which reads it as a token with that subtype.

Read whole now: Bloodcrazed Socialite, Wedding Security, and other lines that sacrifice, bounce or
count "a <Subtype> token".

**A process note.** While D1277 was gating I edited `scripts.ts` with this change by mistake. The
edit was reverted within a minute, the finisher stopped, and D1277 gated again from the start. So
D1277's commit is exactly what its gate ran on, and this change went through its own gate here.

**Tests.** 1 engine test:
- It reads, and offers only the two Blood tokens: not a Food, not a creature token.

Faults injected by hand: 1, caught.
- The old order of the two branches restored.

Coverage: 17,215 of 31,900 cards (+2 over D1277's 17,213), 39,948 of 59,888 lines (+2).

## D1280 — "That many" after an attack: mills, and a discard after the draw

Two more readers behind the "that many" mark (D903):
- "target player mills that many cards" (Screaming Swarm), aimed as the trigger goes on the stack;

  amount (D1195), as the hit player's discard already was (D1196).

Together with D1279 these read Varina, Lich Queen's "Whenever you attack with one or more Zombies,
draw that many cards, then discard that many cards".

**An engine bug found on the way.** A trigger whose first half runs before its question
(`beforeDecisions`, D955) ran that half with a context that left out the event's amount. So
Varina's "draw that many" drew nothing, the discard question saw the old hand, and the engine
answered it alone. The context now carries `eventAmount` as the asking context and the effect's
context do.

**A display fix.** A trigger with "that many" showed the reader's internal mark on the stack and
in the log ("draw \u000e many cards … resolves"). Trigger descriptions now show the printed words,
as D1271 did for the yes/no prompt.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both forms read; "that many" with no amount behind it (an activated ability) stays unread.
- Two Zombies attack: the stack shows the printed words. Two cards are drawn, and the discard of two
  is asked from the hand with the new cards in it.
- Three creatures attack: the target player mills three.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The event's amount left out of the first half's context again.
- One card milled instead of that many.
- One card discarded instead of that many.
- The trigger description left with the mark in it.

## D1281 — One context for a resolution's first half

D1280 found that the part of a resolution run before its question (`beforeDecisions`, D955) was
handed a context missing the event's amount. That context was a third hand-written copy of the
field list, beside the asking context and the effect's own, and it had drifted in three more
places:
- a trigger's X (`triggerX`), so "When ~ enters, draw X cards, then discard a card" drew nothing
  and asked the discard from the old hand;
- the spell itself (`resolving`), which "if this spell was cast from a graveyard" reads;
- the face its source showed (`sourceFace`, CR 701.28f).

It now runs with `askingContext`, the context the questions are worked out from. That context
gains `sourceFace`, so it matches the effect's own apart from the answers.

**Tests.** 1 engine test, failing before the change and passing after:
- A creature cast for X = 2 whose enters trigger draws X and then discards one: two cards are drawn
  before the discard is asked.

## D1283 — "~ or another creature you control enters, that creature …"

"Whenever Ambuscade Shaman or another creature you control enters, that creature gets +2/+2 until
end of turn." D964 reads "that creature" as "it", the event's subject, only where every event is
about another creature. The "~ or another" prologue is two events (D483), the card's own and
another's, so the card's own event kept the clause unread. On an arrival or a death, "that
creature" is the one that arrived or died either way. So the card's own event is now allowed on
those two kinds. A block is still excluded, because there "that creature" is the other creature.

Gruul Ragebeast now reads whole, and `compiled-vs-written` compares it for the first time. The
compiled reading is two triggers (D483's shape) where the hand-written card is one trigger on any
creature of yours. The same arrivals fire it and the creature that entered fights. Added to
`DISAGREE` with that reason; the hand-written script is the one played.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- It reads.
- The Shaman entering pumps itself; a Bear entering later pumps the Bear and not the Shaman.
- On a block, "that creature gets -1/-1" shrinks the attacker and not the blocker.

Faults injected by hand: 2; 1 caught.
- The card's own event refused again: caught.
- The card's own event allowed on any kind, blocks included: not caught. On "Whenever ~ blocks a
  creature" the block referent readers (D480's "that creature gets …", then D1282's borrow) take the
  clause before this rewrite and aim it at the other creature, whatever this guard says. On a block,

  event about another" check, which overlapped with it, was removed.

## D1287 — "During each of your turns, you may cast a creature spell from your graveyard"

Karador, Ghost Chieftain, Gisa and Geralf ("a Zombie creature spell"), and Danitha, New Benalia's
Light ("Once during each of your turns … an Aura or Equipment spell") print the same permission:
one spell a turn through each such permanent, of the kind it names, cast for its printed cost at
its normal timing, on its controller's own turn. Nothing offered it before.

- `CardScript.castsFromGraveyard {fits}`, read with the library search's card filter off the
  printed type line. That reader covers "a creature card", "a Zombie creature card", "an Aura or
  Equipment card", "a permanent card with mana value 2 or less".
- `yardPermission(state, seat, id)` names the permanent letting this seat cast this card now: one of
  the seat's own permanents whose kind fits and whose permission is unused this turn, on the seat's
  own turn, the card in the seat's own graveyard.
- `legalActions` lists those cards beside flashback, escape and retrace, and the play carries
  `yardBy`. It takes retrace's path through every other question (no morph, no foretell, no printed
  alternative cost) but not retrace's land card.
- `autoActions` validates `yardBy` against `yardPermission` and records the use in
  `GameState.yardCastsUsed`, by the permanent's id and the turn.
- The bot sends `yardBy` with the cast.

Read whole now: Karador, Ghost Chieftain, Gisa and Geralf, Danitha, New Benalia's Light. Still
unread:
- Lurrus: the Companion keyword.
- Rivaz: its cast trigger.
- Kess: the exile replacement.
- Edgar, Overflow Submatrix: "enters tapped".
- Exploration Broodship, Kotis, Maestros Ascendancy: an extra cost.
- Muldrotha: one of each permanent type.

A simplification, stated: the record is keyed by the permanent's id, so one that leaves and returns
in the same turn is still counted as having used its permission. The rules make it a new object
(CR 400.7) with a fresh one.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- It reads.
- The creature cards in the graveyard are offered, the instant is not. Cast one and it enters; no
  second is offered, and a second sent anyway is refused.
- Not on an opponent's turn, even for an instant permission while holding priority there; offered

## D1288 — Muldrotha, the Gravetide

"During each of your turns, you may play a land and cast a permanent spell of each permanent type
from your graveyard." D1287's permission with one spell a turn per permanent type rather than one in
all: `castsFromGraveyard.slots` lists artifact, battle, creature, enchantment and planeswalker.
`yardSlotFor` names the key a cast would spend: the permanent's own, or `<permanent>#<type>` for the
first of the card's types still unused this turn. The cast records that key. The land half is the
lands-from-graveyard permission Crucible of Worlds gives, which the turn's land drops already limit.

Two simplifications, stated:
- A card of two permanent types (an artifact creature) uses the first of its types still free, in
  the order above. The rules let the player choose as it is cast.
- With extra land drops, Crucible's permission plays more than one land from the graveyard;
  Muldrotha's allows one.

Read whole now: Muldrotha, the Gravetide.

## D1289 — Graveyard permissions with riders: Kess, Edgar, Overflow Submatrix

D1287's permission line now takes the sentence that follows it on three cards:
- Kess, Dissident Mage: "If a spell cast this way would be put into your graveyard, exile it
  instead." `castsFromGraveyard.exileAfter`; the cast marks the stack object `yardExile`, and
  `spellLeavesStack` exiles it as it does a flashback spell.
- Edgar, Master Machinist: "If you cast a spell this way, that artifact enters tapped."
  `castsFromGraveyard.entersTapped`; the stack object's `yardTapped` taps the permanent as it
  arrives.
- Overflow Submatrix: "that artifact creature enters with a finality counter on it."
  `castsFromGraveyard.entersWithFinality`; the stack object's `yardFinality` puts the counter on as
  it arrives, and D1276's finality replacement exiles it when it would die. The reminder text in
  parentheses is dropped before the line is matched.

The marks are on the stack object rather than looked up at resolution, so a permission that leaves
the battlefield while its spell is on the stack still applies its rider, as the rules want (the
rider is part of how the spell was cast).

Read whole now: Kess, Dissident Mage; Edgar, Master Machinist; Overflow Submatrix.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- All three read whole.
- A sorcery cast under Kess is exiled as it resolves; one cast from hand goes to the graveyard.
- An artifact cast under Edgar enters tapped.
- An artifact creature cast under Submatrix enters untapped with a finality counter, and is exiled
  when destroyed.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The exile on leaving the stack dropped.
- The tapped arrival dropped.
- The finality counter dropped.

Drafting note: the first draft read Overflow Submatrix's rider as "enters tapped". The probe showed
the card unread, and its text is a finality counter; the reader and the test were corrected before
the gate.

## D1290 — Imprisoned in the Moon, and the Auras that make a permanent a Clue, a Food or a Treasure

"Enchanted permanent is a colorless land with "{T}: Add {C}" and loses all other card types and
abilities." The same shape with an artifact: In Too Deep (a colorless Clue with "{2}, Sacrifice this
artifact: Draw a card"), Sugar Coat (a colorless Food), Minimus Containment (a Treasure, colour
kept).

The bonus reader takes "is a [colorless] [Clue|Food|Treasure] land|artifact with "<ability>" and
[it] loses all other [card types and] abilities". "Is a land" with no "in addition to its other
types" replaces its card types (CR 205.1a), so every other card type is removed and its creature
types go. A land keeps its land types. The quoted ability is read by the same reader as Chromatic
Lantern's, and granted by the same continuous effect that takes the abilities away.

Three engine changes make that one ability the only one left:
- `grantedAbilitiesOn`: an effect that both removes all abilities and grants one keeps its own
  grant. Before, the loss cleared the list and skipped the effect, so the grant was lost with
  everything else.
- `manaSources` and `potentialMana`: a permanent that has lost all abilities but been handed one
  afterwards is a mana source for that one only. No printed ability, and no basic land type's mana
  either: an imprisoned Forest is still a Forest and taps for {C}, not {G}. Its intrinsic ability is
  an ability, and goes in layer 6 (CR 305.6, 613.1f).
- The activation loop in `legalActions`: the same, for an ability that is not a mana ability
  (In Too Deep's draw).

And the Enchant line takes a list of three: "Enchant creature, land, or planeswalker", "Enchant
creature, planeswalker, or Clue", "Enchant artifact, creature, or planeswalker" (Planar Disruption,
Tamiyo's Compleation). And "Enchant creature or Food". targetSpecFrom already read all of these.
Only the reader's own allowlist and its character class kept them out.

The list matters. In Too Deep prints "or Clue" because the enchanted creature is no longer a
creature once the Aura applies, and an Aura that could only enchant a creature would fall off
(CR 704.5m). The first test fixture printed "Enchant creature or planeswalker", and the Aura went to
the graveyard, which is correct. The fixture now prints the card's own list.

Read whole now: Imprisoned in the Moon, In Too Deep, Sugar Coat, Minimus Containment.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- All three test Auras read whole.
- An imprisoned creature is a colorless land with no subtypes and no flying, and taps for {C}.
- An imprisoned land taps for {C} only, and its own draw ability is refused.
- An imprisoned Forest keeps its Forest type and makes no green.
- A creature made a Clue is an artifact Clue, and its controller is offered the one ability.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- The effect's own grant dropped with the loss.
- The basic land type's mana kept.
- The activation loop skipping every permanent that has lost all abilities.
- The printed script kept on a stripped mana source.
- The Enchant line without commas.

Coverage: 17,253 of 31,900 cards (+5 over D1289's 17,248), 40,004 of 59,888 lines (+10).

## D1292 — A sacrifice made by the effect, then a search one mana value up: Enigmatic Incarnation, Vivien on the Hunt

"At the beginning of your end step, you may sacrifice another enchantment. If you do, search your
library for a creature card with mana value equal to 1 plus the sacrificed enchantment's mana
value, put that card onto the battlefield, then shuffle." Vivien on the Hunt's +2 is the same with a
creature.

D1265 reads the climb only behind a sacrifice paid as a cost, where the stack object records what
was sacrificed. Here the sacrifice is X of "you may X. If you do, Y". That reader refused the shape
because X and Y both ask a question, and Y's question cannot be held back on X's answer being
empty. This Y needs no holding back. Its candidates are measured from X's answer, so an empty
answer leaves nothing to find, and Y's effect still runs only if X happened.

The changes:
- `CardsDecisionSpec.climbFromFirstAnswer`: the climb measured from the first card an answer of this
  resolution named (still on the battlefield when the search is asked). The first answer that names
  a card, not `answers[0]`: a "you may" asks its yes-or-no ahead of the sacrifice, and that answer
  names nothing.
- The "If you do" reader reads Y with the cost-sacrifice flag on, for this alone: X must be a
  sacrifice asking once, every question Y asks must be a climb, and Y may name "sacrificed" only
  once. A Y that also says "the sacrificed creature's power" would read that from a stack object
  that recorded nothing, a silent 0, so it is not read this way.
- Y's effect reads its own answers, which come after X's. Without this, Y's search took X's answer
  as the card found, and returned the sacrificed enchantment from the graveyard to the battlefield.
  The exploratory test caught it before any assertion was written.
- The climb also takes "the sacrificed enchantment's".

Pin updated: D1265 pinned a made-up effect-paid Vivien line as unread. It now reads whole, and the
bare search with nothing sacrificed at all still does not.

Read whole now: Enigmatic Incarnation. Vivien on the Hunt's +2 reads; its +1 does not yet. Iron
Man's attack trigger ("create a Treasure token, then you may sacrifice …") is not read yet.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests, and the D1265 pin changed:
- It reads whole.
- A 2 sacrificed offers only the threes; the one picked enters, and the enchantment is in the
  graveyard.
- "No" sacrifices nothing and finds nothing.
- With no other enchantment, "Yes" sacrifices nothing, so nothing is offered or found.
- Vivien's +2 reads, and a Y that also names the sacrificed creature's power does not.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The flag ignored, so the climb is measured from the empty stack record.
- `answers[0]` instead of the first answer naming a card.
- Y reading X's answers.
- The "sacrificed only once" guard dropped.

Coverage: 17,255 of 31,900 cards (+1 over D1291's 17,254), 40,007 of 59,888 lines (+2).

## D1293 — "Activate only during combat", "during the declare blockers step", "as an instant"

Three more clauses for the "Activate only …" sentence of an activated ability:
- "During combat" (`ActivationTiming 'combat'`): any player's combat phase, from its beginning to its
  end (CR 506.1), on anybody's turn. Unlike the three existing timings, this one is not about whose
  turn it is, so `atActivationTiming` asks it before the active-seat check. Najeela, the
  Blade-Blossom's "{W}{U}{B}{R}{G}: Untap all attacking creatures. After this phase, there is an
  additional combat phase" is the line that matters.
- "During the declare blockers step" (`'declare-blockers'`): that step, on anybody's turn.
- "As an instant": every activated ability's own timing (CR 602.2), so nothing to add.

The refusal names the clause, as the other timings do.

Most cards that print these clauses still have another part unread: a compound timing ("during
combat after blockers are declared"), a cost, or an effect. Najeela's trigger, "Whenever a Warrior
attacks, you may have its controller create a 1/1 white Warrior creature token that's tapped and
attacking", is not read yet. It watches any player's Warriors, and the token attacks for that
player.

Read whole now: none on its own. Najeela's untap line now reads.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both test creatures read, and Najeela's untap line.
- The combat one is refused in the main phase, with the clause named, and offered at the beginning
  of combat on either player's turn.
- The declare-blockers one is not offered in declare attackers. It is offered in declare blockers
  once blockers are declared, and not at end of combat, where the combat one still is.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The combat check dropped.
- The declare-blockers check dropped.
- "During combat" read as "during your turn".

Coverage: 17,255 of 31,900 cards (+0 over D1292's 17,255), 40,008 of 59,888 lines (+1).

## D1294 — Split cards from card data

Every split card from card data was refused before this ("layout split has more than one face"), so
in an uploaded deck Fire // Ice, Commit // Memory or Expansion // Explosion was cardboard. The engine
already plays split cards: the hand-written Fire // Ice and Wax // Wane cast either half and never
the whole (CR 708). Only the compiler path was missing.

`compileSplit` compiles each half on its own, as a single card. The whole is the shape the engine
already plays:
- both names, both type lines and both costs joined with " // ";
- the halves' colours together;
- their mana values added, which is the card's mana value everywhere but the stack (CR 708.4).

The whole has no script of its own. `derive.ts` reads a compiled def back at play time, and for a
split card its faces are the two halves and nothing else. The round trip used to put the whole card
in front of its faces, which is right for a transforming card and wrong here.

Refused, rather than played wrongly:
- Aftermath (27 cards): the second half may be cast only from the graveyard. Offered from the hand
  like any other half, it would be a spell the card does not allow.
- Rooms (30 cards): an enchantment with two doors, unlocked separately. The engine has no doors yet.

Fuse stays an unread line on each half: each half is still cast on its own, as the card allows, and
casting both together is not offered yet. Of the 69 legal split cards that now compile, 28 read
whole; 17 of the rest are short only of Fuse.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- A split card from data compiles to the split shape: names, types, costs, mana value 3 from 1 and
  2, colours, two faces. Read back from the def at play time, it has no unread line, and a Fuse
  card's line is still reported.
- Aftermath and a Room are refused. Fuse is the only unread line on a Fuse card.
- In a deck: the card is offered as its halves, the whole is refused ("choose which half"), the
  second half is cast for its own cost, and the card goes to the graveyard.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- The old round trip, the whole in front of its halves.
- Aftermath let through.
- Rooms let through.
- The mana value of the first half only.
- The split path dropped.

Coverage: 17,255 of 31,900 cards (+0 over D1293's 17,255), 40,008 of 59,888 lines (+0).

## D1295 — Fuse

"Fuse (You may cast one or both halves of this card from your hand.)" Wear // Tear, Turn // Burn,
Far // Away, Toil // Trouble. CR 702.102: from the hand, both halves may be cast as one spell, for
both costs, with both halves' targets, the left half's instructions first.

The whole card is exactly that spell: its cost is both halves' costs, its types both halves', and
its mana value their sum (CR 702.102c and d). So a fused cast is the whole card cast with `fuse` on
the action, and its script is the whole card's, built by `fusedScript` from the two halves:
- targets: the left half's, then the right's;
- questions: the left half's, then the right's;
- on resolution: the left half's effect, then the right's, each with its own slice of the targets
  (by position, from `targetSlots` when one has gone, D953's rule) and of the answers.

The fused spell is one spell. It is countered only when every target it has is gone (CR 608.2b),
which the engine already does for any spell. Otherwise each half runs with what it still has. The
first draft skipped a half whose targets had all gone, so that its untargeted instructions would not
happen. That is wrong: they still happen. The fault check that rule could not fail is what showed
it, and the rule is gone.

Refused, and the Fuse line left unread:
- a half with anything beyond a spell's targets, questions and effect;
- a divided quantity;
- an "up to" target in the left half, which would move the right half's targets along;
- a "target player …" question in one half when the other half can target a player too, because the
  question finds its player among the whole spell's targets. A question about the caster ("Discard
  a card") is not one of those. The first draft refused any question at all here; the narrower rule
  reads Down // Dirty's shape.

Offered from the hand only, and only as a plain cast from it. The cost shown is "{R}{G}", not the
card's "{R} // {G}". The bot sends `fuse` with the play it picked.

Of the legal split cards (D1294), 39 now read whole, up from 28: eleven fuse cards. A measuring
note: this corpus carries no legality data for split cards, so the legal-pool measure filters all
126 of them out, and D1294's and this increment's gains do not show in the coverage line below. The
split-only figures are from compiling those 126 rows directly.

**Tests.** 7 engine tests, and D1294's Fuse fixture changed to one whose halves do not compose:
- The Fuse line reads when the halves compose. A plain split card is not fused. A clash (both halves
  can aim at a player, and the right asks "target player") stays unread.
- From the hand for "{R}{G}", the two effects in order: the creature destroyed, then 3 life.
- Refused with a half named, on a card without fuse, and from the graveyard.
- With its only target gone, the fused spell is countered whole, both halves.
- Each half acts on its own target: one creature zapped, the other grows.
- Each half reads its own answers: you discard for the left half, the opponent for the right.
- With one half's target gone, the spell resolves, and the other half acts on its own target only.

Faults injected by hand: 7, all caught.
- The offer dropped.
- The hand-only check dropped.
- The right half given every target.
- The left half given every target.
- The halves' targets in the wrong order.
- The right half given every answer.
- The "target player" guard dropped.

Two more from the drafts, not injected: the broad "any question" guard failed the answers test
(the card did not fuse), and the "gone half" rule could not fail and was removed (above). The
left-half and right-half target faults each passed the first version of the tests; the zap-and-grow
fixture and the damage check were added so that they fail.

The first gate failed on the deck-coverage test: `CardScript.fused` is a new script field, and the
test lists every field no pool deck exercises. I had skipped that check before the gate. The field
was added to the list with the test that drives it, and the gate run again before any push.
A process slip on the re-run: the first finisher was still waiting on its coverage measure when the
second started. It wrote its STOP into the second's log, and its exit resumed the paused sweep. The
sweep was paused again and the second gate's own result is the one used; the coverage figure is the
same either way, because only the test file changed between the two runs.

Coverage: 17,255 of 31,900 cards (+0 over D1294's 17,255), 40,008 of 59,888 lines (+0).

## D1297 — The web table sends the cast flags it was dropping

D113's bug again, five times. The table builds the action for a play from a fixed list of flags
(`COST_FLAGS` in `apps/web/src/lib/arena.ts`). Five flags the engine puts on its plays were not on
that list:
- `impended` (D1097, an impending cost);
- `altCast` (D1251, a printed mana or life alternative);
- `fuse` (D1295);
- `aftermath` (D1296);
- `yardBy` (D1287, a graveyard permission), which is a string, so it gets its own line.

So the engine offered each play, and the table sent back an action without the flag. The engine
then refused it as a different cast ("choose which half", "not in your hand"), or, for an
alternative or impending cost, would have charged the printed cost instead. Every engine test
passed, because they build their actions by hand; the bot passes each flag itself. Found while
reading how the table sends special actions, ahead of Rooms. A human tester would have hit it on
the first Karador, fuse card or Snuff Out.

A check of every true-or-false field on a legal play against the client found these five and two
more, `fromHand` and `fromGraveyard`, which only say which row to draw an ability on.

**Tests.** 1 web test: the five plays, each sent with its flag.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- `fuse` dropped from the list.
- `altCast` dropped.
- `aftermath` dropped.
- `yardBy` not sent.

No rules-engine change, so the coverage line below is unchanged.

Coverage: 17,255 of 31,900 cards (+0 over D1296's 17,255), 40,008 of 59,888 lines (+0).

## D1298 — Rooms

A Room (CR 709.5) is a split enchantment with two doors. Casting one door unlocks it as the Room
enters. A locked door can be unlocked later, as a sorcery, by paying its mana cost; that is a special
action, with no stack. A locked door's abilities do nothing. Thirty legal cards, all from Duskmourn;
D1294 refused every one.

**The permanent's script** is both doors', each part scoped to its own door being unlocked. The
model is D638's Class levels (`readClassLevels`), and `roomScript` is the same move:
- activated abilities through `activateOnlyIf`;
- triggers through `condition`;
- statics through a new `while` kind, `source-door-unlocked`.
A door with anything else (a grant, a cost rule, a replacement) refuses the whole Room, so a door
whose rules could not be scoped is never active while locked. That refuses 3 of the 30.

**The state** is `CardInstance.doors`, unlocked by face index:
- A Room cast as a door arrives with that door unlocked, and its "When you unlock this door"
  triggers then, which is why Bottomless Pool cast for {U} bounces a creature at once.
- A Room arriving any other way has every door locked.
- A Room that changes zone is a new object, locked again (CR 400.7).
- Shown to every player in the view, as a Class's level is.

**"When you unlock this door"** is a new trigger event, `door-unlocked`. It reads with no door, and
the merge gives it the door it is printed on, so unlocking one door does not fire the other's.

**Unlocking** is `auto:unlock` {card, door}, modelled on plot (D922):
- Refused for a door the card does not have, a door already unlocked, a permanent you do not
  control, and outside sorcery timing.
- Pays the door's cost, unlocks it, raises the event, and settles.
- Offered by `legalActions` for each locked door the seat can pay for.
- The bot judges it like any other play.
- The web table sends it, one row per door.

"This Room" now refers to the card itself (`SELF_TYPE_WORDS`).

Simplifications, stated:
- A Room's name, mana value and colours on the battlefield are the whole card's. The rules use only
  its unlocked doors' (CR 709.5d); a "mana value 3 or less" check on a Room reads the sum of both
  doors.
- "Fully unlock", which Eerie watches, is not raised yet.

Of the legal split cards, 123 now compile (from 96) and 62 read whole (from 52). The legal-pool
measure still cannot see split cards (D1295's note).

**Tests.** 9 engine tests and 1 web test:
- A Room compiles to one enchantment, the unlock trigger with its door and the static with its
  `while`.
- Cast as its first door: that door unlocked, its unlock trigger fires (3 life), the other door's
  static does nothing, and only the other door is offered to unlock.
- Unlocking the other door: paid, unlocked, its static applies, the first door's trigger does not
  fire again, and unlocking it twice is refused.
- A locked door's end-step trigger does nothing; unlocked, it fires.
- Only as a sorcery (refused and not offered at the beginning of combat), and only a door the card
  has.
- Put onto the battlefield without being cast: both locked, both offered, and unlocking the first
  fires its trigger.
- The bot, with a locked Room and the mana, unlocks a door, and the engine takes every action it
  sends.
- A Room that leaves and comes back is locked.
- A door with a grant, and a door with a rule of another kind, each refuse the Room.
- Web: an unlock play is sent as `auto:unlock` naming its door.

Faults injected by hand: 9 in the engine, all caught.
- The cast door not unlocked on arrival.
- Its trigger not raised on arrival.
- Any door's unlock firing every door's trigger.
- The door `while` always true.
- A door's triggers not scoped.
- A locked door still offered.
- The sorcery-timing check dropped.
- The zone change keeping the doors.
- The key check dropped (it passed the grant fixture, which the statics check also refuses; the
  Steaming Sauna fixture was added so that it fails).

Coverage: 17,255 of 31,900 cards (+0 over D1297's 17,255), 40,008 of 59,888 lines (+0).

## D1299 — Eerie, and fully unlocking a Room

"Eerie — Whenever an enchantment you control enters and whenever you fully unlock a Room, <effect>."
Seventeen legal cards from Duskmourn: Balemurk Leech, Entity Tracker, Gremlin Tamer and kin.

- A Room is fully unlocked when its last locked door is unlocked. `unlockDoor` raises
  `room-fully-unlocked` then, after the door's own event. Every permanent sees it, and "you" is
  whoever unlocked the door.
- The reader takes the line without "and whenever you fully unlock a Room". It reads the rest as
  the enchantment-enters trigger it is, then gives the same trigger again on the second moment. Two
  triggers with one effect, as D635's "enters or is turned face up" is: `TriggerDef.on` is one
  event.
- **A misfiled word, found on the way:** "eerie" was on the keyword list (`KEYWORD_ABILITY_NAMES`),
  so its label was never taken off the line, and every Eerie trigger was unread whatever came after
  it. Eerie is an ability word (CR 207.2c), like Magecraft, and comes off that list.

Read whole now: 12 of the 17. The other five have another unread part: "Whenever ~ or another
enchantment …", a convoke grant, a first-and-second-time count, an "as though it didn't have
defender", and a choice on entering.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- It reads whole, as two triggers: an enchantment entering, and a Room fully unlocked.
- An enchantment of yours entering: each opponent loses 1.
- A Room's first door unlocked does nothing; its last door does.
- An opponent fully unlocking their own Room is not "you".

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- "You" not checked.
- Raised on every unlock, not only the last.
- The second trigger dropped.

Coverage: 17,267 of 31,900 cards (+12 over D1298's 17,255), 40,021 of 59,888 lines (+13).

## D1300 — "Whenever you put one or more counters on …": who put them, and how many

Hapatra, Vizier of Poisons; Ant-Man, Colony Commander; Knight of Wundagore; Generous Patron; Nest of
Scarabs; Obelisk Spider; Casey Jones; Mikey & Leo. 26 legal lines, and the phrase-gap measure's top
row: 81 cards were one counter phrase from finished.

**Who put them.** The `counters-put` event (D633) did not record who put the counters. D881 had
stated this as a gap for Exemplar of Light. Now:
- `GameState.countersBy` is the controller of the stack object resolving. `completeResolution`
  sets it for the length of the resolution and clears it after.
- `addCounters` writes it onto each placement.
- The event is raised with that seat as its actor, falling back to the permanent's controller.
- The matcher's new `byYou` asks for the watcher's controller.
- Exemplar of Light's trigger now has `byYou` too.

**A gap found on the way:** infect's and wither's damage wrote its -1/-1 counters straight onto
the creature, so they were never announced. No "-1/-1 counters are put on" trigger saw them,
Hapatra's included. They are announced now, as put by the damage source's controller (CR 702.80c).

**Every kind.** Placements were recorded for +1/+1, -1/-1, loyalty and the monstrous marker only.
"Whenever you put one or more counters on a creature" is any kind, and Kate Stewart's are time
counters, so every kind but the engine's own markers is recorded now. Every existing counters-put
trigger names its kind, so none of them sees more than before.

**How many.** Each placement carries its amount after Hardened Scales and its kin, and the event's
`eventAmount` and the "that many" mark take it: Nest of Scarabs' "create that many", Casey Jones'
"that much damage".

**The readers:**
- "Whenever you put (a|one or more) [kind] counter(s) on" a creature, another creature, a creature
  you (don't) control, a permanent you control, or a planeswalker.
- The same "on ~" with any named kind.

Read whole now: Ant-Man, Exemplar of Light, Generous Patron, Hapatra, Knight of Wundagore, Mikey &
Leo, Nest of Scarabs, Obelisk Spider, Casey Jones, Stocking the Pantry. Terrasymbiosis and Chekov and
McCoy are held by "Do this only once each turn".

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- The three test cards read.
- Your spell putting -1/-1 counters on their creature makes a Snake.
- Their spell putting -1/-1 counters on your creature is not you: no Snake.
- Wither damage puts its counter on, and it is yours: a Snake.
- "That many": two counters, two Insects.
- "A creature you don't control": theirs draws, yours does not.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- "You" not checked.
- `countersBy` not set.
- "You don't control" not checked.
- The amount not carried.
- Wither's counters not announced.

Coverage: 17,278 of 31,900 cards (+11 over D1299's 17,267), 40,034 of 59,888 lines (+13).

## D1301 — "Do this only once each turn"

"Whenever you put one or more +1/+1 counters on Chekov and McCoy, you may draw that many cards. Do
this only once each turn." 34 legal lines: Terrasymbiosis, Ancient Cornucopia, Corruption of
Towashi, Cosmic Crucible.

Not D532's "This ability triggers only once each turn". The ability triggers every time, and only
the doing is limited, so a "no" to its "you may" does not spend the turn's one. Read in
`triggerRestriction` (only after a "you may"). The trigger it builds keeps a record in the
permanent's `abilityUsedTurn`, beside D532's, written when the effect changed the game.

Once spent, the trigger's condition keeps it off the stack for the rest of the turn. The rules
have it trigger and do nothing; nothing in the pool can tell the two apart, except a card that
counts abilities triggering, and none of those prints this sentence. A condition is asked again as
the ability resolves, so two that triggered together do it once.

The first draft also checked the record inside the effect. That check could not fail any test,
because the condition already does the job on resolution, so it is gone.

Read whole now: 7 more of the 34. The rest have another unread part (connive, "copy it", "cast
target … card").

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- It reads whole.
- Done once, then not even asked again that turn.
- A "no" does not spend it: the next "yes" does it.
- Spent for this turn only: on a later turn it is done again.

Faults injected by hand: 4, 3 caught, 1 removed as redundant.
- The condition dropped.
- The record written even when nothing happened.
- The record read for any turn.
- The check inside the effect, which the resolution condition makes redundant.

On the way, two test-fixture errors of mine: the helper that passes priority answers a "you may"
with no, and my first spell asked a scry question of its own. Each test now answers its question
itself.

Coverage: 17,285 of 31,900 cards (+7 over D1300's 17,278), 40,042 of 59,888 lines (+8).

## D1302 — Counters removed as an effect

"At the beginning of your upkeep, remove a time counter from ~." "Whenever ~ deals combat damage
to a player, remove all -1/-1 counters from it." "{1}: Remove a -1/-1 counter from target
creature." "Whenever you cast a spell, you may remove a slumber counter from ~." The cost form ("Remove
a +1/+1 counter from ~: …") has read for a long time; the effect form had no reader. 563 legal
lines print the phrase, and 335 of them were unread.

`removeCountersEffect`, in the effect chain after the targeted readers, reads:
- a number, or "all";
- of one named kind, or "all counters" of every kind;
- from the card itself, or from a target permanent.
Fewer come off when fewer are there, and none when none are. "All counters" leaves the engine's own
markers, a regeneration shield or a kicked flag, which are not counters. A bare "a counter", which
leaves the kind to the player, stays unread. A "you may" in front reads through the existing
optional reader.

Unread lines with the phrase: 300 now, from 335. Many of the rest name "it" for the permanent, or
pair the removal with a reader that is missing ("Then if it has no … counters on it").

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The three test cards read, and a bare "a counter" stays unread.
- One -1/-1 counter off a target that has two.
- All +1/+1 counters off itself, its oil counters kept.
- All counters off a target, every kind.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The bare "a counter" read.
- One counter asked for, every one removed.
- "All counters" removing nothing.
- A target's counters taken off the source.

Coverage: 17,304 of 31,900 cards (+19 over D1301's 17,285), 40,082 of 59,888 lines (+40).

## D1303 — "Remove … counters from it"

D1302's reader takes "it" now: "Whenever ~ deals combat damage to a player, remove all -1/-1
counters from it", "Whenever a creature you control attacks, remove a -1/-1 counter from it",
"{T}: Remove all -1/-1 counters from it". "It" follows the engine's one rule for it (`itMeans`): the
permanent the event was about, or the card itself when there is no event (an activated ability).

Unread lines with the phrase: 289, from 300.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both test cards read.
- An activated ability's "it" is the card itself: its -1/-1 counters come off.
- A trigger's "it" is the attacking creature: its counter comes off, and the watcher's own stays.

Faults injected by hand: 1, caught: "it" read as the card itself.

Coverage: 17,312 of 31,900 cards (+8 over D1302's 17,304), 40,093 of 59,888 lines (+11).

## D1304 — Exiling chosen cards from your graveyard

"Exile two cards from your graveyard", "exile a creature card from your graveyard": chosen as the
ability resolves, not targeted. 171 legal lines print the phrase; 68 were unread. Its main home is
the opener of "you may X. If you do, Y": Aegis Sculptor's "you may exile two cards from your
graveyard. If you do, put a +1/+1 counter on ~".

- The reader asks for exactly that many cards of that kind, and exiles the ones chosen.
- **A rule for "If you do" with a count, in `optionalEffect`:** an X whose question asks for N cards
  is done only with all N. With fewer there, the engine's question lowers its minimum to what is
  available, so the answer can be short. "If you do" is then false, and X is not done either: you
  cannot choose to do what you cannot do in full. A plain "exile two cards from your graveyard"
  still exiles as many as there are (CR 609.3).
- The one-card openers ("sacrifice a creature", "discard a card") ask for one, so they read as
  before.

Unread lines with the phrase: 57, from 68.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both test cards read.
- "You may exile two … If you do, draw a card": two exiled, one card drawn.
- The same with one card in the graveyard: nothing exiled and nothing drawn.
- A plain "exile two" with one card there exiles that one.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The full-count rule dropped.
- The count read as one.
- The chosen cards not exiled.

A test fixture error of mine on the way: a question with one possible answer is answered by the
engine, so the card was already exiled when the test went looking for it in the graveyard.

Coverage: 17,322 of 31,900 cards (+10 over D1303's 17,312), 40,104 of 59,888 lines (+11).

not a Room gets none.

**Tests.** 1 web test: a Room with its first door unlocked shows both badges, and a split instant

Faults injected by hand: 2, both caught.

- Every split card badged.

## D1306 — Two mana of any one color, granted to a land

Gift of Paradise, Grafted Growth and New Horizons give the enchanted land "{T}: Add two mana of any
one color." The line reader knew "one mana of any color" and the D697 runs ("two mana in any
combination") but not a run of one chosen colour, so all three cards stopped on that line. The
mana-choice reader in `lineScriptFor` now reads "add two (three, four, five) mana of any one color"
as one ability per colour that makes that many of it. The player sees five rows on the land.

Granting the ability exposed two places that pay for a land as a whole:

- **`manaSources` folds every usable tap row into one source.** On a Forest that meant its own
  {G} plus five runs of two. The D697 runs branch needs every row the same length, so the mixed
  rows were merged into one flat choice of one mana, and the land paid one where it can pay two.
  Now, when the longest rows are runs of one colour and every shorter row's colours are among
  them, only the longest rows make the source. Two of a colour is never worse than one of it, and
  every row is still offered to the player.
- **`potentialMana` added up every tap ability's mana,** so the Forest counted three green. A
  permanent's tap abilities now count the most of each kind any one of them makes, because one
  tap pays for one ability. Abilities that don't tap are still added up. Across different kinds
  the count stays optimistic, as before.

**Tests.** 2 tests:
- The Aura compiles whole.
- On the enchanted Forest:
  - there is one source, a run of two from all five colours;
  - two blue and two green are reachable;
  - at least six activations are still offered.

Faults injected by hand: 2, both caught.
- The longest-run fold dropped. The first version of the test missed this, because the old fold
  also gave one source; the test now checks the source's shape.
- Tap abilities added up again.

Compile pins: 1791 of 1791 pass.

Coverage: 17,330 of 31,900 cards (+8 over D1305's 17,322), 40,114 of 59,888 lines (+10).

## D1307 — Counters removed as an X: storage lands and mana batteries

Some costs say "Remove any number of storage counters from ~" or "Remove X charge counters from ~".
The cost reader takes a fixed count of counters, so it refused these, along with every line that
printed one. That covered:
- the storage lands (Mage-Ring Network, Fountain of Cho and the Mercadian lands);
- the five mana batteries;
- Kyren Toy;
- Infused Arrows, Skullmane Baku, Chamber Sentry, Cruel Sadist, Arcbound Javelineer and Auntie
  Blyte.

**The cost.** `AbilityCost.removeXCounters` holds the counter's kind. The X is announced with the
activation, in the same `x` an {X} cost uses (D789):
- `activate` refuses an X larger than the counters the source has, and removes them as the cost is
  paid;
- the X is the ability's X on the stack, so "-X/-X" and "It deals X damage" read it. A line is now
  X-payable when its cost removes X counters, not only when it has {X};
- Talon of Pain and Chamber Sentry have both {X} and "Remove X", which is one X: `xMax` is the
  smaller of what the mana pays and what the counters allow.

**The mana.** Three printed forms make mana once for each counter removed, plus
`AbilityDef.producesPerX` more:
- "Add {R} for each storage counter removed this way" (0 more);
- "Add {B}, then add an additional {B} for each charge counter removed this way" (1 more);
- "Add an amount of {C} equal to X plus one" (1 more).

Tap mana lines normally go to the mana-line parser, which doesn't take this cost. `compile.ts` now
hands such a line to the general reader, as it does for Phyrexian Tower (D666). It keeps the result
only if every ability that comes back removes X counters and has the count.

How many to remove is the player's choice, so these abilities are never the auto-payer's:
- `manaSources` skips them;
- the table offers them with `xMax` equal to the counters held, and asks the X as it does for any
  ability with one;
- `potentialMana` counts them at their most, every counter removed.

**Five storage lands are held back on purpose:** Dwarven Hold, Bottomless Vault, Hollow Trees,
Icatian Store and Sand Silos. Each also says "You may choose not to untap ~ during your untap step"
and charges only at an upkeep where it is still tapped. The untap step answers that choice by
untapping it, unless it holds a control change (D1041), so read whole these lands would never
charge. D1041's pin says exactly this. `compile.ts` therefore leaves their storage line unread
until keeping a land tapped is a real question for its controller.

**Still unread:**
- "Add X mana in any combination of {W} and/or {U}" (Calciform Pools and five others). This is a
  second choice on the activation, and an X doesn't answer it.
- Petalmane Baku's "X mana of any one color".
- Brain in a Jar's "Scry X". A scry asks a question, so it doesn't read with an {X} cost either.

**Tests.** 4 tests:
- Compile: Mercadian Bazaar, the battery, the toy, the Arrows and Cruel Sadist read whole. Only the
  combination line on Calciform Pools and Dwarven Hold's storage line stay unread.
- Mercadian Bazaar with three counters:
  - it is offered with `xMax` 3, and is not a mana source;
  - three red show on the pips;
  - an X of 4 is refused;
  - an X of 2 makes RR, leaves one counter and taps the land.
- The battery with two counters makes RRR. Kyren Toy with none makes C. A battery is not an
  auto-payer source.
- Infused Arrows with three counters is offered `xMax` 3. An X of 2 removes two counters and its
  -2/-2 kills Grizzly Bears.

Faults injected by hand: 7, all caught.
- The X ignored for the mana.
- The counters not removed.
- An X over the counters allowed.
- The auto-payer given the battery.
- No `xMax`.
- The X not payable in the reader. The first version of the test missed this, because Infused
  Arrows reads without it; Cruel Sadist's "It deals X damage" does not, and is now checked.
- The kept-tapped land read whole (caught here and by D1041). The first gate run caught this one:
  the first version read Dwarven Hold whole, and D1041's pin failed.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6400 of 6400 pass.

Coverage: 17,348 of 31,900 cards (+18 over D1306's 17,330), 40,133 of 59,888 lines (+19).

## D1308 — The Spheres: prevent some of the damage a kind of source deals you

"If a red source would deal damage to you, prevent 2 of that damage" (the five Spheres) had no
reader. Neither did its kin:
- Urza's Armor's "a source";
- "a source an opponent controls" (Guardian Seraph, Heart-Shaped Herb, Protection of the Hekma);
- Orbs of Warding's "a creature";
- Sphere of Purity's "an artifact".

These are prevention effects with an amount (CR 615.7), each a static on a permanent.
`CardScript.damageToYouReduced` holds the amount and the kind: a colour, a card type, or the
opponents' sources.

`dealDamage` applies it to each damage event dealt to the permanent's controller, after the
prevent-all effects and before the prevention shields. Each permanent of that controller whose kind
the source matches takes off its amount, and several add up. Damage that prevention can't touch
(D1212) passes through.

How the source is read:
- its colour and type are read live from the source, so a spell on the stack is read from its card;
- its controller is the one passed, otherwise the source permanent's, as `multipliedDamage` reads
  it (D865).

Damage to the controller's creatures is not reduced: these say "to you". Hedron-Field Purists' "to
you or a creature you control" is on a leveler and stays unread. Heart-Shaped Herb's sacrifice line
is unread as before.

**Tests.** 3 tests:
- Compile: the four readings, one of each kind.
- Sphere of Law:
  - three from a red creature is one;
  - one is nothing;
  - three from a green creature is three.
- With Sphere of Law, Urza's Armor and Guardian Seraph:
  - five from the opponent's red creature is one;
  - five from your own red creature is two (the Seraph ignores it);
  - the opponent's damage is not reduced by your Sphere.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- Colour ignored.
- Opponents ignored.
- The largest taken instead of the sum.
- The reduction not applied.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6403 of 6403 pass. Deck coverage passes with the new
field listed as compiler-only.

Coverage: 17,358 of 31,900 cards (+10 over D1307's 17,348), 40,144 of 59,888 lines (+11).

## D1309 — "You may choose not to untap ~": the controller answers

D1041 answered "You may choose not to untap ~ during your untap step" (CR 502.3) for its
controller: kept tapped while the permanent holds a "for as long as ~ remains tapped" control change,
untapped otherwise. That is right for Vedalken Shackles. It is wrong for a storage land, which is
kept tapped so that "At the beginning of your upkeep, if ~ is tapped, put a storage counter on it"
charges it. D1041 left a pin saying a storage land must stay unread until that choice was a real
question. D1307 held back five lands for the same reason: Dwarven Hold, Bottomless Vault, Hollow
Trees, Icatian Store and Sand Silos.

**The answer is now the player's, given ahead of the step.** The choice is made in the untap step,
where nobody has priority and nothing is asked, so the table takes a standing answer:
- `auto:keepTapped {card, keep}` sets or clears `CardInstance.keepTapped` on a permanent of the
  seat's whose card says it;
- every untap step of its controller's after that leaves it tapped, until they say otherwise;
- like `auto:stops`, it is a setting: no priority needed, none passed;
- it is refused on someone else's permanent and on one whose card doesn't say it;
- a zone change clears it (CR 400.7).

It is not a `LegalPlay`, on purpose. The table's auto-pass stops at any seat with a non-mana play,
so a toggle offered at every priority would have stopped it, every time, for anyone with a Shackles
or a storage land.

**The view.** It sends `mayStayTapped` on such a permanent (printed, so public). `keepTapped` goes
to its controller only.

**The web table.**
- The card's sheet shows a "Keep ~ tapped in your untap step" toggle on the viewer's own such
  permanent. Its test id is outside the `play-` prefix the browser driver reads as plays.
- A kept permanent shows a "kept tapped" badge.

With the choice real, the five storage lands read whole: D1307's exclusion in `compile.ts` is gone,
and D1041's pin now says the land reads whole.

**Not done.** The bot never sets the answer, so it keeps none of these tapped. It doesn't press
storage mana either, since that is never an auto-payer source (D1307), so a storage land is a land
it doesn't use.

**Tests.** 3 new tests, and two pins updated:
- A tapped Bottomless Vault, kept tapped:
  - after a round it is still tapped, with one storage counter;
  - released, it untaps at the next untap step;
  - its one counter then makes one black.
- Untouched, it untaps as usual, gains nothing, and the choice is not among the plays.
- Refusals:
  - on the opponent's Vault;
  - on a Swamp.
- Visibility:
  - the controller's view shows both fields;
  - the opponent's view shows only `mayStayTapped`.
- A zone change clears it.
- D1041's storage pin and D1307's compile test now expect the land whole.
- 1 web test: the "kept tapped" badge.

Faults injected by hand: 6, all caught.
- The flag not read by the untap step.
- The flag not set.
- The flag kept on a zone change.
- The flag shown to every seat.
- Any permanent accepted.
- The web badge dropped.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6406 of 6406 pass. Web: typecheck clean, 279 of 279.

Coverage: 17,363 of 31,900 cards (+5 over D1308's 17,358), 40,149 of 59,888 lines (+5).

## D1310 — A delayed draw from a permanent's ability

"Draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep" has read on a spell since D689, as a
delayed trigger on the card itself. It did not read in a permanent's ability. That left Carrier
Pigeons' "When ~ enters, draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep" unread, along with
the other Mirage and Ice Age cantrip permanents (Krovikan Fetish, Pyknite, Barbed Sextant).

It is now the engine-known delayed ability `builtin: 'draw'`, next to D696's sacrifice and exile:
- it is scheduled as the ability resolves;
- it goes on the stack at whoever's upkeep comes next, so the draw is usually at the opponent's
  upkeep;
- the ability's controller draws;
- it has no subject, so it happens whether or not the permanent is still there (CR 603.7c).

**A simplification this inherits, not one it adds.** Barbed Sextant's "{1}, {T}, Sacrifice ~: Add
one mana of any color. Draw a card at the beginning of the next turn's upkeep." now reads the way
Chromatic Sphere's "Add one mana of any color. Draw a card." already did: as an ability that uses
the stack and adds the mana as it resolves. By CR 605.1a it is a mana ability, which never uses the
stack and can be used mid-payment. A mana ability with a second effect is the next thing worth
reading properly. Aleatory's line is still unread, because its coin-flip line is.

**Tests.** 2 tests:
- The Pigeons fixture reads whole.
- After casting it:
  - one delayed draw is waiting;
  - nothing is drawn that turn;
  - at the opponent's next upkeep its controller has one more card;
  - the delayed draw is gone.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- No draw.
- Only at your own upkeep.
- Not the engine-known ability.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6408 of 6408 pass.

Coverage: 17,368 of 31,900 cards (+5 over D1309's 17,363), 40,157 of 59,888 lines (+8).

## D1311 — A mana ability with a second effect (CR 605.1a)

Some abilities add mana and then do something else:
- Chromatic Sphere's "{1}, {T}, Sacrifice ~: Add one mana of any color. Draw a card.";
- the five Eggs' "Add {U}{B}. Draw a card.";
- Barbed Sextant's delayed draw (D1310);
- Pyramid of the Pantheon's "Put a brick counter on ~".

Each could add mana, targets nothing and is not a loyalty ability, so each is a mana ability. It
never uses the stack, and the rest happens as the mana is added. The clause vocabulary had read
the whole line as an ability on the stack: the mana came from a colour question as it resolved,
an opponent could respond to it, and it could not be used in the middle of paying.

A measurement over the legal pool found 25 abilities that print "Add" and were read without
`produces`. The others are loyalty abilities (Chandra, Koth, Ugin), which correctly use the stack,
token makers, and two counted ones (Cabal Stronghold, Crypt of Agadeem) left for later.

The new reader in `lineScriptFor` takes "Add <symbols>. <effect>" and "Add one mana of any color.
<effect>":
- fixed symbols make one mana ability; "any color" makes one per colour, as the choice reader does;
- each carries the second effect as `effect`, which the activation's mana branch already runs
  (D497's pain lands) and settles, so a deferred draw arrives at once;
- only an effect with no target and no question, since a mana ability runs with neither;
- only beside a mana cost. `manaSources` never offers an ability with a mana cost to the
  auto-payer, which taps for mana and would not run the rest. Without the guard, "Sacrifice ~: Add
  one mana of any color. Draw a card." would have been an auto-payer source that never draws.

**Bot.** The bot does not press mana abilities for their own sake, so it no longer cracks a
Chromatic Sphere just for the card, as it could when the line was a stack ability.

**Tests.** 3 tests:
- Compile:
  - the Sphere is five mana abilities, one per colour;
  - the Egg is one, making UB;

## D1313 — A coloured cost increase: the Leeches

"White spells you cast cost {W} more to cast" (Alabaster Leech, Derelor, Andradite Leech and the
rest) is a coloured increase. The cost modifiers (D940) were generic only, and D940's pin kept the
coloured form unread on purpose.

**The modifier.** `costModifiers[].coloured` holds the symbols added, with `generic` 0 beside them.
The reader takes `{W}`…`{G}` only with "more": nothing prints a coloured reduction, and "{B} less"
stays unread.

**Applying it.** `costChangeFor` collects the symbols as `coloured`, counted "for each" as the
generic part is. `withCostChange` now takes the whole change, not just its generic number, and
adds the coloured symbols. Every caller passes the whole change, so all of these agree:
- the plain cast and the alternative costs;
- emerge, entwine, kicker, buyback and replicate;
- delve, convoke and improvise;
- the payment in `castSpell`.

**The table.** The play says it: `costExtra` "{W}" beside the printed "{W}", with the Leech's words
in `costNote`, shown in the play sheet as "+{W}" the way a generic change shows "+{1}".

**Tests.** 3 new tests, and D940's pin updated:
- Compile: the Leech reads as `coloured: ['W']`.
- With the Leech out, a white instant:
  - is not offered, and is refused, off one Plains;
  - with two Plains, is offered with `costExtra` "{W}" and taps both;
  - a colourless instant is not taxed.
- The opponent's white spell is not taxed.
- D940's pin now reads "{B} more" whole and keeps "{B} less" unread.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The colour not added to the cost.
- The cast ignoring a coloured-only change.
- The symbols not collected.

trailing form "Y if it has … counters on it". A trigger already reads the trailing form, asked as
the sentence resolves (D1026). The rewrite is kept to this condition, and skipped when Y has its own
" if ".

The Ordeals' third line, "When you sacrifice ~, …", already read.

## D1318 — Combat damage equal to toughness: Doran

Doran, the Siege Tower prints "Each creature assigns combat damage equal to its toughness rather
than its power." Belligerent Brontodon, Huatli, the Sun's Heart and Rasaad yn Bashir print it as
"Each creature you control …". Neither had a reader, and combat had no way to say it.

**The rule** (CR 510.1a): such a creature assigns its toughness as combat damage. Its power is
unchanged for everything else.

**The engine.** `ContinuousEffect.assignsByToughness` is gathered into the creature's
characteristics like the other combat statics. `combat.ts` now asks `combatDamageOf(ch)` at every
place it assigns damage:
- the unblocked hit;
- a blocked attacker's damage and its trample overflow;
- a blocker's damage, and its split among several attackers;
- the damage-order question.

The power comparisons stay on power, because "a creature with lower power can't block it" is about
power.

**The reader.** It is a static on every creature, or on the controller's, as an anthem is.

Still unread: Arcades, the Strategist and Assault Formation's "each creature you control with
defender" form, and Assault Formation's defender line.

**Tests.** 4 tests:
- Compile: both forms read, with their scopes.
- Under Doran:
  - an unblocked 0/4 hits for four, and its power is still 0;
  - a blocking 3/1 deals one, its toughness, and dies to four.
- Under the Brontodon, the opponent's 3/1 deals three, its power, and still dies.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- Power always used.
- The controller's scope read as everyone's.
- A blocked attacker's damage read from power.

## D1319 — Adamant: at least three mana of one colour spent

Throne of Eldraine's adamant asks how much of one colour paid for a spell: "If at least three white
mana was spent to cast this spell, …". It also comes as "three mana of the same color" and "three
colorless". The engine knew which colours were spent (D742) and how many colours (D917), but not
how much of each.

**The record.** `payFrom` now returns how much of each mana type it took from the pool,
colourless included. The cast puts it on the stack object (`spentByType`), and a permanent's
"you cast it" record keeps it as it resolves (`castPermanents[].spent`, beside D742's colours).

**The condition** is read in the intervening-condition vocabulary. It arrives as "three or more",
because D892 rewrites "at least". It reads the resolving spell's amounts, or for a permanent its
cast record, so a permanent that arrived any other way spent nothing.

## D1325 — The en-Kor redirects

pool's first redirection card. It goes on the protected creature, takes the next N points dealt to

activation is its own shield, so two activations take two points.

## D1326 — "A source of your choice": the Circles of Protection

44 legal lines print "The next time a [red] source of your choice would deal damage to …", and 42
of them were their card's only unread line: the ten Circles of Protection, Cho-Arrim Alchemist,
Charm Peddler, Circle of Despair, Beacon of Destiny and more. Two things were missing: a way to
choose a source, and a shield that knows one.

**The question.** A new decision zone, `'source'`, offers every permanent on every battlefield,
then the spells on the stack, top first. A spell has to be there: the Circle's whole use is to be
activated in response to a Lightning Bolt and name it. The answer is checked against the
candidates, like every card question.
- The web table lights the spells on the stack for it (`StackPanel`'s new `decidable`), alongside
  the permanents on the board, and the hint says "tap a permanent, or a spell on the stack".
- The bot names the top spell on the stack if one is offered. Otherwise it names the opponent's
  most powerful creature, attacking ones first.

**The shield.** `ContinuousEffect.nextDamageFrom` holds the chosen source as `id#seq`, the object
it is now, with the protected player or creature as its scope (`preventNextDamageFrom`).
`dealDamage` asks it before the amount shields, and it takes all of that source's next damage event
there, then is gone. Damage that can't be prevented passes it. With `redirectTo`, the damage goes
to the shield's source instead (Beacon of Destiny's "that damage is dealt to ~ instead").

**The reader** takes:
- an optional colour, or artifact, or creature;
- "to you", "to target creature" or "to any target";
- "prevent that damage" or "that damage is dealt to ~ instead".

Still unread:
- Cho-Arrim Alchemist and Bone Mask, for their second sentences;
- Dark Sphere's "prevent half";
- Shaman en-Kor and Jade Monolith's "target creature … dealt to ~ instead", which differ in where
  the shield sits.

**Tests.** 3 tests:
- The fixture Circle reads whole.
- Its question offers both of the opponent's red Goblins and not the green Bears. Answered with one
  Goblin, that Goblin's next damage to you (five) is prevented whole, then the shield is gone (its
  next one point lands), and the other Goblin was never covered.
- In response to the opponent's red instant aimed at you:
  - the question offers the spell;
  - the bot names it;
  - answered with it, the spell resolves and you lose nothing.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- The shield ignored.
- Never spent.
- No stack spells offered.
- Any colour offered.
- The bot ignoring the stack.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6455 of 6455 pass. Web: typecheck clean, 279 of 279.

## D1327 — Ward paid by discarding a card

"Ward—Discard a card." is printed on 15 legal lines (Forum Necroscribe, Spectral Snatcher, Sunset
Saboteur …). D578 left it unread because the pending payment could charge mana and life but not
a card, and a ward that cost nothing would have been worse than none.

**The payment.** `pendingPayment.discard` is the number of cards owed. The payer chooses them:
- `auto:pay` takes `discarded`, the card ids;
- `payWard` refuses unless there are exactly that many, all different, all in the payer's hand;
- it discards them as part of paying, a discard like any other, so madness and discard triggers
  see it;
- declining counters the spell as before;
- a hand too small to pay is the automatic counter, as an unaffordable mana ward already is
  (`settlePayment`).

`paymentWords` says "discard a card", alone or after mana and life. The prompt reads "Discard a
card or Test Shock is countered by …'s ward".

**The table.** `mustPay.discard` tells the client to choose. The ward prompt shows one "Discard
<card>" button per card in the viewer's hand, in place of the single Pay button.

**The bot** pays with its least valuable cards by `cardWorth`, on both paths it answers from (a
real seat's, and a simulated line's).

**Tests.** 4 tests:
- The fixture reads whole.
- Shocking the warded creature:
  - asks the caster for one card (`mustPay` says "discard a card");
  - a Pay with no card is refused;
  - paying with the Mountain discards it, and the Shock resolves for two.
- Declined, the Shock is countered. With an empty hand, nothing is asked and it is countered.
- The bot discards its {0} card rather than its land.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- Nothing discarded.
- The cards unchecked.
- An empty hand asked.
- The bot discarding its best card. The first try put this fault on the simulation path, where the
  test does not look; on the real-seat path it is caught.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6459 of 6459 pass. Web: typecheck clean, 279 of 279.

## D1328 — "Morph—Reveal a blue card in your hand."

The Legions reveal-morphs had no reader: Dragon's Eye Savants, Horde Ambusher, Ruthless Ripper,
Temur Charger and Watcher of the Roost. Their turn-up cost is showing a card of one colour from
hand (CR 702.37a lets a morph cost be anything).

`AbilityCost.revealColour` holds the colour; a morph cost has been an `AbilityCost` since Zombie
Cutthroat's life.
- `legalActions` offers the turn-up only with a card of that colour in hand.
- `turnUp` refuses without one, and otherwise shows one through the replacement notes, so the
  table sees what was revealed.
- `morphCostText` says "reveal a blue card in your hand" on the play.

**Stated simplification:** the engine reveals the first card of the colour in hand rather than
asking which. Revealing spends nothing, so the only difference is which card the opponent sees.

Still unread on the morph list: "Return two Islands …", "Discard a card", "Sacrifice another
creature", "Sacrifice two Mountains".
