## D1330 — "Discard two cards" as a cost

24 legal lines pay "Discard two cards" or "Discard three cards", and 17 were their card's only
unread line: Ghoulsteed, Haunted Dead, Advanced Stitchwing and Geralf's Masterpiece returning from
the graveyard, Latulla, Anurid Brushhopper, Alexi. D579's `discardACard` was a flag, and D580's
pin refused a count it could not hold.

**The cost.** `AbilityCost.discardCount`, beside `discardACard`, says how many. The player chooses
all of them, sent as `ActivateAction.discards`, as D732's counted sacrifice sends `sacrifices`.
- `activate` refuses anything but that many different cards, each one it may discard, and discards
  them as the cost is paid.
- `legalActions` offers the ability only with enough cards in hand, and says `discardCount` on the
  play.
- The web table collects the discards one tap at a time, as it does a counted sacrifice, and sends
  them as `discards`.

**The bot** does not use a counted discard: two cards is a price it cannot weigh against what it
buys. Taking the guard out is harmless as it happens: the bot would offer a single `discarded`,
which the engine refuses. So the guard keeps the candidate list honest rather than changing play.

Two pins retired, D446-style: "Discard two cards" reads now. Their rows are now "Discard X cards",
a count chosen as it is paid, which still has no field.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests and 1 web test:
- The fixture reads whole.
- From the graveyard with three cards in hand:
  - offered with `discardCount` 2;
  - one card, or the same card twice, is refused;
  - two different cards are discarded, and the creature returns tapped.
- With one card in hand it is not offered, and the bot does not activate it.
- Web: two taps collect two discards and send `discards: [a, c]`.

Faults injected by hand: 4.
- The count unchecked: caught.
- Nothing discarded: caught.
- Offered with one card: caught.
- The bot's guard removed: not caught, for the reason given above.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6468 of 6468 pass. Web: typecheck clean, 280 of 280.

are offered as plays like any instant-speed mana ability.

## D1332 — "Sacrifice any number of …, then … that many"

19 legal lines say "sacrifice any number of" something and then do a thing "that many" or "that
much" times. None of them read, because "that many" pointed back at a count no reader kept. Four
read now: Last-Ditch Effort, Landslide, Malevolent Witchkite, and God-Eternal Bontu's enter
trigger. Bontu's other line, going third from the top of the library, is a separate gap.

**The group.** `sacrificeAnyThenThatMany` runs among the group readers in `composeEffects`.
- **What may be sacrificed** is read by `pluralPermanentKinds`: lands, creatures, artifacts,
  enchantments, planeswalkers, permanents, nonland permanents, tokens and the basic land types, in
  any list. "Other" leaves out the source.
- **What follows** is read with its "that many" marked, as D903 marks it after a damage trigger. It
  runs with the number sacrificed as the event amount, so every "that many" reader already written
  applies: draw, damage, life, tokens, counters.
- **The question** is the controller's, as it resolves, from their own battlefield, nought to all.
- **Refused** when what follows asks a question of its own, because that question would be sized
  before anything was sacrificed. Examples are "discard that many cards" and Scapeshift's "search
  for up to that many". Also refused: an X of its own, or no "that many" at all.

**The bot** sacrifices nothing. What a permanent is worth against a card or a point of damage is
not something it can weigh yet.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The three fixtures read whole, and three near shapes are refused.
- Lands only are offered; two are sacrificed and two cards drawn.
- None chosen: nothing changes.
- Two creatures sacrificed: two damage to the target player.
- "Other permanents": the creature that entered is not offered.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- The count fixed at one.
- Nothing sacrificed.
- "Other" ignored.
- Any kind word accepted.
- The question guard removed: caught by the "discard that many" refusal.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6475 of 6475 pass.

## D1333 — Scapeshift: a question sized by the answer before it

Scapeshift reads whole now: "Sacrifice any number of lands. Search your library for up to that
many land cards, put them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle." D1332 refused it, because
its search is a question of its own, and questions were all worked out before any was answered.

**Questions see the answers so far.** A question worked out as it is asked (`DecisionSpecOf`) now
gets the resolution's answers so far as its context's `decisions`, where they had been empty.
`askOrFinish` works each question out as it is reached, with those answers. Nothing already written
read the empty list, so no existing question changes. The gate's full run is the check on that.

**The search.** `sacrificeAnyThenThatMany` (D1332) takes one following question: a search "for up
to that many". It is read as "any number of", then capped as it is asked at how many permanents the
first answer chose. A library is not changed by what is sacrificed, so asking before the sacrifice
is made gives the same answer. The rest of the effect gets its own answers, without the
sacrifice's, so its "the cards chosen" are the ones found. Any other following question is still
refused. Lich-Knights' Conquest's "Return that many creature cards from your graveyard" is one,
because a creature sacrificed to it could be one of the cards it returns.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The fixture reads whole.
- Two lands sacrificed:
  - the search allows two, and three is refused;
  - two Forests come in tapped;
  - the Swamps go to the graveyard.
- None sacrificed: no search is asked, and the board is unchanged.

D1332's refusal row for this text was removed, because it reads now.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The answers kept out of the context.
- `askOrFinish` working questions out without them.
- The cap removed.
- The rest of the effect given the sacrifice's answer.

Coverage: 17,515 of 31,900 cards (+1 over D1332's 17,514), 40,340 of 59,888 lines (+1).

## D1334 — a permission to cast from the graveyard is not a land drop

Sweep 96001, built at D1326, finished 99 of 100 games. Seed 96041 threw "that card is not in your
hand". A worktree at D1326 replayed it. On turn 53 the bot played a Mountain from its graveyard,
and `playLand`, with no permission to play lands from there, refused.

The offer came from D1287's graveyard casting. A Lurrus-like "cast one permanent spell with mana
value 2 or less from your graveyard" fits a Mountain: a permanent card, mana value 0. The land
branch of `legalActions` then offered the card as a land drop. A land is never cast (CR 305.9).

**The fix.** The land branch skips a card offered only to be cast from the graveyard: flashback,
escape, retrace, aftermath and the permission casts. The land drops out of a graveyard come through
their own entry (`landOnly`): Crucible of Worlds, and Muldrotha's land.

D1335's loop stops it.

graveyard:

- the Mountain is not offered;
- the bot's move is not that land drop, and it applies without a throw.

## D1337 — Remand, Memory Lapse, and a spell returned to its owner's hand

Remand and Memory Lapse are staples, and neither read. The counter read, but its rider sends the
countered card somewhere other than the graveyard, and only D545's exile rider existed.

**The rider.** `counterExileRider` now also takes "If that spell is countered this way, put it into
its owner's hand / on top of its owner's library instead of into that player's graveyard". This
covers Remand, Memory Lapse and Lapse of Certainty. The destination travels on the effect context
as `counteredTo`, as D545's `exileWhenCountered` does. `counterSpell` puts the card there, unless
flashback or a graveyard permission exiles it (CR 702.34a).

**Returned, not countered.** `returnSpellToHand` takes a spell off the stack to its owner's hand. It
is not a counter, so "can't be countered" does not stop it and nothing that watches for a counter
sees one. Flashback still exiles it, and a copy simply ceases to exist. Read for "Return target
spell [you don't control / an opponent controls] to its owner's hand".

"Target spell or creature" and "target spell or permanent" stay unread: Unsubstantiate, Venser,
Brutal Expulsion, Jeskai Revelation. A target that is either a spell or a permanent is a target
kind the engine does not have. Hullbreaker Horror's modes read; its "choose up to one" on a trigger
does not.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests: seat 0 casts Grizzly Bears, and seat 1 answers.
- All three fixtures read whole.
- Remand: the Bears go to seat 0's hand, the stack empties, and Remand draws a card.
- Memory Lapse: the Bears go on top of seat 0's library.
- Returned: the Bears go back to seat 0's hand.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The library sent to the hand.
- The rider ignored.
- The returned spell sent to the graveyard.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6488 of 6488 pass.

## D1338 — "choose up to one —" on a trigger: Hullbreaker Horror

Hullbreaker Horror is on the second staples list, and its trigger did not read: "Whenever you cast
a spell, choose up to one — • Return target spell you don't control to its owner's hand. • Return
target nonland permanent to its owner's hand." D757's modal triggers took "choose one" only. 8
legal cards print "choose up to one" on a trigger.

**The reading.** `modalTriggerFor` takes "choose up to one". No mode at all is a legal answer, and
it is offered as one more mode, "Choose no mode", which does nothing and comes last. The game it
leaves is the one choosing no mode leaves. Where it would have been the one mode left, it is still
offered as a choice, which is right: the player may decline.

The engine's mode choice counts at least one mode, and the stack reads an empty mode list as one
not yet chosen. So a do-nothing mode was the smaller change, against a third meaning for an empty
list.

Hullbreaker Horror and Dreamshackle Geist read whole now. The other six wait on a bullet of their
own: a fight, a perpetual exchange, a Saga, "becomes prepared".

**Tests.** 4 engine tests, on a fixture Horror whose modes are a bounce and a draw:
- It reads whole, with "Choose no mode" last.
- No mode chosen: nothing is returned and nothing drawn.
- The bot answers it: the bounce, aimed at the opponent's Bears and never at its own permanents.
- The draw mode draws.

Faults injected by hand: 1, the no-mode answer removed. Caught by two tests.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6491 of 6491 pass, before the bot test was added.

## D1339 — a target that is a spell or a permanent: Venser and Unsubstantiate

Venser, Shaper Savant, Unsubstantiate, Brutal Expulsion and Jeskai Revelation each point one
target at "target spell or creature" or "target spell or permanent". The engine had no target that
could be either: a spell on the stack and a permanent on the battlefield were different kinds.

**The kind.** `TargetSpec.kind` gains `spell-or-permanent`. In `targeting.ts` the candidate is:
- a spell if it is on the stack, by the spell checks, copies of spells included;
- otherwise a permanent, by every battlefield check: hexproof, shroud, protection.

`legalTargets` lists the stack's spells and then the battlefield. The reader's `filter` narrows the
permanent half to creatures or nonland permanents, and "an opponent controls" narrows both halves.

**The effect.** A spell goes back by D1337's `returnSpellToHand`, and a permanent by the ordinary
bounce. The bot needed nothing new: it already ranks a target by whose it is, for a card on the
stack as for one on the battlefield. The web table offers whatever candidates the engine lists, so
it needed nothing either.

Still unread on their other lines: Fatehold Charm (Empower), Press the Enemy (its free cast), Divide
by Zero ("with mana value 1 or greater", and Learn).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests, on a fixture Unsubstantiate:
- It reads whole, its one target of the new kind.
- With Grizzly Bears on the stack and another on the battlefield, both are offered, and no land is.
- The Bears on the stack go back to their owner's hand, and the stack empties.
- The Bears on the battlefield go back to their owner's hand.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The stack left out of the candidate list.
- A spell refused as a target.
- "Or creature" not checked.
- The spell left on the stack.

## D1340 — Intuition and Gifts Ungiven: a search the opponent splits

Intuition and Gifts Ungiven are on the second staples list, and neither read. Each searches, reveals
what it found, and has an opponent choose where those cards go. Realms Uncharted and Elemental
Teachings print the same shape.

**The reading.** `searchOpponentSplits` reads the whole group, as Fact or Fiction's reader does
(D728):
- The caster searches the library. "Three cards" is exactly three: the search names no quality, so
  it cannot fail to find (CR 701.19b). "Up to four … cards with different names" is nought to
  four, of a card type where one is printed.
- As the opponent's question is reached, the cards found are revealed to the table, and the
  opponent chooses one or two of them (`DecisionZone` `revealed`): the target opponent, or "an
  opponent".
- The chosen cards and the rest go where the card says: hand, graveyard, or onto the battlefield
  tapped. Then the library is shuffled and the reveal ends.

**Different names.** A question may now say its answer's cards must have different names
(`CardsDecisionSpec.distinctNames`). It is carried on the pending question and checked in
`decide`, since no one card is wrong on its own. The candidates are still the whole library.

**The bot.** Searching, it takes its most valuable cards, one of each name. As the opponent, it
hands the caster the least valuable card where the chosen go to hand. Where the chosen go to the
graveyard, it takes the most valuable.

Still unread: Ecological Appreciation (library and graveyard, "mana value X or less") and Threats
Undetected (different powers).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both fixtures read whole.
- Intuition:
  - exactly three are asked for;
  - the opponent chooses from those three;
  - the Forest chosen goes to hand, and the other two to the graveyard.
- Gifts Ungiven:
  - up to four;
  - two Forests are refused, "different names";
  - four different are taken;
  - the two the opponent chose go to the graveyard and the other two to hand.
- The bot as the opponent gives Intuition's caster the Grizzly Bears, the least valuable of the
  three.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- The names check off.
- The flag not carried onto the question.
- The bot's pick reversed.
- The two destinations swapped.
- Nothing revealed.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6500 of 6500 pass. Web: typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,533 of 31,900 cards (+4 over D1339's 17,529), 40,367 of 59,888 lines (+4).

## D1341 — Isochron Scepter: a copy of the imprinted card, cast for nothing

Isochron Scepter is on the second staples list. Its imprint has read since D717. Its ability did
not: "{2}, {T}: You may copy the exiled card. If you do, you may cast the copy without paying its
mana cost." Spellbinder's trigger prints the same two sentences.

**The reading.** `castImprintedCopy` finds the card this permanent imprinted as it is now: an
`imprintedOn` with this permanent's id and its current `objectSeq`. An imprint from before the
permanent last changed zones does not count (CR 400.7). The copy is made in exile by D936's
`copyCardInExile` and offered as a free cast (`pendingOfferedCast`), as cipher's copy is.

Declining the cast leaves the same game as declining to copy, so the two "you may"s are one offer.
The imprinted card never leaves exile, and the copy ceases to exist once it has resolved
(CR 707.12).

Elite Arcanist ("{X} … X is the mana value of the exiled card") stays unread.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests, on a fixture Scepter and an instant that deals 3 damage:
- It reads whole.
- Cast from hand, its imprint exiles the instant and links it to the Scepter as it now is.
- Activated:
  - a copy is offered, not the card;
  - cast at the opponent, the copy deals 3;
  - the card stays in exile, and the copy is gone.
- An imprint from before the Scepter last moved copies nothing.

Faults injected by hand: 2, both caught.
- The object check removed.
- The card itself offered in place of a copy.

## D1342 — mana as much as what was sacrificed: Priest of Yawgmoth and Sacrifice

"Add an amount of {B} equal to the sacrificed artifact's mana value" did not read on a mana ability
or on a spell. D1139 had read "an amount of … equal to ~'s power", but nothing counted the
permanent a cost had sacrificed.

**On a mana ability.** `AbilityDef.producesPerSacrificed` ('power' or 'manaValue') says the
ability's mana is made once for each point of the sacrificed permanent, as it last was.
`producedBy` takes that permanent's stats, and `activate` passes the ones it already records as the
sacrifice is paid (`sacrificedStats`). The result is "two {B} for a two-mana artifact".

A spending restriction refuses the line, because restricted mana is made only by the auto-payer
(D595). This leaves Slobad unread.

**Never the auto-payer's.** No reader of the ability needs a guard. Asked with nothing sacrificed,
`producedBy` makes nothing, and the auto-payer does not offer a source that makes nothing. A skip
written for it was removed when its fault check showed it changed nothing.

**On a spell.** The spell Sacrifice's "Add an amount of {B} equal to the sacrificed creature's
mana value" reads off the stack object's `sacrificedStats`, which its additional cost records.

Priest of Yawgmoth, Red Priest of Yawgmoth, Illuminor Szeras and Sacrifice read whole now. Soldevi
Adnate waits on "Sacrifice a black or artifact creature" as a cost.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The fixtures read whole, with `producesPerSacrificed` 'manaValue'.
- The Priest, sacrificing a three-mana artifact:
  - it is not an auto-payer source;
  - three {B} are made;
  - the artifact goes to the graveyard.
- Sacrifice, sacrificing Hill Giant: four {B}.

Faults injected by hand: 4, three caught.
- The stats not passed: caught.
- One mana however much was sacrificed: caught.
- The spell counting toughness: caught.
- The auto-payer skip removed: not caught, for the reason above.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6507 of 6507 pass.

"… a red or white creature", "… a nontoken creature", "… a noncreature artifact" or "… a nonland
permanent". 16 legal lines print one of these, and 14 of them did not read.

**Colours.** "Sacrifice a/another COLOUR [or COLOUR] creature" sets `sacrificeColours`. That field
is D686's, written for Natural Order's spell cost, and `sacrificeOptions` already honoured it for
any cost, so no engine change was needed.

**Kinds.** `AbilityCost.sacrifice` gains `nontoken-creature`, `nontoken-artifact` and
`noncreature-artifact`, answered by `sacrificeOptions` off the live characteristics and named in a
refusal by `sacrificeWords`. "A nonland permanent" one at a time is D732's counted kind, now read
singly too (Magmaw).

Five lines read now, four of them whole cards. Still unread:
- the five Heralds' "a green creature, a white creature, and a blue creature", three sacrifices in
  one cost;
- Soldevi Adnate's "a black or artifact creature", a colour or a type;
- three whose other text does not read.

## D1344 — Mind's Desire and Urza: a card exiled to be played for nothing

Urza, Lord High Artificer is on the second staples list: "{5}: Shuffle your library, then exile the
top card. Until end of turn, you may play that card without paying its mana cost." D583's
play-from-exile reader left "without paying its mana cost" unread, as a different cost, and two
compile pins held it there. "Shuffle your library" as a sentence of its own did not read either.

**The permission.** `playFromExile` gains `free`. `exileTopToPlay` sets it where the permission

## D1345 — Najeela: whenever anybody's Warrior attacks

Najeela, the Blade-Blossom is on the second staples list. Its activated ability already read. Its
trigger did not: "Whenever a Warrior attacks, you may have its controller create a 1/1 white
Warrior creature token that's tapped and attacking."

**Anybody's Warrior.** D635's "Whenever a Dragon you control attacks" now also takes the type
without "you control": an `attacks` trigger `of: 'any'` with the subtype.

**Its controller's token.** `attackingTokenEffect` takes "have its controller create …". The
tokens go to the attacking creature's controller (the trigger's subject), and attack whom it
attacks. The "you may" is the trigger controller's, read by the ordinary optional wrapper.

**A fault from D1183.** `attackingTokenEffect`'s regex literals had been escaped twice: the
trailing full stop was never stripped, and "create 2 tapped and attacking …" in digits never read.
Both are fixed, and a search of the engine's other regex literals found no more.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- A fixture Najeela reads whole, an `attacks` trigger of any Warrior. A count in digits reads.
- My Warrior attacks: I am asked, and on yes I get a tapped token attacking the same player.
- An opponent's Warrior attacks: I am asked, and the token is theirs, attacking me.
- Declined: no token.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- "Of any" narrowed back to "you".
- The token given to the trigger's controller.
- The digits fix reverted.

## D1347 — Ad Nauseam: a process repeated as many times as the player says

Ad Nauseam is a cEDH staple: "Reveal the top card of your library and put that card into your hand.
You lose life equal to its mana value. You may repeat this process any number of times." D816's
Dark Confidant clause read the first two sentences. The repeat did not, because the plan asks
every question of a resolution from a list fixed before it starts.

**The reading.** `revealRepeatedly` is a fixed list of 60 questions, as D730's punisher rounds are
a fixed list of 40:
- Each question does one reveal as it is reached (`onReach`): the card into hand and its mana value
  lost.
- Each then asks "Reveal another" or "Stop".
- Each after the first is asked only if the answer before it was "Reveal another"
  (`askOnlyIfChosen`), and only while the library has a card. A "Stop" ends the chain, because it
  stays the latest answer with a word for every question after it.
- The last question's "Reveal another" is the effect's own reveal.
- The life is lost card by card. A player at 0 loses as the spell finishes resolving (CR 704.3).

Sixty is a ceiling, as the punisher's forty is: past it the process stops being offered, a known
limit no real game reaches.

**The bot** goes again while it has more than 10 life and a library.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests, with the library's top set to Hill Giant, Forest, Hill Giant:
- A fixture Ad Nauseam reads whole.
- Step by step:
  - the Giant comes before the first question, at 16 life;
  - "Reveal another" brings the Forest, still 16;
  - again brings the second Giant, 12;
  - "Stop" ends it, the stack empty and the fourth card still in the library.
- The bot reveals until it is at 10 or less, and stops above 5.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The chain no longer stopped by "Stop".
- The bot never stopping.
- No life lost.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6524 of 6524 pass.

Coverage: 17,553 of 31,900 cards (+1 over D1346's 17,552), 40,393 of 59,888 lines (+1).

## D1349 — Approach of the Second Sun: the second cast from hand wins

Approach of the Second Sun is on the second staples list: "If this spell was cast from your hand
and you've cast another spell named Approach of the Second Sun this game, you win the game.
Otherwise, put Approach of the Second Sun into its owner's library seventh from the top and you
gain 7 life."

**What the game remembers.** `GameState.spellNamesCastThisGame` counts each seat's spells by name
for the whole game, recorded where the turn's cast counts are and never cleared. "Cast from your
hand" is the stack object's `castFrom`, D607's.

**The reading.** `approachOfTheSecondSun` takes the two sentences as one:
- Cast from hand, with this name cast twice or more by its controller (this one and another), every
  opponent loses the game.
- Otherwise the card goes seventh from the top (the bottom of a shorter library) and the life is
  gained.

**A spell that moves itself** (CR 608.2n). The resolved spell's exit sent the card to its graveyard
whether or not it was still on the stack. A spell whose effect put the card somewhere was then
moved again. The exit now runs only while the card is on the stack.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- A fixture reads whole.
- The first cast: seventh from the top, 27 life, and the name counted once.
- The second copy cast out of exile, not the hand: no win, 34 life.
- The second cast from hand: the opponent loses the game, and the caster is still in it.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The stack check in the exit removed.
- A win on the first cast.
- The count not kept.
- "From your hand" ignored.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6531 of 6531 pass, before the exile test was added.

## D1350 — Scroll Rack: cards from hand traded for the top of the library

Scroll Rack is on the second staples list: "{1}, {T}: Exile any number of cards from your hand face
down. Put that many cards from the top of your library into your hand. Then look at the exiled
cards and put them on top of your library in any order."

**The reading.** `scrollRack` reads the three sentences as one effect:
- **One question.** The cards from hand, nought to all of them, in the order they go back, the first
  chosen on top. The prompt says so, and the answer's order is kept.
- **The cards that were on top** go to hand. They are put there, not drawn, so nothing that counts
  draws sees them.
- **The chosen cards** go on top in that order.
- **The face-down exile between the steps** is not modelled. Nothing can happen between them, so it
  has no game in it.

**The bot** chooses nothing: what to put back is a plan it cannot make. Activated by it, the Rack
costs {1} and changes nothing.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- A fixture reads whole.
- With Hill Giant and Grizzly Bears in hand, both chosen, Bears first:
  - the library's top two are the Bears and then the Giant;
  - the two cards that were there are in hand.
- None chosen: the hand is unchanged.

Faults injected by hand: 2, both caught.
- The order reversed.
- The chosen cards put on top before the top cards were taken, which hands them straight back.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6535 of 6535 pass.

## D1351 — Flash: a creature put in, kept for its cost less {2} or sacrificed

Flash is on the second staples list: "You may put a creature card from your hand onto the
battlefield. If you do, sacrifice it unless you pay its mana cost reduced by up to {2}."

**The reading.** `flashIn` asks two questions:
- **The creature card**, or none.
- **The price.** As this question is reached the creature is put onto the battlefield (`onReach`),
  so it enters before anything is asked. The question is then worked out from the first answer
  (D1333): pay the creature's mana cost with up to {2} of its generic taken off (`reducedCostText`),
  or sacrifice it. A cost the engine cannot pay, an X, offers only the sacrifice. With nothing put
  in, nothing is asked.

The reader takes "reduced by {2}" as well as "reduced by up to {2}", since the clause splitter
drops the words "up to".

**A price worked out from an earlier answer.** D1333 gave a question the answers so far, but only
where it is asked (`askOrFinish`). The payment of a priced answer, its fallback, and the bot's
preferred answer each worked the question out again without them, so Flash's price paid nothing.
All of them now pass the answers given.

**The bot** puts nothing in. When the free creature is worth its price is not a judgement it
makes.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests, Flash with two Hill Giants in hand and two Mountains:
- It reads whole.
- A Giant put in:
  - it is on the battlefield before the price is asked;
  - the price is "Pay {1}{R}";
  - paid, it stays, and both Mountains are tapped.
- Not paid: it is sacrificed.
- Nothing put in: nothing is asked and nothing moves.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The payment working the price out without the answers.
- No sacrifice.
- No {2} off.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6539 of 6539 pass.

## D1352 — Protean Hulk: a search bounded by total mana value

Protean Hulk is on the second staples list: "When Protean Hulk dies, search your library for any
number of creature cards with total mana value 6 or less, put them onto the battlefield, then
shuffle." 22 legal lines print "with total mana value N or less", and none read.

**The bound.** A question may now say its answer's cards must total at most some mana value
(`CardsDecisionSpec.totalManaValueAtMost`). It is carried on the pending question and checked in
`decide`, beside D1340's different names, because no one card is wrong on its own. The candidates
are still every creature card in the library.

**The search.** The library search reader takes "<cards> with total mana value N or less" as the
plain count and kind, with the bound on the question.

**The bot** answers within the bound: the costliest cards first, each taken while the total still
allows it. Its default would have been refused.

Still unread: the targeted spellings ("any number of target … with total mana value"), returns
from a graveyard, and an X total.

## D1354 — targets bounded by their total mana value: Patch Up

D1352 bounded a question by total mana value. The targeted spelling did not read: Patch Up's "Return
up to three target creature cards with total mana value 3 or less from your graveyard to the
battlefield", March from the Tomb, Kairi's mode.

**The bound on a target spec.** `TargetSpec.totalManaValueAtMost` is checked in `checkTargets`
across the targets the spec takes, beside D1216's `sameOwner`: a cast or a trigger aimed past it is
refused. The bot stays inside it on both of its target paths, taking each target while the total
still allows it:
- a spell's or an ability's targets (`chooseTargets`);
- a trigger's, put on the stack (`auto:choose`).

**The reading.** The graveyard return readers want the phrase to end in "cards" before "from your
graveyard", so a bound in the middle stopped the line before it reached `targetSpecFrom`. So
`readEffect` reads the clause without the bound first, and puts the bound on the one target spec
that takes more than one. Any other shape falls through to the readers below, D1353's untargeted
return among them, which reads the bound itself.

Patch Up reads whole now. Scout for Survivors waits on "Put a +1/+1 counter on each of them", and
March from the Tomb on its Ally type.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests, with two Grizzly Bears and a 1-drop in the graveyard:
- A fixture reads whole, the bound on its target spec of three.
- Two Bears (4) are refused as targets. A Bears and the 1-drop (3) return, and the other Bears
  stays.
- A fixture enters trigger's targets, chosen by the bot, total 3 or less.
- The bot's cast is aimed within the total, and the engine accepts it.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The check off.
- The cast path's bot ignoring the total.
- The trigger path's bot ignoring the total.

## D1355 — "Put a counter on each of them" after a sentence that aimed at several

"Put a +1/+1 counter on each of them", "… a stun counter …", "… two stun counters …" follow a
sentence that targets several objects on 27 legal lines, and none read. On 18 cards it was the only
unread line. D723's "put a counter on it" took one target only.

**The rule.** In `composeEffects`, the clause reads when exactly one earlier sentence aims at cards,
with one spec that takes more than one. Each card target that sentence took, still on the
battlefield, gets the counters. Sentences that aim only at players do not count (Homesickness's

meaning of their own (`RULES_COUNTERS`) is refused, as everywhere.

## D1356 — "Any number of target …"

"Any number of target creatures", "… target creature cards from your graveyard", "… target
nonland permanents you control" are printed on about 160 legal lines. The target reader knew
"up to one", "up to two", "one or two" and the rest, and not this one, so none read unless a card
had a hand-written spec (Fireball's "any number of targets", the divided-damage family).

**The rule.** "Any number of" is one more entry in `TARGET_QUANTIFIERS`: optional, with the same
ceiling of 99 Fireball uses (`ANY_NUMBER_OF_TARGETS`), so the graveyard reader and every reader
that shares `TARGET_QUANTIFIER_PREFIX` get it at once. With D1354's total it reads March from the
Tomb: "any number of target Ally creature cards with total mana value 8 or less".

**The bot.** It fills a spec to its count, which is wrong for a count that is only a ceiling. The
new `TargetSpec.botWhileSameSide` tells it to take the best candidate and go on only while the next
is on the same side of its ranking as the first. So "destroy any number of target creatures" takes
the opponents' creatures and stops before its own. When the first is its own permanent on a spec
not marked friendly, it takes that one only (Scapegoat saves one creature, not the board). Its own
graveyard cards are not that case, so March from the Tomb takes as many as the total allows.

Read whole now: March from the Tomb, Scapegoat, Bone Harvest, Gravepurge, Forever Young, Footbottom
Feast, Frantic Salvage, Iname, Life Aspect, Divine Resilience, and others. Strive, printed beside
many of these lines ("costs {2}{U} more to cast for each target beyond the first"), is still unread.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Three fixtures read whole, each spec with a ceiling of 99, optional, and the bot advice.
- Three cards come back within a total of 5; all four (6) are refused.
- The bot's "destroy any number of target creatures" takes both of its opponent's creatures and
  neither of its own.
- The bot's "return any number of target creatures you control" takes one; its March takes more
  than one, within the total.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- No same-side stop.
- No stop after one own permanent.
- The quantifier left out.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6557 of 6557 pass.

Coverage: 17,582 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1355's 17,573), 40,435 of 59,888 lines (+15).

## D1357 — Strive

hand-written card, and only generic.

**The rule.** The line is read into `extraTargetCost` (the generic part) and the new
`CardScript.extraTargetColoured` (one entry per coloured symbol). Where the spell is cast, the
symbols are added once for each target after the first, to the coloured mana the board adds (the

ability word reads too, which is Fireball's own cost line. Hybrid, Phyrexian and X symbols are not
read, and a line with one still refuses the card.

extra target, rather than as many as D1356 would let it take and then a cast it cannot pay for.

Read whole now: Aerial Formation, Ajani's Presence, Blinding Flare, Colossal Heroics, Consign to
Dust, Cruel Feeding, Desperate Stand, Kiora's Dismissal, Phalanx Formation, Rouse the Mob. The

## D1358 — X damage divided as you choose

"~ deals X damage divided as you choose among any number of targets" is printed on 21 legal cards
(Rolling Thunder, Hail of Arrows, Rock Slide, Conflagrate, Fire Covenant and others). D749 read the
fixed amounts, and `TargetSpec.divided` was a number fixed when the card was read, so the X shape
had nowhere to go. D1055 pinned it as refused for that reason.

**The rule.** A new `TargetSpec.dividedX`: the spec still carries `divided` (as 0), so everything that
asks "does this divide" still sees it, and the amount is the X announced. `dividedAmountOf(spec, x)`
gives it, and `checkDivision` takes the X from the cast. An X of nought divides nothing, so the spell
may be cast with no targets and no division. The reader takes the X only where something pays one
(`xPayable`, D1055), and only among "any number of": Fire Covenant's X is life paid, not mana, so it
stays unread.

**The bot** divides the X it casts with (`xDefault`, else `xMax`), using the same three ways of dividing as for a fixed amount.

**The web table** asks for X first, as it does for every X spell, then spends one point per tap up
to that X. `dividedAmount(play, x)` takes the X; the target prompt, the tap reducer and Cast read it.

Read whole now: Rolling Thunder, Hail of Arrows, Rock Slide. The rest have another line unread:
an additional cost (Infernal Harvest, Nahiri's Sacrifice), flashback paid in cards (Conflagrate), a
second sentence about the damage dealt (Aurelia's Fury, Ghired's Belligerence), or an X defined by
the board (Volcanic Wind, Jaws of Stone).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests and 1 web test:
- The fixture reads whole, with `divided: 0, dividedX: true`. The same text on a card with no {X}
  is refused.
- X=3 divided two and one: one Grizzly Bears dies and the other has 1 damage. A division of four
  is refused.
- X=0 is cast with no targets.
- The bot casts it for X=3 off four Mountains, with a division that adds up to 3, and the engine
  accepts the cast.
- Web: X set to 3, then three taps send the cast with `x: 3` and `division: [2, 1]`, and Cast pressed
  at two of three sends nothing.

The D1055 pin that refused this shape now uses a listed count ("one, two, or three target creatures") with X, which is still refused.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- The division check ignoring X.
- No rule for X=0.
- The bot ignoring X.
- The `xPayable` guard removed.
- The web tap reducer ignoring X.

## D1359 — Tokens for what "any number of target" destroyed or exiled

"Destroy any number of target creatures. For each creature destroyed this way, its controller
creates a 4/4 red Dragon creature token with flying." (Descent of the Dragons), and Hour of Need's
exile with a Sphinx. D704 read Terastodon's version, but its glue knew "up to three target" and not
"any number of target", and it was for destroy only.

**The rule.**
- "Any number of target" joins D682's destroy glue.
- An exile glue is added, joining only the sentence "For each creature (or permanent) exiled this
  way, its controller creates …". Other sentences about cards exiled this way read as they did.
- What left the battlefield now also records whether it was exiled (`toExile`, beside D704's
  `toGraveyard`). A token exiled ceases to exist there and was still exiled (CR 111.7).

So an indestructible creature that survives Descent gives no Dragon, and the same creature exiled
by Hour of Need gives a Sphinx.

Read whole now: Descent of the Dragons, Hour of Need. Curse of the Swine's "Exile X target
creatures" is still unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Both fixtures read whole. "Exile any number of target creatures. You gain 1 life for each
  creature exiled this way" is still refused.
- Destroyed: one Dragon each for the two controllers whose Grizzly Bears died, and none for the
  indestructible Wall, which is still on the battlefield.
- Exiled: a Sphinx for each, the Wall included (one for seat 0, two for seat 1).

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- "Exiled" dropped from the token reader.
- The exile glue removed.
- "Any number of target" taken out of the destroy glue.
- "Exiled" read as "put into a graveyard".

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6568 of 6568 pass.

## D1360 — Several chosen targets, and persist or undying handed out

Two small readers.

**"Choose any number of target creatures."** D1146 read "Choose target creature." as a sentence
that names a target and does nothing else, for the sentences after it to borrow. The plural forms
("Choose up to two target creatures", "Choose any number of target creatures you control") were
unread. They read now, creatures only, and only where the whole phrase reads. "Controlled by the
same player", "that share no creature types" and "with equal toughness" are conditions on the set
that the target reader cannot express, so those cards are still refused. Nature's Panoply ("Put a
+1/+1 counter on each of them", D1355) reads whole.

**"Target creature gains undying until end of turn."** Persist and undying are dies triggers, so
granting one is D1062's quoted-grant path with the same trigger a printed persist or undying has
(`comesBackWithACounter`), handed to the creature until end of turn. Undying Evil and Antler
Skulkin read whole. Exactly one "until end of turn" is required, as in D1062. Rhys's trigger and
Cauldron Haze's "each of those creatures" stay unread, because only a one-sentence spell or an
activated ability carries the granted trigger.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Three fixtures read whole. "Choose two target creatures controlled by the same player" and a
  grant with no duration are refused.
- Both chosen Bears get the +1/+1 counter.
- Undying: the Bears comes back with a +1/+1 counter and does not come back a second time.
- Persist: back with a -1/-1 counter. The other Bears, which was not granted it, stays dead.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The plural reader removed.
- Undying read as persist.
- Nothing granted.
- No duration check.

One fault run was cut short by a pipe and left the third fault in place; the full run found it,
and the file was restored from the backup before the gate.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6572 of 6572 pass.

## D1361 — Voting

"Will of the council — Starting with you, each player votes for time or knowledge." Voting
(CR 701.38) is printed on 36 legal lines and had no support at all.

**The question.** One choice question with the two words, asked of each living player in turn
order **starting with the controller** (CR 701.38a), so a player who votes later has seen the
votes before theirs. That is a new `who`, `each-player-from-you`: `each-player` starts from the
active player, which is the wrong order for a vote cast on someone else's turn.

**What follows it** (`voteGroup`). The sentences after the vote are read one at a time, with
the two words known to the readers:
- "for each strength vote" is a count, in any sentence that already reads with a "for each"
  ("Put two +1/+1 counters on ~ for each sprout vote", "You gain 3 life for each harvest vote").
- "For each evidence vote, investigate." does the effect that many times.
- "If time gets more votes, …" and "If knowledge gets more votes or the vote is tied, …" compare
  the two counts. The vote reader handles these itself, because on a trigger a leading "if" is
  intervening, and this one is counted as the effect resolves.

Each sentence must read whole with no target and no question of its own. That is why Tyrant's
Choice (each opponent sacrifices) is refused. The composer cannot place a later question's answers
after an each-player question when the card is read, and the sacrifice would be asked whichever
side won.

**The bot** votes the first word. None of these cards says which word is better for whom, and a
person answers for themselves.

Read whole now: Plea for Power, Coercive Portal, Lieutenants of the Guard, Orchard Elemental.
Still unread:
- Expropriate, whose money vote chooses a permanent for each voter.
- Secret council, where votes are revealed together.
- Votes for a permanent or a player.
- Tyrant's Choice and the others that ask a question after the vote.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Three fixtures read whole, the vote one `each-player-from-you` question with the two words. A
  sacrifice after the vote, and a count of a word nobody votes on, are refused.
- A tie goes to "knowledge or the vote is tied": three cards. Two votes for time: an extra turn
  for the controller and no cards.
- Cast on the opponent's turn, the controller still votes first.
- "Two +1/+1 counters for each sprout vote, 3 life for each harvest vote" gives 2 counters and 3
  life for one of each. Two evidence votes make two Clues and no Treasure.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- The vote asked in turn order rather than from the controller.
- A tie not counted.
- "For each" done once.
- No vote count.
- A count of any word allowed.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6576 of 6576 pass. Web typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,604 of 31,900 cards (+4 over D1360's 17,600), 40,480 of 59,888 lines (+5).

## D1362 — A free shield pressed no more than the damage coming

Sweep 100001 (D1351 build) finished 99 of 100 games. Seed 100010 looped: 2,000 moves in one
declare-blockers step on turn 46, 1,000 of them Outrider en-Kor's "{0}: The next 1 damage that
would be dealt to ~ this turn is dealt to target creature you control instead", aimed at a
Blind-Spot Giant.

D1335 marked the en-Kor's ability as damage prevention, so the bot uses it only while damage is
coming. In combat damage is coming, and each press put up one more shield. The bot's search saw
each one as worth having, so it pressed, passed, let the shield resolve, and pressed again.

**The rule.** A prevention ability is not activated once the shields its source already has up
cover the total power of every creature attacking this seat. That total is the most combat damage
there is to stop. Spells (a Fog) are unchanged, and so is the D1335 rule for when no damage is
coming.

**Tests.** 1 engine test. Outrider en-Kor blocks a 3/3 Hill Giant, which would kill it. The
declare-blockers step is played out for 60 moves, the bot's presses and passes and the opponent's
passes. The bot presses at least once and at most 3 times. Without the rule it pressed 15 times in
the same 60 moves.

Faults injected by hand: 1, caught (the cap removed). A count of the source's activations still on
the stack was written and then removed: the bot never presses again over its own shield on the
stack, so no test reached it.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6577 of 6577 pass.

## D1363 — Expropriate

"Council's dilemma — Starting with you, each player votes for time or money. For each time vote,
take an extra turn after this one. For each money vote, choose a permanent owned by the voter and
gain control of it. Exile Expropriate." On the second staples list since it was drawn up.

D1361's vote reads every sentence but the money one, which asks the caster a question about each
money voter. A question after an each-player vote could not be placed when the card is read. Here
its number depends on the votes.

**The rule.** "For each <word> vote, choose a permanent owned by the voter and gain control of it"
adds eight questions after the vote (`MAX_VOTERS`, more than a pod seats), all asked of the
caster. Each is written as a function of the answers so far (`DecisionSpecOf`, D1333). The k-th is
about the k-th player who voted that word, with candidates from every battlefield owned by that
player. It is skipped where there is no such voter, so it is answered empty and the positions do
not move. Each permanent chosen comes under the caster's control for good. One such sentence per
card, because its answers are the only card answers the vote's effect reads.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The card reads whole, with nine questions: the vote and eight.
- Time and money: the caster is asked to choose among the permanents seat 1 owns, takes the
  Grizzly Bears, gets one extra turn, and Expropriate is exiled.
- Two time votes: two extra turns and no question.
- The caster's own money vote asks about the caster's own permanents.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- Any permanent offered.
- The question tied to any voter rather than the money voters.
- No control change.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6581 of 6581 pass.

Staples: the second list is at 123 of 125. Food Chain, Doomsday and Castle Garenbrig remain (the last
on the first list).

## D1364 — "Where X is the total mana value of …"

"This spell costs {X} less to cast, where X is the total mana value of noncreature artifacts you
control" (Metalwork Colossus), "… of Dragons you control" (Earthquake Dragon), "… of historic
permanents you control" (Excalibur, Sword of Eden), "… of noncreature enchantments you control"
(Nyxborn Behemoth). D1076 read "the total power of creatures you control" for Ghalta, but not a
total of mana values.

**The rule.** `totalAmong` also reads "the total mana value of <group>", for any group `massScope`
reads. Each permanent counts its printed cost (CR 202.3, X as 0), and a face-down permanent counts
nothing (CR 708.2). It is reached through `boardCount`, so a "where X is" cost reduction and an
"equal to" amount both get it.

Read whole now: Metalwork Colossus, Earthquake Dragon, Excalibur. Nyxborn Behemoth has its
sacrifice ability left.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The fixture reads whole.
- Noncreature artifacts printed {3} and {X}{4} take 7 off; an artifact creature does not count.
- The {11} spell is offered off four lands with those two out, and not off three. With no
  artifacts it is not offered off four.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- A count rather than a total.
- Each value off by one.
- The reader removed.

## D1365 — "As long as enchanted permanent is a creature, it gets …"

An Aura that enchants any permanent and helps it only while it is a creature: Akki War Paint, Favor
of Jukai, Gift of Wrath, the Runes, and others, 16 legal lines. D814 read "As long as enchanted
creature is red, it …" but not the permanent form.

**The rule.** The line is one more host-conditional part of the Aura's bonus (`hostConditionalParts`),
with a new `onlyKind` word, `creature`. On a creature the bonus applies as usual. On a permanent that
is not a creature nothing applies. That matters for keywords: indestructible or hexproof on an
artifact would change the game. The same helpful-only rule as D814 holds, so Clawing Torment's
"-1/-1 and can't block" and Short Circuit's "loses flying" are not read.

Read whole now: Akki War Paint, Favor of Jukai, Gift of Wrath. The Runes still have their second
line unread ("As long as enchanted permanent is an Equipment, it has 'Equipped creature has …'").

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- The fixture reads whole.
- On a Grizzly Bears: 4/4 with menace. On an artifact that is not a creature: no menace.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- No creature filter.
- Every permanent counted as a creature.
- The reader removed.

## D1366 — "As long as you control a Jace planeswalker"

Twenty legal lines condition a creature on a planeswalker of one type: Jace's Sentinel, Dovin's
Automaton, Renegade Firebrand, Guardian of the Great Conduit, the planeswalker decks' creatures. For
17 of them it was the card's only unread line. `boardCondition` read "you control a Wizard" and "a
Vehicle", but not "a Jace planeswalker".

**The rule.** A capitalised word followed by "planeswalker" is a planeswalker type (CR 205.3j), asked
of the type line of a planeswalker the player controls. The leading form ("As long as you control a
Jace planeswalker, ~ gets +1/+0") and the trailing form ("~ gets +2/+2 as long as you control a
Garruk planeswalker") both read, because both go through this condition.

18 of the 20 lines read now. The two left are inside an emblem (Gideon of the Trials) and a granted
ability (Lukka).

- Any planeswalker counting: caught.
- The reader removed: caught.
- The type left off the condition (the subtype asked of any permanent) passed. No permanent but a

## D1367 — Doomsday

"Search your library and graveyard for five cards and exile the rest. Put the chosen cards on top
of your library in any order. You lose half your life, rounded up." On the second staples list.

**The reading** (`doomsdayPile`), three questions:
- The library cards, as a search. At least as many as the graveyard cannot supply (five minus its
  size), at most five.
- The graveyard cards: exactly what makes five, or the whole graveyard if it has fewer. Skipped when
  the library gave five.
- The order. This is Ponder's question (`chosenGoTo: 'top'`, D651): every card picked, the first
  picked becomes the top card.

As the order question is reached, everything else in the library and graveyard is exiled and the
graveyard picks go onto the library, so the cards looked at are exactly the pile. The exile is run
again as the spell finishes. That does nothing by then, but it covers an empty pile, where the
order question is never asked. Half the life, rounded up, is lost last.

**One engine change.** Every question took out the cards the same seat had already chosen in the
resolution, so "each player sacrifices" asked twice cannot name one creature twice. Doomsday's
order question is about exactly those cards. The new `CardsDecisionSpec.again` lets a question
offer them.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The card reads whole, as three questions.
- Four library cards and one of two graveyard cards: the library question asks for 3 to 5. Once
  the graveyard pick is in, the library holds just the five and the other graveyard card is
  exiled. The order given is the library's order. The graveyard holds only Doomsday. Life goes
  20 to 10.
- With an empty graveyard: exactly five from the library, no graveyard question, the order as
  given, and 7 life loses 4.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- `again` ignored.
- Nothing exiled as the order is reached.
- The library minimum ignoring the graveyard.
- Half the life rounded down.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6591 of 6591 pass. Web typecheck clean.

(Castle Garenbrig left).

## D1368 — Exile until a kind of card, and cast it free

"Exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card. You may cast that card
without paying its mana cost." (Nico Minoru, Q, Your Illustrious Host), "Target opponent exiles cards
from the top of their library until they exile an instant or sorcery card. You may cast that card
…" (Chaos Wand), and "that player exiles …" on a combat-damage trigger (Dazzling Sphinx). Cascade's
walk (`cascadeFrom`) did this only for the caster's own library, and only with a mana value bound.

**The rule** (`untilCastable`, `exileUntilOffered`):
- The library is the controller's, the target's, or, on a combat-damage trigger, the hit player's.
- The kind is any phrase the library search reads (`libraryFilter`).
- Cards are exiled one at a time from the top until one of the kind turns up.
- That card is offered to the controller free through the ordinary offered cast
  (`pendingOfferedCast`), so the cast's choices are the player's. A card the opponent owns goes to
  that opponent's graveyard once it resolves.
- With "Then … put the exiled cards that weren't cast this way on the bottom … in a random order",
  the rest go to the bottom, and so does the hit if it is declined. Without that sentence everything
  stays exiled (the offer's `stays`).

Read whole now: Nico Minoru, Runaway; Q, Your Illustrious Host; Chaos Wand; Dazzling Sphinx. Gríma
prints its own name as "Grima" in the trigger, so its trigger does not match. The Caretaker and
Strago and Relm each have another clause.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- Both fixtures read whole. The opponent is a target.
- The opponent's first sorcery is offered to the caster for nothing. Cast, it gains the caster 3
  life and goes to its owner's graveyard, and the cards above it go to the bottom of that library.
- On combat damage, the card offered comes from the library of the player hit.
- Declined with the bottom sentence, the hit goes back into the library. Without it, the hit and
  everything above it stay exiled.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- Always the controller's library.
- Any card counted as the hit.
- Nothing sent to the bottom.
- A declined hit never staying.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6595 of 6595 pass.

## D1370 — "Sacrifice it unless it escaped"

Uro, Titan of Nature's Wrath; Kroxa, Titan of Death's Hunger; Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury: "When ~
enters, sacrifice it unless it escaped." Three heavily played cards, and for Uro and Phlage the
only unread line.

**The rule.** The stack object has known since D577 that a spell was cast with escape
(`StackObject.escaped`). The permanent did not, and by the time the enter trigger resolves the
stack object is gone. A new marker, `ESCAPED`, is put on the permanent as it arrives, the same way
surge, kicker and squad are remembered. "Sacrifice it unless it escaped" sacrifices the permanent
unless the marker is there. If it has already left the battlefield, nothing happens. A titan cast
from hand, or put onto the battlefield any other way, is sacrificed.

Read whole now: Uro, Phlage. Kroxa's other trigger ("each opponent discards a card, then each
opponent who didn't discard a nonland card this way loses 3 life") is still unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The fixture reads whole.
- Cast from hand, it is sacrificed as it enters.
- Cast with escape from the graveyard, it stays.

Faults injected by hand: 2, both caught.
- The escape not remembered.
- Never sacrificed.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6601 of 6601 pass.

## D1372 — "Mill three cards. You may put … into your hand. If you don't, …"

## D1374 — Tribute

"Tribute 2 (As this creature enters, an opponent of your choice may put two +1/+1 counters on it.)
When ~ enters, if tribute wasn't paid, …" Eleven legal cards from Born of the Gods, none read
before.

**The rule.**
- Tribute N is an as-it-enters choice (CR 702.104a), read the way riot and unleash are
  (`entersChoice: 'tribute'`): a yes-or-no asked of an opponent as the creature spell resolves,
  before the creature moves.
- Paid, the N +1/+1 counters and a `TRIBUTED` marker go on as it arrives.
- "If tribute wasn't paid" is the trigger's intervening condition on the marker's absence.

Two simplifications, stated:
- "An opponent of your choice" is asked of the next opponent in turn order. In a duel that is the
  only opponent. In a pod, which opponent is not offered as a choice.
- A tribute creature put onto the battlefield without being cast was asked nothing, so its tribute
  was not paid.

Read whole now: 10 of the 11 (Fanatic of Xenagos, Nessian Demolok, Nessian Wilds Ravager, Oracle of
Bones, Ornitharch, Pharagax Giant, Shrike Harpy, Siren of the Fanged Coast, Snake of the Golden
Grove, Thunder Brute).

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- The fixture reads whole.
- The opponent is asked as the spell resolves. Paid: two +1/+1 counters and no life. Declined: no
  counters and 4 life.

`CardScript.tribute` joins the mechanic-coverage exemptions, naming its runtime test.

- Asked of the controller.

## D1375 — "For each opponent, … up to one target … that player controls"

"When Grasp of Fate enters, for each opponent, exile up to one target nonland permanent that player
controls until Grasp of Fate leaves the battlefield." Grasp of Fate is a Commander staple, and the
same shape is on Enigma Thief ("… return up to one target nonland permanent that player controls to
its owner's hand") and others. One target for each opponent, chosen as the trigger goes on the
stack.

**The rule.**
- `TargetSpec.differentControllers` is new: no two of the spec's targets may share a controller.
  It is checked across the chosen targets in `checkTargets`, as D1216's `sameOwner` is.
- The sentence reads as "any number of target <kind>s an opponent controls" (D1356) with that
  flag on, so each opponent loses at most one.
- D575's exile-until-it-leaves shape takes the per-opponent form, and its exile now holds every
  card target. The return already brought back everything the source exiled.
- A clause wrapper does the same for return, tap, untap, destroy and exile without the "until".

**The bot**, in both of its target paths, skips a candidate whose controller it has already taken.
Building the test found that the trigger path (`auto:choose`) did not follow D1356's same-side
advice: a trigger's "destroy any number of target creatures" took every creature, its own included.
That path now stops as `chooseTargets` does.

Read whole now: Grasp of Fate, Enigma Thief, and others the measure counts. Hapatra's next sentence
("Put a stun counter on each of those creatures") is still unread.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests, in a three-player pod:
- Both fixtures read whole.
- Grasp of Fate: two Grizzly Bears of one opponent are refused. One from each opponent is exiled,
  and both come back when the Grasp leaves the battlefield.
- A trigger's "destroy any number of target creatures": the bot takes only its opponents'
  creatures.
- Enigma Thief: the bot takes one from each opponent.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- No controller check.
- The trigger path taking two of one controller.
- The trigger path ignoring the side.
- Only the first target exiled.
- The wrapper's spec left unmarked.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6614 of 6614 pass.

offered when the seat cannot pay, so then there is nothing to ask. One token only, and a token the
token reader cannot build refuses the line.

## D1377 — Evoke by exiling a card of a colour, and Solitude

"Evoke—Exile a black card from your hand." Fury, Grief, Solitude, Subtlety and Endurance, the five
Modern Horizons 2 Elemental Incarnations, all heavily played. D548 read evoke with a mana cost
only, and pinned this form as refused.

**The rule.** `CardScript.evoke.pitch` is the colour. The evoked cast costs no mana and exiles
another card of that colour from the hand, the way D691's pitch spells do. It is offered only while
there is such a card, and the play carries the choices (`discardOptions`), so the table and the bot
pick the card as they do for Force of Will. The sacrifice on arrival is evoke's own.

**Solitude's enter trigger.** "Exile up to one other target creature. That creature's controller
gains life equal to its power." This is Swords to Plowshares' trade, which was read on spells only.
It now reads on a trigger, with "up to one other" and either spelling of the controller. The power
is read before the exile.

Read whole now: Grief, Solitude. Fury's divided damage on a trigger, Subtlety's and Endurance's
enter triggers are still unread.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The fixtures read whole.
- Evoked for another black card with no mana: the card is exiled, the creature enters, its trigger
  gains 1 life, and it is sacrificed.
- With no other black card in hand, evoke is not offered, and a card of another colour is refused.
- Solitude exiles the opponent's Grizzly Bears, and that player gains 2 life.

D548's pin now covers Infestation alone ("Evoke—{1}{B}{B}, Pay 3 life"), which is still refused.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- Any card accepted as the pitch.
- The pitched card kept.
- Evoke offered with nothing to pitch.
- No life for Solitude's target.

## D1378 — Divided damage on triggered and activated abilities

"When Fury enters, it deals 4 damage divided as you choose among any number of target creatures
and/or planeswalkers." Spells have divided a quantity since #119, with the division announced as
the spell is cast. Abilities did not. `auto:choose` and `auto:activate` carried no division, so the
engine refused one, and the compiler left such lines unread: D463 for activated abilities and
loyalty abilities, D534 for triggers.

**The rule.** Both actions now carry `division`. It is announced with the targets, as a spell's is
(CR 601.2d, applied to abilities by 602.2b and 603.3d), and checked by the same `checkDivision`:
one number per target, each at least one, adding up to the amount. The stack object keeps it, so
the effect's `dividedAmong` reads it as a spell's does.

**The bot.** An activated ability goes through the same aimings a dividing spell does, so the
search prices them. A trigger has no search, so `dividedPick` chooses among those options: the one
that kills the most of the opponents' creatures, or the first (everything on the best target) when
none kills more. Options that put any damage on its own side are dropped while one that doesn't
exists. Fury's "any number of target creatures" lists its own creatures too.

**The table.** A waiting trigger that divides is answered the way a dividing spell is aimed: one
tap per point, the share chips on screen, a Back button that peels one point off, and the answer
sent with the last point. There is no Confirm while points are left.

Two places still refuse a division:
- A reflexive "When you do" (Blaster Hulk, Death to Our Enemies), whose queued trigger carries
  none.
- A sentence of several aimed parts (Magma Opus), where the division would have to say which
  part's targets it is about.

Read whole now: Fury, Inferno Titan, Bogardan Hellkite, Gang of Devils, Mogg Mob, Ral, Caller of
Storms, and others.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests and 2 web tests:
- The fixtures read whole.
- Fury's trigger refuses no division and a division of 2 and 1, and takes 2 and 2, which kills
  both Bears.
- The bot aims Fury's trigger at both Bears, 2 and 2, and at nothing of its own.
- Mogg Mob's sacrifice ability, divided 1 to the opponent and 2 to a Bear, is refused without a
  division.
- The table's reducer collects a trigger's division a point at a time and steps back a point.

The old refusal pins (D463's three, D534's Gang of Devils) now assert the reading.

Faults injected by hand: 6, all caught.
- The trigger's division unchecked.
- The trigger's division not kept.
- The bot's trigger branch removed.
- The bot taking the first option instead of the most kills.
- The ability's division not kept.
- The ability's division unchecked.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6624 of 6624 pass. Web tests: 283 of 283. Web
typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,678 of 31,900 cards (+7 over D1377's 17,671), 40,590 of 59,888 lines (+10).

## D1379 — "You may pay {X}. If you do, …"

"When Squealing Devil enters, you may pay {X}. If you do, target creature gets +X/+0 until end of
turn." Also Flameblast Dragon ("{X}{R}"), Rise of the Hobgoblins and Tilonalli's Summoner. A fixed
price ("you may pay {2}. If you do") has been read since D447, with the engine paying it. An X in
the price was refused.

**The rule.** Two questions:
1. The yes-or-no, priced with any fixed part ("{R}" of "{X}{R}") as before.
2. Asked only on a yes: X. This is a number question with a price, `NumberDecisionSpec.payX`.

The range offered stops at the most the seat can pay, with the fixed part counted beside it. So
three Mountains offer X up to three for "{X}" and up to two for "{X}{R}". After the answers, the
engine pays X generic mana after the fixed part. An X that can't be paid by then reads as nought.
The effect is handed the X paid.

**The reading.** A bare X has been read on the spell path only (`xSpellResolution`), because
everywhere else X was zero and a card would "work and do nothing". Here X is the X just paid, so the
effect is read with X marked as "that many" is (D903) and run with the paid X as that amount. That
reads tokens, counters, damage, life and cards. The spell path's X reader is the fallback, given the
card's name for its "~ deals X damage".

Refused:
- An effect that asks its own question.
- X in what a target must be ("target creature card with mana value X", Relentless Dead). The
  target is chosen as the trigger goes on the stack, before X is.

Still unread: the reflexive "When you do" forms (Electro, Isareth, Wildborn Preserver) and the
"X can't be greater than …" riders (Mortarion, Shanna). The bot declines these questions, as it
declines every compiled priced "may" (D447).

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The fixtures read whole.
- "{X}" with three lands: X is offered up to three. X of 2 makes two Goblins and taps two lands.
- Declined: nothing paid, nothing made.
- "{X}{R}" with three lands: X up to two, and X of 2 deals 2 with all three lands tapped.

Faults injected by hand: 5, all caught.
- No clamp.
- X not paid.
- The fixed part not counted in the clamp.
- The effect not handed X.
- The fixed part not priced.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6628 of 6628 pass. Test typecheck and web typecheck
clean.

Coverage: 17,684 of 31,900 cards (+6 over D1378's 17,678), 40,598 of 59,888 lines (+8).

## D1380 — "You may pay {X}. When you do", and a card that calls itself he or she

Two pieces, both on trigger lines.

**The reflexive form of D1379.** "When Electro leaves the battlefield, you may pay {X}. When you
do, he deals X damage to target player." Also Wildborn Preserver, Rose Room Treasurer and Tester of
the Tangential. The first half is D1379's priced yes-or-no and X. The reflexive trigger it queues
(D948) carries the X paid (`reflexive[].amount`), which becomes its stack object's event amount, and
the second half reads X as "that many" (D903). Its targets are chosen as it goes on the stack,
after X is paid (CR 603.12).

**Pronouns.** Oracle text names a character card with its own pronouns: "When Gandalf enters, he
deals 3 damage divided …", "When Momo enters, he deals 4 damage …", "she gains indestructible",
"put a +1/+1 counter on him", "his power". Oracle text has used "they" for players since 2017, so a
gendered pronoun on a card is the card. `selfPronouns` reads them as "it" and "its" on a trigger
line, and never inside a hyphenated name ("She-Hulk"). 13 of the 28 unread trigger lines that do
this now read; the rest wait on other shapes ("for each time he was kicked", "is dealt damage").

Read whole now: Gandalf, Spark Starter; Momo, Rambunctious Rascal; Boomerang, Blade Flinger; Jet,
Freedom Fighter; and others. Electro's trigger reads, and its static line about red mana does not.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The fixtures read whole.
- Pay X of three: the reflexive trigger is aimed after the payment and deals 3.
- "When Test Hero enters, he deals 2 damage to target creature an opponent controls" kills a Bear.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The X not put on the reflexive trigger.
- The X not recorded on the queue.
- No pronoun reading.
- The second half read without the X marked.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6631 of 6631 pass. Test typecheck clean.

## D1381 — A legendary card that calls itself by the name before its epithet

"Whenever Smaug attacks, he deals damage equal to the number of Treasures you control to any
target", on *Smaug the Magnificent*. Oracle text calls a legendary card by its short name after
the first mention. D438 read the short name of a titled card ("Bilbo", for "Bilbo, Retired
Burglar"), which is the part before the comma. A name with an epithet and no comma had no short
name: Smaug the Magnificent, Dáin of the Ancient Halls, Hazoret the Fervent, Gideon of the Trials,
Phage the Untouchable. 43 legal cards use theirs in their own text.

**The rule.** The first word, before "the", "of" or "of the", on a **legendary** card only. The
same shape names ordinary cards whose first word is a common noun: Wall of Kelp, Case of the Lost
Witness, Knight of the Mists. `selfRef` cannot see the type line, so `compileCard` sets the alias
for the card it is compiling (`withEpithetAlias`, the way `withXPayable` carries the mana cost),
and `selfRef` uses it for that card's own name alone.

With D1380's pronouns, Smaug and Dáin now read whole, and so does Hazoret.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The short name reads on a legendary card, for "the" and "of the" alike.
- The short name doesn't read on a card that isn't legendary: its line stays unread.
- The short name's trigger works: the card's arrival gains its 2 life.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- `selfRef` ignoring the alias.
- No legendary check.
- `compileCard` not setting it.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6634 of 6634 pass. Test typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,709 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1380's 17,700), 40,642 of 59,888 lines (+17).

## D1382 — "Loses the game", and Phage the Untouchable

"Whenever Phage deals combat damage to a player, that player loses the game." D690 made "you lose
the game" a rule the engine keeps (`loseTheGame`, with CR 104.3a's "can't lose" for Platinum

**The readers.**

  read as clauses: Door to Nothingness. Through the hit-player swap (D566) this also reads Phage's

  Phage's arrival.
- "Destroy that creature. It can't be regenerated." on a trigger about the creature it fought: the

- Cast from the hand, Phage's controller does not lose.

- Blocked by a 2/2 with a regeneration shield, the blocker is destroyed anyway.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.

- The negation ignored.
- The rider ignored.
- No "loses the game" reader.

- The hand test inverted.

- Creatures counted.

## D1387 — "Where X is that creature's power" on an event

"Whenever another creature enters, you may put X +1/+1 counters on Hamletback Goliath, where X is
that creature's power." D1020 measured the event's creature for "gain life equal to its power" and
"draw cards equal to its power", and D823 did the same for tokens. Any other sentence sized "where
X is its power" or "where X is that creature's power" was unread.

**The rule.** On the same four events (an entry, a death, an attack, a combat hit), the sentence
before "where X is" is read with X marked as "that many" is (D903). The effect is handed the event
creature's size as that amount: live while it is on the battlefield, and as it last was once gone
(CR 608.2h). The amount is never below 0. That reads counters, damage, life and cards through the
existing "that many" readers.

A pump of the card itself is read on its own ("~ gets +X/+0 until end of turn", Arni, Renowned
Champion), because a pump's X isn't a count those readers take. A sentence that already says "that
many" is refused, so the two amounts can't be confused.

Read whole now: Hamletback Goliath, Kresh the Bloodbraided, Arni, Renowned Champion.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The fixtures read whole.
- The Goliath takes three counters when a 3/3 enters.
- Arni gets +3/+0, and its toughness is unchanged.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The self pump raising toughness too.

reads it as the card's name.

## D1392 — A Saga's chapters, compiled

"I — Each opponent sacrifices a creature or planeswalker. II — Each opponent discards a card. III —
Put target creature or planeswalker card from a graveyard onto the battlefield under your control."
The engine has run Sagas since the hand-written ones (CR 714):
- `CardScript.saga`, with a trigger `on: { kind: 'chapter', n }` for each chapter;
- the lore counter as it enters and in each precombat main phase (`advanceSagas`);
- the sacrifice once the last chapter has resolved.

The compiler read none of the 220 legal Sagas.

**The reader.** A chapter line, "I — …" or "I, II — …", is read as a triggered ability's text,
through `triggerFromLine` with an entry prologue. The one trigger it makes is put on the chapter
numbers instead. So a chapter gets everything a trigger's effect does (targets, questions, "you
may", reflexive "when you do"), and a reflexive trigger the text queues comes with it. Anything else
the reading carries refuses the line. The number of chapters is derived from the triggers, as the
hand-written Sagas have it.

296 of the 575 chapter lines on legal Sagas read, and 28 Sagas read whole: The Eldest Reborn,
History of Benalia and The Birth of Meletis among them. Still unread are the chapters that are
another shape: "Exile this Saga, then return it to the battlefield transformed" (Fable of the
Mirror-Breaker and the Kamigawa Sagas), Urza's Saga's granted abilities, and Read ahead.

**Tests.** 2 engine tests:
- A fixture Saga reads whole, with `saga` set and chapters 1, 2 and 3.
- Played out: chapter I as it enters (a Soldier and one lore counter), II on its controller's next
  turn (a second Soldier), III the turn after (3 life), and then it is sacrificed.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- No chapter reader.
- `saga` not set.
- Every chapter numbered I.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6671 of 6671 pass. Test typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,799 of 31,900 cards (+28 over D1391's 17,771), 41,034 of 59,888 lines (+298).

## D1394 — A modal spell cast for an alternative cost is offered once per mode

Sweep 105001 (build a34b730, D1384) finished 99 of 100 games. Seed 105085 threw "choose a mode for
Thunderbolt". The bot had cast Thunderbolt from the top of its library with Bolas's Citadel's life
payment, which is the play `legalActions` offered, and the engine refused it for having no mode. It
is the standing "never offers a play it then refuses" invariant.

**The fault.** A modal spell's printed cast is offered once per legal combination of modes, each
row carrying its `modes` and the modes' targets. The alternative-cost rows (Citadel's life,
pitch, evoke, dash, prototype, awaken, overload and the rest) were built from the card's top-level
target specs, and a modal spell has none. So a modal spell offered through any of them had no mode,
and the engine refused the cast as a mode was required.

**The fix.** The alternative-cost loop now expands the modes the same way: one row per
combination, carrying `modes`, the chosen modes' targets (with awaken's land after them), and the
modes in the description. A combination whose targets can't be filled isn't offered.

Seed 105085 replayed on the a34b730 build with this fix: it finishes on turn 94.

**Tests.** 1 engine test:
- With Bolas's Citadel and a modal instant on top of the library, every Citadel play for it
  carries its modes, and the cast with the player mode deals 3 to the opponent and costs 2 life.

Faults injected by hand: 1, caught: the modes not expanded.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6674 of 6674 pass. Test typecheck and web typecheck
clean.

Coverage: 17,806 of 31,900 cards (+0 over D1393's 17,806), 41,062 of 59,888 lines (+0).
