## D1396 — Read ahead

"Read ahead (As this Saga enters, choose a chapter and start with that many lore counters. Add one
after your draw step. Skipped chapters don't trigger.)" Ten legal Sagas print it, and the line
was unread on all of them (CR 714.3b).

**The rule.** An enters-choice (`entersChoice: 'read-ahead'`), asked as the Saga resolves, the way
riot and the creature-type choice are. The answers run from "Chapter I" to the Saga's last chapter,
counted from its own chapter triggers when the question is asked. Chosen II or later, the Saga gets
that many lore counters and only that chapter triggers. The chapters before it are skipped, and the
arrival's own first counter is not added on top. Chosen I, it is the ordinary arrival. The bot
starts at the beginning. A Saga put onto the battlefield without being cast is asked nothing and
starts at chapter I.

`READ_AHEAD_CHAPTERS` lives in `effects.ts` beside the other answer words, so the resolution in
`automation.ts` and the question in `scripts.ts` share one list.

41 of the 220 legal Sagas read whole.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests, on a fixture three-chapter Saga with read ahead:
- It reads whole.
- Started at chapter III: only chapter III's 3 life, and it is sacrificed.
- Started at chapter II: chapter I is skipped, and it has two lore counters.
- Started at chapter I: the ordinary Saga.

Faults injected by hand: 3, all caught.
- The chosen chapter ignored.
- The chapter not triggered.
- Six answers offered for three chapters.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6680 of 6680 pass. Test typecheck and web typecheck
clean.

Coverage: 17,812 of 31,900 cards (+2 over D1395's 17,810), 41,081 of 59,888 lines (+10).

## D1397 — Restricted mana that floats, marked with what it may pay for

"{2}{G}{G}, {T}: Add six {G}. Spend this mana only to cast creature spells or activate abilities of
creatures." That is Castle Garenbrig, a staple and the last card on the first staples list. D595
read "Spend this mana only …" on a mana ability the auto-payer taps while paying for something its
restriction allows. A pool of plain counts couldn't tell restricted mana from free mana, so
restricted mana never floated: such an ability wasn't a button, and the engine refused it when
pressed. An ability the auto-payer never uses (a mana cost, or a cost other than tapping,
sacrificing itself, life or energy) therefore had no way to be used at all, and D669 left
Garenbrig's line unread.

**The pool.** `GameState.boundMana` holds restricted mana per seat, one entry a mana: its type and
the words of its restriction.
- `spendRestriction` reads the words again when something is paid for, so the state stays
  JSON-safe.
- `manaSources` offers each entry as a source, first and only for a payment its words allow.
- `tapSources` spends an entry rather than tapping anything.
- Entries `payFrom` took out but didn't need go back into the pool still marked. That path is a
  guard: the solver takes one-mana entries only as needed, so no test reaches it.
- The pool empties with the others as a step ends (CR 500.4), and the view shows it.

**The ability.** A restricted mana ability the auto-payer never uses is offered as a play, and
pressing one makes its mana into the restricted pool. Pressing a free one (Ancient Ziggurat) is
allowed too now, with the same result. Only a restriction that needs the
source's chosen type is still made only while paying, where the source is known.

**The reading.** "Add six {G}" beside a mana cost is read as the run of symbols written out; the
data reader takes the words only beside {T}.

**The table.** The arena bar shows restricted mana beside the free pool as outlined pips with what
they may pay for ("only cast creature spells …"), from `boundPips`.

Read whole now: Castle Garenbrig. Food Chain still needs "Exile a creature you control" as a cost
and "1 plus the exiled creature's mana value" as its amount, which is D1398.

D669's pin now asserts Garenbrig's line reads, as a costed ability with six {G} and its
restriction. D595's Ziggurat test now asserts that pressing it floats one marked mana and no free
mana, where it asserted a refusal.

**Tests.** 6 engine tests and 1 web test:
- The fixtures read whole.
- Pressed, the six {G} float marked and the free pool is empty.
- They pay for a 6-mana creature and are spent.
- A {1}{G} creature spends two, and four stay marked.
- An instant isn't offered with them and is refused.
- They empty as the step ends.
- `boundPips` groups the marked mana by what it may pay for.

Faults injected by hand: 6, of which 5 caught.
- Not offered as sources: caught.
- Not removed when spent: caught.
- Made into the free pool: caught.
- Not emptied: caught.
- The restriction not asked: caught.
- The return of unneeded entries removed: **not caught**, as no test reaches it (above).

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6686 of 6686 pass. Web tests: 284 of 284. Test
typecheck and web typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,813 of 31,900 cards (+1 over D1396's 17,812), 41,082 of 59,888 lines (+1).

## D1398 — Exile a creature you control as a cost: Food Chain

"Exile a creature you control: Add X mana of any one color, where X is 1 plus the exiled creature's
mana value. Spend this mana only to cast creature spells." That is Food Chain, a staple on the
second staples list. D1397 made a pressed restricted mana ability float its mana marked; what was
left was the cost and the amount.

**The cost.** `AbilityCost.exileInsteadOfSacrifice`: "Exile a creature you control", "… another
creature you control" and "… an artifact you control" set `sacrifice` as the matching "Sacrifice …"
does, so the choice and its options are the sacrifice's, and the flag says the chosen permanent is
exiled. Paying it moves the permanent to exile: it doesn't die, so no death trigger sees it. Its
size is read as it leaves, as for a sacrifice. The log says "exiles" rather than "sacrifices".

**The amount.** `AbilityDef.producesPerSacrificedPlus`: D1342's `producesPerSacrificed`, plus this
many more. "Add X mana of any one color, where X is (1 plus) the exiled/sacrificed creature's
power/mana value" is read as one row per colour, each with the line's spending restriction.

Read whole now: Food Chain and City of Shadows. The Soul Stone's line reads its cost but not
"Harness".

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The fixtures read whole, as five colour rows that exile, with the +1; a City of Shadows-style line
  reads whole.
- The Hill Giant goes to exile, not the graveyard, and a "whenever another creature you control
  dies" trigger doesn't gain life.
- Exiling a mana value 4 creature makes five of the chosen colour, marked, none free.
- With one Forest, the green pays for a six-mana creature and is spent.
- An instant is paid by the Forest and the five marked stay.

Faults injected by hand: 5, of which 4 caught.
- Sacrificed rather than exiled: caught.
- The +1 dropped: caught.
- The restriction dropped from the rows: caught.
- The flag not set by the cost reader: caught.
- A compile.ts route for the line: **not caught**, because the line reads without it, so that edit
  was removed.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6691 of 6691 pass. Test typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,816 of 31,900 cards (+3 over D1397's 17,813), 41,085 of 59,888 lines (+3).

## D1399 — Colour words in a spending restriction: Eldrazi Temple

"{T}: Add {C}{C}. Spend this mana only to cast colorless Eldrazi spells or activate abilities of
colorless Eldrazi." D595's restriction reader read only type words against a type line, so a colour
word refused the line and Eldrazi Temple's second ability stayed unread.

**What is paid for.** `PaymentFor.spellColors` and `PaymentFor.abilityColors` carry the spell's
colours and the ability's source's colours, as they are now. They're filled where a spell or an
ability is offered and where it is paid for. If they're absent, a restriction that names a colour
refuses.

**The words.** "colorless" (no colours), "multicolored" (two or more) and "monocolored" (exactly one)
are each a test beside the type and subtype words, so "colorless Eldrazi" needs both.
"Colorless" is read before a plural "s" is taken off. "An ability of a colorless permanent" reads
"permanent" as saying nothing more. "Monocolored spells of that color" is still unread: the colour
of the mana made is not read.

Read whole now: Eldrazi Temple and Pillar of the Paruns. Shrine of the Forsaken Gods reads its
restriction but not its "Activate only if you control seven or more lands".

Three pins used "a multicolored spell" as an example of an unread restriction: the Pillar row and
the D497 row in compile.test.ts, and D595's in scripts.test.ts. They now use "monocolored spells
of that color".

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- The fixtures read whole, and four colour restrictions parse.
- The colour words test the colours given, and refuse without them.
- A colorless Eldrazi costing four is cast with the Temple and two Forests.
- Neither a green Eldrazi nor a colorless Golem can be cast with them.
- A colorless Eldrazi's {2} ability is paid by the Temple alone, and a blue Eldrazi's isn't offered.

Faults injected by hand: 7, all caught. The sixth wasn't caught until the ability test was added.
- "colorless" always true: caught.
- The spell's colours not given when offered: caught.
- The spell's colours not given when paid: caught.
- The colours not passed to the test: caught.
- "permanent" not skipped: caught.
- The ability's colours not given when offered: caught, by the ability test.
- The ability's colours not given when paid: caught.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6696 of 6696 pass. Test typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,820 of 31,900 cards (+4 over D1398's 17,816), 41,089 of 59,888 lines (+4).

## D1400 — Urza's Saga, and a 0/0 kept alive by its own static

Three things, the last found by the second.

**A Saga that gains an ability.** "I — Urza's Saga gains "{T}: Add {C}."" and "II — Urza's Saga
gains "{2}, {T}: Create a 0/0 colorless Construct artifact creature token with 'This token gets
+1/+1 for each artifact you control.'"" give the Saga an ability with no end (CR 611.2c).
- `sagaGains` reads the quoted ability as a line of the card's own, with its inner single quotes as
  the double quotes a printed line has.
- `CardInstance.gainedChapters` records the chapters whose gain has resolved on this object. The
  chapter's trigger marks the Saga, if it is still on the battlefield as the trigger resolves.
- A zone change clears the mark, as it clears a Class's level (CR 400.7).
- The ability is live only once marked: an activated ability through `activateOnlyIf`, a trigger
  through `condition`, as D638 scopes a Class's levels.
- One chapter number only; anything else stays unread.

**A search by printed mana cost.** "an artifact card with mana cost {0} or {1}" compares the card's
printed mana cost exactly, so a card whose cost is {X} (mana value 0 in a library) is not one.

Read whole now: Urza's Saga and Down in the Valley.

**A mana line's restriction and then its condition.** Shrine of the Forsaken Gods' "{T}: Add {C}{C}.
Spend this mana only to cast colorless spells. Activate only if you control seven or more lands."
The data reader took both sentences as one restriction, which refused the line. Now each is read as
it would be alone, and a condition that isn't read still refuses the line. Shrine of the Forsaken
Gods reads whole.

**A 0/0 kept alive by its own static died on arrival.** Testing chapter II showed the Construct token
never stayed. Nor did a cast 0/0 artifact creature with "~ gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control".
- `settle` checked state-based actions once before its loop installed each arrival's statics, so the
  first check saw a 0/0 and put it into the graveyard.
- A static is true from the moment its permanent is there (CR 611.3a). `arrivalStatics` now installs
  the arrivals' own statics before that first check, with the script the loop uses.
- A permanent that chooses a type, colour or name as it enters waits for the loop, which answers
  first. The loop's guard finds the effects already there and doesn't install them twice.
- A face-down permanent is skipped, as in the loop.
- This affects every card whose size comes from its own static, and every token made that way.

**Tests.** 11 engine tests:
- Shrine (3): it reads whole with both the restriction and the condition, and a condition it can't
  read refuses the line. Seven lands give the {C}{C} and cast an eight-mana colorless creature. With
  six lands, a seven-mana one can't be cast.
- Urza's Saga (8):
  - The Saga and the search read whole.
  - Once chapter I resolves, the Saga taps for {C}, and a Saga no chapter has resolved on can't.
  - Chapter II's ability isn't offered before chapter II. After it, it makes a 1/1 Construct.
  - Returned to the hand, the card carries no mark.
  - The search offers the {0} and {1} artifacts and not the {X} or {2} ones.
  - A cast 0/0 kept alive by its own static stays, as a 1/1.
  - A chooser put onto the battlefield has both its chosen-type static and its plain one.
  - A face-down creature's static doesn't apply.

Faults injected by hand: 11, of which 10 caught.
- Shrine's condition ignored: caught.
- The two sentences not split: caught.
- An unread condition not refusing the line: caught.
- `arrivalStatics` not called: caught.
- The gained ability not gated: caught.
- The chapter not marking the Saga: caught.
- The mark not cleared on leaving: caught.
- Mana value compared instead of the printed cost: caught.
- The inner quotes not converted: caught.
- The chooser not waiting for the loop: caught, by the chooser test.
- The face-down skip removed: **not caught**. `silenced` in characteristics.ts already mutes a
  face-down source's effects, so the skip only keeps the pre-pass consistent with the loop.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6707 of 6707 pass. Test typecheck clean.

## D1401 — Discard up to N, then draw that many: Fable of the Mirror-Breaker

"Discard up to two cards, then draw that many cards" (Kinetic Augur, Cathartic Pyre, Greasewrench
Goblin), "discard any number of cards, then draw that many cards" (Illuminate History), and "…
that many cards plus one" (Colossus of the Blood Age). Fable of the Mirror-Breaker's chapter II is
"You may discard up two cards. If you do, draw that many cards", as the data prints it. None of
these read.

**The reader.** `discardAnyThenThatMany` is D1332's sacrifice reader with a hand for a battlefield.
- The cards are the controller's choice as the effect resolves: from none up to the number printed,
  and "land cards" narrows them to lands.
- They're discarded, so madness and "whenever you discard" see them.
- "That many" is how many were discarded, run as the event amount.
- "If you do," after "you may discard" is dropped, since a count of none already draws nothing.
- What follows may not ask a question of its own.
- The bot discards nothing, as it sacrifices nothing in D1332.
- "Up two" is read as "up to", as the data reader already takes Scryfall's "if your control a basic
  land" for "you".

**"Draw that many cards plus one"** (or two, or three) is read beside D903's "draw that many cards".

Read whole now: Fable of the Mirror-Breaker, Kinetic Augur, Cathartic Pyre, Colossus of the Blood
Age, Illuminate History, Greasewrench Goblin and Obsessive Astronomer. Jaya Ballard, Daretti,
Cavalier of Flame and Celes read this line, but each has another line still unread. Into the
Night's line is still unread, because it opens with "It becomes night."

**Tests.** 6 engine tests:
- Four fixtures read whole.
- Two discarded draw two, and the two are in the graveyard.
- Discarding none draws none, and three, more than the card allows, is refused.
- "Any number, plus one": discarding one draws two.
- "Up two" asks for up to two once its "you may" is taken.
- "Land cards" offers only the Mountains.

Faults injected by hand: 7, all caught.
- That many read as none: caught.
- The number printed ignored: caught.
- The land filter dropped: caught.
- The plus dropped: caught.
- "Up two" not taken: caught.
- "If you do," not dropped: caught.
- The cards not discarded: caught.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6713 of 6713 pass. Test typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,832 of 31,900 cards (+9 over D1400's 17,823), 41,112 of 59,888 lines (+18).

## D1402 — A search for a card with a keyword: Mystical Teachings

"Search your library for an instant card or a card with flash, reveal it, put it into your hand,
then shuffle." This is Mystical Teachings and Waterlogged Teachings. "A creature card with flying"
and "… with deathtouch" are the same kind of filter.

**The filter.** "<card phrase> with <keyword>" narrows the phrase to cards that print that keyword.
- The keyword is read as a card in a library has it: its printed keyword lines (`printedKeywords`),
  or a hand-written script's `keywords`.
- One keyword only. A word that isn't a keyword leaves the phrase to the branches it reached before.
- Not when the phrase joins two kinds with "or", which D1054's branch splits first.
- D1054's two-phrase branch now takes a keyword after its second phrase, and that phrase may be "a
  card" with nothing before "card".
- Only a keyword: "an instant card or a sorcery card with mana value 3 or less" still doesn't read,
  as before this change.

Read whole now: Mystical Teachings and Waterlogged Teachings. Mwonvuli Beast Tracker's entry line is
still unread.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- Five fixtures read whole.
- "An instant card or a card with flash" offers the instant and the creature with flash, and not
  the creature with flying or the Bears.
- "A creature card with flying" offers the flyer only.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught.
- The keyword not checked: caught.
- The two-phrase branch not taking a keyword: caught.
- The printed keyword lines not read: caught.
- The "or" guard dropped: caught.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6716 of 6716 pass. Test typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,835 of 31,900 cards (+3 over D1401's 17,832), 41,115 of 59,888 lines (+3).

## D1403 — Rotlung Reanimator, seven lands untapped, and Relic of Progenitus

Three widely played Commander cards and their families, from a new list of 355 such cards
(`staples3.txt` in the scratchpad), of which 298 read whole before this.

**"~ or another Cleric dies"** (Rotlung Reanimator, Vengeful Dead, Noxious Ghoul, Serum Tank,
Minotaur, Roxxon CEO). D483's "~ or another <thing> you control" pattern now takes the line
without "you control". The "another" half is then anyone's: Rotlung makes a Zombie for an opponent's
Cleric. Plain "~ or another creature dies" stays with Blood Artist's own row, which has always read
it. Read through the new path, it would give a different shape from Blood Artist's hand-written
script, and the comparison pin in compiled-vs-written.test.ts caught that.

**"Untap up to seven lands"** (Palinchron, Great Whale): the count reader now takes six and seven.

**"Target player exiles a card from their graveyard"** (Relic of Progenitus): the target player
chooses from their own graveyard, as a discard is chosen from their own hand. The count is one to
three.

Read whole now: Rotlung Reanimator, Vengeful Dead, Noxious Ghoul, Serum Tank, Minotaur, Roxxon CEO,
Palinchron, Great Whale and Relic of Progenitus.

**Tests.** 5 engine tests:
- Five fixtures read whole.
- An opponent's Cleric dying makes a Zombie for the Rotlung's controller and none for the opponent,
  and a Bear dying makes none.
- The Rotlung dying makes one.
- The Whale asks to untap up to seven of eight tapped lands.
- The Relic's target player is asked, chooses the Bears, and the Bears are exiled while the other
  card stays.

Faults injected by hand: 4, all caught. The Blood Artist guard was found the other way round: the
whole suite failed the compiled-vs-written pin before the guard existed.
- The "another" half kept to your side: caught.
- "Seven" not read: caught.
- The Relic asking its controller: caught.
- The Relic exiling nothing: caught.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6721 of 6721 pass. Test typecheck clean.

## D1404 — Exile ~ from your hand as a cost: the Spirit Guides

"Exile Simian Spirit Guide from your hand: Add {R}." The card is used from the hand, as cycling is,
but the cost exiles it rather than discarding it. Simian and Elvish Spirit Guide are on the third
staples list.

**The cost.** `AbilityCost.exileSelfFromHand`:
- The cost reader reads "Exile ~ from your hand".
- The ability is offered and activated from the hand, as `discardSelf` is.
- Paying it moves the card to exile, before the mana is made. It isn't a discard, so nothing that
  watches discards sees it.
- On the battlefield the card has nothing to activate.
- The cost reader's guard against costs that charge nothing now counts it. That guard was what
  refused the line.

A compile.ts route for the line was tried and removed, because the line reads without it (a fault
check showed nothing depended on it). D446's pin in compile.test.ts listed "Exile Probe Thing from
your hand" as refused. It now pins "Exile a card from your hand", another card from the hand, which
still has no field.

Read whole now: Simian Spirit Guide and Elvish Spirit Guide.

**Tests.** 3 engine tests:
- The fixture reads whole, as a mana ability whose cost exiles it from the hand.
- From the hand it's offered, and activating it exiles the card for {R}.
- On the battlefield it isn't offered and is refused.

Faults injected by hand: 5, of which 4 caught.
- Not offered from the hand: caught.
- Not activated from the hand: caught.
- Not exiled: caught.
- The guard not counting it: caught.
- The compile.ts route: **not caught**, and removed (above).

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6724 of 6724 pass. Test typecheck clean.

## D1405 — A card that may be cast from its own graveyard: Gravecrawler

"You may cast Gravecrawler from your graveyard as long as you control a Zombie." D1287's permission
belongs to a permanent (Karador, Lurrus) and is used once each turn on its controller's own turn.
Here the card is its own permission.

**The field.** `CardScript.castsSelfFromGraveyard`, with an optional `while`:
- It's read from "You may cast ~ (or this card) from your graveyard", with "as long as …" or "if …"
  after it read by `staticCondition`, the reader a static's condition uses.
- A condition that reader can't read leaves the line unread.
- `yardPermission` answers it first, with the card as its own permit. The card is cast from its
  owner's graveyard for its printed cost at its normal timing, as often as it gets there, and
  only while the condition holds (asked with the card as source and its owner as controller).

Read whole now: Gravecrawler and Skaab Ruinator. Marang River Prowler ("a black or green
permanent"), Oathsworn Vampire ("if you gained life this turn") and Ebondeath need conditions
`staticCondition` doesn't read yet. Their Number Is Legion, a sorcery, prints the plain line and
it is still unread there; why is not yet looked into.

"Has a card behind every mechanic it declares" exempts the field, as it does D1287's, naming this
entry's runtime test as evidence. No built-in deck plays one.

**Tests.** 4 engine tests:
- The fixtures read whole, and an unread condition leaves the line unread.
- With a Zombie on the battlefield the Crawler is cast from the graveyard, and with none it isn't
  offered.
- With no condition, the Ghoul comes back, dies, and is offered again the same turn.
- A card in an opponent's graveyard isn't offered, and casting it is refused.

Faults injected by hand: 4, of which 3 caught.
- The card's own permission not asked: caught.
- The condition not asked: caught.
- An unread condition read as none: caught.
- The owner check removed: **not caught**. The offer lists only the seat's own graveyard, and the
  cast is refused elsewhere, so the check is kept as a second guard.

The scripts tests, compile tests and pins: 6728 of 6728 pass. Test typecheck clean.

Coverage: 17,851 of 31,900 cards (+2 over D1404's 17,849), 41,132 of 59,888 lines (+3).
